A 48-year-old white patient presents to the dermatology clinic with papulosquamous cutaneous lesions that recently appeared on their chest, arms, and the dorsal aspects of their hands. The patient has a family history of autoimmune disorders, including systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Physical examination reveals that the lesions lack induration and do not appear to be leaving scars. Biopsy of the lesion is performed, revealing mild inflammatory infiltrate. Direct immunofluorescence shows a granular deposition at the dermal-epidermal junction. Serology indicates that the patient is positive for anti-Ro/SSA (Sjögren-syndrome-related antigen A).

A 15-year-old white adolescent presents to the dermatology clinic with an asymptomatic rash on their upper back that has persisted for 4 months. Physical examination reveals hyperpigmented scaly papules coalescing into confluent plaques with peripheral reticulated papillomatosis. The patient is overweight but has no history of any other medical conditions.

A 8-year-old patient presents to the clinic for evaluation of a progressively worsening nail dystrophy that began a few months ago. The patient’s parent denies a family history of skin diseases and reports that they have no history of medical problems. On physical examination, all of the patient’s fingernails and toenails show hyperkeratosis, longitudinal ridging, loss of luster, and roughness. Their hair, skin, and oral mucosa are unremarkable. Nail biopsy reveals spongiotic changes and exocytosis of inflammatory cells into the nail epithelia. The results of a fungal culture are negative.

A 54-year-old patient presents with 2 years of gradual hair thinning. They say that their mother also experienced hair thinning starting in her 50s. They deny scalp itch. They deny clumps of hair coming out in the shower or on their pillow. They deny any preceding stressful life events. They deny wearing their hair in tight braids. They deny loss of eyebrows or eyelashes.

A 45-year-old patient presents with 3 months of tender bumps on the shins. They say that 4 months ago, they were hospitalized for abdominal pain and were found to be positive for hepatitis B. They deny ever having tuberculosis. They deny itching or scratching at the bumps. They deny any rash on the trunk or extremities.

A 70-year-old patient presents with 1 year of a non-healing growth on the right cheek. They say they first noticed it when they accidentally bumped into it and it bled easily. They deny any preceding trauma to the lesion.

An 8-year-old patient presents with 1 week of itchy blisters on the ears. They just recently returned from spring break with their family. They deny using any particular products on the ears before the rash. They say that this has occurred yearly for the last several years, always around the same time. They deny proximal muscle weakness. They deny flaking in the scalp.

A 67-year-old patient presents with unrelenting itch present over the last 6 months. They endorse weight loss and fatigue. They deny any liver or kidney disease. They deny exacerbation of itch with water. Physical examination is significant for numerous punctate and linear erosions consistent with excoriations as well as diffuse shoddy lymphadenopathy. A KOH scraping is performed which is negative for scabies.

A 25-year-old patient presents with 6 months of discoloration in the underarms. They deny any blisters or erosions in the areas. They deny any history of diabetes, insulin resistance, or weight gain. They deny itch. They deny discoloration only with sweating. Physical examination reveals reddish-brown patches in the underarms; Wood's lamp reveals coral red fluorescence.

A 72-year-old patient is seen by the Dermatology consult service for a rash which has developed during a prolonged 6-week hospitalization following a hemorrhagic stroke. They are currently intubated, so history is limited, but per chart review, nurses documented the rash starting 5 days ago. They have been experiencing high fevers as well as unexplained transaminitis over the last few days. They have taken atorvastatin and pantoprazole for years, including during the hospitalization. Following the stroke, they were started on carbamazepine for seizure prophylaxis. They contracted MRSA pneumonia 2 weeks ago and have been on vancomycin since then. They have also been on cefepime and micafungin for the last 5 days given the fevers and transaminitis. Physical examination is significant for diffuse erythematous patches extending over the face, chest, back, and extremities, as well as facial edema.

A 25-year-old patient presents with 2 years of pruriginous erythematous plaques with silver scales on elbows, knees and buttocks. They say that their father is known for hand and back arthritis. They deny personal and family history of dermatology conditions and atopy. Physical exam reveals pitting on all 10 fingernails.

A 60-year-old patient presents with a non-healing painful ulcer on their right leg for 4 months. They say they first noticed it after they accidentally bumped into a chair. They are known for rheumatoid arthritis and hypertension, and have taken methotrexate and bisoprolol for years. According to the patient, oral antibiotics and wound debridement have only increased the size of the ulcer. Physical exam reveals a 5x5 cm fibrinous ulcer with violaceous undermined borders on their right shin.

A 10-year-old patient presents with non-blanchable palpable purple papules on both legs for a week. Sore throat preceded the skin lesions. Their parents deny any other history of infectious diseases or new medications. The patient complains about abdominal pain and trouble walking. Their vitals are stable. Physical exam reveals red and swollen ankles on top of palpable purpura on both legs.

A 16-year-old patient presents with an increased number of perinasal dome-shaped smooth flesh-colored papules. They are known to have epilepsy. They deny family history of cancer. The physical exam reveals hypopigmented macules on their back, three café-au-lait patches, skin colored to hypopigmented plaque on the trunk, and flesh-colored papules emerging from nail folds. A biopsy of the facial lesions shows dermal proliferation of fibroblasts in a collagenous stroma associated with increased dilated blood vessels.

A 40-year-old patient complains about squamous papules on their scalp for 10 years. These lesions responded to topical corticosteroids but recur when the treatment is stopped. They deny any systemic symptoms. Physical exam reveals erythematous scaly papules with signs of atrophy and scarring, as well as cicatricial alopecia. Skin biopsy shows lichenoid interface dermatitis with hyperkeratosis and follicular plugging.

A 30-year-old patient presents with itchy skin lesions on their arms and legs. They deny family history of atopy and psoriasis. They do not take any medication and have no risk factors for hepatitis. Review of systems came back negative. Physical exam reveals flat purple papules and plaques on their wrists and shins as well as white plaques with lacy patterns in the oral mucosa.

A 40-year-old patient presents with a recurrent skin eruption on their nose and cheeks for 2 years. These lesions appear usually in the summer following excessive sun exposure, and disappear without scarring. They have complaints about arthritis and chronic fatigue. They deny muscle weakness. Physical exam reveals eroded butterfly-shaped erythematous plaques over the malar area, non-scarring alopecia and oral ulcers.

A 22-year-old patient presents with a follicular eruption that has been present for 2 weeks. They have a history of anorexia nervosa and alcoholism. There is no identifiable preceding incident related to the eruption. They deny a history of atopy, drug use, and new medications. A review of systems shows positive findings for joint pain and bleeding gums. Physical exam reveals ecchymosis and purpuric follicular papules with corkscrew-like hair on their legs and arms.

A 5-year-old patient presents with a plaque on their left leg. The lesion appeared a few months after birth. It has been increasing in size proportionally to their growth. The parents mention that the skin lesion sometimes becomes irritated, erythematous and itchy when the patient plays with it or when they get sick. Physical exam reveals a red-brown well delimited plaque on their left leg without any noticeable erythema or epidermal changes.

A 12-year-old patient presents to clinic with concerns for new red bumps developing on the chest, arms, and legs over the past few months. The patient states the lesions begin as small bumps that slowly grow in size and persist. They deny any pain, itch, or symptoms associated with the lesions. They have not tried any treatment and deny any recent travel. The patient's parent states the patient also has a few light brown patches on the body, and some of their other family members had similar spots. The patient is currently receiving extra classes for learning disability, and recently was evaluated by orthopaedics for spinal irregularities. On physical examination, multiple skin-colored papules that are able to be pushed in with a finger are spread across the chest, arms, and bilateral lower extremities. Seven light tan-brown ovoid uniform patches are scattered throughout the trunk and legs. The bilateral axilla are noted to have a few scattered ovoid tan-brown macules.

A 34-year-old patient presents to clinic complaining of a painful, red spot on the left shoulder that developed about 4 years ago. They deny any trauma that may have incited it. It has been evaluated by multiple dermatologists and treated with intralesional corticosteroid injections, but it continues to enlargen and has become more raised. Physical examination reveals a multilobular violaceous, poorly demarcated firm plaque that is tender to palpation on the left shoulder. Histopathologic analysis of the lesion reveals lesional cells that stain positive for CD34 and negative for Factor 13a.

A 45-year-old patient with a past medical history of knee pain and hypertension complains of dark spots on the lower lip and hands that develop whenever they take certain oral medications. They state the rash has been ongoing for several years, and usually begins as a pink spot with a darker brown-black center. They deny any bleeding or ulceration at the site. Current medications include naproxen, multivitamins, and metoprolol. Physical examination reveals a well-demarcated red-purple patch with a darker red-violaceous center on the dorsal hands and lower lip. The patch is non-painful.

A 67-year-old patient presents complaining of a growing mole on the right side of their cheek. They state the mole was present for several years, but then started growing rapidly on one side a few weeks ago. Sometimes the mole will bleed on its own. They try to avoid picking at the area. Physical examination shows tan-brown ovoid irregularly shaped hyperpigmented macule with focal ulceration. Dermoscopy demonstrates a blue-gray veil in the center of the lesion.

A 13-year-old patient presents to the dermatology clinic with a light patch over both elbow creases that their parent noticed a few months ago. The spots have been growing in size. The patient denies any pain at the site, and thinks they may have scraped their arms that caused the light patch. Physical examination reveals well demarcated depigmented irregularly shaped patches on the bilateral antecubital fossas.

A 45-year-old patient with a past medical history of hypertension presents with concerns of a rash on their left thigh back that their partner noticed two days ago. The rash has been progressively enlargened. Patient denies any pain or any prior treatments. They think the surrounding skin is warm and may be infected, but they deny any drainage. They report that they went hiking eight days ago in Rhode Island. Physical exam demonstrates a non-scaly large targetoid, pink-red patch on the left thigh

A 54-year-old patient is hospitalized for a left lower leg cellulitis and treated with ampicillin. On day 4 of hospitalization, they developed a rash on the neck, under the arms that start as small yellow bumps but rapidly spread. They deny any new lotions or creams. They deny any personal or family history of psoriasis. Physical examination reveals multiple studded monomorphic yellow pustules on erythematous bright pink bases that coalesce into plaques across the flexural neck, bilateral axilla, trunk, and skin folds.

A 66-year-old patient with a past medical history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus type 2 presents to clinic with a mildly painful, pruritic peeling skin on the chest and back that began 4 weeks ago. They deny any new medications, new topical creams or lotions, or laundry detergents. They have been applying vaseline to the spots. They also think they may have a similar spot on the scalp. They deny any similar spots in the mouth, and deny forming any blisters on the skin. Physical exam demonstrates multiple thinly eroded pink-red oval plaques on the chest, scalp, back with yellow brown corn-flake like scale. Ocular and oral mucosa are normal.

A 21-year-old patient presents to clinic with rough, firm spots on both earlobes that developed three months ago when they underwent ear piercings. They have tried over the counter hydrocortisone without any improvement. They note that they have a history of multiple similar spots that developed after they injured themselves, and multiple family members have similar spots. On physical exam, thick pink firm plaques are noted at the sites of ear piercings that extend beyond margin of the scar.

A 35-year-old patient with a past medical history of obesity and tobacco use presents to clinic with a seven month history of boils under the arms and in the groin. They report that the boils come up twice a week under the arms, and once a week in the groin. The individual boils are painful and will often drain foul odorous yellow green material. Many of the boils have been drained in the emergency room. Physical examination reveals multiple painful, tender subcutaneous nodules draining yellow-white malodorous pus in the bilateral axilla and inguinal folds. Scattered double headed comedones and sinus tracts are present.

A 45-year-old patient presents to the primary care clinic with a red, itchy rash on the eyebrows and around the nose that has been ongoing for eight months. They have tried moisturizers to the areas, but the flakiness returns a few days later. They also report they have dandruff on their scalp. They deny any new facial products or using any other creams or lotions. Physical examination reveals greasy yellow scale on poorly demarcated erythematous patches on the eyebrows and bilateral nasal alar creases. Mild white scale is appreciated diffusely across the scalp.

A 24-year-old obese patient presents to the dermatology clinic with darkening, rough skin around the neck for six months. The rash is not painful or itchy. They have tried to clean the area with over the counter shampoo and rubbing alcohol without improvement. They deny any rash elsewhere on the body. The rash always begins as dark patches, and they deny any blistering or redness before the dark spots develop. Physical examination reveals thick, velvety ropey hyperpigmented rough, poorly demarcated plaques circumferentially around the neck.

A 65-year-old African American patient presents to dermatology clinic for multiple non-painful, non-itchy brown spots on the face. They note they started developing when they were 42 years old, and they have increased in number and size. Sometimes they try to remove them with a needle, but they will bleed. Physical exam reveals multiple dark, flat topped ovoid papules, and few pedunculated brown-black papules on the bilateral zygomatic cheeks.

A 5-year-old patient presents to the pediatrician office with complaints of multiple spots that began on the abdomen and spread to the arms and legs. The spots are not itchy or painful, unless they scratch them. Sometimes the skin surrounding the lesion will become very red and painful, but then the lesion and redness fade. The parents report they have tried topical corticosteroids but the lesions do not go away. The parent endorses a history of atopic dermatitis in their family. Physical exam reveals multiple dome-shaped skin-colored to light pink papules with central umbilication and yellow core across the chest, abdomen, and back.

A 65-year-old patient presents to the dermatology clinic for evaluation of eyelid redness and neck rash ongoing for four months that began after they started a new body lotion. They report increasing fatigue when climbing stairs and lifting heavy items over their head. They have not tried any topical treatments. They deny any recent medication changes, fevers, chills, or recent travel. Physical examination reveals poorly demarcated patchy pink erythema affecting the periocular areas with a bright pink poorly demarcated patch diffusely across the upper back and shoulders in the shape of a V. The bilateral dorsal hands reveal thin pink rough plaques on the knuckle joints.

A 53-year-old patient with a past medical history of multiple myeloma presents to dermatology clinic with multiple yellow, irritated spots under the eyes. They report the lesions developed about four months ago, beginning as a red spot that will enlargen, bleed, and then may scab over with yellow material. They deny any new facial creams, topical treatments, or new medications. They do not have any new dogs or cats. Physical examination is remarkable for hepatosplenomegaly and periocular bilaterally are yellow-pink multilobular papules and plaques.

A 34-year-old patient presents with complaints of a severely itchy rash affecting both lower legs that developed three days ago after returning from camping six days ago. They report during the camping trip they often hiked for several hours a day, and they wore shorts due to the humid, hot weather. When the rash began, it began as small red bumps that formed larger fluid-filled bumps. They have tried over-the-counter cortisone that helps with the itch a little bit. They deny any new topical lotions, laundry detergents, or body washes. Physical exam reveals multiple streaks of yellow vesicles on bright pink erythematous bases in a linear distribution on the bilateral lower extremities.

A 75-year-old patient presents with a few day history of blisters developing on their arms and legs. They deny any exposures to poison ivy, any recent travel, and any recent medication changes. Physical examination demonstrates thin urticarial pink plaques on the abdomen and multiple tense bullae without significant underlying erythema scattered on the arms and legs.

A 2-year-old patient with a past medical history of cleft palate presents to clinic with growths on the face. The patient's parent reports the growths were noticed at birth, then slowly grew in size over time before stopping. The patient is meeting all developmental milestones otherwise. Examination reveals a skin-colored papule immediately in the bilateral pre-auricular areas.

A 23-year-old patient presents to urgent clinic with complaints of sunburn. The patient endorses a history of traveling to the beach a week ago and did not apply any sunblock. They endorse fevers, but review of systems is otherwise negative. They noticed a facial rash a few days ago that feels warm to touch on the face. Family history is remarkable for a similar rash in their parent. They do not take any medications. Physical examination of the face reveals bright pink thin plaques on the bilateral cheeks extending onto the nasal bridge but sparing the nasolabial folds bilaterally.

A 16-year-old patient with past medical history of severe nodulocystic acne presents to the emergency room with increasing painful cysts on the trunk after recently starting oral isotretinoin in the past 3 weeks. The patient endorses fevers, chills, joint pain particularly along the chest. Examination reveals multiple inflammatory papules and large cystic nodules with hemorrhagic crust on the chest, shoulders, and back. The sternum is tender to palpation.

A 71-year-old patient with a past medical history of poorly controlled diabetes and heart transplant is noted to have fevers and a black eschar on the nose on day 41 of hospitalization in the ICU. The patient is intubated and unable to provide history. Nurses report the area was first noticed to be darker and then rapidly expanded. Review of current medications include cyclosporine, tacrolimus, insulin, and broad spectrum antibiotics. Physical examination reveals an extensive dark black, necrotic eschar on the nasal bridge and left nasal sidewall, cheek, and lip with surrounding pink erythema. Oral examination reveals black eschars on the upper palate.

A 5-year-old patient with a past medical history of well-controlled eczema presents with light colored patches on the face and forearms noticed by the patient's parents a few days ago. Parents deny any trauma to the sites or any new topical products. The patient denies any pruritus or pain at the affected areas. Examination of the face reveals poorly demarcated ovoid hypopigmented patches on the cheeks and forearms.

A 34-year-old Asian patient presents with multiple spots under the eyes growing over the past several years. They deny any associated pain or pruritus. The growths have remained stable in size. They do not take any medications. Examination is remarkable for multiple flat topped thin skin colored papules under the eyes bilaterally.

A 32-year-old patient with past medical history of poorly controlled HIV presents to clinic with dark spots on the skin and in the mouth. They cannot recall when they first started. They deny any drug or alcohol use. They are not currently taking their antiretroviral therapy. Examination reveals multiple ovoid violaceous ruddy, brown ovoid macules on the trunk, legs, oral palate and plantar feet. A punch biopsy is performed and stains for HHV-8 is positive.

A 1-year-old patient presents with intermittent history of itchy spots on the palms and soles that flare and then resolve over the past 6 months. The parent is unable to identify any clear inciting trigger. They have tried over the counter hydrocortisone but lesions remain. An in office mineral oil preparation is negative for any microorganisms. Physical examination reveals vesiculopustules over the palms, soles, and ankles.

A 14-year-old patient with history of leukemia treated with chemotherapy underwent hematopoietic stem cell transplant and on day 30 post therapy was noted to have a rash on the trunk that rapidly spread to the hands, feet, ears. The patient was also reported to have fevers, chills, diarrhea and new transaminitis. Examination remarkable for acral erythema and scattered pink erythematous macules and poorly demarcated papules on the trunk, extremities with prominent follicular erythema. I also changed "Patient was" to "The patient was" to maintain subject-verb agreement and clarity. No other changes were made to the original text.

A 21-year-old patient presents to the urgent care clinic after returning from the beach seven days ago. About three days ago, they noticed a red worm-like rash on the bottom of their left foot that has been progressively moving. They report walking barefoot on the beach. Examination reveals a serpiginous red-yellow plaque extending from left plantar forefoot to the medial aspect of dorsal foot.

A 65-year-old patient with past medical history of poorly controlled HIV with last known CD4 count less than 200 presents with multiple tender red spots on the tongue, arms, chest, and lips. They report they recently rescued two cats. They deny any drug or alcohol use. Examination reveals axillary lymphadenopathy and multiple friable, dome-shaped papules and nodules on the tongue, mucosal lip, arms, and chest.

A 65-year-old patient with a past medical history of multiple non-melanoma skin cancers presents with a 4 week history of a dry, painful lower lip. They have tried vaseline but their lips always feel dry and sometimes are painful. They deny licking their lips frequently or any other topicals. Examination reveals atrophy of the lower vermillion border with hypopigmentation, thin scaling and scattered erythema and thin erosions with crust on the lower mucosal lip.

A 14-year-old patient with no pertinent past medical history presents with a painless growing black spot on their left hand and arm. They state they think it may have occurred after working with farm animals, including pigs, sheep, and cattle, on their parents' farm. Their parents state it began as a yellow pus spot that slowly enlarged and popped with yellow fluid exiting. Review of symptoms is remarkable for new shortness of breath and otherwise negative. Examination revealed an edematous pink-brown violaceous plaque with central necrotic eschars and surrounding erythema on the left hand and arm. Punch biopsy is performed and demonstrates gram-positive spore-forming rods.

A 6-year-old patient presents to clinic with a 2-month history of worsening itchy rash on the arms and legs that the patient constantly scratches at throughout the day. The parent reports a history of eczema and asthma. The parents deny any recent new exposures to topical products, changes in detergent. They have tried over-the-counter hydrocortisone without improvement. Examination reveals poorly demarcated lichenified plaques along the antecubital fossas and popliteal fossas bilaterally with overlying excoriations.

A 45-year-old patient with no significant past medical history presents to dermatology clinic for evaluation of a rash developing on the chest, arms, back and thickened skin on the palms and soles ongoing for the past 3 months. They deny any recent travel or starting any new topical products. They deny any similar rash developing in the past. They have tried to take over the counter anti-histamines and hydrocortisone without any improvement. Review of systems is negative for joint pain or any other systemic symptoms. Examination reveals multiple bright pink-orange follicular papules coalescing into orange-red plaques with minimal scale on the chest, back, upper and lower extremities with few interspersed uninvolved areas. On the palms and soles are thickened hyperkeratotic red-orange plaques.

A 65-year-old patient presents to dermatology clinic for evaluation of multiple spots on the face present since adolescence but increasing in number. Their past medical history is remarkable for multiple pulmonary cysts, spontaneous pneumothorax and renal cell carcinoma. They report a positive family history of multiple renal cysts and recurrent pneumothorax. Physical examination reveals multiple light hypopigmented to skin colored dome shaped papules on the face and pedunculated hyperpigmented papules on the neck and axilla.

A 8-year-old patient with no significant past medical history presents to the emergency room with fever, headache, malaise and rhinorrhea ongoing for past two days with recent known tick exposure. Parents deny any recent medication exposures. They are admitted to the hospital and over the next few days, they develop a rash beginning on the ankles and wrists that progressively spread onto the trunk. Physical examination reveals blanching erythematous macules on ankles, wrists, and trunk with few scattered petechiae and purpura on the bilateral ankles. They are mildly febrile and labs do not demonstrate any leukocytosis.

A 14-year-old patient presenting to dermatology clinic with rosy cheeks and a history of easy sunburns and frequent respiratory infections. Physical examination demonstrates a prominent nose and ears, telangiectatic erythema in a malar distribution, and faint hypopigmentation on the cheeks. Genetic testing is performed and reveals a BLM/RECQL3 mutation.

A 50-year-old patient with no pertinent medical history presents with a two year history of dark spots on the face. They noticed the dark spots when applying make up one day. They deny any pruritus, pain, trauma or use of any new topical skin products. The dark spots have increased in number and may have slightly grown in size. They have not tried any treatments. Physical examination reveals brown irregular patchy poorly demarcated macules coalescing into patches on the bilateral zygomatic cheeks with some extension on lateral cheeks.

A 17-year-old patient presents with a several year history of a spot on the neck that developed acute onset pain for the past 3 days and warmth. On examination along the left lateral neck is a tender, soft skin colored nodule. Biopsy is performed and reveals stratified squamous epithelium with surrounding lymphoid tissue.

A 56-year-old patient presents with an intensely itchy patch on their right upper back for the past three years with intermittent sensations of numbness and tingling. They deny any trauma to the area. They only apply topical over the counter hydrocortisone without any relief. They deny any history of eczema and only take multivitamins on a daily basis. Examination of the right scapula reveals a poorly defined hyperpigmented ruddy brown ovoid patch without significant lichenification.

A 6-month-old patient presents to dermatology clinic with a red spot on the left forearm that was noticed a few weeks after birth. The parents note that it has become larger over the past few weeks and deny any spontaneous bleeding. The infant does not seem to be bothered by the lesion. Physical examination reveals a bright red ovoid thin plaque with telangiectasias on dermoscopy.

A 70-year-old patient with past medical history of end stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease presents to dermatology clinic complaining of a painful rash on the right leg present for several weeks and enlargening. They admit they often miss hemodialysis sessions. Examination of the right lower leg demonstrates a retiform violaceous plaque with large black eschar. A punch biopsy reveals calcification of small and medium sized vessels with thrombosis.

A 34-year-old patient presents with history of itching all over the body ongoing for the past year. They do not take any medications other than multivitamins. They deny any history of skin conditions. They have tried fexofenadine in the past which helped, but over the counter hydrocortisone only provides minimal relief. Pruritus is worse around areas of tight clothing contacting their skin that occurs within a few minutes. Skin examination reveals linear urticaria on the upper back that develop after two minutes in areas of gentle scratching with a cotton tip applicator.

A 60-year-old patient presents with an intermittently tender spot on the left ear present for six months. They deny any trauma to the area but note they often lay on the left side when sleeping at night. They deny any history of skin cancer. Examination reveals a crusted light pink papule along the left superior helix along the cartilaginous component. A biopsy is performed and reveals an ulcer with underlying dermal fibrosis with adjacent granulation tissue.

A 68-year-old patient presents to dermatology for a slowly enlarging lesion on the left upper back. They deny any personal or family history of skin cancer. The lesion has been present for several years and is slowly enlarging. Sometimes it gets irritated and itchy. They deny any pain or spontaneous bleeding. On examination of the left upper back is a flat-topped, stuck-on appearing thin brown hyperkeratotic papule with milia-like cysts on dermoscopy.

A 7-year-old patient presents for evaluation of facial rash that began three days ago. The patient's parent reports four days before the rash began, the patient had some fevers and thigh muscle aches. Parent notes many other children at the school have had a similar rash. On examination, on the bilateral cheeks are bright pink red lacy reticulated erythematous patches with sparing of the perioral and mesolabial fold with similar faint patches on the bilateral upper arms. No lesions are appreciated in oral mucosa. Patient is up to date with vaccinations.

A 2-day-old patient is noted to have a rash all over the body and distorted feet at birth. A 24 week ultrasound was remarkable for bilateral shortening of the long bones. Physical examination demonstrates light, fine yellow scales along curvilinear distribution on the chest, bilateral upper and lower extremities on background diffuse erythema. The bilateral feet are turned inward with plantar aspect almost sideways. An X-ray of the knees demonstrate focal dot-like calcifications in the epiphyses.

A 40-year-old patient presents for evaluation of spots on the face and stiff fingers. They report a several year history of blue discoloration of the fingertips when exposed to cold climates after prolonged periods of time with some intermittent numbness. Review of systems is remarkable for difficulty swallowing. Physical examination reveals firm white-yellow papules on the bilateral index fingertips, multiple telangiectasias across the face, and tightened skin around all fingers resulting in near claw-like appearance of the hands.

A 12-year-old healthy patient presents for evaluation of rash on the chest and back ongoing for the past 4 days. The parent reports that they first noticed a larger spot on the patient's right flank, then smaller similar lesions began developing all over the chest and back. They deny any history of eczema for the patient or family history. They deny any new topical products. The rash is not painful or itchy. The parent has tried topical over the counter hydrocortisone without any improvement. Physical examination is remarkable for erythematous pink thin papules and plaques with overlying fine thin scale on the back and chest. A larger thin scaly plaque is appreciated on the right flank. A KOH preparation is performed and does not reveal any fungal elements.

A 6-year-old patient with past medical history of aortic root dilation presents for evaluation of loose skin that was noticed at birth but has progressively worsened. Family members have noticed the patient's skin is saggy but thought it may be related to overeating. The patient's parent reports other family members may have similar skin. Physical examination reveals loose, sagging skin of the cheeks, neck, axilla, thighs. A punch biopsy demonstrates loss of elastic fibers. Arm span width to body height ratio is within normal limits.

A 50-year-old African American patient with past medical history of hypertension presents for evaluation of light spots on their legs that they initially noticed one year ago. The lesions are not painful or itchy, but they are concerned that they are increasing in frequency. When they first develop they do not significantly grow in size. They have not tried any treatments. Physical examination demonstrates multiple hypopigmented ovoid macules scattered on the distal shins bilaterally.

A 55-year-old patient with past medical history of medication non-compliance, non-insulin dependent diabetes, hyperlipidemia, and hypertension presents for evaluation of rash around the eyes that began six months ago. They deny applying any topical products to the area. They deny any trauma, pruritus, or pain. The rash has been stable in size since it first began. They deny any ulcerations or erosions of the rash. They have not tried any treatments. Physical examination is remarkable for well-defined, yellow waxy thin flat topped plaques on the medial upper and lower canthi. A shave biopsy is performed and reveals foamy histiocytes in dermis.

A 6-month-old patient with no past medical history presents to the emergency department for evaluation of fevers, difficulty feeding, and skin peeling. The patient's parent reports the patient developed fevers four days ago and then over the past two days developed skin peeling initially around the mouth that then spread to the underarms and groin area. They deny any recent travel, exposure to plants, or any medications. Physical examination is remarkable for periocular crusting, erythema, perioral fissuring, and skin desquamation around the neck, bilateral axilla, groin folds, and popliteal fossas with areas of mild serous crust. Gram stain from a bacterial swab of the neck does not reveal any bacteria.

A 7-month-old patient presents to the emergency department for evaluation of a rash and swelling of the hands and feet. The patient's parent reports the patient developed high fevers up to 103 Farenheit over the past six days, rough skin on the chest, back, arms and swelling in the hands and feet. The parent denies any recent travel or any medication exposures. Review of systems is positive for conjunctival injection. Physical examination is remarkable for palpable cervical lymph nodes, multiple prominent tongue papillae, diffuse background erythematous patches across the chest, back, and arms. Swelling of the hands and feet is appreciated.

A 34-year-old healthy patient presents for evaluation of a bump on their left third finger present over the past nine months. They deny any trauma to the area and first noticed it when getting a manicure. The spot began as a small bump that progressively enlargened with associated depression of the fingernail. Physical examination of the left third finger reveals a translucent nodule along the proximal nail fold with associated longitudinal depression of the nail plate.

A 43-year-old patient presents to clinic for evaluation of hair loss along the frontal scalp ongoing over the past year. They report a twenty year long history of wearing a wig daily and secure their hair in place with a tight headband underneath. They deny any significant pain or pruritus in the areas of hair loss. They have tried numerous over the counter oils and shampoos without any improvement. Physical examination reveals significant hair thinning and regression of the hairline with preservation of the hair follicles along the frontotemporal scalp. No significant perifollicular erythema is appreciated.

A 45-year-old patient with past medical history of recently diagnosed tinea pedis presents for evaluation of a mildly pruritic rash on the thigh and buttock ongoing over the past five days. They report the rash initially began as a red dot but rapidly expands in size with some white flakes in the middle. Physical examination is remarkable for multiple bright pink erythematous annular plaques with white thin collarette of scale along the inner margins. A punch biopsy is performed of an annular plaque and does not reveal any fungal hyphae.

A 6-year-old patient with a history of atopic dermatitis presents with their parent for evaluation of a rash on the right lower leg. The patient's parent reports the rash developed over the past two weeks and may be growing in size after having a few weeks of cold-like symptoms. They deny any new topical products, fragrances, or dyes. They have not tried any treatments. Physical examination is remarkable for multiple pink flat-topped scaly papules coalescing into plaques in a curvilinear distribution on the right posterior thigh and calf. Punch biopsy reveals a lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, superficial perivascular inflammation, and deeper lymphocytic perieccrine inflammation.

A 16-year-old patient with past medical history of mitral valve prolapse presents for evaluation of loose skin. Patient's parents report a several year history of stretchy skin, poor wound healing with some scars healing with thin overlying skin, and easy bruising. There is a family history of similar symptoms amongst other family members. Physical examination reveals soft, significantly extensible skin diffusely, multiple linear scars with atrophic overlying pink patches, and white-yellow papules along the bilateral inner and outer calcaneus upon standing. The patient is able to touch the tip of their nose with their tongue.

A 30-year-old patient presents for evaluation of a dark discoloration on the posterior thighs present for the past month. They deny any topical products applied to the area. They deny any pain or pruritus at the area. They have not tried any treatments. The rash has been stable in size, is constant, and is not significantly growing in size. They work a desk job and reports sitting on a seat warmer over the past several years. Physical examination reveals reticulated lacy brown patches on the posterior thighs and lower buttocks.

A 65-year-old patient with past medical history of hypertension, insulin-dependent diabetes, coronary artery disease, and a 30 year smoking history presents for evaluation of rash ongoing for the past 2 weeks. The patient reports the rash initially began on the upper back and has slowly spread in size. They deny any significant pruritus or pain associated with the rash. They deny using any new topical products. Review of systems is remarkable for twenty pound weight loss, malaise, increasing cough, and shortness of breath. Physical examination reveals symmetric, multiple polycyclic serpiginous concentric pink plaques on the upper back extending onto the lower back. No scale is appreciated.

A 61-year-old patient with past medical history of insulin-dependent diabetes, atrial fibrillation not on anticoagulation presents for evaluation of toenail discoloration. They report a several year history of yellowing and thickening of multiple toenails. They previously were getting their nails clipped at the podiatrist. They have not tried any other treatments. They are an avid swimmer at the local indoor pool. Physical examination reveals hyperkeratotic yellow-white thickening of the bilateral first, second, and third nailplates with significant subungual debris. They deny any rash elsewhere on the body or any history of skin conditions.

A 36-year-old patient with a past medical history of poorly controlled Crohn's disease presents for evaluation of a painful non-healing wound on the left lower leg. The patient endorses a pus bump developing on the left leg two months ago which they initially thought was a spider bite but eventually popped open. They were seen at urgent care a month ago and received one week course of cephalexin without any improvement. Local debridement attempts at bedside by the urgent care provider resulted in significant expansion of the ulcer. Physical examination reveals a well demarcated ovoid ulcer on the left distal shin with violaceous, rolled borders and cribriform base with yellow-red exudate.

A 3-year-old patient presents with their parent for evaluation of a rash present for two days. The parent notes the patient developed a runny nose, cough, and fever four days prior to onset of rash which began as small raised red bumps on the chest and progressively spread to arms and legs. The parent denies any medication exposures or new topical products. Physical examination reveals multiple juicy, monomorphic erythematous pink scattered papules on the arms, legs, buttock with sparing of the chest and back. The patient is up to date with vaccinations.

A 35-year-old African American patient presents for evaluation of a painless tongue growth present for the past three months. They deny biting the site or any inciting trauma. They noted it when brushing their teeth and it has slowly grown in size. Physical examination reveals a pink nodule on the right mid-tongue. An excisional biopsy is performed and reveals pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia and collections of large polygonal cells with abundant cytoplasm and small cytoplasmic inclusions in the dermis.

A 21-year-old patient presents for evaluation of a painful rash on their right index finger. They report a tingling sensation prior to the eruption of red small spots that became more yellow and pus filled. They deny any trauma or topical products applied to the area. They have a history of cold sores on the lips. Physical examination reveals multiple clustered painful, white-yellow vesicles on the right index finger on an erythematous pink base.

A 34-year-old patient with past medical history of anxiety presents for evaluation of a 4 month history of abnormal nail grooves on the bilateral thumbnails. They deny any trauma that may have incited the nail changes. They do not get their nails done and do not wear nail polish. They admit to frequently rubbing their thumbnails with their index finger when they're nervous. Physical examination demonstrates longitudinal depressions on the bilateral midline thumbnails with horizontal ridges.

A 66-year-old patient comes to the physician for a 3-month history of fatigue. They have hypertension and hyperlipidemia. They had a transient ischemic attack 3 years ago. They drink 3 beers a day, and sometimes a couple more on social occasions. They currently take aspirin, simvastatin, hydrochlorothiazide, and metoprolol. Their temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 78, respirations are 19/min, and oxygen saturation on room air is 97%. They are in no distress but show marked pallor and have multiple pinpoint, red, nonblanching spots on their extremities. On palpation, their spleen is significantly enlarged. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin of 8.0 g/dL, a leukocyte count of 80,000/mm3, and a platelet count of 34,000/mm3. A blood smear shows immature cells with large, prominent nucleoli and pink, elongated, needle-shaped cytoplasmic inclusions. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old patient comes to the emergency department for the evaluation of two episodes of red urine since this morning. They have no pain with urination. They report lower back pain and fever. Six months ago, they were diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the right knee that they manage with 1–2 tablets of ibuprofen per day. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the past 45 years. They do not drink alcohol. Their temperature is 38.5°C (101.3°F), pulse is 95/min, and blood pressure is 130/80 mm Hg. Physical examination shows faint, diffuse maculopapular rash, and bilateral flank pain. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Urinalysis shows: Blood +3 Protein +1 RBC 10–12/hpf RBC cast negative Eosinophils numerous Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old patient with AIDS comes to the physician because of a 2-day history of decreasing vision and seeing black spots in their right eye. They have no pain and the left eye is asymptomatic. They were treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago with fluconazole. They were diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago. Current medications include efavirenz, tenofovir, emtricitabine, azithromycin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, multivitamins, and a nutritional supplement. They are 170 cm (5 ft 7 in) tall and weigh 45 kg (99 lbs); BMI is 15.6 kg/m2. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 89/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. Examination shows cervical lymphadenopathy. There are multiple violaceous plaques seen over their trunk and extremities. Fundoscopic examination shows granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages. Their CD4+ T-lymphocyte count is 36/mm3. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old Asian patient comes to the physician for a routine health maintenance examination. On questioning, they have had occasional night sweats during the past 2 months. They have not had fevers or weight loss. Seven months ago, they had an acute myocardial infarction and were treated with percutaneous coronary intervention. They have hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and gastroesophageal reflux disease. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 37 years. Current medications include aspirin, atorvastatin, ramipril, metoprolol, and esomeprazole. They are 178 cm (5 ft 10 in) tall and weigh 89 kg (207 lbs); BMI is 29.7 kg/m2. Their temperature is 37.4°C (99.3°F), pulse is 84/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 145/80 mm Hg. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Cardiac examination shows an S4. There is a nontender skin lesion near the right large toenail. A photograph of the lesion is shown. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of progressive right knee pain for the past 3 months. They report that the pain is worse at night and while doing sports at school. They have not had any trauma to the knee or any previous problems with their joints. Their vital signs are within normal limits. Examination of the right knee shows mild swelling and tenderness without warmth or erythema; the range of motion is limited. They walk with an antalgic gait. Laboratory studies show an alkaline phosphatase of 180 U/L and an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 80 mm/h. An x-ray of the right knee is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old college student comes to the physician because they have been extremely sad for the past 3 weeks and have to cry constantly. Three weeks ago, their partner left them after they were together for 4 years. They have no appetite and have had a 2.3-kg (5.1-lb) weight loss. They have missed several classes because they could not stop crying or get out of bed. They think about their ex-partner all the time. They say that they experienced similar symptoms for about 2 months after previous relationships ended. The patient is 158 cm (5 ft 2 in) tall and weighs 45 kg (100 lb); BMI is 18 kg/m2. Their temperature is 36.1°C (97°F), pulse is 65/min, and blood pressure is 110/60 mm Hg. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. On mental status examination they appear sad and cry easily. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old patient comes to the physician for a follow-up visit. They have a 2-year history of depressed mood and fatigue accompanied by early morning awakening. One week ago, they started feeling a decrease in their need for sleep and now feel rested after about 5 hours of sleep per night. They had two similar episodes that occurred 6 months ago and a year ago, respectively. They report increased energy and libido. They have a 4-kg (8.8-lb) weight loss over the past month. They do not feel the need to eat and say they derive their energy "from the universe". They enjoy their work as a librarian. They started taking fluoxetine 3 months ago. On mental exam, they are alert and oriented to time and place; they are irritable. They do not have auditory or visual hallucinations. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of fever, malaise, and severe right knee joint pain and swelling for 3 days. They had also had episodes of abdominal pain and epistaxis during this period. Five days ago, they had swelling and pain in their left ankle joint which has since resolved. They reports having a sore throat 3 weeks ago while they were camping in the woods, for which they received symptomatic treatment. Their immunizations are up-to-date. Their temperature is 38.7°C (101.6°F), pulse is 119/min, and blood pressure is 90/60 mm Hg. Examination shows a swollen, tender right knee; range of motion is limited. There are painless 3- to 4-mm nodules over the elbow. Cardiopulmonary examination is normal. Their hemoglobin concentration is 12.3 g/dL, leukocyte count is 11,800/mm3, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate is 58 mm/h. Arthrocentesis of the right knee joint yields clear, straw-colored fluid; no organisms are identified on Gram stain. Analysis of the synovial fluid shows a leukocyte count of 1,350/mm3 with 17% neutrophils. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 73-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their child because of increasing forgetfulness over the past 2 years. Initially, they used to misplace keys and forget their pet's name or their phone number. Now, they often forget about what they have seen on television or read about the day before. They used to go for a walk every morning but stopped one month ago after they became lost on their way back home. Their child has prevented them from cooking because they have had episodes of leaving the gas stove oven on after making a meal. They become agitated when asked questions directly but are unconcerned when their child reports their history and says they are overprotective of them. They have hypertension, coronary artery disease, and hypercholesterolemia. Current medications include aspirin, enalapril, carvedilol, and atorvastatin. They are alert and oriented to place and person but not to time. Vital signs are within normal limits. Short- and long-term memory deficits are present. Their speech rhythm is normal but is frequently interrupted as they think of words to frame their sentences. They make multiple errors while performing serial sevens. Their clock drawing is impaired and they draw 14 numbers. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 75-year-old patient comes to the physician for the evaluation of progressive shortness of breath and fatigue over the past month. They report that they cannot climb more than one flight of stairs without experiencing shortness of breath and dizziness. They have hypertension and hyperlipidemia. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the past 50 years. They do not drink alcohol. Their medications include enalapril, atorvastatin, and low-dose aspirin. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 70/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 100/80 mm Hg. Physical examination shows weak peripheral pulses. Cardiac examination is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort. Their discomfort is relieved by voiding. They void 10–15 times per day and wake up 2–3 times per night to void. They have not had any involuntary loss of urine. They have tried cutting down on fluids and taking NSAIDs to reduce the discomfort with minimal relief. Their past medical history is significant for bipolar disorder. They are sexually active with their partner but reports that intercourse has recently become painful. Current medications include lithium. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 65/min, and blood pressure is 110/80 mm Hg. Examination shows tenderness to palpation of the suprapubic region. Urinalysis shows: Color clear pH 6.7 Specific gravity 1.010 Protein 1+ Glucose negative Ketones negative Blood negative Nitrite negative Leukocyte esterase negative WBC 0/hpf Squamous epithelial cells 2/hpf Bacteria None A pelvic ultrasound shows a postvoid residual urine is 25 mL. A cystoscopy shows a normal urethra and normal bladder mucosa. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient comes to the emergency department because of a 24-hour history of severe lower abdominal pain. They have had two episodes of nonbloody vomiting today and have been unable to keep down food or fluids. They have not had a bowel movement since the day before. They have hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis. They had a cholecystectomy 5 years ago. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the last 20 years. Current medications include chlorthalidone, atorvastatin, and naproxen. Their temperature is 38.8°C (101.8­°F), pulse is 102/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 118/78 mm Hg. They are 1.68 m (5 ft 6 in) tall and weigh 94.3 kg (207.9 lbs); BMI is 33.4 kg/m2. Abdominal examination shows a soft abdomen with hypoactive bowel sounds. There is moderate left lower quadrant tenderness. A tender mass is palpable on digital rectal examination. There is no guarding or rebound tenderness. Laboratory studies show: Leukocyte count 17,000/mm3 Hemoglobin 13.3 g/dl Hematocrit 40% Platelet count 188,000/mm3 Serum Na+ 138 mEq/L K+ 4.1 mEq/L Cl- 101 mEq/L HCO3- 22 mEq/L Urea Nitrogen 18.1 mg/dl Creatinine 1.1 mg/dl Which of the following is most appropriate to confirm the diagnosis?

A 47-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 3-week history of generalized fatigue, mild fever, abdominal pain, and nausea. They attended the state fair over a month ago, where they tried a number of regional foods, and wonders if it might have been caused by something they ate. They have also noticed darkening of their urine, which they attribute to not drinking enough water recently. They have type 2 diabetes mellitus. They drink 1–2 beers daily. They work as a nursing assistant in a rehabilitation facility. Current medications include glyburide, sitagliptin, and a multivitamin. They appear tired. Their temperature is 38.1°C (100.6°F), pulse is 99/min, and blood pressure is 110/74 mm Hg. Examination shows mild scleral icterus. The liver is palpated 2–3 cm below the right costal margin and is tender. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 10.6 g/dL Leukocyte count 11600/mm3 Platelet count 221,000/mm3 Serum Urea nitrogen 26 mg/dL Glucose 122 mg/dL Creatinine 1.3 mg/dL Bilirubin 3.6 mg/dL Total 3.6 mg/dL Direct 2.4 mg/dL Alkaline phosphatase 72 U/L AST 488 U/L ALT 798 U/L Hepatitis A IgG antibody (HAV-IgG) positive Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) positive Hepatitis B core IgG antibody (anti-HBc) positive Hepatitis B envelope antigen (HBeAg) positive Hepatitis C antibody (anti-HCV) negative Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of increasing swelling of their legs and generalized fatigue for 1 month. During this period they have also had a productive cough and shortness of breath. They have been unable to carry out their daily activities. They have a history of recurrent respiratory tract infections and chronic nasal congestion since childhood. They have a 3-month history of foul-smelling and greasy stools. They are at 4th percentile for height and weight. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 112/min, respirations are 23/min, and blood pressure is 104/64 mm Hg. Examination shows clubbing of their fingers and scoliosis. There is 2+ pitting edema of the lower extremities. Jugular venous distention is present. Inspiratory crackles are heard in the thorax. Cardiac examination shows a loud S2. The abdomen is mildly distended and the liver is palpated 2 cm below the right costal margin. Hepato-jugular reflux is present. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 64-year-old patient comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. They have had difficulty reading for the past 6 months. They tried using multiple over-the-counter glasses with different strengths, but they have not helped. They have hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Current medications include insulin and enalapril. Their temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 80/min, and blood pressure is 126/84 mm Hg. The pupils are round and react sluggishly to light. Visual acuity in the left eye is 6/60 and in the right eye counting fingers at 6 feet. Fundoscopy shows pallor of the optic disc bilaterally. The cup-to-disk ratio is 0.7 in the left eye and 0.9 in the right eye (N = 0.3). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old patient comes to the physician 3 months after noticing skin changes on their scalp. When they scrape off the crust of the lesion, it reappears after a few days. Occasionally, their scalp itches or they notice a burning sensation. They had a mole removed on their right forearm 5 years ago. They are a retired winemaker. Their vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows multiple rough patches on their scalp. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient comes to the physician for a routine health maintenance examination. They feel well. They underwent appendectomy at the age of 25 years. They have a history of hypercholesterolemia that is well controlled with atorvastatin. They are an avid marathon runner and run 8 miles per day four times a week. Their father died of myocardial infarction at the age of 42 years. The patient does not smoke or drink alcohol. Their vital signs are within normal limits. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. Their abdomen is soft and nontender with a surgical scar in the right lower quadrant. Laboratory studies are within normal limits. An ECG is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their child because of gradually progressive yellow discoloration of their skin and generalized pruritus for the past 2 weeks. During this period, their appetite has decreased and they have had a 6.3-kg (14-lb) weight loss. They report that their stool appears pale and their urine is very dark. Three years ago, they had an episode of acute upper abdominal pain that was treated with IV fluids, NSAIDs, and dietary modification. They have stopped drinking alcohol since then; they used to drink 1–2 beers daily for 40 years. They have smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for the past 50 years. Their vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows yellowing of the conjunctivae and skin. The abdomen is soft and nontender; a soft, cystic mass is palpated in the right upper quadrant. Serum studies show: Bilirubin, total 5.6 mg/dL Direct 4.8 mg/dL Alkaline phosphatase 192 U/L AST 32 U/L ALT 34 U/L Abdominal ultrasonography shows an anechoic cystic mass in the subhepatic region and dilation of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 6-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of a 3-day history of progressive rash. The rash started on their face and now involves the entire body. For the past week, they have had a cough and a runny nose. They are visiting from the Philippines with their family. They are in first grade and spend their afternoons at an after-school child care program. Immunization records are not available. Their temperature is 39.5°C (103°F), pulse is 115/min, and blood pressure is 105/66 mm Hg. Examination shows generalized lymphadenopathy. There is an erythematous maculopapular, blanching, and partially confluent exanthem on their entire body. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 43-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of chest pain. They describe the pain as intermittent and burning-like. They state that they have tried using proton pump inhibitors but have had no relief of their symptoms. They have had a 5-kg (11-lb) weight loss over the past 2 months. Their temperature is 36.7°C (98.1°F), pulse is 75/min, and blood pressure is 150/80 mm Hg. Examination shows tightness of the skin of the fingers; there are small nonhealing, nonpurulent ulcers over thickened skin on the fingertips. Fine inspiratory crackles are heard at both lung bases. There is mild tenderness to palpation of the epigastrium. Which of the following is most likely associated with their diagnosis?

A 28-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department with shortness of breath and chest pain, 35 minutes after they were involved in a high-speed motor vehicle collision. They were the helmeted driver of a scooter hit by a truck. On arrival, they are alert and oriented with a Glasgow Coma Scale rating of 14. Their temperature is 37.3°C (99.1°F), pulse is 103/min, respirations are 33/min and blood pressure is 132/88 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 94%. Examination shows multiple abrasions over their abdomen and extremities. There is a 2.5-cm (1-in) laceration on the left side of the chest. There are decreased breath sounds over the left base. Cardiac examination shows no abnormalities. The abdomen is soft and there is tenderness to palpation over the left upper quadrant. Bowel sounds are normal. Their hemoglobin concentration is 13.6 g/dL, leukocyte count is 9,110/mm3, and platelet count is 190,000/mm3. A chest x-ray is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 54-year-old patient comes to the physician because of diarrhea that has become progressively worse over the past 4 months. They currently have 4–6 episodes of foul-smelling stools per day. Over the past 3 months, they have had fatigue and a 5-kg (11-lb) weight loss. They returned from Bangladesh 6 months ago after a year-long business assignment. They have osteoarthritis and hypertension. Current medications include amlodipine and naproxen. They appear pale and malnourished. Their temperature is 37.3°C (99.1°F), pulse is 76/min, and blood pressure is 140/86 mm Hg. Examination shows pale conjunctivae and dry mucous membranes. Angular stomatitis and glossitis are present. The abdomen is distended but soft and nontender. Rectal examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 8.9 g/dL Leukocyte count 4100/mm3 Platelet count 160,000/mm3 Mean corpuscular volume 110 μm3 Serum Na+ 133 mEq/L Cl- 98 mEq/l K+ 3.3 mEq/L Creatinine 1.1 mg/dL IgA 250 mg/dL Anti-tissue transglutaminase, IgA negative Stool culture and studies for ova and parasites are negative. Test of the stool for occult blood is negative. Fecal fat content is 22 g/day (N < 7). Fecal lactoferrin is negative and elastase is within normal limits. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 68-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their spouse for the evaluation of confusion and memory deficits for the last month. During this period, they have also had mild weakness in their left leg. They have hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Their current medications include enalapril and atorvastatin. They have smoked two packs of cigarettes daily for the last 45 years. They drink a glass of wine every day. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 75/min, and blood pressure is 135/85 mm Hg. They are oriented only to person. They recall 2 out of 3 objects immediately and none after 5 minutes. The patient is unable to lift their eyebrows or to smile. Muscle strength is decreased in the left lower extremity. A T2-weighted MRI scan of the head shows several hyperintense round lesions in the frontal and temporal lobe at the border of the gray and white matter. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 9-year-old patient is brought to the physician for a well-child examination. Their parent says their teachers report them being easily distracted, lagging behind their classmates in most of the subjects, and frequently falling asleep during class. They say that the patient has complained of leg pain on multiple occasions. The patient is at the 45th percentile for height and 35th percentile for weight. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows ptosis and a high-arched palate. Muscle strength is decreased in the face and hands. Muscle strength of the quadriceps and hamstrings is normal. Sensation is intact. Percussion of the thenar eminence causes the thumb to abduct and then relax slowly. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department 15 minutes after falling 7 feet onto a flat-top wooden post. On arrival, they are in severe pain and breathing rapidly. Their pulse is 135/min, respirations are 30/min, and blood pressure is 80/40 mm Hg. There is an impact wound in the left fourth intercostal space at the midaxillary line. Auscultation shows tracheal deviation to the right and absent breath sounds over the left lung. There is dullness to percussion over the left chest. Neck veins are flat. Cardiac examination shows no abnormalities. Two large-bore intravenous catheters are placed and intravenous fluid resuscitation is begun. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of chest pain, dry cough, and shortness of breath. They describe two painless masses in their neck, which they say appeared 4 months ago and are progressively increasing in size. During this time, they have had week-long episodes of fever interspersed with 10-day periods of being afebrile. They report that their clothes have become looser over the past few months. They drink alcohol occasionally. Their temperature is 38°C (100.4°F), pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 105/60 mm Hg. Physical examination shows two nontender, fixed cervical lymph nodes on either side of the neck, which are approximately 2.2 cm and 4.5 cm in size. The tip of the spleen is palpated 3 cm below the left costal margin. An x-ray of the chest shows discrete widening of the superior mediastinum. Which of the following is most appropriate to confirm the diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient comes to the physician for a routine health maintenance examination. They feel well. They have type 2 diabetes mellitus. There is no family history of serious illness. They work as an engineer at a local company. They do not smoke. They drink one glass of red wine every other day. They do not use illicit drugs. Their only medication is metformin. They are 180 cm (5 ft 11 in) tall and weigh 100 kg (220 lb); BMI is 31 kg/m2. Their vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows a soft, nontender abdomen. The liver is palpated 2 to 3 cm below the right costal margin. Laboratory studies show an aspartate aminotransferase concentration of 100 U/L and an alanine aminotransferase concentration of 130 U/L. Liver biopsy shows hepatocyte ballooning degeneration, as well as inflammatory infiltrates with scattered lymphocytes, neutrophils, and Kupffer cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of a 3-week history of generalized fatigue and easy bruising. During the past week, they have also had fever and severe leg pain that wakes them up at night. Their temperature is 38.3°C (100.9°F), pulse is 120/min, and respirations are 30/min. Examination shows cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy. The abdomen is soft and nontender; the liver is palpated 3 cm below the right costal margin, and the spleen is palpated 2 cm below the left costal margin. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL Leukocyte count 63,000/mm3 Platelet count 27,000/mm3 A bone marrow aspirate predominantly shows immature cells that stain positive for CD10, CD19, and TdT. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 36-year-old patient with HIV comes to the physician because of a 3-day history of pain and watery discharge in their left eye. They also have blurry vision and noticed that they are more sensitive to light. Their right eye is asymptomatic. They had an episode of shingles 7 years ago. They were diagnosed with HIV 5 years ago. They admit that they take their medication inconsistently. They wear contact lenses. Current medications include abacavir, lamivudine, efavirenz, and a nutritional supplement. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 89/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. Examination shows conjunctival injection of the left eye. Visual acuity is 20/20 in the right eye and 20/80 in the left eye. Extraocular movements are normal. Their CD4+ T-lymphocyte count is 90/mm3. A photograph of the left eye after fluorescein administration is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department with fatigue, dry cough, and shortness of breath for 3 days. They report a slight fever and have also had 3 episodes of watery diarrhea earlier that morning. Last week, they attended a business meeting at a hotel and notes some of their coworkers have also become sick. They have a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. They take atorvastatin, hydrochlorothiazide, and lisinopril. They appear in mild distress. Their temperature is 102.1°F (38.9°C), pulse is 56/min, respirations are 16/min, and blood pressure is 150/85 mm Hg. Diffuse crackles are heard in the thorax. Examination shows a soft and nontender abdomen. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 13.5 g/dL Leukocyte count 15,000/mm3 Platelet count 130,000/mm3 Serum Na+ 129 mEq/L Cl- 100 mEq/L K+ 4.6 mEq/L HCO3- 22 mEq/L Urea nitrogen 14 mg/dL Creatinine 1.3 mg/dL An x-ray of the chest shows infiltrates in both lungs. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 5-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of early morning headaches for the past 6 months. During this period, they have had severe nausea and occasional episodes of vomiting. For the past month, they have had difficulty walking and intermittent double vision. They were born at term and have been healthy apart from an episode of sinusitis 8 months ago that resolved spontaneously. They are at the 60th percentile for height and 50th percentile for weight. Their temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 80/min, and blood pressure is 105/64 mm Hg. Examination shows normal muscle strength and 2+ deep tendon reflexes bilaterally. They have a broad-based gait and impaired tandem gait. Fundoscopy shows bilateral swelling of the optic disc. There is esotropia of the left eye. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 1-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of fever and crying while passing urine for 2 days. They were born at term and have been healthy since. Three months ago, they were treated for a urinary tract infection with oral cefixime. Their temperature is 39°C (102.2°F), pulse is 144/min, and blood pressure is 85/40 mm Hg. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Their leukocyte count is 14,000/mm3. Urine dipstick shows leukocyte esterase and nitrites; urinalysis shows WBCs and gram-negative rods. Urine culture results are pending. Renal ultrasonography shows hydronephrosis of the left kidney. Empirical antimicrobial therapy is initiated, following which the patient's symptoms improve. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 53-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of intermittent severe left neck, shoulder, and arm pain and paresthesias of the left hand. The pain radiates to the radial aspect of their left forearm, thumb, and index finger. They first noticed their symptoms after helping a friend set up a canopy tent. There is no family history of serious illness. They appear healthy. Vital signs are within normal limits. When the patient extends and rotates their head to the left and downward pressure is applied, they report paresthesias along the radial aspect of their left forearm and thumb. There is weakness when extending the left wrist against resistance. The brachioradialis reflex is 1+ on the left and 2+ on the right. The radial pulse is palpable bilaterally. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their spouse because of a 1-year history of abnormal behavior. During this time they have been irritable, restless, and have had multiple episodes of hearing voices. Over the past month, they have also had difficulty swallowing. They have a 2-year history of depression. They were let go by their employer 6 months ago because they could no longer handle all their tasks and often forgot about assignments. Their parent committed suicide at the age of 50. The patient has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily over the past 20 years. They have a history of smoking cocaine for 8 years but stopped 1 year ago. Vital signs are within normal limits. On mental status examination, they are confused and oriented to person and place only. Neurologic examination shows a delayed return to neutral ankle position after triggering the plantar reflex. Physical examination shows irregular, nonrepetitive, and arrhythmic movements of the neck and head. The patient has poor articulation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 36-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 12-month history of upper abdominal pain. The pain is worse after eating, which they report as 7 out of 10 in intensity. Over the last year, they have also had nausea, heartburn, and multiple episodes of diarrhea with no blood or mucus. Eight months ago, they underwent an upper endoscopy, which showed several ulcers in the gastric antrum, the pylorus, and the duodenum, as well as thick gastric folds. The biopsies from these ulcers were negative for H. pylori. Current medications include pantoprazole and over-the-counter antacids. They appear anxious. Vital signs are within normal limits. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. The abdomen is soft and there is tenderness to palpation in the epigastric and umbilical areas. Test of the stool for occult blood is positive. A repeat upper endoscopy shows persistent gastric and duodenal ulceration with minimal bleeding. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 24-year-old patient comes to the physician because of progressively worsening joint pain. They have had diffuse, aching pain in their knees, shoulders, and hands bilaterally for the past few months, but the pain has become much more severe in the past few weeks. They also report night sweats and generalized malaise. On physical examination, radial and pedal pulses are weak. There are erythematous nodules over the legs that measure 3–5 cm. Laboratory studies show: Hematocrit 33.2% Hemoglobin 10.7 g/dL Leukocyte count 11,300/mm3 Platelet count 615,000/mm3 Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 94 mm/h Serum C-reactive protein 40 mg/dL (N=0.08–3.1) Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 1-day history of progressive pain and blurry vision of their right eye. They have difficulties opening the eye because of pain. Their left eye is asymptomatic. They wear contact lenses. They have bronchial asthma treated with inhaled salbutamol. They work as a kindergarten teacher. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 85/min, and blood pressure is 135/75 mm Hg. Examination shows a visual acuity in the left eye of 20/25 and the ability to count fingers at 3 feet in the right eye. A photograph of the right eye is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 56-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their spouse because of slurred speech and left facial droop for the past 30 minutes. During this period, they have also had numbness on the left side of their face. They have never had such an episode before. They have hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Their father died of lung cancer 1 week ago. The patient has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 30 years. They drink one glass of wine daily. Their current medications include metformin, sitagliptin, enalapril, and atorvastatin. They are 168 cm (5 ft 6 in) tall and weigh 86 kg (190 lb); BMI is 30.5 kg/m2. They are oriented to time, place, and person. Their temperature is 37°C (98.7°F), pulse is 97/min, and blood pressure is 140/90 mm Hg. Examination shows drooping of the left side of the face. Their speech is clear. Examination shows full muscle strength. Deep tendon reflexes are 2+ bilaterally. A finger-nose test and their gait are normal.
