Cardiopulmonary examination shows a right-sided carotid bruit. A complete blood count and serum concentrations of creatinine, glucose, and electrolytes are within the reference ranges. An ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy. A noncontrast CT scan of the brain shows no abnormalities. On the way back from the CT scan, their presenting symptoms resolve. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their spouse for forgetfulness, confusion, and mood changes for the past 4 months. Their symptoms started with misplacing items such as their wallet and keys around the house. Two months ago, they became unable to manage their finances as it became too difficult for them. Last week, they became lost while returning home from the grocery store. Their spouse reports that they show “no emotion” and that they are seemingly not concerned by their recent symptoms. They have hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and coronary artery disease. Current medications include aspirin, metoprolol, lisinopril, metformin, and rosuvastatin. Their pulse is 56/min and blood pressure is 158/76 mm Hg. Neurologic examination shows loss of sensation on their right leg and an unsteady gait. When asked to stand with their eyes closed and palms facing upward, their right arm rotates inward. An MRI of the brain shows multiple deep white matter lesions. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 9-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parent because of a 3-day history of face and foot swelling, dark urine, and a rash on their hands and feet. The parent reports that the patient has had a low-grade fever, shortness of breath, and a dry cough for the past 8 days. They have had generalized weakness and pain in their right knee and ankle. They have a ventricular septum defect that was diagnosed at birth. The patient appears lethargic. Their temperature is 38.4 (101.1°F), pulse is 130/min, respirations are 34/min, and blood pressure is 110/60 mm Hg. Examination shows small, non-blanching, purple lesions on their palms, soles, and under their fingernails. There is edema of the eyelids and feet. Funduscopic examination shows retinal hemorrhages. Holosystolic and early diastolic murmurs are heard. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 11.3 g/dL Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 61 mm/h Leukocyte count 15,000/mm3 Platelet count 326,000/mm3 Urine Blood 4+ Glucose negative Protein 1+ Ketones negative Transthoracic echocardiography shows a small outlet ventricular septum defect and a mild right ventricular enlargement. There are no wall motion abnormalities, valvular heart disease, or deficits in the pump function of the heart. Blood cultures grow Streptococcus pyogenes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 58-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 2-year history of progressively worsening pain in their knees and fingers. The knee pain is worse when they walk for longer than 30 minutes. When they wake up in the morning, their fingers and knees are stiff for about 15 minutes. They cannot recall any trauma to the joints. They were treated with amoxicillin following a tick bite 2 years ago. They are otherwise healthy and only take a multivitamin and occasionally acetaminophen for the pain. They drink 1–2 glasses of wine daily. They are 160 cm (5 ft 3 in) tall and weigh 79 kg (174 lb); BMI is 31 kg/m2. Their temperature is 36.9°C (98.4°F), pulse is 70/min, and blood pressure is 133/78 mm Hg. Examination of the lower extremities reveals mild genu varum. Range of motion of both knees is limited; there is palpable crepitus. Complete flexion and extension elicit pain. Tender nodules are present on the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints of the index, ring, and little fingers bilaterally. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 49-year-old patient comes to the physician because of tender, red nodules that appeared on their chest 3 days ago. Three weeks ago, they had similar symptoms in their right lower limb and another episode in their left foot; both episodes resolved spontaneously. They also have diarrhea and have had a poor appetite for 1 month. They have a history of dry cough and joint pain, for which they take albuterol and aspirin as needed. They have smoked 2 packs of cigarettes daily for 15 years. They do not drink alcohol. Physical examination shows a linear, erythematous lesion on the right anterior chest wall, through which a cord-like structure can be palpated. The lungs are clear to auscultation. The abdomen is soft, nontender, and non-distended. Examination of the legs is normal. An ultrasound of the legs shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis of the underlying condition?

A 35-year-old patient comes to the physician for the evaluation of increasing weakness and numbness of the upper extremities for 5 days. During the past 2 days, they have had urinary incontinence not related to sneezing or laughing. Last summer, they had weakness and numbness of their right lower extremity that was worse when they were outside; they regained their strength 3 weeks later. They have no history of serious illness. They have had 10 sexual partners in their lifetime and use condoms inconsistently. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows an impaired tandem gait. There is mild spasticity and muscle strength is decreased in both upper extremities. Deep tendon reflexes are 4+ bilaterally. The abdominal reflex is absent. Muscle strength in the right lower extremity is mildly decreased. Sensation to vibration and fine touch is decreased over the upper extremities. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 4-year-old patient is brought to the physician in December for episodic shortness of breath and a nonproductive cough for 3 months. These episodes frequently occur before sleeping, and they occasionally wake up because of difficulty breathing. Their parent also reports that they became short of breath while playing with friends at daycare on several occasions. They are allergic to peanuts. They are at the 55th percentile for height and weight. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows mild scattered wheezing in the thorax. An x-ray of the chest shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient comes to the physician because of increasing shortness of breath and a non-productive cough for 2 months. They have been unable to perform their daily activities. They have had malaise and bilateral ankle pain during this period. They noticed their symptoms after returning from a vacation to Arizona. They are a research assistant at the university geology laboratory. They are originally from Nigeria and visit their family there twice a year; their last trip was 3 months ago. Their temperature is 37.8°C (100°F), pulse is 100/min, respirations are 24/min, and blood pressure is 112/72 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 94%. There is no palpable cervical or axillary lymphadenopathy. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Their left eye is notable for ciliary injection and photophobia. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. A complete blood count is within the reference range. An x-ray of the chest is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old patient is brought to the physician for the evaluation of recurrent skin lesions. The episodes of lesions started at the age of 2 months and multiple treatment options have been attempted without success. They have also had several episodes of respiratory tract infections, enlarged lymph nodes, and recurrent fevers since birth. The patient attends daycare. Their older sibling has asthma. The patient's immunizations are up-to-date. They are at the 5th percentile for length and 10th percentile for weight. They appear ill. Their temperature is 38°C (100.4°F), pulse is 100/min, and blood pressure is 100/60 mm Hg. Examination shows several raised, erythematous lesions of different sizes over the face, neck, groins, and extremities; some secrete pus. Cervical and axillary lymph nodes are enlarged bilaterally. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 46-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department 15 minutes after being involved in a motor vehicle collision where they were the unrestrained driver. On arrival, they are unconscious. Their respirations are 24/min, and palpable systolic blood pressure is 60 mm Hg, and pulse is 141/min and irregularly irregular. Examination shows multiple ecchymoses over the chest. There is a 3-cm (1.2-in) laceration over the abdomen and a 4-cm (1.6-in) laceration over the scalp. Jugular venous pressure is increased. Bilateral crackles are heard at the lung bases. Cardiac examination shows no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. The abdomen is soft. Two large bore intravenous catheters are inserted and 0.9% saline infusion is begun. Focused assessment with sonography in trauma (FAST) is negative. An electrocardiogram shows absent p-waves. After 5 minutes, their pulse is 160/min and palpable systolic blood pressure is 50 mm Hg. Vasopressors are administered. One hour later, the patient dies. Which of the following was the most likely diagnosis?

A 52-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department with severe epigastric discomfort and left-sided chest pain radiating to the back that began after waking up. They have also vomited several times since the pain began. They underwent an esophagogastroduodenoscopy the previous day for evaluation of epigastric pain. They have ischemic heart disease and underwent a coronary angioplasty 3 years ago. Their mother died of pancreatic cancer when she was 60 years old. Their current medications include aspirin, clopidogrel, metoprolol, ramipril, and rosuvastatin. They are pale, anxious, and diaphoretic. Their temperature is 37.9°C (100.2°F), pulse is 140/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 100/60 mm Hg in their upper extremities and 108/68 mm Hg in their lower extremities. Pulse oximetry on room air shows oxygen saturation at 98%. An S4 is audible over the precordium, in addition to crepitus over the chest. Abdominal examination shows tenderness to palpation in the epigastric area. Serum studies show an initial Troponin I level of 0.031 ng/mL (N < 0.1 ng/mL) and 0.026 ng/mL 6 hours later. A 12-lead ECG shows sinus tachycardia with nonspecific ST-T changes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 9-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parent because of multiple episodes of staring and facial grimacing that have occurred over the past 3 weeks. There are no precipitating factors for these episodes and they last for several minutes. They do not respond to their family members during these episodes. One week ago, their sibling witnessed an episode in which they woke up while sleeping, stared, and made hand gestures. They do not remember any of these episodes but do recall having a vague muddy taste in their mouth prior to the onset of these symptoms. After the episode, they feel lethargic and are confused. Physical and neurologic examinations show no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old patient comes to the physician because of stiffness and pain in multiple joints. They say that the fingers on both of their hands have become increasingly stiff and difficult to move over the past 8 months. They also complain of nails that break easily and look spotty as well as chronic back pain. They had a urinary tract infection a year ago that was treated with antibiotics. They are sexually active with 2 partners and use condoms inconsistently. Their vitals are within normal limits. A photograph of their right hand is shown. There are multiple, well-demarcated red plaques with silvery-white scales over the shins and back. Serum studies show a negative rheumatoid factor and ANA. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25 year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their partner after they cut their forearms with a knife. They have had multiple visits to the emergency department in the past few months for self-inflicted wounds. They claim that their partner is the worst person in the world. They and their partner have broken up 20 times in the past 6 months. They say they cut themselves not because they want to kill themselves; they feel alone and empty and want their partner to take care of them. Their partner claims that they are prone to outbursts of physical aggression as well as mood swings. They say that these mood swings last a few hours and vary from states of exuberance and self-confidence to states of self-doubt and melancholy. On examination, the patient appears well-dressed and calm. They have normal speech, thought processes, and thought content. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An otherwise healthy 52-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of palpitations. They say that they can feel their heart beat in their chest all the time. For the past 3 weeks, they have shortness of breath on exertion. They have not had chest pain, orthopnea, or nocturnal dyspnea. They emigrated from Nepal at the age of 25 years. They do not take any medications. Their temperature is 36.5°C (97.7°F), pulse is 103/min, and blood pressure is 138/56 mm Hg. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Cardiac examination is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of a 4-week history of generalized fatigue and malaise. They were born at term and have been healthy since. Their parent has a history of recurrent anemia. They appear pale. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F) and pulse is 97/min. Examination shows pale conjunctivae and jaundice. The abdomen is soft and nontender; the spleen is palpated 3–4 cm below the left costal margin. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 9.3 g/dL Mean corpuscular volume 81.3 μm3 Mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration 39% Hb/cell Leukocyte count 7300/mm3 Platelet count 200,000/mm3 Red cell distribution width 19% (N = 13–15) Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 23-year-old patient comes to the physician because of increasing pain and swelling of their hands and wrists for 3 days. They have been unable to continue their daily activities like writing or driving. They have had a nonpruritic generalized rash for 4 days. They had fever and a runny nose one week ago which resolved with over-the-counter medication. They are sexually active with a partner and use condoms inconsistently. They work as an attendant at an amusement park. Their temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 118/72 mm Hg. Examination shows swelling and tenderness of the wrists as well as the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints. Range of motion at the wrists is limited. A lacy macular rash is noted over the trunk and extremities. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies, including erythrocyte sedimentation rate and anti-nuclear antibody and anti-dsDNA serology, show no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 58-year-old patient comes to the physician because of burning pain in their neck and arms for a year. They have also had paresthesias in their hands during this period. They have had increasing weakness in both hands during the past 3 months. They have type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. They were involved in a motor vehicle collision 3 years ago. Current medications include metformin, sitagliptin, enalapril, atorvastatin, and aspirin. They have had 7 sexual partners in their lifetime; they use condoms inconsistently. They are oriented to time, place, and person. Vital signs are within normal limits. The pupils are equal and reactive to light. Examination of the upper extremities shows decreased muscle strength, absent reflexes, and decreased hand grip with fasciculations bilaterally. Sensation to temperature and pain is absent over the chest and bilateral upper arms. Vibration and joint position sensations are present in the upper limbs. Cranial nerve examination shows no focal findings. Examination of the lower extremities shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 66-year-old white patient comes to the physician because of a 10-day history of fatigue and lower leg swelling. Over the past 6 months, they have had a 3.6-kg (8-lb) weight loss. They have chronic bronchitis and use an albuterol inhaler as needed. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 44 years and drink one alcoholic beverage daily. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 88/min, and blood pressure is 120/75 mm Hg. They appear thin. Examination shows 2+ pretibial edema bilaterally. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL Leukocyte count 8500/mm3 Platelet count 130,000/mm3 Serum Urea nitrogen 23 mg/dL Glucose 77 mg/dL Creatinine 1.6 mg/dL Albumin 1.8 mg/dL Total cholesterol 475 mg/dL Urine Blood negative Glucose negative Protein 4+ WBC 0–1/hpf Fatty casts numerous An x-ray of the chest shows a right upper lobe density. A CT scan of the chest shows a 2.5 x 3.5 x 2-cm right upper lobe mass. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 50-year-old patient comes to the emergency department because of severe lower chest pain for the past hour. The pain radiates to the back and is associated with nausea. They have had two episodes of non-bloody vomiting since the pain started. They have a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 30 years. They drink five to six beers per day. Their medications include enalapril and metformin. Their temperature is 38.5°C (101.3°F), pulse is 110/min, and blood pressure is 90/60 mm Hg. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Examination shows a distended abdomen with epigastric tenderness and guarding but no rebound; bowel sounds are decreased. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 14.5 g/dL Leukocyte count 5,100/mm3 Platelet count 280,000/mm3 Serum Na+ 133 mEq/L K+ 3.5 mEq/L Cl- 98 mEq/L Total bilirubin 1.0 mg/dL Amylase 160 U/L Lipase 880 U/L (N = 14–280) An ECG shows sinus tachycardia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 11-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after they were found screaming and clutching their head. They have had nausea and occasional episodes of vomiting for 1 week, fever and left-sided headaches for 2 weeks, and increasing tooth pain over the past 3 weeks. They have no history of ear or sinus infections. They are in moderate distress. Their temperature is 38.7°C (101.7°F), pulse is 170/min, respirations are 19/min, and blood pressure is 122/85 mmHg. They are confused and only oriented to person. The pupils react sluggishly to light. Fundoscopic examination shows papilledema bilaterally. Extraocular movements are normal. Flexion of the neck causes hip flexion. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of a recurrent pruritic rash on their face and scalp. They report that they have been using a new shaving cream once a week for the past 5 months. A year ago, they were diagnosed with HIV and are currently receiving triple antiretroviral therapy. They drink several six-packs of beer weekly. Vital signs are within normal limits. A photograph of the rash is shown. A similar rash is seen near the hairline of the scalp and greasy yellow scales are seen at the margins of the eyelids. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 10-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department 15 minutes after they had a seizure. Their parent reports that they complained of sudden nausea and seeing “shiny lights,” after which the corner of their mouth and then their face began twitching. Next, they let out a loud scream, dropped to the floor unconscious, and began to jerk their arms and legs as well for about two minutes. On the way to the hospital, the patient regained consciousness, but was confused and could not speak clearly for about five minutes. They had a fever and sore throat one week ago which improved after treatment with acetaminophen. They appear lethargic and cannot recall what happened during the episode. Their vital signs are within normal limits. They are oriented to time, place, and person. Deep tendon reflexes are 2+ bilaterally. There is muscular pain at attempts to elicit deep tendon reflexes. Physical and neurologic examinations show no other abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parents because of concerns about their behavior during the past year. Their parents report that they often fail to answer when they call them and has regular unprovoked episodes of crying and screaming. At kindergarten, they can follow and participate in group activities, but does not follow their teacher's instructions when these are given to them directly. They are otherwise cheerful and maintains eye contact when spoken to but does not respond when engaged in play. They get along well with friends and family. They started walking at the age of 11 months and can speak in two-to-three-word phrases. They often mispronounce words. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old patient comes to the physician because of increased urinary frequency over the past month. They also report having dry mouth and feeling thirsty all the time despite drinking several liters of water per day. They have not had any weight changes and their appetite is normal. They have a history of obsessive compulsive disorder treated with citalopram. They drink 1–2 cans of beer per day. Their vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show: Serum Na+ 130 mEq/L Glucose 110 mg/dL Osmolality 265 mOsmol/kg Urine Osmolality 230 mOsmol/kg The patient is asked to stop drinking water for 3 hours. Following water restriction, urine osmolality is measured every hour, whereas serum osmolality is measured every 2 hours. Repeated laboratory measurements show a serum osmolality of 280 mOsmol/kg and a urine osmolality of 650 mOsmol/kg. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-month-old patient is brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of progressive difficulty breathing and a dry cough. Five weeks ago, they were diagnosed with diffuse hemangiomas involving the intrathoracic cavity and started treatment with prednisolone. They appear uncomfortable and in moderate respiratory distress. Their temperature is 38°C (100.4°F), pulse is 150/min, respirations are 50/min, and blood pressure is 88/50 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 87%. Oral examination shows a white plaque covering the tongue that bleeds when scraped. Chest examination shows subcostal and intercostal retractions. Scattered fine crackles and rhonchi are heard throughout both lung fields. Laboratory studies show a leukocyte count of 21,000/mm3 and an increased serum beta-D-glucan concentration. An x-ray of the chest shows symmetrical, diffuse interstitial infiltrates. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 3-week-old newborn is brought to the physician by their parents because of poor feeding, irritability, and frequent vomiting over the past week. The vomitus is greenish in color and smells strange. Their parents have tried to feed them every 4 hours, but the patient often spits up or refuses to eat. The patient was born at term and had their first bowel movement at 50 hours of life. They have since had one bowel movement daily. They are at the 50th percentile for length, 10th percentile for weight, and 40th percentile for head circumference. They do not appear to be in acute distress. Their temperature is 36.9°C (98.4°F), pulse is 140/min, respirations are 40/min, and blood pressure is 90/60 mm Hg. Physical examination shows that the patient has small, low-set ears, a broad and flat nasal bridge, and a large space between the first and second toes bilaterally. The abdomen is distended. When the finger is removed following a rectal exam, there is an explosive release of stool from the patient's rectum. An x-ray of the abdomen shows a section of dilated colon followed by a segment of colon without stool or air. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 59-year-old patient comes to the emergency department 25 minutes after the onset of severe left periorbital pain and blurred vision in the same eye. The pain began soon after they entered a theater to watch a movie. They have a headache and vomited twice on the way to the hospital. Two weeks ago, they had acute sinusitis that resolved spontaneously. They have atrial fibrillation and hypertension. Current medications include metoprolol and warfarin. Their temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 101/min, and blood pressure is 140/80 mm Hg. Visual acuity is counting fingers at 3 feet in the left eye and 20/20 in the right eye. The left eye shows conjunctival injection and edematous cornea. The left pupil is mid-dilated and irregular; it is not reactive to light. Extraocular movements are normal. Fundoscopic examination is inconclusive because of severe corneal edema. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 9-month-old infant is brought to the physician because of a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash began on their trunk and spread to their extremities. Five days ago, they were taken to the emergency department for fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. They were born at term and have no history of serious illness. Their immunizations are up-to-date. Current medications include acetaminophen. Their temperature is 37.2°C (99.0°F) and pulse is 120/min. Examination shows a maculopapular rash that blanches on pressure. A photograph of the rash is shown. Posterior auricular lymphadenopathy is present. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parents because of 2 episodes of screaming in the night over the past week. The parents report that their child woke up suddenly screaming, crying, and aggressively kicking their legs around both times. The episodes lasted several minutes and were accompanied by sweating and fast breathing. The parents state that they were unable to stop the episodes and that their child simply went back to sleep when the episodes were over. The patient cannot recall any details of these incidents. They have a history of obstructive sleep apnea. They take no medications. Their vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 29-year-old African-American patient comes to the physician with a 2-week history of progressive fatigue and shortness of breath on exertion. Last week they noticed that their eyes were gradually turning yellow and their urine was dark. They have a family history of type II diabetes. They deny changes in urinary frequency, dysuria, or nocturia. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6° F), blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, and heart rate is 80/min. Examination shows pale conjunctivae, splenomegaly, and jaundice. There is no lymphadenopathy. Laboratory studies show: Hematocrit 19.5% Hemoglobin 6.5 g/dL WBC count 11,000/mm3 Platelet count 300,000/mm3 Reticulocyte count 8% Serum Total bilirubin 6 mg/dL Direct bilirubin 1.0 mg/dL Urea nitrogen 9 mg/dL Creatinine 1 mg/dL Lactate dehydrogenase 365 U/L Peripheral blood smear shows gross polychromasia with nucleated red blood cells and spherocytes. Direct Coombs' test is positive. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old patient comes to the physician because of painless swelling in their left foot for 4 months. The swelling was initially accompanied by redness, which has since resolved. They have not had fever or chills. They have a history of coronary artery disease, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. They have had 3 sexual partners over the past year and use condoms inconsistently. Their mother had rheumatoid arthritis. Current medications include clopidogrel, aspirin, metoprolol, losartan, atorvastatin, and insulin. They are 180 cm (5 ft 11 in) tall and weigh 95 kg (209 lb); BMI is 29 kg/m2. Vital signs are within normal limits. Cardiovascular examination shows no abnormalities. Examination of the feet shows swelling of the left ankle with collapse of the midfoot arch and prominent malleoli. There is no redness or warmth. There is a small, dry ulcer on the left plantar surface of the 2nd metatarsal. Monofilament testing shows decreased sensation along both feet up to the shins bilaterally. Their gait is normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parent because of increasingly withdrawn behavior for the last two years. Their parent reports that in the last 2–3 years of high school, their child has spent most of their time in their room playing video games. They do not have any friends and have never had a romantic partner. They usually refuse to attend family dinner and avoid contact with their siblings. The patient states that they prefer being on their own. When asked how much playing video games means to them, they reply that “it's okay.” When their parent starts crying during the visit, they appear indifferent. Physical and neurologic examinations show no other abnormalities. On mental status examination, their thought process is organized and logical. Their affect is flattened. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 71-year-old patient comes to the physician for a health maintenance examination. Aside from occasional lower back pain in the last couple of years, they feel well. They had a right-sided myocardial infarction 4 years ago. Currently, they have no shortness of breath and have no anginal symptoms. They have a 30 pack-year history of smoking but stopped smoking 10 years ago and do not drink alcohol. Their pulse is 59/min, and their blood pressure is 135/75 mm Hg. Physical examination reveals 1+ lower extremity edema. Cardiac and pulmonary auscultation show no abnormalities. There is no lymphadenopathy. Their laboratory studies show a hemoglobin of 13.2 g/dL and serum protein of 10.1 g/dL. ECG shows known Q wave abnormalities unchanged since the last ECG one year ago. A serum protein electrophoresis with immunofixation is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to establish the diagnosis?

A 16-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of yellowish discoloration of their eyes and generalized fatigue since they returned from a 2-week class trip to Guatemala 2 days ago. During their time there, they had watery diarrhea, nausea, and lack of appetite for 3 days that resolved without treatment. They also took primaquine for malaria prophylaxis. Three weeks ago, they had a urinary tract infection that was treated with nitrofurantoin. Their immunizations are up-to-date. Their temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 82/min and blood pressure is 110/74 mm Hg. Examination shows scleral icterus. There is no lymphadenopathy. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL Leukocyte count 6400/mm3 Platelet count 234,000/mm3 Reticulocyte count 1.1% Prothrombin time 12 sec (INR=1) Serum Bilirubin Total 2.8 mg/dL Direct 0.2 mg/dL Alkaline phosphatase 43 U/L AST 16 U/L ALT 17 U/L γ-Glutamyltransferase 38 U/L (N = 5–50) Anti-HAV IgG positive Anti-HBs positive A peripheral blood smear shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 63-year-old patient comes to the physician for the evaluation of a skin lesion on their chest. They first noticed the lesion 2 months ago and think that it has increased in size since then. The lesion is not painful or pruritic. They have type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and glaucoma. The patient has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the last 40 years and drinks two to three beers on the weekend. Current medications include metformin, atorvastatin, topical timolol, and a multivitamin. Vital signs are within normal limits. The lesion is partly elevated on palpation and does not change its form on pinching. A photograph of the lesion is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 37-year-old patient comes to the emergency department with their spouse because of a 3-day history of severe pain in their right arm. They also report that they cannot move their right arm. The symptoms began after the patient woke up one morning, having slept on their side. They are otherwise healthy. They work as a waiter and say that they feel exhausted from working several night shifts per week. They add that they “can barely keep their eyes open” when looking after their child the next day. Since the onset of the pain, they have been unable to work and are fully dependent on their spouse, who took an extra shift to make enough money to pay their monthly bills. The patient appears relaxed but only allows themselves to be examined after their spouse convinces them. Their vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows 1/5 muscle strength in the right arm. Reflexes are normal. They have no sensation to light touch over the entire right arm and forearm. When a pin prick test is conducted, the patient rapidly withdraws the right arm. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old patient comes to the emergency department with their partner 2 hours after an episode of loss of consciousness. They were seated and were being tattooed on their right upper flank when they became diaphoretic, pale, and passed out. According to their partner, the patient slipped to the floor and their arms and legs moved in a jerky fashion for a few seconds. They regained consciousness within half a minute and were alert and fully oriented immediately. They have no history of serious illness. They work as an event manager and have had more stress than usual due to a recent concert tour. They appear well. Their temperature is 37°C (98.4°F), pulse is 68/min, respirations are 16/min, and blood pressure is 120/72 mm Hg. Their cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. Neurologic examination shows no focal findings. An ECG shows an incomplete right bundle branch block. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 50-year-old patient comes to the emergency department for evaluation of right-sided facial weakness that they noticed after waking up. One month ago, they also experienced right-sided neck pain and headache that began after returning from a hunting trip to New Hampshire the week before. They took ibuprofen to relieve symptoms, which subsided a week later. They have a 5-year history of hypertension controlled with drug therapy. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 35 years and they drink two beers daily. Their vital signs are within the normal range. Physical examination shows right-sided drooping of the upper and lower half of the face. The patient has difficulties smiling and they are unable to close their right eye. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

An 18-month-old patient is brought to the physician by their parents for the evaluation of passing large amounts of dark red blood from their rectum for 2 days. Their parents noticed that they have also had several episodes of dark stools over the past 3 weeks. The parents report that their child has been sleeping more and has been more pale than usual over the past 24 hours. The patient's appetite has been normal and they have not vomited. They are at the 50th percentile for height and 50th percentile for weight. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 135/min, respirations are 38/min, and blood pressure is 90/50 mm Hg. Examination shows pale conjunctivae. The abdomen is soft and nontender. There is a small amount of dark red blood in the diaper. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 9.5 g/dL Hematocrit 30% Mean corpuscular volume 68 μm3 Leukocyte count 7,200/mm3 Platelet count 300,000/mm3 Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 42-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 12 month history of progressive fatigue and shortness of breath with exertion. Five years ago, they emigrated from Eastern Europe. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 20 years. They have a history of using methamphetamines and cocaine but quit 5 years ago. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows jugular venous pulsations 9 cm above the sternal angle. The lungs are clear to auscultation. There is a normal S1 and a loud, split S2. An impulse can be felt with the fingers left of the sternum. The abdomen is soft and nontender. The fingertips are enlarged and the nails are curved. There is pitting edema around the ankles bilaterally. An x-ray of the chest shows pronounced central pulmonary arteries and a prominent right heart border. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 5-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of a 10-day history of intermittent fevers and painful swelling of the right ankle. They have not had trauma to the ankle. They have a history of sickle cell disease and had an episode of dactylitis of their left index finger 3 years ago. Current medications include hydroxyurea and acetaminophen as needed for the ankle pain. Their temperature is 38°C (100.4°F), blood pressure is 125/68 mm Hg, pulse is 105/min, and respirations are 14/min. Examination shows a tender, swollen, and erythematous right ankle with point tenderness over the medial malleolus. X-ray of the right ankle demonstrates marked periosteal thickening and elevation, as well as a central sclerotic lesion with a lucent rim over the right lateral malleolus. A bone biopsy culture confirms the diagnosis. Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?

A previously healthy 60-year-old patient comes to their physician because of progressively worsening shortness of breath for the past 2 months. They do not experience shortness of breath at rest. They also occasionally have a dry cough. They have not had fever, chills, or night sweats. They have smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for the past 40 years. They drink a beer daily and occasionally more on weekends. They do not use illicit drugs. They are 183 cm (6 ft 0 in) tall and weigh 66 kg (145 lbs); BMI is 19.7 kg/m2. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 94/min, respirations are 21/min, and blood pressure is 136/88 mm Hg. Lung auscultation reveals a prolonged expiratory phase and end-expiratory wheezing. Spirometry shows an FEV1:FVC ratio of 62%, an FEV1 of 60% of predicted, and a total lung capacity of 125% of predicted. The diffusion capacity of the lung (DLCO) is decreased. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department 3 hours after having a 2-minute episode of violent, jerky movements of their right arm at school. They were sweating profusely during the episode and did not lose consciousness. They remember having felt a chill down their spine before the episode. Following the episode, they experienced weakness in the right arm and were not able to lift it above their head for 2 hours. Three weeks ago, they had a sore throat that resolved with over-the-counter medication. They were born at term and their parent remembers them having an episode of jerky movements when they had a high-grade fever as a toddler. There is no family history of serious illness, although their parent passed away in a motor vehicle accident approximately 1 year ago. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 98/min, and blood pressure is 94/54 mm Hg. Physical and neurologic examinations show no abnormalities. A complete blood count and serum concentrations of glucose, electrolytes, calcium, and creatinine are within the reference range. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 30-year-old patient comes to the physician because of nervousness and difficulty sleeping over the past 4 weeks. They have difficulty falling asleep at night because they cannot stop worrying about their relationship and their future. Three months ago, their new partner moved in with them. Before this relationship, they had been single for 13 years. They report that their partner does not keep things in order in the way they were used to. Sometimes, they put their dirty dishes in the kitchen sink instead of putting them in the dishwasher directly. They refuse to add any groceries to the shopping list when they are used up. They have also suggested several times that they have dinner at a restaurant instead of eating at home, which enrages them because they like to plan each dinner of the week and buy the required groceries beforehand. The patient says that they really love their partner but that they will never be able to tolerate their “flaws.” Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. On mental status examination, they are cooperative but appear distressed. Their affect has little intensity or range. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old patient presents to a counselor at the urging of their parents because they are concerned that they might be depressed. After recently breaking up with their long-term partner, they moved back in with their parents because they could not handle making decisions alone. Soon after the breakup, they started going on 5–7 dates a week. They have been unemployed for 3 years, as their partner took care of all the bills. In the past year, they thought of looking for a job but never felt confident enough to start the process. Their parent arranges their doctor's appointments and handles their car maintenance. They describe feeling uneasy when they are alone. They have hypothyroidism treated with levothyroxine. They do not smoke or drink alcohol. Vital signs are normal. Mental status exam shows a neutral affect. Neurologic examination shows no focal findings. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old African-American patient comes to the physician after an episode of hemoptysis. Over the past 8 months, they have had a nonproductive cough, fatigue, and a 9-kg (20-lb) weight loss. They drink a glass of wine every night and do not smoke. They have a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis. They do not take any medications. They have never traveled out of the country. They work as an accountant. Their temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse is 94/min, and blood pressure is 130/90 mm Hg. Lungs are clear to auscultation. An x-ray of the chest shows a 2.5-cm nodule with irregular borders at the apex of the left lung with no mediastinal or hilar enlargement. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department because of a 1-day history of malaise and abdominal pain. Six weeks ago, they had vomiting and watery diarrhea for 2 days that resolved without treatment. Twelve weeks ago, they underwent orthotopic liver transplantation for alcoholic cirrhosis. At the time of discharge, their total serum bilirubin concentration was 1.0 mg/dL. They stopped drinking alcohol one year ago. Their current medications include daily tacrolimus, prednisone, valganciclovir, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Their temperature is 37.7°C (99.9°F), pulse is 95/min, and blood pressure is 150/80 mm Hg. They appear uncomfortable and have mild jaundice. Examination shows scleral icterus. The abdomen is soft and tender to deep palpation over the right upper quadrant, where there is a well-healed surgical scar. Their leukocyte count is 2500/mm3, serum bilirubin concentration is 2.6 mg/dL, and serum tacrolimus concentration is within therapeutic range. Which of the following is the next appropriate step in diagnosis?

A 47-year-old patient comes to the emergency department because of urinary and fecal incontinence for 6 hours. Earlier in the day, they suffered a fall at a construction site and sustained injuries to their back and thighs but did not seek medical attention. They took ibuprofen for lower back pain. Their temperature is 36.9°C (98.4°F), pulse is 80/min, and blood pressure is 132/84 mm Hg. Examination shows tenderness over the lumbar spine, bilateral lower extremity weakness, absent ankle jerk reflexes, and preserved patellar reflexes. There is decreased rectal tone. An ultrasound of the bladder shows a full bladder. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 3-week history of abdominal bloating and increased frequency of stools. They describe the stools as bulky, foul-smelling, and difficult to flush. They also have a 4-month history of recurrent dull upper abdominal pain that usually lasts for a few days, worsens after meals, and is not relieved with antacids. They have had a 10-kg (22-lb) weight loss in the past 4 months. They have no personal or family history of serious illness. They have smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for 37 years. They have a 12-year history of drinking 6 to 8 beers daily. They are 160 cm (5 ft 3 in) tall and weigh 52 kg (115 lb); BMI is 20 kg/m2. Their vital signs are within normal limits. Abdominal examination shows mild epigastric tenderness without rebound or guarding. Bowel sounds are normal. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 72-year-old patient comes to the emergency department 4 hours after the sudden onset of a diffuse, dull, throbbing headache. During this time, they also report blurred vision, nausea, and one episode of vomiting. They have a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Their medications include hydrochlorothiazide, lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. They have smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the past 30 years and drinks 1–2 glasses of wine per day. Their temperature is 36.6 °C (97.9 °F), pulse is 90/min, respirations are 14/min, and blood pressure is 185/110 mm Hg. Fundoscopic examination shows bilateral blurring of the optic disc margins. Physical and neurologic examinations show no other abnormalities. A complete blood count and serum concentrations of electrolytes, urea nitrogen, and creatinine are within the reference range. Urinalysis shows 2+ protein but no WBCs or RBCs. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of right hip pain that started that afternoon. Their parent reports that they have also been limping since the pain developed. They say that the pain worsens when they move or walk. They participated in a dance recital yesterday, but their parent believes that they were not injured at the time. They were born at term and have been healthy except for an episode of nasal congestion and mild cough 10 days ago. Their parent has rheumatoid arthritis and their grandparent has osteoporosis. They are at the 50th percentile for height and 50th percentile for weight. Their temperature is 37.5°C (99.6°F), pulse is 105/min, respirations are 16/min, and blood pressure is 90/78 mm Hg. Their right hip is slightly abducted and externally rotated. Examination shows no tenderness, warmth, or erythema. They are able to bear weight. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin concentration of 12.3 g/dL, a leukocyte count of 8,500/mm3, and an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 12 mm/h. Ultrasound of the right hip shows increased fluid within the joint. X-ray of the hips shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old patient comes to the physician because of right-sided blurry vision and eye pain for 4 days. They have a 6-day history of low-grade fever, headache, and malaise. One year ago, they were diagnosed with Crohn disease. Their only medication is prednisone. Their temperature is 38°C (100.4°F), pulse is 84/min, and blood pressure is 112/75 mm Hg. The right eyelid is erythematous and tender; there are multiple vesicles over the right forehead and the tip of the nose. Visual acuity is 20/20 in the left eye and 20/80 in the right eye. Extraocular movements are normal. The right eye shows conjunctival injection and reduced corneal sensitivity. Fluorescein staining shows a corneal lesion with a tree-like pattern. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parent for a follow-up examination. They have a history of recurrent asthma attacks. The parent reports that the patient has also had mild abdominal pain for the past 2 weeks. The patient's current medications include daily inhaled fluticasone and inhaled albuterol as needed. They appear well. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 100/min, and blood pressure is 130/85 mm Hg. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Cardiac examination shows no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Abdominal examination shows a left-sided, nontender, smooth abdominal mass that does not cross the midline. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. A complete blood count and serum concentrations of electrolytes, urea nitrogen, and creatinine are within the reference range. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old patient comes to the emergency department for pain and swelling of their left knee one day after injuring it while playing soccer. While sprinting on the field, they slipped as they attempted to kick the ball and landed on the anterior aspect of their knee. They underwent an appendectomy at the age of 16 years. Their vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows a swollen and tender left knee; range of motion is limited by pain. The tibial tuberosity shows tenderness to palpation. The left tibia is displaced posteriorly when force is applied to the proximal tibia after flexing the knee. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. An x-ray of the left knee joint shows an avulsion fracture of the tibial condyle. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parents because of a 4.5-kg (10-lb) weight loss during the last 3 months. During this period, they have complained of abdominal pain and fullness, and their parents feel that they have been eating less. Their parents also report that their urine has appeared pink for several weeks. They have been performing poorly in school lately, with reports from teachers that they have not been paying attention in class and have been distracting to other students. They were born at term and have been healthy except for a history of several infantile seizures. Their vital signs are within normal limits. They are at the 60th percentile for height and 20th percentile for weight. Physical examination shows a palpable abdominal mass, abdominal tenderness in the left upper quadrant, and left costovertebral angle tenderness. There are several ellipsoid, hypopigmented macules on the back and legs and a 4-cm raised plaque of rough, dimpled skin on the right lower back that is the same color as the surrounding skin. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department because of intermittent sharp right upper quadrant abdominal pain and nausea for the past 10 hours. They vomited three times. There is no associated fever, chills, diarrhea, or urinary symptoms. They have two children who both attend high school. They appear uncomfortable. They are 165 cm (5 ft 5 in) tall and weigh 86 kg (190 lb); BMI is 32 kg/m2. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 100/min, and blood pressure is 140/90 mm Hg. They have mild scleral icterus. The abdomen is soft and nondistended, with tenderness to palpation of the right upper quadrant without guarding or rebound. Bowel sounds are normal. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin count 14 g/dL Leukocyte count 9,000 mm3 Platelet count 160,000 mm3 Serum Alkaline phosphatase 238 U/L Aspartate aminotransferase 60 U/L Bilirubin Total 2.8 mg/dL Direct 2.1 mg/dL Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 24-year-old patient comes to the physician with a wound on their forearm. They say that they injured themselves by absentmindedly walking into a glass door. They do not have health insurance. They have had 5 jobs in the past 8 months. They quit each job after 3–4 weeks because they found the work beneath them. They were imprisoned 6 years ago for credit card fraud. They were released from prison on parole a year ago. They were expelled from school at the age of 13 years for stealing school property and threatening to assault a teacher. They have parented 6 children with 4 partners. They say that they do not provide child support because they need the money for their own personal expenses. The patient's vital signs are within normal limits. Examination of the forearm shows a 6 cm long, 0.5 cm deep wound with neat edges on the dorsal surface of the left forearm. There are bruises on the left shoulder, back, and the proximal phalanges of the right hand. On mental status examination, the patient is alert and calm. Their mood is described as cheerful. Their thought process, thought content, and speech are normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of persistent pain in their right shoulder. The pain is localized to the top of the shoulder and is worse with movement. They have stiffness in the right shoulder that is worse in the morning and usually lasts 20 minutes. The patient reports that they are unable to brush their hair and has stopped going to their regular tennis lessons because of the pain. They do not recall any fall or trauma. When their right arm is passively abducted in an arc, there is pain between 60 and 120 degrees of abduction. When asked to lower the right arm slowly from 90 degrees of abduction, they are unable to hold their arm up and it drops to their side. Passive range of motion is normal. Injection of 5 mL of 1% lidocaine into the right subacromial space does not relieve the pain or improve active range of motion of the right arm. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old patient comes to the emergency department because of decreased vision and black spots in front of their left eye for the past 24 hours. They state that it feels as if 'a curtain is hanging over their eye.' They see flashes of light intermittently. They have no pain or diplopia. They underwent cataract surgery on the left eye 2 weeks ago. They have hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Their sister has open-angle glaucoma. Current medications include metformin, linagliptin, ramipril, and hydrochlorothiazide. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows a visual acuity in the right eye of 20/25 and the ability to count fingers at 3 feet in the left eye. The pupils are equal and reactive. The corneal reflex is present. The anterior chamber shows no abnormalities. The confrontation test is normal on the right side and shows nasal and inferior defects on the left side. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. The patient is awaiting dilation for fundus examination. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old patient comes to the emergency department because of worsening shortness of breath and a productive cough for 3 days. They sustained trauma to the right hemithorax during a fight 3 weeks ago. They had significant pain and mild shortness of breath following the incident but did not seek medical care. They do not smoke or drink alcohol. They are a construction worker. Their temperature is 38.4°C (101.1°F), pulse is 95/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 120/75 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 96%. Pulmonary examination shows decreased breath sounds over the right lower lung fields. CT scan of the chest shows fractures of the right 7th and 8th ribs, right pleural splitting and thickening, and a dense fluid collection in the pleural space. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 37-year-old patient comes to the physician because of right-sided inguinal pain for the past 8 weeks. During this period, the patient has had increased pain during activities such as walking and standing. They have no nausea, vomiting, or fever. Their temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F), pulse is 73/min, and blood pressure is 132/80 mm Hg. The abdomen is soft and nontender. There is a visible and palpable groin protrusion above the inguinal ligament on the right side. Bulging is felt during Valsalva maneuver. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 63-year-old patient comes to the physician for the evaluation of difficulty walking for the last 6 months. They report weakness in their lower legs that improves with exercise and throughout the day. Three months ago, they started adding flax seeds to their breakfast because they are frequently constipated. They have hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. They have smoked 2 packs of cigarettes daily for the last 45 years. Their current medications include enalapril and metformin. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows dry mucous membranes. Muscle strength in the lower extremities is decreased. Sensation to pinprick and light touch is normal. Deep tendon reflexes are 1+ bilaterally. Active muscle contraction or repeated muscle tapping increases reflex activity. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 56-year-old patient comes to the physician for a routine health maintenance examination. They have had mild pain in their left groin for 2 weeks. They were admitted to the hospital 1 month ago for myocardial infarction. Cardiac catheterization and angiography showed occlusion of the left anterior descending artery and they underwent placement of 2 stents. They have hypertension and hypercholesterolemia. There is no family history of serious illness. They have smoked 2 packs of cigarettes daily for 30 years. Current medications include aspirin, clopidogrel, rosuvastatin, and enalapril. Their temperature is 36.7°C (98°F), pulse is 88/min, and blood pressure is 130/84 mm Hg. Examination shows a 3-cm (1.2-in), tender, pulsatile mass in the left thigh, below the inguinal ligament. There is mild erythema of the overlying skin. A loud murmur is heard on auscultation of the mass. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. There is no edema in the lower limbs. Femoral and pedal pulses are palpable bilaterally. Neurologic examination shows no focal findings. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 50-year-old patient comes to the physician for a routine checkup. They have had a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of their neck for 2 months. They do not have a fever or any discharge from the swelling. They underwent a colectomy for colon cancer at the age of 43 years. They have type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. Current medications include insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen. They have worked as a traffic warden for the past 6 years and frequently play golf. They appear healthy. Their temperature is 37.3°C (99.1°F), pulse is 88/min, and blood pressure is 130/86 mm Hg. Examination of the neck shows a 2.5-cm (1-in) firm, mobile, and painless nodule. The skin over the nodule cannot be pinched. The lungs are clear to auscultation. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. A photograph of the lesion is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old patient develops reduced urine output and a serum creatinine concentration of 2.9 mg/dL three days after being hospitalized for acute diverticulitis. On admission, a complete blood count showed a hemoglobin concentration of 15.5 g/dL and a leukocyte count of 14,000/mm3. Urinalysis showed 2+ proteinuria, and serum studies showed a blood glucose of 145 mg/dL and a creatinine concentration of 1.2 mg/dL. A CT scan of the abdomen confirmed the diagnosis. Therapy with intravenous ketoprofen, piperacillin, and tazobactam was begun, and the patient was placed on bowel rest. They have a history of hypertension, chronic constipation, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Prior to admission, their medications were insulin, metoprolol, and losartan. Today, their temperature is 37.7°C (99.9°F), pulse is 97/min, respirations are 12/min, and blood pressure is 135/87 mm Hg. The abdomen is soft on physical examination, and there is tenderness to palpation of the left lower quadrant. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's current renal findings?

A 4-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of progressive intermittent pain and swelling in both knees and right ankle and wrist for 3 months. They have been taking acetaminophen and using ice packs, both of which relieved their symptoms. The affected joints feel "stuck" and difficult to move when they wake up in the morning, but they can move them freely after a few minutes. They have also occasional mild eye pain that resolves spontaneously. Five months ago they were diagnosed with upper respiratory tract infection that resolved without treatment. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows that the affected joints are swollen, erythematous, and tender to touch. Slit-lamp examination shows an anterior chamber flare with signs of iris inflammation bilaterally. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 12.6 g/dl Leukocyte count 8,000/mm3 Segmented neutrophils 76% Eosinophils 1% Lymphocytes 20% Monocytes 3% Platelet count 360,000/mm3 Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 36 mm/hr Serum Antinuclear antibodies 1:320 Rheumatoid factor negative Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient comes to the emergency department because of blurry vision for 10 hours. They have also had urinary urgency and discomfort while urinating for the past 4 days. They have been feeling increasingly weak and nauseous since yesterday. They have a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and arterial hypertension. One year ago they were treated for an infection of their eyes. They drink 2–3 glasses of wine weekly. Current medications include captopril, metoprolol, metformin, and insulin. Their temperature is 37.5°C (99.5°F), pulse is 107/min, and blood pressure is 95/70 mm Hg. Visual acuity is decreased in both eyes. The pupils are equal and reactive to light. The corneal reflexes are brisk. The mucous membranes of the mouth are dry. The abdomen is soft and not distended. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old patient is brought to the physician because they have excessively dry skin. Their parent says that they have had dry, scaly skin since they were 6 months old. They say it is worse in winter and better in summer. There is no associated itching, redness, or discharge. Examination reveals generalized fine scales with coarse skin all over the body, except in the skin creases of the neck and in the cubital and popliteal fossae (see image). There are multiple papular elevations at the base of hair follicles and darkening of the palmar and plantar creases. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old graduate student comes to the physician for a two-month history of repeated thoughts and anxiety that they are going to be harmed by someone on the street. The anxiety worsened after witnessing a pedestrian getting hit by a car two weeks ago. They say, “That was a warning sign.” On their way to school, they now often leave an hour earlier to take a detour and hide from people that they think might hurt them. They are burdened by their coursework and fears that their professors are meaning to fail them. They say their friends are concerned about them but that they do not understand because they were not present at the accident. The patient has no known history of psychiatric illness. On mental status exam, they are alert and oriented, and shows full range of affect. Thought processes and speech are organized. Their memory and attention are within normal limits. They deny auditory, visual, or tactile hallucinations. Urine toxicology screening is negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 13-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parents for the evaluation of progressive hair loss over the past 2 months. The parents report that they have noticed an increased number of hairless patches on their child's head. The patient denies any itching. There is no personal or family history of serious illness. The patient states that they have been feeling tense since their partner broke up with them. They do not smoke or drink alcohol. They do not use illicit drugs. Their vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows ill-defined patchy hair loss and hair of different lengths with no scaling or reddening of the scalp. Further examination shows poor hair growth of the eyebrows and eyelashes. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department because of a fall that occurred while they were taking a shower earlier that morning. Their spouse heard them fall and entered the bathroom to find all four of their extremities twitching. The episode lasted approximately 30 seconds. They were unsure of what had happened and were unable to answer simple questions on awakening. They have regained orientation since that time. They have hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Current medications include metoprolol and atorvastatin. Their temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 72/min, respirations are 19/min, and blood pressure is 130/80 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 98%. Cranial nerve examination shows no abnormalities. They have 5/5 strength in all extremities. Examination shows full muscle strength. Sensation to pinprick, light touch, and vibration is normal and symmetrical. A noncontrast head CT is performed and shows a slightly hyperdense mass. Follow-up MRI shows a homogeneous, well-circumscribed 4-cm mass with compression of the adjacent white matter, and a hyperintense rim around the mass on T2 weighted imaging. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 18-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their coach, 30 minutes after injuring their left knee while playing field hockey. They were tackled from the left side and have been unable to bear weight on their left leg since the accident. They fear the left knee may be unstable upon standing. There is no personal or family history of serious illness. The patient appears uncomfortable. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows a swollen and tender left knee; range of motion is limited by pain. The medial joint line is tender to touch. The patient's hip is slightly flexed and abducted, and the knee is slightly flexed while the patient is in the supine position. Gentle valgus stress is applied across the left knee and medial joint laxity is noted. The remainder of the examination shows no further abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a skin lesion on their nose. The patient has had the lesion for 11 months and it has increased in size over the past few months. They are a farmer and live together with their partner. Their mother died of metastatic melanoma at the age of 67 years. The patient has smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for the past 30 years and drinks 1–2 glasses of whiskey on weekends. Their temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F), pulse is 75/min, and blood pressure is 140/78 mm Hg. Examination of the skin shows a nontender lesion at the right root of the nose. An image of the lesion is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 77-year-old patient is brought to the physician for gradually increasing confusion and difficulty walking for the past 4 months. Their daughter is concerned because they have been forgetful and seem to be walking more slowly. They have been distracted during their weekly bridge games and their usual television shows. They have also had increasingly frequent episodes of urinary incontinence and now wear an adult diaper daily. They have hyperlipidemia and hypertension. Current medications include lisinopril and atorvastatin. Their temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F), pulse is 84/min, respirations are 15/min, and blood pressure is 139/83 mmHg. They are confused and oriented only to person and place. They recall 2 out of 3 words immediately and 1 out of 3 after five minutes. They have a broad-based gait and take short steps. Sensation is intact and muscle strength is 5/5 throughout. Laboratory studies are within normal limits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 65-year-old patient comes to the emergency department 1 hour after a loss of consciousness. Their spouse said they suddenly fainted while they were adjusting their necktie. They regained consciousness within 30 seconds and were fully alert and oriented. They have had two similar episodes in the last year. They have anxiety and take alprazolam as needed. They smoke half a pack of cigarettes daily and drink two glasses of wine with dinner each night. Their temperature is 37.2°C (98.9°F), pulse is 70/min and regular, respirations are 13/min, blood pressure is 130/82 mm Hg when supine and 122/80 mm Hg while standing. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. Neurologic examination shows no focal findings. A complete blood count shows no abnormalities. Bedside cardiac monitoring shows infrequent premature ventricular contractions and QRS voltage below 5 mm in leads II and III. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of abdominal distention and twitching of their feet, which their parent noticed a week ago. The patient has also had a low-grade fever for 5 days. They have not had a bowel movement in 3 days. They were born at term and have been healthy since. They are at the 40th percentile for height and 20th percentile for weight. Their temperature is 38.1°C (100.6°F), pulse is 128/min, and blood pressure is 135/82 mm Hg. Examination shows an irregular palpable mass that crosses the midline of the abdomen. The liver is palpated 3 cm below the right costal margin. There are erratic movements of the eyes. A 24-hour urine collection shows elevated homovanillic acid and vanillylmandelic acid levels. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 73-year-old patient comes to the physician because of worsening bilateral lower extremity pain for the past 8 months. The pain begins after walking one to two blocks and radiates bilaterally down the buttocks with cramping and tingling. They report that the pain is worse while walking downhill and is relieved by sitting and leaning forward. They have hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. They had a myocardial infarction at the age of 55 years and an abdominal aortic aneurysm repair at the age of 60 years. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the past 30 years. They do not drink alcohol or use illicit drugs. Their current medications include sitagliptin, metformin, atorvastatin, metoprolol succinate, amlodipine, and hydrochlorothiazide. Their temperature is 37.5°C (99.5°F), pulse is 82/min, respirations are 17/min, and blood pressure is 150/87 mm Hg. Examination shows full muscle strength. Sensation is reduced bilaterally in the feet and toes. Straight leg raise is negative. X-ray of the spine shows degenerative changes. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A previously healthy 17-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their parent for further evaluation after elective removal of their wisdom teeth. During the procedure, the patient had persistent bleeding from the teeth's surrounding gums. Multiple gauze packs were applied with minimal effect. The patient has a history of easy bruising. The parent says their relative had similar problems when their wisdom teeth were removed, and that they also have a history of easy bruising and joint swelling. The patient takes no medications. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 108/74 mm Hg. Laboratory studies show: Hematocrit 35% Leukocyte count 8,500/mm3 Platelet count 160,000/mm3 Prothrombin time 15 sec Partial thromboplastin time 60 sec Bleeding time 6 min Fibrin split products negative Serum Urea nitrogen 20 mg/dL Creatinine 1.0 mg/dL Bilirubin Total 1.0 mg/dL Direct 0.5 mg/dL Lactate dehydrogenase 90 U/L Peripheral blood smear shows normal-sized platelets. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after the sudden onset of severe, migrating anterior chest pain, shortness of breath, and sweating at rest. They have hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Medications include atorvastatin, hydrochlorothiazide, lisinopril, and metformin. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 25 years. They are in severe distress. Their pulse is 110/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 150/85 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 98%. Cardiac examination shows a grade 3/6, high-pitched, blowing, diastolic murmur heard best over the right sternal border. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Femoral pulses are decreased bilaterally. An ECG shows sinus tachycardia and left ventricular hypertrophy. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old patient comes to their physician because of fatigue. They have been coming to the office multiple times a month for various minor problems over the past six months. During the appointments, they insist on a first name basis and flirt with their physician. They always dress very fashionably. When their assistant enters the room, they tend to start fidgeting and interrupt their conversation. When the physician tells them politely that their behavior is inappropriate, they begin to cry, complaining that no one understands them and that if people only listened to them, they would not be so exhausted. They then quickly gather themselves and state that they will just have to keep looking for a physician who can help them, although they have doubts they will ever find the right physician. They do not have a history of self harm or suicidal ideation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 74-year-old Hispanic patient comes to the physician because of a three-week history of dizziness upon standing and a brief loss of consciousness one hour ago. The patient suddenly collapsed on their way to the bathroom after waking up in the morning. They did not sustain any injuries from their collapse. They have a history of gastroesophageal reflux disease, gout, and a family history of a grand mal seizure (the patient's mother died of a grand mal seizure at the age of 53 years). They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 55 years. They drink three beers and two glasses of whiskey daily. Current medications include ranitidine, allopurinol, and other medications for various conditions. They are 166 cm (5 ft 5 in) tall and weigh 62 kg (137 lb); BMI is 22.5 kg/m2. They appear pale. Temperature is 36.7°C (98.0°F), pulse is 83/min, and blood pressure is 125/80 mm Hg supine and 100/70 mm Hg one minute after standing with no change in pulse rate. Physical examination shows conjunctival pallor. A plopping sound is heard on auscultation, immediately followed by a low-pitched, rumbling mid-diastolic murmur heard best at the apex. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. An ECG shows regular sinus rhythm. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their foster mother because of complaints from their teachers regarding poor performance at school for the past 8 months. They do not listen to their instructions, often talk during class, and rarely complete their school assignments. They do not sit in their seat in the classroom and often cut in line at the cafeteria. Their foster mother reports that they run around a lot inside the house and refuse to help their sibling with chores and errands. They frequently interrupt their foster mother's conversations with others and talk excessively. She has found them trying to climb on the roof on multiple occasions. They were placed in foster care because of neglect by their biological parents 3 years ago. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Neurologic examination shows no focal findings. Mental status examination shows a neutral affect. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of fatigue and myalgia. Over the past month, they have had intermittent episodes of nausea. They have a history of intravenous drug use, but they have not used illicit drugs for the past five years. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 14 years and drinks one alcoholic beverage daily. They take no medications. Their last visit to a physician was 4 years ago. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 90/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. Physical examination shows jaundice and hepatosplenomegaly. There are also blisters and erosions on the dorsum of both hands. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 12 g/dL Leukocyte count 8,300/mm3 Platelet count 250,000/mm3 Serum Glucose 170 mg/dL Albumin 3.0 g/dL Total bilirubin 2.2 mg/dL Alkaline phosphatase 80 U/L AST 92 U/L ALT 76 U/L Hepatitis B surface antigen negative Hepatitis B surface antibody positive Hepatitis B core antibody positive Hepatitis C antibody positive Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 48-year-old patient comes to the physician because of worsening shortness of breath and nocturnal cough for the past 2 weeks. On two occasions, their cough was bloody.
