They had a heart condition as a child that was treated with antibiotics. They emigrated to the US from Kazakhstan 15 years ago. Pulmonary examination shows crackles at both lung bases. Cardiac examination is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 13-year-old Hispanic patient is brought to the physician by their parent because of left groin pain for 1 month. The pain radiates to their left knee and is aggravated on walking. They fell during soccer practice 5 weeks ago but did not see a doctor about it and does not recall any immediate and persistent pain after the event. They have hypothyroidism. Their only medication is levothyroxine. Their immunizations are up-to-date. They appear uncomfortable. They are at the 50th percentile for height and at the 95th percentile for weight. Their temperature is 37.1°C (98.9°F), pulse is 77/min, respirations are 14/min, and blood pressure is 100/70 mm Hg. The patient has a left-sided, antalgic gait. The left lower extremity is externally rotated. The left hip is tender to palpation and internal rotation is limited by pain. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 13.1 g/dL Leukocyte count 9,100/mm3 Platelet count 250,000/mm3 Serum TSH 3.6 μU/mL Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old patient comes in to the emergency department with their parent for swelling of their left periorbital region. Yesterday morning they woke up with a painful, warm, soft lump on their left eyelid. Eye movement does not worsen the pain. Physical examination shows redness and swelling of the upper left eyelid, involving the hair follicles. Upon palpation, the swelling drains purulent fluid. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old patient has crampy abdominal pain five days after undergoing an open abdominal aortic aneurysm repair. During this period, they have also had two episodes of loose, bloody stools. Their surgery was complicated by severe blood loss requiring the administration of vasopressors and multiple transfusions. Cefazolin was administered as a perioperative antibiotic. The patient has hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and coronary artery disease. The patient has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes daily for 50 years and drinks 3–4 glasses of wine every week. Their current medications include hydrochlorothiazide, atorvastatin, amlodipine, aspirin, and metoprolol. They appear ill. Their temperature is 38.0°C (100.4°F), pulse is 110/min, and blood pressure is 96/58 mm Hg. Physical examination shows a distended abdomen with absent bowel sounds. The abdomen is exquisitely tender to palpation in all quadrants. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Cardiac examination shows an S4 gallop. An x-ray of the abdomen shows air-filled distended bowel. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of a progressive rash for 2 days. The rash started behind the ears and now involves the trunk and extremities. Over the past 4 days, they have had mild sore throat, red, itchy eyes, and headache. They were born at term and have been healthy except for recurrent episodes of tonsillitis and occasional asthma attacks. Two weeks ago, they were treated for tonsillitis that resolved with penicillin therapy. They immigrated with their family from Brazil 3 weeks ago. Their immunization status is unknown. The patient appears weak and lethargic. Their temperature is 38°C (100.4°F), pulse is 100/min, and blood pressure is 100/60 mm Hg. Examination shows postauricular and suboccipital lymphadenopathy. There is a non-confluent, pink maculopapular rash over the torso and extremities. Their palms and soles show no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old patient comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. They have a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. They have hypertension and ulcerative colitis which was diagnosed via colonoscopy 5 years ago. Current medications include lisinopril and rectal mesalamine. They are sexually active with 2 partners and use condoms inconsistently. Their temperature is 37.3°C (99.1°F), pulse is 86/min, and blood pressure is 130/84 mm Hg. Examination shows scleral icterus and multiple scratch marks on the trunk and extremities. The lungs are clear to auscultation. The abdomen is soft and nontender. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 11.5 g/dL Leukocyte count 7500/mm3 Platelet count 280,000/mm3 Serum Na+ 138 mEq/L Cl- 101 mEq/L K+ 4.7 mEq/L Urea nitrogen 18 mg/dL Glucose 91 mg/dL Creatinine 0.8 mg/dL Bilirubin Total 1.5 mg/dL Direct 0.9 mg/dL Alkaline phosphatase 460 U/L AST 75 U/L ALT 78 U/L Anti-nuclear antibody negative Antimitochondrial antibodies negative Abdominal ultrasound shows thickening of the bile ducts and focal bile duct dilatation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 56-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of worsening pain in their left buttock. The pain is described as a deep, dull ache that is worse at night. They do not report any recent trauma. They have hyperlipidemia. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the past 30 years and drinks one beer every night. They do not use illicit drugs. Their only medication is simvastatin. Physical examination shows tenderness over the left gluteal region. Neurologic examination shows no focal findings. An x-ray of the pelvis shows a 4-cm, poorly defined, osteolytic lesion in the left ilium with a moth-eaten pattern of bone destruction, multiple well-defined sclerotic lesions, and an aggressive periosteal reaction. The remainder of the physical examination, including examination, shows no abnormalities. Chest x-ray and abdominal ultrasonography show no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old patient comes to the physician because of constipation and decreased appetite during the past several months. In the past 2 weeks, they have also noticed an increasing frequency of urination. They have not had any dysuria or flank pain. They have a history of hypertension, calcium pyrophosphate crystal arthritis, and alcoholic cirrhosis. Current medications include hydrochlorothiazide, rifaximin, lactulose, and naproxen as needed for the joint pain. They quit drinking 5 years ago. They do not smoke cigarettes. Their vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows decreased bowel sounds but is otherwise unremarkable. Serum studies show: Creatinine 1.1 mg/dL Calcium 11.8 mg/dL Phosphorus 2.1 mg/dL Magnesium 1.6 mg/dL Total protein 6 g/dL Albumin 3.1 g/dL AST 53 U/L ALT 43 U/L Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department after coughing up copious amounts of blood-tinged sputum at their nursing home. They recently had an upper respiratory tract infection that was treated with antibiotics. They have a long-standing history of productive cough that has worsened since they had a stroke 3 years ago. They smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for 40 years until the stroke, after which they quit. The patient appears distressed and short of breath. Their temperature is 38°C (100.4°F), pulse is 92/min, and blood pressure is 145/85 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 92%. Physical examination shows digital clubbing and cyanosis of the lips. Coarse crackles are heard in the thorax. An x-ray of the chest shows increased translucency and tram-track opacities in the right lower lung field. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 21-year-old patient comes to the physician because of pruritus and a hypopigmented rash on their upper body for 5 days. They first noticed the symptoms after returning from a business trip last week in the Bahamas. While they were there, they visited a couple of beaches and went hiking with some coworkers. The rash initially started as a single lesion on their upper back but since then has extended to their shoulders. They have a history of type 1 diabetes mellitus controlled with an insulin pump. They work as an office manager and have no known exposure to melanocytotoxic chemicals. They have been sexually active with three partners over the past year and use condoms inconsistently. They are 183 cm (6 ft) tall and weigh 80 kg (176 lb); BMI is 23.9 kg/m2. Their temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), pulse is 78/min, and blood pressure is 130/84 mm Hg. A photograph of the rash is shown. One month ago, their hemoglobin A1C was 7.8%. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 58-year-old patient with type 2 diabetes mellitus comes to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of dysphagia and swelling in the neck and lower jaw. They have had tooth pain on the left side over the past week, which has made it difficult for them to sleep. Four weeks ago, they had a 3-day episode of flu-like symptoms, including sore throat, that resolved without treatment. They have a history of hypertension. Current medications include metformin and lisinopril. They appear distressed. They are 180 cm (5 ft 11 in) tall and weigh 100 kg (220 lbs); their BMI is 31.6 kg/m2. Their temperature is 38.4°C (101.1°F), pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 110/80 mm Hg. Oral cavity examination shows a decayed lower left third molar with drainage of pus. There is submandibular and anterior neck tenderness and swelling. Their leukocyte count is 15,600/mm3, platelet count is 300,000/mm3, and fingerstick blood glucose concentration is 250 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old patient undergoes a laparoscopic appendectomy for acute appendicitis. During the procedure, a black, discolored liver is noted. Other than the recent appendicitis, the patient has no history of serious illness and takes no medications. They have no medication allergies. They do not drink alcohol or use illicit drugs. They have an uncomplicated postoperative course. At their follow-up visit 3 weeks later, their vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows scleral icterus, which the patient states has been present for many years. Abdominal examination shows healing scars without drainage or erythema. Serum studies show: Aspartate aminotransferase 30 IU/L Alanine aminotransferase 35 IU/L Alkaline phosphatase 47 mg/dL Total bilirubin 5.2 mg/dL Direct bilirubin 4.0 mg/dL Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 71-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department because of severe, progressive left leg pain and tingling for 8 hours. The symptoms began while they were watching television. For several months, the patient has noticed calf cramping when going for long walks, as well as occasional foot tingling and numbness, but did not seek medical attention. They have no history of recent injuries. They have poorly-controlled hypertension, hyperlipidemia, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and osteoarthritis. They smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 35 years but quit 15 years ago. They drink three beers every night. Current medications include lisinopril, metoprolol succinate, atorvastatin, metformin, and ibuprofen. They appear to be in severe pain and are clutching their left leg. Their temperature is 37.4°C (99.3°F), pulse is 110/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 163/94 mm Hg. The lungs are clear to auscultation. There is a harsh II/VI systolic ejection murmur best heard at the right upper sternal border. The abdomen is soft and nontender. The left leg is cool to the touch with decreased popliteal, posterior tibial, and dorsalis pedis pulses. There is 5/5 strength on left hip, knee, and ankle testing. The left hip, knee, and ankle show no gross effusion, erythema, or tenderness to palpation. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 38-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 1-month history of a painless, nonpruritic skin lesion on their right thigh. They initially thought it was an insect bite, but it has slowly increased in size over the past weeks. Their temperature is 36.7°C (98°F), pulse is 75/min, and blood pressure is 128/76 mm Hg. Physical examination shows a 0.8-cm hyperpigmented papule. When the skin lesion is squeezed, the surface retracts inwards. A photograph of the lesion is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 61-year-old patient comes to the physician because of fatigue, diarrhea, and crampy abdominal pain for 3 weeks. The abdominal pain is worse after eating. During the past week, they have had up to 4 watery stools daily. They have also had pain in their mouth and gums for 6 days. They have not had nausea, vomiting, or fever. Four months ago, they went on a 1-week trip to the Dominican Republic. They have atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and hypothyroidism. Current medications include levothyroxine, metoprolol, and warfarin. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 40 years. Their temperature is 37.9°C (100.2°F), pulse is 81/min, and blood pressure is 120/75 mm Hg. Examination shows two 1-cm, tender ulcerative lesions in the mouth. Abdominal examination shows mild tenderness to palpation in the right lower quadrant without guarding or rebound. Bowel sounds are normal. Their hemoglobin concentration is 11.5 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume is 77 fL, leukocyte count is 11,800 mm3, and platelet count is 360,000 mm3. Colonoscopy with biopsy of the colonic mucosa is performed. Analysis of the specimen shows non-caseating granulomas and neutrophilic inflammation of the crypts. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old patient comes to the physician because of increasing generalized fatigue for 1 month. They have been unable to do normal household duties or go for their evening walks during this period. They have hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Their father died of liver cancer at the age of 60 years. They do not smoke. They drink one alcoholic beverage daily. Current medications include atorvastatin, enalapril, metformin, and insulin glargine. They are 170 cm (5 ft 7 in) tall and weigh 100 kg (220 lb); BMI is 34.6 kg/m2. Their temperature is 36.6°C (97.9°F), pulse is 116/min, and blood pressure is 140/90 mm Hg. Examination shows hyperpigmented skin over the nape of the neck and extremities. The liver is palpated 4 cm below the right costal margin. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 10.6 g/dL Mean corpuscular volume 87 μm3 Leukocyte count 9,700/mm3 Platelet count 182,000/mm3 Serum Glucose 213 mg/dL Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL Albumin 4.1 mg/dL Total bilirubin 1.1 mg/dL Alkaline phosphatase 66 U/L AST 100 U/L ALT 69 U/L γ-glutamyl transferase 28 U/L (N=5–50) Hepatitis B surface antigen negative Hepatitis C antibody negative Iron studies Iron 261 μg/dL Ferritin 558 ng/dL Transferrin saturation 83% Anti-nuclear antibody negative Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to confirm the diagnosis?

A 58-year-old patient comes to the physician because of intermittent painful retrosternal dullness for 4 weeks. The pain is recurrent and occurs when they exert themselves or when they are outside during cold weather. They also experience shortness of breath and palpitations during these episodes. The symptoms resolve spontaneously when they stop or sit down for a while. Over the past few days, the episodes have increased in frequency. They have hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and osteoarthritis. Their left leg was amputated below the knee after a motorcycle accident 25 years ago. They are currently waiting for a new prosthesis and walk with crutches. Current medications include captopril, glyburide, and ibuprofen. They do not smoke or drink alcohol. Their pulse is 88/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 144/90 mm Hg. Cardiac examination shows no abnormalities. An x-ray of the chest shows no abnormalities. An ECG shows a normal sinus rhythm without any signs of ischemia. Serum cardiac markers are within the reference range. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 15-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parents for evaluation of their “weird” behavior. The parents report that their child tortured their cat to death two weeks ago. Over the past year, they have been accused of stealing a car and setting a fire at their school. They have no history of serious illness. They attend a local high school, and their performance at school is very poor compared to their classmates. They often lose their temper and argue with their teachers. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 2 years. They do not drink alcohol. Their mother has a 10-year history of schizophrenia controlled with medication. On mental status examination, they are oriented to person, place, and time. The pupils are equal and reactive to light. Their speech is normal in rate and rhythm, and their thought process is organized. Short- and long-term memory are intact. Attention and concentration are poor. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

clinical_context: A 27-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department after sustaining a fall from their bicycle 1 hour ago. The patient was on their way to work as they lost their balance, hitting their head on the sidewalk. They had an initial loss of consciousness for a couple of minutes following the accident. They currently have nausea and a headache. They have vomited twice during the last 30 minutes. They have no history of a serious illness. The patient does not smoke or drink alcohol. They have never used illicit drugs. They take no medications. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 50/min, respirations are 10/min, and blood pressure is 160/90 mm Hg. They are oriented to person, place, and time. Their lungs are clear to auscultation. Cardiac examination shows bradycardia but no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. The abdomen is soft and nontender. There is a bruise on the right temporal side of the head. While performing the remainder of the physical examination the patient starts having a seizure. Intravenous lorazepam is administered and they are admitted to the intensive care unit. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 32-year-old patient comes to the emergency department for acute pain in the left eye. They report having awoken in the morning with a foreign body sensation. They had forgotten to remove their contact lenses before sleeping. Following lens removal, they experienced immediate pain, discomfort, and tearing of the left eye. They report that the foreign body sensation persists and that rinsing with water has not improved the pain. They have been wearing contact lenses for 4 years and occasionally forget to remove them at night. They have no history of serious medical illness. On examination, the patient appears distressed with pain and photophobia in the left eye. Administration of a topical anesthetic relieves the pain. Visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes. Ocular motility and pupillary response are normal. The corneal reflex is normal and symmetric in both eyes. Which of the following is most likely to establish the diagnosis in this patient?

A 10-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of high-grade fever, myalgia, and generalized fatigue for 3 days. They returned from a vacation to northern Brazil 4 days ago. They took the appropriate medications and immunizations prior to their visit. There is no family history of serious illness. They appear ill. Their temperature is 39.4°C (103°F), pulse is 110/min and blood pressure is 94/54 mm Hg. Examination shows jaundice of the conjunctivae and skin. The abdomen is soft and nontender; the spleen is palpated 2 to 3 cm below the left costal margin. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL Leukocyte count 4,650/mm3 Platelet count 200,000/mm3 Serum Glucose 56 mg/dL Creatinine 0.8 mg/dL Bilirubin Total 4.7 mg/dL Direct 0.9 mg/dL Lactate dehydrogenase 212 U/L Which of the following is the most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 48-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their spouse because they have become increasingly restless and anxious. Their spouse says that they have seemed sad and irritable for the past 4 months. They lost their job as a store clerk because they often lied to avoid work, and spent most of their days on the phone placing bets on football games. They avoid all family-related events because they have borrowed money from most of their relatives. They are hopeful that their symptoms will improve once they are able to win some of their money back. They previously smoked 8–10 cigarettes daily but quit 1 month ago. They drink beer on the weekends. On examination, they are uncooperative and dismissive. They are mildly tremulous. Neurologic examination is normal. They are oriented to person, place, and time. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department after a fall. They have been seen by the triage nurse but have not been evaluated by a physician. They are heard yelling down the hallway, requesting to speak to “whoever is in charge.” They refuse to talk to the emergency resident and insist on talking to the attending physician despite being informed that the attending is currently resuscitating a patient who was in a car accident. They say that they deserve better treatment because they have made numerous contributions to the field of medicine. When asked about their work, they mention that they were a medical device salesman. They are accompanied by their partner, who appears embarrassed. Their partner claims that they frequently make a scene and apologizes for their behavior. On mental status examination, the patient is oriented to person, place, and time. They appear agitated and speak in short, pressured sentences. There is no disorder of thought process or content. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 20-year-old patient comes to the physician because of recurrent abdominal cramps, bloating, and diarrhea for 4 months. They describe their stools as greasy, foul-smelling, and difficult to flush. During this time they have had a 6-kg (13.2-lb) weight loss. They have no personal or family history of serious illness. Physical examination shows pallor and cheilitis. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin concentration of 11 g/dL. Serum concentrations of electrolytes, urea nitrogen, and creatinine are within the reference range. Test of the stool for occult blood is negative and stool microscopy reveals no pathogens and no leukocytes. Analysis of a 24-hour stool sample shows 12 g of fat. The patient is asked to consume 25 g of d-xylose. Five hours later, its concentration is measured in urine at 2 g (N = > 4 g/5 h). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 3-day history of decreased urine output, progressively worsening bilateral pedal edema, and fatigue. They have a 4-month history of persistent lower back pain. They have hypercholesterolemia and stable angina pectoris. Current medications include atorvastatin, aspirin, and ibuprofen. Their pulse is 80/min, respirations are 16/min, and blood pressure is 150/100 mm Hg. Examination shows periorbital and pedal edema and pallor. There is tenderness of the lumbar spinal vertebrae. Straight leg raise test is negative. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 8.9 mg/dl Serum Urea nitrogen 20 mg/dl Creatinine 2.4 mg/dl Calcium 11.2 mg/dl Alkaline phosphatase 140 U/L X-ray of the spine shows diffuse osteopenia and multiple lytic lesions. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient comes to the physician because of shortness of breath while lying on their back over the past month. During this period, they have also had several episodes of bloody coughing. The patient reports that they had a heart problem when they were a child that was treated with antibiotics. They emigrated to the US from Russia 5 years ago. There is no family history of serious illness. Pulmonary examination shows crackles at both lung bases. Cardiac examination is shown. An ECG shows tachycardia and no P waves. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department 35 minutes after being involved in a high-speed motor vehicle collision. On arrival, they are alert, have mild chest pain, and minimal shortness of breath. They have one episode of vomiting in the hospital. Their temperature is 37.3°C (99.1°F), pulse is 108/min, respirations are 23/min, and blood pressure is 90/70 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 92%. Examination shows multiple abrasions over their trunk and right upper extremity. There are coarse breath sounds over the right lung base. Cardiac examination shows no murmurs, rubs, or gallop. Infusion of 0.9% saline is begun. They subsequently develop increasing shortness of breath. Arterial blood gas analysis on 60% oxygen shows: pH 7.36 pCO2 39 mm Hg pO2 68 mm Hg HCO3- 18 mEq/L O2 saturation 81% An x-ray of the chest shows patchy, irregular infiltrates over the right lung fields. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 6-week history of tingling pain in the sole of their right foot when they raise it above chest level during exercises. They report that they started exercising regularly 2 months ago and that their right calf cramps when they use the incline feature on the treadmill, forcing them to take frequent breaks. The pain completely disappears after resting for a few minutes. They have an 8-year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus. They have smoked two packs of cigarettes daily for 34 years. Their only medication is metformin. Their pulse is 82/min, and blood pressure is 170/92 mm Hg. Straight leg raise test elicits pallor and tingling pain in the right foot. There is no pain in the back. Their muscle strength is normal. Femoral pulses are palpable; right pedal pulses are absent. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parents because of irritable mood that started 5 days ago. Since then, they have been staying up late at night working on a secret project. They are energetic despite sleeping less than 4 hours per day. Their parents report that they seem easily distracted. They are usually very responsible, but this week they spent their paycheck on supplies for their project. They have never had similar symptoms before. In the past, they have had episodes where they felt too fatigued to go to school and slept until 2 pm every day for 2 weeks at a time. During those times, their parents noticed that they cried excessively, were very indecisive, and expressed feelings of worthlessness. Two months ago, they had an asthma exacerbation and were treated with bronchodilators and steroids. They tried cocaine once in high school but have not used it since. Vital signs are within normal limits. On mental status examination, they are irritable but cooperative. Their speech is pressured and their thought process is linear. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old patient comes to the physician for the evaluation of an 8-week history of blood in their stool. Two months ago, they had an episode of bronchitis and were treated with amoxicillin. Since then, they have noticed blood in their stool and on the toilet paper occasionally. The patient has had intermittent constipation for the past 5 years. Six months ago, they had severe left lower quadrant pain and fever that resolved with antibiotic therapy. They underwent a colonoscopy 3 years ago, which did not show any evidence of malignancy. They take levothyroxine for hypothyroidism. They had smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 45 years, but quit smoking 10 years ago. They drink one glass of red wine every night. They appear pale. They are 180 cm (5 ft 11 in) tall and weigh 98 kg (216 lb); BMI is 32 kg/m2. Their temperature is 36°C (96.8°F), pulse is 85/min, and blood pressure is 135/80 mm Hg. Physical examination shows pale conjunctivae. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. The abdomen is soft and nontender with no organomegaly. Digital rectal examination shows no masses. Test of the stool for occult blood is positive. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 11 g/dL Mean corpuscular volume 76 μm3 Red cell distribution width 17% (N = 13–15) Leukocyte count 5,000/mm3 Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department 20 minutes after they sustained a stab wound to their back during an altercation. They report weakness and numbness of the lower extremities. They have no history of serious illness. On arrival, they are alert and cooperative. Their pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 100/65 mm Hg. Examination shows a deep 4-cm laceration on their back next to the vertebral column at the level of the T10 vertebra. Neurologic examination shows right-sided flaccid paralysis with a diminished vibratory sense ipsilaterally, decreased sensation to light touch at the level of their laceration and below, and left-sided loss of hot, cold, and pin-prick sensation at the level of the umbilicus and below. Deep tendon reflexes of their right lower extremity are 4+ and symmetrical. Babinski sign is absent bilaterally. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 16-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parents for evaluation because of extreme irritability, fatigue, and loss of appetite for 3 weeks. Five months ago, their grandfather, whom they were very close to, passed away from chronic lymphocytic leukemia. They used to enjoy playing soccer but quit their soccer team last week. When they come home from school they go straight to bed and sleep for 11–12 hours each night. They previously had good grades, but their teachers report that they have been disrespectful and distracted in class and failed an exam last week. They tried alcohol twice at a party last year and they have never smoked cigarettes. Vital signs are within normal limits. On mental status examination, they avoid making eye contact but cooperate with the exam. Their affect is limited and they describe an irritable mood. They are easily distracted and have a difficult time focusing for an extended conversation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 12-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of fever, malaise, and a painful, itchy rash on the right shoulder for 2 weeks. The patient's parent says the patient's condition has worsened over the past 4 days. They have a history of atopic dermatitis. They have lived with their parent at several public shelters since they separated from their other parent 2 months ago. Their immunizations are up-to-date. There is cervical lymphadenopathy. Laboratory studies show no abnormalities. A photograph of the rash is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old patient comes to the physician because of increasing blurring of vision in both eyes. They say that the blurring has made it difficult to read, although they have noticed that they can read a little better if they hold the book below or above eye level. They also require a bright light to look at objects. They report that their symptoms began 8 years ago and have gradually gotten worse over time. They have hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Current medications include glyburide and lisinopril. When looking at an Amsler grid, they say that the lines in the center appear wavy and bent. An image of the retina, as viewed through fundoscopy is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of a painless skin lesion on their neck. The lesion has gradually become darker in color. Sometimes it is itchy. They also noticed one similar lesion on their lower back. They are a retired gardener. They have smoked half a pack of cigarettes daily for 40 years. Their temperature is 36.7°C (98°F), pulse is 72/min, and blood pressure is 123/78 mm Hg. Physical examination shows a 0.8-cm hyperpigmented papule on their neck and a 0.6-cm hyperpigmented papule on their lower back, both of which have a greasy and wax-like appearance. A photograph of the neck is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 73-year-old patient comes in to the emergency department because of nausea and severe pain in their upper abdomen and right shoulder blade for the past day. They were able to eat a little for breakfast but vomited up the meal a couple of hours later. They have type 2 diabetes mellitus treated with metformin. They have smoked half a pack of cigarettes daily for 40 years and drinks 4 beers every week. They appear acutely distressed. Their temperature is 38.8°C (102°F), pulse is 124/min, and blood pressure is 92/68 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 95%. The abdomen is soft and there is tenderness to palpation of the right upper quadrant with soft crepitus. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 14.3 g/dL Leukocyte count 18,100/mm3 Platelet count 216,000/mm3 Serum Aspartate aminotransferase (AST, SGOT) 41 U/L Alanine aminotransferase (ALT, SGPT) 19 U/L Alkaline phosphatase 110 U/L Total bilirubin 0.9 mg/dL Direct bilirubin 0.2 mg/dL Albumin 4.1 g/dL Ultrasonography of the right upper quadrant shows a gallbladder with an air-filled, thickened wall and no stones in the lumen. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 37-year-old patient comes to the physician because of increasing swelling and pain of their right knee for the past month. They have not had any trauma to the knee or previous problems with their joints. They have hypertension. Their only medication is hydrochlorothiazide. They work as a carpet installer. They drink two to three beers daily. They are 170 cm (5 ft 7 in) tall and weigh 97 kg (214 lb); BMI is 33.6 kg/m2. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 88/min, and blood pressure is 122/82 mm Hg. Examination of the right knee shows swelling and erythema; there is fluctuant edema over the lower part of the patella. The range of flexion is limited because of the pain. The skin over the site of their pain is not warm. There is tenderness on palpation of the patella; there is no joint line tenderness. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old patient comes to the emergency department because of difficulty walking for the past 4 hours. They first noticed their symptoms after getting up this morning and their foot dragging while walking. They feel tired. They have a history of chronic sinusitis. Six months ago, they were diagnosed with asthma. Current medications include an albuterol inhaler and inhaled corticosteroids. Their temperature is 38.9°C (102°F), pulse is 80/min, and their blood pressure is 140/90 mm Hg. Auscultation of their lungs shows diffuse wheezing over bilateral lung fields. Physical examination shows tender subcutaneous nodules on the extensor surfaces of the elbows. There are palpable, non-blanching erythematous lesions on both shins. Dorsiflexion of the right foot is impaired. Sensation to pinprick, light touch, and vibration is decreased over the ulnar aspect of the left forearm. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 11.3 g/dL Leukocyte count 24,500 Segmented neutrophils 48% Eosinophils 29% Lymphocytes 19% Monocytes 4% Platelet count 290,000/mm3 Serum Urea nitrogen 32 mg/dL Creatinine 1.85 mg/dL Urine Blood 2+ Protein 3+ Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 50-year-old patient comes to the physician for the evaluation of recurrent episodes of chest pain, difficulty breathing, and rapid heart beating over the past two months. During this period, they have had a 4-kg (8.8-lb) weight loss, malaise, pain in both knees, and diffuse muscle pain. Five years ago, they were diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B infection and were started on tenofovir. Their temperature is 38°C (100.4°F), pulse is 110/min, and blood pressure is 150/90 mm Hg. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities except for tachycardia. There are several ulcerations around the ankle and calves bilaterally. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 11 g/dL Leukocyte count 14,000/mm3 Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 80 mm/h Serum Perinuclear anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies negative Hepatitis B surface antigen positive Urine Protein +2 RBC 6-7/hpf Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 78-year-old patient comes to the physician for evaluation of progressive hearing loss in both ears over the past year. They have difficulties understanding conversations in crowded places and when more than one person talks at the same time. They have no dizziness, ear discharge, ringing noise, or ear pain. They have a history of hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Medications include enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. Vital signs are within normal limits. Otoscopic examination shows pearly gray, translucent tympanic membranes with a normal light reflex. A vibrating 512 Hz tuning fork is placed on the left mastoid process. Once the patient no longer hears a tone, the fork is held over the ipsilateral ear and the patient reports to hear the tone again. The same test is repeated on the right side with similar results. There is no lateralization when a vibrating 512 Hz tuning fork is placed in the middle of the forehead. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department because they have had abdominal pain and vomiting for the past day. The pain is intermittent, diffuse in nature, and worse after meals. They do not have loose or bloody stools. They have had a nonpruritic rash on their legs and swelling of their ankles for 6 days. They were treated with oral amoxicillin for a sore throat 2 weeks ago. Their immunizations are up-to-date. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination of the lower extremities shows non-blanching, raised erythematous papules. The left ankle joint is swollen and warm, and its range of motion is limited by pain. Abdominal examination shows tenderness to palpation in the left lower quadrant without guarding or rebound. Bowel sounds are normal. Test of the stool for occult blood is positive. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL Leukocyte count 11,800/mm3 Platelet count 431,000/mm3 Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 45 mm/h Serum Glucose 72 mg/dL Creatinine 0.9 mg/dL Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 6-month history of tinnitus and progressive hearing loss in the left ear. They have type 2 diabetes mellitus and Raynaud syndrome. Their current medications include metformin, nifedipine, and a multivitamin. They appear well. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. A vibrating tuning fork is placed on the left mastoid process. Immediately after the patient does not hear a tone, the tuning fork is held over the left ear and they report hearing the tuning fork again. The same test is repeated on the right side and shows the same pattern. The vibration tuning fork is then placed on the middle of the forehead and the patient hears the sound louder in the right ear. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parents because they are concerned with their behavior. They have temper outbursts six or seven times per week, which last anywhere between 5 minutes to half an hour or until they become tired. According to their parent, they scream at others and throw things in anger “when things don't go their way.” They say these outbursts started when they were 6 and a half years old and even between the outbursts, they are constantly irritable. They had been suspended from school three times in the past year for physical aggression, but their grades have remained unaffected. They appear agitated and restless. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. During the mental status examination, they are uncooperative and refuse to answer questions. What is the most likely diagnosis in this child?

A 28-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after being involved in a high-speed motor vehicle collision in which they were the unrestrained driver. On arrival, they are semiconscious and incoherent. They have shortness of breath and are cyanotic. Their pulse is 112/min, respirations are 59/min, and blood pressure is 128/89 mm Hg. Examination shows a 3-cm (1.2-in) laceration on the forehead and multiple abrasions over the thorax and abdomen. There is crepitation on palpation of the thorax on the right. Auscultation of the lung shows decreased breath sounds on the right side. A crunching sound synchronous with the heartbeat is heard best over the precordium. There is dullness on percussion of the right hemithorax. The lips and tongue have a bluish discoloration. There is an open femur fracture on the left. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Arterial blood gas analysis on room air shows: pH 7.31 PCO2 55 mm Hg PO2 42 mm Hg HCO3- 22 mEq/L O2 saturation 76% The patient is intubated and mechanically ventilated. Infusion of 0.9% saline is begun. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old patient comes to the physician because of episodes of watery stools for the past 6 weeks. During this period, they have also had recurrent episodes of reddening of the face, neck, and chest that last up to 30 minutes, especially following alcohol consumption. They have hypertension. They smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 20 years but quit 8 years ago. They drink two glasses of wine daily. Current medications include enalapril. They appear pale. They are 185 cm (6 ft 1 in) tall and weigh 67 kg (147.7 lb); BMI is 19.6 kg/m2. Their temperature is 36.7°C (98°F), pulse is 85/min, and blood pressure is 130/85 mm Hg. Scattered expiratory wheezing is heard throughout both lung fields. Cardiac examination shows no abnormalities. The abdomen is soft and mildly tender. The remainder of the physical examination shows no abnormalities. A complete blood count and serum concentrations of urea nitrogen and creatinine are within the reference range. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 29-year-old patient comes to the physician for the evaluation of progressive loss of vision in their left eye and gradual blurring of vision in their right eye over the past 2 months. They also say that they have had occasional headaches and have noticed a decrease in their sense of smell lately. The patient's only medication is fexofenadine for seasonal allergies. They are 158 cm (5 ft 2 in) tall and weigh 61 kg (135 lbs); BMI is 24.7 kg/m2. Vital signs are within normal limits. Visual acuity is 20/40 in the right eye and there is minimal light perception in the left eye. In the swinging flashlight test, both of their eyes dilate as the light moves from the right to left eye. Fundoscopy shows papilledema in the right optic disc and a pale left optic disc. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 36-year-old patient, gravida 1, para 1, has back pain and numbness in their lower extremities after an emergency cesarean delivery of a healthy 3856-g (8-lb, 8-oz) newborn. They had a placental abruption and lost approximately 2000 ml of blood. During the procedure, they received two units of packed red blood cells and intravenous fluids. They have no history of serious illness and take no medications. They are sexually active with one partner, and they use condoms inconsistently. They are alert and oriented to person, place, and time. Their temperature is 37.2°C (98.9°F), pulse is 90/min, respirations are 15/min, and blood pressure is 94/58 mm Hg. Examination shows decreased sensation to temperature and pinprick below their waist and 0/5 muscle strength in their lower extremities. They feel the vibrations of a tuning fork placed on both of their great toes. Deep tendon reflexes are absent in the lower extremities and 2+ in the upper extremities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 9-year-old patient is brought to their primary care physician because of a 4-month history of early morning headaches and worsening fatigue. The headaches are often accompanied by nausea and sometimes relieved by vomiting. They stopped going to their ballet lessons 2 weeks ago because they were embarrassed about falling frequently and having increasing difficulty performing the steps. Their temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F), pulse is 98/min, and blood pressure is 105/65 mm Hg. They have a broad-based gait. While standing with both feet together and raising their arms, closing their eyes does not affect their balance. They are unable to perform rapid, alternating movements with their hands. An MRI of the brain is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 64-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 7.2-kg (16-lb) weight loss over the past 6 months. For the last 4 weeks, they have also had intermittent constipation and bloating. Four months ago, they spent 2 weeks in Mexico with their child. They have never smoked. They drink one glass of wine daily. They appear thin. Their temperature is 38.3°C (101°F), pulse is 80/min, and blood pressure is 136/78 mm Hg. The lungs are clear to auscultation. The abdomen is distended and the liver is palpable 4 cm below the right costal margin with a hard, mildly tender nodule in the left lobe. Test of the stool for occult blood is positive. Serum studies show: Alkaline phosphatase 67 U/L AST 65 U/L ALT 68 U/L Hepatitis B surface antigen negative Hepatitis C antibody negative A contrast-enhanced CT scan of the abdomen is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 6-month history of muscle weakness. During this period, the patient has had low energy, intermittent nosebleeds, and a 5-kg (11-lb) weight loss. They also report progressive hearing and vision problems. They have a history of pins-and-needles sensation, numbness, and pain in their feet. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows a palpable liver tip 2–3 cm below the right costal margin. There is nontender lymphadenopathy in the groins, axillae, and neck. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 8.8 g/dL White blood cells 6,300/mm3 Platelet count 98,000/mm3 Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 70 mm/h Serum Na+ 136 mmol/L K+ 3.6 mmol/L Cr 1.3 mg/dL Ca2+ 8.6 mg/dL Aspartate aminotransferase 32 U/L Alanine aminotransferase 36 U/L Alkaline phosphatase 100 U/L Lactate dehydrogenase 120 U/L A serum protein electrophoresis exhibits a sharp, narrow spike of monoclonal IgM immunoglobulin. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old patient is brought to the physician for pain and increasing swelling over their scalp for 1 month. They have not had any trauma to the area. There is no family or personal history of serious illness. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows a 3-cm solitary, tender mass over the right parietal bone. X-ray of the skull shows a solitary osteolytic lesion. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 10.9 g/dL Leukocyte count 7300/mm3 Serum Na+ 136 mEq/L K+ 3.7 mEq/L Cl- 103 mEq/L Ca2+ 9.1 mg/dL Glucose 71 mg/dL Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 36-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department for right upper quadrant abdominal pain that began 3 days ago. The pain is nonradiating and has no alleviating or exacerbating factors. They deny any nausea or vomiting. They immigrated from Mexico 6 months ago and currently work at a pet shop. They have been healthy except for 1 week of bloody diarrhea 5 months ago. They are 182 cm (5 ft 11 in) tall and weigh 120 kg (264 lb); BMI is 36 kg/m2. Their temperature is 101.8°F (38.8°C), pulse is 85/min, respirations are 14/min, and blood pressure is 120/75 mm Hg. Lungs are clear to auscultation. They have tenderness to palpation in the right upper quadrant. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 11.7 g/dL Leukocyte Count 14,000/mm Segmented neutrophils 74% Eosinophils 2% Lymphocytes 17% Monocytes 7% Platelet count 140,000/mm3 Serum Na+ 139 mEq/L Cl- 101 mEq/L K+ 4.4 mEq/L HCO3- 25 mEq/L Urea nitrogen 8 mg/dL Creatinine 1.6 mg/dL Total bilirubin 0.4 mg/dL AST 76 U/L ALT 80 U/L Alkaline phosphatase 103 U/L Ultrasonography of the abdomen shows a 4-cm round, hypoechoic lesion in the right lobe of the liver with low-level internal echoes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 36-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a painless lump on their neck for 3 months that has increased in size. They appear healthy. Examination shows a 2.5-cm (1-in) firm, irregular swelling on the left side of the neck that moves with swallowing. There is painless cervical lymphadenopathy. Ultrasound of the neck shows a solitary left lobe thyroid mass with increased vascularity and hyperechogenic punctate regions. A fine needle aspiration biopsy is scheduled for the following week. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 43-year-old patient comes to the physician for evaluation of a headache they have had for the last 6 months. The patient reports that nothing helps to relieve the headache and that it is more severe in the morning. Throughout the last 2 months, they have been unable to maintain an erection and states that their sexual desire is low. There is no personal or family history of serious illness. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 80/min, and blood pressure is 150/90 mm Hg. Examination shows an enlarged nose, forehead, and jaw and widened hands, fingers, and feet. Their hands are sweaty. Their serum glucose concentration is 260 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 14-year-old patient is brought to the physician for the evaluation of back pain for the past six months. The pain is worse with exercise and when reclining. They attend high school and are on the swim team. They also state that they lift weights on a regular basis. They have not had any trauma to the back or any previous problems with their joints. They have no history of serious illness. Their parent has a disc herniation. Palpation of the spinous processes at the lumbosacral area shows that two adjacent vertebrae are displaced and are at different levels. Muscle strength is normal. Sensation to pinprick and light touch is intact throughout. When the patient is asked to walk, a waddling gait is noted. Passive raising of either the right or left leg causes pain radiating down the ipsilateral leg. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 3-week history of abdominal pain, loose, non-bloody stools, and intermittent nausea. They also report intermittent fever. They have not had vomiting, tenesmus, or rectal pain. They have no history of serious illness and take no medications. Their vital signs are within normal limits. Rectal exam is unremarkable. Laboratory studies show a leukocyte count of 15,200/mm3 and an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 44 mm/h. Test of the stool for occult blood and stool studies for infection are negative. A CT scan of the abdomen shows mural thickening and surrounding fat stranding of discrete regions of the terminal ileum and transverse colon. A colonoscopy is performed and biopsy specimens of the affected areas of the colon are taken. Which of the following findings is most specific for this patient's most likely diagnosis?

A 54-year-old patient comes to the physician for the evaluation of difficulty swallowing of both solids and liquids for 1 month. During the past 5 months, they have also had increased weakness of their hands and legs. They sail regularly and are unable to hold the ropes as tightly as before. Ten years ago, they were involved in a motor vehicle collision. Examination shows atrophy of the tongue. Muscle strength is decreased in the right upper and lower extremities. There is muscle stiffness in the left lower extremity. Deep tendon reflexes are 1+ in the right upper and lower extremities, 3+ in the left upper extremity, and 4+ in the left lower extremity. Plantar reflex shows an extensor response on the left foot. Sensation to light touch, pinprick, and vibration is intact. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 31-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department because of fever and increasing confusion for the past day. They have bipolar disorder with psychotic features and hypothyroidism. Current medications are lithium, haloperidol, and levothyroxine. They drink one beer with dinner every night. Their speech is confused and they are oriented to person only. Their temperature is 40°C (104°F), pulse is 124/min, and blood pressure is 160/110 mm Hg. They appear acutely ill. Examination shows diaphoresis and muscle rigidity. Deep tendon reflexes are 1+ bilaterally. There is minor rigidity of the neck with full range of motion. Their lungs are clear to auscultation. The abdomen is soft and nontender. Their leukocyte count is 15,100/mm3 and serum creatine kinase activity is 1100 U/L. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old patient comes to the emergency department because of recurrent episodes of fatigue, palpitations, nausea, and diaphoresis over the past 6 months. The episodes have become more frequent in the last 2 weeks and they have missed work several times because of them. Their symptoms usually improve after they drink some juice and rest. They have had a 2-kg (4.5-lb) weight gain in the past 6 months. They have a history of bipolar disorder, hypertension, and asthma. Their sister has type 2 diabetes mellitus and their mother has a history of medullary thyroid carcinoma. Their medications include lithium, hydrochlorothiazide, aspirin, and a budesonide inhaler. Their temperature is 36.3°C (97.3°F), pulse is 92/min and regular, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 118/65 mm Hg. Abdominal examination shows no abnormalities. Serum studies show: Na+ 145 mEq/L K+ 3.9 mEq/L Cl- 103 mEq/L Calcium 9.2 mg/dL Glucose 88 mg/dL Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 5-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their parent because of multiple episodes of nausea and vomiting that last about 2 hours. During this period, they have had 6–8 episodes of bilious vomiting and abdominal pain. The vomiting was preceded by fatigue. The patient feels well between these episodes. They have missed several days of school and have been hospitalized 2 times during the past 6 months for dehydration due to similar episodes of vomiting and nausea. The patient has lived with their parent since their parents divorced 8 months ago. Their immunizations are up-to-date. They are at the 60th percentile for height and 30th percentile for weight. They appear emaciated. Their temperature is 36.8°C (98.8°F), pulse is 99/min, and blood pressure is 82/52 mm Hg. Examination shows dry mucous membranes. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Abdominal examination shows a soft abdomen with mild diffuse tenderness with no guarding or rebound. The remainder of the physical examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 13-month-old patient is brought to the physician for the evaluation of rectal bleeding that occurred earlier that morning. The patient has also had several itchy and red skin lesions that started on their scalp and spread downwards. The parents report that their child has had six episodes of bilateral otitis media since birth. Their immunizations are up-to-date. They are at the 3rd percentile for height and weight. Their vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows several eczematous lesions over the scalp, neck, and upper and lower extremities, as well as multiple red spots that do not blanch on pressure. The remainder of the physical examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 9.4 g/dL Leukocyte count 11,500/mm3 Platelet count 30,000/mm3 Prothrombin time 14 sec Partial thromboplastin time 33 sec Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 2-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parent after they noticed multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on their abdomen. The child attends daycare three times per week, and this past week one child was reported to have similar lesions. Their immunizations are up-to-date. Their sibling had chickenpox one month ago. They are at the 50th percentile for height and the 60th percentile for weight. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows several skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department after being involved in a rear-end collision, in which they were the restrained driver of the back car. On arrival, they are alert and active. They report pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin. Temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 116/min, respirations are 19/min, and blood pressure is 132/79 mm Hg. Physical examination shows tenderness over both knee caps. The right groin is tender to palpation. The right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 63-year-old patient comes to the emergency department because of a 1-day history of progressive blurring and darkening of their vision in the right eye. Upon waking up in the morning, they suddenly started seeing multiple dark streaks. They have migraines and type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed at their last health maintenance examination 20 years ago. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 40 years. Their only medication is sumatriptan. Their vitals are within normal limits. Ophthalmologic examination shows visual acuity of 20/40 in the left eye and 20/100 in the right eye. The fundus is obscured and difficult to visualize on fundoscopic examination of the right eye. The red reflex is diminished on the right. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parents for a well-child visit. During their last well-child visit 9 months ago, the patient had not begun talking. The parents report that their child frequently avoids eye contact and has no friends at daycare. They were born at term and have been healthy except for an episode of otitis media 6 months ago, which was treated with amoxicillin. Their immunizations are up-to-date. They are at the 95 percentile for height, 20 percentile for weight, and 95 percentile for head circumference. They appear shy. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 120/min, and blood pressure is 100/55 mm Hg. Examination shows elongated facial features and large ears. The patient does not speak. They do not follow instruction to build a stack of 2 blocks. Throughout the examination, they continually open and close a purse and do not maintain eye contact. Which of the following findings is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 66-year-old patient comes to the emergency department because of a 1-day history of chest pain, palpitations, and dyspnea on exertion. They had a similar episode 3 days ago and were diagnosed with an inferior wall myocardial infarction. They were admitted and a percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty was successfully done that day. A fractional flow reserve test during the procedure showed complete resolution of the stenosis. Laboratory tests including serum glucose, lipids, and blood count were within normal limits. They were discharged the day after the procedure on a drug regimen of aspirin, simvastatin, and isosorbide dinitrate. At the time of discharge, they had no chest pain or dyspnea. Presently, their vitals are normal and ECG at rest shows new T-wave inversion. Which of the following is the most reliable test for rapidly establishing the diagnosis in this patient?

A 71-year-old patient comes to the physician accompanied by their spouse because of a 6-month history of worsening episodic upper abdominal pain and an 8-kg (17.6-lb) weight loss. The pain is dull, nonradiating, worse after eating, and occasionally associated with bloating and diarrhea. Their symptoms have not improved despite 4 weeks of treatment with omeprazole. They attribute their weight loss to recently eating very small portions and avoiding fatty foods. They have hypertension and hypercholesterolemia. They underwent a coronary artery bypass graft operation for coronary artery disease 8 years ago. Current medications include lisinopril, metoprolol, atorvastatin, and aspirin. They have smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for 20 years and drinks 1–2 beers daily. Their pulse is 79/min and blood pressure is 138/89 mm Hg. Examination shows a soft abdomen without tenderness to palpation or guarding. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 53-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department following an episode of loss of consciousness 1 hour ago. They had just finished micturating, when they fell down. Their spouse heard the noise and found them unconscious on the floor. They regained consciousness after 30 seconds and were able to talk normally with their spouse immediately. There was no urinary incontinence. On arrival, they are alert and oriented. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. Neurologic examination shows no focal findings. Serum concentrations of glucose, creatinine, and electrolytes are within the reference range. An electrocardiogram shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 3-day history of a swollen right knee. Over the past several weeks, they have had similar episodes affecting the right knee and sometimes also the left elbow, in which the swelling lasted an average of 5 days. They have a history of a rash that subsided 2 months ago. They live in Connecticut with their partner and work as a landscaper. Their temperature is 37.8°C (100°F), pulse is 90/min, respirations are 12/min, and blood pressure is 110/75 mm Hg. Physical examination shows a tender and warm right knee; range of motion is limited by pain. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Their hematocrit is 44%, leukocyte count is 10,300/mm3, and platelet count is 145,000/mm3. Serum electrolyte concentrations are within normal limits. Arthrocentesis is performed and the synovial fluid is cloudy. Gram stain is negative. Analysis of the synovial fluid shows a leukocyte count of 70,000/mm3 and 80% neutrophils. Serologic testing confirms the diagnosis. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

A 23-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their partner because of acute agitation and bizarre behavior. The partner reports that, over the past 3 months, the patient has become withdrawn and stopped pursuing hobbies that they used to enjoy. One month ago, they lost their job because they stopped going to work. During this time, they have barely left their apartment because they believe that the FBI is spying on them and controlling their mind. They used to smoke marijuana occasionally in high school but quit 5 years ago. Physical and neurologic examinations show no abnormalities. On mental status examination, they are confused and suspicious with marked psychomotor agitation. Their speech is disorganized and their affect is labile. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old patient is brought to the physician because their parent is concerned about their lack of appetite. They have had a 4-kg (8.8-lb) weight loss over the past 4 months. The patient states that they do not “feel like eating so much”. Over the last year their academic performance in school has decreased and they have had a lot of disputes with their parents concerning their future. Their parent says that they have also become more nervous and restless. Their grandmother had a problem with their thyroid. They are sexually active with two partners and use condoms inconsistently. They are at 60th percentile for height and at 15th percentile for weight. They appear thin. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 104/min, and blood pressure is 135/80 mm Hg. The pupils are 9 mm large, round and minimally reactive to light. Deep tendon reflexes are 2+ bilaterally. There is fine tremor of their hands. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient comes to the physician because of an 8-month history of worsening difficulties swallowing food and retrosternal chest discomfort. They report that they sometimes have a feeling of “food getting stuck” in their throat and hear a “gurgling sound” from their throat while eating. They say that they occasionally cough up pieces of undigested food. They have noticed a bad taste in their mouth and bad breath. They have not had fever or weight loss. They have been visiting Mexico every year for the past 7 years. They have Raynaud disease treated with nifedipine. Their father died because of gastric cancer. They had smoked one-half pack of cigarettes daily for 20 years but stopped 25 years ago. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Their hemoglobin concentration is 14 g/dL, leukocyte count is 9800/mm3, and platelet count is 215,000/mm3. An ECG shows sinus rhythm with no evidence of ischemia. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 25-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 4-day history of bloody stools. During this time, they have not had nausea, vomiting, abdominal cramps, or pain while defecating. They have had recurrent episodes of non-bloody diarrhea for the past 6 months. Their father died of colon cancer at the age of 39 years. Their vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows small, painless bony swellings on the mandible, forehead, and right shin. There are multiple non-tender, subcutaneous nodules with central black pores present over the trunk and face. Fundoscopic examination shows multiple, oval, darkly pigmented lesions on the retina. Colonoscopy shows approximately 150 colonic polyps. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 64-year-old patient comes to the physician because of several episodes of dizziness during the last month. The episodes last between 30–40 seconds and during the episodes they feel as though they are spinning. Episodes usually occur immediately after lying down or suddenly sitting up from a reclined position. They also sometimes happen when they suddenly turn their head to look at something. They have no nausea. Last month, they had an upper respiratory tract infection that resolved spontaneously. They have hypertension treated with hydrochlorothiazide. Otoscopic examination shows no abnormalities. There is no lateralization when a vibrating 512 Hz tuning fork is placed in the middle of the forehead. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 63-year-old patient comes to the physician because of increasing generalized fatigue for 3 months. They are having more difficulty with keeping up with their activities of daily living and have lost 2.5 kg (5.5 lb) over the past month. They have hypertension and hyperlipidemia. They do not smoke and drinks two to three beers on weekends. Their medications include lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, and atorvastatin. Their temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 85/min, respirations are 15/min, and blood pressure is 125/73 mm Hg. Examination shows pale conjunctivae. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Their hematocrit is 27.3%, leukocyte count is 4500/mm3, and platelet count is 102,000/mm3. A peripheral blood smear shows numerous blast cells that stain positive for myeloperoxidase, CD33, and CD34. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old patient comes to the physician because of recurrent episodes of nausea and abdominal discomfort for the past 4 months. The discomfort is located in the upper abdomen and sometimes occurs after eating, especially after a big meal. They have tried to go for a walk after dinner to help with digestion, but their complaints have only increased. For the past 3 weeks they have also had symptoms while climbing the stairs to their apartment. They have type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and stage 2 peripheral arterial disease. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the past 45 years. They drink one to two beers daily and occasionally more on weekends. Their current medications include metformin, enalapril, and aspirin. They are 168 cm (5 ft 6 in) tall and weigh 126 kg (278 lb); BMI is 45 kg/m2. Their temperature is 36.4°C (97.5°F), pulse is 78/min, and blood pressure is 148/86 mm Hg. On physical examination, the abdomen is soft and nontender with no organomegaly. Foot pulses are absent bilaterally. An ECG shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 13-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of a 1-month history of progressive difficulty breathing through their nose and a 2-week history of recurrent severe nosebleeds. When they hold the right nostril shut, they are unable to breathe nasally and their sense of smell is reduced. They have a 6-year history of asthma, which is well controlled with inhaled albuterol. Vital signs are within normal limits. Nasal inspection shows a pink, lobulated mass filling the left nasal cavity. The septum is deviated to the right side. The mass bleeds on touch. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

An 8-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parents because of difficulty sleeping. One to two times per week for the past 2 months, they have woken up frightened in the middle of the night, yelling and crying. They have not seemed confused after waking up, and they are consolable and able to fall back asleep in their parents' bed. The following day, they seem more tired than usual at school. They recall that they had a bad dream and look for ways to delay bedtime in the evenings. They have met all their developmental milestones to date. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old college student comes to the physician for a sudden loss of visual acuity of their right eye. They noticed that they were unable to read the time on the alarm clock when they woke up in the morning. When they close their right eye, they are able to see sharply. When they close their left eye, they have blurry double vision. They do not recall trauma to their eye but have been working long nights on their honors thesis. They have a history of occasional shoulder luxation. They are 180 cm (5 ft 11 in) tall, and weigh 62 kg (136 lbs); their BMI is 19.1 kg/m2. Their vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, slender and long fingers are noted. They have several flat, demarcated brownish nevi on their left cheek. Ocular examination shows upward temporal subluxation of their right lens. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 45-year-old patient comes to the physician because of right foot pain for 3 months. They have a burning sensation in the plantar area between the third and fourth metatarsals that radiates to the third and fourth digits. They had a right distal radius fracture that was treated with a splint and physical therapy three months ago. They are an account executive and wear high heels to work every day. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination of the right lower extremity shows intact skin. The posterior tibial and dorsalis pedis pulses are palpable. When pressure is applied to the sole of the foot between the metatarsal heads the patient feels pain and there is an audible click. Tapping on the affected area causes pain that shoots into the third and fourth digits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old patient comes to the physician for the evaluation of recurrent episodes of nosebleeds over the past 6 months. The nosebleeds occur spontaneously and stop after 10 minutes after pinching the nose at the nostrils. They have no history of serious illness except for prolonged bleeding following wisdom teeth extraction 2 years ago. They do not smoke or drink alcohol. They take no medications. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination of the nose shows no abnormalities. There are several bruises on the lower extremities. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 15 g/dL Leukocyte count 6,000/mm3 Platelet count 220,000/mm3 Bleeding time 9 minutes Prothrombin time 13 sec Partial thromboplastin time 55 sec Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 59-year-old patient is brought to the emergency room by their spouse. Thirty minutes ago, they were carrying heavy moving boxes from their house to a truck when they felt short of breath and suddenly lost consciousness. Their spouse states that they fell to the ground and were unresponsive for 15 seconds before they regained consciousness. They were not confused after this episode. They do not have chest pain. On questioning, they recall experiencing episodic shortness of breath and chest tightness while playing tennis over the past year. These symptoms resolved with rest. They have no personal history of serious illness and take no medication. Vital signs are within normal limits. Their temperature is 36.7°C (98°F), heart rate is 95/min and pulse is delayed but regular, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 104/80 mm Hg. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 59-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when they climb stairs and during the night. They have not had chest pain or palpitations. Eight weeks ago, they had fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion. They have a 10-year history of hypertension. They have smoked half a pack of cigarettes daily for 16 years. Their only medication is enalapril. Their pulse is 78/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 145/95 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 96%. Diffuse end-expiratory wheezes are heard on pulmonary auscultation. An x-ray of the chest shows no abnormalities. Spirometry shows an FEV1:FVC ratio of 65% and an FEV1 of 60%. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 4-month history of persistent cough productive of white phlegm. They cough consistently throughout the day, and they have not noticed any particular triggers that make it worse. They have also recently experienced some shortness of breath with exertion. They have not had any weight loss, fever, or chills. They had similar symptoms last year, which lasted about 6 months. They have hypertension, for which they take amlodipine. They have worked in construction for the past 10 years. They have smoked a pack of cigarettes per day for 30 years. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows an end-expiratory wheeze throughout all lung zones. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 43-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of progressive muscle pain and stiffness that worsens with exercise. They also have difficulty climbing stairs, getting out of chairs, and putting things on shelves or in cupboards. They have had constipation, occasional headaches, and a 9-kg (20-lb) weight gain during the past year. They have hypertension controlled with atenolol and amlodipine. They have used calamine lotion for the past 6 months for dry skin. Their pulse is 80/min and their blood pressure is 138/76 mm Hg. Physical examination shows weakness of the proximal muscle groups. They have delayed tendon reflex relaxation, with a mounding of the muscle surface occurring just before relaxation. Creatine kinase level is 3,120 U/L. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 60-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of a slowly enlarging painless ulcer on their lower lip. One year ago they had a painful rash near their upper lip that resolved completely with acyclovir therapy. They have a 10-year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus treated with metformin. They have worked in construction for the past 33 years. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 35 years. Examination shows a 0.5 x 0.5 cm nontender ulcer with everted edges on the midline of their lower lip. The erythematous ulcer bleeds upon palpation. They have numerous moles of varying sizes all over their body. There are no palpable cervical lymph nodes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 13-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of progressive left leg pain for 2 months, which has started to interfere with their sleep. Their parent has been giving them ibuprofen at night for “growing pains,” but their symptoms have not improved. One week before the pain started, the patient was hit in the thigh by a baseball, which caused their leg to become red and swollen for several days. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows marked tenderness along the left mid-femur. Their gait is normal. Laboratory studies show a leukocyte count of 21,000/mm3 and an ESR of 68 mm/h. An x-ray of the left lower extremity shows multiple lytic lesions in the middle third of the femur, and the surrounding cortex is covered by several layers of new bone. A biopsy of the left femur shows small round blue cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old patient comes to the physician because of progressive fatigue and lower back pain for the past 4 months. The back pain worsened significantly after they had a minor fall while doing yard work the previous day. For the past year, they have had a feeling of incomplete emptying of their bladder after voiding. Their vital signs are within normal limits.
