Examination shows bilateral paravertebral muscle spasm, severe tenderness over the second lumbar vertebra, and mild tenderness over the lower thoracic vertebrae. Neurologic examination shows no abnormalities. Their hemoglobin is 10.5 g/dl, alkaline phosphatase is 110 U/L, and serum calcium is 11.1 mg/dl. An x-ray of the skull is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 67-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 3-week history of fatigue and worsening back and abdominal pain. During this period, they have also had excessive night sweats and a 4.6-kg (10-lb) weight loss. They have had swelling of the neck for 3 days. They do not smoke or drink alcohol. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows a 4-cm, supraclavicular, nontender, enlarged and fixed lymph node. The spleen is palpated 2 cm below the left costal margin. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 10.4 g/dL Mean corpuscular volume 87 μm3 Leukocyte count 5,200/mm3 Platelet count 190,000/mm3 Serum Lactate dehydrogenase 310 U/L A CT scan of the thorax and abdomen shows massively enlarged paraaortic, axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Histopathologic examination of an excised cervical lymph node shows lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department because of sudden loss of vision in their right eye that occurred 50 minutes ago. They do not have eye pain. They had several episodes of loss of vision in the past, but their vision improved following treatment with glucocorticoids. They have coronary artery disease, hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and multiple sclerosis. They underwent a left carotid endarterectomy 3 years ago. They had a myocardial infarction 5 years ago. Current medications include aspirin, metoprolol, lisinopril, atorvastatin, metformin, glipizide, and weekly intramuscular beta-interferon injections. Their temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F), pulse is 80/min, and blood pressure is 155/88 mm Hg. Examination shows 20/50 vision in the left eye and no perception of light in the right eye. The direct pupillary reflex is brisk in the left eye and absent in the right eye. The indirect pupillary reflex is brisk in the right eye but absent in the left eye. Intraocular pressure is 18 mm Hg in the right eye and 16 mm Hg in the left eye. A white, 1-mm ring is seen around the circumference of the cornea in both eyes. Fundoscopic examination of the right eye shows a pale, white retina with a bright red area within the macula. The optic disc appears normal. Fundoscopic examination of the left eye shows a few soft and hard exudates in the superior and nasal retinal quadrants. The optic disc and macula appear normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a progressive swelling in their mouth that they first noticed 5 years ago. Initially, the swelling was asymptomatic but has now caused some difficulty while chewing food for the past month. They have no pain. They have not undergone any dental procedures in the past 5 years. They have bronchial asthma. Their only medication is an albuterol inhaler. They appear healthy. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 70/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. Examination shows a 1.5-cm smooth, unilobular, bony hard, nontender mass in the midline of the hard palate. There is no cervical or submandibular lymphadenopathy. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 37-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department 15 minutes after falling down a flight of stairs. On arrival, they have shortness of breath, right-sided chest pain, right upper quadrant abdominal pain, and right shoulder pain. They are otherwise healthy. They take no medications. They appear pale. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 115/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 85/45 mm Hg. Examination shows several ecchymoses over the right chest. There is tenderness to palpation over the right chest wall and right upper quadrant of the abdomen. Bowel sounds are normal. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. Neck veins are flat. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 66-year-old patient has new, intermittent upper abdominal discomfort that worsens when they walk around. They also have new shortness of breath that resolves with rest. There were no complications during surgery or during the immediate postsurgical period. Ambulation was restarted on the first postoperative day. They have type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 25 years. Prior to admission, their medications included metformin, simvastatin, and lisinopril. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 80/min, respirations are 16/min, and blood pressure is 129/80 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 98%. The abdomen is soft and shows two healing surgical scars with moderate serous discharge. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. An ECG at rest shows no abnormalities. Cardiac enzyme levels are within the reference range. An x-ray of the chest and abdominal ultrasonography show no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 46-year-old obese patient comes to the emergency room because of paresthesias in their feet and a hypopigmented skin lesion on their knee that they first noticed 6 weeks ago. They have also had fever, fatigue, and malaise for the last week. They have a history of chronic autoimmune thyroiditis for which they take levothyroxine. They immigrated from Indonesia 3 years ago to join their family in the United States. Their temperature is 38.7°C (101.7°F) and blood pressure is 122/84 mm Hg. Physical exam shows a well-defined hypopigmented skin lesion approximately 3 cm in diameter over the anterior aspect of the right knee. The area has no hair growth and remains dry although they are diaphoretic. There is diminished sensation to light touch and pinprick in the skin lesion when compared to surrounding skin. There is reduced light touch sensation in the big toes bilaterally. After obtaining a skin biopsy of the lesion to confirm the diagnosis, which of the following is the most appropriate initial pharmacotherapy?

A 23-year-old patient comes to the physician because of lightening of their skin on both hands, under their eyes, and on their neck for 2 years. During this period the lesions slowly grew in size. There is no itchiness or pain. They regularly visit their family in India. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows sharply demarcated, depigmented skin patches on the dorsum of both hands, in the periocular region, and on the neck. Sensation of the skin is intact. The lesions fluorescence blue-white under Wood's lamp. Which of the following findings is most likely to be associated with this patient's diagnosis?

A 71-year-old patient comes to their doctor because they are having trouble staying awake in the evening. Over the past year, they have noticed that they get tired unusually early in the evenings and have trouble staying awake through dinner. They also experience increased daytime sleepiness, fatigue, and difficulty concentrating. They typically go to bed around 9 PM and get out of bed between 2 and 3 AM. They do not have any trouble falling asleep. They take 30-minute to 1-hour daytime naps approximately 3 times per week. They have no history of severe illness and do not take any medication. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient comes to the physician because of worsening abdominal pain over the last several months. They have also had recent feelings of sadness and a lack of motivation at work, where they are employed as a computer programmer. They deny suicidal thoughts. They have a history of multiple kidney stones. They have a family history of thyroid cancer in their father and uncle, who both underwent thyroidectomy before age 30. Their temperature is 37°C (98°F), blood pressure is 138/86 mm Hg, and pulse is 87/min. Physical examination shows diffuse tenderness over the abdomen and obesity but is otherwise unremarkable. Serum studies show: Na+ 141 mEq/L K+ 3.6 mEq/L Glucose 144 mg/dL Ca2+ 12.1 mg/dL Albumin 4.1 g/dL PTH 226 pg/mL (normal range 12–88 pg/mL) Results of a RET gene test return abnormal. The physician refers them to an endocrine surgeon. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

Three days after undergoing coronary bypass surgery, a 67-year-old patient becomes unresponsive and hypotensive. They are intubated, mechanically ventilated, and a central line is inserted. Vasopressin and noradrenaline infusions are begun. A Foley catheter is placed. Six days later, they have high unrelenting fevers. They are currently receiving noradrenaline via an infusion pump. Their temperature is 39.6° (102.3°F), pulse is 113/min, and blood pressure is 90/50 mm Hg. Examination shows a sternal wound with surrounding erythema; there is no discharge from the wound. Crackles are heard at both lung bases. Cardiac examination shows an S3 gallop. Abdominal examination shows no abnormalities. A Foley catheter is present. Their hemoglobin concentration is 10.8 g/dL, leukocyte count is 21,700/mm3, and platelet count is 165,000/mm3. Samples for blood culture are drawn simultaneously from the central line and peripheral IV line. Blood cultures from the central line show coagulase-negative cocci in clusters on the 8th postoperative day, and those from the peripheral venous line show coagulase-negative cocci in clusters on the 10th postoperative day. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 19-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 2 day history of blood-speckled stools and a protruding rectal mass. They have no abdominal pain, altered bowel habits, or fever. Their mother has inflammatory bowel disease. Their vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows multiple, small, hyperpigmented maculae on the lips, buccal mucosa, palms, and soles. The abdomen is soft with no organomegaly. Rectal examination shows a 4-cm pedunculated polyp with superficial excoriations on the mucosa. A colonoscopy shows 14 polyps. A biopsy shows hamartomatous mucosal polyps. This patient's diagnosis is most likely associated with which of the following conditions?

A 32-year-old patient comes to the physician because of flank pain, myalgia, and reddish discoloration of their urine for the past 2 days. One week ago, they had a fever and a sore throat and were prescribed antibiotics. They are otherwise healthy and have no history of serious illness. Their temperature is 37.9°C (100.2°F), pulse is 70/min, and blood pressure is 128/75 mm Hg. Physical examination shows a soft abdomen and no costovertebral angle tenderness. Examination of the mouth and pharynx shows no abnormalities. There is a faint maculopapular rash over the trunk and extremities. Serum creatinine is 2.4 mg/dL. Urinalysis shows: Protein 2+ Blood 2+ RBC 20–30/hpf WBC 12/hpf Bacteria none Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old patient is brought to the physician for worsening mental status over the past 2 months. Their partner reports they were initially experiencing lapses in memory and over the past 3 weeks they have begun having difficulties performing activities of daily living. Yesterday, they became lost heading to the post office down the street. They have hypertension treated with lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide. Vital signs are within normal limits. They are alert but verbally uncommunicative. Muscle strength is normal. Reflexes are 2+ in bilateral upper and lower extremities. They have diffuse involuntary muscle jerking that can be provoked by loud noises. Mental status examination shows a blunt affect. A complete blood count and serum concentrations of glucose, creatine, and electrolytes are within the reference range. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old patient comes to the physician for the evaluation of blindness in their right eye that suddenly started 1 hour ago. They have no feeling of pain, pressure, or sensation of a foreign body in the right eye. They have a history of major depressive disorder treated with fluoxetine. The patient attends college and states that they have had a lot of stress lately due to relationship problems with their partner. They do not smoke or drink alcohol. They do not use illicit drugs. They appear anxious. Their vital signs are within normal limits. Ophthalmologic examination shows a normal-appearing eye with no redness. Slit lamp examination and fundoscopy show no abnormalities. A visual field test shows nonspecific visual field defects. An MRI of the brain shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 10-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department for the evaluation of one episode of vomiting and severe headache since this morning. Their parent says they also had difficulty getting dressed on their own. They have not had any trauma. The patient appears nervous. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 100/min, and blood pressure is 185/125 mm Hg. They are confused and oriented only to person. Ophthalmic examination shows bilateral optic disc swelling. There is an abdominal bruit that is best heard at the right costovertebral angle. A complete blood count is within normal limits. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 17-year-old patient is brought to the physician for the evaluation of fatigue for the past 6 months. During this period, they have had a 5-kg (11-lbs) weight loss. They state that they have no friends. When they are not in school, they spend most of their time in bed. They have no history of serious illness. Their parent has major depressive disorder. They appear pale and thin. They are at 25th percentile for height, 10th percentile for weight, and 20th percentile for BMI; their BMI is 19.0. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 65/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. Examination shows dry skin, brittle nails, and calluses on the knuckles. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 12.3 g/dL Serum Na+ 133 mEq/L Cl- 90 mEq/L K+ 3.2 mEq/L HCO3- 30 mEq/L Ca+2 7.8 mg/dL Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old patient comes to the physician because they feel sad and have had frequent, brief episodes of crying for the last month. During this period, they sleep in every morning and spend most of their time in bed playing video games or reading. They have not been spending time with friends but still attend a weekly book club and continue to plan their annual family reunion. They stopped going to the gym, eat more, and have gained 4 kg (8.8 lb) over the past 4 weeks. Three weeks ago, they also started to smoke marijuana a few times a week. They drink one glass of wine daily and do not smoke cigarettes. They are currently unemployed; they lost their job as a physical therapist 3 months ago. Their vital signs are within normal limits. On mental status examination, they are calm, alert, and oriented to person, place, and time. Their mood is depressed; their speech is organized, logical, and coherent. They deny suicidal thoughts. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 54-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a painful skin lesion on their right leg for 1 month. It initially started out as a small red spot but has rapidly increased in size during this period. They remember an ant bite on their leg prior to the lesion occurring. They were treated for anterior uveitis 8 months ago with corticosteroids. They have Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension. Current medications include insulin, mesalamine, enalapril, and aspirin. They returned from Wisconsin after visiting their child 2 months ago. Their temperature is 37.6°C (98°F), pulse is 98/min, and blood pressure is 126/88 mm Hg. Examination shows pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities. There is a 4-cm tender ulcerative lesion on the anterior right leg with a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders. There are dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs. Femoral and pedal pulses are palpated bilaterally. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of a generalized rash for 3 days. During this period, they have had severe itching and were not able to sleep well. They have also had fever, headache, and some muscle pain. Five days ago, they had a runny nose which subsided with over-the-counter medications. They returned from a camping trip 1 week ago. They attend a daycare center. The patient is at the 55th percentile for height and at the 50th percentile for weight. Their temperature is 38.2°C (100.7°F), pulse is 97/min, and blood pressure is 96/60 mm Hg. Examination of the skin shows several macules, papules, and crusted lesions over their face, trunk, and extremities. There are a few fluid-filled vesicles over their abdomen and back. There is no cervical lymphadenopathy. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of watery discharge from their right eye for 2 weeks. They and their parents, who are refugees from Sudan, arrived in Texas a month ago. Their immunization status is not known. They are at the 25th percentile for weight and the 50th percentile for height. Their temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), pulse is 90/min, and respirations are 18/min. Examination of the right eye shows matting of the eyelashes. Everting the right eyelid shows hyperemia, follicles, and papillae on the upper tarsal conjunctiva. Slit-lamp examination of the right eye shows follicles in the limbic region and the bulbar conjunctiva. There is corneal haziness with neovascularization at the 12 o'clock position. Examination of the left eye is unremarkable. Direct ophthalmoscopy of both eyes shows no abnormalities. Right pre-auricular lymphadenopathy is present. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 33-year-old patient comes to the emergency department because of repeated episodes of severe headache for the past 3 days. They are currently having their 2nd episode of the day. They usually have their first episode in the mornings. The pain is severe and localized to their right forehead and right eye. They had similar symptoms last summer. They work as an analyst for a large hedge fund management company and spend the majority of their time at the computer. They have been under a lot of stress because of overdue paperwork. They also have chronic shoulder pain. They have been using indomethacin every 6 hours for the pain but have had no relief. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 15 years. They appear restless. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows drooping of the right eyelid, tearing of the right eye, and rhinorrhea. The right pupil is 2 mm and the left pupil is 4 mm. There is localized tenderness to their right supraspinatus muscle. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after being involved in a motorcycle accident. They lost control at high speed and were thrown forward onto the handlebars. On arrival, they are alert and responsive. They have abdominal pain and superficial lacerations on their left arm. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows a tender, erythematous area over their epigastrium. The abdomen is soft and non-distended. A CT scan of the abdomen shows no abnormalities. Treatment with analgesics is begun, the lacerations are cleaned and dressed, and the patient is discharged home after 2 hours of observation. Four days later, the patient returns to the emergency department with gradually worsening upper abdominal pain, fever, poor appetite, and vomiting. Their pulse is 91/min and blood pressure is 135/82 mm Hg. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their mother because she is worried about their strange behavior. Over the past 3 years, they have been dressing all in black and wears a long black coat, even in the summer. The mother reports that her child has always had difficulties fitting in. They do not have any friends and spend most of their time in their room playing online games. They are anxious at college because they are uncomfortable around other people, and their academic performance is poor. Rather than doing their coursework, they spend most of their time reading up on paranormal phenomena, especially demons. They say that they have never seen any demons, but sometimes there are signs of their presence. For example, a breeze in an enclosed room is likely the “breath of a demon”. Mental status examination shows laborious speech. The patient avoids eye contact. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old patient comes to the emergency department for right wrist pain and swelling 2 hours after falling on an outstretched hand while playing softball. The pain worsened when they attempted to pitch after the fall. They have eczema and type 1 diabetes mellitus. Current medications include insulin and topical clobetasol. They appear uncomfortable. Examination shows multiple lichenified lesions over their forearms. The right wrist is swollen and tender; range of motion is limited by pain. There is tenderness to palpation in the area between the tendons of the abductor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis brevis, and extensor pollicis longus muscle. The thumb can be opposed actively towards the other fingers. Muscle strength of the right hand is decreased. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 39-year-old patient comes to the emergency department because of increasing shortness of breath over the past 3 months. They have been unable to climb the 3 flights of stairs to their apartment. Six years ago, they were diagnosed with HIV. They are currently receiving triple antiretroviral therapy, but they say that they often miss doses. Their temperature is 38.1°C (100.6° F), pulse is 90/min, respirations are 22/min, and blood pressure is 160/70 mm Hg. There is a grade 4/6 holodiastolic murmur heard best at the right sternal border. The pupils are 4 mm, round, and not reactive to light. When a pen tip is advanced closer to the face, the pupils constrict. Extraocular movements are intact. When asked to stand, hold their arms in front of them, and close their eyes, they lose their balance and take a step backward. An x-ray of the chest shows widening of the mediastinum. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 33-year-old patient comes to the physician because of vision impairment in their right eye for the past 2 weeks. During this period, they were unable to distinguish colors with their right eye. They also report pain with eye movement. They have no double vision. They occasionally have headaches that are relieved by ibuprofen. One year ago, they had a similar episode that affected their left eye and resolved spontaneously. They have no history of serious illness. They work at a library and enjoy reading, even in poor lighting conditions. Their vital signs are within normal limits. The pupils are equal, round, and reactive to light and accommodation. Without correction, visual acuity is 20/50 in the left eye, and 20/100 in the right eye. With spectacles, the visual acuity is 20/20 in the left eye and 20/100 in the right eye. Slit lamp examination shows no abnormalities. A CT scan of the head shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 4-month history of intermittent lower abdominal cramps associated with diarrhea, bloating, and mild nausea. During this period, they have had a 5-kg (11-lb) weight loss. They feel like they cannot fully empty their bowels. They have no history of serious illness. They have a high-fiber diet. Their father is of Ashkenazi Jewish descent. They appear well. Their temperature is 36.9°C (98.5°F), pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 130/90 mm Hg. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Cardiac examination shows no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Abdominal examination shows mild tenderness to palpation in the right lower quadrant without guarding or rebound. Bowel sounds are normal. Test of the stool for occult blood is negative. Their hemoglobin concentration is 10.5 g/dL, leukocyte count is 12,000 mm3, platelet count is 480,000 mm3, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate is 129 mm/h. A barium enema shows ulceration and narrowing of the right colon. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 1-year history of intermittent buzzing in both their ears. They say they sometimes have episodes of mild dizziness which resolve spontaneously. They have a 15-year history of type 1 diabetes mellitus and episodes of low back pain. They do not smoke or drink alcohol. Current medications include insulin and aspirin. They work as a trombonist for a symphony orchestra. Their vital signs are within normal limits. On otoscopic examination, the tympanic membrane appears normal. Bone conduction is greater than air conduction in both ears. Weber test shows no lateralization. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 43-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department because of severe retrosternal pain radiating to the back and left shoulder for 4 hours. The pain began after attending a farewell party for their coworker at a local bar. They had 3–4 episodes of nonbilious vomiting before the onset of the pain. They have hypertension. Their father died of cardiac arrest at the age of 55 years. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the last 23 years and drinks 2–3 beers daily. Their current medications include amlodipine and valsartan. They appear pale. Their temperature is 37° C (98.6° F), pulse is 115/min, and blood pressure is 90/60 mm Hg. There are decreased breath sounds over the left base and crepitus is palpable over the thorax. Abdominal examination shows tenderness to palpation in the epigastric region; bowel sounds are normal. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 16.5 g/dL Leukocyte count 11,100/mm3 Serum Na+ 133 mEq/L K+ 3.2 mEq/L Cl- 98 mEq/L HCO3- 30 mEq/L Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL An ECG shows sinus tachycardia with left ventricular hypertrophy. Intravenous fluid resuscitation and antibiotics are begun. Which of the following is the most appropriate test to confirm the diagnosis in this patient?

A 5-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of high-grade fever and generalized fatigue for 5 days. Two days ago, they developed a rash on their trunk. They returned from a family hiking trip to Montana 1 week ago. Their immunization records are unavailable. Their temperature is 39.8°C (103.6°F), pulse is 111/min, and blood pressure is 96/60 mm Hg. Examination shows injection of the conjunctivae bilaterally. The tongue and pharynx are erythematous. Tender cervical lymphadenopathy is present on the left. There is a macular rash over the trunk and extremities. Bilateral knee joints are swollen and tender; range of motion is limited by pain. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old patient comes to the physician for decreased exercise tolerance. Over the past four months, they have noticed progressively worsening shortness of breath while walking their dog. They also become short of breath when lying in bed at night. Their temperature is 36.4°C (97.5°F), pulse is 82/min, respirations are 19/min, and blood pressure is 155/53 mm Hg. Cardiac examination shows a high-pitch, decrescendo murmur that occurs immediately after S2 and is heard best along the left sternal border. There is an S3 gallop. Carotid pulses are strong. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old patient is brought to the physician for evaluation of pallor and increasing lethargy for 2 days. One week ago, they experienced abdominal pain, vomiting, and bloody diarrhea that have since subsided. The patient's parent states that they returned early from a 6-week roadtrip in Mexico because of these symptoms. Their parents have been giving them oral rehydration solution. Their immunizations are up-to-date. They appear pale. Their temperature is 38.4°C (101.1°F), pulse is 130/min, respirations are 35/min, and blood pressure is 95/50 mm Hg. Examination shows scleral icterus. The abdomen is soft and nontender; there is no rebound or guarding. Bowel sounds are hyperactive. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 8.5 g/dL Mean corpuscular volume 94 μm3 Leukocyte count 18,000/mm3 Platelet count 45,000/mm3 Prothrombin time 12 sec Partial thromboplastin time 34 sec Serum Urea nitrogen 28 mg/dL Creatinine 1.6 mg/dL Bilirubin Total 2.5 mg/dL Direct 0.1 mg/dL Lactate dehydrogenase 1658 U/L A blood smear shows schistocytes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old patient is brought to the physician for a well-child examination. They have no history of serious illness. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 95/min, and blood pressure is 96/52 mm Hg. Examination shows a 2/6 continuous, low-pitched murmur over the left upper sternal border that radiates towards the neck. The murmur disappears when they flex their neck. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old patient comes to the physician because of increasing pain in the right hip for 2 months. The pain is intermittent, presenting at the lateral side of the hip and radiating towards the thigh. It is aggravated while climbing stairs or lying on the right side. Two weeks ago, the patient was treated with a course of oral prednisone for exacerbation of asthma. Their current medications include formoterol-budesonide and albuterol inhalers. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows tenderness to palpation over the upper lateral part of the right thigh. There is no swelling. The patient is placed in the left lateral decubitus position. Abducting the extended right leg against the physician's resistance reproduces the pain. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. An x-ray of the pelvis shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 39-year-old patient comes to the physician for difficulty sleeping and poor concentration at work. They sleep with the lights turned on and wake up frequently during the night with palpitations and profuse sweating. Three weeks ago they were sexually assaulted in their car. Since the assault they have avoided using their car and only use public transportation. They also have nightmares of their attacker. They have been sent home from work for yelling at their coworkers. They have Hashimoto thyroiditis. Current medications include levothyroxine. They have been treated for pelvic inflammatory disease in the past. They have tried alcohol and melatonin to help them sleep. Mental status examination shows a depressed mood and a negative affect. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 69-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a cough for the past 3 months. The cough is mostly dry, but the patient recalls a recent episode in which they coughed up mucus with dark red streaks. They have felt tired for the past few months. Over the past month, they have had poor appetite and a 5-kg (11-lb) weight loss. They also have occasional back pain, which has worsened in recent weeks. They have no recent travel history. They have smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for 30 years. They do not drink alcohol. Their vitals are within normal limits. Auscultation of the lungs reveals wheezing in the lower right lung field. There is no peripheral lymphadenopathy. The liver is of normal size, and the spleen is not palpable. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin concentration of 13.5 g/dL, serum calcium concentration of 12.3 mg/dL, and a total serum protein of 7.0 g/dL. X-rays of the chest are shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old African American patient comes to the physician because of fatigue and muscle weakness for the past 5 weeks. During this period, they have had recurrent headaches and palpitations. They have hypertension and major depressive disorder. They work as a nurse at a local hospital. They have smoked about 6–8 cigarettes daily for the past 10 years and drinks 1–2 glasses of wine on weekends. Current medications include enalapril, metoprolol, and fluoxetine. They are 160 cm (5 ft 6 in) tall and weigh 60 kg (132 lb); BMI is 21.3 kg/m2. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 75/min, and blood pressure is 155/85 mm Hg. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Cardiac examination shows no abnormalities. The abdomen is soft and nontender; bowel sounds are normal. Their skin is dry and there is no edema in the lower extremities. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 13.3 g/dL Serum Na+ 146 mEq/L Cl- 105 mEq/L K+ 3.0 mEq/L HCO3- 30 mEq/L Urea nitrogen 10 mg/dL Glucose 95 mg/dL Creatinine 0.8 mg/dL Urine Blood negative Glucose negative Protein negative RBC 0–1/hpf WBC none Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 55-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of inappropriate behavior for the past 6 months. They have been making inappropriate comments and jokes while talking to friends and family members. They were arrested 3 weeks ago while trying to kiss strangers on the street. They have no interest in talking to their daughter or playing with their grandchildren. During this period, they have developed a strong desire for chocolate pudding and potato chips and have gained 10 kg (22 lb). They appear unkempt. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination is unremarkable. Mental status examination shows apathy and a blunt affect. They avoid answering questions and instead comment on the individuals they saw in the waiting room. Mini-Mental State Examination score is 28/30. A complete blood count and serum concentrations of glucose, creatine, and electrolytes are within the reference range. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

One week after undergoing sigmoidectomy with end colostomy for complicated diverticulitis, a 67-year-old patient has upper abdominal pain. During the surgery, they were transfused two units of packed red blood cells. Their postoperative course was uncomplicated. Two days ago, they developed fever. They are currently receiving parenteral nutrition through a central venous catheter. They have type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and hypercholesterolemia. They are oriented to person, but not to place and time. Prior to admission, their medications included metformin, valsartan, aspirin, and atorvastatin. Their temperature is 38.9°C (102.0°F), pulse is 120/min, and blood pressure is 100/60 mmHg. Examination shows jaundice of the conjunctivae. Abdominal examination shows tenderness to palpation in the right upper quadrant. There is no rebound tenderness or guarding; bowel sounds are hypoactive. Laboratory studies show: Leukocytes 13,500 /mm3 Segmented neutrophils 75 % Serum Aspartate aminotransferase 140 IU/L Alanine aminotransferase 85 IU/L Alkaline phosphatase 150 IU/L Bilirubin Total 2.1 mg/dL Direct 1.3 mg/dL Amylase 20 IU/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A previously healthy 4-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of blisters and redness on their neck and chest for 2 days. They have also had a fever. They are lethargic and have not eaten well since the rash appeared. They have not had coughing, wheezing, or dysuria. They are an only child and there is no family history of serious illness. Their immunizations are up-to-date. Their temperature is 38.9°C (102°F), pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 80/40 mm Hg. Examination shows flaccid blisters over their neck and trunk that rupture easily. Areas of erythematous moist skin are also noted. Twirling an eraser over the trunk results in a blister. Oropharyngeal examination is normal. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 12 g/dL Leukocyte count 22,000/mm3 Segmented neutrophils 77% Eosinophils 3% Lymphocytes 18% Monocytes 2% Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 60 mm/h Urinalysis is normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

Shortly after undergoing a bipolar prosthesis for a displaced femoral neck fracture of the left hip acquired after a fall the day before, an 80-year-old patient suddenly develops dyspnea. The surgery under general anesthesia with sevoflurane was uneventful, lasting 98 minutes, during which the patient maintained oxygen saturation readings of 96–100% on 8 L of oxygen. They have a history of hypertension, osteoporosis, and osteoarthritis of their right knee. Their medications include ramipril, naproxen, ranitidine, and a multivitamin. They appear cyanotic, drowsy, and are oriented only to person. Their temperature is 38.6°C (101.5°F), pulse is 135/minute, respirations are 36/min, and blood pressure is 155/95 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 81%. There are several scattered petechiae on the anterior chest wall. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin concentration of 10.5 g/dL, a leukocyte count of 9,000/mm3, a platelet count of 145,000/mm3, and a creatine kinase of 190 U/L. An ECG shows sinus tachycardia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of pain in their right thumb and wrist that radiates to their elbow. It is worse when they hold their infant and improves with the use of an ice pack. Six months ago, they slipped on a wet floor and fell on their right outstretched hand. Their parent takes methotrexate for chronic joint pain. The patient takes ibuprofen as needed for their current symptoms. Examination of the right hand shows tenderness over the radial styloid with swelling but no redness. There is no crepitus. Grasping their right thumb and exerting longitudinal traction toward the ulnar side elicits pain. Range of motion of the finger joints is normal. There is no swelling, redness, or tenderness of any other joints. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 64-year-old patient comes to the physician 3 days after noticing a lump in their right groin while they were bathing. They have no history of trauma to the region. They have hypercholesterolemia and hypertension treated with atorvastatin and labetalol. They have smoked 2 packs of cigarettes daily for 35 years. Their vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows a 4-cm (1.6-in), nontender, pulsatile mass with a palpable thrill at the right midinguinal point. On auscultation, a harsh continuous murmur is heard over the mass. Femoral and pedal pulses are palpable bilaterally. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old patient comes to the emergency department because of weakness and fatigue for 2 days. They have also noticed that their urine is darker than usual. For the past week, they have had a persistent non-productive cough and low-grade fever. They have seasonal allergies. They drink one to two glasses of wine on social occasions and do not smoke. Their temperature is 37.9°C (100.2°F), pulse is 88/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 110/76 mm Hg. They have conjunctival pallor and scleral icterus. Cardiopulmonary examination shows bibasilar crackles. The remainder of the physical examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show: Leukocyte count 8,000/mm3 Hemoglobin 7.1 g/dL Hematocrit 21% Platelet count 110,000/mm3 MCV 94 μm3 Serum Total bilirubin 4.3 mg/dL Direct 1.1 mg/dL Indirect 3.2 mg/dL AST 15 U/L ALT 17 U/L LDH 1,251 U/L Haptoglobin 5.8 mg/dL (N = 41–165) An x-ray of the chest shows bilateral patchy infiltrates. A peripheral blood smear shows spherocytes. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 16-year-old high school student is brought to the physician by their parents for their repeated behavioral problems at home and school during the past 10 months. Their teachers describe their behavior as uncooperative and disruptive as they persistently refuse to answer questions, insult their teachers, and annoy their classmates on a daily basis. At home, their parents try to address their frequent violations of curfew, but attempts at discussing the issue often result in the patient losing their temper and screaming at their parents. Their grades have deteriorated over the past year. They have no history of psychiatric illness. On questioning, the patient refuses to answer and frequently disrupts the physician’s conversation with the parents. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 3-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of a 3-day history of a pruritic skin rash on their chest. Their parent says that they have no history of dermatological problems. They were born at term and have been healthy except for recurrent episodes of otitis media. Their immunizations are up-to-date. They appear pale. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 110/min, respirations are 26/min, and blood pressure is 102/62 mm Hg. Examination shows vesicles and flaccid bullae with thin brown crusts on the chest. Lateral traction of the surrounding skin leads to sloughing. Examination of the oral mucosa shows no abnormalities. Complete blood count is within the reference range. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their mother because of a change in their personality. The mother reports that over the past 7 months her child has become increasingly withdrawn; they have not answered any phone calls or visited their family and friends. They had always been a quiet person, who needed some time on their own, but they used to meet with friends at least once a week. The patient says that they cannot leave the house because aliens are watching them and “stealing their thoughts”. They do not drink alcohol. They used to smoke marijuana occasionally but quit 1 year ago. Their vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. On mental status examination, it is impossible to follow the patient's sequence of thoughts. They are anxious and have a flat affect. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department for the evaluation of worsening upper abdominal pain that they first noticed this morning after waking up. The pain is of tearing and burning quality and radiates to their back. Yesterday, they underwent an upper endoscopy and were diagnosed with gastritis and a large hiatal hernia. They have hypertension, hypercholesteremia, and a left bundle branch block that was diagnosed 5 years ago. The patient's mother died of myocardial infarction at the age of 70 years, and their father died of aortic dissection at the age of 65 years. The patient smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the past 40 years, but quit 10 years ago. They drink three beers daily. Current medications include hydrochlorothiazide, amlodipine, atorvastatin, and pantoprazole. The patient appears to be in mild distress. Their temperature is 37.8°C (100.4°F), pulse is 103/min, and blood pressure is 135/89 mm Hg in the left arm and 132/90 mm Hg in the right arm. Cardiopulmonary examination shows crackling with every heartbeat. Abdominal examination shows tenderness to palpation in the epigastric region; bowel sounds are normal. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 16.0 g/dL Leukocyte count 11,000/mm3 Na+ 140 mEq/L K+ 4.2 mEq/L Cl- 101 mEq/L HCO3- 25 mEq/L Creatinine 1.3 mg/dL Alanine aminotransferase 21 U/L Aspartate aminotransferase 43 U/L Lipase 40 U/L (N = 14–280) Troponin I 0.025 ng/mL (N < 0.1) Chest x-ray shows a large hiatal hernia and mediastinal lucency. A 12-lead EKG shows sinus tachycardia and a left bundle branch block. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 26-year-old nurse comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of fatigue. They have had a lot of stress at work and have been on sick leave for 2 weeks, but state that they would like to return to work. They have had several episodes of lower abdominal pain. They say, "I know I have cancer." They request a diagnostic laparoscopy. They were diagnosed with peptic ulcer disease 6 months ago. Their only medication is omeprazole. The patient appears pale. Their temperature is 36.5° C (97.7° F), pulse is 120/min, and blood pressure is 90/65 mm Hg. On mental status examination they are tired and have a depressed mood. Physical examination shows pale conjunctivae and dry mucous membranes. There are numerous crusts along the course of their left arm veins. A grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur is heard along the right-upper sternal border. Abdominal examination shows no abnormalities. There is generalized weakness of the proximal muscles. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 7.5 g/dL Mean corpuscular volume 89 μm3 Reticulocyte count 13.3% Serum Sodium 139 mEq/L Potassium 3.9 mEq/L Calcium 8.5 mg/dL Test of the stool for occult blood is negative. Abdominal ultrasonography shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old patient comes to the physician because of progressive fatigue and shortness of breath for 2 months. The dyspnea occurs on moderate exertion and during the night; they sometimes wake up coughing and “gasping for air.” They have also had several episodes of heart pounding and palpitations. Two weeks ago, they had a runny nose and a productive cough. They have type 2 diabetes mellitus and peripheral arterial disease. They have never smoked. They drink one to two beers occasionally. They have a history of intravenous illicit drugs use but have not used in over 25 years. Current medications include aspirin, atorvastatin, and metformin. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows bilateral basilar rales. Cardiac auscultation is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of increasing pain and swelling of the left knee for 2 months. The pain has awoken them from their sleep on multiple occasions. They tried ibuprofen but have had no relief of their symptoms. There is no family or personal history of serious illness. Vital signs are within normal limits. On examination, the left knee is mildly swollen and tender; range of motion is limited by pain. An x-ray of the left knee is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old patient comes to the physician because of 1 week of progressive left anterior knee pain. The pain is worse after sitting for a prolonged period of time and while ascending stairs. They first noticed the pain the day after a basketball game. They have often taken painful blows to the side of the knees while playing basketball but do not recall this having happened in the last game. Four weeks ago, they were diagnosed with a chlamydial urinary tract infection and treated with azithromycin. They are sexually active with one partner; they use condoms inconsistently. Their vital signs are within normal limits. They are 178 cm (5 ft 10 in) tall and weigh 62 kg (137 lb); BMI is 19.6 kg/m2. Physical examination shows tenderness over the left anterior knee that is exacerbated with anterior pressure to the patella when the knee is fully extended; there is no erythema or swelling. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old patient comes to the physician for right lower abdominal pain for 6 months. They have multiple non-bloody, watery bowel movements daily and experiences abdominal cramping. Sometimes, they feel sudden palpitations, are short of breath, and their face becomes red. They have lost 7 kg over the past 3 months. They went on a 3-week hiking trip to Cambodia 6 months ago. They have smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for 15 years. Their temperature is 37˚C (98.6°F), their pulse is 72/min and their blood pressure is 125/70 mm Hg. On physical examination, tiny blood vessels are noted on their face and arms. Lung auscultation shows bilateral wheezing. The abdomen is soft and nondistended. There is localized tenderness to the right lower quadrant, but no rebound tenderness or guarding. Laboratory studies show: Leukocyte count 4,600 /mm3 Segmented neutrophils 61 % Eosinophils 2 % Platelet count 254,000 /mm3 Hemoglobin 13.1 g/dL Serum Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 110 IU/L Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 128 IU/L C-reactive protein 8 mg/dL (N = 0–10) Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old patient comes to the physician because of an increasingly painful swelling behind their right knee for the past 2 months. During this time, they have also had intermittent low-grade fever and they have been more fatigued than usual. They have not had any trauma to the knee. Over the past year, they have had occasional pain in their hands and wrists bilaterally. They have hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. They drink 1–2 glasses of wine daily and occasionally more on weekends. Current medications include enalapril, metformin, and glimepiride. Their mother and older brother have osteoarthritis. They are 165 cm (5 ft 5 in) tall and weigh 68 kg (150 lb); BMI is 25 kg/m2. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows a 3-cm nontender mass in the right popliteal fossa that becomes prominent when the knee is extended. There is mild swelling and redness of their right knee joint. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient with asthma comes to the physician because of a 1-month history of progressively worsening shortness of breath and cough. They also have a history of chronic sinusitis and foot drop. Current medications include an albuterol inhaler and inhaled corticosteroid. Physical examination shows diffuse wheezing over both lung fields and tender subcutaneous nodules on both elbows. Laboratory studies show a leukocyte count of 23,000/mm3 with 26% eosinophils and a serum creatinine of 1.7 mg/dL. Urine microscopy shows red blood cell casts. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 69-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of severe right hip pain. The pain is worse at night. They have chronic headaches and back pain for which they take vitamin D, calcium supplements, and ibuprofen. Examination shows hip tenderness and mild sensorineural hearing loss. X-ray of the hip shows a radiolucent lesion in the ilium with a moth-eaten appearance, wide transition zone, and an aggressive periosteal reaction. Wide excision of the lesion is performed. A photomicrograph of a section of the lesion is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 47-year-old patient comes to the physician because of repetitive tongue twisting and abnormal movements of the hands and legs that started several days ago. They have a 2-year history of schizophrenia that has been controlled with fluphenazine. Two weeks ago, they were switched to risperidone. Examination shows protrusion of the tongue and smacking of the lips. They make twisting movements of the arms and frequently tap their right foot. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 73-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after the sudden onset of right-sided body weakness. Their spouse reports that they do not seem to understand simple questions. They have type 2 diabetes mellitus and have smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for 45 years. The patient speaks fluently, but they answer questions with nonsensical phrases and cannot repeat single words. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their partner because of persistent sadness for the past 2 months. During this period, they also have had difficulty sleeping and an increased appetite. They had similar episodes that occurred 2 years ago and 9 months ago that each lasted for 4 months. Between these episodes, they reported feeling very energetic and rested after 3 hours of sleep. They often went for long periods of time without eating. They work as a stock market trader and received a promotion 5 months ago. They regularly attend yoga classes on the weekends with their friends. On mental status examination, they have a blunted affect. They deny suicidal thoughts and illicit drug use. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old patient with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus comes to the physician because of increasing shortness of breath and a dry cough over the past 6 months. They have smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the past 40 years. Chest auscultation shows scattered expiratory wheezes in both lung fields. Spirometry shows an FEV1:FVC ratio of 65% and an FEV1 of 70% of predicted. Their diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) is 42% of predicted. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parent because of a 1-month history of pain in their right leg. Their parent has been giving them ketorolac at night to improve their sleep, but the pain has not improved. Physical examination shows marked tenderness along the right mid-femur. An x-ray of the right lower extremity shows several lytic lesions in the diaphysis of the femur and a surrounding cortex covered by several layers of new bone. A biopsy of the right femur shows small round blue cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 2-day history of difficulty sleeping. They worry that the lack of sleep will ruin their career prospects as a model. They have been coming to the physician multiple times over the past year for minor problems. They are dressed very extravagantly and flirt with the receptionist. When they are asked to sit down in the waiting room, they begin to cry and say that no one listens to them. When they are called to the examination room, they move close to the physician, repeatedly intend to touch their cheek, and make inappropriate comments. They do not have a history of self-harm or suicidal ideation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 5-day history of swelling in their left arm. Two months ago, they were diagnosed with a deep venous thrombosis in the left calf. They have had a 7-kg (15-lb) weight loss in the last 3 months. They have smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the past 25 years. Their only medication is warfarin. Physical examination shows warm edema of the left forearm with overlying erythema and a tender, palpable cord-like structure along the medial arm. Their lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Duplex sonography shows thrombosis of the left basilic and external jugular veins. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to confirm the underlying diagnosis?

A 30-year-old patient comes to the physician because of increasing weakness in both legs for 7 days. They also report a tingling sensation in their legs that is exacerbated by taking a hot shower. They are sexually active with one partner and do not use condoms. Their temperature is 37.8°C (100.1°F). Physical examination shows decreased muscle strength and clonus in both lower extremities. Patellar reflex is 4+ bilaterally and plantar reflex shows an extensor response on both sides. Abdominal reflex is absent. An MRI of the brain is shown. Which of the following findings is most likely to further support the diagnosis in this patient?

A 28-year-old patient is brought to a counselor by their parent after they found out that they are being physically abused by their partner. The parent reports that they refuse to end the relationship with their partner despite the physical abuse. They say that they feel uneasy when their partner is not around. They add, “I'm worried that if I leave them, my life will only get worse.” They have never been employed since they got married because they are convinced that nobody would hire them. Their partner takes care of most household errands and pays all of the bills. Physical examination shows several bruises on the thighs and back. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 52-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 6-month history of shortness of breath and nonproductive cough. They have smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for 15 years. Cardiopulmonary examination shows fine inspiratory crackles bilaterally. There is clubbing present in the fingers bilaterally. Pulmonary function tests (PFTs) show an FVC of 78% of expected and an FEV1/FVC ratio of 92%. A CT scan of the chest is shown. Which of the following is the most likely underlying diagnosis?

A previously healthy 75-year-old patient comes to the physician with a 6-month history of fatigue, weight loss, and abdominal pain. They drink 2 oz of alcohol on the weekends and do not smoke. They are retired but previously worked in a factory that produces plastic pipes. Abdominal examination shows right upper quadrant tenderness; the liver edge is palpable 2 cm below the ribs. A liver biopsy specimen shows pleomorphic spindle cells that express PECAM-1 on their surface. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old patient is brought to the physician for recurrent 3–4 minutes episodes of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. They are nonresponsive during these episodes and do not remember them afterward. They recall a muddy taste in their mouth before the onset of symptoms. One week ago, their sibling witnessed an episode where they woke up, stared, and made hand gestures. After the incident, they felt lethargic and confused. Examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 52-year-old patient with HIV infection is brought to the emergency department 20 minutes after they had a generalized tonic-clonic seizure. They appear lethargic and confused. Laboratory studies show a CD4+ count of 89 cells/μL (N > 500). A CT scan of the head with contrast shows multiple ring-enhancing lesions in the basal ganglia and subcortical white matter. An India ink preparation of cerebrospinal fluid is negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 59-year-old patient has abdominal pain. During the procedure, they were transfused 3 units of packed red blood cells. They are currently receiving total parenteral nutrition. Their temperature is 38.9°C (102.0°F), pulse is 115/min, and blood pressure is 100/60 mm Hg. Examination shows tenderness to palpation in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen. Bowel sounds are hypoactive. Serum studies show: Aspartate aminotransferase 142 U/L Alanine aminotransferase 86 U/L Alkaline phosphatase 153 U/L Total bilirubin 1.5 mg/dL Direct bilirubin 1.0 mg/dL Amylase 20 U/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 15-month-old patient is brought to the physician because of the sudden appearance of a rash on their trunk that started 6 hours ago and subsequently spread to their extremities. Four days ago, they were taken to the emergency department because of a high fever and vomiting. They were treated with acetaminophen and discharged the next day. The fever persisted for several days and abated just prior to appearance of the rash. Physical examination shows a rose-colored, blanching, maculopapular rash, and postauricular lymphadenopathy. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An infectious disease investigator is evaluating the diagnostic accuracy of a new interferon-gamma-based assay for diagnosing tuberculosis in patients who have previously received a Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine. Consenting participants with a history of BCG vaccination received an interferon-gamma assay and were subsequently evaluated for tuberculosis by sputum culture. Results of the study are summarized in the table below. Tuberculosis, confirmed by culture No tuberculosis Total Positive interferon-gamma assay 90 6 96 Negative interferon-gamma assay 10 194 204 Total 100 200 300 Based on these results, what is the sensitivity of the interferon-gamma-based assay for the diagnosis of tuberculosis in this study? The text does not contain any references to gender, so no modifications were necessary to remove gender markers.

An 8-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of an intermittent, diffuse abdominal pain. They have also had a nonpruritic rash on their legs and swelling of their ankles for 1 week. Two weeks ago, they had a sore throat, which was treated with oral amoxicillin. Examination of the lower extremities shows non-blanching, raised erythematous papules. The ankle joints are swollen and warm, and their range of motion is limited by pain. Laboratory studies show a platelet count of 450,000/mm3. Test of the stool for occult blood is positive. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 81-year-old patient comes to the physician because of increased exertional dyspnea and dizziness over the past 8 weeks. They have hypertension for which they take lisinopril. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the past 50 years. Physical examination shows weak peripheral pulses. Cardiac examination is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old patient comes to the physician because of an 8-month history of upper abdominal pain. During this period, they have also had nausea, heartburn, and multiple episodes of diarrhea with no blood or mucus. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the past 18 years. They do not use alcohol or illicit drugs. Current medications include an antacid. The abdomen is soft and there is tenderness to palpation in the epigastric and umbilical areas. Upper endoscopy shows several ulcers in the duodenum and the upper jejunum as well as thick gastric folds. Gastric pH is < 2. Biopsies from the ulcers show no organisms. Which of the following tests is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 4-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parent because of fatigue and generalized weakness for 4 months. Examination shows decreased muscle tone. Their fasting serum glucose concentration is 41 mg/dL. The physician suspects a defect in one of the enzymes involved in the carnitine shuttle. Increased serum concentration of which of the following should most raise suspicion of a different diagnosis?

A 19-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 1-month history of mild fatigue and weakness. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Their hemoglobin concentration is 11 g/dL and mean corpuscular volume is 74 μm3. Hemoglobin electrophoresis shows 10% HbA2 (normal < 3.5%). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 46-year-old patient comes to the physician for an 8-month history of headache that is more severe in the mornings. Their blood pressure is 151/92 mm Hg. Examination shows enlargement of the nose, forehead, and jaw as well as the hands, fingers, and feet. Ophthalmologic examination shows impaired vision in the outer peripheral fields of both eyes. Laboratory studies show a serum glucose concentration of 225 mg/dL. Which of the following findings is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 4-year-old patient is brought to the physician for a painless lump on their neck. They have no history of serious illness and their vital signs are within normal limits. On examination, there is a firm, 2-cm swelling at the midline just below the level of the hyoid bone. The mass moves cranially when they are asked to protrude their tongue. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of progressive headaches, dizziness, and recurrent episodes of vomiting for 3 weeks. They have a history of surgical removal of a sac-like protuberance on their lower back soon after birth. Neurologic examination shows ataxia. Fundoscopy shows bilateral optic disk swelling. An MRI of the brain is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old patient comes to the physician because of headaches and blurry vision for the past 6 months. They also report frequent episodes of vomiting over the last month. Their father has died of renal cell carcinoma at the age of 37 years. Examination shows 20/40 vision bilaterally. Fundoscopic examination shows bilateral optic disc swelling and growth of capillary vessels in the temporal peripheral retina. An MRI of the brain shows an infratentorial mass. The patient undergoes surgical resection of the mass. A photomicrograph of the resected specimen is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old patient comes to the physician because of recent fatigue and weakness that is exacerbated by cross-country skiing. Four weeks ago, they were diagnosed with pneumonia; sputum cultures on Eaton agar showed organisms that lacked a cell wall. Physical examination shows conjunctival pallor and cyanosis of the fingertips. Both lungs are clear to auscultation. Which of the following findings is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 34-year-old patient comes to the physician with a 2-month history of difficulty concentrating at work. They are worried they may lose their job due to poor performance. They feel constantly tired but attribute their fatigue to waking up early most mornings and being unable to fall back asleep. Their partner has noticed that they have been speaking more slowly than usual and their appetite has decreased. They used to enjoy dance classes with their partner but have not been as interested in this recently. They are a veteran who returned from a deployment to Afghanistan 2 years ago. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 1-year history of intermittent episodes of shortness of breath, chest tightness, palpitation, dizziness, sweaty hands, and a feeling of impending doom. They say that their symptoms occur when they go for a walk or wait in line for coffee. They report that they no longer leave the house by themselves because they are afraid of being alone when their symptoms occur. They only go out when their partner accompanies them. They do not smoke or use illicit drugs. Within a few hours after each episode, physical examination and laboratory studies have shown no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 28-year-old patient comes to the emergency department because of dizziness and palpitations for 2 days. Prior to the onset of the symptoms, they attended a party where they lost several drinking games. An ECG is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of progressively worsening shortness of breath on exertion. They are concerned that they have asthma and would like to be started on albuterol. Which of the following findings is most likely to indicate a different diagnosis in this patient?

A 53-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of cough and progressively worsening difficulty walking up the stairs in their apartment. They have noticed that it is easier for them to climb the stairs after they have exercised. They have also had a 4.6-kg (10.1-lb) weight loss over the past 6 months. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 35 years. Examination shows dry mucous membranes. The pupils are equal and react sluggishly to light. Muscle strength in the proximal lower extremity is initially 3/5 but increases to 5/5 after repeated muscle tapping. Their achilles reflex is 1+. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

One week after discharge from the neonatal intensive care unit to a regular pediatric ward, a 1450-g (3-lb 1-oz) infant has respiratory distress and wheezing. After birth, the patient was intubated and mechanically ventilated for 3 weeks because of hypoxia. They required a 60% fraction of inspired oxygen to achieve adequate oxygen saturation. Their temperature is 36.9°C (98.4°F), pulse is 144/min, respirations are 59/min, and blood pressure is 65/35 mm Hg. Physical examination shows labored breathing, intercostal retractions, and crackles at both lung bases. There is bluish discoloration around the lips. An x-ray of the chest shows interspersed areas of atelectasis, granular densities, and hyperinflation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department because of sudden, painless loss of vision in their right eye that occurred 30 minutes ago while watching TV. They have coronary artery disease, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus; they have had trouble adhering to their medication regimen. Their blood pressure is 160/85 mm Hg. Examination shows 20/50 vision in the left eye and no perception of light in the right eye. Direct pupillary reflex is present in the left eye, but absent in the right eye. Accommodation is intact bilaterally. Intraocular pressure is 16 mm Hg in the left eye and 18 mm Hg in the right eye. Fundoscopic examination of the right eye shows a pale, white retina with a bright red area within the macula. The optic disc appears normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 66-year-old patient comes to the physician with a 4-month history of recurrent crusty lesions on the dorsal surface of their hands. When they scrape off the crusts, they reappear after a few days. The lesions are mildly pruritic and occasionally burn. They work as a landscaper. A photograph of their right hand is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 64-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a dry cough and progressively worsening shortness of breath for the past 2 months. They have not had fever, chills, or night sweats. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the past 45 years. They appear thin. Examination of the lung shows a prolonged expiratory phase and end-expiratory wheezing. Spirometry shows decreased FEV1:FVC ratio (< 70% predicted), decreased FEV1, and a total lung capacity of 125% of predicted. The diffusion capacity of the lung (DLCO) is decreased. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old patient comes to the physician because of an 8-month history of weakness and intermittent burning pain in their neck, shoulders, and arms. They were involved in a motor vehicle collision 1 year ago. Examination of the upper extremities shows absent reflexes, muscle weakness, and fasciculations bilaterally. Sensation to temperature and pain is absent; vibration and proprioception are preserved. The pupils are equal and reactive to light. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their partner because they have appeared increasingly agitated over the last week. They feel restless, have not been able to sleep well, and have been pacing around their house continuously in an attempt to relieve their symptoms. Two weeks ago, they were diagnosed with schizophrenia and treatment with fluphenazine was initiated. Today, physical examination is interrupted multiple times because they are unable to sit or stand still for more than a couple minutes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 1-week history of fever, weakness, diffuse abdominal pain, and multiple lumps on their body. They have recently returned to the USA from a 3-month agricultural internship in South America. Physical examination shows enlarged superficial cervical and inguinal lymph nodes. There is tender hepatomegaly. A photomicrograph of a liver biopsy sample after methenamine silver staining is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 54-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 6-month history of dull, persistent pain and swelling of their right leg. The pain is worse at the end of the day and is relieved by walking or elevating their feet. Two years ago, they developed acute deep vein thrombosis in their right calf after a long flight, which was treated with anticoagulants for 6 months. Physical examination shows 2+ pitting edema of their right leg. The skin around the right ankle shows a reddish-brown discoloration and multiple telangiectasias. They have dilated varicose veins in the right leg. Which of the following is most likely to establish the diagnosis?

A 72-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department after an episode of hemoptysis. They have a chronic cough that is productive of copious sputum. Six years ago, they had a stroke that left them with difficulty swallowing. They smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 40 years, but quit 2 years ago. Their respirations are 25/min and labored. Physical examination shows digital clubbing. An x-ray of the chest shows tram track opacities in the lower lung fields. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of increased urination. They have also had dry mouth and excessive thirst despite drinking several gallons of water daily. They have a history of obsessive-compulsive disorder treated with citalopram. They drink 1–2 cans of beer daily. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Serum studies show a Na+ concentration of 130 mEq/L, a glucose concentration of 185 mg/dL, and an osmolality of 265 mOsmol/kg. Urine osmolality is 230 mOsmol/kg. The patient is asked to stop drinking water for 3 hours. Following water restriction, repeated laboratory studies show a serum osmolality of 280 mOsmol/kg and a urine osmolality of 650 mOsmol/kg. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old patient comes to the physician for a 6-month history of dry cough, hoarseness, and chest pain. They do not smoke and have not lost weight. Laboratory studies show no abnormalities. An x-ray of the chest shows a mass that projects across the right hilum. A CT scan of the chest is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parent because of a change in their behavior over the past 8 months. The parent says that their child has become increasingly withdrawn; they have not answered any phone calls or visited their family and friends. The patient says that they have to stay at home because a foreign intelligence service is monitoring them. They think that they are using a magnetic field to read their mind. Mental status exam shows disjointed and perseverative thinking. They are anxious and have a flat affect. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old patient comes to the physician because of difficulty sleeping. They are afraid of falling asleep and get up earlier than desired. Four months ago, they were the driver in a car accident that resulted in the death of their unborn child. They have vivid nightmares of the event and report that they frequently re-experience the accident. They blame themselves for the death of their child, have stopped working as an accountant, avoid driving in cars, and have withdrawn from their parents and close friends. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 56-year-old patient comes to the emergency department because of a 3-day history of malaise, dysuria, blurred vision, and a painful, itchy rash. The rash began on their chest and face and spread to their limbs, palms, and soles. One week ago, they were diagnosed with trigeminal neuralgia and started on a new medicine. They appear ill. Their temperature is 38°C (100.4°F) and pulse is 110/min. Physical examination shows conjunctival injection and ulceration on the tongue and palate. There is no lymphadenopathy. Examination of the skin shows confluent annular, erythematous macules, bullae, and desquamation of the palms and soles. The epidermis separates when the skin is lightly stroked. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 58-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of diffuse muscle pain, malaise, pain in both knees, recurrent episodes of abdominal and chest pain. They have also had a 5-kg (11-lb) weight loss over the past 4 months. Four years ago, they were diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B infection and were started on tenofovir. There are several ulcerations around the ankle and calves bilaterally. Perinuclear anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies are negative. Urinalysis shows proteinuria and hematuria. Muscle biopsy shows a transmural inflammation of the arterial wall with leukocytic infiltration and fibrinoid necrosis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A group of investigators is evaluating the diagnostic properties of a new blood test that uses two serum biomarkers, dityrosine and Nε-carboxymethyl-lysine, for the clinical diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in children. The test is considered positive only if both markers are found in the serum. 50 children who have been diagnosed with ASD based on established clinical criteria and 50 children without the disorder undergo testing. The results show: Diagnosis of ASD No diagnosis of ASD Test positive 45 15 Test negative 5 35 Which of the following is the specificity of this new test? The text is already gender-neutral.

A 63-year-old patient comes to the physician with a 4-week history of fatigue, crampy abdominal pain, watery diarrhea, and pain in their mouth and gums. They returned from a 2-week trip to the Dominican Republic 2 months ago. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 45 years. Examination shows three 1.5-cm, painful ulcers in the mouth. Abdominal examination shows mild tenderness to palpation in the right lower quadrant without guarding or rebound. Their hemoglobin concentration is 11.2 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume is 75 fL, and leukocyte count is 11,900 mm3. Colonoscopy shows a cobblestone mucosa. A photomicrograph of a biopsy specimen is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An otherwise healthy 56-year-old patient comes to the physician for a 2-year history of recurrent upper abdominal pain and fullness that worsens after meals. Urea breath test is positive.
