An endoscopy shows diffuse mucosal atrophy and patchy erythema, but no ulcer. A biopsy from which of the following areas is most likely to yield an accurate diagnosis?

A 23-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their partner 10 minutes after ingesting at least 15 acetaminophen tablets. They have been admitted to the hospital several times in the past few months after attempted self-harm. They claim that their partner is “extremely selfish” and “does not care for them.” They say they feel lonely and want their partner to pay attention to them. Their partner says that they have broken up 10 times in the past year because they are prone to outbursts of physical aggression as well as mood swings. They say that these mood swings last a few hours and can vary from states of “exuberance and affection” to states of “depression.” On examination, the patient appears well-dressed and calm. They have normal speech, thought processes, and thought content. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 21-year-old patient comes to the military base physician for evaluation of progressive discomfort in their right shoulder for the past 4 months. They joined the military 6 months ago and are part of a drill team. In anticipation of an upcoming competition, they have been practicing rifle drills and firing exercises 8 hours a day. Physical examination shows tenderness to palpation and a firm mass in the superior part of the right deltopectoral groove. Range of motion is limited by pain and stiffness. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old patient comes to the emergency department for 2 days of severe headaches. The pain is most intense on their left forehead and eye. They had similar symptoms last summer. They have been taking indomethacin every 6 hours for the last 24 hours but have not had any relief. They have smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the past 5 years. They work as an accountant and describe their work as very stressful. Physical examination shows drooping of the left eyelid, tearing of the left eye, and rhinorrhea. The left pupil is 2 mm and the right pupil is 4 mm. There is localized tenderness along the right supraspinatus muscle. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 31-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 5-month history of intermittent flank pain. Over the past 2 years, they have had five urinary tract infections. Their blood pressure is 150/88 mm Hg. Physical examination shows bilateral, nontender upper abdominal masses. Serum studies show a urea nitrogen concentration of 29 mg/dL and a creatinine concentration of 1.4 mg/dL. Renal ultrasonography shows bilaterally enlarged kidneys with multiple parenchymal anechoic masses. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old patient comes to the physician for a 1-month history of fever, chest pain with deep breathing, and a 4-kg (9 lb) weight loss. Their temperature is 38°C (100.4°F). An x-ray of the chest shows a subpleural nodule in the right lower lobe with right hilar lymphadenopathy. Histological examination of a right hilar lymph node biopsy specimen shows several granulomas with acellular cores. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old patient comes to the physician because of palpitations, shortness of breath, diarrhea, and abdominal cramps for 2 months. Physical examination shows cutaneous flushing of the face. Auscultation of the chest shows bilateral wheezing. A 24-hour urine collection shows increased 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA) concentration. A contrast-enhanced CT scan of the abdomen shows an intestinal tumor with extensive metastasis to the liver. A diagnosis of an inoperable disease is made and the patient is started on treatment with octreotide. Six weeks later, the patient's symptoms have improved except for their abdominal pain and frequent loose stools. The physician suggests enrolling the patient in a trial to test additional treatment with a new drug that has been shown to improve symptoms in other patients with the same condition. The expected beneficial effect of this new drug is most likely caused by inhibition of which of the following?

A 46-year-old patient comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. Two weeks ago, they underwent laparoscopic herniorrhaphy for an indirect inguinal hernia. During the procedure, a black liver was noted. They have a history of intermittent scleral icterus that resolved without treatment. Serum studies show: Aspartate aminotransferase 30 IU/L Alanine aminotransferase 35 IU/L Alkaline phosphatase 47 mg/dL Total bilirubin 1.7 mg/dL Direct bilirubin 1.1 mg/dL Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 58-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 4-day history of abdominal pain and vomiting. Initially, the vomitus was food that they had recently eaten, but it is now bilious. They have had similar complaints several times in the past 6 years. They have smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the past 25 years and drinks 24 oz of alcohol daily. They are 160 cm (5 ft 3 in) tall and weigh 48 kg (105 lb); BMI is 19 kg/m2. Their vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows an epigastric mass. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parent because of irritability, mood swings, and difficulty sleeping over the past 10 days. A few days ago, they quit their job and spent all of their savings on supplies for a “genius business plan.” They have been energetic despite sleeping only 1–2 hours each night. They were diagnosed with major depressive disorder 2 years ago. Mental status examination shows pressured speech, a labile affect, and flight of ideas. Throughout the examination, they repeatedly state “I feel great, I don't need to be here.” Urine toxicology screening is negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a painless neck lump and a 2-month history of difficulty swallowing. They have a history of recurrent nephrolithiasis and episodic hypertension. Physical examination shows a 3 × 3-cm, nontender nodule at the level of the thyroid cartilage. A photomicrograph of a section of tissue obtained by core needle biopsy of the nodule is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old patient comes to the physician for evaluation of a lump in their left axilla that they first noticed 1 year ago. They report that the size of the mass has varied over time and that there have been similar masses in their neck and groin. They have not had fever, weight loss, or night sweats. Physical examination shows a nontender, rubbery mass in the left axilla and a similar, smaller mass in the right groin. Their spleen is palpable 3 cm below the left costal margin. Laboratory studies, including complete blood count, are within reference ranges. Genetic analysis obtained on resection of the axillary mass shows a t(14;18) translocation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parent because of a 2-week history of generalized fatigue, intermittent fever, and occasional bleeding from their nose. Their temperature is 38.3°C (100.9°F). They appear pale. Physical examination shows cervical lymphadenopathy and multiple petechiae on their trunk. The spleen is palpated 3 cm below the left costal margin. Their hemoglobin concentration is 9.3 g/dL, leukocyte count is 63,000/mm3, and platelet count is 30,000/mm3. A bone marrow aspirate predominantly shows immature leukocytes that stain positive for CD10, CD19, and terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase (TdT), and negative for myeloperoxidase. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old patient comes to the physician for evaluation of multiple red spots on their trunk. They first noticed these several months ago, and some appear to have increased in size. One day ago, they scratched one of these spots, and it bled for several minutes. Physical examination shows the findings in the photograph. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 59-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 1-year history of pain and stiffness in their fingers and knees. The stiffness lasts for about 10 minutes after they wake up in the morning. They also report that their knee pain is worse in the evening. They drink one glass of wine daily. Their only medication is acetaminophen. They are 175 cm (5 ft 9 in) tall and weigh 102 kg (225 lb); BMI is 33 kg/m2. Physical examination shows firm nodules on the distal interphalangeal joints of the index, ring, and little fingers of both hands. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old medical student comes to the physician with a 3-week history of night sweats and myalgias. During this time, they have also had a loss of 3.6-kg (8-lb) weight. They returned from a 6-month tropical medicine rotation in Cambodia 1 month ago. A chest x-ray (CXR) shows reticulonodular opacities suggestive of active tuberculosis (TB). The student is curious about their likelihood of having active TB. They read a study that compares sputum testing results between 2,800 patients with likely active TB on a basis of history, clinical symptoms, and CXR pattern and 2,400 controls. The results are shown: Sputum testing positive for TB Sputum testing negative for TB Total Active TB likely on basis of history, clinical symptoms, and CXR pattern 700 2100 2,800 Active TB not likely on basis of history, clinical symptoms, and CXR pattern 300 2100 2,400 Total 1000 4200 5,200 Which of the following values reflects the probability that a patient with a diagnosis of active TB on the basis of history, clinical symptoms, and CXR pattern actually has active TB?

A 4-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of a 1-month history of generalized fatigue. During the past week, they have also had fever and severe leg pain that keeps them awake at night. Examination shows cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy. Their liver is palpated 4 cm below the right costal margin and the spleen is palpated 3 cm below the left costal margin. Their hemoglobin concentration is 10.2 g/dL, leukocyte count is 64,500/mm3, and platelet count is 29,000/mm3. A bone marrow aspirate predominantly shows immature cells that stain positive for CD10, CD19, and TdT. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of generalized fatigue. On examination, they appear pale. They also have multiple pinpoint, red, nonblanching spots on their extremities. Their spleen is significantly enlarged. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin concentration of 8.3 g/dL, a leukocyte count of 81,000/mm3, and a platelet count of 35,600/mm3. A peripheral blood smear shows immature cells with large, prominent nucleoli and pink, elongated, needle-shaped cytoplasmic inclusions. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department 12 hours after the sudden onset of shortness of breath and substernal chest pain at rest; the pain is increased by inspiration. They have also had a nonproductive cough, fever, and malaise for the past 5 days. They do not smoke or use illicit drugs. Their temperature is 38°C (100.4°F), pulse is 125/min, respirations are 32/min, and blood pressure is 85/45 mm Hg. Physical examination shows distended neck veins. Auscultation of the chest discloses bilateral basilar rales and muffled heart sounds. An ECG shows sinus tachycardia, diffuse ST segment elevation, low voltage QRS complexes, and fluctuating R wave amplitude. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 15-year-old patient comes to the physician for the evaluation of a painless swelling under the left lower jaw for 5 months. Their 18-year-old sibling has a history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia that has been in remission for 11 years. The patient's temperature is 37°C (98.6°F). Physical examination shows a 3 × 2 cm swelling on the left side, 4 cm below the base of the mandible and anterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle. The swelling is soft and fluctuant. It does not move with swallowing, and forced exhalation against a closed glottis does not increase the size of the swelling. Ultrasound shows a round mass with uniform low echogenicity and no internal septations. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old patient comes to the emergency department because of a 3-day history of pain in the left cheek. The pain occurs every few hours, lasts 30–60 seconds, and is aggravated by chewing and brushing. They have a history of pain with a vesicular rash in the right axillary area one year ago. They had an upper respiratory infection 2 weeks ago. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 51-year-old patient comes to the emergency department because of a 1-day history of severe pain in their left knee. To lose weight, they recently started jogging for 30 minutes a few times per week. They have type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension treated with metformin and chlorothiazide. Their sibling has rheumatoid arthritis. They are sexually active with two partners and use condoms inconsistently. On examination, their temperature is 38.5°C (101.3°F), pulse is 88/min, and blood pressure is 138/87 mm Hg. The left knee is swollen and tender to palpation with a significantly impaired range of motion. A 1.5-cm, painless ulcer is seen on the plantar surface of the left foot. Which of the following is most likely to help establish the diagnosis?

A 26-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their spouse because of bizarre and agitated behavior for the last 6 weeks. They think that the NSA is spying on them and controlling their mind. Their spouse reports that the patient has become withdrawn and at times depressed for the past 3 months. They lost their job because they stopped going to work 4 weeks ago. Since then, they have been working on an invention that will block people from being able to control their mind. Physical and neurologic examinations show no abnormalities. On mental status examination, they are confused and suspicious with marked psychomotor agitation. Their speech is disorganized and their affect is labile. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 11-year-old patient comes to the physician with their parent because of a 2-day history of passing “cola-colored“ urine. During the past week, their parent noticed episodes of facial swelling. The patient had a rash on their face about 4 weeks ago. A renal biopsy after immunofluorescence is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of fatigue, muscle weakness, paresthesias, headache, and palpitations. Their pulse is 75/min and blood pressure is 152/94 mm Hg. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Serum studies show: Sodium 144 mEq/L Potassium 2.9 mEq/L Bicarbonate 31 mEq/L Creatinine 0.7 mg/dL Further evaluation shows low serum renin activity. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parent because of generalized weakness and difficulty walking for the past month. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin concentration of 6.6 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume of 74 μm3, platelet count of 150,000/mm3, and serum total bilirubin of 2 mg/dl. An MRI of the spine shows low signal intensity in all vertebral bodies and a small epidural mass compressing the spinal canal at the level of L1. A CT scan of the head shows osteopenia with widening of the diploic spaces in the skull. A biopsy of the epidural mass shows erythroid colonies with an abundance of megakaryocytes and myeloid cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 11-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parents because of a mildly pruritic rash on their trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, they developed a low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache, followed by a facial rash 4 days later. The facial rash did not involve the perioral skin. Their temperature is 37.4°C (99.3°F). A photograph of the rash on their lower arms is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old patient comes to the emergency department because of a 12-hour history of a severe headache. They do not smoke or use illicit drugs. Their blood pressure at admission is 180/125 mm Hg. Physical examination shows a bruit in the epigastric region. Fundoscopy shows bilateral optic disc swelling. Which of the following investigations is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 58-year-old white patient with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of a painless lesion on their lower lip. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 20 years. They have worked as a fruit picker for the past 25 years. Their current medications include captopril and metformin. Examination of the oral cavity shows a single ulcer near the vermillion border. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 21-year-old patient comes to the physician because of nervousness and difficulty sleeping over the past 2 weeks. Three months ago, they started a new team project at their job. They say that they have trouble falling asleep at night because they think about the project. They insist on checking the work of their teammates and spend several hours each week making elaborate lists and schedules. They refuse to let others take on more tasks because they think that only they can complete them satisfactorily. The project deadline has already been postponed once. They say, “My teammates never understand how important it is to do things the right way.” Ever since high school, they have used the majority of their time to plan out assignments and do not have time to regularly participate in social activities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An otherwise healthy 25-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of intermittent palpitations and worsening shortness of breath on exertion. They have not had chest pain or nocturnal dyspnea. The patient is 195 cm (6 ft 5 in) tall and weighs 70 kg (154 lbs); BMI is 18.4 kg/m2. Their pulse is 110/min and blood pressure is 140/60 mm Hg. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Cardiac examination is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 31-year-old patient comes to the emergency department because of chest pain for the last 3 hours. They describe the pain as a sharp, substernal chest pain that radiates to the right shoulder; they say “Please help me. I'm having a heart attack.” They have been admitted to the hospital twice over the past week for evaluation of shortness of breath and abdominal pain but left the hospital the following day on both occasions. The patient does not smoke or drink alcohol but is a known user of intravenous heroin. They have been living in a homeless shelter for the past 2 weeks after being evicted from their apartment for failure to pay rent. Their temperature is 37.6°C (99.6°F), pulse is 90/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 125/85 mm Hg. The patient seems anxious and refuses a physical examination of their chest. Their cardiac troponin I concentration is 0.01 ng/mL (N = 0–0.01). An ECG shows a normal sinus rhythm with nonspecific ST-T wave changes. While the physician is planning to discharge the patient, the patient reports numbness in their arm and insists on being admitted to the ward. On the following day, the patient leaves the hospital without informing the physician or the nursing staff. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their neighbors 30 minutes after they found them unconscious in their yard. Their neighbors report that they have been spending more time at home by themselves because they recently lost their job. On arrival, they are unable to provide a history. They appear anxious. Their pulse is 76/min, respirations are 13/min, and blood pressure is 114/72 mm Hg. Examination shows significant weakness of the left upper and lower extremities. They are unable to plantarflex the ankle while supine. They are able to stand on their toes. Their gait is unsteady. Deep tendon reflexes are 3+ and symmetric. A CT scan of the head shows no abnormalities. An MRI of the brain and MR angiography show no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their parent because of a sudden loss of consciousness. They have asthma and have been hospitalized multiple times. Their parent has type 2 diabetes mellitus. They are somnolent and diaphoretic. Serum studies show a glucose concentration of 22 mg/dL and a potassium concentration of 2.4 mEq/L. A dextrose infusion is administered, after which their glucose concentration normalizes and their symptoms improve. They are admitted to the hospital for further observation. Overnight, they have another episode of decreased consciousness. Serum studies taken during the episode show a glucose concentration of 19 mg/dL, an insulin concentration of 108 mIU/L (N=2.6–24.9), and a C-peptide concentration of 0.3 ng/mL (N = 0.8–3.1). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 64-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department because of a 2-hour history of nausea, vomiting, and retrosternal pain that radiates to the back. Abdominal examination shows tenderness to palpation in the epigastric area. A CT scan of the patient's chest is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old patient comes to the physician because of an episode of bloody vomiting this morning and a 1-week history of burning upper abdominal pain. Two weeks ago, they sustained a head injury and was in a coma for 3 days. An endoscopy shows multiple, shallow hemorrhagic lesions predominantly in the gastric fundus and greater curvature. Biopsies show patchy loss of epithelium and an acute inflammatory infiltrate in the lamina propria that does not extend beyond the muscularis mucosa. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old patient comes to the emergency department because of dizziness, nausea, and vomiting for 4 days. Their temperature is 37.3°C (99.1°F), pulse is 100/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Arterial blood gas analysis on room air shows: pH 7.58 PCO2 43 mm Hg PO2 96 mm Hg HCO3- 32 mEq/L The most appropriate next step in diagnosis is measurement of which of the following?

A 55-year-old patient comes to the physician because of fatigue and worsening abdominal pain for 4 weeks. They also report excessive night sweats and a 5.4-kg (12-lb) weight loss during this time. They have a neck swelling for 4 days. Physical examination shows a nontender, enlarged, and fixed supraclavicular lymph node. There is splenomegaly. A CT scan of the thorax and abdomen shows massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Analysis of an excised cervical lymph node shows lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 47-year-old patient comes to the physician because of body aches for the past 9 months. They also have stiffness of the shoulders and knees that is worse in the morning and tingling in the upper extremities. Examination shows marked tenderness over the posterior neck, bilateral mid trapezius, and medial aspect of the left knee. A complete blood count and erythrocyte sedimentation rate are within the reference ranges. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae and then spread to their trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, they were diagnosed with acute sinusitis and were started on amoxicillin. They have no history of adverse drug reactions and immunizations are up-to-date. Their temperature is 37.5°C (99.5°F), pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. Physical examination shows periorbital edema and multiple erythematous, annular plaques of variable sizes over their entire body. One of the lesions in the right popliteal fossa has an area of central clearing and the patient's mother reports that it has been present for over 24 hours. Urinalysis is normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 5-month history of a pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. They have no history of serious illness and take no medications. A skin biopsy of the rash shows intraepidermal accumulation of edematous fluid and widening of intercellular spaces between keratinocytes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 71-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 4-month history of worsening cough and a 4.5-kg (10-lb) weight loss. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 35 years. Physical examination shows wheezing over the right lung fields. Laboratory studies show a serum calcium concentration of 12.5 mg/dL. X-rays of the chest are shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a progressive swelling and pain in their right ring finger for the past 2 days. The pain began while playing football, when their finger got caught in the jersey of another player who forcefully pulled away. Examination shows that the right ring finger is extended. There is pain and swelling at the distal interphalangeal joint. When the patient is asked to make a fist, their right ring finger does not flex at the distal interphalangeal joint. There is no joint laxity. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 69-year-old white patient comes to the physician because of a 15-day history of fatigue and lower leg swelling. Over the past 8 months, they have had a 3.8-kg (8.3-lb) weight loss. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 48 years. Vital signs are within normal limits. They appear thin. Examination shows 2+ pretibial edema bilaterally. An x-ray of the chest shows a right upper lobe density. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 11.3 g/dL Leukocyte count 8600/mm3 Platelet count 140,000/mm3 Serum Urea nitrogen 25 mg/dL Glucose 79 mg/dL Creatinine 1.7 mg/dL Albumin 1.6 mg/dL Total cholesterol 479 mg/dL Urine Blood negative Glucose negative Protein 4+ WBC 0–1/hpf Fatty casts numerous Light microscopic examination of a kidney biopsy reveals thickening of glomerular capillary loops and the basal membrane. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 49-year-old patient comes to the physician with a 2-month history of mild abdominal pain, nausea, and several episodes of vomiting. They often feel full after eating only a small amount of food. Abdominal examination shows mild right upper quadrant tenderness and a liver span of 16 cm. Ultrasonography shows a 5 x 4 cm hyperechoic mass in the left lobe of the liver. The mass is surgically excised. A photomicrograph of the resected specimen is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-month-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their parent because of an 8-hour history of difficulty feeding and decreased arousability. Their parent says that the symptoms began after they rolled over and fell from the bed. Their vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows regions of purple discoloration in the T4–T10 dermatomes bilaterally and tense fontanelles. Fundoscopy shows bilateral optic disc swelling with dot-and-blot hemorrhages extending to the ora serrata. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old patient reports swelling and pain in their right leg, three days after undergoing laparoscopic colectomy. They were diagnosed with colon cancer 1 month ago. Their temperature is 38.5°C (101.3°F). Physical examination shows swelling of the right leg from the ankle to the thigh. There is no erythema or rash. Which of the following is likely to be most helpful in establishing the diagnosis?

A previously healthy 25-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 3-week history of fever, recurrent headaches, and anorexia. One month ago, they returned from a camping trip in Chile. Their temperature is 39.3°C (102.8°F). Examination shows a swelling in the left periorbital region and axillary, cervical, and inguinal lymphadenopathy. A blood sample is obtained. Processing of the sample with which of the following methods is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A previously healthy 4-year-old patient is brought to the physician for evaluation of a 3-week history of recurrent vomiting and difficulty walking. Examination shows a broad-based gait and bilateral optic disc swelling. An MRI shows an intracranial tumor. A ventriculoperitoneal shunt is placed, and surgical excision of the tumor is performed. A photomicrograph of a section of the tumor is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 1-month history of double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and weakness when trying to brush their hair. They report that these symptoms are worse after they exercise and disappear after they rest for a few hours. Physical examination shows drooping of their right upper eyelid that worsens when the patient is asked to gaze at the ceiling for 2 minutes. There is diminished motor strength in the upper extremities. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 13-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of a 4-month history of worsening dizziness, nausea, and feeling clumsy. An MRI of the brain shows a well-demarcated, 4-cm cystic mass in the posterior fossa. The patient undergoes complete surgical resection of the mass. Pathologic examination of the surgical specimen shows parallel bundles of cells with eosinophilic, corkscrew-like processes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 69-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 3-week history of headache and worsening vision. Ophthalmologic examination shows a visual acuity of 20/120 in the right eye and 20/80 in the left eye. Physical examination shows no other abnormalities. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin of 14.2 g/dL and total serum calcium of 9.9 mg/dL. A photomicrograph of a peripheral blood smear is shown. Serum electrophoresis shows increased concentration of a pentameric immunoglobulin. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their mother because she has been worried about her child's strange behavior for the past 2 years. They do not have any friends and spend most of their time alone in their room. They usually wear a long, black, hooded cloak. They are anxious at college because they are uncomfortable around other people, and their academic performance is poor. They collect rare crystals and say that they support their “sixth sense.” Mental status examination shows slow, hesitant speech, and they avoid eye contact. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 18-month-old patient is brought to the physician by their parent because of a 2-day history of fever and a pruritic rash that started on their trunk and then progressed to their face and extremities. They have not received any childhood vaccinations because their parents believe that they are dangerous. Their temperature is 38.0°C (100.4°F). A photograph of the rash is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by ambulance 30 minutes after their neighbor found them unconscious on a running trail. Their neighbor reports that they have been training for a marathon since the beginning of the summer. They are alert and oriented but become irritable when realizing that they are at a hospital and refuse to answer questions. They appear tired. They are 174 cm (5 ft 7 in) tall and weigh 51 kg (112 lb). Their temperature is 35.5°C (96°F), pulse is 44/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 84/48 mm Hg. Examination shows dry, scaly skin and dry mucous membranes. Cardiopulmonary examination shows a high-frequency, mid-to-late systolic murmur that is heard best at the apex. Their hemoglobin concentration is 11.9 g/dL. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 2-year-old patient is brought to the emergency room by their parent because of persistent crying and refusal to move their right arm. The episode began 30 minutes ago after the parent lifted them up by the arms. They appear distressed and are inconsolable. On examination, their right arm is held close to their body in a flexed and pronated position. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An otherwise healthy 45-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 1-year history of episodic abdominal cramps, bloating, and flatulence. The symptoms worsen when they have pizza or ice cream and have become more frequent over the past 4 months. Lactose intolerance is suspected. Which of the following findings would most strongly support the diagnosis of lactose intolerance?

A 38-year-old patient comes to the physician because of persistent sadness and difficulty concentrating for the past 6 weeks. During this period, they have also had difficulty sleeping. They add that they have been “feeling down” most of the time since their partner broke up with them 4 years ago. Since then, they have only had a few periods of time when they did not feel that way, but none of these lasted for more than a month. They report having no problems with appetite, weight, or energy. They do not use illicit drugs or alcohol. Mental status examination shows a depressed mood and constricted affect. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old patient comes to the physician with a 3-month history of right flank pain. Urinalysis shows 60 RBC/hpf. Renal ultrasound shows a 3 cm, well-defined mass in the upper pole of the right kidney. A photomicrograph of a section of the resected mass is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parent because of painless lesions on their face that they have had since shortly after birth. They recently moved to the USA from Indonesia where they had limited access to healthcare. A photograph of the lesions is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 16-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their host parents for evaluation of a progressively pruritic rash over their shoulders and buttocks for the past 6 months. They recently came to the United States from Nigeria to attend a year of high school. They report that it has been increasingly difficult for them to read the whiteboard during classes. Physical examination shows symmetrically distributed papules 4–8 mm in diameter, excoriation marks, and patchy hyperpigmentation over their shoulders, waist, and buttocks. There is nontender inguinal lymphadenopathy and several firm, nontender subcutaneous nodules along the right iliac crest. Six skin snip biopsies are taken from the pelvic girdle, buttocks, and thigh, and are then incubated in saline. After 24 hours, microscopic examination shows motile microfilariae. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old patient comes to the physician because of fatigue and a 5-kg (11-lb) weight loss over the past 6 months despite a good appetite. They take no medications. They do not smoke or use illicit drugs. Physical examination shows hepatosplenomegaly and diffuse, nontender lymphadenopathy. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin concentration of 11 g/dL and a leukocyte count of 16,000/mm3. A direct antiglobulin (Coombs) test is positive. A photomicrograph of a peripheral blood smear is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old patient is brought to the physician for intermittent fevers and painful swelling of the left ankle for 2 weeks. They have no history of trauma to the ankle. They have a history of sickle cell disease. Current medications include hydroxyurea and acetaminophen for pain. Their temperature is 38.4°C (101.2°F) and pulse is 112/min. Examination shows a tender, swollen, and erythematous left ankle with point tenderness over the medial malleolus. A bone biopsy culture confirms the diagnosis. Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?

A 38-year-old patient comes to the emergency department because of progressive headache, blurry vision, and nausea for 1 day. Four days ago, they were diagnosed with a right middle ear infection. They appear lethargic. Their temperature is 39.1°C (102.3°F), and blood pressure is 148/95 mm Hg. Ophthalmologic examination shows bilateral swelling of the optic disc. The corneal reflex in the right eye is absent. Sensation to touch is reduced on the upper right side of the face. Serum studies show increased concentrations of fibrin degradation products. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old patient who emigrated from Pakistan 2 weeks ago is brought to the emergency department because of lower limb weakness for one day. One week ago, they had a 3-day episode of flu-like symptoms that resolved without treatment. They have not yet received any routine childhood vaccinations. Deep tendon reflexes are 1+ in the right lower extremity and absent in the left lower extremity. Analysis of cerebrospinal fluid shows a leukocyte count of 38 cells/mm3 (68% lymphocytes), a protein concentration of 49 mg/dL, and a glucose concentration of 60 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 66-year-old patient comes to the physician for a follow-up examination after a below-knee amputation of the right lower leg. Three weeks ago, they had an acute arterial embolism that could not be revascularized in time to save the leg. They now report episodic hot, shooting, and tingling pain in the right lower leg that began shortly after the amputation. They have type 2 diabetes mellitus. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the past 30 years. Their current medications are metformin and prophylactic subcutaneous heparin. Their temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 78/min, and blood pressure is 135/88 mm Hg. Physical examination shows a slightly erythematous stump with clean sutures. The skin overlying the stump is warm and well-perfused. Muscle strength and sensation are normal throughout the remaining extremity and the left lower extremity. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 16-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parent because of concerns about their behavior during the past 2 years. They do not have friends and spend most of the time reading by themselves. Their parent says that they come up with excuses to avoid family dinners and other social events. They state that they like reading and feel more comfortable on their own. On mental status examination, their thought process is organized and logical. Their affect is flat. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old patient comes to the physician because of progressive swelling of the left lower leg for 4 months. One year ago, they had an episode of intermittent fever and tender lymphadenopathy that occurred shortly after they returned from a trip to India and resolved spontaneously. Physical examination shows 4+ nonpitting edema of the left lower leg. Their leukocyte count is 8,000/mm3 with 25% eosinophils. A blood smear obtained at night confirms the diagnosis. Treatment with diethylcarbamazine is initiated. Which of the following is the most likely route of transmission of the causal pathogen?

A 62-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of 6 months of progressive weakness in their arms and legs. During this time, they have also had difficulty swallowing and holding their head up. Examination shows pooling of oral secretions. Muscle strength and tone are decreased in the upper extremities. Deep tendon reflexes are 1+ in the right upper and lower extremities, 3+ in the left upper extremity, and 4+ in the left lower extremity. Sensation to light touch, pinprick, and vibration are intact. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 56-year-old patient comes to the physician for a follow-up examination one week after a chest x-ray showed a solitary pulmonary nodule. They have no history of major medical illness. They have smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the past 30 years. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. A tuberculin skin test is negative. A CT scan of the chest shows a 2.1-cm well-circumscribed, calcified nodule in the periphery of the right lower lung field. A CT-guided biopsy of the lesion is performed. Histological examination of the biopsy specimen shows regions of disorganized hyaline cartilage interspersed with myxoid regions and clefts of ciliated epithelium. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 81-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their daughter after they were found wandering on the street. For the last 3 months, they often have a blank stare for several minutes. They also claim to have seen strangers in the house on several occasions who were not present. They have hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and were diagnosed with Parkinson disease 8 months ago. Their current medications include carbidopa-levodopa, hydrochlorothiazide, and atorvastatin. Their blood pressure is 150/85 mm Hg. They have short-term memory deficits and appear confused and disheveled. Examination shows bilateral muscle rigidity and resting tremor in their upper extremities. They have a slow gait with short steps. Microscopic examination of the cortex of a patient with the same condition is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 39-year-old patient with a history of migraine headaches is brought to the emergency room because of a severe, sudden-onset, throbbing headache and double vision for 1 hour. They say that they have been having frequent headaches. Their blood pressure is 93/61 mm Hg. Visual field testing shows decreased visual acuity and loss of peripheral vision in both eyes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 61-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of intermittent fever, easy fatiguability, and a 4.4-kg (9.7-lb) weight loss. Physical examination shows conjunctival pallor. The spleen is palpated 5 cm below the left costal margin. Laboratory studies show a leukocyte count of 75,300/mm3 with increased basophils, a platelet count of 455,000/mm3, and a decreased leukocyte alkaline phosphatase score. A peripheral blood smear shows increased numbers of promyelocytes, myelocytes, and metamyelocytes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 59-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after having a seizure. Their partner reports that the patient has been having recurrent headaches and has become increasingly irritable over the past 3 months. Physical examination shows a spastic paresis of the right lower extremity. The Babinski sign is present on the right side. An MRI of the brain is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of fatigue, weight loss, and multiple painless swellings on their neck and axilla. They report that their swellings become painful after they drink alcohol. Physical examination shows nontender cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy. A lymph node biopsy specimen shows giant binucleate cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parent for the evaluation of abdominal pain and trouble sleeping for the past 6 months. Their parent says they complain of crampy abdominal pain every morning on school days. They started attending a new school 7 months ago and their parent is concerned because they have missed school frequently due to the abdominal pain. They also have trouble falling asleep at night and ask to sleep in the same room with their parents every night. They have not had fever, vomiting, diarrhea, or weight loss. They sit very close to their parent and start to cry when their parent steps out of the room to take a phone call. Abdominal examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A pathologist receives a patient sample for analysis. Cells in the sample are first labeled with fluorescent antibodies and then passed across a laser beam in a single file of particles. The light scatter and fluorescent intensity of the particles are plotted on a graph; this information is used to characterize the sample. This laboratory method would be most useful to establish the diagnosis of a patient with which of the following?

A 44-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 3-week history of productive cough, fever, and lethargy. They also have several skin lesions over their body. Their symptoms began 3 weeks after they returned from a camping trip in Kentucky. Three years ago, they underwent kidney transplantation for polycystic kidney disease. Current medications include sirolimus and prednisone. Their temperature is 38°C (100.4°F). Diffuse crackles are heard over the lung fields. There are 4 white, verrucous skin patches over their chest and upper limbs. A photomicrograph of a skin biopsy specimen from one of the lesions is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 61-year-old patient comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of a cough productive of clear mucoid sputum. They have smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 33 years. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Chest x-ray shows a 2-cm solid nodule in the periphery of the lower left lobe. A bronchial biopsy of the mass shows numerous mucin-filled epithelial cells lining the alveolar basement membrane. The cells have prominent nucleoli, coarse chromatin, and some cells have multiple nuclei. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parent because they claim to have spoken to their recently-deceased grandfather. The grandfather, who lived with the family and frequently watched the patient for their parents, died 2 months ago. The patient was taken out of preschool for 3 days after their grandfather's death but has since returned. Their teachers report that the patient is currently doing well, completing their assignments, and engaging in play with other children. When asked about how they feel, the patient becomes tearful and says, “I miss my grandpa. I sometimes talk to them when my parent is not around.” Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician after an injury during a rugby game. The patient states that they were tackled and ever since then has had pain in their knee. The patient has tried NSAIDs and ice to no avail. The patient has no past medical history and is currently taking a multivitamin, fish oil, and a whey protein supplement. On physical exam you note a knee that is heavily bruised. It is painful for the patient to bear weight on the knee, and passive motion of the knee elicits some pain. There is laxity at the knee to varus stress. The patient is wondering when they can return to athletics. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old patient presents to clinic in emotional distress. They state they have been unhappy for the past couple of months and are having problems with their sleep and appetite. Additionally, they report significant anxiety regarding thoughts of dirtiness around the house. They state that they clean all of the doorknobs 5-10 times per day and that, despite their actions, the stress related to cleaning is becoming worse. What is this patient's diagnosis?

A 17-year-old patient presents to the emergency department for eye pain. The patient states that they have had left eye pain for the past week that has been steadily worsening. The patient denies any changes to their vision, trouble moving their left eye, or recent trauma. The patient smokes one pack of cigarettes a day, drinks alcohol socially, and has had unprotected sex with six partners this past month. Their current medications include loratadine, nasal saline spray, and diphenhydramine. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 100/55 mmHg, pulse is 72/min, respirations are 11/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. On physical exam, you note a healthy young patient. Cardiopulmonary exam is within normal limits. Their physical exam reveals the finding in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient comes into your office for an eye exam. The patient states they have had some trouble seeing over the last few weeks. They deny a history of pain. They have a history of HIV. They state that they were diagnosed with HIV about 20 years ago due to their intravenous drug usage. They have not used any drugs in the past 10 years, but state they also do not take their medications. Their last CD4+ count (6 months ago) was 42. Their vitals are normal and Figure A shows their fundoscopic exam. On eye exam, the patient has both some central and peripheral vision loss. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient is brought to the emergency room by their spouse because they have been acting confused for the past day. They are febrile, with an oral temperature of 103.6 deg F; vital signs are otherwise stable. Their physical exam is significant for the finding shown in Figure A; they have never noticed lesions like these before. They also have subtle right-sided weakness affecting upper and lower extremities. Labs reveal: hemoglobin 7.0 g/dL, hematocrit 21%, white blood count of 10.2 x 10^3 µL, and platelet count of 20 x 10^3 per µL. PT/INR and PTT are normal. A peripheral blood smear is shown in Figure B. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A parent brings their 4-year-old child to the pediatrician. Over the last eight months, the child has been exhibiting several "odd" behaviors. Most importantly, they repeatedly say that they are playing games with a friend named "Steven," though the parent is certain that they do not exist. The parent has often found them acting out magical scenarios as though someone else is present, when no one is there. What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 25-year-old patient presents to your clinic in significant distress. They state they have excruciating, stabbing pain around the left side of their head, and their left eye will not stop tearing. These types of headaches have been occurring for the past week every morning when they awaken and last around 60 minutes. They deny any aura, nausea, or vomiting. They deny any other past medical history. What is this patient's diagnosis?

A 22-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with itchy eyes. The patient recently moved to the northern US and states that they have experienced bilateral itching and watering of their eyes. They state that it is very distracting and is making it hard for them to work. The patient denies any recent sick contacts and lives alone. They work as a machinist and are currently struggling with their finances. The patient has a past medical history of asthma, and their current medications include albuterol, fluticasone, fish oil, and whey protein supplements. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 100/65 mmHg, pulse is 60/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Cardiopulmonary exam is within normal limits. You notice the bilateral findings seen in Figure A. Otoscopy reveals bilateral clear tympanic membranes. The rest of the patient's physical exam is within normal limits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 52-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician. The patient has been feeling very tired lately and thinks that they look more pale. The physician orders a complete blood count, which shows: Hgb 8.5 g/dL; WBC 1,200/microliter; platelets 70,000/microliter. The patient is referred for bone marrow biopsy, which shows the findings in Figure A. Which of the following is the correct diagnosis?

A 68-year-old patient presents with a 6-month history of worsening fatigue and weight loss. They are especially concerned about a recent episode in which they noticed a blurring of their vision and headache; they also note that their “memory is not as good as it used to be,” which their partner confirms. Physical exam is notable only for pallor and general weakness. Laboratory studies reveal anemia as well as an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate. Serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP) reveals a sharp, narrow spike of monoclonal IgM; serum IgM concentration is 6.3 g/dL. What is the most likely diagnosis in this case?

A 45-year-old non-English-speaking, Asian patient presents to your office. They show you a lesion on their elbow (Figure A). They have been having decreased sensation in that area and now cannot feel sharp pinpricks on your physical exam. The lesion is biopsied (Figure B). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old patient with a history of chronic kidney disease presents to their primary care physician complaining of recurrent chest pain with activity. The patient used to have chest pain when they mowed their lawn. Now they get chest pain whenever they walk short distances such as to get their mail. The pain resolves on its own when the patient sits and rests. Their temperature is 98.2°F (36.8°C), blood pressure is 157/98 mm Hg, pulse is 80/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for an obese patient who is in no distress. An initial ECG is unchanged from a previous ECG. The patient's first troponin is 0.06 ng/mL which is unchanged from previous troponins. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old African American patient is brought into the emergency department by their parent. The parent states that the patient was diagnosed with a urinary tract infection by their PCP and provided with medications a few days ago. Today, they started having abdominal pain and shortness of breath. On exam, the patient has normal vitals, but has mild jaundice and states that they are short of breath. Their parent states that their relative had had a similar episode when they were treated for malaria. The patient's CBC is significant for a hemoglobin of 8.7 and their MCV is 90. Figure A shows the peripheral smear. Coombs test is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old patient is brought to the pediatrician by their parent for complaints of a diffuse, itchy rash over their abdomen, back, and upper legs. The rash first appeared about 1 week ago. They have otherwise been well, and they have no known sick contacts. On exam they are afebrile and cooperative. Their skin exam (Figure A) is notable for a single large, well-circumscribed pink plaque over their mid-abdomen, and many pink papules of varying sizes over their abdomen, back, and thighs. On follow-up a month later, the rash has largely resolved without intervention. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old patient presents to the emergency department complaining of ear pain. They state it started a few days ago and it has been gradually worsening. They also endorse subjective fevers and neck stiffness. The patient is an adamant swimmer and swims 2-3 times per day. They have a history of diabetes, hypertension, and morbid obesity. Their temperature is 103°F (39.4°C), blood pressure is 177/99 mmHg, pulse is 110/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for weakness and tingling in their hand. The patient is an avid bodybuilder and has noticed that their grip strength has gradually worsened in both hands with symptoms worse at the end of a long workout. The patient has a past medical history of anabolic steroid use in high school. Their current medications include a multivitamin, fish oil, and whey protein supplements. On physical exam, you note a muscular patient. The patient has a loss of sensation bilaterally over the volar surface of the 4th and 5th digits and over the medial aspect of the volar forearm. The patient has 3/5 grip strength of their left hand and 2/5 grip strength of their right hand. There is also notable weakness of finger adduction and abduction. The rest of the patient's physical exam is within normal limits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old patient comes into your clinic with a new concern. They state that about 20 years ago, they were shot in their right quadriceps while serving in the military. Since then, they have had a wound that partially heals, but has never closed completely. Now, the patient describes the wound as somewhat different. They state it is ulcerated with elevated edges and has been bleeding. You perform a full thickness biopsy of the lesion as shown in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old high school student presents to your office for recent mood and skin changes. The patient is a high school senior who is competing on the wrestling team and recently has lost weight to drop two weight classes over the past several months. They state they have dry, cracking, and irritated skin, as well as a sensation of tingling in their hands and feet. The patient also states that they have not been feeling themselves lately. They find themselves more irritable and no longer enjoy many of the activities they once enjoyed. They find that they often feel fatigued and have trouble concentrating. The patient does not have a significant past medical history and is not on any current medications. The patient admits to drinking alcohol and smoking marijuana on special occasions. They state that they use supplements that their other team members use. Physical exam is significant for acne, dry, cracked skin around the patient's mouth in particular, and decreased sensation in their lower extremities. Laboratory values are as follows: Serum: Na+: 137 mEq/L Cl-: 101 mEq/L K+: 4.1 mEq/L HCO3-: 24 mEq/L BUN: 15 mg/dL Glucose: 79 mg/dL Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL Ca2+: 9.2 mg/dL Mg2+: 1.5 mEq/L Homocysteine: 11.2 µmol/L (normal: 4.6 to 8.1 µmol/L) AST: 11 U/L ALT: 11 U/L Alkaline phosphatase: 27 U/L Albumin: 4.5 g/dL Total protein: 6.9 g/dL Total bilirubin: 0.5 mg/dL Direct bilirubin: 0.3 mg/dL Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 18-year-old patient comes to see their primary care physician for a physical for school. They state they have not had any illnesses last year and are on their school's volleyball team. They exercise daily, do not use any drugs, and have never smoked cigarettes. On physical exam you note bruising around the patient's neck, and what seems to be burn marks on their back and thighs. The physician inquires about these marks. The patient explains that these marks are the result of their sexual activities. They state that in order for them to be aroused they have to engage in acts such as hitting, choking, or anything else that they can think of. The physician learns that the patient lives with their partner and that they are in a very committed relationship. They are currently monogamous with this partner. The patient is studying with the hopes of going to law school and is currently working in a coffee shop. The rest of the patient’s history and physical is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old patient presents to their family physician with a complaint of painful joints for the past 2 weeks. They report symmetric bilateral joint pain in their hands, knees, and ankles. They have never had this before, and their past medical history is notable only for asthma. They state the pain is worse in the morning and improves throughout the day. Review of systems is notable for a recent low-grade fever with malaise. They work as a school teacher and are sexually active. Their temperature is 97.9°F (36.6°C), blood pressure is 120/84 mmHg, pulse is 70/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. The patient is instructed to take ibuprofen and acetaminophen for their joint pain. They return 1 month later stating that they have not needed to take the medications as their pain has been absent for the past 3 days. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old patient with no significant medical history comes to your office complaining of pain and stiffness in their hands upon wakening in the morning. You perform an x-ray (Figure A). What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 75-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with a painful rash. They note their side began to hurt several days prior without any visible skin changes; however, over the past 2 days a rash has developed. The patient's past medical history is only notable for diabetes mellitus type II. They were recently started on an antibiotic for sinusitis as well. In their spare time, they go hiking and recently returned from a hiking trip 2 days ago. They are currently sexually active. Their temperature is 99.0°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 154/88 mmHg, pulse is 83/min, respirations are 12/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient with no significant medical history comes to your office complaining of pain and stiffness in their hands upon wakening in the morning for the past several months. The stiffness generally lasts one to two hours, per the patient. You perform an x-ray (Figure A). What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with shortness of breath. The patient has had worsening shortness of breath for the past year. They have a past medical history of asthma and constipation. Their current medications include albuterol and sodium docusate. The patient was an officer in the navy and currently lives at home with their spouse. They have a 52 pack-year smoking history. Pulmonary function testing is performed at this visit as revealed in Figure A. The results of this test at this visit are revealed by the blue loop, as compared to their results 12 years ago as seen in the green dotted loop of Figure A. Which of the following is a possible diagnosis for this patient's presentation?

A 49-year-old patient complains of no symptoms, but on a routine complete blood count (CBC) has a white blood cell count of 40,000 per uL. A peripheral blood smear demonstrates leukocytosis with myeloid cells present at various stages of differentiation, with more mature cells present at a greater percentage than less mature cells (Figure A). What is the likely diagnosis?

A 1-week old child is brought into your office for a normal check-up when you notice bruising on their arm. The parent states the child was born at home and had a "natural birth". They also state that the child is eating and having yellow seedy stools 4-8 times per day. They took lamotrigine for their seizures, but they had regular check-ups and were told everything was normal. They do state that they have noticed that the child bruises easily. On exam, the vitals are normal, but the child has pin-point spots on their arms where they were held by the parent that do not disappear with pressure (Figure A). Their PT and aPTT are elevated, but the bleeding time is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient comes to your office complaining of white spots on their tongue. They report that they first noticed them about one week ago. They deny pain or difficulty swallowing. Their past medical history is significant for asthma, hepatitis C, and heroin abuse. They had previously been homeless and only recently went to the doctor one month ago for the first time in over five years. At that time, their primary care physician prescribed sofosbuvir, an albuterol inhaler, and daily inhaled fluticasone, which they have been using as directed. They are sexually active with one partner. Their last HIV test was negative, and they do not have a history of sexually transmitted diseases. They deny current alcohol or intravenous drug use. They smoke a pack a day of cigarettes and report they have been smoking since they were 16. On physical examination, you note lesions on the oral mucosa that are easily scraped off, as shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the best treatment for this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old athlete comes into your office for pain in their right foot. They state that they have no prior medical history and take no medications. They are an avid runner and runs in marathons, but recently switched to barefoot running from their normal shoes. They run around 50 miles per week and states that their pain is getting worse and worse with each run. On exam, their vitals are within normal limits, but there is pain upon palpation of the second metatarsal of their right foot. Their pulses and sensation are intact in all extremities. Figure A is an anteriorposterior (AP) radiograph of their right foot. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by ambulance. The patient was found unconscious in their bedroom after a suicide attempt. The patient had cut their wrists using a kitchen knife. The patient is unresponsive and pale. Their temperature is 96°F (35.6°C), blood pressure is 70/35 mmHg, pulse is 190/min, respirations are 19/min, and oxygen saturation is 92% on room air. Pressure is applied to their bilateral wrist lacerations. Their Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) is 7. A full trauma assessment is performed and reveals no other injuries. IV fluids are started as well as a rapid transfusion sequence. Norepinephrine is administered. Repeat vitals demonstrate that their blood pressure is 100/65 mmHg and pulse is 100/min. The patient is responsive and seems mildly confused. Resuscitation is continued and the patient's GCS improves to 15. Thirty minutes later, the patient's GCS is 11. Their temperature is 103°F (39.4°C), blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg, pulse is 122/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. The patient complains of flank pain. Laboratory values are ordered and demonstrate the following: Hemoglobin: 9 g/dL Hematocrit: 27% Leukocyte count: 10,500 cells/mm^3 with normal differential Haptoglobin: 11 mg/dL Platelet count: 198,000/mm^3 Serum: Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 101 mEq/L K+: 4.4 mEq/L HCO3-: 23 mEq/L BUN: 27 mg/dL Glucose: 99 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.5 mg/dL Ca2+: 10.0 mg/dL Bilirubin: 3.2 mg/dL AST: 22 U/L ALT: 15 U/L Which of the following describes the most likely diagnosis?

A 1-year-old patient presents to their pediatrician for episodes of crying and being hunched over. They have also had decreased oral intake during this time. They are generally healthy and have no medical issues. Their temperature is 97.0°F (36.1°C), blood pressure is 94/54 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. The patient appears well and is playing; however, while in the office they have another spell of crying and being hunched over. An ultrasound is performed as seen in Figure A. Which of the following vaccines is associated with this patient's most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old patient is undergoing a bone marrow transplantation for treatment of a non-Hodgkin lymphoma that has been refractory to several rounds of chemotherapy and radiation over the past 2 years. They have been undergoing a regimen of cyclophosphamide and total body irradiation for the past several weeks in anticipation of their future transplant. This morning, they report developing a productive cough and are concerned because they noted some blood in their sputum this morning. The patient also reports pain with inspiration. Their temperature is 101°F (38.3°C), blood pressure is 115/74 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 19/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. A chest radiograph and CT are obtained and shown in Figures A and B respectively. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old patient presents to the emergency department complaining of excruciating pain in their left calf. They state that they were bitten by a spider three days ago; however, yesterday their calf became swollen, red, and extremely painful. Their vital signs are: T 102.8 F, HR 112 bpm, and BP 134/76. On exam, their distal left leg is swollen, extremely tender to palpation, and appears purple and dusky. You note crepitus is present. A biopsy is performed and the results are shown in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old is brought into the emergency room after a bicycle vs motored vehicle accident. They were unconscious after hitting the side of their head on the road, but recovered consciousness after a few minutes. They started to ride their bicycle again, but then developed a severe headache with nausea and vomiting, at which time they called EMS. While in the hospital, the patient is confused and cannot provide a history. They quickly lose consciousness and their CT scan is displayed in Figure 1. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 11-year-old patient is brought into the clinic by their parents, who are distraught over their behavior. They state that over the past several months the patient has started to act oddly, combing the hair of their toy dolls for hours without stopping and repetitively counting their steps in the house. They are often brought to tears when confronted about these behaviors. The patient has no past medical history. When questioned about family history, the parent states they have needed close medical follow-up in the past, but declines to elaborate. The patient's vital signs are all within normal limits. On physical exam the patient is a well-nourished 11-year-old in no acute distress. They have occasional motor tics, but the remainder of the exam is benign. What is the diagnosis in this patient?

A 70-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with sudden episodes of dizziness that resolve in certain positions. On further questioning they describe a false sense of motion with occasional spinning sensation consistent with vertigo. They deny any recent illnesses or hearing loss aside from presbycusis. Their vital signs are normal. During the physical exam the patient reports an episode of vertigo after transitioning from sitting to supine and horizontal nystagmus is concurrently noted. What is the mostly likely diagnosis?

A 39-year-old patient comes into your office with multiple complaints of recent onset. They have been feeling fatigued and have started having leg and thigh pain bilaterally, along with weakness. In addition, they state that they recently started noticing some redness around their eyes along with a rash on their shoulders as shown in Figure A. Of note, they take simvastatin for their hyperlipidemia, and took a short course of steroids recently for an allergic reaction. Their vitals are within normal limits. Their CK is 400 U/L, ESR is 70 mm/hr, and ferritin is 500 mcg/L. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with a severe headache. They state it is 10/10 in intensity and state that it is associated with chewing. They describe it as a dull pain over the sides of their head. The patient is otherwise healthy and is not currently taking any medications. Their temperature is 97.0°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 111/74 mmHg, pulse is 83/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for pain and tenderness over the mandibular and temporal region that is worsened when the patient opens and closes their mouth. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old patient is brought to their primary care physician for being excessively sad and withdrawn lately. The patient states they were recently in a relationship for the past 5 months that just ended. They state they did everything right in the relationship including cooking, cleaning, organizing, and being there for their partner. The relationship ended 1 week ago and since then, the patient has not known what to do with themselves. They say they counted on their partner to structure their day and give them things to do and simply cannot manage without them. They have not been doing laundry, cooking, or bathing during this time. This has happened to them multiple times in the past. They have begun writing songs about their breakup to cope, but it is not working. Their temperature is 98.8°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, pulse is 82/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a sad young patient and the finding in Figure A which is on their other arm as well. Which of the following is the most likely defense mechanism utilized in this patient's underlying diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient with no significant medical history comes to your office complaining of pain and stiffness in their hands upon awakening in the morning. They say the pain and stiffness tends to go away an hour or so after waking up. On physical exam, you note scaly rashes on their elbows bilaterally. You obtain radiographs, shown in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old patient with a history of peripheral vascular disease and a below the knee amputation, presents to the emergency room with excruciating abdominal pain and vomiting for the last 6 hours. Vital signs are T 101.0 F HR 136 BP 150/96 RR 18 Sat 93% on room air. Abdominal exam shows a non-distended, exquisitely tender abdomen which the patient refuses to allow them to examine. While assessing peripheral pulses, they note that they are irregular. A rectal exam is Guaiac positive. Laboratory values are notable for a leukocytosis and a lactic acid of 6.8 mmol/L. An ECG is shown in Figure A. What is the next best step in diagnosis?

A 62-year-old homeless patient presents to the emergency department with severe chest pain. The patient states they have felt unwell for the past several days and endorses lower back pain, chest pain, pain with swallowing, a cough, and a subjective fever. Several weeks ago, the patient had dental pain which they have been treating by drinking alcohol. Their temperature is 104°F (40.0°C), blood pressure is 114/64 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 92% on room air. Exam is notable for submandibular erythema and a coarse, rasping sound when auscultating the heart sounds. A CT of the chest is performed as seen in Figure A and an ECG is performed as seen in Figure B. Laboratory values are notable for a troponin of 1.0 ng/mL (normal < 0.4 ng/mL) and a creatinine of 2.5 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient presents to clinic complaining of coughing up small amounts of blood daily for the past week. They deny smoking, sick contacts, or recent travel. Chest radiographs demonstrate interstitial pneumonia with patchy alveolar infiltrates suggestive of multiple bleeding sites. Urinalysis is positive for blood and protein. A positive result is returned for anti-glomerular basement membrane antibody (anti-GBM Ab). What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 64-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with a chief complaint of left knee pain. They describe acute-onset knee pain last evening that was accompanied by redness of the skin around the joint. They deny any precipitating injury or recent activity that could have caused this pain. They describe a similar episode that occurred in their right knee 2 months ago; they did not seek medical treatment, and the pain mitigated after 5 days. Physical examination is significant for the following: left knee is warm-to-touch, erythematous, and extremely tender to palpation; range of motion in flexion and extension is limited by pain; crepitus noted with passive movement of the knee joint. The patient is noted to be afebrile with all vital signs within normal limits. Aspiration of the left knee joint is ordered and reveals the findings shown in Figure A. Which of the following findings could also be seen in this patient, associated with their current diagnosis?

A 68-year-old patient is admitted to your care four days after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) for a myocardial infarction (MI). The patient has a history of insulin-controlled diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. Of note, the patient states that after the surgery, they had resolution of their chest pain, but they have started experiencing chest pain again. The patient states that the pain is exacerbated by deep breaths but feels better when they lean forward compared to lying down flat. On exam, their vitals are normal, and there are no murmurs heard on auscultation. Their CK-mB returns as normal, and their repeat electrocardiogram (ECG) is shown in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 45-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with a 1-week history of a painful mass in their neck. The patient reports the mass has slowly been enlarging over this time span and has become more painful to the touch. They also report night sweats, weight loss, and diarrhea. Review of systems is notable only for a minor cold a few weeks ago. Their temperature is 100°F (37.8°C), blood pressure is 122/80 mmHg, pulse is 160/min, respirations are 19/min, and oxygen saturation is 100% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a diffusely enlarged thyroid that is tender to the touch. An ECG is performed as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 69-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for pain in their arm. The patient states that their father recently died of a heart attack which motivated them to join their local gymnasium. After completing a set of weight lifting, they felt a "pop" in their right arm, followed by pain. Since the incident, they have been unable to carry items or lift their arm over their head without difficulty and pain.
