The patient has a past medical history of obesity, diabetes, hypertension, and constipation. Their current medications include lisinopril, metformin, insulin, and fiber supplements. On physical exam, you note pain with flexion of the forearm and abduction of the arm with 1/5 strength. There is also weakness of abduction of the affected arm with 3/5 strength. Inspection of the upper extremity reveals the finding in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old is brought into your office by their parent. Their parent states that they are having 10-20 episodes per day where they stop responding to their parent and are found staring out of the window. During these periods, they blink more frequently than normal, but return to their normal self afterwards. These episodes last 30 to 60 seconds. Their parent states that all of their milestones have been normal and they had an uncomplicated birth. Their parent also denies any other recent illness. On exam, their vitals are normal. During one of these episodes in the office, their EEG shows three-per-second spike and wave discharge. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old patient presents to your office for their annual physical exam. They have no complaints at this time and their chronic hypertension is well controlled. You notice a.5cm papule on the patient's eyelid that has a pink pearly appearance, rolled borders, and overlying telangiectasias. On further questioning, you find out the patient was a door-to-door salesman and spent a lot of time outdoors, and they did not wear sunscreen. They have fair skin and blonde hair. The patient states that they first noticed the lesion about 6 months prior, and it has grown slightly since then. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old Caucasian patient presents to their primary care physician for evaluation of progressive weakness and shortness of breath. They have had progressive shortness of breath over the last year with an intermittent non-productive cough. In addition, they complain of difficulty raising their arms to brush their hair. Their temperature is 99.6°F (37.6°C), pulse is 80/min, blood pressure is 130/85 mmHg, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. Neurologic exam shows 4/5 strength in the deltoid muscles bilaterally. Diffuse dry crackles are heard on lung auscultation. A faint erythematous rash is noted on the malar cheeks, periorbital areas, lateral proximal thighs, and the elbows. Which of the following tests is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 55-year-old obese patient is admitted to your floor for chronic fevers. They state they have had fevers of over 101F as measured on their oral thermometer for the past month. Their vitals are T 100.9 F, HR 95 and regular, RR 16, BP 150/95. On history, they state that they have a history of diabetes and are noncompliant with their insulin. They were recently treated for a foot infection with antibiotics, but their fevers have remained. Their last HbA1C was 8.5%. On exam, the patient has no gross deficits, but does admit to pain in their left lower leg and foot. Physical exam reveals a Grade IV ulcer, as displayed in Figure A. They state they have severe pain when bearing weight on their left leg. Otherwise, all extremities have diminished pulses and sensation. There is no erythema in the surrounding area and no areas of fluctuance. Figure B shows AP and lateral radiographs of the patient's left leg. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old patient is brought to the pediatrician by their parent, who relates a primary complaint of a recent history of five independent episodes of vomiting over the last 10 months, most recently 3 weeks ago. Each time, they have awoken early in the morning appearing pale, feverish, lethargic, and complaining of severe nausea. This is followed by 8-12 episodes of non-bilious vomiting over the next 24 hours. Between these episodes they return to normal activity. They have no significant past medical history and take no other medications. Review of systems is negative for changes in vision, gait disturbance, or blood in their stool. Their family history is significant only for migraine headaches. Vital signs and physical examination are within normal limits. Initial complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel, and abdominal radiograph were unremarkable. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with two days of severe abdominal pain and fever. The patient has a history of gallstones, for which they were scheduled to have a cholecystectomy in two weeks. On physical exam, their abdomen is tender to palpation over the epigastrium, without rebound or guarding. The patient is noticeably jaundiced. Laboratory evaluation is notable for a leukocytosis and a total bilirubin of 6.4 mg/dL. What is the diagnosis in this patient?

A 56-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for dizziness. They say that their symptoms began approximately 1 month prior to presentation and are associated with nausea and ringing of the ears. They describe their dizziness as a spinning sensation that has a start and end and lasts approximately 25 minutes. This dizziness is severe enough that they cannot walk or stand. Their symptoms are fluctuating, and they deny any tunnel vision or feelings of fainting. However, they have abruptly fallen to the ground in the past and denied losing consciousness. Medical history is significant for a migraine with aura treated with zolmitriptan, type 2 diabetes managed with metformin, and hypertension managed with lisinopril. Their blood pressure is 125/75 mmHg, pulse is 88/min, and respirations are 16/min. On physical exam, when words are whispered into their right ear, they are unable to repeat the whispered words aloud; however, this is normal in the left ear. Air conduction is greater than bone conduction with Rinne testing, and the sound of the tuning fork is loudest in the left ear on Weber testing. Which of the following is most likely the diagnosis?

A 6-year-old patient is brought to the pediatrician complaining of itchy eyes. The parent states that they have noted that the patient has been tearing and that both of their eyes have been red for the past 4 days. The patient denies any pain but has had a runny nose for the past week. The parent states that the patient has not had any sick contacts, and they have been home from school for summer vacation. They notice that the patient's symptoms seem to improve in the evening after they shower. Their temperature is 97.0°F (36.1°C), blood pressure is 100/66 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old previously healthy patient is brought to your office by their parent. The parent reports the child has been crying and pulling at their right ear over the past 2 days, and reports the patient has been febrile the past 24 hours. The patient’s past medical history is unremarkable, although the parent reports the patient had a “common cold” a week ago which resolved without intervention. Their temperature is 101.6 deg F (38.7 deg C), blood pressure is 100/70 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, and respirations are 22/min. Otoscopic exam is seen in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician complaining of headaches in their left temple and scalp area, neck stiffness, occasional blurred vision, and pain in their jaw when chewing. The appropriate medical therapy is initiated, and a subsequent biopsy of the temporal artery reveals arteritis. Five months later, the patient returns to their physician with a complaint of weakness, leading to difficulty climbing stairs, rising from a chair, and combing their hair. The patient states that this weakness has worsened gradually over the last 2 months. They report that their headaches, jaw pain, and visual disturbances have resolved. Physical examination is significant for 4/5 strength for both hip flexion/extension as well as shoulder flexion/extension/abduction. Initial laboratory work-up reveals ESR and creatine kinase levels within normal limits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient's current presentation?

A 32-year-old patient comes in to see their physician because they have had undiagnosed abdominal pain for the past 3 and a half years. Their pain is not related to meals and does not correspond to a particular time of day, although they do report nausea and bloating. In the past two years they have had two endoscopies, a colonoscopy, and an exploratory laparoscopy - without any results. They are very concerned because their mother has a history of colon cancer. The patient has been unable to work or maintain a social life because they're constantly worrying about their condition. What is this patient's most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient is brought to their primary care provider by their concerned partner. They report the patient has had this "thing" on their eye for years and refuses to seek care. They deny any pain or discharge from the affected eye. A picture of the patient's eye is shown below. Given the diagnosis, what are you most likely to discover when taking this patient's history?

A 71-year-old patient presents to their primary care doctor for a lesion on their skin. The patient states they are generally healthy but has noticed this lesion enlarging over the past several months. They worked in the navy and are not currently taking any medications. Their temperature is 98.1°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 123/83 mmHg, pulse is 85/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A on the patient's head. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient who is an established patient presents to your office. They are complaining of increased urination and increased thirst. They have recently began taking several over-the-counter vitamins and supplements. On further review, they report they have also been having abdominal pain and constipation. They deny significant weight changes. Their fingerstick blood glucose in your office is 96 mg/dL. Which of the following test is most likely to provide the diagnosis?

A 28-year-old homeless patient with a past medical history significant for asthma comes to your clinic complaining of a chronic rash on their scalp and feet. They describe the rash as “dry and flaky,” and reports it has been present for at least a year. They were using a new dandruff shampoo they got over the counter, with little improvement. The patient reports it is extremely itchy at night, to the point that they can't sleep. On exam, you note a scaly patch of alopecia, enlarged lymph glands along the posterior aspect of their neck, and fine scaling in between their toes and on the heel and sides of their foot. Their temperature is 99°F (37°C), blood pressure is 118/78 mmHg, and pulse is 81/min. Which of the following is the most accurate test for the suspected diagnosis?

A 7-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with swelling around their eye. This has happened to them before but has never been this severe. The lesion started a few days ago but has become increasingly red and painful. Physical exam reveals the lesion in Figure A which is tender to palpation. Their cranial nerves are intact and there is no pain with extraocular movements. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old patient presents to the emergency department after a motor vehicle accident. The patient was an unrestrained driver in a head-on collision. They have a past medical history of asthma, depression, and anxiety. They are not currently taking any medications. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg, pulse is 115/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. The patient's cardiopulmonary exam is within normal limits. The patient is breathing on their own and has strong distal pulses. Ultimately, the patient is discharged with follow up instructions after no significant fractures or injuries are found. The patient then presents 4 months later to their primary doctor with weakness. The patient's strength in their upper extremities is 1/5. They have reduced sensation in their upper extremities as well. The patient's lower extremities reveal 5/5 strength with intact sensation. A chest radiograph and basic labs are ordered. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old patient presents with sudden-onset pain in their lower back. They say they were exercising in the gym several hours ago when they felt a sharp pain. The pain is radiating down the side of their leg and into their foot. On physical exam, their vital signs are as follows: HR 95, BP 120/70, T 37.2 degrees C. They have extreme pain shooting down their leg with a straight leg raise. Their sensation to light touch and pin-prick is intact throughout. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-month-old infant is brought to the office by their parents who are concerned about a recent rash. The infant is crying and has a erythematous, pruritic rash that affects their face, forearms, thighs, and scalp as noted in Figure A. The patient's vitals are T 97.8, HR 110, BP 90/60, RR 18. Of note, one parent admits to a medical history of significant allergies, and the other parent suffers from asthma, treated by albuterol. Which of the following is the best diagnosis?

A 29-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with complaints of pain in their joints. They state it started a few days ago and has persisted since. They state that they are otherwise healthy and are not currently taking any medications. The patient is in the military and is currently in basic training. Review of systems is notable for discomfort with urination. Their temperature is 99.0°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 133/90 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. The knee and ankle joints demonstrate pain with passive range of motion, but there are no signs of erythema, edema, or crepitus. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old patient presents to the clinic for malaise. They have been in their usual state of health until 2 weeks ago, when they noticed weakness and dyspnea upon exertion. They deny any orthopnea, paroxymal noctural dyspnea, or weight loss. They endorse occasional fevers but have not checked their temperature at home. They also report worsening pain in their eyes that occasionally causes headaches and occasional joint pain. Their temperature is 98.6°F (37°C), blood pressure is 120/70 mmHg, pulse is 70/min, and respirations are 15/min. Physical exam shows injected sclera bilaterally. They deny pain with eye movement. Their lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Cardiac auscultation reveals an S3 with an occasionally split S2. A chest radiograph is obtained and shown in Figure A. Their lower extremities reveal skin findings shown in Figure B. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 8-year-old patient presents to the emergency department for a cough, fever, and a runny nose. The patient is an immigrant from Lebanon and has never seen a doctor before. They have been given antibiotics for infections every few months for similar symptoms in the past. They have seasonal allergies and have always been sick since they were a child. Their temperature is 101°F (38.3°C), blood pressure is 100/64 mmHg, pulse is 89/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 96% on room air. Physical exam is notable for bilateral coarse breath sounds. They appear well otherwise. A chest radiograph is performed as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 36-year-old patient presents to the emergency room with subacute worsening of chronic chest pain and shortness of breath with exertion. The patient is generally healthy, lifts weights regularly, and does not smoke. Their temperature is 97.8°F (36.6°C), blood pressure is 122/83 mm Hg, pulse is 80/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Cardiac auscultation reveals a crescendo-decrescendo murmur heard right of the upper sternal border with radiation into the carotids. An ECG shows left axis deviation and meets criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy. An initial troponin is < 0.01 ng/mL. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with a 2-day onset of right-lower quadrant and right flank pain. They also state that over this period of time they have felt dizzy, light-headed, and short of breath. They deny any recent trauma or potential inciting event. Their vital signs are as follows: T 37.1 C, HR 118, BP 74/46, RR 18, SpO2 96%. Physical examination is significant for an irregularly irregular heart rhythm as well as bruising over the right flank. The patient's medical history is significant for atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. Their medication list includes atorvastatin, losartan, and coumadin. IV fluids are administered in the emergency department, resulting in an increase in blood pressure to 100/60 and decrease in heart rate to 98. Which of the following would be most useful to confirm this patient's diagnosis and guide future management?

A 25-year-old patient with Hodgkin's lymphoma presents with a several day history of edema. Lab studies show: Serum Na+: 140 mmol/L Serum K+: 3.5 mmol/L Serum albumin: 1.9 g/dL Total serum bilirubin: 1.0 mg/dL Serum creatinine: 1.2 mg/dL Urinalysis shows 4+ proteinuria and fatty casts. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old patient presents to their pediatrician with a rash and intermittent abdominal pain and swelling of their legs and arms. They have also begun to complain of pain in their knees and hands with no history of trauma. Their temperature is 97.6°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 100/80 mmHg, pulse is 89/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A as well as symmetric swelling in the joints of the upper extremities. Their abdomen is currently nontender and not painful. Laboratory studies are pending, and the results of a urinalysis are notable only for positive blood and protein in the urine. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 75-year-old patient with a history of hypertension and diabetes presents to their primary care physician for blurry vision and difficulty driving at night. The patient reports a gradual blurring of vision in both eyes over the last 10 years. They state that they are retired and were not bothered by the blurriness but are now having difficulty driving at night due to glare from oncoming traffic. The patient denies any eye pain, flashes, floaters, tearing, redness, or periods of complete vision loss. They live at home alone, smoke 1 pack per day, drink 2 alcoholic drinks every night, and eat mostly canned food. Their temperature is 98.5°F (36.9°C), blood pressure is 184/110 mmHg, pulse is 70/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Cranial nerves II-XII are grossly intact and the patient has a stable gait. The patient's vision is 20/100 in both eyes. Slit-lamp exam is performed as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 47-year-old patient with a history of hypertension presents to your outpatient clinic for numbness, tingling in their right hand that has been slowly worsening over the last several months. They have tried using a splint but receives minimal relief. They are an analyst for a large consulting firm and spends most of their workday in front of a computer. Upon examination, you noticed that the patient has a prominent jaw and their hands appear disproportionately large. Their temperature is 99 deg F (37.2 deg C), blood pressure is 154/72 mmHg, pulse is 87/min, respirations are 12/min. A fasting basic metabolic panel shows: Na: 138 mEq/L, K: 4.1 mEq/L, Cl: 103 mEq/L, CO2: 24 mEq/L, BUN: 12 mg/dL, Cr: 0.8 mg/dL, Glucose: 163 mg/dL. Which of the following tests would be most helpful in identifying the underlying diagnosis?

A 7-year-old patient presents to an urgent care center for a rash that began approximately 2 days ago. According to their parent, it began as a pink rash on their face and has subsequently spread to their trunk. The child was adopted and has not yet begun care with their pediatrician. Their temperature is 100.2°F (37.9°C), blood pressure is 104/74 mmHg, pulse is 99/min, respirations are 19/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the rash in Figure A and posterior cervical lymphadenopathy. The child is otherwise interactive and is quietly playing with toys. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 43-year-old Caucasian patient with a long history of uncontrolled migraines presents to general medical clinic with painless hematuria. They are quite concerned because they have never had symptoms like this before. Vital signs are stable, and their physical examination is benign. They deny any groin pain, flank pain, or costovertebral angle tenderness. They deny any recent urinary tract infections or dysuria. Urinary analysis confirms hematuria and a serum creatinine returns at 3.0. A renal biopsy reveals papillary necrosis and a tubulointerstitial infiltrate. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician complaining of intense itching on the back of their left calf. They state that they noticed a red and blistering rash this morning and do not recall experiencing a similar rash in the past. Their social history is notable for a job at the zoo. Their temperature is 97.7°F (36.5°C), blood pressure is 120/74 mmHg, pulse is 70/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Their physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. Which of the following findings would be found in the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old patient presents with a recent onset of upsetting dreams, anxiety, and disturbing flashbacks. The patient reports that they returned from active duty in Iraq 3 months ago and was adjusting to life back at home until about 7 weeks ago when they began having intense fear of loud noises and seeing sudden flashbacks to bombing attacks they endured during their time in Iraq. They had to take a leave from their army instructor duties as they were not able to handle the familiar settings of practice shooting ranges and sudden loud explosions during battalion training. After refusing to leave their house, they were finally persuaded by their partner to visit your clinic. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old patient presents to their pediatrician for severe developmental delay. On exam they are noted to have macrocephaly, hypertelorism, large protruding ears, a large jaw, and a long thin face. Suspicious of what the diagnosis may be, the pediatrician orders a PCR and DNA sequencing. The results reveal an expansion of 250 repeats of CGG. What is the diagnosis of the patient?

A 29-year-old patient presents to the emergency department after experiencing a motor vehicle accident. The patient was the front seat passenger in a head-on collision. The patient is responsive only to painful stimuli. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg, pulse is 150/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. The patient is started on IV fluids and is given blood products. A FAST exam reveals no signs of intra-abdominal bleeding. A chest radiograph is ordered as seen in Figure A. A pelvic binder is placed and fluid and blood resuscitation is continued. Fifteen minutes later their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 110/70 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. The patient is now able to respond to questions. The patient's lab values are ordered and are as below: Serum: Na+: 137 mEq/L Cl-: 102 mEq/L K+: 4.2 mEq/L HCO3-: 24 mEq/L BUN: 20 mg/dL Glucose: 110 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL Ca2+: 9.6 mg/dL AST: 12 U/L ALT: 14 U/L Hemoglobin: 11 g/dL Hematocrit: 30% Leukocyte count: 6,500 cells/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 255,000/mm^3 The patient suddenly becomes short of breath. A chest radiograph is ordered as seen in Figure B. A FAST exam is repeated and is within normal limits. Repeat lab values are ordered as below: Hemoglobin: 13 g/dL Hematocrit: 36% Leukocyte count: 6,000 cells/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 250,000/mm^3 Which of the following best describes the most likely diagnosis?

A 15-year-old patient presents to their physician with dyspnea and fatigue for several months. Their past medical history is insignificant. They deny smoking, alcohol, and drug use and do not take any medications except for doxycycline for acne. Their temperature is 97.6°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 120/81 mmHg, pulse is 95/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical examination is notable for a palpable spleen below the left seventh intercostal space and scleral icterus. Laboratory tests are ordered as seen below. Hemoglobin: 10 g/dL Hematocrit: 30% Leukocyte count: 7,500/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 207,000/mm^3 Total bilirubin: 7.0 mg/dL Direct bilirubin: 1.4 mg/dL Lactate dehydrogenase: 450 U/L (normal value 80-280 U/L) Haptoglobin: 15 mg/dL (normal value is 30-220 mg/dL) Reticulocyte count: 10% A peripheral blood smear is shown in Figure A. A direct Coomb test is negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 16-year-old Caucasian patient presents to your family practice office complaining of itchiness. They deny other symptoms. They also deny tobacco, alcohol, or other illicit drug use and are not sexually active. They have no other significant past medical or surgical history aside from a meniscal repair from a wrestling injury sustained two years ago from which they have recovered fully. Vitals are T 98.3, HR 67, BP 110/70. On exam you note several pruritic, erythematous, slightly raised annular patches with central clearing on their back. Which of the following additional tests or features are sufficient to make the diagnosis of this patient's skin lesion?

A 34-year-old patient presents to the clinic complaining of a rash that appeared on their left forearm after a scratch three days ago. This is not the first time they have experienced such a rash, as the patient states they had a similar looking lesion on their elbows three years ago. Upon further questioning, they state that their older sibling has had problems with their skin, but they are unsure of the diagnosis. On physical exam you find a circular and scaly, pearl-colored rash superimposed over an abrasion on their left forearm (Figure A). Of note, the patient has the following nail appearance (Figure B). What is the diagnosis in this patient?

A 13-year-old patient comes to your office complaining of dry, scaling skin (Figure A). They are particularly concerned about the appearance of their skin around their peers. They indicate that they did not start having problems until they were 5 years of age, after which their skin has progressively become drier and scalier. They have tried all types of over-the-counter moisturizers with no resolution. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old patient presents to the medicine clinic with swelling around the right side of their chin and neck (Image A). They report pain when moving their jaw and chewing. Their symptoms developed two days after receiving an uncomplicated tonsillectomy. They have been followed by a general medical physician since birth and have received all of their standard health maintenance procedures. Vital signs are stable with the exception of a temperature of 38.4 degrees Celcius. The area in question on the right side is exquisitely tender. The remainder of their exam is benign. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old patient with a past medical history of diabetes and obesity presents to the clinic with joint pain. They have severe pain in both of their knees for which they have been taking ibuprofen daily. Their temperature is 98.2°F (36.8°C), blood pressure is 177/109 mmHg, pulse is 80/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. Radiography of the knee shows the finding in Figure B. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old patient is brought into your clinic with a 5 day history of decreased oral intake, body aches and lymphadenopathy. They have no significant medical history. Upon further questioning you find that the patient frequently plays outside, where they enjoy chasing the neighborhood cats and dogs. They have had no recent sick contacts or travel to foreign countries. The patient's vital signs are: temperature 100.4F, HR 80, BP 105/75 and RR 15. Physical exam is significant for a 1-cm erythematous and tender lymph node in the right posterior cervical area (Figure 1). There is a nearly healed scratch in the right occipital region. What is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 53-year-old patient presents to your office for abdominal discomfort. The patient states they first noticed pain on their right flank several months ago, and it has been gradually getting worse. For the past week, they have also noticed blood in their urine. Prior to this episode, they have been healthy and does not take any medications. The patient denies fever, chills, and dysuria. They have a 40 pack-year smoking history. Vital signs are T 37 C, HR 140/90 mmHg, HR 84/min, RR 14/min, O2 98%. Physical exam is unremarkable. CBC reveals a hemoglobin of 17 and hematocrit of 51%, and urinalysis is positive for red blood cells, negative for leukocytes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-year-old patient presents to their family physician with a 1-day history of a rash. They deny any history of a similar rash or any dermatologic diagnoses in the past. The parent states that their family was in upstate New York for the past week; however, the child has had no other new events or exposures. Their temperature is 98.0°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 104/74 mmHg, pulse is 87/min, respirations are 12/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. Which of the following diagnoses shares the same pathophysiology as this patient's diagnosis?

A 38-year-old patient with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus, obesity, and hyperlipidemia presents to their primary care physician for evaluation of new bilateral blisters on their hands. They say that they first noticed these blisters shortly after returning from a weekend trip to the beach two weeks prior. They deny any fevers, joint pains, or other skin rash during this period. The patient works in the adult entertainment industry. On examination, there are multiple flaccid blisters of the bilateral dorsal hands with hemorrhagic crusts, mild scarring, and hyperpigmentation. In addition, increased hair growth is noted on the bilateral malar cheeks. Their temperature is 99.1° F (37.3° C), pulse is 95/min, blood pressure is 130/87 mmHg, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Their laboratory results are: Serum: Na+: 140 mEq/L K+: 4.5 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L HCO3-: 21 mEq/L BUN: 20 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL Glucose: 104 mg/dL Leukocyte count: 9,000/mm^3 Hemoglobin: 12.4 g/dL Platelets: 400,000/mm^3 Anti-nuclear antibody titer 1:320 Which of the following would confirm the diagnosis in this patient?

A 9-year-old patient is brought to the pediatrician by their parent who is concerned about a new rash. The patient is otherwise feeling well, is up to date on vaccinations, and has not traveled recently. The family lives in an old apartment building. They are currently excelling in school and have many friends. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old patient presents to clinic complaining of 3 months of weight loss, epigastric pain after meals, diarrhea, and acholic stools. On physical exam they have jaundice and a right upper quadrant mass, but no abdominal tenderness. They have a palpable left supraclavicular node. They also have multiple tender areas of inflamed skin on their chest wall and legs. The patient states that these patches change location over time. CT scan of their abdomen is seen in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 36-year-old patient with a history of end stage renal disease secondary to poorly controlled type I diabetes on peritoneal dialysis presents to their nephrologist's office with chest pain, shortness of breath, and extreme fatigue. They have a history of inadequate dialysis due to poor compliance. In the office, the patient's vitals are BP: 94/58; HR: 90; RR: 20; T: 98.0 F. EKG is shown below (Figure A). The patient is immediately taken to the emergency department. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old patient presents to an outpatient clinic during winter for persistent rhinorrhea. They state it is persistent and seems to be worse when they go outside. Otherwise, they state they are generally healthy and only have a history of constipation. Their temperature is 98.7°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 144/91 mmHg, pulse is 82/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Nasal sputum cytology reveals eosinophilia and boggy turbinates. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 79-year-old patient is admitted to the intensive care unit for hospital acquired pneumonia, a COPD flare, and acute heart failure requiring intubation and mechanical ventilation. On their first night in the intensive care unit, their temperature is 99.7°F (37.6°C), blood pressure is 107/58 mm Hg, and pulse is 150/min which is a sudden change from their previous vitals. Physical exam is notable for jugular venous distension and a rapid heart rate. The ventilator is checked and is functioning normally. Which of the following is the best next step in management for the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old patient presents to your office one day after an injury. Yesterday they tried to play basketball with their grandchildren and they were doing well until they jumped to get the ball and landed awkwardly on their right foot, after which they could not bear weight on their foot. On exam, their right foot is significant for swelling with tenderness to palpation anterior to the Achilles tendon. The patient has no tenderness over their medial or lateral malleoli. Figure A is a radiograph of their right foot with the area of traumatic injury. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 49-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for the first time in twelve years. Their chief complaint is a new onset of diarrhea, which nothing seems to improve. They first noticed this diarrhea about a month ago. They complain of greasy stools, which leave a residue in the toilet bowl. Review of systems is notable for alcohol consumption of 12-16 cans of beer per day for the last two decades. Additionally, the patient endorses losing 12 lbs unintentionally over the last month. Vital signs are within normal limits and stable. Exam demonstrates a patient who appears older than stated age; abdominal exam is notable for epigastric tenderness to palpation. What is the next step in diagnosis?

A 30-year-old previously healthy patient presents to your office with complaints of facial pressure and rhinorrhea for the past 3 weeks. The patient reports that several weeks prior, they had a “common cold” which resolved. However, they have since developed worsening facial pressure, especially over their cheeks and forehead. They report over 1 week of green tinged rhinorrhea. Their temperature is 100.1 deg F (37.8 deg C), blood pressure is 120/70 mmHg, pulse is 85/min, and respirations are 15/min. Nasal exam reveals edematous turbinates and purulent discharge. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old patient is brought to the emergency room by their parents in severe pain. They state that they fell on their outstretched right arm while playing with friends. They are unable to move their right arm, which is being supported by their left. On exam, their vitals are normal. Their right extremity reveals normal pulses without swelling in any compartments, but there is crepitus above the elbow upon movement. The patient is able to flex and extend their wrist, but this is limited by pain. The patient has decreased sensation along their thumb and is unable to make the "OK" sign with their thumb and index finger. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for foot pain. The patient states that they have pain in their foot and toes whenever they exert themselves or are at work. The patient is an executive at a medical device company and works 60 hours/week. They are currently training for a marathon. They have a past medical history of anxiety, constipation, and irritable bowel syndrome. Their current medications include clonazepam, sodium docusate, and hyoscyamine. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 100/60 mmHg, pulse is 50/min, respirations are 10/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Cardiac and pulmonary exams are within normal limits. Examination of the lower extremity reveals 5/5 strength with 2+ reflexes. Palpation of the interdigital space between the third and fourth toes elicits pain and a clicking sound. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 8-year-old patient presents to the general pediatrics clinic with hip pain. The pain started several weeks ago on their left side and has worsened over the past several days. Their right hip is painless. Their temperature is 98.0°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 107/68 mm Hg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 16/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam reveals an antalgic gait, decreased range of motion in the left hip, and mild thigh muscle atrophy. A radiograph is shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 46-year-old patient was found unconscious in the field and brought to the emergency department by EMS. The patient was intubated in transit and given a 2 liter bolus of normal saline. On arrival, the patient's blood pressure is 80/60 mmHg and temperature is 37.5C. Jugular veins are flat and capillary refill time is 4 seconds. Vascular parameters are measured and are as follows: Cardiac index - Low; Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) - Low; Systemic vascular resistance - High. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 15-year-old patient is brought into their pediatrician's office by their parent because the parent thinks they have attention issues. The parent explains that they started high school four months ago and had lackluster grades in a recent progress report despite having earned consistent top marks in middle school. The parent complains that they never talk to them at home anymore. The patient yells at their parent in the exam room, and the parent is escorted out of the room. The patient scoffs that their parent is so overbearing, ruining their good days with criticism. They begin to chew gum and states that they hate hanging out with their peers on the cheerleading squad. They deny experiencing physical abuse from anyone or having a sexual partner. They have seen kids smoke marijuana underneath the football field bleachers, but do not go near them and deny smoking cigarettes. They deny any intention to harm themselves or others, think their grades went down because their teachers are not as good as their middle school teachers, and state they think they learn best by watching explanations through online videos. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 21-year-old patient presents to the clinic complaining of feeling tired during the day. They are concerned as their grades in school have worsened and they do not want to lose their scholarship. Upon further questioning, the patient describes frequently experiencing a dreamlike state before falling asleep and after waking up. They also have frequent nighttime awakenings where they find themselves unable to move. They deny snoring. The patient does not drink alcohol or abuse any other drugs. The patient's BMI is 21 kg/m2, and their vital signs are all within normal limits. What is this patient's diagnosis?

An 18-year-old patient with a history of recurrent pharyngitis presents to your clinic with fever, sore throat and decreased oral intake. The patient states that their symptoms have been present for about 1-week, although over the past couple of days they have gotten much worse. The patient's vital signs are as follows: temperature is 102.2 deg F (39.0 deg C), pulse is 94/min, blood pressure is 110/68 mmHg and respirations are 14/min. On physical exam the patient appears uncomfortable, barely opening their mouth when speaking. There is tender lymphadenopathy bilaterally. Examination of the oropharynx is demonstrated in Figure A. A heterophile test is performed and later comes back negative. What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 8-year-old patient is brought to the pediatrician by their distraught parent who is concerned about "light spots" that first appeared 4 months ago and have been slowly expanding over different parts of their body. They are not bothered by these areas, and they do not itch, burn, or bleed. They have otherwise been well. There is no family history of this skin condition, though their parent has a history of hypothyroidism. Their skin exam is notable for smooth, hypopigmented patches over their bilateral knuckles, knees, and inner thighs, as seen in Figure A. Their exam is also notable for a tuft of leukotrichia over their occiput, as seen in Figure B. Which of the following will help to confirm the diagnosis?

A 17-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with a concern for a puffy cheek. They have noticed they have had a puffy cheek for the past month despite exercising more often and eating a healthy diet. The patient states they are an otherwise healthy student, does not smoke, and is not sexually active. Their temperature is 97.9°F (36.6°C), blood pressure is 114/74 mmHg, pulse is 105/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a healthy young patient with a nontender abdomen. Exam reveals the finding in Figure A as well as poor dentition. Their BMI is 26 kg/m^2 and they have normal development for their age. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below. Hemoglobin: 10 g/dL Hematocrit: 30% Leukocyte count: 12,900/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 191,000/mm^3 Serum: Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L K+: 3.0 mEq/L HCO3-: 29 mEq/L BUN: 23 mg/dL Glucose: 99 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.2 mg/dL Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 53-year-old farmer presents to the clinic for evaluation of a pigmented lesion on their arm. They state that they first noticed the lesion last year, but they believe that it has been slowly growing in size. They otherwise do not have any complaints and are generally healthy. Which of the following findings on physical exam would suggest a malignant diagnosis?

A 32-year-old patient who was previously healthy is brought to the emergency department by their concerned partner who states that they are acting very abnormally. They state that over the past day they have developed a fever, become progressively more confused, and are "just not acting like themselves." On exam, they exhibit altered mental status. Their vitals are demonstrated as: T: 39 deg C, HR: 102 bpm, BP: 130/90 mmHg, RR: 12, SaO2: 100%. The emergency physician obtains a lumbar puncture which demonstrates the following CSF analysis: normal opening pressure, elevated lymphocyte count, elevated protein, elevated RBCs, and normal glucose. An MRI is obtained to confirm the diagnosis and is illustrated in Figure A. Which of the following organisms is most likely responsible for this patient's presentation?

A parent brings their 3-year-old child to the doctor because they are worried that the child might be harming themselves by constantly banging their head on the wall. They have been exhibiting this behavior for a few months. The parent is also worried because the child has started to speak less than they used to and does not respond when their name is called. The child seems aloof during playtime with other children and seems to have lost interest in most of their toys. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with right knee pain for the last week. They state that they first noticed it after a long flight on their way back to the United States from Russia, where they had run a marathon along a mountain trail. The patient describes the pain as dull, aching, and localized to the front of their kneecap, and it worsens with sitting but improves with standing. Aspirin has not provided significant relief. The patient has a history of a torn anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) on the right side from a soccer injury three years ago. In addition, they were treated for gonorrhea last month after having intercourse with a new partner. At this visit, the patient’s temperature is 98.5°F (36.9°C), blood pressure is 112/63 mmHg, pulse is 75/min, and respirations are 14/min. Which of the following is most likely to establish the diagnosis?

A 60-year-old patient with a history of chronic back pain presents to the emergency department with abdominal pain. They state their back pain has been worsening recently, requiring more pain medications. Their temperature is 97.6°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 122/80 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 12/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. The patient is laying still on their back and is moaning in pain. There is notable tenderness in all quadrants with rebound tenderness. The patient's heart rate is 90/min after receiving hydromorphone. A radiograph is performed as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old IV drug user comes into the emergency department after four days of pain in their right ankle. The patient is lethargic and unable to answer any questions about their medical history. Their vitals are HR 110, T 101.5, RR 20, BP 100/60. Their physical exam is notable for track marks in their toes and their right ankle is erythematous and swollen. Moving any part of the right foot creates a 10/10 pain. A radiograph reveals no evidence of fractures. A Gram stain of the joint fluid aspirate demonstrates purple cocci in clusters. The fluid is yellow, opaque, with more than 70,000 cells/mm^3 (80% neutrophils). What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 43-year-old patient with a history of hepatitis C and current intravenous drug use presents with 5 days of fever, chills, headache, and severe back pain. On physical exam, temperature is 100.6 deg F (38.1 deg C), blood pressure is 109/56 mmHg, pulse is 94/min, and respirations are 18/min. They are thin and diaphoretic with pinpoint pupils, poor dentition, and track marks on their arms and legs. A high-pitched systolic murmur is heard, loudest in the left sternal border and with inspiration. They are admitted to the hospital and started on broad-spectrum antibiotics. One of the blood cultures drawn 12 hours ago returns positive for Staphylococcus aureus. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to confirm the diagnosis?

A 69-year-old patient with no significant past medical history except for hypertension receives an X-ray of their skull (Figure A) after their car was rear-ended in a parking lot resulting in neck soreness. No fracture but what is the likely diagnosis of this incidental finding?

A 25-year-old patient comes into your office for a yearly physical exam and check up. They have no current complaints and states that their family is healthy. They were originally born in Italy and are up to date with all of their vaccinations. Their physical exam is within normal limits and their vitals are HR 80, BP 125/70, T 97.9 F, RR 11. Their CBC is significant for Hgb 12.0, Hct 35, WBC 6.5, and Plts 210. Upon obtaining the differential for their low hemoglobin, you see an MCV of 65 along with a reticulocyte count of 4%. Their iron studies are within normal limits. Figure A shows their peripheral blood smear. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old patient with a history of ulcerative colitis presents to the emergency room with a four-day history of nausea, bloody diarrhea, and abdominal pain. They are on medical management with 5-aminosalicylic acid (5 ASA). Examination shows an ill-appearing patient with a tense, tympanitic abdominal exam. They are unable to be fully examined due to the abdominal pain. Vitals are T 38.2 C, HR 102 bpm BP 133/92 mmHg, RR 20 bpm, and O2 Sat 100% on room air. In the ED, an abdominal radiograph is shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the diagnosis?

A 69-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for pain when they walk. They state that the pain is the worst in their left great toe but is also present in their hips and knees. They say that their symptoms are worse with activity and tend to improve with rest. Their symptoms have progressively worsened over the past several years. They have a past medical history of obesity, type II diabetes mellitus, smoking, and hypertension. They drink roughly ten beers per day. Their current medications include metformin, insulin, lisinopril, and hydrochlorothiazide. The patient has a recent travel history to Bangkok where they admit to having unprotected sex. On physical exam, examination of the lower extremity results in pain. There is crepitus of the patient's hip when their thigh is flexed and extended. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with jaundice and diffuse abdominal pain. They deny any previous medical problems and say they do not take any medications, drugs, or supplements. Their temperature is 97.6°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 133/87 mmHg, pulse is 86/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 100% on room air. Physical exam is notable for sclera which are icteric and there is tenderness to palpation over the right upper quadrant. Laboratory studies are ordered as seen below. Hepatitis B surface antigen: Positive Hepatitis B surface IgG: Negative Hepatitis B core antigen: Positive Hepatitis B core IgG: Positive Hepatitis B E antigen: Positive Hepatitis B E IgG: Positive Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 43-year-old patient presents to a new primary care physician complaining of anxiety. They have been worrying non-stop recently about the possibility that their partner will lose their job as a teacher. Their partner, who is present, assures the physician that their job is entirely secure and states that they have "fretted" for their entire relationship, though the exact topic causing their anxiety varies over time. They also worry excessively about everyday tasks, such as whether they will catch the train on time and whether their house in Southern California is sufficiently earthquake-proof. They have no way to overcome these worries. They endorse other symptoms including poor sleep (associated with racing thoughts about their various worries), fatigue, and impaired concentration at work, all of which have been present for at least the past year. Their vital signs are within normal limits and there are no abnormalities on physical exam. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old patient with a history of chronic constipation presents to the emergency department with a two-day history of left lower quadrant abdominal pain. They are found to have a temperature of 100.8F, BP 140/90, HR 85, and RR 16. On physical examination, they are tender to light palpation in the left lower quadrant and exhibits voluntary guarding. Rectal examination reveals heme-positive stool. Laboratory values are unremarkable except for a WBC count of 12,500 with a left shift. Which of the following tests would be most useful in the diagnosis of this patient's disease?

An obese 42-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with a complaint of left knee pain for the past 3 months. They describe the pain as affecting the inside part of the knee as well as the front of the knee, below the kneecap. They deny any inciting injury or trauma to the knee but report that the pain is worse when they are climbing up stairs or rising from a chair. Physical examination is significant for localized tenderness to palpation over the left anteromedial proximal tibia, 6 cm inferior to the joint line. There is no joint effusion noted. Valgus stress testing is negative for any pain or instability of the knee joint. Radiographs of the left knee are obtained and reveal only mild arthritis, without evidence of any fractures or bony lesions. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 54-year-old African American patient presents to the emergency department with shortness of breath. They were at home watching television when their symptoms began. They have a past medical history of COPD, alcohol abuse, diabetes, asthma, obesity, pancreatitis, peripheral neuropathy, and hypertension. They have a 30 pack-year smoking history as well. Their current medications include albuterol, insulin, nicotine patches, duloxetine, hydroxyurea, and lisinopril. Chest radiography confirms the diagnosis of a spontaneous pneumothorax. A chest tube is placed, and the patient is transferred to the medical floor. Laboratory results are ordered and are seen below: Hemoglobin: 9 g/dL Platelet count: 180,000/mm^3 Mean corpuscular volume: 125 µm^3 Reticulocyte count: 0.3% Serum: Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 102 mEq/L K+: 4.2 mEq/L HCO3-: 24 mEq/L BUN: 20 mg/dL Glucose: 133 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.4 mg/dL Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL Vitamin B12: 197 ng/L AST: 22 U/L ALT: 10 U/L Troponins: undetectable On the medical floor, the patient complains of continued fatigue and minor chest pain. A peripheral smear is ordered as seen in Figure A. An EKG is ordered and demonstrates a right bundle branch block which is unchanged from previous EKGs. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old patient with a psychiatric history of bipolar disorder is brought into the emergency department by emergency medical services. The patient is unconscious, but the parent states that they walked into the patient's room with the patient lying on the floor and an empty bottle of unknown pills next to them. The patient has previously tried to commit suicide 2 years ago. Upon presentation, the patient's vitals are HR 110, BP 105/60, T 99.5, RR 22. The patient soon has 5 episodes of non-bilious non-bloody vomiting. Upon physical exam, they have pain in the right upper quadrant and their liver function tests are AST 1050 U/L, ALT 2050 U/L, ALP 55 U/L, Total Bilirubin 0.8 mg/dL, Direct Bilirubin 0.2 mg/dL. You are awaiting their toxicology screen. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old patient with a history of alcohol abuse and cirrhosis presents to the emergency department with profuse vomiting. The patient is aggressive, combative, emotionally labile, and has to be chemically restrained. The patient continues to vomit and blood is noted in the vomitus. Their temperature is 99.2°F (37.3°C), blood pressure is 139/88 mmHg, pulse is 106/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 100% on room air. The patient complains of sudden onset chest pain during their physical exam. A crunching and rasping sound is heard while auscultating the heart. Which of the following is the pathophysiology of the most likely diagnosis?

A 37-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with a chief complaint of diarrhea. The patient states that their symptoms have worsened recently. They work as a farmer and are dressed in tattered and old denim. They live alone, and this is the first time they have come to town in years. The patient’s diet is mostly dairy products and some meat products. They deny any systemic symptoms and state that diarrhea tends to occur right after a meal. They also claim that at times they struggle to fall asleep, and sometimes they feel they lack energy. The patient is instructed to avoid consuming dairy products for a week and to return with a report of their symptoms. As you set up the return appointment with this patient, you notice that they are rather emotionless. They also state that they lack anybody that they can list as an emergency contact, so they leave that section of their medical forms blank. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for a follow-up appointment. The patient was the front seat driver in a head-on collision which resulted in a femur and pelvic fracture which was treated appropriately. The patient spent 3 weeks in the hospital and was then discharged 2 weeks ago. The patient has a past medical history of diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidemia. They smoke 3 packs of cigarettes per day and drink 4 alcoholic beverages every night. The patient says that they have been attempting to engage in sexual activities with their partner but have been unable to do so. They state this has never been a problem for them before. They also report new-onset minor headaches and trouble sleeping for which they are taking trazodone. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 12-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with left knee pain for the past 6 weeks. They recently joined the field hockey team at their school. The pain is the most severe when they are running up and down the stairs at the school stadium. The pain decreases when they go home and rest after practice. They additionally admit to tripping and landing on their left knee 5 days ago. Physical exam shows a knee with a healing abrasion over the left patella. The tibial tuberosity is tender to palpation. A radiograph of the knee is presented in figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 11-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with heavy drooling. The patient was being watched by their babysitter when she found them in this manner. Their temperature is 99.1°F (37.3°C), blood pressure is 107/58 mmHg, pulse is 119/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a young patient in acute distress who is drooling. The patient states they are in pain and can’t swallow. The patient’s tongue seems abnormally enlarged and erythematous. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with epigastric pain. The patient states that they were at home watching television when their symptoms began. Otherwise, the patient has no complaints. The patient has a past medical history of obesity, hypertension, alcohol abuse, diabetes, and constipation. Their current medications include insulin, metformin, lisinopril, and sodium docusate. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 160/95 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Laboratory values and an abdominal ultrasound are ordered and are currently pending. An abdominal radiograph is ordered as seen in Figure A. On physical exam, the patient is clinically intoxicated. Cardiopulmonary exam is within normal limits. The patient is started on IV fluids and given morphine. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for knee pain. The pain started yesterday and has not improved since then. The patient is generally in good health. They attend college and play soccer for their school's team. Three days ago, they were slide tackled during a game and their leg was struck from the outside. They fell to the ground and sat out for the rest of the game. It was not until yesterday that they noticed swelling in their knee. They also feel as if their knee is unstable and do not feel confident bearing weight on their leg during athletic activities. Their past medical history is notable for asthma, which is currently treated with an albuterol inhaler. On physical exam, you note bruising over their leg, knee, and lateral thigh, and edema of their knee. Passive range of motion of the knee is notable only for minor clicking and catching of the joint. The patient's gait appears normal, though the patient states that their injured knee does not feel stable. Further physical exam is performed and imaging is ordered. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with pain in their right eye. The patient states that their eye hurts and that they cannot see well. They cannot remember when their symptoms started or what caused them. The patient has a past medical history of schizophrenia and IV drug abuse. Their current medications include intramuscular haloperidol and nicotine patches. The patient has a 20 pack-year smoking history. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 120/68 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. On physical exam, you note a poorly kempt patient and the findings in Figure A. Pain is elicited upon examination of cranial nerve III in the right eye. The patient is unable to read a chart on the wall of the exam room and complains of double vision. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 46-year-old patient arrives at your clinic complaining of a 5-month history of fatigue and “numbness.” They describe a “tingling” sensation in their fingers and feet, and say sometimes they cannot feel them at all. They admit to being an IV heroin user with their last use being yesterday evening. The patient has also been homeless for three years. They report that they were sexually assaulted at a shelter, so they are afraid to go back. Instead, they buy their own meals, when they can, with donations. The patient is currently sexually active with two partners. They have never had testing for sexually transmitted diseases. The patient reports blurry vision, but admits they have not been to an eye doctor for over five years. They deny fever, headache, palpitations, night sweats, abdominal pain, urinary symptoms, or rashes. On exam, the patient appears emaciated. Neurologic examination shows a decreased vibratory sense and proprioception in the fingers and toes. Pupils are equally reactive to light and accommodation. The patient has mild difficulty rising from a chair without using their upper extremities to assist. A CBC is drawn, and results include: Leukocyte count and differential: Leukocyte count: 4,400/mm^3 Segmented neutrophils: 60% Bands: 3% Eosinophils: 2% Basophils: < 1% Lymphocytes: 26% Monocytes: 7% Hemoglobin: 9.5 g/dL Platelet count: 250,000/mm^3 Mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration: 32% Mean corpuscular volume: 123 µm^3 Reticulocyte count:.8% A peripheral blood smear is drawn and shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for stiffness in their arm. They state that they have been having trouble combing their hair and reaching objects that are high on the shelf. The patient has a past medical history of diabetes mellitus type II, obesity, and hypertension. Their current medications include metformin, insulin, lisinopril, and hydrochlorothiazide. The patient admits to leading a sedentary life in which they tend to stay home and watch television. They do not engage in any physical or strenuous activity. On physical exam the patient has decreased passive and active range of motion of their shoulder. Strength of the patient's upper extremity is 4/5. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for a wellness check-up. They state that recently they have been feeling well other than headaches that occur occasionally, which improve with ibuprofen and rest. They have a past medical history of hypertension and headaches and are currently taking hydrochlorothiazide. Their temperature is 99.2°F (37.3°C), blood pressure is 157/108 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam reveals a patient who appears healthy. A normal S1 and S2 are auscultated on cardiac exam, and their lungs are clear with good air movement bilaterally. From their previous visit, it was determined that they have an elevated aldosterone and low renin level. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below. Serum: Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L K+: 3.7 mEq/L HCO3-: 29 mEq/L BUN: 20 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient with a history of chronic hepatitis C infection, hypertension, type II diabetes mellitus, and congestive heart failure presents to their primary care physician with complaints of a new rash. They state that they first noticed the rash two weeks prior, and endorse intermittent itchiness. The patient works as a butcher at a local meat processing shop and is sexually active with several partners. They do not use barrier protection. The patient’s temperature is 98.6°F (37.0°C), pulse is 90/min, blood pressure is 155/95 mmHg, and respirations are 12/min. Physical exam is notable for Figure A. Fine, lace-like white lines are also noted on the patient’s buccal mucosa. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with dizziness. They state they have experienced a sustained sensation of the room spinning that is low grade and constant since this morning. The patient occasionally feels nauseous and has been taking diphenydramine to sleep which helps with their symptoms. The patient is generally healthy, has no other medical conditions, and only endorses eating more garlic recently to get over a cold they had a few days ago. Their temperature is 98.7°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 122/81 mmHg, pulse is 82/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a healthy patient. The patient is sat upright, their head is turned slightly to the right, and they are laid back flat rapidly. This does not provoke any symptoms even when repeated on the left side. A nystagmus is notable on cranial nerve exam as well as bilateral decreased hearing. The patient’s tandem gait is unstable; however, their baseline gait appears unremarkable despite the patient stating they have a sustained sensation of imbalance. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old patient is brought to the pediatrician by their parents because of the rash shown in Figure A. The parents report that their child had an episode of pharyngitis one week ago. The child reports feeling nauseated recently and says their knees have been bothering them. Past medical history is insignificant. A stool sample is positive for occult blood. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with a fever, chills, cough, and aches that started 3 days ago. They have also experienced night sweats and chills during this time frame. This morning, they noticed warts and a few small bleeding lesions on their skin. The patient has a past medical history of type I diabetes and asthma and is currently taking insulin, albuterol, and fluticasone. They are generally healthy and just returned from a trip visiting family in the southeastern United States. Their temperature is 102°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 129/82 mmHg, pulse is 107/min, respirations are 19/min, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. Physical exam demonstrates an ill-appearing young patient. Pulmonary exam is notable for bilateral coarse breath sounds. Dermatologic exam reveals the findings in Figure A. A chest radiograph is obtained as seen in Figure B. Further diagnostic studies and tests are sent off and are currently pending. Which of the following is the best treatment for the most likely diagnosis?

A 47-year-old patient presents to their ophthalmologist for abnormal vision. The patient was discharged from the hospital 2 weeks ago after a motor vehicle accident where they were given 1L of blood. They also underwent several surgical procedures including enucleation of the right globe and exploratory abdominal laparotomy to stop internal bleeding. Currently, they state that they have noticed decreased vision in their left eye. The patient has a past medical history of poorly controlled diabetes, asthma, and atopic dermatitis. Their temperature is 98.9°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 167/108 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. Physical exam is notable for 20/200 vision in the patient's left eye, which is worse than usual. The patient's left eye appears red and irritated. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 69-year-old patient presents to the emergency department in severe abdominal pain. They state they were discharged from the hospital three days ago after being treated for a kidney infection with intravenous antibiotics. Over the last five days, they have developed watery diarrhea and have been in almost constant pain which has now increased to an intensity of 10/10. On exam, their vitals are T 102.3F, HR 125, BP 89/45, RR 20. They have pain with palpation along their lower quadrants with questionable guarding. Their CBC is significant for a white blood cell (WBC) count of 25,000 cells/mcL along with Na 140, K 3.3, Cl 90 and HCO3- 15. Their lactic acid is 3.6 mmol/L. Figure A illustrates a radiograph of their abdomen. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with abdominal pain. The patient states that they have pain in their back that radiates to their abdomen. The pain started yesterday and is episodic. They describe the pain as a 10/10 when it occurs. The patient has a past medical history of asthma, anxiety, and chlamydia that was appropriately treated. Their current medications include fluoxetine. The patient's lab values are ordered as seen below. Hemoglobin: 14 g/dL Hematocrit: 40% Leukocyte count: 8,500 cells/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 225,000/mm^3 Serum: Na+: 140 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L K+: 4.9 mEq/L HCO3-: 24 mEq/L BUN: 22 mg/dL Glucose: 89 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.2 mg/dL Ca2+: 10.0 mg/dL AST: 11 U/L ALT: 11 U/L Urine: Color: amber Nitrites: negative Na+: 12 mmol/24 hours Beta-hCG: positive Red blood cells: 11/hpf Which of the following is the best test for this patient's most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old patient presents to the emergency department for muscle weakness. They state that they were at a rave when they were found down by one of their friends. Their friend waited with them to recover, but they have felt ill and abnormally weak. The patient admits to using MDMA, marijuana, and alcohol. Physical exam reveals a patient who responds slowly to your questions. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below. Urine: Color: Amber Marijuana: Positive Cocaine: Positive MDMA: Positive Blood: Positive An ECG is ordered as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old patient presents to the ED complaining of worsening abdominal pain over the last few hours. They also report nausea, but deny fever, vomiting, or changes in the appearance of their bowel movements. Their medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, coronary artery disease, stroke, atrial fibrillation, and peptic ulcer disease. Due to their recurrent bleeding peptic ulcers, they do not take warfarin. Their surgical history is significant for an appendectomy as a child. Their medications include metformin, lisinopril, metoprolol, and omeprazole. They have a 50-pack-year history of smoking. Their temperature is 37.6 C (99.7 F), blood pressure is 146/80 mm Hg, pulse is 115/min, and respiratory rate is 20/min. On physical exam, they are in acute distress due to the pain. Pulmonary auscultation reveals scattered wheezes and decreased air entry. Their heart rate is irregularly irregular, with no murmurs, rubs or gallops. Abdominal exam is significant for decreased bowel sounds and diffuse tenderness. Initial laboratory evaluation is as follows: Na 138 mEq/L, Cl 101 mEq/L, HCO3 12 mEq/L, BUN 21 mg/dL, Cr 0.9 mg/dL, glucose 190 mg/dL, amylase 240 U/L (normal < 65 U/L). What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 28-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with lower extremity weakness. They were in their usual state of health until 10 days ago. They then began to notice their legs were “tiring out” during their workouts. This progressed to difficulty climbing the stairs to their apartment. They have asthma and use albuterol as needed. They have no significant surgical or family history. They smoke marijuana daily but deny use of other recreational drugs. They are sexually active with their partner of 2 years. They have never traveled outside of the country but were camping 3 weeks ago. They report that they had diarrhea for several days after drinking unfiltered water from a nearby stream. On physical examination, they have 1/5 strength in their bilateral lower extremities. They use their arms to get up from the chair. Achilles and patellar reflexes are absent. A lumbar puncture is performed, and results are as shown below: Cerebral spinal fluid: Color: Clear Pressure: 15 cm H2O Red blood cell count: 0 cells/µL Leukocyte count: 3 cells/ µL with lymphocytic predominance Glucose: 60 mg/dL Protein: 75 mg/dL A culture of the cerebral spinal fluid is pending. Which of the following is the part of the management for the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with shortness of breath. They are an immigrant and do not speak English, but it is clear they are struggling to breathe. You observe the patient struggling to breathe and coughing up large amounts of mucous. A phone call to their home nurse reveals that they have a past medical history of diabetes for which they are not currently taking their medications. They also state the patient recently recovered from a long flight back from their native country where they were visiting a relative in prison. Their temperature is 99.1°F (37.3°C), blood pressure is 167/108 mmHg, pulse is 112/min, respirations are 25/min, and oxygen saturation is 78% on room air. A chest radiograph is obtained as seen in Figure A. Physical exam reveals a distressed patient who is not cooperative with the exam secondary to their discomfort. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old patient presents to their primary care provider complaining of a facial rash. They say the rash began 3 weeks ago after hiking in the White Mountains of New Hampshire this summer. Since that time they have also experienced pain in their hands and wrists that is worse in the morning and accompanied by subjective fevers. They deny chest pain, shortness of breath, nausea, or vomiting. Vital signs are 99.6°F (37.6°F), blood pressure is 134/82 mmHg, pulse is 88/min, and respirations are 18/min. Examination demonstrates a rash on the patient's face that spares the nasolabial folds along with oral ulcers. The metacarpophalangeal joints are tender to palpation, and range of motion is limited by pain. Complete blood count demonstrates normocytic anemia with thrombocytopenia. Which of the following is the next best step in diagnosis?

A 62-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for a regular checkup. The patient worked as a farmer their entire life but recently retired. Since then, they have been sailing the world. They endorse a recent 7 pound weight loss which they attribute to their sailing activities. Otherwise, the patient has no other complaints and feels that they are doing well. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension. Their current medications include atorvastatin, lisinopril, and aspirin. The patient smokes cigarettes and drinks alcohol occasionally. On physical exam, you note an elderly patient in no current distress. Abdominal exam reveals mild epigastric bruising which the patient attributes to sailing. Musculoskeletal exam demonstrates crepitus of the patient's hips. Dermatologic exam reveals the finding in Figure A which the patient has not noticed before, as well as diffuse minor bruises which the patient attributes to their recreational activities. The patient's gait is stable, and they demonstrate 5/5 strength in their upper and lower extremities. Which of the following is the most likely underlying diagnosis for this patient's presentation?

A 27-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with worsening cough and asthma. The patient reports that they were in their usual state of health until 1 month ago, when they developed a cold. Since then their cold has improved, but they continue to have a cough and worsening asthma symptoms. They say that they have been using their rescue inhaler 3 times a day with little improvement. They are studying for an accounting exam and states that their asthma is keeping them up at night and making it hard for them to focus during the day. The patient admits to smoking tobacco. Their smoking has increased from a half pack per day since they were 17 years old to 1 pack per day during the past month to cope with the stress of their exam. The patient’s temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 110/74 mmHg, pulse is 75/min, and respirations are 15/min with an oxygen saturation of 97% on room air. Physically examination is notable for mild expiratory wheezes bilaterally. Labs are obtained, as shown below: Serum: Na+: 144 mEq/L Cl-: 95 mEq/L K+: 4.3 mEq/L HCO3-: 23 mEq/L Urea nitrogen: 24 mg/dL Glucose: 100 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.6 mg/dL Leukocyte count and differential: Leukocyte count: 13,000/mm^3 Segmented neutrophils: 63% Eosinophils: 15% Basophils: < 1% Lymphocytes: 20% Monocytes: 1.3% Hemoglobin: 13.5 g/dL Hematocrit: 50% Platelets: 200,000/mm^3 Urinalysis reveals proteinuria and microscopic hematuria. Which of the following is associated with the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old Caucasian patient presents to their primary care physician for routine care. They have a longstanding history of diabetes mellitus type 2, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia for which they take metformin, amlodipine, and atorvastatin. They are generally happy with their health, but do complain of mild discomfort in their chest after dinner each night as well as intermittent itching of their upper back.
