They smoke one pack of cigarettes per day and drinks two glasses of wine on the weekends. They work as a landscaper at their local golf course. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), pulse is 70/min, blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, and respirations are 12/min. The most recent hemoglobin A1c from two years prior was 6.4% and their fasting fingerstick glucose in the office today is 120 mg/dL. Physical exam is notable for a well-appearing overweight individual with a lesion on their upper back (Figure A). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old patient presents to the emergency department complaining of a “curtain” suddenly obscuring their vision in their right eye. They report that for the past few weeks, they have experienced intermittent episodes of seeing flashes of light as well as floaters blocking their visual field. They deny any eye pain or irritation. They note that since they were a child, they have relied on wearing glasses with thick lenses due to a high degree of myopia. Which of the following images on ophthalmoscopy corresponds with this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with chest pain. They state that their symptoms started a few days ago and have been gradually worsening. The patient admits to drinking alcohol recently and has been vomiting frequently. The patient has a past medical history of alcohol abuse and regularly presents to the emergency department. Their temperature is 102°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 107/65 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for foul-smelling breath and poor dentition with erythema and edema of the patient’s gums. Pain is elicited when the patient swallows and the patient complains that their voice has sounded different recently. Crepitus is palpated in the submandibular region. Dermatologic exam reveals the finding in Figure A. The patient’s ECG demonstrates a left bundle branch block which is consistent with previous ECGs. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 59-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning causing them to experience several episodes of nausea and vomiting. Upon arriving, the patient’s symptoms have resolved. They state their symptoms occurred as they were going to bed. They have never experienced this before, but felt extremely dizzy for roughly 3 minutes. They currently feel at their baseline. The patient is otherwise healthy and only has a history of eczema. Their temperature is 97.7°F (36.5°C), blood pressure is 134/85 mmHg, pulse is 85/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a healthy patient with a normal gait. The patient has a physiologic nystagmus and their cranial nerve exam is unremarkable. The patient’s head is turned to the left and they are laid back on the stretcher, which exacerbates severe symptoms with a nystagmus notable. The patient’s symptoms improve after 2 minutes of being in this position. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient with a body mass index of 45 kg/m^2 presents to their primary care doctor with right hip pain. They assert that the pain is instigated by walking up and down stairs around a construction site which they oversee. On physical exam, their hips are symmetric and equal with no tenderness to palpation bilaterally. Their left lower extremity appears grossly normal with full range of motion. Their right knee appears symmetric, but the patient whimpers when the anteromedial part of the tibial plateau is pressed. No other parts of their knee are tender. No tenderness is elicited with extension, flexion, varus, and valgus movements of the knee. McMurray's test is negative with both internal and external rotation of the right leg. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old patient is found unconscious outside their home by a passing neighbor and is brought to the emergency department by ambulance. Cardio-pulmonary resuscitation is performed and the patient awakens but remains somnolent and confused. They are unable to answer questions or provide any medical history. Their temperature is 98.2°F (36.8°C), blood pressure is 108/62 mmHg, pulse is 110/min and respirations are 20/min. Physical exam shows decreased arousal. Pupils are round, symmetric, and reactive to light bilaterally. Fundoscopy is normal. The patient winces to palpation of the epigastric region and bilateral costovertebral angles. Initial labs are drawn and are shown below: Serum: Na+: 137 mEq/L K+: 3.1 mEq/L Cl-: 92 mEq/L HCO3-: 6 mEq/L BUN: 36 mg/dL Glucose: 100 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.7 mg/dL Bladder catheterization is notable for mildly bloody urine and microscopic analysis is shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the next step in management for the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 62-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with skin lesions. The patient states that they have felt itchy recently, then noticed skin lesions that broke out this morning prompting them to come to the emergency department. The patient states that they recently went camping and hiking in the woods. The patient drinks 1-2 beers per day and smokes 1 pack of cigarettes per day. They are currently sexually active with multiple partners and do not use condoms. The patient was discharged 1 week ago for pneumonia which was treated with azithromycin; however, they feel that their symptoms may be returning. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 157/78 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. On physical exam, you note the findings in Figure A on the patient's arm. The skin lesions are thick and do not break when pressure is applied. Which of the following best describes the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old patient is brought in to the pediatrician by their parent because they are concerned that the patient is not gaining weight. They report that the patient has a good appetite, eats a varied diet of solid foods, and drinks 2 cups of milk a day. The patient’s parent also reports that they have foul-smelling stools over 6 times a day. The patient has a history of recurrent bronchiectasis and chronic sinusitis. On physical examination, multiple nasal polyps are appreciated and scattered rhonchi are heard over both lung fields. The patient is below the 25th percentile in height and weight. Genetic testing is ordered to confirm the suspected diagnosis. Which of the following is most common complication associated with the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old patient with a past medical history of HIV on antiretroviral therapy presents to the emergency department with a rash. They were recently treated for streptococcal pharyngitis, smoke 1 pack of cigarettes per day, and use IV drugs regularly. The patient lives alone, owns 2 cats, and enjoys hiking and outdoor activities. They state that the rash was initially localized but has been spreading. They state that it is tender to the touch. The patient's vitals are within normal limits, and physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient comes to the emergency department complaining of blood in their urine and severe back pain. They report that the pain is left-sided, colicky, and began acutely this morning. The pain occasionally radiates to their left groin. They also report increased urinary frequency and an episode of blood-tinged urine. According to the patient, this has happened multiple times before. Their medical history is also notable for hypertension, type II diabetes mellitus, and obstructive sleep apnea. Their current medications include aspirin, metformin, and lisinopril. The patient’s temperature is 100.4°F (38°C), blood pressure is 148/85 mmHg, pulse is 71/min, and respirations are 14/min with an oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. Physical examination is significant for left-sided costovertebral angle tenderness. A urine dipstick is heme-positive. A urinalysis is pending. Labs are drawn, as shown below: Serum: Na+: 144 mEq/L Cl-: 95 mEq/L K+: 4.3 mEq/L HCO3-: 23 mEq/L Urea nitrogen: 18 mg/dL Glucose: 142 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL Calcium: 7.8 mg/dL A radiograph is obtained, as shown in Figure A. In addition to increasing fluid intake, which of the following can help the patient prevent future episodes of the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their parents for worsening symptoms. The patient recently saw their pediatrician for an acute episode of sinusitis. At the time, the pediatrician prescribed decongestants and sent the patient home. Since then, the patient has developed a nasal discharge with worsening pain. The patient has a past medical history of asthma which is well controlled with albuterol. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 90/48 mmHg, pulse is 124/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. On physical exam, you note a healthy young patient. Cardiopulmonary exam is within normal limits. Inspection of the patient's nose reveals a unilateral purulent discharge mixed with blood. The rest of the patient's exam is within normal limits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old patient presents to the emergency department after a motor vehicle accident. The patient was at a stop when they were rear-ended from behind by a vehicle traveling at 11 miles per hour. The patient complains of severe back pain but states they otherwise feel well. The patient is currently seeing a physical therapist who is giving them exercises to alleviate the back pain that is present every morning, relived by activity, and worse with inactivity. They are a student at the university and are struggling with their grades. Their temperature is 98.4°F (36.9°C), blood pressure is 117/78 mmHg, pulse is 116/min, respirations are 12/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam demonstrates a decreased range of motion of the patient's spine and tenderness to palpation over the vertebrae. The rest of the exam is deferred due to pain. The patient is requesting a note to excuse them from final exams and work. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 61-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with complaint of sudden onset, painless vision loss in their left eye upon waking up this morning. The patient says that they had no visual abnormalities prior to the incident and has had 20/20 vision in both eyes since undergoing cataract surgery the previous year. Their past medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia. An ophthalmology consult is called, and fundoscopic examination confirms the diagnosis (Figure A). Which of the following is the most likely cause for this patient’s vision loss?

A 47-year-old patient presents to the emergency department due to a rash. They state the rash started last night and is very concerning to them. The patient cannot remember being exposed to any environmental stimuli such as new detergents or poison ivy. The patient recently started following with a primary care provider who is helping them manage their arthritis and a new onset cough. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 127/68 mmHg, pulse is 125/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the findings of coalescing erythematous macules, bullae, desquamation, and mucositis only on the upper half of their back. Cardiopulmonary exam and abdominal exam are within normal limits. Inspection of the patient’s oropharynx reveals ulcers and erythema. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old patient is brought in by their parent to their pediatrician for headache and nausea. Their headaches began approximately 3 weeks ago and occur in the morning. Throughout the 3 weeks, their nausea has progressively worsened, and they had 2 episodes of emesis 1 day ago. On physical exam, cranial nerves are grossly intact, and their visual field is intact. The patient has a broad-based gait and difficulty with heel-to-toe walking, as well as head titubation. Fundoscopy demonstrates papilledema. A T1 and T2 MRI of the brain is demonstrated in Figures A and B, respectively. Which of the following is most likely the diagnosis?

A 24-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for a wellness exam. They currently have no acute concerns but have been feeling hopeless, have a poor appetite, difficulty with concentration, and trouble with sleep. They say that they have poor self-esteem and that their symptoms have been occurring for the past 3 years. They have had moments where they felt better, but it lasted a few weeks out of the year. They currently live alone and do not pursue romantic relationships because they feel they are not attractive. They have a past medical history of asthma. Their mother is alive and healthy. Their father committed suicide and suffered from major depressive disorder. On physical exam, the patient has a gloomy demeanor and appears restless and anxious. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 71-year-old patient arrives to your clinic complaining of sudden vision loss. They report that they had been in their usual state of health, until waking up this morning unable to see out of their right eye. They deny pain, but report their right eye “feels funny.” The patient’s medical history is significant for a previous myocardial infarction, hypertension, and osteoporosis. Their current medications include aspirin, metoprolol, rovustatin, lisinopril, and alendronate. The patient’s temperature is 98°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 145/86 mmHg, pulse is 62/min, and respirations are 12/min with an oxygen saturation of 98% O2 on room air. On physical exam, the patient's pupils are symmetrical in size and equally reactive to light with accommodation. Fundoscopic exam of the right eye is shown in Figure A. Left optic fundus is unremarkable. Of the following, what is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with joint pain. They state that since yesterday they have had joint pain, and today they noticed a rash. The patient does not have a significant past medical history. The patient smokes cigars, drinks 1 to 4 drinks per day, is sexually active, and uses cocaine occasionally. Their temperature is 101°F (38.3°C), blood pressure is 125/65 mmHg, pulse is 80/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam reveals pustular skin lesions and an inflamed and painful right knee that is warm to the touch. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment for the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old patient presents to their primary care provider for fatigue. They state that they have felt fatigued for the past 6 months and have tried multiple diets and sleep schedules to improve their condition, but none have succeeded. They have no significant past medical history. They are currently taking a multivitamin, folate, B12, iron, fish oil, whey protein, baby aspirin, copper, and krill oil. Their temperature is 98.8°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 107/58 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Laboratory values are as seen below. Hemoglobin: 8 g/dL Hematocrit: 24% Leukocyte count: 6,500/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 147,000/mm^3 Physical exam is notable for decreased proprioception in the lower extremities and 4/5 strength in the patient's upper and lower extremities. Which of the following is the best next step in management to confirm the diagnosis?

A 19-year-old university student presents to the student clinic with painful joints. They state that over the past week their right wrist has become increasingly stiff. This morning they noticed pain and stiffness in their left ankle and left knee. The patient has celiac disease and takes a daily multivitamin. They say they are sexually active with multiple partners. They smoke marijuana but deny intravenous drug abuse. They recently traveled to Uganda to volunteer at a clinic that specialized in treating patients with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). They also went on an extended hiking trip last week in New Hampshire. Physical exam reveals swelling of the right wrist and a warm, swollen, erythematous left knee. The left Achilles tendon is tender to palpation. There are also multiple vesicopustular lesions on the dorsum of the right hand. No genital discharge is appreciated. Arthrocentesis of the left knee is performed. Synovial fluid results are shown below: Synovial fluid: Appearance: Cloudy Leukocyte count: 40,000/mm^3 with neutrophil predominance Gram stain is negative. A synovial fluid culture is pending. Which of the following is the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old African American patient presents to their primary care physician with complaints of shortness of breath, fevers, and generalized joint pains. Vital signs are all stable and within normal limits. Physical examination is significant for cervical lymphadenopathy, coarse breath sounds bilaterally, and lesions on their bilateral legs, shown in Figure A. A chest radiograph is obtained and is shown in Figure B. Which of the following findings would be most consistent with this patient's likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their coworker for loss of consciousness. While working in the office, they fell from their chair, hit their head on a carpeted floor, and began to have generalized tonic-clonic seizures. The episode lasted approximately 3 minutes, and they felt confused afterwards. Upon interviewing the patient, they do not recall what happened prior or during the convulsive episode. They currently endorse a headache and tongue pain. They deny bowel or bladder incontinence. They report having night sweats and an unintentional 15-pound loss over the course of 2 months. They deny any alcohol use but report to have smoked 1 pack of cigarettes per day for the past 15 years, and previously worked as a farmer. Physical examination is notable for mild left-sided weakness, bilateral tongue bites, and findings demonstrated in Figure A. A non-contrast CT scan of the head is demonstrated in Figure B. Which of the following is most likely the diagnosis?

A 41-year-old patient comes to the office for an evaluation of a rash. They report the rash started 2 months ago on their knees and the rash has now appeared on their elbows. They deny pain or burning, but say the areas are mildly itchy and when they scratch them, they bleed. The patient is embarrassed because they work as a massage therapist. They report some fatigue, but attribute it to stress. They deny headache, weight loss, or joint pains. They have seasonal allergies and take daily loratadine. They had a tonsillectomy as a child. Their sibling has alopecia and their child has vitiligo. They smoke 1 pack a day and deny alcohol or other recreational drug use. They are sexually active with their partner of 15 years. On physical examination, there are symmetric erythematous plaques with overlying scales on the extensor surfaces of bilateral knees and elbows. One of the plaques is shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old patient with a past medical history of IV drug use and obesity presents to the emergency department with fever. They report fatigue and nasal congestion for about one week, which they think they caught from their sister who has an upper respiratory infection. They have no history of cardiac disease and endorse recent IV drug use. Their temperature is 101.8°F (38.8°C), blood pressure is 132/87 mmHg, pulse is 106/min, respirations are 15/min, and SpO2 is 97%. On physical exam, they appear to be in moderate distress. Their lungs are clear to auscultation, they have distant cardiac sounds, and the physical exam finding in Figure A is seen. Two sets of blood cultures drawn 12 hours apart are both positive for Staphylococcus aureus. Which of the following would be necessary to confirm the diagnosis of this patient’s illness?

A 6-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with hip pain that started this morning. The patient claims the pain is severe and is stopping them from skateboarding. The patient recently recovered from an upper respiratory infection that they caught from their siblings but has otherwise been healthy. The patient has a past medical history of obesity. Their temperature is 98.1°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 100/55 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. On physical exam, you note an obese patient in no acute distress. Cardiopulmonary exam is within normal limits. Inspection of the hip reveals no abnormalities or swelling. The hip exhibits a normal range of motion and physical exam only elicits minor pain. The patient's gait appears normal and pain is elicited when the patient jumps or runs. Which of the following is the best next step in management for this patient's most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for fatigue, weight loss, and diffuse pruritus. The patient has a past medical history of multiple admissions for severe abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea as well as several episodes of ascending cholangitis which were successfully treated. They are currently a member of Alcoholics Anonymous. Their temperature is 98.2°F (36.8°C), blood pressure is 124/75 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Urinalysis is notable only for a dark urine sample with no red blood cells present. A rectal exam reveals pale stool and grossly visible blood. Physical exam is otherwise notable for pruritis, jaundice, and scleral icterus. Which of the following is the most likely underlying diagnosis?

A 17-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for eye pain. The patient states that it has been going on for the past 3 days and has been steadily worsening. They recently suffered a superior orbital fracture secondary to playing football without a helmet that required no treatment other than to refrain from contact sports. The patient's past medical history is non-contributory, and their vitals are within normal limits. Physical exam demonstrates pain and swelling inferior to the patient's eye near the lacrimal duct. When pressure is applied to the area, expressible pus is noted. Cranial nerves II-XII are grossly intact. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 69-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with hip and back pain. The patient states that this weekend they had a barbecue. When they were lifting a heavy object they suddenly felt pain in their lower back. They describe the pain as in their buttocks but states that at times it travels down their leg. The patient states that it feels, "electrical." The patient has a past medical history of obesity, diabetes, depression, anxiety, diverticulosis, constipation, and a surgical repair of their anterior cruciate ligament. Their current medications include metformin, insulin, lisinopril, fluoxetine, and sodium docusate. Which of the following is most likely to help confirm the diagnosis?

A 30-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician complaining of headaches. They state that over the past month they have been trying to study for an accounting exam, but they find it increasingly more difficult to focus due to their headaches. They also complain of lower extremity muscle cramping. They have no significant past medical history and take ibuprofen and acetaminophen as needed. The patient’s temperature is 98°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 168/108 mmHg, and pulse is 75/min. Labs are obtained, as shown below: Serum: pH (VBG): 7.50 Na: 146 mEq/L K+: 3.2 mEq/L Cl-: 104 mEq/L HCO3-: 32 mEq/L Urea nitrogen: 20 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL Glucose: 85 mg/dL An ultrasound reveals a hypoechoic lesion within the right adrenal gland. A 2 cm right-sided homogeneous adrenal mass is confirmed with computed tomography. Which of the following findings is associated with the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with a chief complaint of "failing health." They state that they typically can converse with animals via telepathy, but are having trouble right now due to the weather. They have begun taking an assortment of Peruvian herbs to little avail. Otherwise they are not currently taking any medications. The patient lives alone and works in a health food store. They state that their symptoms have persisted for the past eight months. On physical exam, you note a healthy young patient who is dressed in an all burlap ensemble. When you are obtaining the patient's medical history there are several times they are attempting to telepathically connect with the animals in the vicinity. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old medical student returns from a volunteer mission trip in Nicaragua with persistent cough and occasional hemoptysis for 3 weeks. A purified protein derivative test revealing a 20 mm wheal and a chest radiograph with hilar lymphadenopathy support a diagnosis of active tuberculosis. The patient is started on appropriate therapy. Among the prescribed medications, one drug inhibits carbohydrate polymerization of the pathogen's cell wall. What is the most likely complaint that the patient may present with because of this drug?

A 70-year-old patient presents to an ophthalmology clinic for bilaterally blurred vision. Their symptoms have progressed gradually over several years, but they recently became concerned when they noticed that they could no longer read their newspaper without the help of a magnifying glass. They also mention that their eyes have been “playing tricks on them,” pointing out that the edges of the examination table appear curved, when they know they are usually straight. Physical exam is unremarkable. Fundoscopic exam (shown in Figure A) is similar in both eyes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old homeless patient is brought to the emergency department after they were found unconscious at the park. The patient's past medical history is unknown; however, they were admitted to the emergency department 2 times over the past year for severe pain treated with hydromorphone and IV fluids. Their temperature is 100°F (37.8°C), blood pressure is 97/48 mmHg, pulse is 140/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. The patient smells of alcohol and is covered in emesis. Basic laboratory values are ordered as seen below. Hemoglobin: 6 g/dL Hematocrit: 20% Leukocyte count: 6,500/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 197,000/mm^3 Reticulocyte count: 0.4% Which of the following is associated with the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician complaining of subjective fever, cough, and night sweats. They state that over the past 2 months they have “not felt like myself.” They have lost 12 lbs over this time period. Two weeks ago, they started experiencing night sweats and cough. This morning they decided to take their temperature and reports it was “high.” They have a history of HIV and admit to inconsistently taking their anti-retrovirals. A chest radiograph reveals a cavitary lesion in the left upper lobe. An interferon-gamma release assay is positive, and the patient is started on appropriate antimicrobial therapy. A month later they are seen in clinic for follow-up. Lab work is obtained, as shown below: Leukocyte count: 11,000/mm^3 with normal differential Hemoglobin: 9.2 g/dL Platelet count: 400,000/mm^3 Mean corpuscular volume (MCV): 75 µm^3 Based on these results, a peripheral smear is sent and shows Pappenheimer bodies. Which of the following is the most accurate test for the patient’s diagnosis?

A 28-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with lateral knee pain that started this morning. The patient is a college student who is currently on the basketball team. They state their pain started after they twisted their knee. Their current medications include albuterol and ibuprofen. The patient's vitals are within normal limits and physical exam is notable for tenderness to palpation over the lateral right knee. When the patient lays on their left side and their right hip is extended and abducted it does not lower to the table in a smooth fashion and adduction causes discomfort. The rest of their exam is within normal limits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 12-month-old patient is brought in by their parent who is worried about pallor. They say that the patient has always been fair-skinned, but over the past month relatives have commented that they appear more pale. The parent says that the patient seems to tire easy, but plays well with their older sibling and has even started to walk. They deny bloody or black stools, easy bruising, or excess bleeding. They states that the patient is a picky eater, but they love crackers and whole milk. On physical examination, pallor of the conjunctiva is noted. There is a grade II systolic ejection murmur best heard over the lower left sternal border that increases when the patient is supine. Labs are drawn as shown below: Leukocyte count: 6,500/mm^3 with normal differential Hemoglobin: 6.4 g/dL Platelet count: 300,000/mm^3 Mean corpuscular volume (MCV): 71 µm^3 Reticulocyte count: 2.0% Serum iron: 34 mcg/dL Serum ferritin: 6 ng/mL (normal range 7 to 140 ng/mL) Total iron binding capacity (TIBC): 565 mcg/dL (normal range 240 to 450 mcg/dL) On peripheral blood smear, there is microcytosis, hypochromia, and mild anisocytosis without basophilic stippling. Which of the following is the next best step in management for the patient’s diagnosis?

A 59-year-old patient presents to their ophthalmologist for an annual eye exam. The patient reports feeling well and has noticed some changes in their visual acuity. Medical history is significant for hypertension, type II diabetes, and ankylosing spondylitis. They are currently taking lisinopril, metformin, and naproxen. Family history is significant for glaucoma in their parents. Their intraocular pressure is 17 mmHg in the left eye and 18 mmHg in the right eye. The patient undergoes a slit-lamp examination and the findings are shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 52-year-old patient presents to the clinic with a headache and dizziness for the past month. The patient reports that about 4 weeks ago they developed a “nagging” headache. They thought they had a cold, so they tried over the counter ibuprofen that provided only mild and temporary relief. Recently, they also started feeling dizzy and nauseous, which only resolves when they step outside to shovel the snow. The patient’s medical history is significant for hypertension, type II diabetes mellitus, and asthma. Their medications include amlodipine, metformin, glimepiride, and a fluticasone/salmeterol inhaler. The patient has been living at their upstate cabin for the past 5 weeks but denies other recent travel. They deny smoking tobacco or illicit drug use. The patient’s temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 130/78 mmHg, pulse is 72/min, and respirations are 16/min with an oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. The patient is currently asymptomatic while sitting in the office, and physical examination is unremarkable. Labs are drawn, as shown below: Hemoglobin: 20 g/dL Hematocrit: 60% Leukocyte count: 10,050 cells/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 350,000/mm^3 Which of the following underlies the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old patient presents to their pediatrician for a wellness checkup. They have no complaints and state that they were recently hired as a construction worker. The patient has a past medical history of asthma and antisocial personality disorder. They are not currently taking any medications. They admit to smoking 1 pack of cigarettes per day. Their temperature is 98.8°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 127/78 mmHg, pulse is 70/min, respirations are 16/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the findings in Figure A. Which of the following is the diagnostic finding for this patient's most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with fatigue and a change in their memory. The patient and their spouse state that over the past several weeks the patient has been more confused and irritable and has had trouble focusing. They have had generalized and non-specific pain in their muscles and joints and are constipated. Their temperature is 99.3°F (37.4°C), blood pressure is 172/99 mmHg, pulse is 79/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is unremarkable. Laboratory studies are ordered as seen below. Hemoglobin: 9.0 g/dL Hematocrit: 30% Leukocyte count: 6,500/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 166,000/mm^3 MCV: 78 fL Serum: Na+: 141 mEq/L Cl-: 103 mEq/L K+: 4.6 mEq/L HCO3-: 25 mEq/L BUN: 20 mg/dL Glucose: 99 mg/dL Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to the emergency department for abdominal pain. The patient states that they have had abdominal pain for a while, but it became unbearable today and they are concerned. They also endorse a weight loss of 20 pounds this past month and complain of bulky and foul-smelling stools. The patient is homeless and is currently living by a local wash where they obtain their drinking water and clean their clothes. They admit to recently eating raw meat that they found. The patient has a past medical history of alcohol abuse, malnutrition, Wernicke-Korsakoff psychosis, IV drug use, and a recent hospitalization for intoxication of unknown etiology. The patient is not taking any medications currently. Their temperature is 99.1°F (37.3°C), blood pressure is 100/67 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 11/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. On physical exam, the patient complains of epigastric tenderness. Cardiopulmonary exam is within normal limits. The patient is started on IV fluids, thiamine, folate, magnesium, and dextrose. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below: Hemoglobin: 9.0 g/dL Hematocrit: 25% Leukocyte count: 5,500 cells/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 222,000/mm^3 Serum: Na+: 137 mEq/L Cl-: 102 mEq/L K+: 4.1 mEq/L HCO3-: 24 mEq/L BUN: 24 mg/dL Glucose: 68 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.4 mg/dL Ca2+: 9.8 mg/dL Amylase: 22 U/L Lipase: 22 U/L Aspartate aminotransferase (AST): 58 U/L Alanine aminotransferase (ALT): 18 U/L A computed tomography (CT) scan is obtained as seen in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old homeless patient presents to the emergency department for a rash. They state they have noticed the rash for the past several weeks and that it has not been improving. The patient has no history of medical care and no previous diagnoses. Review of systems is positive for a persistent dry cough and recent weight loss. Their temperature is 100°F (37.8°C), blood pressure is 107/68 mmHg, pulse is 110/min, respirations are 16/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old patient presents to the emergency department after a head-on motor vehicle collision. The patient is currently not responding to questions and is subsequently intubated. An initial FAST exam is negative. Their temperature is 97.5°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 62/42 mmHg, and pulse is 185/min. A massive transfusion protocol is initiated. The patient’s vitals improve to a pulse of 100/min and a blood pressure of 92/62. A chest radiograph is performed as seen in Figure A. After the chest radiograph has been performed, the patient’s vitals are 60/45 mmHg with a pulse of 178/min. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for a skin rash that has recently developed and is very itchy. The patient has a past medical history of asthma, seasonal allergies, constipation, anxiety, and depression. Their current medications include albuterol, fluticasone, diphenhydramine, fluoxetine, metformin, and clonazepam. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 139/67 mmHg, pulse is 80/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Pulmonary exam is notable for mild wheezes and good air movement. Cardiac exam reveals a normal rate and rhythm. Dermatologic exam reveals the findings seen in Figure A. Which of the following best describes the most likely diagnosis?

A 15-year-old patient presents to their primary care doctor for "eye pain." They state that they have noticed their left eye hurting more over the past four days. They normally wear disposable contact lenses daily but could not wear them because of the heightened sensation of something foreign in their eye. They have noticed occasional sensitivity to light. They deny any headaches, changes in vision, or pain with eye movement. They further deny any frank ocular or oral discharge but feel like something might pop if they squeeze hard enough. An image of their left eye is seen in Figure A. The right eye is completely healthy appearing. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 43-year-old patient is asked to be seen in the hospital for a worsening rash. They were admitted to the hospital 3 days ago after a fall. Their blood alcohol level at the time was 0.16%. Two days ago they noticed a rash forming on their legs. Since then, the rash has worsened. They deny pain or bleeding but endorse mild pruritis. Their medical history is significant for alcohol abuse, intravenous drug use, and hepatitis C. They do not take any medications. The patient’s temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 130/74 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, and respirations are 16/min. On physical examination, there is an abrasion on their right elbow and their right hip. There is no drainage or fluctuance. They have 1+ pitting edema of their bilateral lower extremities. The patient’s right leg is shown in Figure A, which is nearly identical to the left leg. There are also a few scattered violaceous papules on their buttocks. The appearance of the rash does not change with palpation. A skin biopsy is obtained, which reveals neutrophils perivascularly and within the vessel walls along with edema and fibrinoid necrosis. Immunofluorescence shows deposition of fibrinogen, C3, IgG, and IgM within the vessel walls. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with dizziness. They state they have experienced a sustained sense of disequilibrium for the past 2 days. They feel that the floor is unstable/moving. The patient is otherwise healthy and does not have any other medical diagnoses. The patient is currently taking vitamin C as multiple family members are currently ill and they do not want to get sick. Their temperature is 98.1°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 120/83 mmHg, pulse is 73/min, respirations are 16/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a horizontal nystagmus. The Dix-Hallpike maneuver does not provoke symptoms and examination of the patient’s cranial nerves is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with fever, nausea, and vomiting. The patient states that their symptoms started last night and have persisted to this morning. They have a past medical history of asthma, and their current medications include albuterol and fluticasone. Their temperature is 102°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 110/60 mmHg, pulse is 95/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. On physical exam, the patient seems uncomfortable. They request that the lights in the room stay turned off during the physical exam. The patient's cardiac exam demonstrates a normal rate and rhythm, and their pulmonary exam is clear to auscultation bilaterally. Musculoskeletal exam reveals diminished mobility of the neck in all four directions, with flexion of the neck causing the patient discomfort. Lumbar puncture is performed and results are seen below. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF): Cell count: 175/mm^3 Cl-: 119 mEq/L Glucose: 49 mg/dL Pressure: 150 mmH2O Total protein: 55 mg/dL Which of the following is the best treatment for this patient's most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with retrosternal pain that started this evening. The patient states that their symptoms started as they were going to bed after taking their medications. They describe the pain as sudden in onset, worse with swallowing, and not associated with exertion. The patient has a past medical history of diabetes, anemia, and congestive heart failure and is currently taking metoprolol, insulin, metformin, iron, and lisinopril. Their temperature is 99.2°F (37.3°C), blood pressure is 125/63 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 100% on room air. Physical exam is notable for an obese patient who appears uncomfortable. An initial electrocardiogram (ECG) demonstrates sinus rhythm, and a set of troponins are pending. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with a chief complaint of joint and muscle pain. They state that they have a general aching/pain in their joints that lasts all day. They state that the pain is constant and is not relieved by rest or activity. In addition, the patient complains of pain in their hands at times. Finally, they occasionally notice trouble swallowing when they are eating. The patient has a past medical history of anxiety and is not currently taking any medications. On physical exam, you note a healthy young patient with a sunburn. Their hands are mildly edematous, and you note the findings in Figure A. Laboratory values are ordered and are below: Serum: Na+: 145 mEq/L K+: 4.4 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L HCO3-: 24 mEq/L BUN: 9 mg/dL Glucose: 70 mg/dL Creatinine:.7 mg/dL Ca2+: 10 mg/dL Mg2+: 1.8 mEq/L Which of the following antibodies is most likely to aid in making the diagnosis in this patient?

A 27-year-old patient presents with acute abdominal pain in their right upper quadrant. The pain came on suddenly while they were eating dinner. After this pain they began feeling dizzy and came to the emergency department. In the ED, their blood pressure is 75/40 mmHg, pulse is 100/minute, and they are afebrile. On physical exam, they feel too light-headed to ambulate. They demonstrate normal bowel sounds with tenderness upon palpation in the right upper quadrant. The patient is deemed too unstable for imaging. An abdominal radiograph and CT are reviewed from a recent previous visit to the ED for mild abdominal pain, and are shown in Figures A and B, respectively. Which of the following specific additional findings in their history supports the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old patient is brought to their pediatrician by their parent who is worried about their clumsiness. They state that over the past 3 months they have noticed progressive weakness. They used to climb trees and run outside with their cousins, but now they say they get “too tired.” They’ve recently noticed them starting to “walk funny,” despite having “muscular legs.” Upon physical examination, the patient has calf muscle hypertrophy. They use their arms to rise out of the chair. Labs are obtained that show an elevated creatine kinase. Genetic analysis detects a dystropin gene mutation. A muscle biopsy is performed that reveals reduced dystrophin. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old nurse presents with left-sided chest pain and nonproductive cough. They think both the chest pain and the cough began about two months ago. They recently joined a meditation group and found that the deep breathing exercises exacerbate their chest pain. The patient denies headaches, fever, or chills. They report a 3 lb weight loss over the last two weeks, which they attribute to a change in their diet that they and their partner recently started. The patient drinks a glass or two of whiskey on the weekends and is a non-smoker. The patient’s medical history is significant for type II diabetes and Hodgkin lymphoma. They were treated with chemotherapy and radiation 25 years ago without complications. Their current medications include metformin and glyburide. Their HbA1c is 7.5%. Their temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 121/82 mmHg, pulse is 86/min, respirations are 12/min, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. Physical exam is notable for coarse rhonchi in the left lung. There is no appreciable lymphadenopathy. A chest radiograph is performed, which is shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 25-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with lower back pain. They state that they have had the pain for the past two years. The patient works as a butcher, and recently was moving heavy meat carcasses. The patient states that their pain is worse in the morning and that nothing improves it aside from swimming. The patient has a past medical history of anabolic steroid abuse, acne, hypertension, and obesity. Their current medications are hydrochlorothiazide, ibuprofen, topical benzoyl peroxide, and acetaminophen. On physical exam, there is no tenderness upon palpation of the spine. There is limited range of motion of the spine in all 4 directions. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 66-year-old patient presents to the clinic for evaluation of a new skin lesion on their hand. They are concerned because the lesion has grown rapidly over the previous 2 weeks. They endorse traumatizing the area and notes that there was some bleeding. Their past medical history is significant for chronic renal failure for which they received a renal transplant 5 years prior, as well as multiple surgeries for skin cancers. Their current medications include aspirin, atorvastatin, prednisone, tacrolimus, and mycophenolate mofetil. Physical exam is notable for a 2 x 2.5 cm nodular lesion of the dorsal hand (Figure A). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 80-year-old patient comes to the clinic for a follow-up visit. They have a long history of diabetes mellitus and recently had their diabetic screening exams (including a hemoglobin A1c of 7.2%), a normal foot examination, and normal lipid levels. Although they failed metformin and sulfonylurea therapy, the patient's diabetes is now well-controlled with glargine and insulin lispro. The patient states that they still drive and can see highway billboards and signs without trouble. They rarely read, opting to spend their retirement playing golf. During the patient's eye exam one month ago, the ophthalmologist's fundoscopic examination revealed scattered bright yellow drusen seen in Figure A. Visual examination today is 20/40 OD (right eye) and 20/40 OS (left eye). Two years ago, their visual acuity was 20/20 in both eyes. They state that they just have dry eyes and need to blink several times in order to get a perfect visual exam score. They deny any floaters, diplopia, or blurred vision. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 75-year-old patient presents to the physician with a complaint of a frequent need to void at nighttime, which has been disrupting their sleep. They note embarrassingly that they are often unable to reach the bathroom in time, and experiences urinary leakage throughout the night as well as during the day. The patient undergoes urodynamic testing and a urinalysis is obtained which is normal. They are instructed by the physician to perform behavioral training to improve their bladder control. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis contributing to this patient’s symptoms?

A 68-year-old patient is brought to their primary care physician's office by their spouse due to "itchy" blisters. They report that they were gardening yesterday when the patient began complaining of generalized itching. They then woke up this morning with multiple pruritic blisters. Their spouse tried using calamine lotion with no significant improvement. The patient’s medical history is significant for early dementia, asthma, hypertension, and inflammatory bowel syndrome. Their medications include aspirin and lisinopril. Their temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 121/82 mmHg, pulse is 86/min, respirations are 12/min, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. Physical examination shows areas of excoriation and tense bullae on their arms. A punch biopsy is obtained for immunofluorescence, which is shown in Figure A. Which of the following is associated with the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with vomiting. They state that they have experienced severe vomiting starting last night that has not been improving. They state that their symptoms improve with hot showers. The patient has presented to the emergency department with similar complaints several times in the past as well as for intravenous drug abuse. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 127/68 mmHg, pulse is 110/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is deferred as the patient is actively vomiting. Which of the following is associated with the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with pain along the bottom of their foot. The patient is a long-time runner but states that the pain has been getting worse recently. They state that when running and at rest they have a burning and aching pain along the bottom of their foot that sometimes turns to numbness. Taking time off from training does not improve their symptoms. The patient has a past medical history of surgical repair of their Achilles tendon, ACL, and medial meniscus. They are currently not taking any medications. The patient lives with their partner and they both practice a vegan lifestyle. On physical exam the patient states that they are currently not experiencing any pain in their foot but rather is experiencing numbness/tingling along the plantar surface of their foot. Strength is 5/5 and reflexes are 2+ in the lower extremities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with pain and a rash on their finger. They state that it started a week ago and think it is associated with cutting their finger on a pipe. They are generally healthy and have no past medical history. Their temperature is 98.7°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 129/82 mmHg, pulse is 83/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A, and there is pain with palpation of the finger. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with severe pain. The patient, who is a construction worker, was at work when they suddenly experienced severe pain in their arms, legs, chest, and back. They have experienced this before and were treated 2 months ago for a similar concern. Their temperature is 100°F (37.8°C), blood pressure is 127/68 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for tenderness to palpation of the patient's legs, chest, abdomen, and arms. Laboratory values are obtained and shown below. Hemoglobin: 10 g/dL Hematocrit: 30% Leukocyte count: 8,500/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 199,000/mm^3 Serum: Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L K+: 4.9 mEq/L HCO3-: 25 mEq/L BUN: 23 mg/dL LDH: 327 U/L Glucose: 99 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL AST: 12 U/L ALT: 10 U/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 77-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with a change in their mental status. The patient’s daughter states that they can cook and clean up after themselves and only needs help paying bills. Yesterday the patient seemed fine; however, this morning she noticed that they struggled to perform simple tasks and was forgetful while cooking, leaving the stove on. They recently returned from a trip to Mexico and admit to drinking unfiltered water and eating local cuisines while abroad. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension and diabetes. Their temperature is 97.5°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 187/118 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 16/min, and oxygen saturation is 100% on room air. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with nausea and vomiting. The patient states that they have felt nauseous for the past week and began vomiting last night. They thought their symptoms would resolve but decided to come in when their symptoms worsened. They feel that their symptoms are exacerbated with large fatty meals and when they drink alcohol. Their partner recently returned from a cruise with symptoms of vomiting and diarrhea. The patient has a past medical history of poorly managed diabetes, constipation, anxiety, dyslipidemia, and hypertension. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 197/128 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. Physical exam reveals a systolic murmur heard loudest along the left upper sternal border. Abdominal exam reveals an obese, tympanitic and distended abdomen with a 3 cm scar in the right lower quadrant. Vascular exam reveals weak pulses in the lower extremities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with left hip pain, stiffness, and hearing loss. The patient has a past medical history of diabetes and obesity. They played professional football when they were younger and are currently retired. The patient lives at home alone and admits to having lost some weight recently. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 167/98 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. A CT scan of the head is shown in Figure A, completed as a part of the workup for migraine at a recent emergency department visit. Physical exam reveals bilateral hearing loss but is otherwise unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with altered mental status. They were at work as a construction worker when their coworkers found them down at the work site. The patient recently underwent anesthesia for an appendectomy several months ago. They also have a past medical history of schizophrenia well controlled with haloperidol and are currently taking phenytoin for epilepsy. They are also currently taking propranolol for anxiety and hyperthyroidism. Their temperature is 106°F (41.1°C), blood pressure is 109/62 mmHg, pulse is 170/min, respirations are 23/min, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. Physical exam is notable for an altered patient with a Glasgow Coma Scale of 10. They have minimal muscle tone and are incoherent when answering questions. The patient is covered in sweat and dirt. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with eye pain. They state that for the past 2 days they have experienced severe eye pain and discharge from their eye. The patient has a past medical history of type I diabetes and is currently taking insulin. Their temperature is 102°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 127/68 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. Examination of cranial nerve III elicits pain. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old patient with a history of abdominal and thigh pain that runs in their family is brought into the emergency room by their parent. Their parent states they have a "blood disease." They also state the child was coughing and had fever to 101.1 F over the last three days and has been suddenly feeling much worse. On exam, the vitals are HR 110, BP 100/60, RR 20, T 101.5 F. CBC is significant for Hgb 3.2, WBC 2.1, Hct 10, Plts 30000. The reticulocyte count is 1% and the MCV is 81. Bone marrow biopsy shows hypocellular marrow with fatty tissue. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with a fever and a rash. This morning the patient was irritable and had a fever which gradually worsened throughout the day. They also developed a rash prior to presentation. They were previously healthy and are not currently taking any medications. Their temperature is 102.0°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 90/50 mmHg, pulse is 160/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a scarlatiniform rash with flaccid blisters that rupture easily, covering more than 60% of the patient’s body surface. The lesions surround the mouth but do not affect the mucosa, and palpation of the rash is painful. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old patient presents to your clinic with a 6-month history of pain in their hands. The pain is worse in the morning but is present throughout the day despite their use of ibuprofen. Additionally, their left 4th finger recently began to swell and is particularly painful. They have also begun to notice changes in their nails, which have become brittle. Prior to the onset of symptoms, they made multiple visits to the clinic with complaints of pain in their lower back and ankles that was eventually well controlled with ibuprofen. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), pressure is 138/88 mmHg, pulse is 78/min, and respirations are 18/min. Inspection of the hands demonstrates the physical examination findings present in Figure A. Additionally, a rash on the right elbow is identified and pictured in Figure B. The distal interphalangeal joints of the left hand are tender to palpation, as is the second distal interphalangeal joint of the right hand. The Achilles tendons are tender bilaterally, and ultrasonography is consistent with mild Achilles tendonitis bilaterally. Testing for HLA-B27 is positive. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old patient presents to the emergency department after a motor vehicle collision. They were the front seat unrestrained driver in a head-on collision. The patient has a Glasgow Coma Scale of 5 and is subsequently intubated. Physical exam is notable for subcutaneous emphysema in the clavicular area. Needle decompression and chest tube placement are performed, and the patient is stabilized after receiving 2 units of blood and 2 liters of fluid. Chest radiography demonstrates proper tube location and resolution of the pneumothorax. The patient is transferred to the trauma intensive care unit. On the unit, a repeat chest radiograph is notable for a recurrent pneumothorax with the chest tube in place. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 69-year-old patient is brought to clinic by their daughter for poor memory. She states that over the past two years the patient's memory has been slowly declining though they have been able to take care of themselves, pay their own rent, and manage their finances. However, two months ago she noticed a sharp decline in the patient's cognitive functioning as well as their gait. Then one month ago, she noticed a similar decline in the patient's functioning again that came on suddenly. The patient has a past medical history of diabetes mellitus type II, hypertension, obesity, and dyslipidemia. Current medications include hydrochlorothiazide, lisinopril, metformin, and glipizide. The patient's blood pressure is 165/95 mmHg, pulse is 82/minute, they are afebrile, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Cardiac exam reveals a crescendo-decrescendo murmur heard in the left upper sternal border that radiates to the carotids. Abdominal exam is benign, and neurologic exam reveals an unsteady gait. Which of the following findings is associated with the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old patient is brought into clinic by their daughter for increasing confusion. The daughter states that over the past 2 weeks, she has noticed that the patient “seems to stare off into space.” She reports they have multiple episodes a day during which they will walk into a room and forget why. She is also worried about their balance. She endorses that they have had several falls, the worst being 3 weeks ago when they tripped on the sidewalk getting the mail. The patient denies loss of consciousness, pre-syncope, chest pain, palpitations, urinary incontinence, or bowel incontinence. They complain of headache but deny dizziness. They report nausea and a few episodes of non-bloody emesis but deny abdominal pain, constipation, or diarrhea. The patient’s medical history is significant for atrial fibrillation, diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis. They take aspirin, warfarin, insulin, lisinopril, simvastatin, and ibuprofen. They drink a half glass of whisky after dinner every night and smoke a cigar on the weekends. On physical examination, they are oriented to name and place but not to date. They are unable to spell "world" backward. When asked to remember 3 words, they recall only 2. There are no motor or sensory deficits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department for a headache. The patient’s parent states that they normally have headaches in the morning; however, they tend to dissipate as the day goes on. They state the patient is otherwise healthy. The patient’s vitals are unremarkable. Physical exam is notable for a healthy young child. Notably, their gait is ataxic and they seem uncoordinated. An MRI scan of the head is performed as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with back pain. The patient states that they have gradually worsening back pain that seems to have worsened after moving furniture the other day. They also state that while they walk, they feel numbness and weakness in their legs. The only time the patient states their back pain is improved is when they are riding their bike or pushing a cart at the grocery store. The patient has a past medical history of osteoporosis, dyslipidemia, and diabetes. They drink 3 alcoholic drinks every day and have a 44 pack-year smoking history. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 157/108 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a non-tender spine with normal mobility in all 4 directions. Radiography of the spine and basic labs are ordered. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 37-year-old machinist presents to their primary care physician with eye problems. The patient states that they have had a mass in their eye that has persisted for the past month. The patient has a past medical history of blepharitis treated with eye cleansing and squamous cell carcinoma of the skin treated with Mohs surgery. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 157/102 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a firm and rubbery nodule palpable inside the patient's left eyelid. Physical exam does not elicit any pain. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 58-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician complaining of a facial rash. They state that they have had the rash for at least 10 years. The rash is on both cheeks and spreads across their nose. It normally comes and goes, but is exacerbated by sun exposure. The patient was recently fired, and is embarrassed of their rash, which has prevented them from accepting job interviews. They have tried various over the counter lotions and soaps with little improvement. They have no other complaints. Their medical history is significant for mild osteoarthritis and coronary artery disease. They take aspirin, simvastatin, and ibuprofen. On physical examination, you note telangiectasias on their bilateral eyelids. The rash is shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for fatigue. They state they have not felt like themselves recently and had to take a few days off of work secondary to fatigue. They have lost 10 pounds over the past month. They drink 4 drinks per day and smoke 1 pack of cigarettes per day, which they have done for the past 20 years. Their temperature is 99.0°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 128/65 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 11/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below. Hemoglobin: 9 g/dL Hematocrit: 27% Leukocyte count: 2,500/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 293,000/mm^3 A biopsy of the bone marrow is performed which demonstrates hypocellular and fibrotic bone marrow and a peripheral smear is performed as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old patient is sent to the emergency department by their primary care physician for hypertension. They were at a general health maintenance appointment when their blood pressure was found to be 180/115 mmHg; thus, prompting their primary doctor to send them to the emergency room. The patient is otherwise currently asymptomatic and states that they feel well. The patient has no other medical problems other than their hypertension and their labs that were drawn last week were within normal limits. Their temperature is 98.3°F (36.8°C), blood pressure is 197/105 mmHg, pulse is 88/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is unremarkable. Laboratory values are redrawn at this visit and shown below. Hemoglobin: 15 g/dL Hematocrit: 46% Leukocyte count: 3,400/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 177,000/mm^3 Serum: Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 102 mEq/L K+: 4.0 mEq/L HCO3-: 24 mEq/L BUN: 29 mg/dL Glucose: 139 mg/dL Creatinine: 2.3 mg/dL Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for fatigue. The patient states that they have not been sleeping well and requests sleep medication to help them with their fatigue. They recently changed their diet to try to increase their energy and has been on a vegetarian diet for the past several months. The patient has no significant past medical history. They smoke 1 pack of cigarettes per day and drink 5 alcoholic beverages per day. The patient has lost 12 pounds since their last visit 1 month ago. Physical exam demonstrates a tired patient. They appear thin, and their skin and sclera are icteric. Abdominal ultrasound is notable for a thin-walled and enlarged gallbladder. A urine sample is collected and is noted to be amber in color. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old patient arrives to the emergency room complaining of chest pain and difficulty breathing. They report the dyspnea started two months ago after having the flu. At first, the difficulty breathing occurred whenever they went up and down one flight of stairs, but since then the dyspnea has gotten progressively worse. This morning they developed chest pain and difficulty breathing while sitting at the kitchen table. The patient’s medical history is significant for hypertension, type II diabetes mellitus, and rheumatoid arthritis. Their medications include aspirin, lisinopril, metformin, and sulfasalazine. The patient’s temperature is 97°F (36.1°C), blood pressure is 130/78 mmHg, pulse is 88/min, and respirations are 14/min with an oxygen saturation of 97% O2 on room air. On physical exam, you note jugular venous distension during both inspiration and expiration, mild abdominal distention, and 2+ bilateral lower extremity edema. Radiography is demonstrated in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old patient presents to the gastroenterologist for chronic diarrhea and weight loss. They report that the diarrhea began 3 months ago. They deny seeing blood in their stool but states that their stool is foul-smelling and often “floats in the bowl.” They report that since their symptoms began they “can’t wear pants without belts.” They have not weighed themselves recently. Their normal diet consists of mainly red meats, cheese, fast food, and sugary, carbonated drinks. The patient recently immigrated from Barbados 1 year ago but has not been back since. Their medical history includes arthritis and hypothyroidism. They take aspirin and levothyroxine. The patient’s temperature is 100.9°F (38.3°C), blood pressure is 130/78 mmHg, pulse is 82/min, and respirations are 14/min. Physical examination reveals skin hyperpigmentation and swollen, painful elbows and knees. A fecal occult blood is positive. A colonoscopy is done with a biopsy and Periodic acid-Schiff staining, as shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the best long-term therapy for the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with fatigue that has gradually been worsening over the past month. The patient rarely sees their physician and came in today as they are unable to go to their exercise classes anymore. They also endorse joint pain in their right knee and hip that has been gradually worsening. The patient's vitals are notable only for hypertension. Physical exam reveals a fatigued appearing patient. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below: Hemoglobin: 8 g/dL Hematocrit: 25% Leukocyte count: 1,500/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 47,000/mm^3 A peripheral smear is performed as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old college student presents to their student health clinic complaining of a scaly rash on their right inner thigh. They report that the rash is itchy and first appeared 4 months ago. A similar rash occurred last year, which improved with a topical cream they purchased over the counter, but they do not remember the name. The patient has a history of attention deficient disorder and atopic dermatitis. Their medications include methylphenidate and betamethasone. The patient has been a wrestler since high school and currently wrestles for the university. They report they are doing well in their classes. They admit to smoking marijuana recreationally and having a few beers on the weekends with their friends. They went to Costa Rica for a 2-week mission trip 6 months ago. Physical exam reveals a lesion as shown in Figure A. Potassium hydroxide scrapings of the lesion confirm the diagnosis. Which of the following is the best treatment for the patient's most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old patient is brought in to your clinic by their parent, who is complaining of the patient's “dry scalp and hair loss.” They report a scaling spot on the patient's scalp developed around 2 months ago, soon after moving to a new school, which then became a larger bald spot. They deny that anyone in the household is exhibiting similar symptoms, but do recall a note that came home from school warning of a lice outbreak. Thus far, they have only tried daily baths with little improvement. The patient denies pain or itchiness, but the parent reports they do notice the patient scratching their scalp. The parent also reports that since the patient has started at the new school, they have noticed an increase in the patient's tics including excessive blinking and clearing of their throat. The patient's medical history is significant for asthma, allergic rhinitis, and attention deficient hyperactivity disorder. Their current medications include fluticasone, salmeterol, loratadine, and methylphenidate. Family history includes obsessive compulsive disorder in an older sibling. The parent also reports their parent had a debilitating skin and joint disorder. On examination, you note swollen lymph glands at the back of the patient's ears and neck, and there are residual black dots within a patch of alopecia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old patient presents to the emergency department after an episode of light-headedness. They were using the bathroom when they felt light-headed and fell to the floor. Their daughter found them and brought them into the emergency department right away. The patient has a past medical history of obesity and diabetes mellitus. They came to the emergency department 1 week ago for a similar complaint. The patient states that they have otherwise felt well with the exception of fatigue, constipation, an odd sensation in their chest, and a decreased appetite and desire to drink recently causing them to lose 10 pounds. Their temperature is 98.0°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 122/88 mmHg, pulse is 92/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam reveals a cardiopulmonary exam within normal limits and stable gait. The patient has an obese abdomen with abdominal distension. Strength is 5/5 in the upper and lower extremities. Which of the following is associated with the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with back pain. They are currently intoxicated but state that they are having severe back pain and are requesting morphine and lorazepam. The patient has a past medical history of alcohol abuse, drug seeking behavior, and IV drug abuse and does not routinely see a physician. Their temperature is 102°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 127/68 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for tenderness over the thoracic and lumbar spine. The pain is exacerbated with flexion of the spine. The patient’s laboratory values are notable for the findings below. Hemoglobin: 12 g/dL Hematocrit: 36% Leukocyte count: 16,500/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 197,000/mm^3 Serum: Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L K+: 4.3 mEq/L HCO3-: 25 mEq/L BUN: 20 mg/dL Glucose: 99 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL CRP: 5.2 mg/L Further imaging is currently pending. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-month-old patient is brought to the ED by their parent because of abdominal pain. Two weeks ago, they noticed the patient had a fever and looser stools, but both resolved after a few days. One week ago, the patient began to experience periodic episodes during which they would curl up into a ball, scream, and cry. The episodes lasted a few minutes, and were occasionally followed by vomiting. Between events, the patient was completely normal. They say the episodes have become more frequent over time, and this morning, they noticed blood in the patient's diaper. In the ED, the patient's vitals are within normal ranges, and their physical exam is normal. After confirming the diagnosis with an abdominal ultrasound, what is the next step in management?

A 52-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician at the insistence of their spouse who reports that they have been complaining of vague abdominal pain over the last several months. They ask if you think the patient's skin appears yellow. Vitals signs and laboratory findings are as follows: T 98.7F, HR 73, BP 114/68, RR 14, O2 100%. Hemoglobin 9.7, Hematocrit 31.2, WBC 6, Platelets 146. Amylase and lipase are within normal limits. You order a CT scan (Figure A). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their spouse for altered mental status. They report that the patient was in their usual state of health until 3 days ago when they developed a headache and fever. Then today they found the patient lying in the bedroom in the dark. When they turned on the light, the patient covered their eyes. Other than that, the patient was minimally responsive. The patient is adopted and does not know their family history. Their spouse reports that the patient occasionally has a beer or two with dinner, and works as a landscaper. The patient’s temperature is 103°F (39.5°C), blood pressure is 131/78 mmHg, pulse is 84/min, and respirations are 14/min with an oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. Physical examination is notable for neck stiffness and a rash that is shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the best treatment for the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old patient presents to the physician with complaints of fatigue, weakness, and loss of appetite for the past 3-4 months despite attempts to adjust their sleep schedule to accommodate more rest. As part of their work up, a peripheral blood smear is obtained and is shown in Figure A. On physical examination, the patient has a smooth, swollen tongue and diminished vibratory sensation in their lower extremities. Given the patient’s most likely diagnosis, which of the following associated pathologies should be screened for in this patient?

A 23-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with bloody vomitus. The patient is an alcoholic and has presented similarly before. They are given ondansetron; however, they continue to vomit. The patient complains of sudden substernal chest pain and dysphagia after another bout of vomiting. Their temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 117/60 mmHg, pulse is 122/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is notable for an uncomfortable patient with subcutaneous emphysema in the patient’s neck and supraclavicular areas. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old patient presents to their pediatrician for a wellness checkup. The patient states they feel well and have been excelling in school. They are on their school's wrestling and football team and are currently sexually active with their partner. Physical exam reveals an energetic young patient with the finding seen in Figure A, which is coarse upon palpation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 10-year-old patient is admitted to the medical floor for a respiratory infection. The patient lives in a foster home and has been admitted many times. Since birth, the patient has had repeated episodes of pain/pressure over their frontal sinuses and a chronic cough that produces mucus. They were recently treated with amoxicillin for an infection. The patient is in the 25th percentile for height and weight which has been constant since birth.
