Their guardians state that the patient has normal bowel movements and has been gaining weight appropriately. The patient has a history of tricuspid stenosis. They also recently had magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of their chest which demonstrated dilation of their airways. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 90/58 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 94% on room air. Physical exam is notable for bruises along the patient's shins which the guardians state are from playing soccer. The rest of the exam is deferred because the patient starts crying. Which of the following findings is associated with this patient's most likely underlying diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with painful skin lesions. The patient has had similar lesions for the past several months but states they have worsened recently. They have a past medical history of diabetes, a middle ear infection, and urinary tract infection, which were treated with antibiotics. The patient has allergies to latex and sulfa drugs. They work as a mountain ranger and regularly hike through forestry. Their temperature is 98.4°F (36.9°C), blood pressure is 167/108 mmHg, pulse is 95/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam demonstrates the lesions seen in Figure A which separate and break open when minimal pressure is applied. Oral mucosal erosions are also seen upon inspection of the oropharynx. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old patient is seen in the hospital for a sacral rash. The patient has been hospitalized for the past 3 weeks for a heart failure exacerbation. When the nurse went to bathe them this morning, they noticed a red rash over their sacrum. The patient reports mild discomfort and denies pruritus. The patient has chronic kidney disease, urinary incontinence, ischemic cardiomyopathy, gout, and poor mobility. Their current medications include aspirin, furosemide, metoprolol, lisinopril, spironolactone, and prednisone that was started for a recent gout flare. The patient’s temperature is 97°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 110/62 mmHg, pulse is 68/min, and respirations are 13/min with an oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. On physical examination, there is a 4 cm x 6 cm patch of non-blanchable erythema over the patient’s sacrum that is mildly tender to palpation. Labs are obtained, as shown below: Leukocyte count: 10,000/mm^3 with normal differential Hemoglobin: 15.2 g/dL Platelet count: 400,000/mm^3 Serum: Na: 138 mEq/L K+: 4.3 mEq/L Cl-: 104 mEq/L HCO3-: 25 mEq/L BUN: 26 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.5 mg/dL Glucose: 185 mg/dL A hemoglobin A1c is pending. Which of the following is the best management for the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old immigrant from Nigeria presents to the emergency department for sudden, severe pain and swelling in their lower extremity. They were at a rehabilitation hospital when their symptoms became apparent. The patient has a past medical history of obesity, diabetes, bipolar disorder, and tonic-clonic seizures. Their current medications include metformin, insulin, lisinopril, and valproic acid. The patient is a prominent IV drug and alcohol user who has presented to the ED many times for intoxication. On physical exam, you note anasarca and asymmetric lower extremity swelling. Based on the results of a doppler ultrasound of their swollen lower extremity, heparin is started. The patient is then transferred to the general medicine floor for continued management. Laboratory studies are shown below. Serum: Na+: 137 mEq/L K+: 5.5 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L HCO3-: 24 mEq/L Urea nitrogen: 22 mg/dL Ca2+: 5.7 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.7 mg/dL Glucose: 70 mg/dL What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 58-year-old patient presents with their spouse to their primary care physician for an annual check-up. The patient reports that they have been in their usual state of health except for a recent worsening of their seasonal allergies. Their spouse states that this happens every spring and that the patient's symptoms include sneezing, runny nose, and watery eyes. The spouse also asks about a lesion on the patient's face that they noticed several weeks ago when the patient was wiping their nose. The patient has a history of hypertension and well-controlled diabetes. They take lisinopril, aspirin, and metformin as prescribed. The patient's temperature is 98°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 130/78 mmHg, pulse is 72/min, and respirations are 14/min. Physical examination is notable for mild conjunctival injection bilaterally and a nodule located inferior to the left nasal ala, as shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the best therapy for the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-week-old patient presents to the emergency department with vomiting. Their parents report that they suddenly started vomiting this morning and have shown no interest in feeding since then. They describe the vomitus as green and without any traces of blood. Prior to today, the patient was feeding, voiding, and stooling well. They were noted to have surpassed their birth weight at their last office visit one week ago. In the emergency room, their temperature is 97.6°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 78/56 mmHg, pulse is 148/min, and respirations are 44/min. On physical exam, the patient is in mild distress. They have no dysmorphic features, and their mucous membranes are dry. Their abdomen is soft and distended. Bowel sounds are hypoactive. An abdominal radiograph is performed and can be seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the best next step in the diagnosis of this condition?

A 34-year-old patient arrives to your office complaining of a recurrent rash. The first time the patient noticed the rash was after going in the water at the beach six weeks ago. They report that since then, they have developed similar appearing pink and itchy rashes on their arms and legs. They state that the rashes eventually resolve on their own. The patient works as a forest ranger at a national park. Their medical history is significant for systemic lupus erythematous and asthma. Their current medications include NSAIDS and an albuterol inhaler. They report that they have seasonal allergies but no food intolerances. Their temperature is 98°F (36.7°C), pulse is 70/min, blood pressure is 118/77 mmHg, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Upon physical examination, you appreciate diffuse, mild expiratory wheezes. There is no evidence of airway obstruction. When ice is placed on their leg, a rash appears, as pictured in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient is brought into the emergency department after a car ran into them while they were riding their bike. The patient is conscious and alert. They state that their arm is in pain and they are requesting morphine. The patient's past medical history is non-contributory and they are not currently on any medications. Their temperature is 97.5°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 124/65 mmHg, pulse is 122/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. An initial splint is placed. A radiograph is performed and physical exam is notable for the findings in Figure A when the patient is asked to extend their fingers. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parents due to observations of rapid, random, horizontal and vertical eye movements along with occasional jerking movements of their limbs and head. CT scan reveals an abdominal mass that crosses the midline. Further work-up reveals elevated 24-hour urinary homovanillic acid and vanillylmandelic acid. Which of the following diseases pathologically originates from the type of cells as this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old patient presents to clinic complaining of multiple symptoms including skin lesions and worsening bone pain. They just returned from a 6-month stay in Guatemala, where they volunteered to build homes in an underdeveloped community. While they were there, they developed scaling papulonodular skin lesions on their left hand and right wrist. They also complain of bone pain, specifically in their right forearm and right thigh, and a persistent dry cough. They state they have been very tired lately, which is why it took them so long to see a doctor when they returned from their trip. Since returning, they have been living in Arizona for the past 2 weeks with their brother who owns 2 parrots and a dog. The patient’s temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 110/68 mmHg, pulse is 88/min, and respirations are 17/min with an oxygen saturation of 97% on room air. Their complete blood count reveals pancytopenia. A peripheral blood smear shows evidence of lymphoblasts. A computed tomography of the chest reveals multiple, centrilobular nodules in the left upper lobe. A radiograph of the right thigh and right upper extremity shows osteolytic bone lesions. A biopsy of the skin lesion on their left hand is obtained, and the results are shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with weakness. They state that at the end of the day they feel so fatigued and weak that they can hardly care for themselves. They currently feel this way. The patient has had multiple illnesses recently and has been traveling, hiking, and camping. Their temperature is 98.0°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 124/84 mmHg, pulse is 82/min, respirations are 12/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for 2/5 strength of the upper extremities and 4/5 strength of the lower extremities. Visual exam is notable for mild diplopia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician concerned about their weight. They state they have been gaining weight though do not feel they have changed their diet. The patient also states they have felt fatigued lately and not themselves. They deny taking any medications or using any illicit substances at baseline. Their temperature is 99.2°F (37.3°C), blood pressure is 177/108 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for an obese patient with striae on the abdomen. A 24-hour urine free cortisol is collected and demonstrates an elevated cortisol level; however, a high dose of dexamethasone when administered results in no attenuation of cortisol release. A CT scan of the abdomen is within normal limits. Which of the following is associated with the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department for bowling at a local bowling alley while inappropriately dressed. The patient refused to speak with police and was seen conversing with inanimate objects in the back of the police car. The patient states that their clothes were contaminated by assassins who have been tracking them for years. The patient refuses to answer any further questions, and continues to whisper toward someone else. The patient has a past medical history of homelessness, alcohol abuse, marijuana use, and cocaine abuse. Physical exam is notable for a healthy young patient who seems mistrustful of all hospital personnel. The patient is started on a medication and is transferred to the psychiatric inpatient unit. The patient’s condition improves, but they still often speak of a contamination that is on their clothes and skin that is coming from external parties. The patient is started on a new medication. They are then sent to group therapy, followed by physical activity in the yard. The physician is called over when the patient is found down in the recreation yard while they were exercising. The patient is not responsive, and their limbs seem to resist passive force. Their temperature is 104°F (40°C), pulse is 112/min, blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. Which of the following best describes the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for a routine physical exam. They are concerned about a burning sensation that they feel in their throat whenever they eat large meals and are concerned they may have esophageal cancer like their uncle. The patient has a past medical history of irritable bowel syndrome and constipation. Their current medications include whey protein supplements, fish oil, a multivitamin, and sodium docusate. The patient is concerned about their performance in school and fears they may fail out. They recently did poorly on an exam and it has caused them significant stress. They also are worried that their partner is going to leave them. The patient claims that they thought they were going to be an incredible doctor some day, but now they feel like a terrible person. The patient also states that they feel guilty about their grandfather's death which occurred 1 year ago and they often reexperiences the funeral in their mind. They regularly have trouble sleeping for which they take melatonin. The patient has been praying every 4 hours with the hopes that this will make things go better for them. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient presents to their primary care provider for shoulder pain. They report that they initially thought the pain was due to "sleeping funny" on the arm, but that the pain has now lasted for 4 weeks. They deny trauma to the joint and say that the pain is worse when reaching overhead to retrieve things from their kitchen cabinets. On physical exam, the patient's shoulders are symmetric, and the right lateral shoulder is tender to palpation. The shoulder has full passive and active range of motion, although pain is reproduced on active abduction of the right arm above 90 degrees. Pain is also reproduced on passively internally rotating and then lifting the shoulder. The patient is able to resist elbow flexion without pain, and they otherwise have 5/5 strength. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old patient presents to the emergency department after a motor vehicle accident. They were the unrestrained front seat driver in a head-on collision. The patient is unresponsive and their medical history is unknown. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 67/38 mmHg, pulse is 190/min, respirations are 33/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. The patient is started on IV fluids, blood products, and norepinephrine. A FAST exam is performed and a pelvic binder is placed. One hour later, their temperature is 98.3°F (36.8°C), blood pressure is 119/66 mmHg, pulse is 110/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. The patient is currently responsive. Management of the patient's pelvic fracture is scheduled by the orthopedic service. While the patient is waiting in the emergency department, they suddenly complain of feeling hot, aches, and a headache. The patient's temperature is currently 101°F (38.3°C). They have not been given any pain medications and their past medical history is still unknown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 63-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with periorbital swelling. They state that they were gardening, came inside, looked in the mirror, and then noticed their eyelids were swollen. They deny pain, pruritus, or visual disturbances. They state that they were drinking “a lot of water" to prevent dehydration, because it was hot outside this morning. Their medical history is significant for rheumatoid arthritis. They take methotrexate and acetaminophen as needed. The patient’s temperature is 98°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 168/108 mmHg, and pulse is 75/min. Physical examination is notable for periorbital edema, hepatomegaly, and bilateral 1+ pitting lower extremity edema. Labs and a urinalysis are obtained, as shown below: Leukocyte count: 11,000/mm^3 Hemoglobin: 14 g/dL Serum: Na: 138 mEq/L K+: 4.3 mEq/L Cl-: 104 mEq/L HCO3-: 25 mEq/L Urea nitrogen: 26 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.4 mg/dL Glucose: 85 mg/dL Aspartate aminotransferase (AST, GOT): 15 U/L Alanine aminotransferase (ALT, GPT): 19 U/L Albumin: 2.0 g/dL Urine: Protein: 150 mg/dL Creatinine: 35 mg/dL An abdominal ultrasound reveals an enlarged liver with heterogeneous echogenicity and enlarged kidneys with increased echogenicity in the renal parenchyma. A biopsy of the kidney is obtained. Which of the following biopsy findings is associated with the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 12-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their parent for a rash. The patient had a sore throat a few days ago with symptoms initially well-controlled with lozenges. However, today they had a rash covering their body, which prompted their presentation. The parent states that they did smear an herbal remedy on the rash with no alleviation in symptoms and also gave them a single dose of amoxicillin left over from a previous infection. The patient is up to date on their vaccinations and has no past medical conditions. Their temperature is 101°F (38.3°C), blood pressure is 102/68 mmHg, pulse is 97/min, respirations are 19/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the findings in Figures A and B. The rash seen in Figure B is very coarse. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient presents to the emergency department for shortness of breath. They were at home working on their car when they suddenly felt very short of breath, which failed to improve with rest. They state they were working with various chemicals and inhalants while trying to replace a broken piece in the engine. The patient was brought in by paramedics and is currently on 100% O2 via nasal cannula. The patient has a 52 pack-year smoking history and drinks 2 to 3 alcoholic drinks every night. They have a past medical history of asthma but admit to not having seen a physician since high school. Their temperature is 98.2°F (36.8°C), blood pressure is 157/108 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 29/min, and oxygen saturation is 77%. Physical exam demonstrates tachycardia with a systolic murmur heard best along the right upper sternal border. Breath sounds are diminished over the right upper lobe. Bilateral lower extremity pitting edema is noted. Which of the following best describes the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician after noticing a new growth on their back. Their spouse first saw it several weeks ago and they thought it was a scab that would resolve, but it has persisted. The patient denies any itching or pain. They have a past medical history of gastroesophageal reflux for which they take omeprazole. They are also an active smoker with a 45 pack-year history. The patient has a family history of colon cancer in their father and stroke in their mother. At this visit, the patient’s temperature is 98.6°F (37.0°C), pulse is 76/min, blood pressure is 128/85 mmHg, and respirations are 13/min. Cardiopulmonary and abdominal exams are unremarkable. Skin examination of their back is shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old patient with a history of IV drug and alcohol abuse presents to the emergency department with back pain. They state that their symptoms started 3 days ago and have been gradually worsening. Their temperature is 102°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 127/68 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for tenderness over the mid thoracic spine. Laboratory values are only notable for a leukocytosis and an elevated ESR and CRP. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old patient with type II diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and hypothyroidism presents to the emergency room with 6 months of worsening headaches and vision changes. Initially, their headaches were dull and infrequent, but they now occur daily and have become quite severe. They state that their symptoms are worse in the morning. They do not improve substantially with ibuprofen or acetaminophen. The patient requests prescription medication as they can no longer tolerate the pain. They have also been experiencing fatigue, nausea, increased thirst, and frequent urination. Their current medications include insulin, metformin, atorvastatin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, and levothyroxine. They confirm that they have been taking all their medications as prescribed. They also reveal that their peripheral vision has been getting worse, though they think this may be due to old age. Their temperature is 97.9°F (36.6°C), blood pressure is 139/89 mmHg, pulse is 82/min, respirations are 11/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for mild impairment of their lateral visual fields. A non-contrast CT scan of the head is performed and shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old student has an appointment with their primary care physician for an annual check-up. They are in their usual state of health. They say their sophomore year of college went well, and they’re currently been home working as a lifeguard for the summer. They ask about a good sunscreen to prevent their “sun-spots.” They report that every summer for the last 2 years they have developed an “uneven” rash that sometimes is itchy but is otherwise asymptomatic. The rash never bothered them until recently when their friends and other pool attendees started asking if they're "peeling from a bad sunburn." Their past medical history is significant for well-controlled type I diabetes mellitus. They are currently on insulin. Physical examination shows cutaneous lesions on the chest and upper extremities, which are depicted in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 59-year-old African American patient presents to the emergency department for fever and back pain that has persisted for 2 days. The patient states that the pain is episodic and intense. Their symptoms have not responded to acetaminophen. The patient endorses having lost 7 pounds recently without trying to lose weight. They also state that they have had abdominal pain and trouble focusing at work as well as a recent cough and fever which they attribute to allergies. The patient’s past medical history is notable for a recent distal radius fracture and a 50 pack-year smoking history. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 127/67 mmHg, pulse is 99/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for left-sided flank tenderness. The patient assumes an antalgic position in the stretcher. Chest radiography is performed as seen in Figure A. Laboratory studies are ordered as seen below. Hemoglobin: 14 g/dL Hematocrit: 44% Leukocyte count: 10,500/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 195,000/mm^3 Serum: Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L K+: 4.3 mEq/L HCO3-: 25 mEq/L BUN: 20 mg/dL Phosphate: 1.5 mg/dL Glucose: 99 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL Ca2+: 12.2 mg/dL AST: 12 U/L ALT: 10 U/L Ultrasound reveals unilateral hydronephrosis. Which of the following is the most likely underlying diagnosis for this patient’s presentation?

A 22-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by police after they were found undressing themselves outside in 110°F weather. The patient refuses to answer any questions as they suspect that their care team is spying on them. The patient recently started college and has presented to the emergency department once before for polysubstance intoxication. The patient attempts to assault a nurse, is restrained, and given diphenhydramine and haloperidol. When the patient is able to be examined, they are somnolent and non-responsive. Their temperature is 104°F (40°C), blood pressure is 147/98 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. They do not comply with any commands, and it is not possible to freely manipulate their extremities due to rigidity. Their mucous membranes are dry. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old patient presents to their nearby clinic for a non-healing and painful leg ulcer. The sore started approximately 3 weeks ago as a tender nodule. They first noticed the bump after hitting their shin during a soccer game. The lesion later “opened up” into an ulceration. The patient also complains of lower back pain and intermittent diarrhea for the past four months. The patient’s medical history is non-significant except for chlamydia for which they were successfully treated. They use acetaminophen for the back pain but take no other medications. The patient is sexually active with two partners. They smoke marijuana daily. They report they recently returned from their summer volunteering at a children’s soccer program in Uganda. While there they reports getting bit by mosquitos and took anti-malarial medication as prescribed. Physical examination shows limited spine flexion and a lesion as pictured in Figure A. Labs are drawn and are shown below: Hemoglobin: 10.9 g/dL Leukocyte count: 10,800/mmm^3 Platelet count: 320,000/mm^3 Urinalysis: Protein: Negative Blood: Negative Nitrites: Negative Bacteria: None White blood cells: 1-2/hpf Red blood cells: 3-5/hpf Stool cultures are negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with weakness of their right arm. The patient states they have experienced these symptoms for a few weeks; however, today their hand felt so weak they dropped their cup of tea. The patient has a past medical history of diabetes. They drink 2-7 alcoholic drinks per day and have smoked 2 packs of cigarettes per day since they were 25. The patient admits to using anabolic steroids. They have lost 17 pounds since they last came to the emergency department 1 month ago. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 177/108 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam reveals decreased sensation in the right arm and 2/5 strength in the right arm and 5/5 strength in the left arm. The patient states that they are experiencing a dull aching and burning pain in their right arm during the exam. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old patient presents to the emergency department after an episode of syncope. They state that for the past month, ever since starting a new job, they have experienced an episode of syncope or near-syncope every morning while they are getting dressed. The patient states that they now get dressed, shave, and put on their tie sitting down to avoid falling when they faint. They have never had this before and are concerned it is stress from their new job as they have been unemployed for the past 5 years. They are wondering if they can get a note for work since they were unable to head in today secondary to their presentation. The patient has no significant past medical history and is otherwise healthy. Their temperature is 99.2°F (37.3°C), blood pressure is 122/83 mmHg, pulse is 92/min, respirations are 16/min, and oxygen saturation is 100% on room air. Cardiopulmonary and neurologic exams are within normal limits. An initial ECG and laboratory values are unremarkable as well. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old patient presents to the emergency department after a motor vehicle collision. The patient was the back seat restrained passenger in a vehicle that was rear ended at 25 miles/hour. The patient has a past medical history of diabetes, hypertension, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Their temperature is 97.5°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 97/68 mmHg, pulse is 130/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. The patient is subsequently worked up receiving a chest radiograph, ECG, FAST exam, and serum chemistries. A cardiac catheterization reveals equilibration in diastolic pressure across all cardiac chambers. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 66-year-old patient is brought into the emergency department by their daughter for a change in behavior. Yesterday the patient seemed more confused than usual and was asking the same questions repetitively. Their symptoms have not improved over the past 24 hours, thus the decision to bring them in today. Last year, the patient was almost completely independent but they then suffered a "series of falls," after which their ability to care for themselves declined. After this episode they were no longer able to cook for themselves or pay their bills but otherwise had been fine up until this episode. The patient has a past medical history of myocardial infarction, hypertension, depression, diabetes mellitus type II, constipation, diverticulitis, and peripheral neuropathy. Their current medications include metformin, insulin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, sodium docusate, atorvastatin, metoprolol, fluoxetine, and gabapentin. On exam you note a confused patient who is poorly kept. They have bruises over their legs and their gait seems unstable. They are alert to person and place, and answer some questions inappropriately. The patient's pulse is 90/minute and their blood pressure is 170/100 mmHg. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 15-year-old patient is brought in to see their pediatrician by their parent to examine the patient's acne. The patient asserts that they maintain excellent hygiene. They use mild soap and water to wash their face and have not manually disturbed any skin lesion. However, their parent noticed that one of their "acne" ruptured while eating dinner, producing a foul odor and a cheese-like white exudate. The patient has a past medical history of asthma and eczema. Their current medications include albuterol, fluticasone, and topical corticosteroids as needed. Examination of the patient's face reveals a firm, movable, nontender lesion shown in Figure A. The remainder of their scalp, face, and neck are unremarkable. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with a headache. They state that they felt a bad headache come on this morning while they were gardening and carrying heavy pots, and it has not been improving. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension and diabetes which is currently being treated by their primary care physician. Their temperature is 99.0°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 157/99 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 16/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. A head CT is ordered as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the best explanation for the most likely diagnosis?

A 69-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for a general checkup. The patient works as a farmer and gardens in their spare time. The patient has a past medical history of poorly managed diabetes mellitus type II, and irritable bowel syndrome. Their current medications include lisinopril, metformin, insulin, fiber supplements, and a multivitamin. On physical exam, you note an obese patient. Inspection of the patient's scalp reveals the finding in Figure A. The patient is sent home and instructed to keep a blood glucose journal and to return with it in three months. Three months later, the patient returns with their glucose journal. In addition, they complain of a cut on their scalp that is not seeming to heal. The patient's glucose journal reveals an average blood glucose of 175 mg/dL. On inspection of the patient's scalp, you note the finding in Figure B. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 21-year-old patient presents to their primary care provider for fatigue. They report that they graduated from college last month and returned 3 days ago from a 2 week vacation to Vietnam and Cambodia. For the past 2 days, they have developed a worsening headache, malaise, and pain in their hands and wrists. The patient has a past medical history of asthma managed with albuterol as needed. They are sexually active with multiple partners, and they use condoms “most of the time.” On physical exam, the patient’s temperature is 102.5°F (39.2°C), blood pressure is 112/66 mmHg, pulse is 105/min, respirations are 12/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. They have tenderness to palpation over their bilateral metacarpophalangeal joints and a maculopapular rash on their trunk and upper thighs. Tourniquet test is negative. Laboratory results are as follows: Hemoglobin: 14 g/dL Hematocrit: 44% Leukocyte count: 3,200/mm^3 Platelet count: 112,000/mm^3 Serum: Na+: 142 mEq/L Cl-: 104 mEq/L K+: 4.6 mEq/L HCO3-: 24 mEq/L BUN: 18 mg/dL Glucose: 87 mg/dL Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL AST: 106 U/L ALT: 112 U/L Bilirubin (total): 0.8 mg/dL Bilirubin (conjugated): 0.3 mg/dL Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 41-year-old patient presents to their primary care provider after seeing bright red blood in the toilet bowl after their last two bowel movements. They report that the second time they also noticed some blood mixed with their stool. The patient denies abdominal pain and any changes in their stool habits. They note a weight loss of eight pounds in the last two months. Their past medical history is significant for an episode of pancreatitis two years ago for which they were hospitalized for several days. They drink 2-3 beers on the weekend, and they have never smoked. They have no family history of colon cancer. Their temperature is 97.6°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 135/78 mmHg, pulse is 88/min, and respirations are 14/min. On physical exam, their abdomen is soft and nontender to palpation. Bowel sounds are present, and there is no hepatomegaly. Which of the following is the best next step in diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient presents to the emergency room with persistent fever, nausea, and vomiting for the past 3 days. While waiting to be seen, they quickly become disoriented and agitated. Upon examination, they have visible signs of difficulty breathing with copious oral secretions and generalized muscle twitching. The patient’s temperature is 104°F (40°C), blood pressure is 90/64 mmHg, pulse is 88/min, and respirations are 18/min with an oxygen saturation of 90% on room air. When the nurse tries to place a nasal cannula, the patient becomes fearful and combative. The patient is sedated and placed on mechanical ventilation. Which of the following is a risk factor for the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with altered mental status. The patient has not been feeling well since yesterday, and this morning their roommate found them unarousable. The patient is generally healthy and is a college athlete. They recently broke their nose in a soccer game, and it is currently healing with only gauze in their nose to stop occasional bleeding. They otherwise have no significant medical history. Their temperature is 102°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 87/58 mmHg, pulse is 130/min, respirations are 24/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old African American patient presents to their primary care physician for a wellness checkup. They state that they have lost 20 pounds over the past 2 months yet have experienced an increased appetite during this period. They endorse hyperhidrosis and increased urinary volume and frequency. Physical exam is notable for an anxious patient and a regular and tachycardic pulse. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below. Serum: Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L K+: 4.3 mEq/L HCO3-: 25 mEq/L Ca2+: 12.2 mg/dL The patient's urine calcium level is elevated. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old patient comes to the office complaining of dysphagia that started 4-5 months ago. They report that they initially had difficulty swallowing only solid foods. More recently, they have noticed some trouble swallowing liquids. The patient also complains of fatigue, a chronic cough that worsens at night, and burning chest pain that occurs after they eat. They say that they have used over-the-counter antacids for “years” with mild relief. They deny any change in diet, but say they have “gone down a pant size or 2.” The patient has hypertension and hyperlipidemia. They take amlodipine and atorvastatin. They smoked 1 pack of cigarettes a day for 12 years while in the military but quit 35 years ago. They drink 1-2 beers on the weekend while they are golfing with their friends. Their diet consists mostly of pasta, pizza, and steak. The patient's temperature is 98°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 143/91 mmHg, and pulse is 80/min. Their BMI is 32 kg/m^2. Physical examination reveals an obese patient in no acute distress. No masses or enlarged lymph nodes are appreciated upon palpation of the neck. Cardiopulmonary examination is unremarkable. An endoscopy is performed, which identifies a lower esophageal mass. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 31-year-old patient presents to the general health clinic for a routine checkup. They admit to being in good health and have no medical concerns. They drink alcohol regularly and smoke marijuana occasionally. They have been sexually active for the past 10 years and have had over 25 sexual partners. They use barrier protection most of the time. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 127/88 mmHg, pulse is 80/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam demonstrates multiple skin lesions on the patient's arms and around the anus that resemble the finding in Figure A. Which of the following is the best confirmatory test for the most likely underlying diagnosis in this patient?

A 45-year-old African American patient presents to their primary care physician with a chief concern of constant fatigue. They state that it started a few days ago and has been steadily worsening. The patient has a past medical history of constipation and depression and is currently taking TMP-SMX for a urinary tract infection. They went to the emergency department for an episode of severe and diffuse pain 2 months ago. The patient is a vegan and lives with their partner. Their temperature is 98.3°F (36.8°C), blood pressure is 129/68 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Laboratory values are obtained and shown below. Hemoglobin: 9 g/dL Hematocrit: 30% Leukocyte count: 6,500/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 197,000/mm^3 Serum: Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L K+: 5.3 mEq/L HCO3-: 25 mEq/L BUN: 27 mg/dL LDH: 544 U/L Coombs test: Positive Glucose: 99 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL Ca2+: 9.9 mg/dL AST: 12 U/L ALT: 10 U/L A peripheral smear is ordered as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with chest pain and shortness of breath. The patient states that they feel out of breath and that their heart is racing. They were on a transatlantic flight when their symptoms started. They have a past medical history of obesity, diabetes, and hypertension. Their current medications include lisinopril, atorvastatin, insulin, and metformin. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 197/108 mmHg, pulse is 160/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. An EKG is obtained as seen in Figure A. A CT pulmonary angiogram is demonstrated in Figure B. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for fatigue. This has persisted for the past several months and has been steadily worsening. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension and diabetes; however, they are not currently taking any medications and do not frequently visit their physician. The patient has lost 20 pounds since their last visit. Their laboratory values are shown below: Hemoglobin: 9 g/dL Hematocrit: 29% Mean corpuscular volume: 90 µm^3 Serum: Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L K+: 4.3 mEq/L Ca2+: 11.8 mg/dL Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with a new-onset seizure. The patient was at home watching television when they suddenly began jerking their limbs and not responding according to their partner. The patient works as a gardener and is often dehydrated but drinks large volumes of water to compensate for their work. They do not wear protective gear or sunscreen while working. They have smoked 1.5 packs of cigarettes per day for the past 40 years. They drink liquor before bed every night. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension and diabetes and recently lost 9 pounds. Physical exam is within normal limits. Which of the following is the most likely underlying diagnosis in this patient?

A 67-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with a fever and altered mental status. The patient has a history of Alzheimer dementia and is typically bed bound. Their son found them confused with a warm and flushed complexion, thus prompting their presentation. The patient has a past medical history of dementia, diabetes, and hypertension and typically has a visiting home nurse come to administer medications. Prior to examination, they are given haloperidol and diphenhydramine as they are combative and will not allow the nurses near them. Their temperature is 102.9°F (39.4°C), blood pressure is 104/64 mmHg, pulse is 170/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 100% on room air. Physical exam is notable for dry and flushed skin and a confused patient. There is no skin breakdown, and flexion of the patient’s neck elicits no discomfort. Laboratory studies are drawn as seen below. Hemoglobin: 15 g/dL Hematocrit: 45% Leukocyte count: 4,500/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 227,000/mm^3 Serum: Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L K+: 4.3 mEq/L HCO3-: 24 mEq/L BUN: 30 mg/dL Glucose: 97 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.5 mg/dL Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL AST: 12 U/L ALT: 10 U/L Urine: Color: Yellow Bacteria: Absent Nitrites: Negative Red blood cells: Negative An initial chest radiograph is unremarkable. The patient is given 3 liters of Ringer's lactate and an electric fan to cool off. Two hours later, their temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 154/94 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 100% on room air. The patient’s mental status is at the patient’s baseline according to the son. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient presents to the emergency department complaining of a left-sided headache and right-sided blurry vision. They state that 2 weeks ago they developed dark urine and abdominal pain. They thought it was a urinary tract infection so they took trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole that they had left over. They planned on going to their primary care physician today but then they developed headache and blurry vision so they came to the emergency department. The patient states they are otherwise healthy. Their family history is significant for a brother with sickle cell trait. On physical examination, there is mild abdominal tenderness, and the liver edge is felt 4 cm below the right costal margin. Labs are drawn as below: Hemoglobin: 7.0 g/dL Platelets: 149,000/mm^3 Reticulocyte count: 5.4% Lactate dehydrogenase: 3128 U/L Total bilirubin: 2.1 mg/dL Indirect bilirubin: 1.4 mg/dL Aspartate aminotransferase: 78 U/L Alanine aminotransferase: 64 U/L A peripheral smear shows polychromasia. A Doppler ultrasound of the liver shows decreased flow in the right hepatic vein. Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain is pending. Which of the following tests, if performed, would most likely identify the patient’s diagnosis?

A 32-year-old patient presents to the emergency department due to severe, intractable headaches, and bilateral ocular pain. Their symptoms began approximately 2 weeks prior to presentation and have progressively worsened. They initially had right-sided headaches that were sharp, interfered with sleep, and were unresponsive to pain medications. The headache was around their right eye and cheek, and they noticed diplopia with right lateral gaze. Their symptoms were accompanied by fatigue, fever, and edema around the right eye. Approximately 2 days after these symptoms, they developed swelling around the left eye. Medical history is significant for a recent rhinosinusitis infection. Their temperature is 101°F (38.3°C), blood pressure is 133/72 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, and respirations are 18/min. On physical exam, there is ptosis, proptosis, chemosis, and periorbital swelling of both eyes. There is hyperesthesia in the bilateral ophthalmic and maxillary divisions of the trigeminal nerve. Fundoscopic exam demonstrates bilateral papilledema. There is mydriasis and eye muscle weakness in all directions. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with a fever and fatigue. They state that they have not felt well since they returned from a hiking trip in Alabama. They are generally healthy and have no other medical conditions. Their temperature is 101°F (38.3°C), blood pressure is 127/85 mmHg, pulse is 108/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam including a full dermatologic inspection is unremarkable. Laboratory studies are ordered as seen below. Hemoglobin: 13 g/dL Hematocrit: 39% Leukocyte count: 2,200/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 77,000/mm^3 Serum: Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L K+: 4.3 mEq/L HCO3-: 24 mEq/L BUN: 19 mg/dL Glucose: 98 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.3 mg/dL Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL AST: 92 U/L ALT: 100 U/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old patient presents to their pediatrician’s office for muscle weakness. The patient is accompanied by their parent who states that they have difficulty running and walking up the stairs. The parent has noticed mild weakness when the patient attempts to sit up from a supine position since they were 4-years-old. Medical history is significant for fractures involving the arms and legs secondary to falling. On physical exam, the child does not appear to be in distress and is conversational. They have a waddling gait along with lumbar lordosis and bilateral calf enlargement. The patient uses their hands to push themselves into an upright position when arising from the floor. They have absent patellar and ankle-jerk reflexes. Which of the following is the best next step to confirm the diagnosis?

A 33-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with shoulder pain. They state that they can't remember a specific instance when the injury occurred. They are a weight lifter and compete in martial arts. The patient has no past medical history and is currently taking a multivitamin. Physical exam demonstrates pain with abduction of the patient's right shoulder and with external rotation of the right arm. There is subacromial tenderness with palpation. Their left arm demonstrates 10/10 strength with abduction as compared to 4/10 strength with abduction of the right arm. Which of the following best confirms the underlying diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient presents to the emergency department after a motor vehicle collision. The patient was the front seat unrestrained driver in a head on collision. The patient’s echocardiogram (ECG) is notable only for sinus tachycardia. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 107/58 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. The patient is given 2 liters of Ringer lactate solution and morphine. Initial workup demonstrates that the patient’s pulmonary capillary wedge pressure and troponins are elevated. The patient is currently complaining of chest pain. Physical exam is notable for an uncomfortable patient with bruising over their chest wall. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with dizziness. They state their symptoms started a few days ago and have been gradually worsening. The patient recently had a cold that they recovered from spontaneously. They state that laying down flat may cause dizziness to return and also they endorse a ringing in their ears. Their temperature is 98.7°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 159/92 mmHg, pulse is 88/min, respirations are 12/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is notable for predominantly left-sided hearing loss and horizontal nystagmus. The patient’s initial laboratory tests are unremarkable and an MRI is performed as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician. They were brought in by their daughter as they have refused to see a physician for the past 10 years. The patient has been having worsening abdominal pain. They claim that it was mild initially but has gotten worse over the past week. The patient has been eating lots of vegetables recently to help with their pain. The patient has a past medical history of constipation and a 50 pack-year smoking history. They are not currently taking any medications. On review of systems, the patient endorses trouble defecating and blood that coats their stool. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 197/128 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. On abdominal exam, the patient complains of right upper quadrant tenderness and a palpable liver edge that extends 4 cm beneath the costal margin. The patient states that they feel pain when pressure is applied and then suddenly released to the right upper quadrant. The patient's skin has a yellow hue to it. HEENT exam is notable for poor dentition, normal sclera, and normal extraocular movements. There are no palpable lymph nodes. Laboratory studies are ordered as seen below. Hemoglobin: 9 g/dL Hematocrit: 30% Leukocyte count: 7,500/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 199,000/mm^3 Serum: Na+: 140 mEq/L Cl-: 101 mEq/L K+: 4.0 mEq/L HCO3-: 23 mEq/L BUN: 29 mg/dL Glucose: 197 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.4 mg/dL Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL Total bilirubin: 1.1 mg/dL AST: 150 U/L ALT: 112 U/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient is referred by their primary care provider to a neurologist for leg pain. They report a 6-month history of progressive bilateral lower extremity pain that is worse in their left leg. The pain is 5/10 in severity at its worst and is described as a "burning" pain. They have noticed that the pain is acutely worse when they walk downhill. They have started riding their stationary bike more often as it relieves their pain. Their past medical history is notable for hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and a prior myocardial infarction. They also sustained a distal radius fracture the previous year after falling on their outstretched hand. They take aspirin, atorvastatin, metformin, glyburide, enalapril, and metoprolol. They have a 30-pack-year smoking history and drinks 2-3 glasses of wine with dinner every night. Their temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 145/85 mmHg, pulse is 91/min, and respirations are 18/min. On exam, they are well-appearing and in no acute distress. A straight leg raise is negative. A valsalva maneuver does not worsen their pain. Which of the following is the most appropriate test to confirm this patient's diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to the emergency department after a motor vehicle collision. The patient has a Glasgow coma scale of 7 and is immediately intubated. They have a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes, and acute coronary syndrome. Their temperature is 97.9°F (36.6°C), blood pressure is 174/114 mmHg, and pulse is 50/min. Physical exam is notable for a patient who is currently intubated and sedated. They have multiple bruises and a hematoma over their scalp. An ECG is performed as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old patient is brought by ambulance to the emergency department after a motor vehicle accident. They were the front seat driver in a head-on collision. They are currently unconscious. The patient’s past medical history is only notable for an allergy to amoxicillin as they developed a rash when it was given for a recent upper respiratory infection 1 week ago. Otherwise, they are a college student in good health. The patient is resuscitated. A FAST exam is notable for free fluid in Morrison’s pouch. An initial assessment demonstrates only minor bruises and scrapes on their body. After further resuscitation, the patient becomes responsive and begins vomiting. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 66-year-old patient presents to the emergency department complaining of palpitations. They say that they have been experiencing palpitations and lightheadedness for the past 6 months, but before this morning the episodes usually resolved on their own. The patient’s medical history is significant for a transient ischemia attack 2 months ago, hypertension, and diabetes. They take aspirin, metformin, and lisinopril. They state their grandfather died of a stroke, and their mom has a "blood disorder." An electrocardiogram is obtained that shows an irregularly irregular rhythm with rapid ventricular response, consistent with atrial fibrillation. They are given intravenous metoprolol, which resolves their symptoms. In addition to starting a beta-blocker for long-term management, the patient meets criteria for anticoagulation. Both unfractionated heparin and warfarin are started. Five days later, the patient begins complaining of pain and swelling of their left lower extremity. A Doppler ultrasound reveals thrombosis in their right popliteal and tibial veins. A complete blood count is obtained that shows a decrease in platelet count from 245,000/mm^3 to 90,000/mm^3. Coagulation studies are shown below: Prothrombin time (PT): 15 seconds Partial thromboplastin time (PTT): 37 seconds Bleeding time: 14 minutes Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old patient is brought to the pediatrician by their parent who is concerned about progressive leg weakness. Their parent reports that the patient used to play outside with their neighbors for hours, but for the past few months they have seen the patient sitting on the sidewalk after 15 minutes because they’re too tired. The patient says their legs are “sleepy.” The patient’s parent has also had to remove the carpets from the house because the patient kept tripping over the edges. The parent reports that the patient is shy but cooperates well with their siblings and other children. They can say their first and last name and just started counting. Their parent states they learned to fully walk by 15 months of age. They were hospitalized for bronchiolitis at 12 months of age, which resolved with supportive care. They had an uncomplicated surgery for a congenital condition at 7 months of age. They have no other chronic medical conditions and take no medications. They are up to date on their vaccinations including a flu vaccine 2 weeks ago. The patient’s parent has systemic lupus erythematous and their relative has dermatomyositis. On physical examination, bilateral calves are large in circumference compared to the thighs. Strength is 3/5 in bilateral quadriceps and 4/5 in bilateral calves. Sensation is intact. Achilles tendon reflexes are 1+ bilaterally. The patient can hop on one leg, but gets tired after 10 jumps. They have a slight waddling gait. Which of the following is the most appropriate test to confirm the diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient with a past medical history of diabetes and hypertension presents to the emergency department with chest pain. Their symptoms started yesterday and seem to be worsened by exertion. They are currently not experiencing any pain. An ECG is obtained while the patient is in triage as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for a general checkup. The patient has been feeling poorly for the past several weeks and has been losing weight. They state that they often feel weak and too tired to play with their friends. They are no longer interested in many recreational activities they used to be interested in. The patient's parents state that a few of their child's friends have been sick lately. Their temperature is 102°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 77/48 mmHg, pulse is 110/min, respirations are 24/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. On exam, you note a fatigued appearing child who has lost 10 pounds since their last appointment. Left upper quadrant tenderness and a mass is noted on abdominal exam. Which of the following best describes the most likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old patient comes to the primary care clinic with their parent complaining of right knee pain. They report that the pain started about a month ago, and since then it has gotten progressively worse. The knee pain is not constant but becomes most noticeable when going up or down the stairs. They also endorse that their knee becomes uncomfortable towards the end of class. Their parent is worried because the pain is affecting their ability to play basketball, and they have college scouts coming to watch them play. The patient has no chronic medical conditions. They had a tonsillectomy as a child. They take a multivitamin and use ibuprofen as needed for the pain. On physical examination, there is tenderness at the inferior pole of the patella, without swelling or overlying skin changes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with anxiety and trouble swallowing. They state that their symptoms have slowly been getting worse over the past year, and they now struggle to swallow liquids. They recently recovered from the flu. Review of systems is notable only for recent weight loss. The patient has a 33 pack-year smoking history and is a former alcoholic. Physical exam is notable for poor dental hygiene and foul breath. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 52-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for abdominal pain and diarrhea. The patient states that they have been experiencing watery diarrhea for weeks now. During this same period they state they have been constantly thirsty and do not have the same energy levels that they once had. The patient has a past medical history of anxiety and depression and is currently taking fluoxetine. They were recently treated for a middle ear infection and sinusitis with amoxicillin-clavulanic acid one week ago. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 110/58 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Laboratory values are obtained and shown below. Serum: Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L K+: 2.9 mEq/L HCO3-: 27 mEq/L BUN: 25 mg/dL Glucose: 99 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.4 mg/dL Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL AST: 12 U/L ALT: 10 U/L Which of the following is associated with the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old patient with history of asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease presents to the emergency department with resting dyspnea for the past 2 hours after watching their granddaughter play soccer. Despite albuterol, ipratropium, magnesium, methylprednisolone, and high flow nasal cannula, the patient agrees to elective intubation and is transferred to the intensive care unit. Their hospital course is prolonged by pneumonia, which is managed with vancomycin, pipercillin-tazobactam, and gentamicin to cover for ventilator-associated etiologies. They are maintained on nasogastric tube feeds, lactated ringer fluid boluses, and subcutaneous heparin for deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis. On hospital day 7, the patient proves difficult to wean from their ventilator due to labored tachypnea. As the nurse rotates the patient to change their sacral pressure ulcer dressing, the patient's peak airway pressure increases sharply to 55 cm H2O. The nurse noted that the patient was wincing at the time. Their temperature is 100.1°F (38.1°C), blood pressure is 100/50 mmHg, and pulse is 100/min. Their respirations are 22/min on the ventilator despite a set respiratory rate of 14/min. Their laboratory results are shown below: Leukocyte count and differential: Leukocyte count: 18,000/mm^3 Segmented neutrophils: 90% Bands: 10% Eosinophils: 5% Basophils: 2% Lymphocytes: 2% Monocytes: 1% Serum: Na+: 135 mEq/L Cl-: 107 mEq/L K+: 3.2 mEq/L HCO3-: 18 mEq/L Urea nitrogen: 45 mg/dL Glucose: 89 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.3 mg/dL Alkaline phosphatase: 100 U/L Aspartate aminotransferase (AST, GOT): 250 U/L Alanine aminotransferase (ALT, GPT): 300 U/L Gamma-Glutamyltransferase (GGT): 2 U/L Amylase: 10 IU/dL Lipase: 5 IU/dL Bedside

A 33-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department when they experienced sudden chest pain. The patient was visiting their partner on the oncology floor when they suddenly felt chest pain and became short of breath. The patient has a past medical history of asthma. Their temperature is 98.3°F (36.8°C), blood pressure is 129/61 mmHg, pulse is 129/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. An ECG is performed as seen in Figure A, and a chest radiograph is performed as seen in Figure B. An initial set of cardiac troponins is notable for a value of 0.8 ng/mL and a D-dimer is elevated. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with hematemesis. Their son said that the patient had complained of gnawing abdominal pain that worsened before and improved after meals for the past 3 weeks. They frequently travel for work and are often stressed. They drink alcohol socially and do not smoke tobacco or marijuana. They have not had anything to eat or drink for the past 24 hours due to the pain, but coughed up "several cup of" frank red blood before arrival. Their temperature is 98°F (37°C), blood pressure is 80/50 mmHg, pulse is 140/min, respirations are 23/min, and oxygen saturation is 96% on room air. Gastric ultrasound reveals high gastric residual volume. The patient is empirically started on 3 units of uncrossmatched O-negative blood transfusion and pantoprazole. The patient's initial laboratory data return in the meantime: Hemoglobin: 5 g/dL Hematocrit: 18 % Leukocyte count: 8,000/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 400,000/mm^3 Serum: Na+: 140 mEq/L Cl-: 115 mEq/L K+: 3.2 mEq/L HCO3-: 26 mEq/L BUN: 60 mg/dL Glucose: 104 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL Blood type: AB Rhesus status: negative After bedside esophageogastroduodenoscopy with stapling of several peptic ulcers, repeat labs are obtained in 2 hours. The patient now complains of feeling hot with intermittent shivering. They deny any other symptoms. Their temperature is 101°F (38.3°C), blood pressure is 100/55 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 20/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Their lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally, and no accessory respiratory muscle use is observed. No rash is seen. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient presents to their family doctor complaining of chronic cough with occasional chest pain. They state that when they exert themselves or cough, they experience pain in the right side of the chest with difficulty breathing. They state that they lost 20 pounds over the last 3 months. They have been a single landlord earning passive income since they divorced 30 years ago. They have never smoked and drinks alcohol socially. They deny any marijuana, cocaine, or heroin use. They have not traveled anywhere in years, preferring the comfort of their home. On exam, the patient is an emaciated individual with an unremarkable cardiac exam. Auscultation of the lungs reveals decreased breath sounds and dullness to percussion over the right upper lobe. Chest radiograph is shown in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient presents to the emergency department for pain in multiple joints. They state that they have had symmetric joint pain that started yesterday and has been worsening. It is affecting their wrists, elbows, and shoulders. They also endorse a subjective fever and some fatigue but deny any other symptoms. The patient works as a schoolteacher and is generally healthy. They are currently sexually active with 2 partners and use condoms occasionally. Their temperature is 100°F (37.8°C), blood pressure is 122/85 mmHg, pulse is 88/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Their laboratory values are within normal limits. Physical exam is notable for joint stiffness and pain in particular of the metacarpophalangeal (MCP), proximal interphalangeal (PIP), and the wrist. The patient is discharged with ibuprofen. Four weeks later, the patient follows up at their primary doctor and notes that their symptoms have improved and they are no longer taking any medications for symptom control. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 59-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for fatigue. In general, they have been in good health; however, they recently have experienced some weight loss, abdominal pain, and general fatigue. They have a past medical history of anxiety, diabetes, a fracture of their foot sustained when they tripped, and a recent cold that caused them to miss work for a week. Their current medications include metformin, insulin, buspirone, vitamin D, calcium, and sodium docusate. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 150/100 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam reveals a calm patient. A mild systolic murmur is heard in the left upper sternal region. The rest of the physical exam is within normal limits. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below. Hemoglobin: 12 g/dL Hematocrit: 36% Leukocyte count: 66,500/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 177,000/mm^3 Leukocyte alkaline phosphatase: elevated Serum: Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L K+: 4.3 mEq/L BUN: 20 mg/dL Glucose: 120 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL Ca2+: 10.9 mEq/L AST: 12 U/L ALT: 10 U/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old Japanese patient presents to their primary care doctor with complaints of headache and palpitations. They are a business analyst who was recently promoted to a senior role at their company. They have noticed that they feel more anxious at work and at home with their kids. They have been trying to eat to keep their strength up, but think that tea and soup are easier to digest given their anxiety. They said that years ago they had their tonsil size reduced by radiation because "that's what the doctor recommended." On physical exam, there is a palpable, non-tender swelling in the front of their neck that moves with swallowing. There is no cervical lymphadenopathy. An ultrasound of the thyroid reveals a large, hypoechoic nodule shown in Figure A. The doctor refers the patient to a specialist for a fine-needle aspiration biopsy. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with an enlarged mass on their elbow they noticed this morning. They state that they have never seen it before. The patient has a past medical history of diabetes and a 35 pack-year smoking history. They recently started boxing to get into shape. Their vitals are within normal limits. Physical exam is notable for a mass seen in Figure A, which is rubbery and non-tender. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old patient presents to their primary care provider with a complaint of fever, cough, and fatigue for the past 7 days. The patient reports that their symptoms are interfering with their responsibilities as a graduate student. Review of systems is positive for decreased appetite and myalgia but negative for sore throat, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or constipation. They have been in a relationship with their current partner for the past 2 months. Temperature is 100.8°F (38.2°C), blood pressure is 123/84 mmHg, pulse is 96/min, and respirations are 18/min. Inspection of the throat shows no erythema or petechiae. No cervical lymphadenopathy is appreciated. Laboratory results yield the following: Serum: Hemoglobin: 14 g/dL Hematocrit: 47% Leukocyte count: 18,000/mm^3 with 65% lymphocytes Platelet count: 342,000/mm^3 Alkaline phosphatase: 65 U/L Total bilirubin: 0.9 mg/dL Direct bilirubin: 0.11 mg/dL AST: 140 U/L ALT: 132 U/L Heterophile antibodies: Negative A peripheral smear of the patient’s blood is obtained and can be seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient is seen in the hospital for new onset shortness of breath. The patient was hospitalized 5 days ago after initially presenting with chest pain. They were found to have an ST-elevation myocardial infarction. They underwent percutaneous coronary intervention with stent placement with resolution of their chest pain. They state that they were doing well until yesterday when they developed dyspnea while walking around the hall and occasionally when getting out of bed to use the bathroom. Their shortness of breath has since progressed, and they are now having trouble breathing even at rest. Their medical history is also significant for type II diabetes mellitus and hypercholesterolemia. They take aspirin, clopidogrel, metformin, and atorvastatin. Their temperature is 97°F (36.1°C), blood pressure is 133/62, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 20/min, and oxygen saturation is 88% on room air. On physical examination, there is a holosystolic murmur that radiates to the axilla and an S3 heart sound. Coarse crackles are heard bilaterally. An electrocardiogram, a chest radiograph, and cardiac enzyme levels are pending. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with weakness of their legs which has progressed to an inability for them to stand. The patient works as a school teacher in Alaska and regularly goes hiking and camping. They recently returned from a camping trip where they hiked through tall brush and drank from mountain streams. The patient was also involved in a motor vehicle accident 2 days ago but did not seek treatment. The patient has a medical history that is unremarkable and is currently taking multivitamins and other than a recent bout of diarrhea is generally healthy. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 120/68 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a very anxious patient with 1/5 strength of the patient’s lower extremities and 2/5 strength of their trunk muscles with diminished sensation. Laboratory studies are ordered as seen below. Hemoglobin: 15 g/dL Hematocrit: 43% Leukocyte count: 6,500/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 194,000/mm^3 Serum: Na+: 138 mEq/L Cl-: 102 mEq/L K+: 4.4 mEq/L HCO3-: 24 mEq/L BUN: 20 mg/dL Glucose: 120 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL pH: 7.44 PaCO2: 10 mmHg PaO2: 90 mmHg AST: 12 U/L ALT: 10 U/L The patient complains about difficulty breathing. Repeat laboratory values are notable for the findings below. pH: 7.35 PaCO2: 30 mmHg PaO2: 80 mmHg The patient is intubated and sent to the MICU. Which of the following risk factors is associated with the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old patient is brought into the emergency room for complaints of acute onset chest pain and shortness of breath. They have a history of mental retardation and live at home with their adoptive parents. Their parents inform you that they have not seen a doctor since they were adopted as a child and that they currently take no medications. The patient’s temperature is 99.1°F (37.3°C), pulse is 108/min, blood pressure is 125/70 mmHg, respirations are 25/min, and oxygen saturation is 92% on 2L nasal canula. Physical exam is notable for a tall, thin individual with high-arched feet and mild pectus excavatum. There is mild asymmetry in the lower extremities with discomfort to dorsiflexion of the larger leg. Lung auscultation reveals no abnormalities. What is the next step in the diagnosis of this patient’s underlying disorder?

A 69-year-old patient with no significant past medical history presents to their primary care doctor for a travel evaluation. They plan to tour countries in the Middle East and Southeast Asia as part of their post-retirement celebration and request recommendations on necessary immunizations. They deny any history of venous thromboembolism, previous surgeries, or dependence on any medications. They regularly row, run outside, and regularly participate in competitions to stay in shape. Their temperature is 97°F (36.1°C), blood pressure is 116/78 mmHg, pulse is 60/min, and respirations are 15/min. Auscultation of their lungs and heart are unremarkable for any unusual rales or murmurs, respectively. Their musculoskeletal exam is grossly equal and symmetric bilaterally with no evidence of ataxia on gait assessment. Their skin exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with back pain. They state that it started yesterday and has been gradually getting worse. They state that the pain is worsened with moving and lifting and is relieved with rest and ibuprofen. They have a past medical history of smoking and IV drug abuse and state they last used IV drugs 2 days ago. They think their symptoms may be related to lifting a heavy box. Their temperature is 99.3°F (37.4°C), blood pressure is 122/88 mmHg, pulse is 77/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is notable for focal back pain lateral to the patient’s spine on the left. There is no midline tenderness and the rest of the patient’s exam is unremarkable. There are scars in the antecubital fossae bilaterally. Laboratory values including a C-reactive protein are unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with a sore throat. They say their symptoms have persisted for the past several days and have become so severe that they can no longer eat food. The patient has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. They are a freshman in college and recently joined a fraternity. The patient drinks 4 to 5 drinks every day of the week and smokes marijuana. Their temperature is 100°F (37.8°C), blood pressure is 117/68 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. Bilateral symmetrical posterior cervical lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly are also noted. Which of the following is the best next step in management for the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient is brought into the emergency department by ambulance. The patient was at an appointment to receive welfare when they began acting abnormally. The patient was denied welfare. Shortly afterwards, they no longer responded to questions and stared blankly off into space, not responding to verbal stimuli. Other than odd lip-smacking behavior, they were motionless. Several minutes later, they became responsive but seemed confused. The patient has a past medical history of drug abuse and homelessness and is not currently taking any medications. Their temperature is 98.9°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 124/78 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam reveals cranial nerves II-XII as grossly intact with 5/5 strength in the upper and lower extremities and a stable gait. The patient seems confused when answering questions and has trouble remembering the episode. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by police. The patient was found intoxicated at a local bar. The patient is combative and smells of alcohol. The patient has a past medical history of alcoholism, IV drug use, and schizophrenia. Their current medications include IM haloperidol and ibuprofen. The patient is currently homeless and has presented to the emergency department similarly multiple times. Their temperature is 97.0°F (36.1°C), blood pressure is 130/87 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 96% on room air. Physical exam is deferred due to patient non-compliance. Laboratory values reveal an acute kidney injury and a normal PT/PTT. The patient is started on IV fluids and ketorolac to control symptoms of a headache. The patient begins to vomit into a basin. The nursing staff calls for help when the patient’s vomit appears grossly bloody. Which of the following best describes the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with a rash. The patient’s parents state that they have been more ill lately. They report that they recently developed a rash on their head that now seems to be spreading to the rest of their body. Their symptoms started 3 days ago and have considerably worsened since then. The patient is otherwise healthy. They have not seen a pediatrician nor have they attended general checkup or milestone appointments. The patient’s parents have tried giving them homeopathic remedies including tuber oil to help them feel better with little success. Otherwise, the parents regularly take their child hiking and swimming in outdoor streams. Their temperature is 102°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 106/68 mmHg, pulse is 167/min, respirations are 25/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. The child appears very ill and confused. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old patient presents to the emergency department after a motor vehicle collision. They were the front seat unrestrained driver in a head-on collision at 25 miles per hour. Their temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 129/66 mmHg, pulse is 127/min, respirations are 16/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. The primary and secondary survey are performed and are only notable for bruising along their chest wall bilaterally. An initial pelvic radiograph, an electrocardiogram (ECG) are performed and are unremarkable. A chest radiograph is performed and is notable for a sternal fracture and several rib fractures. The patient is given morphine and their heart rate subsequently improves to 80/min. The patient is observed in the emergency department over the next 6 hours and their laboratory values and a repeat ECG return within normal limits. The patient suddenly complains of shortness of breath. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 127/68 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 28/min, and oxygen saturation is 91% on room air.
