A repeat chest radiograph is performed as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for a wellness checkup. The patient states they have been doing well and currently has no concerns. The patient's daughter states that she feels they are abnormally fatigued and has complained of light-headedness whenever they garden. They also admit that they fainted once. The patient has a past medical history of type II diabetes, hypertension, and constipation. They recently had a "throat cold" that they recovered from with rest and fluids. Their temperature is 98.9°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 167/98 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 12/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam reveals a systolic murmur heard best along the right upper sternal border. An ECG is performed and demonstrates no signs of ST elevation. Cardiac troponins are negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old patient presents to the emergency department after losing consciousness at a jiu jitsu competition. The patient was choked and lost consciousness briefly for roughly 10 seconds before returning to their baseline level of consciousness without any confusion. They are presenting to the emergency department for further evaluation. The patient generally does not see their primary care physician but is otherwise healthy. Their temperature is 99.3°F (37.4°C), blood pressure is 122/88 mmHg, pulse is 77/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Basic laboratory studies are performed and are unremarkable. An ECG is performed as seen in Figure A. Current cardiac troponins are pending. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old college student presents to the emergency room with persistent vague abdominal pain, vomiting, and nausea. Notably, they also report getting full with meals sooner than usual. They have recently been pledging at a fraternity and have participated in binge drinking, marijuana use, cocaine use, and intramural sports. They admit to sharing drinks and paraphernalia with other fraternity members and states that several of them have been ill recently. The patient has a past medical history of asthma and depression. They admit to using large amounts of ibuprofen recently to control pain secondary to minor orthopedic injuries from intramural sports. Physical exam demonstrates mild tachycardia and epigastric tenderness. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 127/68 mmHg, pulse is 105/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. A CT scan is performed and shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient is brought by ambulance to the emergency department after being hit by a car while walking on the sidewalk. They are conscious and deny any pain, bleeding, or memory loss. The patient states that they are a veterinarian for farm animals, primarily horses. Their temperature is 98.7°F (37°C), blood pressure is 120/70 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, and respirations are 15/min. Physical exam reveals a small bruise over their right elbow and right upper quadrant as well as some scrapes on their right lateral thigh. Radiography of their right arm, hip, and knee are unremarkable. Abdominal ultrasound reveals no free fluid, but demonstrates a 6 x 4 cm cystic mass in the right hepatic lobe seen in Figure A. Computed tomography confirmed the cystic mass size and location. Their complete blood count is shown below: Leukocyte count and differential: Leukocyte count: 13,000 /mm^3 Segmented neutrophils: 60% Bands: 0 % Eosinophils: 10% Basophils: 6% Lymphocytes: 18% Monocytes: 6% Hemoglobin: 14 g/dL Platelet count: 160,000 /mm^3 What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for a new patient visit. The patient reports chronic fatigue but states that they otherwise feel well. Their past medical history is not known, and they are not currently taking any medications. The patient admits to drinking 7 alcoholic beverages per day and smoking 1 pack of cigarettes per day. Their temperature is 99.4°F (37.4°C), blood pressure is 157/98 mmHg, pulse is 99/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 100% on room air. Physical exam demonstrates mild pallor but is otherwise not remarkable. Laboratory studies are ordered as seen below. Hemoglobin: 9 g/dL Hematocrit: 33% Leukocyte count: 6,500/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 190,000/mm^3 Mean corpuscular volume (MCV): 60 femtoliters Free iron: 272 mcg/dL Total iron binding capacity (TIBC): 175 mcg/dL Ferritin: 526 ng/mL Reticulocyte count: 2.8% Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for a change in their behavior over the past few months. Initially, the patient was noted to be behaving inappropriately including using foul language and grabbing people unexpectedly. This has progressed to a worsening of their memory and trouble caring for themselves. Their temperature is 98.1°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 162/103 mmHg, pulse is 83/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a patient who laughs inappropriately at times and who is a poor historian. When they are engaged in conversation, they exhibit word finding difficulty and are rather inattentive. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old patient is accompanied by their spouse to the primary care clinic for hand tremors. They state that they first noticed the tremor of their left hand 1 year ago. Since then, the tremor has been worsening and now they can hardly relax when trying to read. Their spouse says that they are also worried about their memory. They had to take over the finances several weeks ago after learning that the patient had forgotten to pay the bills for the past few months. The patient’s medical history is significant for hypertension. They take aspirin and amlodipine. Their mother had schizophrenia. The patient drinks 1-2 beers a night and is a former cigar smoker. On physical examination, they speak softly and have reduced facial expressions. They have a resting tremor that is worse on the left, and they resist manipulation of their bilateral upper extremities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with increased fatigue. They state that they have been feeling very tired lately but today lost consciousness while walking up the stairs. They report mild abdominal distension/discomfort, weight loss, a persistent cough, and multiple episodes of waking up drenched in sweat in the middle of the night. The patient does not see a primary care physician but admits to smoking 2 to 3 packs of cigarettes per day and drinking 1 to 3 alcoholic beverages per day. They recently traveled to Taiwan and Nicaragua. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 177/98 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. On physical exam, you note a fatigued appearing elderly patient who is well-groomed. Cardiopulmonary exam reveals mild expiratory wheezes. Abdominal exam is notable for a non-pulsatile mass in the left upper quadrant. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below. Hemoglobin: 12 g/dL Hematocrit: 36% Leukocyte count: 105,500/mm^3 Platelet count: 197,000/mm^3 Serum: Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L K+: 4.3 mEq/L HCO3-: 25 mEq/L BUN: 20 mg/dL Glucose: 92 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.4 mg/dL Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL Leukocyte alkaline phosphatase score: 25 (range 20 - 100) AST: 12 U/L ALT: 17 U/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 78-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for persistent back pain. The patient states that they have had back pain for awhile; however, this past weekend they were helping their child move heavy furniture. Since the move, their symptoms have been more severe. The patient states that the pain is constant and occurs throughout the day. On review of systems, the patient endorses a recent 15 pound weight loss and constipation. Their temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 137/79 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Cardiovascular exam is notable for a murmur at the right sternal border that radiates to the carotids. Pulmonary exam reveals mild bibasilar crackles. Musculoskeletal exam is notable for mild midline tenderness of the lower thoracic spine and the upper segment of the lumbar spine. No bruising or signs of external trauma are observable on the back. Symptoms are not exacerbated when the patient is lying down and their straight leg is lifted. Strength is 5/5 in the lower and upper extremities. The patient's sensation is intact bilaterally in their lower and upper extremities. Laboratory values are ordered and return as seen below. Hemoglobin: 11 g/dL Hematocrit: 34% Leukocyte count: 10,500/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 288,000/mm^3 Serum: Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L K+: 4.3 mEq/L HCO3-: 25 mEq/L BUN: 20 mg/dL Glucose: 99 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.6 mg/dL Ca2+: 11.8 mg/dL AST: 12 U/L ALT: 12 U/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 59-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with sudden onset abdominal pain that started this morning. The patient has a past medical history of alcoholism, obesity, and peptic ulcer disease and their current medications include ibuprofen, acetaminophen, and naproxen. Their temperature is 98°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 117/58 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 16/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is notable for diffuse abdominal tenderness with a positive Murphy sign and epigastric tenderness. The patient is currently vomiting and smells of alcohol. A radiograph is obtained as seen in Figure A and laboratory values are pending. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old patient presents from home hospice with a change in their mental status. They have seemed more confused lately and are unable to verbalize their symptoms. Their temperature is 102°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 117/65 mmHg, pulse is 110/min, respirations are 19/min, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a right upper quadrant mass that elicits discomfort when palpated. Ultrasound is notable for pericholecystic fluid and gallbladder wall thickening without any gallstones. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with a sensation of fluttering in their chest. They have had these symptoms intermittently in the past, but states that this time their symptoms have been persistent. They are currently studying for exams and have been drinking roughly 10 cups of coffee per day. Their temperature is 98°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 115/60 mmHg, pulse is 124/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is only notable for tachycardia. An electrocardiogram (ECG) is obtained as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with confusion starting this morning. Their partner states that they initially complained of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and fatigue after eating. They have vomited 3 times and progressively became more confused. Their past medical history is notable for morbid obesity, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, a sleeve gastrectomy 1 month ago, and depression with multiple suicide attempts. Their temperature is 98.0°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 104/54 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Their physical exam is notable for generalized confusion. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below. Serum: Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L K+: 3.9 mEq/L HCO3-: 24 mEq/L BUN: 22 mg/dL Glucose: 41 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL C-peptide level: normal Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old patient presents to the emergency department for chest pain. They were working in their yard when their symptoms started. They initially felt a "pull" in their chest. This was followed by them feeling light headed. The patient has no past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. Their temperature is 98.4°F (36.9°C), blood pressure is 137/77 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. An ECG is performed as seen in Figure A. Initial laboratory values and troponins are pending. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 24-year-old patient presents to the emergency department after a motor vehicle accident. They were the unrestrained driver in a head-on collision. The patient was ejected from the front seat and found by paramedics outside their car. In the trauma bay, the patient is started on IV fluids, blood products, and vasopressors. A FAST exam and chest radiograph are performed (Figure A), and multiple lacerations are repaired. After the initial resuscitation, their temperature is 98.4°F (36.9°C), blood pressure is 107/58 mmHg, pulse is 122/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. The patient is conscious and complains of severe left shoulder pain and shortness of breath. They also vomit several times. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old patient with a history of diabetes mellitus, COPD, and a ST-elevation myocardial infarction currently on dialysis presents with shortness of breath for the past 2 hours. The patient missed their recent dialysis appointment and has been noncompliant with their other medications. The patient found out their best friend died this morning and has felt worse since this event. Their temperature is 98.7°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 87/48 mmHg, pulse is 130/min, respirations are 27/min, and oxygen saturation is 92% on room air. A bedside ultrasound demonstrates an anechoic rim surrounding the heart with poor cardiac squeeze, global hypokinesis, and right ventricular collapse with pleural sliding. Laboratory values are notable for 2 cardiac troponins that measure 0.72 ng/mL and 0.71 ng/mL. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old patient presents to the emergency department after an episode of syncope. They state that they were at home when they suddenly felt weak and experienced back pain that has been persistent. They state that they vomited forcefully several times after the episode. The patient has a past medical history of diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, and depression. They smoke 1.5 packs of cigarettes per day and drink 10 alcoholic beverages each night. Their temperature is 97.5°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 107/48 mmHg, pulse is 130/min, respirations are 19/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. A chest radiograph is within normal limits. Physical exam is notable for abdominal tenderness and the patient resting in an antalgic position. Urinalysis is currently pending but reveals a concentrated urine sample. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient presents to the emergency department after an episode of palpitations followed by syncope. They awoke after being unconscious for several seconds but still has a sensation of palpitations. The patient is not currently followed by a primary care doctor but states that they have never had any health problems. Their temperature is 98.5°F (36.9°C), blood pressure is 133/91 mmHg, pulse is 95/min, respirations are 19/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. An electrocardiogram (ECG) is performed as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with chest pain and shortness of breath. They have a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes, and obesity. Their temperature is 98.6°F (37.0°C), blood pressure is 177/118 mmHg, pulse is 127/min, respirations are 11/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. An electrocardiogram is performed and the patient is started on aspirin and metoprolol. The patient is treated appropriately and transferred to the medical floor. On the second day of their hospitalization, the patient reports having abdominal pain. Their serum lipase is 272 U/L and their creatinine is 1.6 mg/dL. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. They are requesting pain medication for their abdominal pain. Which of the following is the most likely underlying diagnosis?

A 24-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with a longstanding history of diarrhea. They report recurrent, foul-smelling, loose stools and a 35 lb weight loss over the past 3 years. They also state that two months ago, they developed an "itchy, bumpy" rash on their elbows and forearms which has since resolved. They deny recent camping trips or travel outside of the country. On physical exam they appear thin, their conjunctiva and skin appear pale, and their abdomen is mildly distended. Which of the following tests would confirm this patient's diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with a chief concern of abdominal pain and diarrhea. The patient states that for the past 4 days they have experienced abdominal pain, diarrhea, weakness and a subjective fever. They also endorse a weight loss of 11 pounds during this time. The patient has a past medical history of celiac disease, constipation, and depression. Their current medications include fish oil, a multivitamin, sodium docusate, and fluoxetine. Their temperature is 98.5°F (36.9°C), blood pressure is 110/75 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a patient in mild distress. Cardiac and pulmonary exams are within normal limits. Abdominal exam is notable for generalized tenderness and increased bowel sounds. Oral exam is notable for multiple shallow painful ulcers. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below: Hemoglobin: 12 g/dL Hematocrit: 36% Leukocyte count: 8,000 cells/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 227,500/mm^3 Serum: Na+: 141 mEq/L Cl-: 101 mEq/L K+: 4.5 mEq/L HCO3-: 24 mEq/L BUN: 17 mg/dL Glucose: 82 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL Ca2+: 10.1 mg/dL AST: 12 U/L ALT: 11 U/L A stool guaiac test is performed which returns positive. The patient is started on IV fluids and morphine. Which of the following best describes the most likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old patient is brought to the pediatrician by their parent for an initial visit. They recently immigrated from Cambodia. Through an interpreter, the patient reports 6 months of mild exertional dyspnea. They deny chest pain or palpitations. Their medical history is unremarkable and they have never had any surgeries. Their family history is significant for hypertension and diabetes. Their parent died of tuberculosis. The patient’s vaccination history is unknown. Their temperature is 98°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 113/71 mmHg, and pulse is 82/min. Their BMI is 24 kg/m^2. Physical examination shows a well-nourished, cooperative patient without any grossly dysmorphic features. Cardiac auscultation reveals a grade II systolic ejection murmur along the left upper sternal border and a mid-diastolic rumble along the left sternal border. S1 is normal and the splitting of S2 does not change with inspiration. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 74-year-old patient with a past medical history of hypertension, peripheral artery disease, and migraine headaches presents to the emergency department with a two hour history of severe abdominal pain. The patient cannot recall any similar episodes, although they note occasional abdominal discomfort after eating. They describe the pain as sharp periumbilcal pain. They deny recent illness, fever, chills, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Their last normal bowel movement was yesterday evening. Their temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 110/min, blood pressure is 140/80 mmHg, and respirations are 20/min. On exam, the patient is grimacing and appears to be in significant discomfort. Heart and lung exams are within normal limits. The patient’s abdomen is soft and non-distended with diffuse periumbilical pain on palpation. There is no rebound tenderness or guarding, and bowel sounds are present. The rest of the exam is unremarkable. Labs in the emergency room show: Serum: Na+: 144 mEq/L Cl-: 105 mEq/L K+: 3.7 mEq/L HCO3-: 20 mEq/L BUN: 15 mg/dL Glucose: 99 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.2 mg/dL Ca2+: 10.7 mg/dL Phosphorus: 5.2 mg/dL Lactate: 7.0 mmol/L Amylase: 240 U/L Hemoglobin: 13.4 g/dL Hematocrit: 35% Leukocyte count: 12,100 cells/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 405,000/mm^3 What is the next best step in diagnosis?

A 25-year-old patient presents to the emergency department for a fever and abdominal pain. The patient states that their pain has been worsening over the past week in the setting of a fever. They have a past medical history of IV drug abuse and multiple admissions for septic shock. Their temperature is 102°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 94/54 mmHg, pulse is 133/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 100% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a murmur over the left upper sternal border. Abdominal exam reveals left upper quadrant tenderness. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below. Hemoglobin: 15 g/dL Hematocrit: 44% Leukocyte count: 16,700/mm^3 Platelet count: 299,000/mm^3 Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old patient presents to the physician with progressive weight loss for the last 3 months. They also say they frequently sweat profusely at night and have a recurring low-grade fever, for which they take acetaminophen. The patient denies any symptoms like cough, breathlessness, or gastrointestinal symptoms. Their temperature is 37.1ºC (98.8ºF), pulse is 76/min, blood pressure is 116/78 mm Hg, and respiratory rate is 13/min. On physical examination, they have generalized pallor. Bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy is present. Examination of their abdomen reveals non-tender hepatosplenomegaly in the right upper quadrant. Laboratory evaluation confirms the diagnosis of Hodgkin’s lymphoma. Which of the following viral infections is most likely to have played a role in the pathogenesis of this patient’s malignancy?

A 70-year-old patient is at their dermatologist’s office for the treatment of a severely pruritic erythroderma with scaling on their buttocks that has been slowly progressing over the past two weeks. The patient works as a truck driver and has a history of hypertension treated with enalapril. The patient reports having tried an over-the-counter cream on the rash without improvement. The vital signs are within normal range. On physical exam, they have multiple confluent and well-demarcated pink patches on their buttocks and legs with some scaling and enlarged inguinal lymph nodes. The dermatologist orders a skin biopsy that reveals Pautrier microabscesses. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 11-month-old patient presents with a scaly erythematous rash on their back for the past 2 days. No significant past medical history. Family history is significant for the fact that the patient’s parents are first-degree cousins. In addition, their older sibling had similar symptoms and was diagnosed with a rare unknown skin disorder. On physical examination, whitish granulomatous plaques are present in the oral mucosa, which exhibit a tendency to ulcerate, as well as a scaly erythematous rash on their back. A complete blood count reveals that the patient is anemic. A plain radiograph of the skull shows lytic bone lesions. Which of the following immunohistochemical markers, if positive, would confirm the diagnosis in this patient?

A 68-year-old patient presents to the emergency department complaining of difficulty in breathing for the past 2 days. They have had recurrent episodes of bacterial pneumonia in the right lower lobe during the last 6 months. Their last episode of pneumonia started 7 days ago for which they are being treated with antibiotics. They have a 35-pack-year smoking history. Past medical history is significant for hypertension for which they take lisinopril. Physical examination reveals decreased breath sounds and dullness to percussion in the right lung base. Chest X-ray reveals a large right-sided pleural effusion, and chest CT scan shows a large mass near the hilum of the right lung. Cytologic examination of pleural fluid shows evidence of malignancy. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis of this patient?

A 73-year-old patient presents to the office, complaining of “weird blisters” on their right hand, which appeared 2 weeks ago. The patient says that they initially had a rash, which progressed to blisters. They deny any trauma or known contact with sick people. They are worried because they haven’t been able to garden since the rash appeared, and they were planning on entering their roses into an annual competition this month. Their vital signs are stable. On physical exam, the patient has multiple bullae accompanied by red, papular lesions on their right hand, which progress to their forearm. The right axillary lymph nodes are swollen and tender. What is the treatment for the most likely diagnosis of this patient?

A 19-year-old patient with a known history of malabsorption presents with a painful red tongue, red eyes, and cracked lips. They say their symptoms gradually onset 4 months ago after moving away from home for college. They also complain of photophobia, spontaneous lacrimation, and itchy dermatitis. Past medical history is significant for a long-standing malabsorption syndrome, which they say they haven’t been able to maintain their normal diet or take their vitamins regularly due to their busy schedule. The patient is afebrile and vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, they have a malnourished appearance with significant pallor. Conjunctival injection is present bilaterally. Which of the following diagnostic tests will be most helpful to support the diagnosis of the most likely vitamin deficiency in this patient?

A 50-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department due to chest pain and shortness of breath for the last 2 hours. They describe the chest pain as squeezing in nature and radiating towards their left arm. It is associated with nausea and sweating. They have a similar history in the past, which is mostly aggravated with strenuous activities and relieved with sublingual nitroglycerin. They have a history of uncontrolled diabetes and hypercholesterolemia for the last 10 years. Their last HbA1c was 8.0 %. Their blood pressure is 150/90 mm Hg, pulse rate is 90/min, respiratory rate is 20/min, and temperature is 36.8°C (98.3°F). Oxygen saturation in room air is 98%. ECG shows ST-segment elevation in leads I, II, and aVF. They are being prepared for coronary angioplasty. Elevation in which of the following enzymes is most significant in the diagnosis of this patient?

A 5-year-old patient presents with a rash and a persistent fever of 41.0°C (105.8°F), not relieved by Tylenol. The patient’s parent says that their symptoms started 5 days ago and have not improved. The rash started on their trunk and now is present everywhere including the palms and soles. Their birth history is normal. Their pulse is 120/min and respiratory rate is 22/min. On physical examination, the patient is agitated and ill-appearing. There is significant swelling of the distal upper and lower extremities bilaterally. The pharynx is hyperemic (see image). Generalized edema with non-palpable cervical lymphadenopathy is noted. Muscle tone is normal. Remainder of exam is unremarkable. Laboratory findings are significant for the following: Laboratory test Hb 9 g/dL RBC 3.3/mm3 Neutrophilic leukocytosis 28,000/mm3 Normal platelet count 200,000/mm3 Serum ɣ-GT increased Hyperbilirubinemia 2.98 mg/dL AST and ALT are normal, but there is markedly increased serum CRP. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 25-year-old patient presents with abdominal pain and discomfort for the past 3 days. They were diagnosed with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) a couple of years ago, managed until recently with imipramine, psyllium, and loperamide. 5 days ago, because they had developed alternating diarrhea and constipation, bloating, and abdominal pain on their medication, they were started on alosetron. Their current temperature is 39.0°C (102.2°F), the heart rate is 115/min, the blood pressure is 90/60 mm Hg and the respiratory rate is 22/min. Abdominal examination shows diffuse tenderness to palpation with guarding but no rebound. Bowel sounds are hypoactive on auscultation. A fecal occult blood test is positive and laboratory tests show their white cell count to be 15,800/µL. Arterial blood gas (ABG) analysis reveals a metabolic acidosis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 34-year-old patient presents to a clinic with complaints of abdominal discomfort and blood in the urine for 2 days. They have had similar abdominal discomfort during the past 5 years, although they do not remember passing blood in the urine. They have had hypertension for the past 2 years, for which they have been prescribed medication. There is no history of weight loss, skin rashes, joint pain, vomiting, change in bowel habits, and smoking. On physical examination, there are ballotable flank masses bilaterally. The bowel sounds are normal. Renal function tests are as follows: Urea 50 mg/dL Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL Protein Negative RBC Numerous The patient underwent ultrasonography of the abdomen, which revealed enlarged kidneys and multiple anechoic cysts with well-defined walls. A CT scan confirmed the presence of multiple cysts in the kidneys. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 16-year-old patient presents after suffering a tonic-clonic seizure. They say it had a duration of 2 minutes and a postictal period of 10 minutes. Patient denies any similar episodes in the past. Past medical history is unremarkable. Family history is significant for their mother and older sibling who died of colorectal cancer at ages 40 and 20, respectively. On physical examination, the patient is drowsy but arousable and responsive to commands. Both pupils are symmetrical and responsive to light. An MRI of the brain reveals an infratentorial hypointense cerebellar mass with a small cystic area. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 7-year-old patient with a sore throat, fever, and generalized malaise is admitted to the pediatric floor. On physical examination, they have diffuse white exudate on both tonsils, and also a palpable spleen with mild hepatomegaly. Their blood smear shows large and abundant lymphocytes with blue-gray cytoplasm, irregular nuclei, and dark chromatin with inconspicuous nucleoli. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old patient presents to their primary care provider for evaluation of nocturnal cough and dyspnea. They have been a smoker for the past 15 years with a 7.5-pack-year smoking history. They have no significant medical history and take no medications. Their blood pressure is 118/76 mm Hg, the heart rate is 84/min, the respiratory rate is 15/min, and the temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F). A sputum sample shows Charcot-Leyden crystals and Curschmann spirals. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old patient presents to the office with complaints of epigastric discomfort for the past 6 months. They add that the discomfort is not that bothersome as it does not interfere with their daily activities. They do not have any other complaints at the moment. The past medical history is insignificant. They are a non-smoker and do not consume alcohol. They recently came back from a trip to South America where they visited a relative who owned a sheep farm. On physical examination, they have a poorly palpable epigastric non-tender mass with no organomegaly. The hepatitis B and C serology are negative. The liver CT scan and MRI are shown. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old patient presents with a recent history of frequent falls. The images below depict their movements when they try to get up from the floor. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 13-year-old patient has been suspended 5 times this year for arguing with teachers. They have presented a pattern of negativism and hostility that has lasted for about 8 months. When asked about the suspensions, they admit that they lose their temper easily and often blame the principal for not being fair to them. They usually find an argument before finishing their homework. At home, they go out of their way to annoy their siblings. They get furious if their legal guardian finds out about it and confiscates their smartphone. Which of the following is an additional behavior characteristic of this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old patient presents to a surgeon with a painless, slowly growing ulcer in the periauricular region for the last 2 months. On physical examination, there is an irregular-shaped ulcer, 2 cm x 1 cm in its dimensions, with irregular margins and crusting over the surface. The patient is a fair-skinned individual who loves to go sunbathing. There is no family history of malignancy. After a complete physical examination, the surgeon performs a biopsy of the lesion under local anesthesia and sends the tissue for histopathological examination. The pathologist confirms the diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma of the skin. When they ask about the cause, the surgeon explains that there are many possible causes, but it is likely that they have developed squamous cell carcinoma on their face due to repeated exposure to ultraviolet rays from the sun, especially ultraviolet B (UVB) rays. If the surgeon’s opinion is correct, which of the following mechanisms is most likely involved in the pathogenesis of the condition?

A 51-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department because of an aggressive cough with copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum. They say they have had this cough for about 11 years with exacerbations similar to their presentation today. They also report that their cough is worse in the morning. They were evaluated multiple times in the past because of recurrent bouts of bronchitis that have required treatment with antibiotics. They are a non-smoker. On physical examination, the blood pressure is 125/78 mm Hg, pulse rate is 80/min, respiratory rate is 16/min, and temperature is 36.7°C (98.0°F). Chest auscultation reveals crackles and wheezing over the right middle lobe and the rest of their physical examinations are normal. The chest X-ray shows irregular opacities in the right middle lobe and diffuse airway thickening. Based on this history and physical examination, which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old patient presents to a medical office for a consultation regarding a mole on their nose that is increasing in size. They also complain of frequent headaches, which they associate with stress on the job. They work as a civil engineer and spend much of their time outside. Their past medical history is positive for bronchial asthma; nevertheless, their vitals are stable. The mole is 8 mm in diameter, has irregular borders, and is brown in color. A biopsy is performed and sent for genetic analysis. A mutation is found. A mutation in which gene is characteristic of this patient’s main diagnosis?

A 40-year-old patient presents to their family physician with a 3-week history of swollen neck. The small, round, and painless swelling, which was detected 3 weeks ago in the middle of their neck, has now increased in size. The swelling is associated with sweaty palms and soles, insomnia, irritability, nervousness, and fatigue; however, the patient does not complain of fever, cervical lymphadenopathy, weight loss, vision problems, or body swelling. The patient’s medical history is negative for similar symptoms or a thyroid disorder. The vital signs are within normal limits. Local examination reveals a 3 x 3 cm round, non-tender, non-fluctuant, and non-pulsatile swelling in the anterior triangle of their neck. The patient carries a total white blood cell count of 10,200/mm3, including 70% neutrophils, 30% lymphocytes, and zero eosinophils. The erythrocyte sedimentation rate is 20 mm/hr (normal, 0–29 mm/hr). What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old patient presents to the clinic with right-sided chest pain and difficulty breathing for the past 10 days. When it began, the pain was mild, but as time went on, it increased to a level at which they found it difficult to breathe. Two years ago, they were diagnosed with clear cell carcinoma of the kidney. Vital signs include: pulse rate is 72/min, blood pressure is 122/80 mm Hg, respiratory rate is 16/min, and temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F). On physical examination, the trachea appears to have deviated to the left, respiratory movements are diminished, there is decreased resonance on percussion, and there is an absence of breath sounds over the right hemithorax. Which of the following is the most likely clinical diagnosis in this patient?

A 78-year-old patient presents to the hospital because of shortness of breath and chest pain that started a few hours ago. 3 weeks ago they had surgery for a total hip replacement with a prosthesis. The patient was treated with prophylactic doses of low-weight heparin until they were discharged. They did not have a fever, expectoration, or any accompanying symptoms. They have a history of right leg deep vein thrombosis that occurred 5 years ago. Their vital signs include: heart rate 110/min, respiratory rate 22/min, and blood pressure 150/90 mm Hg. There were no significant findings on the physical exam. Chest radiography was within normal limits. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 11-month-old patient with a history of recurrent pneumonia, ear infections, and diarrhea presents to the clinic with another chest cold. They send a blood specimen to flow cytometry for analysis. The result is Bruton’s X-linked Agammaglobulinemia. Which combination of markers was helpful to make this diagnosis?

A 28-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with diffuse abdominal pain and nausea for the past 5 hours. The pain started with a dull ache but is now quite severe. They note that they “just don’t feel like eating” and have not eaten anything for almost a day. Although the nausea is getting worse, the patient has not vomited. They note no medical issues in the past and are not currently taking any medications. They admit to drinking alcohol (at least 2–3 bottles of beer per day after work and frequent binge-drinking weekends with friends). They say that they do not smoke or use illicit drugs. Vital signs include: pulse rate 120/min, respiratory rate 26/min, and blood pressure 100/70 mm Hg. On examination, the patient’s abdomen is diffusely tender. Their breath smells like alcohol, with a fruity tinge to it. Bowel sounds are present. No other findings are noted. Fingerstick glucose is 76mg/dL. After the examination, the patient suddenly and spontaneously vomits. Which of the following is the underlying mechanism of the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 60-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by police officers because they were acting strangely in public. The patient was found talking nonsensically to characters on cereal boxes in the store. Past medical history is significant for multiple hospitalizations for alcohol-related injuries and seizures. The patient’s vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows a disheveled patient who is oriented to person, but not time or place. Neurologic examination shows nystagmus and severe gait ataxia. A T1/T2 MRI is performed and demonstrates evidence of damage to the mammillary bodies. The patient is given the appropriate treatment for recovering most of their cognitive functions. However, significant short-term memory deficits persist. The patient remembers events from their past such as the school and college they attended, their current job, and the names of family members quite well. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 7-year-old patient presents to the clinic with their parent, who notes that the way in which they play has changed and that they have been limping, favoring their left leg. When asked, the patient states that their left knee hurts. They are afebrile and vital signs are stable. The patient is well nourished and meeting all developmental milestones. On physical examination, the knee has a full range of motion; however, passive motion elicits pain in the left hip. An X-ray is performed and reveals a flattened left femoral head. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 51-year-old white patient is not relevant to this case. Parents bring an 11-month-old baby to the clinic because the baby has a fever of 39.0°C (102.2°F). The baby is irritated and crying constantly. They are up to date on immunizations. A complete physical examination reveals no significant findings, and all laboratory tests are negative. Five days after resolution of their fever, they develop a transient maculopapular rash. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old patient presents to the office complaining of bloating and consistent fatigue. Past medical notes on their record show that they have seen several doctors at the clinic in the past year for the same concerns. During the discussion, they admit that coming to the doctor intensifies their anxiety and they do not enjoy it. However, they came because they fear that they have colon cancer and say, “There’s gotta be something wrong with me, I can feel it.” Past medical history is significant for obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). They see a therapist a few times a month. Their grandfather died of colon cancer at 75. Today, their blood pressure is 120/80 mm Hg, heart rate is 90/min, respiratory rate is 18/min, and temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F). Physical examination reveals a well-nourished, well-developed patient who appears anxious and tired. Their heart has a regular rhythm and their lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Their abdomen is soft, non-tender, and non-distended. No masses are palpated, and a digital rectal examination is unremarkable. Laboratory results are as follows: Serum chemistry Hemoglobin 13 g/dL Hematocrit 38% MCV 90 fl TSH 4.1 μU/mL Fecal occult blood test negative Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old patient with Down syndrome presents with their parent. The patient's parent says that they aren’t playing or eating as much as they used to and seems lethargic. Expected developmental delays are present and stable. Physical examination reveals dry mucous membranes and abdominal distention with no tenderness to palpation. An abdominal radiograph is shown in the image below. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 52-year-old Caucasian patient presents to the clinic for evaluation of a mole on their back that they find concerning. They state that their partner noticed the lesion and believes that it has been getting larger. On inspection, the lesion is 10 mm in diameter with irregular borders. A biopsy is performed. Pathology reveals abnormal melanocytes forming nests at the dermo-epidermal junction and discohesive cell growth into the epidermis. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old school teacher visits their doctor because of disfiguring skin lesions that started to appear in the past few days. The lesions are mostly located on their chest, shoulders, and back. They are 2–5 mm in diameter, droplike, erythematous papules with fine silver scales. Besides a sore throat and laryngitis requiring amoxicillin several weeks ago, they have no significant medical history. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 9-year-old patient is brought to a physician by their parent for evaluation of generalized weakness, increased urination, and increased thirst. The parent mentions that their child is always tired, and seems to be getting worse. They prefer watching television rather than going out and playing with other kids. Furthermore, they have had frequent episodes of constipation since birth. Except for frequent cravings for salty foods, the patient eats a regular diet. The patient was delivered healthy and is fully immunized. The medical history is unremarkable, and they take no medications. They have no siblings. Their parents are professionals. The pulse is 90/min, the blood pressure is 110/75 mm Hg, and the respiratory rate is 15/min. They are in the bottom 10th percentile for height and weight according to their age. The remainder of the physical examination is unremarkable. They recently had a urinalysis that showed elevated urinary calcium excretion. Additional lab testing results are as follows: Serum electrolytes Sodium 135 mEq/L Potassium 3.2 mEq/L Chloride 95 mEq/L Plasma renin activity 10 ng/mL/hr (normal, 0.5–3.3 ng/mL/hr) Plasma aldosterone concentration 20 ng/dL (normal, 2–9 ng/dL) What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient presents to the office with shortness of breath on exertion and a dry cough that they have had for about a year. They are a heavy smoker with a 25-pack-years history. Their vitals include: heart rate 95/min, respiratory rate 26/min, and blood pressure 110/75 mm Hg. On examination, they present with nail clubbing and bilateral and persistent crackling rales. The chest radiograph shows basal reticulonodular symmetric images, with decreased lung fields. The pulmonary function tests show the following: diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide (DLCO) is 43% and reference SaO2 is 94% and 72%, at rest and with exercise, respectively. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old patient presents with pruritus and progressive weakness for the past 3 months. They say they feel excessively tired during the daytime and are losing interest in activities that used to be fun. The patient reports a history of heavy alcohol use and drinks around 20 ounces per week. Laboratory studies show: Proteins 6.5 g/dL Albumin 4.5 g/dL Globulin 1.9 g/dL Bilirubin 5.8 mg/dL Serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 86 U/L Serum aspartate transaminase (AST) 84 U/L Serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP) 224 U/L Antinuclear antibody (ANA) positive Antimitochondrial antibody (AMA) positive anti-HBs positive anti-HBc negative Which is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 35-year-old African American patient presents with fever, abdominal pain, and severe weakness since yesterday. On physical examination, the patient is jaundiced and shows a generalized pallor. Past medical history is significant for recently receiving anti-malaria prophylaxis before visiting Nigeria. Laboratory tests show normal glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) levels. Peripheral smear shows the presence of bite cells and Heinz bodies. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 38-year-old patient presents with pruritus and jaundice. Past medical history is significant for ulcerative colitis diagnosed 2 years ago, well managed medically. They are vaccinated against hepatitis A and B and deny any recent travel abroad. On physical examination, prominent hepatosplenomegaly is noted. Which of the following would confirm the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 21-year-old patient is brought to the office by their parents due to concerns about their behavior. They describe their child as aloof and a loner who earns average to below average grades in school. Today, their heart rate is 90/min, respiratory rate is 17/min, blood pressure is 110/65 mm Hg, and temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F). On physical examination, they appear gaunt and anxious. Their heart has a regular rhythm, and their lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. CMP, CBC, and TSH are normal. A urine toxicology test is negative. During the examination, they avoid eye contact and appear detached. When asked about their social life, they claim that they do not care about making friends and prefer to be alone. They say they enjoy going to the movies, but they enjoy doing this alone. They have not had a romantic partner before and take little pleasure in intimacy. They deny experiencing hallucinations or delusions. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 10-month-old infant is brought in by their parents because they are vomiting and not passing stool. Their parents say they have vomited multiple times over the past couple of hours, but the most recent vomit was green. The patient has no significant past medical history. On physical examination, the patient is irritable and crying. On palpation in the periumbilical region, an abdominal mass is present. Emergency laparotomy is performed, which shows a part of the patient’s intestine folded into the section adjacent to it. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 55-year-old patient presents with severe fatigue and fever. Their past medical history is significant for a recent history of mononucleosis from which they fully recovered 8 weeks ago. On physical examination, the patient seems pale. A chest radiograph shows multiple enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes. A biopsy of one of the enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes is performed and shows the presence of multinucleated cells with an ‘owl-eye’ appearance in a hypocellular background. This patient’s most likely condition is very aggressive and associated with a very poor prognosis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 32-year-old patient presents to their family physician with a long history of depression, irritability, and, more recently, personality changes. As their partner comments, they have stopped engaging in activities they used to enjoy like dancing, drumming lessons, and yoga. The patient denies changes in skin pigmentation and assures they keep a balanced diet low in fat and carbohydrates. During the physical examination, jaundice and dark rings encircling the iris of the eye are noted, as well as hepatomegaly and gait disturbances. For a follow-up visit, the patient brings a battery of laboratory tests that includes a complete blood count showing normocytic normochromic anemia, a negative Coombs, normal iron levels, normal fasting glucose levels, elevated aminotransferases from the liver biochemical tests, bilirubin, and decreased serum ceruloplasmin levels. Antinuclear antibodies are negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient presents to an urgent care clinic because they coughed up blood this morning. Although they had a persistent cough for the past 3 weeks, they had never coughed up blood until now. Their voice is hoarse and they admit that it has been like that for the past few months. Both their past medical history and family history are insignificant. They have smoked a pack of cigarettes a day since the age of 20 and drink wine every night before bed. Their vitals are: heart rate of 78/min, respiratory rate of 14/min, temperature of 36.5°C (97.8°F), blood pressure of 140/88 mm Hg. An indirect laryngoscopy reveals a rough vegetating lesion on the free border of the right vocal cord. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old patient who works as a resident in general surgery presents feeling "burned out" for the last 2 months. They say they have been working extremely long hours under stressful conditions, which makes them irritable, edgy, unfocused, and forgetful. They say they also have severe anxiety about how these symptoms are affecting their performance at work, making it difficult for them to sleep even when they have time off. The patient is referred for counseling and is prescribed some mild sleep aids. At follow-up a few months later, they say they are feeling much improved due to improved staffing at the hospital and a more manageable workload. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 32-year-old patient comes to the emergency room because of severe breathlessness for the past few hours. Over the course of a few years, they have been treated for asthma by several physicians, but their symptoms have continued to progress. They don’t smoke and never did. Both their father, who died at the age of 40 years, and their uncle (father’s brother), died with chronic obstructive pulmonary disorder. They have never smoked in their life. Their respiratory rate is 19/min and temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F). On physical examination, the patient has significantly longer exhalation than inhalation. Their expiratory time is longer than 6 seconds. Clubbing is present. Chest auscultation reveals bilateral crackles. Mild hepatomegaly is present. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient who recently emigrated as a refugee from Somalia presents with fever, weight loss, fatigue, and exertional chest pain. They say their symptoms began 3 weeks ago and that their appetite has decreased and they have lost 3 kg (6.6 lb) in the last 3 weeks. They deny any history of cardiac disease. Their past medical history is unremarkable. The patient admits that they have always lived in poor hygienic conditions in overcrowded quarters and in close contact with cats. Their vital signs include: blood pressure 120/60 mm Hg, pulse 90/min, and temperature 38.0°C (100.4°F). Physical examination reveals generalized pallor. A cardiac examination reveals an early diastolic murmur loudest at the left third intercostal space. Abdominal examination reveals a tender and mildly enlarged spleen. Prominent axillary lymphadenopathy is noted. Laboratory investigations reveal a WBC count of 14,500/μL with 5% bands and 93% polymorphonuclear cells. An echocardiogram reveals a 5-mm vegetation on the aortic valve with moderate regurgitation. Three sets of blood cultures are taken over 24 hours followed by empiric antibiotic therapy with gentamicin and vancomycin. The blood cultures show no growth after 5 days. Following a week of empiric therapy, the patient continues to deteriorate. Which of the following would most likely confirm the diagnosis in this patient?

A 76-year-old patient presents to their physician with their daughter for evaluation of memory loss and disorientation that has become progressively worse over the last few years. The patient's daughter states that the memory loss started with her parent forgetting things ''here and there'' and the memory loss has progressed to the patient forgetting the names of loved ones and getting lost in familiar places. The medical history is non-contributory. On examination, the patient is awake and alert but only oriented to self (not time or place). The cardiopulmonary and neurologic exams are within normal limits. Routine lab work is performed to rule out infection and is found to be within normal limits. Four years later the patient passes away and an autopsy is performed to confirm the presumptive diagnosis. Brain biopsy slides are shown. What histologic features confirm this patient’s diagnosis?

A 10-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with sudden shortness of breath. They were playing in the school garden and suddenly started to complain of abdominal pain. They then vomited a few times. An hour later in the hospital, they slowly developed a rash on their chest, arms, and legs. Their breathing became faster with audible wheezing. On physical examination, their vital signs are as follows: the temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), the blood pressure is 100/60 mm Hg, the pulse is 130/min, and the respiratory rate is 25/min. A rash is on their right arm, as shown in the image. After being administered appropriate treatment, the patient improves significantly, and they are able to breathe comfortably. Which of the following is the best marker that could be measured in the serum of this patient to help establish a definitive diagnosis?

A 28-year-old patient presents with a yellow coloration of their skin. They say they feel well and deny any recent history of nausea, fatigue or fever, or discoloration of their urine or stool. The patient reports episodes with similar symptoms in the past. Family history is significant for similar symptoms in their father. The patient is afebrile and vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, they are jaundiced. Scleral icterus is present. Laboratory findings are significant only for an unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia. Liver enzymes are normal, and there is no bilirubin present in the urine. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment for this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old patient presents to the clinic with complaints of occasional low-grade fever and joint pain for 1 month. They also complain of morning stiffness in the proximal interphalangeal joints of both hands, which lasts for 5 to 10 minutes. They recently noticed a pink rash on their nose and cheekbones. Their family history is significant for similar complaints in their mother. They are not taking any medications. On examination, their temperature is 37.6°C (99.6°F), pulse is 74/min, blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg, and respirations are 18/min. Aphthous ulcers are noted on their oral mucosa. Which of the following tests would be most specific for confirming the diagnosis in this patient?

A 28-year-old patient is referred to the dermatologist for 2 months of increasing appearance of multiple smooth, circular patches of complete hair loss on their scalp. They say that the patches have associated pruritus and a burning sensation, and are not improving with the over-the-counter products recommended by their hair stylist. They deny pulling their hair intentionally. Physical examination reveals no epidermal inflammation or erythema, and no fluorescence is detected under Wood’s lamp. A punch biopsy shows a peribulbar lymphocytic inflammatory infiltrate surrounding anagen follicles, resembling a swarm of bees. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 45-year-old construction worker presents to their primary care physician with a painful and swollen wrist joint. A joint aspiration shows crystals, which are shown in the accompanying picture. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 16-month-old patient is brought to the pediatrician after their parents noticed the appearance of a rash on their face, torso, and limbs. The patient has been ill for almost 2 weeks, initiating with fever, malaise, coryza, headache, nausea, diarrhea, and a rash on both of their cheeks. Physical examination is unremarkable except for an erythematous maculopapular rash on the face, trunk, and extremities with a reticular pattern (as shown in the photograph). What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old patient presents with substernal chest pain for the past hour. They describe the chest pain as severe, squeezing in nature, diffusely localized to the substernal area and radiating down their left arm. They also have associated nausea, dizziness, and diaphoresis. They deny any recent history of fever, chest trauma, palpitations, or syncope. Past medical history is significant for gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), managed medically with a proton pump inhibitor for the last 3 months. They also have uncontrolled diabetes mellitus type 2 and hypercholesterolemia diagnosed 10 years ago. Their last HbA1c was 8.0. The vital signs include: blood pressure 140/90 mm Hg, pulse 100/min, respiratory rate 20/min, temperature 36.8°C (98.3°F) and oxygen saturation 98% on room air. They are administered sublingual nitroglycerin which lessens their chest pain. Chest radiograph seems normal. Electrocardiogram (ECG) shows ST-segment elevation in anterolateral leads. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis of this patient?

A 26-year-old patient presents to the behavioral health clinic for assistance overcoming their fear of public speaking. They have always hated public speaking. Two weeks ago, they were supposed to present a research project at school but had to leave the podium before the presentation. They recalled that their heart was racing, their palms were sweating, and that they could not breathe. These symptoms resolved on their own after several minutes, but they felt too embarrassed to return to college the next day. This had also happened in high school where, before a presentation, they started sweating and felt palpitations and nausea that also resolved on their own. They are scheduled for another presentation next month and are terrified. They state that this only happens in front of large groups and that they have no problems communicating at small gatherings. Other than their fear of public speaking, they have a normal social life and many friends. They enjoy their classes and a part-time job. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old patient presents to the emergency department due to sudden chest pain and difficulty breathing for the past 3 hours. The pain is felt in the retrosternal area and radiates up to their left shoulder and arm; it worsens on inspiration, and is relieved when they are leaning forward. Their heart rate is 61/min, respiratory rate is 16/min, temperature is 36.5°C (97.7°F), and blood pressure is 115/78 mm Hg. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Pericardial friction rub is heard on auscultation. Laboratory results show elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels. An ECG is performed. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old patient, with a recent ischemic stroke due to a right middle cerebral artery thromboembolism, presents for evaluation. In addition to the abnormal neurologic findings, there are significant hepatosplenomegaly and multiple lymphadenopathies. Laboratory findings are significant for the following: Hemoglobin 9.5 g/dL Erythrocyte count 13,600/mm³ Platelet count 95,000/mm³ Urinalysis reveals the presence of Bence-Jones proteins. Bone marrow biopsy shows numerous small lymphocytes mixed with plasmacytoid dendritic cells and plasma cells, increased numbers of mast cells, and the presence of Russell bodies and Dutcher bodies in plasma cells. A diagnosis of lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma is confirmed after further laboratory evaluation. Which of the following infectious agents would most likely be found in this patient, as well? They are otherwise healthy is not applicable in this case as the patient has multiple health issues, so no additional changes were made to the original text beyond removing the gender marker from the age description and no pronouns were present to replace.

A 50-year-old patient presents to their primary care provider complaining of smelling abnormal odors on several occasions. They say that they smell burnt rubber even though there is nothing burning and no one around them can smell what they do. This symptom has been intermittently bothering them for the past 6 months. Also during this period, they had occasional nosebleeds. They work as a high school teacher. Although their work gets a little stressful around the exam season, they say they are able to cope well. Family history is unremarkable. They do not smoke or drink alcohol and deny the use of any medication. Physical examination reveals unilateral nasal obstruction with some dried blood in the nasal passage. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old patient presented to the hospital with right upper quadrant abdominal pain. They have a history of hepatitis B. They underwent a CT of their abdomen which revealed a large mass (11.3 cm x 7.2 cm in diameter) with a metastatic retroperitoneal lymph node. They were diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma and initially received radiotherapy while on the transplant list to prevent local expansion of their malignancy. 3 months after radiotherapy, the patient experienced hematemesis and melena. They were admitted to the emergency department for evaluation. Their vitals were: blood pressure 84/56 mmHg, heart rate 92/min, and respiratory rate 20/min. Laboratory evaluation revealed severe anemia with a hemoglobin level of 5.7 g/dL, INR 1.8 and platelets of 68,000 cells/mm3. They received a blood transfusion. An endoscopic examination demonstrated diffuse edematous hyperemic mucosa and multiple hemorrhagic patches with active oozing in the antrum. What is the most likely diagnosis for the lesions seen in endoscopy?

A 55-year-old truck driver is brought to a physician by their spouse. They state that the patient developed a fever and began feeling weak 3 days ago, but has refused medical help. They have been unable to go to work because of their symptoms. The patient has been previously hospitalized for a tricuspid valve replacement surgery 1 year ago and takes aspirin daily. The medical history is also relevant for myocardial infarction 3 years ago and hypertension for the past 10 years, for which they take lisinopril. Their blood pressure is 140/80 mm Hg, the pulse is 82/min, the respirations are 18/minute, and the temperature is 37.2°C (98.9°F). On examination, several hemorrhages are noted on the nail beds of several fingers. Which of the following findings would be most helpful in establishing a diagnosis?

A 3-year-old patient is brought to the pediatrician by their parents who are concerned that they are not developing normally. They say they do not talk and avoid eye contact. They prefer to sit and play with blocks by themselves rather than engaging with other children. They also note that they will occasionally have violent outbursts in inappropriate situations. They are otherwise healthy. In the office, the patient sits quietly in the corner of the room stacking and unstacking blocks. Examination of the patient shows a well-developed individual with no physical abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 25-year-old patient presents to the office for a 3-day history of fever and fatigue. Upon further questioning, they say that they also had constant muscular pain, headaches, and fever during these days. They add additional information by giving a history of regular unprotected sexual relationship with multiple partners. They are a non-smoker and drink alcohol occasionally. The heart rate is 102/min, respiratory rate is 18/min, temperature is 38.0°C (100.4°F), and blood pressure is 120/80 mm Hg. On physical examination, they are icteric and hepatosplenomegaly is evident with diffuse muscular and abdominal tenderness particularly in the right upper quadrant. The serologic markers show the following pattern: Anti-HAV IgM negative HBsAg positive Anti-HBs negative IgM anti-HBc positive Anti-HCV negative Anti-HDV negative What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old chronic smoker presents to the physician with a complaint of worsening left shoulder pain for several months which has become acutely worse the past 2 weeks and now radiates down their left arm. Physical examination reveals a palpable 2 x 1.5 cm supraclavicular lymph node along with decreased grip strength in their left hand. Examination of the face reveals partial ptosis of the left eyelid and miosis of the left eye. Laboratory testing shows the following values: Sodium (Na+) 135 mEq/L Potassium (K+) 3.6 mEq/L Chloride (Cl-) 100 mEq/L BUN 12 mg/dL Creatinine (Cr) 0.6 mg/dL Magnesium (Mg2+) 1.5 mg/dL Phosphate 3 mg/dL Calcium (Ca2+) 8.5 mg/dL An X-ray of the chest reveals a soft tissue mass at the apex of the left lung with possible involvement of the first rib. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 75-year-old patient presents with episodic abdominal pain following meals for the past few years. They say these episodes have worsened over the past month. Past medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed 30 years ago, managed with metformin. Their most recent HbA1C last month was 10%. Vital signs include: blood pressure 110/70 mm Hg, pulse 80/min, and respiratory rate 16/min. Physical examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 24-year-old patient presents with fever, abdominal pain, and bloody bowel movements. They say their symptoms onset 2 days ago and have not improved. They describe the abdominal pain as moderate, cramping in character, and poorly localized. 1 week ago, they say they were on a camping trip with their friends and had barbecued chicken which they thought tasted strange. The patient denies any chills, hemoptysis, hematochezia, or similar symptoms in the past. The vital signs include: pulse 87/min and temperature 37.8°C (100.0°F). Physical examination is significant for moderate tenderness to palpation in the periumbilical region with no rebound or guarding. Stool is guaiac positive. Which of the following is a complication associated with this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 14-year-old patient is brought to the office by their parents because they state that for the past 2 months they have been feeling constantly tired, and also noticed a dull pain in the pit of their stomach. The patient has no relevant family history. The vital signs include a heart rate of 105/min, a respiratory rate of 16/min, a temperature of 37.0°C (98.6°F), and a blood pressure of 111/66 mm Hg. On physical exam, the abdomen is distended with hepatomegaly 5 cm underneath the xiphoid process. The complete blood count results are as follows: Hemoglobin 17.6 g/dL Hematocrit 64% RBC 6.02 x 1012/L Leukocyte count 26,300/mm3 Neutrophils 55% Bands 2% Eosinophils 1% Basophils 0% Lymphocytes 29% Monocytes 2% Platelet count 480,000/mm³ Erythropoietin < 1.0 mU/mL The coagulation test results are as follows: Partial thromboplastin time (activated) 30.9 s Prothrombin time 14.0 s The abdominal Doppler ultrasound imaging is shown in the picture. What is the most likely etiology of this patient’s diagnosis?

A 24-year-old patient of Ashkenazi Jewish descent presents with recurrent bloody diarrhea and abdominal pain. They say they feel well otherwise. Review of systems is significant for a 4 kg weight loss over the past month. Physical examination is significant for multiple aphthous oral ulcers. Colonoscopy reveals a cobblestone pattern of lesions of the mucosa of the intestinal wall involving the sigmoid colon. The patient is informed of the diagnosis and medication to treat their condition is prescribed. On a follow-up visit 6 weeks later, the patient presents with non-productive cough, chest pain, dyspnea on exertion, and worsening oral lesions. A chest radiograph reveals a diffuse interstitial pattern. Which of the following enzymes is inhibited by the medication most likely prescribed for their initial diagnosis?

A 70-year-old patient presents for their annual check-up. They say they feel well except for occasional abdominal pain. They describe the pain as 4/10–5/10 in intensity, diffusely localized to the periumbilical and epigastric regions, radiating to the groin. The pain occurs 1–2 times a month and always subsides on its own. The patient denies any recent history of fever, chills, nausea, vomiting, change in body weight, or change in bowel and/or bladder habits. Their past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and peripheral vascular disease, managed with lisinopril and simvastatin. The patient reports a 40-pack-year smoking history and 1–2 alcoholic drinks a day. The blood pressure is 150/100 mm Hg and the pulse is 80/min. Peripheral pulses are 2+ bilaterally in all extremities. Abdominal exam reveals a bruit in the epigastric region along with mild tenderness to palpation with no rebound or guarding. There is also a pulsatile abdominal mass felt on deep palpation at the junction of the periumbilical and the suprapubic regions. The remainder of the physical exam is normal. Laboratory studies show: Serum total cholesterol 175 mg/dL Serum total bilirubin 1 mg/dL Serum amylase 25 U/L Serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 20 U/L Serum aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 16 U/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 24-year-old patient presents to the office for a physical exam and drug screening requested by their parole officer. They have a history of multiple run-ins with the law, including theft, destruction of property, and assault and battery. Patient confesses that they have always been the 'problem child' in their home and always got into trouble with authority figures. Past medical records reveal testimonies from their parent describing episodes of physically aggressive behavior in school starting at before 12. Although a single parent, their parent states there were no stressful changes or issues at home. Today's urine toxicology screens are negative. Which of the following is most likely this patient’s diagnosis?

A 9-year-old patient is brought in by their parent because of bruising on their torso and limbs. The patient’s parent denies any other symptoms and says they are otherwise healthy. Physical examination shows multiple petechiae and bruising on the torso and extremities bilaterally. The remainder of the physical exam is unremarkable. A complete blood count is normal. Their coagulation profile reveals: Prothrombin time (PT) 12 sec Activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) 60 sec Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 1-year-old, pale-looking patient presents with high-grade fever and ecchymosis, which they have been experiencing for the past 2 weeks. The patient has achieved all developmental milestones on time and has no history of medical illness in the past. Lab investigations reveal the following: Hemoglobin 5.5 g/dL WBC 112,000/mm3 Platelets 15,000/mm3 ESR 105/1st hour The patient is referred to a hematologist, who suspects that they may be suffering from the neoplastic proliferation of immature B cells. The physician decides to do a flow cytometry analysis. Detection of which of the following markers would help confirm the suspected diagnosis?

A 30-year-old patient who recently emigrated from Southeast Asia presents with heartburn and a bad taste in their mouth. They say the symptoms have been present for the last 6 months and are much worse at night. They describe the pain as moderate to severe, burning in character, and localized to the epigastric region. They mention that 1 month ago, they were tested for Helicobacter pylori back in their country and completed a course of multiple antibiotics, but there has been no improvement in their symptoms. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 58-year-old patient with a history of hepatitis C infection presents to their physician because of unintentional weight loss and weakness. They have lost 6.8 kg (15 lb) within the last 6 months. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows jaundice, splenomegaly, and caput medusae. A complete metabolic panel is ordered. Which of the following tests is the most likely to result in a diagnosis?

A 35-year-old patient, with a history of neurofibromatosis type 2 (NF2) diagnosed 2 years ago, presents with hearing loss in the right ear and tinnitus. The patient says that symptoms have been gradually progressive. They have difficulty hearing speech as well as loud sounds. They also give a history of occasional headaches and vertigo on and off for 1 month, which is unresponsive to paracetamol. Their vitals include: blood pressure 110/78 mm Hg, temperature 36.5°C (97.8°F), pulse 78/min and respiratory rate 11/min. Tuning fork tests reveal the following: Left Right Rinne’s test Air conduction > bone conduction Air conduction > bone conduction Weber test Lateralized to left ear Other physical examination findings are within normal limits. An MRI of the head is ordered which is as shown in image 1. A biopsy is done which shows cells staining positive for S100 but negative for glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP). The histopathological slide is shown in image 2. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old patient is brought to a clinic with complaints of fever and sore throat for 2 days. This morning, they developed a rash on their face and neck which is progressing towards the trunk. The teachers in their school report that none of their classmates has similar symptoms. They have a normal birth history. On physical examination, the child looks healthy. The heart rate is 90/min, respiratory rate is 20/min, temperature is 39.0°C (102.2°F), and blood pressure is 90/50 mm Hg. An oropharyngeal examination reveals circumoral pallor with a red tongue, as shown in the photograph below. The chest and cardiac examinations are within normal limits. No hepatosplenomegaly is noted. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old patient is brought to the office by their parent because of a large head contusion and altered mental status. At first, the parent says their child got injured when a “pot fell from a shelf onto their head.” Later, they change the story and say that the child hit their head after “tripping over a football.” Physical examination shows cracks in the suture lines of the skull, and there is a flattened appearance to the bone. The patient's parent arrives to inquire on how their child is “recovering from their fall down the stairs.” Upon request to interview the patient alone, the parents refuse, complaining loudly about the request. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 5-year-old patient is brought to the office by their parent with complaints of facial puffiness and “frothy” urine for 4 days. The puffiness first started in their eyes and then spread to the face. Their parent does not provide any history of similar symptoms in the past. Past medical history is non-significant. Their birth history is uneventful and all their vaccinations are up to date. The vital signs include: blood pressure 100/62 mm Hg, pulse 110/min, temperature 36.7°C (98.0°F), and respiratory rate 16/min. On examination, there is pitting edema of the upper and lower extremities bilaterally. Urinalysis results are as follows: pH 6.2 Color light yellow RBC none WBC 3–4/HPF Protein 4+ Cast Fat globules Glucose absent Crystal none Ketone absent Nitrite absent 24-hour urine protein excretion 4.1 g A renal biopsy is sent which shows normal glomeruli on light microscopy. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old patient goes to their primary care provider for a checkup after some blood work showed lymphocytosis 3 months ago. They say they have been feeling a bit more tired lately but don’t complain of any other symptoms. Past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. They take lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, and atorvastatin. Additionally, their right hip was replaced three years ago due to osteoarthritis. Family history is noncontributory.
