They drink socially and do not smoke. Today, they have a heart rate of 95/min, respiratory rate of 17/min, blood pressure of 135/85 mm Hg, and temperature of 36.8°C (98.2°F). On physical exam, they look well. Their heartbeat has a regular rate and rhythm and lungs that are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Additionally, they have mild lymphadenopathy of their cervical lymph nodes. A complete blood count with differential shows the following: Leukocyte count 5,000/mm3 Red blood cell count 3.1 million/mm3 Hemoglobin 11.0 g/dL MCV 95 um3 MCH 29 pg/cell Platelet count 150,000/mm3 Neutrophils 40% Lymphocytes 40% Monocytes 5% A specimen is sent for flow cytometry that shows a population that is CD 5, 19, 20, 23 positive. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old patient presents with episodic abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea for the past week. They say that the abdominal pain is diffusely localized to the periumbilical region and is dull and cramping in character. They also report episodes of painful, bloody diarrhea up to 7 times per day. A colonoscopy is performed and shows continuous erythema, superficial ulcers, and pseudopolyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon. A biopsy is taken and sent for histological evaluation. One of the slides from the biopsy is shown in the image below. Which of the following histopathologic findings characteristic of this patient’s most likely diagnosis is marked by the yellow circle?

A 54-year-old gardener with diabetes mellitus from the Northeast Jillin Province in China acquired a small scratch from a thorn while working in their flower garden. After 3 weeks, they noticed a small pink, painless bump at the site of the scratch. They were not concerned by the bump; however, additional linearly-distributed bumps that resembled boils began to appear 1 week later that were quite painful. When the changes took on the appearance of open sores that drained clear fluid without any evidence of healing (as shown on the image), they finally visited their physician. The physician referred the gardener for a skin biopsy to confirm their working diagnosis and to start treatment as soon as possible. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 65-year-old patient presents with pain in their left thigh for a week. They describe the pain as dull and constant, boring in nature, and localized deep below the thigh muscle. They say it is worse at night. Physical examination is significant for tenderness and warmth over the anterior aspect of the left thigh. A plain radiograph of the left femur shows increased cortical thickness with widened intercortical space. Laboratory studies show: Alkaline phosphatase 925 U/L Serum calcium 9.2 mg/dL Serum phosphorus 4.4 mg/dL Findings on bone biopsy are shown in the image. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 52-year-old patient presents with a 5-week history of multiple cutaneous ulcers on their left forearm and neck, which they first noticed after returning from a 2-month stay in rural Peru. They do not recall any trauma or arthropod bites. The lesions began as non-pruritic erythematous papules that became enlarged, ulcerated, and crusted. There is no history of fever or abdominal pain. They have been sexually active with a single partner since their marriage at 24 years of age. The physical examination reveals erythematous, crusted plaques with central ulceration and a raised border. There is no fluctuance, drainage, or sporotrichoid spread. A punch biopsy was performed, which revealed an ulcerated lesion with a mixed inflammatory infiltrate. Amastigotes within dermal macrophages are seen on Giemsa staining. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old patient presents to the office because of extreme fatigue for the past 2 days. They are also worried about their skin looking yellow. They do not have any other complaints and deny fever and headache. They admit to using illicit intravenous drugs in the past. They do not have any immunization records because they moved from Africa to the US at the age of 18. Their vital signs are as follows: heart rate 72/min, respiratory rate 14/min, temperature 37.9°C (100.2°F), and blood pressure 100/74 mm Hg. Physical examination is not significant except for mild diffuse abdominal tenderness. Their blood is drawn for routine tests and shows an alanine aminotransferase level (ALT) of 2,000 IU/L. A hepatitis viral panel is ordered which shows: Anti-HAV IgM negative HBsAg positive Anti-HBs negative IgM anti-HBc positive Anti-HCV negative Anti-HDV negative What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old patient who was recently ill with an upper respiratory infection presents to the emergency department with weakness in their lower limbs and difficulty breathing. Their symptoms began with a burning sensation in their toes along with numbness. They claim that the weakness has been getting worse over the last few days and now involving their arms and face. Currently, they are unable to get up from the chair without some assistance. Their temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), the blood pressure is 145/89 mm Hg, the heart rate is 99/min, the respiratory rate is 12/min, and the oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. On physical examination, they have diminished breath sounds on auscultation of bilateral lung fields with noticeably poor inspiratory effort. Palpation of the lower abdomen reveals a palpable bladder. Strength is 3 out of 5 symmetrically in the lower extremities bilaterally. The sensation is intact. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old patient presents with sexual dysfunction. Past medical history is significant for diabetes mellitus type 1 diagnosed 25 years ago, managed with insulin, and for donating blood 6 months ago. The patient denies any history of smoking or alcohol use. They are afebrile, and their vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows a bronze-colored hyperpigmentation on the dorsal side of the arms bilaterally. Routine basic laboratory tests are significant for a moderate increase in glycosylated hemoglobin and hepatic enzymes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 82-year-old patient presents to the emergency department because of excruciating right flank pain and fever for the past 2 days. They state that they are having trouble urinating. Their past medical history is unremarkable. A urinalysis is performed and comes back positive for leukocytes and gram-negative bacilli. A contrast computed tomography of the abdomen is performed and reveals a large retroperitoneal mass compressing the right ureter, leading to hydronephrosis of the right kidney. The mass is excised. Histopathologic evaluation of the mass is shown in the image below, and it is determined to be malignant. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 52-year-old patient presents with erosions in their mouth that are persistent and painful. They say that symptoms appeared gradually 1 week ago and have progressively worsened. They also note that, several days ago, flaccid blisters appeared on their skin, which almost immediately transformed to erosions as well. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 49-year-old patient otherwise healthy presents to the outpatient department with swelling of the neck. Family history is negative for any thyroid disorders. Physical examination shows a nontender thyroid gland with a nodule on the right side. The thyroid gland is mobile on deglutition. Cervical lymphadenopathy is present. Fine needle aspiration and cytology show empty appearing nuclei with central clearing, nuclear grooves and branching structures interspersed with calcific bodies. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 31-year-old patient is referred to a neurologist due to their gradually increasing eccentric behavior and involuntary movements, especially the movements of their arms and hands. They also have difficulty with their short-term memory. Past medical history is otherwise noncontributory. Their parent had similar symptoms before they died but those symptoms started at the age of 33. Their blood pressure is 125/92 mm Hg, pulse is 90/min, respiratory rate 12/min, and temperature is 36.6°C (97.9°F). Physical exam reveals involuntary writhing movements of hands, slow eye movements, and sporadic rigidity. The physician explains that this is an inherited disorder where the symptoms occur progressively at an earlier age than the parent and often with increased severity in the future generations. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis of this patient?

A 35-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their coworkers after a sudden onset of vision loss. They are a lawyer and lost 3 cases in the past week. Yesterday, they experienced weakness and paralysis of their left wrist. Past medical history is significant for acid reflux. Physical examination reveals 2/4 in reflexes and 5/5 in muscular strength in all extremities. They appear indifferent to their current situation and present with a flat affect. Slurring of words is absent. CT without contrast and MRI of the brain are unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient presents with a history of repeated episodes of discoloration of the fingers over the last 3 years. They mention that the episodes are usually triggered by exposure to cold, which leads to a sequential white, blue, and red discoloration of their fingers, followed by resolution of the symptoms. During an episode, they experience pain and numbness in the affected fingers. The episodes are usually of short duration and do not interfere with their life, so they did not seek medical advice till now. Which of the following additional clinical features in this patient would most likely support the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient presents to the office because of shortness of breath and chest tightness on exertion which they noticed for the past 2 months. They were diagnosed with asthma 1 month ago but say that the asthma medication has not improved their breathing. They do not smoke and work as a hotel manager. Examination shows mildly jaundiced conjunctivae, several spider nevi on their upper torso, and a barrel-chested appearance. A chest X-ray is obtained. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old patient presents with “yellowing” of the skin. They say they have been having intermittent upper abdominal pain, which is relieved by Tylenol. They also recall that they have lost some weight over the past several months but cannot quantify the amount. Their past medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus. They report a 40-pack-year smoking history. The patient is afebrile and vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination reveals mild jaundice and a palpable gallbladder. Laboratory findings are significant for the following: Total bilirubin 13 mg/dL Direct bilirubin: 10 mg/dL Alkaline phosphatase (ALP): 560 IU/L An ultrasound of the abdomen reveals a hypoechoic mass in the epigastric region. The patient is scheduled for a CT abdomen and pelvis with specific organ protocol for further evaluation. Which of the following best describes this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

During a humanitarian medical mission in rural Vietnam, a medical resident encounters a 50-year-old patient with a year-long history of a pruritic rash on their upper body and face, along with numbness and tingling sensation of both of their palms. They mostly work on their family’s rice farm, where they also take care of livestock. A physical examination revealed multiple erythematous macules and papules on the face, arms, chest, and back, as well as thinning of the eyebrows and loss of some eyelashes. Additional findings include hypopigmented macules around the elbows, which are insensitive to light touch, temperature, and pinprick. The grip strength is slightly diminished bilaterally with the conservation of both bicipital reflexes. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old patient presents with facial flushing, weakness, and chronic diarrhea for the past month. They deny any history of smoking, alcohol use, or recreational drug use. The patient was on a trip to Thailand 2 years ago with their family but denies any recent travel. Their blood pressure is 120/88 mm Hg, pulse is 78/min, temperature is 37.2°C (99.0°F), and respiratory rate is 16/min. Laboratory findings are unremarkable, except for a potassium level of 3.3 mmol/L and serum calcium of 11 mg/dL. The attending physician suspects that this might be a case of a genetic mutation in the menin 1 gene on chromosome 11 and orders a genetic analysis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 26-year-old professional soccer player is brought to the emergency department due to an episode of syncope during a game. They have felt increasing shortness of breath during the past 3 months. During the past week, they have been feeling chest pain upon exertion. They also tell the doctor that their brother had a sudden death a couple of years ago. Their heart rate is 98/min, respiratory rate is 18/min, temperature is 36.5°C (97.7°F), and blood pressure is 110/72 mm Hg. On physical examination, there is a harsh crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur immediately after S1; it is best heard on the apex, and it radiates to the axilla. There is also an early diastolic murmur heard in early diastole, which is best heard with the bell of the stethoscope. When the Valsalva maneuver is performed, the murmur becomes louder. An ECG and an echocardiogram are performed, which confirm the diagnosis. What is the most likely cause of this patient’s condition?

A 21-year-old patient presents to the emergency room with right arm pain and limited range of motion. They do not recall trauma to the arm. They also complain of diarrhea and nausea. They are sexually active with one partner and admit to having pain during intercourse. There is vague and diffuse tenderness to palpation in all four abdominal quadrants. No erythema or edema is noted on the right arm. The fecal occult test is negative. Past records show that this patient has been in the ER 7 times in the past year with similar symptoms. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with complaints of fluctuating mood for the past 2 years. They feel great and full of energy for some months when they are very creative with tons of ideas just racing through their mind. They are noted to be very talkative and distracted by their different ideas. During these times, they are very productive and able to accomplish much at work and home. However, these periods are frequently followed by a prolonged depressed mood. During this time, they have low energy, poor concentration, and low self-esteem. The accompanying feeling of hopelessness from these cycling “ups” and “downs” have them eating and sleeping more during the “downs.” They do not remember a period within the last 2 years where they felt “normal.” What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old patient, who was previously healthy, is taken to the emergency department due to agitation during the past 24 hours. During the past week, their family members noticed a yellowish coloring of their skin and eyes. They occasionally use cocaine and ecstasy, and they drink alcohol (about 20 g) on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behavior and does not use appropriate protection. Physical examination shows heart rate of 94/min, respiratory rate of 13/min, temperature of 37.0°C (98.6°F), and blood pressure of 110/60 mm Hg. The patient shows psychomotor agitation, and they are not oriented to time and space. Other findings include asterixis, jaundice on the skin and mucous membranes, and epistaxis. The rest of the physical examination is normal. The laboratory tests show: Hemoglobin 16.3 g/dL Hematocrit 47% Leukocyte count 9,750/mm3 Neutrophils 58% Bands 2% Eosinophils 1% Basophils 0% Lymphocytes 24% Monocytes 2% Platelet count 365,000/mm3 Bilirubin 25 mg/dL AST 600 IU/L ALT 650 IU/L TP activity < 40% INR 1,5 What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old student presents to the college health clinic with a 1-week history of fever, sore throat, nausea, and fatigue. They could hardly get out of bed this morning. There are no pets at home. They admit to having recent unprotected sex. The vital signs include: temperature 38.3°C (101.0°F), pulse 72/min, blood pressure 118/63 mm Hg, and respiratory rate 15/min. On physical examination, they have bilateral posterior cervical lymphadenopathy, exudates over the palatine tonsil walls with soft palate petechiae, an erythematous macular rash on the trunk and arms, and mild hepatosplenomegaly. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 12-year-old patient presents with recurrent joint pain that migrates from joint to joint and intermittent fever for the last several weeks. They also say that they have no appetite and have been losing weight. The patient is afebrile, and vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, they are pale with diffuse petechial bleeding and bruises on their legs. An abdominal examination is significant for hepatosplenomegaly. Ultrasound of the abdomen confirms hepatosplenomegaly and also shows multiple enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes. A complete blood count (CBC) shows severe anemia and thrombocytopenia with leukocytosis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 35-year-old patient visits their primary care provider with complaints of easy fatigability, breathlessness on exertion, and altered sensations in their lower limbs. Past medical history is positive for hypertension. They take hydrochlorothiazide and lisinopril, a multivitamin every day, and other medications. Family history is noncontributory. They drink alcohol almost every day and smoke cigarettes when they drink. Today their heart rate is 95/min, respiratory rate is 17/min, blood pressure is 130/92 mm Hg, and temperature of 37.0°C (98.6°F). Overall, they have marked pallor with slight bluing of their lips and distal fingertips. Their heart has a regular rate and rhythm and their lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Additionally, they have loss of touch, and vibration sense in both of their lower limbs. Their CBC is as follows: Hemoglobin 8.0 g/dL MCV 112 fL WBC 2,500/mm3 Platelets 95,000/mm3 What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 12-year-old patient presents to the pediatric dermatologist with an expanding, but otherwise asymptomatic erythematous patch on their right shoulder, which they first noticed 3 days ago. The patient states the rash started as a small red bump but has gradually progressed to its current size. No similar lesions were observed elsewhere by them or their parent. They have felt ill and their parent has detected intermittent low-grade fevers. During the skin examination, a target-like erythematous patch, approximately 7 cm in diameter, was noted on the left shoulder (as shown in the image). Another notable finding was axillary lymphadenopathy. On further questioning it was revealed that the patient went camping with their grandfather approximately 11 days ago; however, they do not recall any insect bites or exposure to animals. The family has a pet cat living in their household. Based on the history and physical examination results, what is the most likely diagnosis?

A 52-year-old patient presents with mild epigastric pain and persistent heartburn for the past 2 months. An endoscopy is performed and reveals inflammation of the stomach mucosa without evidence of ulceration. A biopsy is performed and reveals intestinal metaplasia with destruction of a large number of parietal cells. They are diagnosed with chronic atrophic gastritis. Which of the following is characteristic of this patient’s diagnosis?

A 75-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with their child because they are convinced that people are stealing from them. Their child claims they have been misplacing their medications and money throughout the house. They recently lost their spouse to old age and have become reclusive and no longer want people to visit. Physical examination is unremarkable and the patient is oriented to person, time, and place. A mini-mental status examination (MMSE) is performed and they have difficulty recalling words after 5 minutes and also have problems with serial subtraction. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 44-year-old patient is brought to the clinic by their spouse insisting that they have been acting strange lately. They are a dentist by profession and have no known medical conditions. For the past 6 weeks, they have insisted on listening to the 6 PM news on the radio. They are adamant that the news anchor is referencing their life during the broadcasts. Apart from this, their spouse states that they are fine. They and their spouse deny the use of any prescribed medications or illicit drugs. They are a non-smoker and drink alcohol only on social occasions. Physical examination and routine laboratory investigations are normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70 year-old patient comes to the clinic for generalized fatigue. They say that they are more tired than before and have difficulty catching their breath while walking upstairs. They feel tired quickly doing their usual activity such as gardening and shopping. They do not have any symptoms of fever, change in bowel habits, abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, or weight loss. Their appetite is normal. Their last colonoscopy was done 10 years ago and it was normal. Their blood pressure is 116/74 and heart rate is 87/min. On physical examination, their conjunctivae are pale. A routine blood test shows iron deficiency anemia with hemoglobin of 10 gm/dL. Their stool is positive for occult blood. They are then sent for a colonoscopy (image is shown). What is the most likely diagnosis for the above condition?

A 67-year-old patient presents with fatigue, progressive abdominal distention and yellow skin coloration for the past 2 weeks. They deny fever, chills, or other symptoms. Past medical history is unremarkable. They report heavy alcohol consumption for the past several years but say they quit recently. On physical examination, the patient appears jaundiced and is ill-appearing. There is shifting dullness on abdominal percussion with a positive fluid wave. Sclera are icteric. Bilateral breast tenderness is present. Laboratory findings are significant for the following: Hgb 13 g/dL Leukocyte count 4,500/mm3 Platelets 86,000/mm3 Aspartate transaminase (AST) 108 U/L Alanine transaminase (ALT) 55 U/L GGT 185 U/L Urea 23 mg/dL Iron 120 μg/dL Ferritin 180 μg/dL Transferrin saturation 40% Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 40-year-old farmer from Ohio seeks evaluation at a clinic with complaints of a chronic cough, fevers, and anorexia of several months duration. On examination, they have generalized lymphadenopathy with hepatosplenomegaly. A chest radiograph reveals local infiltrates and patchy opacities involving all lung fields. Fine needle aspiration of an enlarged lymph node shows the presence of intracellular yeast. A fungal culture shows the presence of thick-walled spherical spores with tubercles and microconidia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 16-year-old patient presents with a long-standing history of anemia. Past medical history is significant for prolonged neonatal jaundice and multiple episodes of jaundice without fever. On physical examination, the patient shows generalized pallor, scleral icterus, and splenomegaly. Their hemoglobin is 10 g/dL, and examination of a peripheral blood smear shows red cell basophilic stippling. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 14-month-old Caucasian patient is admitted to the pediatric clinic with an 8-month history of diarrhea, abdominal tenderness and concomitant failure to thrive. One of the possibilities that may cause these symptoms is Crohn’s disease, and on the basis of the attending pediatrician’s experience, the pre-test probability of this diagnosis was estimated at 40%. According to Fagan’s diagram (picture), if the likelihood ratio of a negative test result (LR-) is 0.04, what is the chance that this is the right diagnosis?

A 31-year-old patient presents with pruritic vesicles on the right side of their torso. They note that the lesions appeared 2 days ago and have not improved. One day prior to their appearance, they say that they experienced a burning sensation in the affected area. The patient is afebrile and vital signs are within normal limits. Upon physical examination, there are painful vesicles noted that are localized to the right T10 skin dermatome. Which of the following complications is associated with this patient’s likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient was referred to a dermatology clinic due to a changing discoloration of their fingers from white to red to blue. Although they have not had any recent changes in their daily routines, they also complain of increasing fatigue, muscle weakness, and weight loss. They have a blood pressure of 126/77 mm Hg, respiratory rate of 14/min, and heart rate of 88/min. Physical examination reveals regular heart and lung sounds. Anti-U1 RNP antibodies and increased creatinine kinase were found in their serum. What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 14-year-old patient is brought to the office by their step-parents because they were recently caught beating a stray cat in an alley near their home. They have a police record which includes vandalism, shoplifting, and running away on two occasions. They have also received several detentions and threats of expulsion from school due to bullying and being too aggressive with the younger students. Past medical history is significant for a history of ADHD previously treated with methylphenidate, but now they do not take anything. Their biological family placed them and their sibling into the foster care system. Their step-parents try to provide support and nurturing home life but the patient is very resistant and often acts out. What is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

An 18-month-old patient is presented to the emergency department by their parents due to swelling in their right knee after playing in the park. Their parents say there was no obvious injury. After questioning, a parent says that a relative of theirs had similar problems. The vital signs include heart rate 146/min, respiratory rate 26/min, temperature 37.1°C (98.8°F) and blood pressure 90/52 mm Hg. On physical examination, the swelling of the right knee is evident. The rest of the physical findings are unremarkable. The ultrasound is compatible with the hemarthrosis of the right knee. The complete blood count (CBC) results are as follows: Hemoglobin 12.2 g/dL Hematocrit 36% Leukocyte count 7,300/mm3 Neutrophils 45% Bands 3% Eosinophils 1% Basophils 0% Lymphocytes 44% Monocytes 2% Platelet count 200,000/mm³ The coagulation test results are as follows: Partial thromboplastin time (activated) 52.0 s Prothrombin time 14.0 s Reticulocyte count 1.2% Thrombin time < 2 seconds deviation from control What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old patient from Thailand presents with low-grade fever, chronic cough, and night sweats for 3 months. They describe the cough as productive and producing white sputum that is sometimes streaked with blood. They also say they have lost 10 lb in the last 3 months. Past medical history is unremarkable. The patient denies any smoking history, alcohol, or recreational drug use. The vital signs include blood pressure 115/75 mm Hg, heart rate 120/min, respiratory rate 20/min, and temperature 36.6℃ (97.8℉). On physical examination, the patient is ill-looking and thin with no pallor or jaundice. Cardiopulmonary auscultation reveals some fine crackles in the right upper lobe. A chest radiograph reveals a right upper lobe homogeneous density. Which of the following tests would be most helpful in making a definitive diagnosis of active infection in this patient?

A 58-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with severe chest pain and uneasiness. They say that symptoms onset acutely half an hour ago while they were watching television. They describe the pain as being 8/10 in intensity, sharp in character, localized to the center of the chest and retrosternal, and radiating to the back and shoulders. The patient denies any associated change in the pain with breathing or body position. They say they have associated nausea but deny any vomiting. They deny any recent history of fever, chills, or chronic cough. Their past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes mellitus for which they take lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, simvastatin, and metformin. They report a 30-pack-year smoking history and have 1–2 alcoholic drinks during the weekend. Family history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and an ST elevation myocardial infarction in their father and paternal uncle. Their blood pressure is 220/110 mm Hg in the right arm and 180/100 mm Hg in the left arm. On physical examination, the patient is diaphoretic. Cardiac exam reveals a grade 2/6 diastolic decrescendo murmur loudest over the left sternal border. Remainder of the physical examination is normal. The chest radiograph shows a widened mediastinum. The electrocardiogram (ECG) reveals non-specific ST segment and T wave changes. Intravenous morphine and beta-blockers are started. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 30-year-old patient comes to the emergency room with a chief complaint of left chest pain and a productive cough with purulent sputum for 1 week. They also complain of shortness of breath. They said they had been previously diagnosed with influenza but did not follow the doctor’s instructions. Their vitals include: heart rate 70/min, respiratory rate 22/min, temperature 38.7°C (101.7°F), blood pressure 120/60 mm Hg, and SO2 80%. Their hemogram and chest X-ray findings are as follows: Hemoglobin 14 mg/dL Hematocrit 45% Leukocyte count 12,000/mm3 Neutrophils 82% Lymphocytes 15% Monocytes 3% Platelet count 270,000/mm3 Chest X-ray alveolar infiltrates in the left base with air bronchograms What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old patient presents to the office for shortness of breath. The shortness of breath started a year ago and is exacerbated by physical activity. They have been working in the glass manufacturing industry for 20 years. Their vital signs include: heart rate 72/min, respiratory rate 30/min, and blood pressure 130/80 mm Hg. On physical exam, there are diminished respiratory sounds on both sides. On the chest radiograph, interstitial fibrosis with reticulonodular infiltrate is found on both sides, and there is also an eggshell calcification of multiple adenopathies. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient presents to your office complaining of difficulty swallowing, and they describe that "there is something in the back of their throat". Furthermore, they also feel an "achy" chest pain that has been getting progressively worse over the last few weeks. They deny having any fever, shortness of breath, cough, abdominal pain, heartburn, nausea, or vomiting. The patient has a history of wrist fracture as a child, migraines, and a recent diagnosis of myasthenia gravis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old patient visits the office with complaints of fever and abdominal pain for the past 6 days. They are also concerned about their weight loss as they weigh 3.6 kg (8 lb) less, today, than they did 2 months ago. They have a previous history of being admitted to the hospital for recurrent cholangitis. The vital signs include: heart rate 97/min, respiratory rate 17/min, temperature 39.0°C (102.2°F), and blood pressure 114/70 mm Hg. On physical examination, there is tenderness on palpation of the right upper quadrant. The laboratory results are as follows: Hemoglobin 16 g/dL Hematocrit 44% Leukocyte count 18,000/mm3 Neutrophils 60% Bands 4% Eosinophils 2% Basophils 1% Lymphocytes 27% Monocytes 6% Platelet count 345,000/mm3 Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 57 IU/L Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 70 IU/L Alkaline phosphatase 140 U/L Total bilirubin 8 mg/dL Direct bilirubin 5 mg/dL An ultrasound is also done on the patient which is shown in the picture. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 13-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their parents for 5 days of abdominal pain, fever, vomiting, and mild diarrhea. Their parents have been giving them acetaminophen in the past 3 days, which they stopped 24 hours ago when they noted blood in the patient's urine. Upon admission, the patient has a fever of 39.6°C (103.3°F) and is hemodynamically stable. While waiting for the results of the laboratory tests, the patient develops intense left flank pain, and nausea and vomiting intensifies. Their condition rapidly deteriorates with an abnormally high blood pressure of 180/100 mm Hg, a heart rate of 120/min, and labored breathing leading to ventilatory failure. Under these conditions, the ER team immediately transfers the patient to the pediatric ICU, however, the patient dies shortly after. The pathologist shares with you some excerpts from the complete blood count and peripheral smear report: Hemoglobin 7 mg/dL Mean 14.0 g/dL (-2SD: 13.0 g/dL) MCV 85 fL; 80–96 fL Platelets 60,000; 150,000–450,000 Peripheral smear Schistocytes (+); Schistocytes (-) White blood cells 12,900; 4,500–11,000 What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by the police after they were found running around a local park naked and screaming late at night. During intake, the patient talks non-stop about the government spying on them and their family, but provides little useful information besides their name and date of birth. Occasionally they refer to themselves in the third person. They refuse to eat anything and will only drink clear fluids because they are afraid of being poisoned. A medical records search reveals that the patient has been treated for psychotic behavior and occasional bouts of severe depression for several years. Today, their heart rate is 90/min, respiratory rate is 19/min, blood pressure is 135/85 mm Hg, and temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F). On physical exam, they appear gaunt and anxious. Their heart has a regular rate and rhythm and their lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. CMP, CBC, and TSH are normal. A urine toxicology test is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old patient presents with a history of intermittent fever for the last 2 days. They say their episodes of fever are accompanied by shaking and chills. They mention that their father has been recently recovered from chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum malaria, which was treated successfully with quinine. On physical examination, their temperature is 38.9°C (102°F), pulse rate is 110/min, blood pressure is 116/80 mm Hg, and respiratory rate is 18/min. Examination of their abdomen reveals splenomegaly. Their blood sample is sent for the examination of the peripheral smear, which confirms the diagnosis of Plasmodium falciparum malaria. The patient is placed on treatment with oral quinine. After 5 days, the patient returns with improved symptoms of malaria but with complaints of a headache, tinnitus, nausea, and dizziness. The patient mentions that they have been taking a drug for the last 3 months to control their dyspepsia symptoms. Which of the following drugs is most likely to have caused the above-mentioned symptoms in this patient?

A 37-year-old patient is being evaluated for involuntary movements, difficulty swallowing food, and personality change. They have entered a clinical trial that is studying the interaction of certain neuromediators in patients with similar (CAG) n trinucleotide repeat disorders. The laboratory results of 1 of the candidates for the clinical trial are presented below: Acetylcholine ↓ Dopamine ↑ Gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) ↓ Norepinephrine unchanged Serotonin unchanged Which trinucleotide disorder most likely represents the diagnosis of this patient?

A 55-year-old patient presents with severe pruritus and fatigue. They deny any similar symptoms in the past. No significant past medical history. Upon physical examination, scleral icterus is present, and significant hepatosplenomegaly is noted. Mild peripheral edema is also present. Laboratory findings are significant for elevated serum levels of bilirubin, aminotransferases, alkaline phosphatase (ALP), γ-glutamyl transpeptidase (GGTP), immunoglobulins, as well as cholesterol (especially HDL fraction). Antiviral antibodies are not present. The erythrocyte sedimentation rate is also elevated. Anti-mitochondrial antibodies are found. A liver biopsy is performed, and the histopathologic examination shows bile duct injury, cholestasis, and granuloma formation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 79-year-old patient presents to the office due to shortness of breath with moderate exertion and a slightly productive cough. They have a medical history of 25 years of heavy smoking. Their vitals include: heart rate 89/min, respiratory rate 27/min, and blood pressure 120/90 mm Hg. The physical exam shows increased resonance to percussion, decreased breath sounds, and crackles at the lung base. Chest radiography shows signs of pulmonary hyperinflation. Spirometry shows a forced expiratory volume in the first second (FEV1) of 48%, a forced vital capacity (FVC) of 85%, and an FEV1/FVC ratio of 56%. According to these results, what is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old patient presents to the office for evaluation of a lesion on their upper arm that appeared a few months ago and has not healed. The patient appears healthful but has a history of cardiovascular disease. They state that their friend at the industrial ammunition factory where they work told them they should “get it looked at.” The patient admits to some nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea over the past year, but they state that they “feel fine now.” On physical examination, the lesion is an erythematous, scaly, ulcerated plaque on the flexor surface of their upper arm. The rest of the exam is within normal limits. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old patient complains of fatigue and pallor. They say symptoms that started several months ago and have been becoming more serious with time. They report that they have been exercising regularly and have been adhering to a strict vegan diet. The patient has no significant past medical history and takes no current medications. They deny any smoking history, alcohol use, or recreational drug use. They are tachycardic, but otherwise, their physical examination is unremarkable. A complete blood count (CBC) shows anemia with a low MCV (mean corpuscular volume), and a peripheral blood smear shows small erythrocytes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 47-year-old patient visits the outpatient clinic with complaints of heartburn and chest pain for the past 6 months. Their pain is retrosternal and was initially only associated with intake of solid foods, but it now occurs with liquids as well. Antacids do not relieve their pain anymore. They are worried about the pain as it is getting worse with time. They also had an unintentional weight loss of 2.7 kg (6 lb) during this period. Physical examination including the abdominal examination is normal. Laboratory investigations reveal: Hgb 10 mg/dL White blood cell total count 5 x 10^9/L Platelet count 168 x 10^9/ L Hematocrit 38% Red blood cell count 4.2 x 10^12/ L Esophagogastroduodenoscopy reveals an exophytic mass in the lower third of the esophagus with ulcerations and mucous plugs. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 10-month-old patient is brought to the clinic with a history of recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. Their parent reports that their wheezing is exacerbated by crying, feeding, and flexion of the neck, and is relieved by extension of the neck. Occasionally they vomit after feeding. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old patient presents to the office with complaints of intense anal pain every time they have a bowel movement. The pain has been present for the past 4 weeks, and it is dull and throbbing in nature. It is associated with mild bright red bleeding from the rectum that is aggravated during defecation. They have no relevant past medical history. When asked about their sexual history, they report practicing anal intercourse. The vital signs include heart rate 98/min, respiratory rate 16/min, temperature 37.6°C (99.7°F), and blood pressure 110/66 mm Hg. On physical examination, the anal sphincter tone is markedly increased, and it’s impossible to introduce the finger due to severe pain. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 43-year-old patient presents for a routine checkup. They say they have been uncontrollably grimacing and smacking their lips for the past 2 months, and these symptoms have been getting progressively worse. Past medical history is significant for schizophrenia, managed medically with clozapine. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 44-year-old patient presents to a clinic for the evaluation of difficulty swallowing for the past few days. They say that they have noticed progressively worsening chest pain when they attempt to swallow solids or liquids. They work from a home office, have not had any recent sick contacts, and are currently not sexually active. Their medical history includes AIDS. Their current medications include emtricitabine, rilpivirine, and tenofovir. Their temperature is 38.1°C (100.6°F), pulse is 72/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 136/84 mm Hg. A physical examination is notable for a dry mouth with red mucosa and no distinct plaques or patches, and a supple neck with no masses or cervical lymphadenopathy. An esophagogastroduodenoscopy shows small white patches within the esophageal lumen. A biopsy of one of the lesions is performed and the microscopic appearance of the finding is shown below. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old patient presents to the office complaining of a sore throat, difficulty swallowing, and difficulty opening their mouth for the past 5 days. They state that they had symptoms like this before and "was given some antibiotics that made them feel better". They are up to date on their immunizations. On examination, their temperature is 39.5°C (103.2°F) and they have bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy. An oropharyngeal exam is difficult, because the patient finds it painful to fully open their mouth. However, you are able to view an erythematous pharynx as well as a large, unilateral lesion superior to the left tonsil. A rapid antigen detection test is negative. Which of the following is a serious complication of the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old nursing home staff presents to the emergency room with complaints of palpitations and chest pain for the past 2 days. They were working at the nursing home for the last year but have been trying to get into modeling for the last 6 months and trying hard to lose weight. They are a non-smoker and occasionally drink alcohol on weekends with friends. On examination, they appear well nourished and are in no distress. The blood pressure is 150/84 mm Hg and the pulse is 118/min. An ECG shows absent P waves. All other physical findings are normal. What is the probable diagnosis?

A 68-year-old patient from California presents for a routine checkup. They do not have any complaints. They say that they have tried to keep themselves healthy and active by jogging and gardening since their retirement at age 50. They add that they spend their mornings in the park and their afternoons in their garden. They have no significant medical history. The patient denies any smoking history and drinks alcohol occasionally. On physical examination, the following lesion is seen on their scalp (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old patient is brought by their parents to the office for bloody diarrhea and a seizure. The parents say they started having fever, abdominal pain, and diarrhea about 3 days ago, but the bloody diarrhea started 12 hours ago. The seizure was the last symptom to appear 3 hours ago, and it consisted of repetitive movement of arms and legs with loss of consciousness. Their 4-year-old sibling had a similar case with bloody diarrhea 2 weeks ago. Their vital signs include: blood pressure is 130/85 mm Hg, their respiratory rate is 25/min, their heart rate is 120/min, and their temperature is 39.2°C (102.6°F). On physical examination, they look pale and sleepy, the cardiopulmonary auscultation is normal, the abdomen is painful on palpation, and the skin assessment reveals the presence of disseminated pinpoint petechiae. The urinalysis show hematuria. The Coombs test is negative. The complete blood count results are as follows: Hemoglobin 7 g/dL Hematocrit 25 % Leukocyte count 17,000/mm3 Neutrophils 70% Bands 2% Eosinophils 1% Basophils 0% Lymphocytes 22% Monocytes 5% Platelet count 7,000/mm3 Their coagulation tests are as follows: Partial thromboplastin time (activated) 30 seconds Prothrombin time 12 seconds Reticulocyte count 1 % Thrombin time < 2 seconds deviation from control What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old patient presents with exertional dyspnea and fatigue for the past 3 months. Their past medical history is significant for multiple episodes of mild diarrhea for many years, which was earlier diagnosed as irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). They deny any current significant gastrointestinal symptoms. The patient is afebrile and vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination reveals oral aphthous ulcers and mild conjunctival pallor. Abdominal examination is unremarkable. There is a rash present on the peripheral extremities bilaterally (see image). Laboratory findings are significant for evidence of microcytic hypochromic anemia. FOBT is negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

An 82-year-old patient presents with 2 months of foul-smelling, greasy diarrhea. They say that they also have felt very tired recently and have had some associated bloating and flatus. They deny any recent abdominal pain, nausea, melena, hematochezia, or vomiting. They also deny any history of recent travel and states that their home has city water. Which of the following tests would be most appropriate to initially work up the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 35-year-old patient with a history of Crohn disease presents for a follow-up appointment. They say that lately, they have started to notice difficulty walking. They say that some of their friends have joked that they appear to be walking as if they were drunk. Past medical history is significant for Crohn disease diagnosed 2 years ago, managed with natalizumab for the past year because their intestinal symptoms have become severe and unresponsive to other therapies. On physical examination, there is gait and limb ataxia present. Strength is 4/5 in the right upper limb. A T1/T2 MRI of the brain is ordered and is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 50-year-old patient is evaluated for a 2-year history of intermittent, nonproductive, chronic cough, as well as mild dyspnea with exertion. They have a 20-pack-year history of smoking and are a current smoker. Their medical history is significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which they have controlled with diet and exercise. They also take lisinopril. On physical examination, blood pressure is 125/76 mm Hg, pulse rate is 78/min, respiratory rate is 15/min, oxygen saturation is 98% (breathing room air), and their BMI is 25 kg/m2. There is no jugular venous distention. Heart sounds are normal, and there is no murmur. Auscultation of the lungs reveals faint, bilateral wheezing. No peripheral edema is noted. The remainder of the examination is normal. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis for this patient?

A 54-year-old patient presents with increasing shortness of breath on exertion for the past few months. They also complain of associated fatigue and some balance issues. The patient denies swelling of their feet and difficulty breathing at night or while lying down. Physical examination is significant for conjunctival pallor. A peripheral blood smear reveals macrocytosis and hypersegmented granulocytes. Which of the following substances, if elevated in this patient’s blood, would support the diagnosis of vitamin B12 deficiency?

A 10-year-old patient with previously diagnosed sickle cell anemia presents to the emergency room with a low-grade fever, malaise, petechiae on their arms, and a rash on their face. They regularly take hydroxyurea and receive blood transfusions to treat their condition. Their blood tests show a hemoglobin of 4.0 g/dL, MCV of 87 fl, and 2% reticulocyte count. An attempted bone marrow biopsy was a dry, empty tap. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 18-month-old patient presents to the clinic with their parent for evaluation of a rash around the eyes and mouth. Their parent states that the rash appeared 2 weeks ago and seems to be very itchy because the patient scratches their eyes often. The patient is up to date on all of their vaccinations and is meeting all developmental milestones. They have a history of asthma that was recently diagnosed. On examination, the patient is playful and alert. They have scaly, erythematous skin surrounding both eyes and their mouth. Bilateral pupils are equal and reactive to light and accommodation, and conjunctiva is clear, with no evidence of jaundice or exudates. The pharynx and oral mucosa are within normal limits, and no lesions are present. Expiratory wheezes can be heard in the lower lung fields bilaterally. What is this most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 25-year-old patient of Mediterranean descent makes an appointment with their physician because their skin and sclera have become yellow. They complain of fatigue and fever that started at the same time icterus appeared. On examination, they are tachycardic and tachypneic. The oxygen (O2) saturation is < 90%. They have increased unconjugated bilirubin, hemoglobinemia, and an increased number of reticulocytes in the peripheral blood. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 10-year-old patient is brought to a pediatric clinic by their parents with pain and weakness in the lower extremities for the past 3 weeks. The patient’s parent says that they have been active until the weakness and pain started during their soccer practice sessions. They say they also experience muscle cramps, especially at night. Their parent adds that, recently, the patient constantly wakes up in the night to urinate and is noticeably thirsty most of the time. The patient denies any recent history of trauma to their legs. Their vaccinations are up to date and their family history is unremarkable. Their vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination is unremarkable. Laboratory findings are shown below: Laboratory test Serum potassium 3.3 mEq/L Serum magnesium 1.3 mEq/L Serum chloride 101 mEq/L pH 7.50 Pco2 38 mm Hg HCO3- 20 mEq/L Po2 88 mm Hg Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 35-year-old patient presents with a mass on the central part of their neck. They report it has been growing steadily for the past 2 weeks, and they have also been experiencing fatigue and recurrent fevers. No significant past medical history. The patient denies any smoking history, or alcohol or recreational drug use. They deny any recent travel in the previous 6 months. On physical examination, there are multiple enlarged submandibular and cervical lymph nodes that are firm, mobile, and non-tender. A biopsy of one of the lymph nodes is performed and shows predominantly lymphocytes and histiocytes present in a pattern ‘resembling popcorn’. A flow cytometry analysis demonstrates cells that are CD19 and CD20 positive and CD15 and CD30 negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 11-year-old patient presents to the office with their parent for the evaluation of weight loss, rash, and several weeks of bloating and diarrhea. The parent states that the patient’s parent had similar symptoms at their age. On physical examination, the patient is pale with dry mucous membranes. There is a vesicular rash on the bilateral lower extremities which they say is ‘very itchy’. Which of the following laboratory findings would confirm the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 50-year-old patient presents to the office with complaints of fever and chills for 4 weeks. They add that they are fatigued all the time and have generalized weakness. They have drenching night sweats and have had 2 episodes of non-bilious vomiting over the past few days. They traveled to the Netherlands for 4 days a month ago. Their symptoms started a few days after they returned home. Laboratory testing revealed the following: Hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL Hematocrit 29% Leukocyte count 2,950/mm3 Neutrophils 59% Bands 3% Eosinophils 1% Basophils 0% Lymphocytes 31% Monocytes 4% Platelet count 60,000/mm3 Unconjugated bilirubin 12 mg/dL Alanine aminotransferase 200 IU/L Aspartate aminotransferase 355 IU/L The peripheral blood smear showed basophilic ring- and pear-shaped structures inside many red cells and extracellular basophilic rings on Wright-Giemsa staining. Further evaluation revealed parasitemia and a few schistocytes, poikilocytes, and merozoites in tetrad formation. The findings are most consistent with which diagnosis?

A 5-year-old patient presents for a routine checkup. The patient's parents say they have been looking pale and tired lately. Their family history is unremarkable. Upon physical examination, several bruises are seen, as well as petechial bleeding on their limbs. A complete blood count shows leukocytosis with severe anemia and thrombocytopenia. A peripheral blood smear shows 35% blasts. Ultrasonography of the abdomen shows hepatosplenomegaly and a chest radiograph reveals a mediastinal mass. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 46-year-old patient presents with a 5-month history of worsening dry cough, occasional shortness of breath, and fatigue. They say they are now having trouble walking a full block. For the past week, they also have noticed bilateral swelling of the lower legs. They deny chest pain, fever, chills, syncope, or bloody sputum. Current vitals include: temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse 63/min, blood pressure 128/91 mm Hg and respiratory rate 15/min. On physical examination, there is elevated jugular venous pressure, decreased breath sounds bilaterally at the lung bases, and 1+ non-pitting edema bilaterally in the lower extremities. A chest X-ray demonstrates a slightly enlarged cardiac silhouette. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the diagnosis of this patient?

A 45-year-old patient presents to the emergency room with fever and headache. They recently had a middle ear infection. On physical examination, when the head is passively flexed towards the chest, then flexion of the knee is observed. In addition, they report that their headache increases after rotating their head horizontally. Lumbar puncture and CSF analysis were done. Which of the following laboratory findings would best represent your suspected diagnosis?

An 11-year-old patient complains of pain in the leg while playing. Blood pressure in the upper limb is 140/90 mm Hg and lower limbs are 110/70 mm Hg. There is a brachiofemoral delay in the pulse. Auscultation shows a loud S1, loud S2, and S4. There is a presence of an ejection systolic murmur in the interscapular area. Chest X-ray reveals the notching of the ribs. What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient? The text already used neutral language, referring to the individual as a "child" and later as a "patient", which is gender-neutral.

A 75-year-old patient is brought by a patrolman to the emergency department because of altered mental status. They were found wandering next to the highway. The patient was unable to answer questions and collapsed in transit. Their vitals are: temperature, 33.0°C (91.4°F); pulse, 40/min; respirations,12/min; blood pressure, 80/50 mm Hg; and oxygen saturation, 85% on room air. Physical examination shows decorticate posturing, incomprehensible speech, eyes opening to pain, dry hair, coarse and waxy skin, and non-pitting edema around the face and all extremities. Electrocardiogram shows sinus bradycardia. Laboratory studies show: Calcium 9.0 mg/dL Hematocrit 34% Potassium 4.0 mEq/L Sodium 120 mEq/L TSH 110.0 µU/mL Thyroxine (T4) 1.2 µg/dL Triiodothyronine (T3) 70 ng/dL Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 62-year-old patient is referred to a gastroenterologist because of difficulty swallowing for the past 5 months. They have difficulty swallowing both solid and liquid foods, but there is no associated pain. They deny any shortness of breath or swelling in their legs. They immigrated from South America 10 years ago. They are a non-smoker and do not drink alcohol. Their physical examination is unremarkable. A barium swallow study was ordered and the result is given below. Esophageal manometry confirms the diagnosis. What is the most likely underlying cause of this patient’s condition?

A 25-year-old patient presents to the emergency department after numerous episodes of vomiting. The patient states that they think they ‘ate something weird’ and has been vomiting for the past 48 hours. They say that they came to the hospital because the last few times they "threw up blood". They are hypotensive with a blood pressure of 90/55 mm Hg and a pulse of 120/min. After opening an intravenous line, a physical examination is performed which is normal except for mild epigastric tenderness. An immediate endoscopy is performed and a tear involving the mucosa and submucosa of the gastroesophageal junction is visualized. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 58-year-old patient presents with a lump on their neck. They say the mass gradually onset 2 months ago and has been progressively enlarging. They deny any pain, weight loss, fevers, chills, or night sweats. Past medical history is significant for HIV, diagnosed 5 years ago, managed on a new HAART regimen they just started. The patient is afebrile and vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows a 3 cm mobile firm mass on the left lateral side of the neck immediately below the level of the thyroid cartilage. A biopsy of the mass is performed and reveals atypical mononuclear cells in a background of eosinophils, plasma cells, histiocytes, atypical T-lymphocytes, and bilobed cells (shown in image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 40-year-old patient has complaints of dyspnea, cough, and arthritis in their ankle joints. A CT scan reveals multiple granulomas in both lungs, as well as bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy. On examination, cutaneous nodules over the trunk are found. Erythrocyte sedimentation rate, angiotensin-converting enzyme, and serum calcium levels are elevated. They are treated with steroids. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A pathologist receives a skin biopsy specimen from a patient who is suspected to have developed graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) following allogeneic stem-cell transplantation. The treating physician informs the pathologist that they are specifically concerned about the diagnosis as the patient developed skin lesions on the 90th-day post-transplantation and therefore, by definition, it should be considered a case of acute GVHD. However, the lesions clinically appear like those of chronic GVHD. The pathologist examines the slide under the microscope and confirms the diagnosis of chronic GVHD. Which of the following findings on skin biopsy is most likely to have helped the pathologist to confirm the diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to the office because they have been feeling weak. For the past 2 years, they have been urinating a considerable volume every time they go to the bathroom. They have no past medical history. Their heart rate is 86/min, respiratory rate is 15/min, temperature is 37.4°C (99.3°F), and blood pressure is 111/79 mm Hg. Laboratory studies are significant for the following: Calcium 13.8 mg/dL PTH 230 pg/mL Their complete metabolic panel is otherwise within normal limits. Imaging studies show subperiosteal resorption and osteoporosis. Scintigraphy reveals the most common pathologic condition associated with the patient’s diagnosis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 48-year-old patient with a history of osteoarthritis and hypertension presents to the office complaining of persistent abdominal pain for the last 2 months. They describe the pain as 'burning and achy' that is worse when they eat, which has led to a weight loss of 4.5 kg (10.0 lb). The patient is currently taking lisinopril and atenolol for their blood pressure and ibuprofen as needed for their osteoarthritis. Their temperature is 37.1°C (98.7°F), heart rate is 75/min, and blood pressure is 120/80 mm Hg. An endoscopy is performed and a gastric ulcer is visualized and biopsied. The biopsy reveals H. pylori infection. Which of the following is the most likely predisposing factor to this patient’s diagnosis?

A parent brings in their 7-year-old patient because they are worried about the patient's behavior after the teacher called. The patient's parent says they were told that the patient has not been doing their assignments and frequently tells their teachers that they forget about them. In addition, the patient tends to have a difficult time sitting still in class and frequently disrupts the other children. This behavior has been going on for about 8 months, but recently it worsened prompting the teacher to bring it to the parent's attention. The patient's parent was surprised to hear about these issues; however, they admit that they need to repeat themselves several times when asking the patient to complete their chores. The patient also has trouble sitting still when doing homework. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 60-year-old patient presents to their physician as part of their routine annual medical check-up. They have no specific complaints but mention that they have often experienced fatigue over the past few months. Their past medical history is noncontributory. On physical examination, their temperature is 37.2°C (98.8°F), pulse rate is 84/min, blood pressure is 130/86 mm Hg, and respiratory rate is 18/min. On general examination, mild pallor is present. Palpation of the abdomen reveals splenomegaly, which extends 6.35 cm (2.5 in) below the left costal margin. There is no hepatomegaly. Laboratory studies show the following values: Hemoglobin 9.7 g/dL Total leukocyte count 30,000/mm3 Granulocytes 83% Lymphocytes 10% Eosinophils 5% Basophils 1% Monocytes 1% Platelet count 700,000/mm3 The physician orders a bone marrow biopsy analysis of hematopoietic cells. The report shows the presence of a t(9;22)(q34; q11) translocation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 50-year-old patient presents to a physician with painless, black, severely swollen pustules on their left hand. Examination reveals extensive swelling around the wound. Microscopy reveals gram-positive bacilli with a bamboo stick appearance. Culture shows large, gray, non-hemolytic colonies with irregular borders. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with a headache, vertigo, confusion, and dyspnea. A relevant history cannot be obtained from the patient because they seem confused and give incoherent responses to questions. Their spouse says that they were cleaning the kitchen this morning until the curtains caught on fire earlier this morning from the stove’s flame. Their vitals include: pulse 100/min, respirations 20/min, blood pressure 130/80 mm Hg, oxygen saturation 97% on room air. On physical examination, the patient is oriented x 0. The skin has a bright cherry-red color. Laboratory testing shows: pH 7.35 PaO2 90 mm Hg pCO2 40 mm Hg HCO3- 26 mEq/L SpO2 97% Blood lactate 11 mmol/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 43-year-old patient with a history of chronic alcoholism presents with a chronic cough and dyspnea. They say they traveled to Asia about 4 months ago and their symptoms started shortly after they returned. Their temperature is 40.2°C (104.4°F) and pulse is 92/min. Physical examination reveals poor personal hygiene and a cough productive of foul blood-streaked sputum. Auscultation reveals decreased breath sounds on the right. A chest radiograph reveals an ill-defined circular lesion in the right middle lobe. Which of the following is true regarding this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 46-year-old patient presents to the clinic with a 2-week history of fever, fatigue, and coughing up blood. On questioning, they note that they have also experienced some weight loss over the past 4 months and a change in the color of their urine, with intermittent passage of dark-colored urine during that time. The patient does not have a prior history of cough or hemoptysis and has not been in contact with anyone with a chronic cough. The cough was originally productive of rust-colored sputum, but it has now progressed to the coughing up of blood and sputum at least twice daily. Sputum production is approximately 2 spoonfuls per coughing episode. Vital signs include: temperature 36.7°C (98.0°F), respiratory rate 42/min, and pulse 88/min. Physical examination reveals an anxious but tired-looking patient with mild respiratory distress and mild pallor. Laboratory and antibody tests are ordered and the findings include the following: Laboratory test Hematocrit 34% Hepatitis antibody test negative Hepatitis C antibody test negative 24-hour urinary protein 2 g Urine microscopy more than 5 RBC under high power microscopy Antibody test C-ANCA negative Anti MPO/P-ANCA positive Serum urea 140 mg/dL Serum creatinine 2.8 mg/dL Renal biopsy shows glomerulonephritis with crescent formation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 30-year-old patient presents with restlessness and an inability to sit or lie down for the past 2 days. Past medical history is significant for schizophrenia, diagnosed 3 weeks ago and managed medically. Vital signs are a blood pressure of 140/90 mm Hg and a pulse of 96/min. On physical examination, the patient is fidgety and anxious but well-oriented. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 50-year-old farmer from Jamaica presents to their physician with a wart-like lesion on their left foot. They are a plantain farmer and often farm barefoot because of the pleasant climate. Physical examination reveals warty, cutaneous nodules that resemble the florets of cauliflower. On a KOH preparation, irregular, dark brown, yeast-like bodies with septae are noted. Culture on Sabouraud agar reveals sclerotic bodies. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 53-year-old patient is being evaluated for a 3-week history of fatigue, difficulty to concentrate, dyspnea with exertion, dizziness, and digital pain that improves with cold. They have smoked half a pack of cigarettes a day since they were 20. Their current medical history involves hypertension. They take enalapril daily. The vital signs include a blood pressure of 131/82 mm Hg, a heart rate of 95/min, and a temperature of 36.9°C (98.4°F). On physical examination, splenomegaly is found. A complete blood count reveals thrombocytosis of 700,000 cells/m3. Lab work further shows decreased serum iron, iron saturation, and serum ferritin and increased total iron binding capacity. A blood smear reveals an increased number of abnormal platelets, and a bone marrow aspirate confirmed the presence of dysplastic megakaryocytes. A mutation on their chromosome 9 confirms the physician’s suspicion of a certain clonal myeloproliferative disease. The patient is started on hydroxyurea. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 75-year-old patient presents with sudden loss of vision. They say that they were reading when suddenly they were not able to see the print on half of the page. Their symptoms started 4 hours ago and are accompanied by a severe posterior headache. Vital signs reveal the following: blood pressure 119/76 mm Hg, pulse 89/min, SpO2 98% on room air. The patient was unable to recognize their relative when they arrived to see them. A noncontrast CT of the head shows no evidence of hemorrhagic stroke. What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 60-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by police officers because they were seen acting strangely in public. The patient was found talking nonsensically to the characters on cereal boxes in a grocery store. Past medical history is significant for multiple hospitalizations for alcohol-related injuries and alcohol withdrawal seizures. Vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, the patient is disheveled and oriented x1. Neurologic examination shows horizontal nystagmus and severe ataxia is also noted, that after interviewing the patient, they forget the face of persons and the questions asked shortly after they walk out the door. They, however, remember events from their distant past quite well. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 75-year-old patient is evaluated in the emergency department for increasing shortness of breath for the last 8 months. They also complain of a dry cough for the last 6 months. Initially, their shortness of breath occurs with exertion, but now they feel it at rest as well. They have no other complaints. They have a sedentary lifestyle and had a hip replacement surgery recently. The past medical history is significant for hypertension for which they are taking lisinopril. The patient is a lifetime non-smoker. The blood pressure is 135/85 mm Hg, pulse rate is 85/min, and the temperature is 36.6°C (97.9°F). Physical examination reveals fine inspiratory crackles and digital clubbing. A chest X-ray reveals peripheral reticular opacities associated with traction bronchiectasis predominantly at the lung bases. The pulmonary function test results reveal a decreased FEV1, a decreased FVC, and a preserved FEV1/FVC ratio. High-resolution CT scan of the chest is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 47-year-old alcoholic patient presents to the office for a 72-hour history of intense right hemithorax pain. They also complain of fever, chills, and sweating that started 10 days ago, as well as persistent coughing with abundant malodorous sputum. Chest radiography shows a round consolidation with hydro-aerial levels in the middle third of the right hemithorax. Sputum samples for a direct exam, culture, and bradykinin (BK) are sent. What is the correct diagnosis?

A 5-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their guardian because of multiple injuries. They say that the patient sustained these injuries while playing. Radiographic findings show multiple fractures in various stages of healing. Physical examination shows the findings in the image below. What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 55-year-old patient with a history of myocardial infarction 3 months ago presents with feelings of depression. They say that they have become detached from their friends and family and have daily feelings of hopelessness. They say they have started to avoid strenuous activities and are no longer going to their favorite bar where they used to spend a lot of time drinking with their friends. The patient says these symptoms have been ongoing for the past 6 weeks, and their partner is starting to worry about their behavior. They note that they continue to have nightmares that they are having another heart attack. They say they are even more jumpy than they used to be, and they startle very easily. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

An 82-year-old patient visits their primary care provider complaining of a vague cramping pain on the right side of their abdomen for the past 6 hours. They are also experiencing symptoms and had an episode of vomiting earlier today and two episodes yesterday. Past medical history includes third-degree heart block, gastroesophageal reflux disease, hypertension, hypothyroidism, and chronic cholecystitis with cholelithiasis. They are not a good candidate for cholecystectomy due to cardiac disease and are treated with analgesics and ursodeoxycholic acid. Their medications include chlorthalidone, omeprazole, levothyroxine, and occasional naproxen for pain. Vitals are normal. A supine abdominal X-ray reveals air in the gallbladder and biliary tree (saber sign), small bowel obstruction, and a large radiolucent gallstone impacted in the small bowel. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old patient presents with progressively worsening headache, photophobia, and intermittent fever that have lasted for 6 days. They say their headache is mostly frontal and radiates down their neck. They deny any recent history of blood transfusions, recent travel, or contact with animals. Their past medical history is unremarkable. They are sexually active with a single partner for the past 3 years. Their temperature is 38.5°C (101.3°F). On physical examination, they appear pale and diaphoretic. A fine erythematous rash is noted on the neck and forearms. A lumbar puncture is performed and CSF analysis reveals: Opening pressure: 300 mm H2O Erythrocytes: None Leukocytes: 72/mm3 Neutrophils: 10% Lymphocytes: 75% Mononuclear: 15% Protein: 100 mg/dL Glucose: 70 mg/dL Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 3-month-old patient presents for routine health maintenance. The patient has coarse facial features and stiff joint movements with restricted passive and active range of motion. They also have problems following objects with their eyes and seem not to focus on anything. On physical examination, the corneas are clouded, and the patient fails to meet any 3-month developmental milestones. Genetic testing and histopathology are performed and reveal failure of a cellular structure to phosphorylate mannose residues on glycoproteins. An electron microscopy image of one of this patient’s cells is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 13-year-old patient presents after losing consciousness during class 30 minutes ago. According to their friends, they were doing okay since morning, and nobody noticed anything abnormal. The patient’s mother says that they do not have any medical conditions. She also says that the patient has always been healthy but has recently lost weight even though they were eating as usual. Their vital signs are a blood pressure of 100/78 mm Hg, a pulse of 89/min, and a temperature of 37.2°C (99.0°F). Their breathing is rapid but shallow. Fingerstick glucose is 300 mg/dL. Blood is drawn for additional lab tests, and they are started on intravenous insulin and normal saline. Which of the following HLA subtypes is associated with this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old patient presents with yellow discoloration of their eyes and skin for the past week. They also say they have pain in the right upper quadrant for the past few days. They are fatigued constantly and have recently developed acute onset itching all over their body. The patient denies any allergies. Past medical history is significant for ulcerative colitis diagnosed 2 years ago, managed medically. They are vaccinated against hepatitis A and B and deny any recent travel abroad. There is scleral icterus present, and mild hepatosplenomegaly is noted. The remainder of the physical examination is unremarkable. Laboratory findings are significant for: Total bilirubin 3.4 mg/dL Prothrombin time 12 s Aspartate transaminase (AST) 158 IU/L Alanine transaminase (ALT) 1161 IU/L Alkaline phosphatase 502 IU/L Serum albumin 3.1 g/dL Perinuclear antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (p-ANCA) positive Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 6-month-old baby presents to their pediatrician for the evaluation of recurrent bacterial infections. They are currently well but have already been hospitalized multiple times due to their bacterial infections. Their blood pressure is 103/67 mm Hg and heart rate is 74/min. Physical examination reveals light-colored skin and silver hair. On examination of a peripheral blood smear, large cytoplasmic vacuoles containing microbes are found within the neutrophils. What diagnosis do these findings suggest?

A 33-year-old patient presents with yellowing of the eyes. They say symptoms onset acutely 3 days ago and have not improved. They say they have had similar episodes for the past 10 years. Each episode is self-limited, lasting no more than 3–5 days. The patient denies any recent history of nausea, weight loss, abdominal pain, light-colored stools, dark urine, or pruritus. Current medications are herbal supplements and a multivitamin. The patient is afebrile and vital signs are within normal limits. Their BMI is 32 kg/m2. Physical exam is unremarkable. Laboratory findings are significant for the following: Total bilirubin 3 mg/dL Direct bilirubin 0.2 mg/dL AST/ALT/Alkaline phosphatase Normal Hematocrit/lactate dehydrogenase (LDH)/haptoglobin Normal Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 38-year-old patient presents with fever and acute onset chest pain for the past 12 hours. They describe the pain as severe, sharp and stabbing in character, and localized to the retrosternal area. They also say the pain is worse when they breathe deeply or coughs. Past medical history is significant for recently diagnosed systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Their vital signs include: blood pressure 110/75 mm Hg, pulse 95/min, and temperature 38.0°C (100.4°F). Physical examination is significant for a friction rub heard best at the lower left sternal border. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 52-year-old African-American patient presents to the office complaining of difficulty swallowing for 1 week, and described it as "food getting stuck in their throat". Their discomfort is mainly for solid foods, and they do not have any problem with liquids. They further add that they have frequent heartburn and lost 5 pounds in the last month because of this discomfort. They sometimes take antacids to relieve their heartburn. Their past medical history is insignificant. They are an occasional drinker and smoke a half pack of cigarettes a day.
