On examination, their skin is shiny and taut especially around their lips and fingertips. A barium swallow study is ordered. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old patient who is a professional baseball player presents with stiffness in their hands. They say they are unable to bat as they would like and feel like they lack power in their swings. They also have noticed that they sometimes seem to be dragging their feet while walking, and their voice seems to have changed. On physical examination, strength is 3 out of 5 in the extensor and flexor muscle groups in both upper and lower limbs bilaterally. Sensation is intact. Widespread muscle fasciculations are noted. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 23-year-old patient presents with fatigue and increased daytime somnolence. They say their symptoms began gradually 6 months ago and have progressively worsened and have begun to interfere with their job as a computer programmer. They are also bothered by episodes of paralysis upon waking from naps and report visual hallucinations when falling asleep at night. They have been under the care of another physician for the past several months, who prescribed them the standard pharmacotherapy for their most likely diagnosis. However, they have continued to experience an incomplete remission of symptoms and have been advised against increasing the dose of their current medication because of an increased risk of adverse effects. Which of the following side effects is most closely associated with the standard drug treatment for this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient presents with fever, pain, and swelling of the right leg. They say that their right leg swelling has gradually worsened over the last 2 weeks. They have also noted worsening fatigue and anorexia. Two days ago, they developed a low-grade fever. Their past medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed 5 years ago and managed with metformin. Their temperature is 38.0°C (100.4°F), pulse is 110/min, blood pressure is 110/72 mm Hg, and respiratory rate is 16/min. On physical examination, there is a painful swelling of the right lower extremity extending to just below the knee joint. The overlying skin is tense, glossy, erythematous, and warm to touch. A diagnosis of cellulitis is established and appropriate antibiotics are started. Which of the following best describes the organism most likely responsible for this patient’s condition?

A 15-year-old patient is brought to the emergency room for evaluation of malaise, dyspnea, and yellow skin and sclera. On examination, they are tachycardic, tachypneic, and the O2 saturation is less than 90%. The levels of unconjugated bilirubin and hemoglobinemia are increased, and there is an increased number of reticulocytes in the peripheral blood. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 50-year-old patient presents with severe abdominal pain. Past medical history is significant for a peptic ulcer. Physical examination is limited because the patient will not allow abdominal palpation due to the pain. The attending makes a presumptive diagnosis of peritonitis. Which of the following non-invasive maneuvers would be most helpful in confirming the diagnosis of peritonitis in this patient?

A 36-year-old patient presents for a pre-employment health assessment. They have no complaints. Their last annual physical examination 8 months ago was normal. They have no significant past medical history. They are a nonsmoker and say they quit all alcohol consumption last year. A complete hepatic biochemistry panel is performed, which is significant for a serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP) level 5 times the upper limit of the normal range. Immunologic tests are positive for antimitochondrial antibodies. A liver biopsy is performed and reveals an inflammatory infiltrate surrounding the biliary ducts. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 25-year-old patient presents with slightly yellow discoloration of their skin and eyes. They say they have had multiple episodes with similar symptoms before. They deny any recent history of nausea, fatigue, fever, or change in bowel/bladder habits. No significant past medical history. The patient is afebrile and vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, they are jaundiced, and their sclera is icteric. Laboratory findings are significant only for a mild unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia. The remainder of laboratory results is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 54-year-old patient presents with fever, abdominal pain, nausea, and bloody diarrhea. They say that their symptoms started 36 hours ago and have not improved. Past medical history is significant for a left-leg abscess secondary to an injury they sustained from a fall 4 days ago while walking their dog. They have been taking clindamycin for this infection. In addition, they have long-standing gastroesophageal reflux disease, managed with omeprazole. Their vital signs include: temperature 38.5°C (101.3°F), respiratory rate 19/min, heart rate 90/min, and blood pressure 110/70 mm Hg. Which of the following is the best course of treatment for this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old patient is brought in to the office by their parents. They state that their child has recently been more irritable than usual, and they occasionally become pale and blue. Their parents note that they were diagnosed with a heart murmur, but it was never treated. Physical examination reveals a small child in distress. They are laying on the examination table with their knees drawn to their chest. Cardiac auscultation reveals a harsh, systolic ejection murmur that is best heard at the upper left sternal border. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 18-month-old patient is brought to the emergency room by their parent because of wheezing for 1 day. The baby has never had similar symptoms. They also have a runny nose and a cough. They are not feeding well. Their immunizations are up-to-date. Their rectal temperature is 38.8°C (101.8°F), the heart rate is 120/min, and the respiratory rate is 23/min. On examination, a clear nasal discharge is noticed with intercostal retractions. Chest auscultation reveals bilateral fine rales and diffuse fine wheezing. A chest X-ray is given in the exhibit. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old patient presents with an episodic history of swelling of the face, hands, and neck and a single episode of difficulty swallowing. They also have a history of frequent, severe abdominal pain. At the time of their visit, their blood pressure is 126/84 mm Hg, heart rate is 82/min, and respiratory rate is 15/min. Physical examination is unremarkable except for a swollen right hand as shown in the image below. Imaging studies are normal and do not reveal any cause of their pain. Their C1 inhibitor level is less than 6% of the reference value. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 24-year-old patient and their mother arrive for a psychiatric evaluation. She is concerned about their health and behavior ever since they dropped out of graduate school and moved back home 8 months ago. They are always very anxious and preoccupied with thoughts of school and getting a job. They also seem to behave very oddly at times such as wearing their winter jacket in summer. They say that they hear voices but they cannot understand what they are saying. When prompted they describe a plot to have them killed with poison seeping from the walls. Today, their heart rate is 90/min, respiratory rate is 17/min, blood pressure is 110/65 mm Hg, and temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F). On physical exam, they appear gaunt and anxious. Their heart has a regular rate and rhythm and their lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. CMP, CBC, and TSH are normal. A urine toxicology test is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old patient is brought to a pediatric clinic by their parent because they had difficulty swallowing for 4 days. They were diagnosed with asthma 3 months ago and have been using an inhaler as directed by the pediatrician. The patient does not have a fever or a cough and is not short of breath. They deny pain during swallowing. Their vital signs include: temperature 35.8℃ (96.5℉), respiratory rate 14/min, blood pressure 90/40 mm Hg, and pulse 80/min. The oral examination reveals a slightly raised white lesion over their tongue (as shown in the provided photograph) and oropharynx. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 9-year-old patient presents with dyspnea, palpitations, joint pain, and fever for the past week. They say that their symptoms started 2 weeks ago with bilateral knee pain which has shifted to both ankles over the past week. They say they noticed bilateral leg swelling since yesterday. Past medical history is significant for a severe sore throat, fever, chills, and myalgia 1 month ago which resolved after a week. Their vital signs include: respiratory rate 22/min, temperature 37.7°C (100.0°F), blood pressure 90/60 mm Hg, pulse 90/min, and SpO2 88% on room air. On physical examination, the patient is ill-appearing with pallor and bilateral pitting edema of legs. The apex beat is prominently located in the 5th intercostal space in the mid-axillary line. Crepitus is noted over both lung bases bilaterally. A loud 3/6 pansystolic murmur is heard at the apex radiating towards the axilla. S3 and S4 sounds are noted at the left sternal border and cardiac apex. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 4-month-old patient is brought in because they reject food and are losing weight. They had several upper respiratory tract infections during the last 2 months. Upon examination, hepatosplenomegaly is noted, as well as mild hypotonia. During the next few weeks, hepatosplenomegaly progresses, the patient fails to thrive, and they continue to reject food. They have a blood pressure of 100/70 mm Hg and heart rate of 84/min. Blood tests show pancytopenia and elevated levels of transaminases. Slit lamp examination shows bilateral cherry-red spots on the macula. Chest X-ray shows a reticulonodular pattern and calcified nodules. Biopsy of the liver shows foamy histiocytes. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old Hispanic patient presents to the office for a regular health checkup. They have been waiting for their hip replacement surgery for osteoarthritis, which they were diagnosed with for the past 5 years. They admit to having taken high doses of painkillers for hip pain management, but now they don’t provide any pain relief. Their vital signs include: blood pressure 110/70 mm Hg, pulse 78/min, temperature 36.7°C (98.1°F), and respiratory rate 10/min. On physical examination, there is a limited range of motion of their right hip. The laboratory results are as follows: Hemoglobin 12 g/dL Red blood cell 5.1 million cells/µL Hematocrit 45% Total leukocyte count 6,500 cells/µL Neutrophils 71% Lymphocyte 14% Monocytes 4% Eosinophil 11% Basophils 0% Platelets 240,000 cells/µL Urinalysis shows: pH 6.2 Color light yellow RBC 7–8/ HPF WBC 10-12 /HPF Protein 1+ Cast none Glucose absent Crystal none Ketone absent Nitrite negative 24-hr urine protein excretion 0.9 g Urine for culture No growth noted after 48 hours of inoculation at 37.0°C (98.6°F) What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 13-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department with respiratory distress, fever, and a productive cough. Past medical history is significant for a history of recurrent bronchopneumonia since the age of 5, managed conservatively with antibiotics and mucolytic therapy. The patient’s weight was normal at birth, but they suffered from a failure to thrive, although there was no neonatal history of chronic diarrhea or jaundice. Their current vitals are a respiratory rate of 26/min, a pulse of 96/min, a temperature of 38.8℃ (101.8°F), a blood pressure of 90/60 mm Hg, and oxygen saturation of 88% on room air. On physical examination, there is coarse crepitus bilaterally and both expiratory and inspiratory wheezing is present. The chest radiograph shows evidence of diffuse emphysema. A sweat chloride test and nitro tetrazolium test are both within normal limits. A complete blood count is significant for the following: WBC 26300/mm3 Neutrophils 62% Lymphocytes 36% Eosinophils 2% Total bilirubin 0.8 mg/dL Direct bilirubin 0.2 mg/dL SGOT 100 U/L SGPT 120 U/L ALP 200 U/L Results of serum protein electrophoresis are shown in the figure. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 70-year-old Caucasian patient presents with a 2-week history of blood-tinged sputum. Their past medical history is significant for peptic ulcer disease for which they underwent triple-drug therapy. They are a lifetime non-smoker and worked as a teacher before retiring at the age of 60 years. A review of systems is significant for a weight loss of 6.8 kg (15 lb) over the last 5 months. Their vitals include: blood pressure 135/85 mm Hg, temperature 37.7°C (99.9°F), pulse 95/min, and respiratory rate 18/min. Physical examination is unremarkable. A contrast CT scan of the chest shows an irregular mass in the peripheral region of the inferior lobe of the right lung. A CT-guided biopsy is performed and reveals malignant tissue architecture and gland formation with a significant amount of mucus. Which of the following is the most significant risk factor for this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 7-day-old newborn patient presents to the emergency department with a history of fever, irritability, and generalized erythema. During the first 2 days of clinical manifestations, the parents of the child tried to control the symptoms using acetaminophen; however, the newborn continued to be ill, and blisters were noticeable around the buttocks, hands, and feet. During the physical examination, the vital signs include body temperature 39.0°C (102.3°F), heart rate 130/min, and respiratory rate 45/min. Ears, nose, and oral mucosa preserved their integrity, while the skin presents with diffuse blanching erythema and flaccid blisters with a positive Nikolsky’s sign. What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 25-year-old construction worker presents to the office due to a yellowish discoloration of their skin and eyes for the past 2 weeks. They also complain of nausea and loss of appetite for the same duration. The past medical history is insignificant. They are a smoker, but recently has grown a distaste for smoking. The vital signs include: heart rate 83/min, respiratory rate 13/min, temperature 36.5°C (97.7°F), and blood pressure 111/74 mm Hg. On physical examination, there is mild hepatomegaly. The results of the hepatitis viral panel are as follows: Anti-HAV IgM positive HBsAg negative IgM anti-HBc negative Anti-HCV negative HCV-RNA negative Anti-HDV negative Anti-HEV negative What is the most common mode of transmission for this patient’s diagnosis?

A 26-year-old patient presents to the office complaining of persistent epigastric pain for the past 2 months. They state that their pain is worse a few hours after they eat. Their father had similar symptoms. Past medical history is insignificant. They are a non-smoker and do not drink alcohol. The vital signs include blood pressure 120/90 mm Hg, heart rate 83/min, and temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F). Physical examination is insignificant except for mild epigastric tenderness. A metabolic panel reveals the following: Serum sodium 136 mEq/L Serum potassium 4.2 mEq/L Calcium 13.2 mg/dL Bicarbonate 26 mEq/L Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy reveals multiple duodenal ulcers. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 56-year-old patient presents to the emergency room with severe substernal chest pain associated with a 2-hour history of breathlessness and sweating. An electrocardiogram shows an ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. Cardiac enzyme levels confirm a diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction. The patient is rushed to the catheter lab for angioplasty with stenting. The patient complains of recurrent chest pain in the ICU 56 hours post-angioplasty. Which of the following enzymes facilitates the patient’s diagnosis based on their current symptoms?

A 4-month-old neonate is brought to the pediatrician because of feeding problems and recurrent infections. They have a blood pressure of 104/65 mm Hg and heart rate of 91/min. On physical examination, they have a cleft palate, malformed jaw, structural cardiac abnormalities, and diminished cell-mediated responses. Laboratory investigations reveal hypocalcemia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 52-year-old patient seeks evaluation at a medical clinic with complaints of back pain and increased fatigue for 6 months. For the past week, the back pain has radiated to their legs and is stabbing in nature (7/10 in intensity). There are no associated paresthesias. They unintentionally lost 4.5 kg (10.0 lb) in the past 6 months. There is no history of trauma to the back. The past medical history is insignificant and they do not take any medications. The physical examination is normal. The laboratory results are as follows: Hemoglobin 10 g/dL Hematocrit 30% Mean corpuscular volume 80 fL Serum creatinine 1.5 mg/dL Serum total protein 9 g/dL Serum albumin 4.2 g/dL Serum calcium 11.2 mg/dL A peripheral blood smear shows normocytic normochromic cells. An X-ray reveals multiple osteolytic lesions in the vertebrae and long bones. Serum protein electrophoresis shows a monoclonal spike. A bone marrow biopsy shows increased plasma cells making up greater than 50% of the total cell population. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

On the 4th day of hospital admission due to pneumonia, a 69-year-old patient develops non-bloody diarrhea and abdominal pain. They are currently treated with ceftriaxone. Despite the resolution of fever after the first 2 days of admission, their temperature is now 38.5°C (101.3°F). On physical examination, they have mild generalized abdominal tenderness without abdominal guarding or rebound tenderness. Laboratory studies show re-elevation of leukocyte counts. Ceftriaxone is discontinued. Given the most likely diagnosis in this patient, which of the following is the most sensitive test?

A 20-year-old patient comes to the clinic complaining of fever and a sore throat for 5 days. They receive oral penicillin from their primary doctor. After a day of antibiotic treatment, they developed gross hematuria. As a child, they recall having multiple episodes of hematuria. The vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, pharyngeal edema and cervical lymphadenopathy are present. Their laboratory examination reveals the following: WBC 11,000/mm3 Neutrophils 76% Lymphocytes 23% Eosinophils 1% Platelets 150,000/mm3 Hemoglobin 14 g/dL Hct 41.2% BUN 16 mg/dL Creatinine 0.9 mg/dL ASO titer 100 Urinalysis shows hematuria but no proteinuria. Immunofluorescence shows granular IgA immune complex deposits in the mesangium. Hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and HIV serology are negative. ASO titers and C3 levels are within normal limits. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient presents to the emergency room complaining of left shoulder pain for several weeks. They say that the pain often worsens when they try to sleep on their left side. Although they tried several pain medications, none of the pain medications helped. They are an amateur tennis player who practices on weekends. They deny any trauma during their practice sessions. On examination of the shoulder joint, severe tenderness was present localized to the greater tuberosity of the left shoulder joint along with biceps tendon tenderness over the bicipital groove. The range of motion was limited to the left side. An X-ray of the joint showed narrowing of the acromiohumeral space with sclerosis and spurring of the acromion. Routine blood test results are normal except for the rheumatoid factor, which is positive. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient is brought into the emergency department by their spouse for slurred speech and right-sided weakness. The patient has a significant past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. The spouse reports the patient went to bed last night normally but woke up this morning with the symptoms mentioned. Physical examination shows right-sided hemiparesis along with the loss of vibration and proprioception. Cranial nerve examination shows a deviated tongue to the left. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old patient presents to the clinic for a recurrent rash that has remitted and relapsed over the last 2 years. The patient states that they have tried multiple home remedies when they have flare-ups, to no avail. The patient is wary of medical care and has not seen a doctor in at least 15 years. On examination, they have multiple disc-shaped, erythematous lesions on their neck, progressing into their hairline. The patient notes no other symptoms. Lab work is performed and is positive for antinuclear antibodies. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 12-year-old patient comes to the clinic with a grossly enlarged abdomen. They have a history of frequent episodes of weakness, sweating, and pallor that are eliminated by eating. Their development has been slow. They started to walk unassisted at 2 years and were not performing well at school. Physical examination reveals a blood pressure of 100/60 mm Hg, heart rate of 80/min, and temperature of 36.9°C (98.4℉). On physical examination, the liver is enlarged, firm, and palpable up to the pelvis. The spleen and kidney are not palpable. Laboratory investigation reveals low blood glucose and pH with high lactate, triglycerides, ketones, and free fatty acids. The liver biopsy revealed high glycogen content. Hepatic glycogen structure was normal. The enzyme assay performed on the biopsy tissue revealed very low glucose-6-phosphatase levels. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 56-year-old patient comes to the clinic for a check-up. They present with a 1-year history of worsening shortness of breath and weight loss. They are a former construction worker, and worked in a steel mill when they were in high school. They are an active smoker with a 36-pack-year smoking history. The blood pressure is 130/78 mm Hg, pulse rate is 90/min, respiratory rate is 17/min, and the BMI is 31 kg/m2. The patient is afebrile and the oxygen saturation at rest is 95% on room air. The pulmonary examination reveals a mildly prolonged expiratory phase, and no wheezing or crackles are auscultated. A pulmonary function test is recommended for the patient, and 2 weeks later they return with a report that shows an FEV1/FVC ratio of 60% and FEV1 of 50% of the predicted value. The lung volumes show a total lung capacity of 110% of predicted value, a residual volume of 115% of predicted value, and a DLCO of 60% of predicted value. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old patient is hospitalized due to depression and suicidal ideation. They have a 5-year history of chaotic relationships that last only a few short weeks or months. Each relationship has left them feeling abandoned, empty, and extremely upset. During these periods, the patient confesses to shopping and making big purchases on impulse. They say they get bored easily and move on to the next adventure. The patient denies any changes in appetite, energy level, or concentration. On examination, multiple linear lacerations of varying phases of healing were noted on their forearms and trunk. Following consultation, they praise physicians to be ‘the best people on the planet’, but when the nurse came in to take their blood, they furiously stated that ‘all nurses are incompetent and cruel’. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old patient presents to the office with complaints of perianal pain during defecation and perineal heaviness for 1 month. They also complain of discharge around the anus, and bright red bleeding during defecation. The patient provides a history of having a sexual relationship with others without using any methods of protection. The physical examination demonstrates edematous verrucous anal folds that are of hard consistency and painful to the touch. A proctosigmoidoscopy reveals an anal canal ulcer with well defined, indurated borders on a white background. A biopsy is taken and the results are pending. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient presents for a routine checkup. They say they have arthralgia in their hands and wrists. No significant past medical history. The patient takes no current medications. Family history is significant for their grandfather who died of liver cirrhosis from an unknown disease. They deny any alcohol use or alcoholism in the family. The patient is afebrile and vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, there is bronze hyperpigmentation of the skin and significant hepatomegaly is noted. The remainder of the exam is unremarkable. Which of the following is true about this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old patient presents with a painless neck mass that has gradually increased in size. The mass is anteromedial to the right sternocleidomastoid muscle and has been present for 3 years. The mass increased in size and became more tender following an upper respiratory infection. An ultrasound of the neck identifies a single, round cystic mass with uniform, low echogenicity, and no internal septations. A contrast-enhanced CT scan of the neck shows a homogeneous mass with low attenuation centrally and with smooth rim enhancement. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 53-year-old patient presents to the office complaining of persistent abdominal pain. They state that they have gained 4.5 kg (10.0 lb) because the pain is only relieved by eating. The patient also admits that they have had numerous loose, foul-smelling stools over the last few weeks with associated nausea. They have taken some over the counter antacids without relief or change in symptoms. Their blood pressure is 132/76 mm Hg, respiratory rate is 14/min, and heart rate is 75/min. Physical examination reveals mild tenderness to palpation of the upper abdomen. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old patient presents with loose stools and left lower quadrant abdominal pain. They say they pass 8–10 loose stools per day. The volume of each bowel movement is small and appears mucoid with occasional blood. The patient reports a 20-pack-year smoking history. They also say they recently traveled abroad about 3 weeks ago to Egypt. The vital signs include: blood pressure 120/76 mm Hg, pulse 74/min, and temperature 36.5°C (97.8°F). On physical examination, mild to moderate tenderness to palpation in the left lower quadrant with no rebound or guarding is present. Rectal examination shows the presence of perianal skin ulcers. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 4-month-old adopted infant is brought to the pediatrician because of feeding problems and recurrent fungal and bacterial infections. Their family has almost no background information about the infant. They report that the infant is a little fragile and looks different compared to other infants their age. Physical evaluation reveals a cleft lip with intact hard and soft palate and mild jaw malformation. An echocardiogram reveals an interrupted aortic arch. Further investigation reveals leukopenia and mild hypocalcemia. These findings support a diagnosis of which of the following?

A 60-year-old patient, who was a coal miner for more than 15 years presents with complaints of a cough and shortness of breath. Their cough started 6 years ago and is dry and persistent. The shortness of breath started 4 months ago and is exacerbated by physical activity. When interviewed, their physician discovers that they don’t take any safety measures when working in the mines. Vital signs include: heart rate 85/min, respiratory rate 32/min, and blood pressure 125/90 mm Hg. On physical examination, there are diminished respiratory sounds on both sides. On their chest X-ray, interstitial fibrosis with reticulonodular infiltrate with honeycombing is found on both sides. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-month-old patient is brought in by their parents with an 8-month history of diarrhea, abdominal tenderness and concomitant failure to thrive. The pediatric attending physician believes that Crohn’s disease is the best explanation of this patient’s symptoms. Based on the pediatric attending physician’s experience, the pretest probability of this diagnosis is estimated at 40%. According to Fagan nomogram (see image). If the likelihood ratio of a negative test result (LR-) for Crohn’s disease is 0.04, what is the chance that this is the correct diagnosis in this patient with a negative test result?

A 27-year-old patient from Southern California presents with progressive chest pain, non-productive cough, and shortness of breath for the past 24 hours. They deny any similar symptoms in the past. They deny any family history of cardiac disease, recent travel, or exposure to sick contacts. Their temperature is 38.5°C (101.3°F), pulse is 105/min, blood pressure is 108/78 mm Hg, and the respiratory rate is 32/min. On physical examination, the patient is cachectic and ill-appearing. Bilateral pleural friction rubs are present on pulmonary auscultation. Antecubital track marks are noted bilaterally. An echocardiogram is performed and results are shown below. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 35-year-old patient presents with pain in their feet during exercise and at rest. They say that their fingers and toes become pale upon exposure to cold temperatures. They have an extensive smoking history, but no history of diabetes mellitus nor hyperlipidemia. They used to exercise frequently but have stopped because of the symptoms. On inspection, a tiny ulcer is found on their toe. On laboratory analysis, their blood sugar, blood pressure, and lipids are all within the normal range. Which is the most probable diagnosis?

A 42-year-old patient is in the hospital recovering from a cholecystectomy performed 3 days ago that was complicated by cholangitis. They are being treated with IV piperacillin-tazobactam. They call the nurse to their room because they say that their heart is racing. They also demand that someone come in to clean the pile of garbage off of the floor because it is attracting flies. Their pulse is 112/min, respiratory rate is 20/min, temperature is 38.0°C (100.4°F), and blood pressure is 150/90 mm Hg. On physical examination, the patient appears sweaty, distressed, and unable to remain still. They are oriented to person, but not place or time. Palpation of the abdomen shows no tenderness, rebound, or guarding. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 6-month-old patient presents to a pediatrician for the evaluation of recurrent bacterial infections. They have a history of a variety of bacterial infections since birth. Physical examination reveals light-colored skin with silver-colored hair. The pediatrician suspects an immunodeficiency disorder and decides to order several tests. Study of the patient's neutrophils reveals that they contain large cytoplasmic vacuoles. Genetic studies show a mutation in the LYST gene. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 34-year-old patient with no significant prior medical history presents to the clinic with several days of bloody stool. They also complain of constipation and straining, but they have no other symptoms. They have no family history of colorectal cancer or inflammatory bowel disease. They do not smoke or drink alcohol. Their vital signs are as follows: blood pressure is 121/81 mm Hg, heart rate is 77/min, and respiratory rate is 15/min. There is no abdominal discomfort on physical exam, and a digital rectal exam reveals bright red blood. Of the following, which is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old patient presents with progressive hearing loss for the past 4 months. They say that they aren’t hearing high frequency sounds like they used to, especially in large rooms. Their past medical history shows significant bilateral lens dislocations 6 months ago. Family history reveals that their mother had chronic hematuria and their grandfather suffered from corneal dystrophy and died from renal failure at age 51. The vital signs include: blood pressure 145/95 mm Hg, pulse 78/min, and respiratory rate 19/min. On physical examination, the patient has mild to moderate bilateral sensorineural high-frequency hearing loss. A slit-lamp examination is shown in the exhibit (see image). The remainder of the exam is unremarkable. Laboratory findings are significant for microscopic hematuria. Which of the following tests would most likely confirm the diagnosis in this patient?

A 64-year-old patient is admitted with a history of altered mental status. They were in their usual state of health until a few days ago when they started to become confused, lethargic, forgetful, and repeating the same questions. Over the last few days, they sometimes appear perfectly normal, and, at other times, they have difficulty recognizing their family members. Yesterday, they were screaming that the room was filled with snakes. Past medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, managed medically, and chronic kidney disease, for which they undergo regular hemodialysis on alternate days. There is no history of smoking, alcohol use, or illicit drug use. Their vitals include: blood pressure 129/88 mm Hg, pulse 112/min, temperature 38.2°C (100.8°F), and respiratory rate 20/min. The patient is oriented only to person and place. Their mini-mental state examination (MMSE) score is 18/30, where they had difficulty performing basic arithmetic calculations and recalled only 1 out of 3 objects. Nuchal rigidity is absent. Muscle strength is 5/5 bilaterally. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

clinical_context: A 12-year-old patient presents with progressive clumsiness and difficulty walking. They walk like a 'drunken-person' and have experienced frequent falls. They were born at term and have gone through normal developmental milestones. Their vaccination profile is up to date. They deny fever, chills, nausea, vomiting, chest pain, and shortness of breath. They have no history of alcohol use or illicit drug use. Their elder sibling experienced the same symptoms. The physical examination reveals normal higher mental functions. Their extraocular movements are normal. Their speech is mildly dysarthric. Their muscle tone and strength in all 4 limbs are normal. Their ankle reflexes are absent bilaterally with positive Babinski’s signs. Both vibration and proprioception are absent bilaterally. When they are asked to stand with their eyes closed and with both feet close together, they sway from side to side, unable to stand still. X-ray results show mild scoliosis. Electrocardiogram results show widespread T-wave inversions. Their fasting blood glucose level is 143 mg/dL. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old patient with no significant past medical history, social history, or family history presents to their pediatrician with itching in their groin. They say this started during summer workouts leading up to this season. They deny having any rash anywhere else on their body. The blood pressure is 123/78 mm Hg, pulse is 67/min, respiratory rate is 15/min, and temperature is 38.1°C (98.7°F). Physical examination reveals an erythematous, well-demarcated patch with peripheral scale on the left thigh, pubic region, and perineum. There is no apparent genital involvement with the rash. How can you confirm the suspected diagnosis?

A 42-year-old patient comes to their physician with a history of fever, non-bloody diarrhea, and headache for 10 days. They also complain of anorexia and abdominal pain. They returned from a trip to India 3 weeks ago. Their temperature is 40.0°C (104.0°F), pulse is 65/min, respirations are 15/min, and blood pressure is 135/80 mm Hg. They have developed a blanchable rash on their chest and trunk. A photograph of the rash is shown. Examination of the heart, lungs, and abdomen show no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 15 g/dL Mean corpuscular volume 95 μm3 White blood cell count 3400/mm3 Percent segmented neutrophils 40% Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 51-year-old patient presents for a routine check-up. They have no complaints. At their last annual visit, their physical and laboratory tests were unremarkable. Their past medical history is significant for hypercholesterolemia, well managed with rosuvastatin, and hypertension, well managed with hydrochlorothiazide. Their current medications also include aspirin. The patient is afebrile, and their vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination is unremarkable. Their laboratory tests are significant for the following: WBC 29,500/mm3 Hematocrit 26.1% Hemoglobin 9.1 g/dL Platelet count 298,000/mm3 A peripheral blood smear and differential shows 92% small normocytic lymphocytes. The patient’s diagnosis is confirmed by bone marrow biopsy and flow cytometry. They are monitored through regular follow-up visits. Three years after the initial diagnosis, the patient presents with swollen cervical and axillary lymph nodes, unintentional weight loss of 4.5 kg (approx. 10 lb), and “rib pain” on their right side. On physical examination, there is palpable, firm, non-tender cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy bilaterally. They also have moderate splenomegaly, which, when palpated, elicits pain. Which of the following is the best treatment for this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 10-year-old patient is brought in by their parent with increasing abdominal pain for the past week. The patient’s parent says they have been almost constantly nauseous over that time. They deny any change in their bowel habits, fever, chills, sick contacts or recent travel. The patient has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. The patient is at the 90th percentile for height and weight and has been meeting all developmental milestones. The temperature is 36.8℃ (98.2℉). On physical examination, the patient’s abdomen is asymmetrically distended. Bowel sounds are normoactive. No lymphadenopathy is noted. A cardiopulmonary examination is unremarkable. Palpation of the right flank and right iliac fossa reveals a 10 × 10 cm firm mass which is immobile and tender. The laboratory findings are significant for the following: Hemoglobin 10 g/dL Mean corpuscular volume 88 μm3 Leukocyte count 8,000/mm3 Platelet count 150,000/mm3 Serum creatinine 1.1 mg/dL Serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) 1,000 U/L An ultrasound-guided needle biopsy of the flank mass was performed, and the histopathologic findings are shown in the exhibit (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 63-year-old patient presents to the physician with fever for 5 days. They have had increasing fatigue and dyspnea for the past 2 months. During this time, they have lost 3 kg (6.6 lb). They received outpatient treatment for pneumonia last month. They had urinary tract infection 2 weeks ago. They take no other medications other than daily low dose aspirin and recent oral antibiotics. They do not smoke or drink alcohol. The vital signs include: temperature 38.5°C (101.3°F), pulse 93/min, respiration rate 18/min, and blood pressure 110/65 mm Hg. On physical examination, they have petechiae distally on the lower extremities and several purpura on the trunk and extremities. Several enlarged lymph nodes are detected in the axillary and cervical regions on both sides. The examination of the lungs, heart, and abdomen shows no abnormalities. The laboratory test results are as follows: Hemoglobin 10 g/dL Mean corpuscular volume 90 μm3 Leukocyte count 18,000/mm3 Platelet count 40,000/mm3 A Giemsa-stained peripheral blood smear is shown by the image. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-month-old African American patient is brought to the emergency department because of fever, lethargy, and lack of appetite for 6 days. The patient's parent says they fell off the changing table 10 days ago and landed on their left side, which they say has been tender since then. Their vital signs include: temperature 38.0°C (100.4°F), blood pressure 85/41 mm Hg, pulse 132/min. Physical examination reveals conjunctival pallor and reduced range of motion at the left hip. C-reactive protein (CRP) is raised. A magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan shows signs of infection in the medullary canal of the left femoral bone and surrounding soft tissues. Blood cultures are positive for Salmonella. Which of the following would most likely confirm the underlying diagnosis in this patient?

A 52-year-old patient presents to the urgent care center with several hours of worsening abdominal discomfort with radiation to the back. The patient also complains of malaise, chills, nausea, and vomiting. Social history is notable for alcoholism. On physical exam, they are febrile to 39.5°C (103.1°F), and they are diffusely tender to abdominal palpation. Complete blood count is notable for 13,500 white blood cells, bilirubin 2.1, lipase 842, and amylase 3,210. Given the following options, what is the most likely diagnosis?

A 9-year-old patient is brought to their pediatrician by their parent for the evaluation of recent-onset seizures. They have had 2 episodes of generalized tonic-clonic seizures in the past 3 days. Each episode lasted for 1–2 minutes and aborted spontaneously. There is no history of fever, headache, altered behavior, diarrhea, vomiting, or previous seizure episodes. Past medical history is unremarkable. Physical examination reveals: blood pressure 102/64 mm Hg, heart rate 89/min, respiratory rate 16/min, and temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F). They look anxious but oriented to time and space. Multiple flat hyperpigmented spots are present over their body, each more than 5 mm in diameter. Axillary freckling is present. Cranial nerves are intact. Muscle strength is normal in all 4 limbs with a normal sensory examination. Gait is normal. An eye examination is shown in the exhibit. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old patient presents to their family physician because of sinusitis and nasal drainage for 3 months. The nasal drainage is purulent and occasionally hemorrhagic. They have only temporary improvement after trying multiple over the counter medications. Over the last 2 weeks, they also have fatigue and joint pain, mainly affecting the ankles, knees, and wrists. Vital signs include: temperature 36.9°C (98.4°F), blood pressure 142/91 mm Hg, and pulse 82/min. On examination, there is inflammation and bleeding of the nasal mucosa, along with tenderness to percussion over the maxillary sinuses. Urine dipstick reveals 4+ microscopic hematuria and 2+ proteinuria. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient comes to the office complaining of a dry mouth for the past few months. They have to drink water more frequently, as they find it difficult to chew and swallow solid foods. They have to wake up 3–5 times each night to drink due to intense thirst. They also complain of a foreign body sensation in both the eyes for the past month. They have had no joint pain, fever, weight loss, or urinary or bowel changes. They do not smoke cigarettes but drink alcohol socially. Their mother has rheumatoid arthritis for which they take methotrexate, and their father died of carcinoma 7 years ago. Their temperature is 36.7°C (98°F), blood pressure is 130/75 mm Hg, pulse is 80/min, respirations are 14/min, and BMI is 28 kg/m2. On examination, the eyes and oral cavity appear dry, and dental caries are present. No lymphadenopathy is noted. Cardiopulmonary and abdominal examinations are negative. Laboratory results are shown below: Complete blood count: Hemoglobin 10 g/dL Leukocytes 13,500/mm3 Platelets 170,000/mm3 ESR 65 mm/hr Antinuclear antibody Positive Rheumatoid factor Positive Anti dsDNA Negative Anti Ro Positive Anti-CCP Negative Anti Jo 1 Negative Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old patient presents to their family physician with recurrent retrosternal chest pain. They have had similar episodes for the past 7 months along with difficulty swallowing solid as well as liquid food. They recently completed an 8-week course of a proton pump inhibitor, but they are still bothered by the feeling that food gets stuck down their 'food pipe'. Their pain is not related to exertion. They deny any history of acid reflux disease. Their blood pressure is 125/81 mm Hg, respirations are 21/min, pulse is 78/min, and temperature is 36.7°C (98.1°F). They currently do not have pain. A barium swallow X-ray image is normal. Which of the following test would aid in the diagnosis of this patient's condition?

A 19-year-old college student is brought to the emergency department with persistent vomiting overnight. They spent all day drinking beer yesterday at a college party according to their friends. They appear to be in shock and when asked about vomiting, they say that they vomited up blood about an hour ago. At the hospital, their vomit contains streaks of blood. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), respirations are 15/min, pulse is 107/min, and blood pressure is 90/68 mm Hg. A physical examination is performed and is within normal limits. Intravenous fluids are started and a blood sample is drawn for typing and cross-matching. An immediate upper gastrointestinal endoscopy reveals a longitudinal mucosal tear in the distal esophagus. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their spouse with complaints of sudden-onset slurring for the past hour. They are also having difficulty holding things with their right hand. They deny fever, head trauma, diplopia, vertigo, walking difficulties, nausea, and vomiting. Past medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and hypercholesterolemia for which they take a baby aspirin, metformin, ramipril, and simvastatin. They have a 23-pack-year cigarette smoking history. Their blood pressure is 148/96 mm Hg, the heart rate is 84/min, and the temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F). On physical examination, extraocular movements are intact. The patient is dysarthric, but their higher mental functions are intact. There is a right-sided facial weakness with preserved forehead wrinkling. Their gag reflex is weak. Muscle strength is mildly reduced in the right hand. They have difficulty performing skilled movements with their right hand, especially writing, and have difficulty touching far objects with their index finger. They are able to walk without difficulty. Pinprick and proprioception sensation is intact. A head CT scan is within normal limits. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old patient presents to the pediatrician with their parents. They are fully vaccinated and met most developmental milestones. Their fine motor milestones are delayed; at present, they cannot eat by themselves and have difficulty in self-dressing. Their intelligence quotient (IQ) is 65. They listen quietly while spoken to and engage in play with their classmates. They neither talk excessively nor remain mute, but engage in normal social conversation. There is no history of seizures and they are not on any long-term medical treatment. On physical examination, their vital signs are stable. Their height and weight are normal for their age, but their occipitofrontal circumference is less than the 3rd percentile for their age. Their neurologic examination is also normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old patient presents to the clinic with chronic abdominal discomfort and cramping. They seek medical attention now as they are concerned about the diarrhea that they have developed that is occasionally mixed with tiny streaks of blood. Their medical history is significant for lactose intolerance and asthma. They have a family history of wheat allergy and reports that they have tried to make themselves vomit on several occasions to lose weight. After counseling the patient about the dangers of bulimia, physical examination reveals the rectum is red, inflamed, tender, and a perirectal abscess is seen draining purulent material. Colonoscopy demonstrates scattered mucosal lesions involving the colon and terminal ileum. A complete blood count is given below: Hb%: 10 gm/dL Total count (WBC): 12,500/mm3 Differential count: Neutrophils: 50% Lymphocytes: 40% Monocytes: 5% ESR: 22 mm/hr What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient is brought to the office at the insistence of their fiancé to be evaluated for auditory hallucinations for the past 8 months. The patient's fiancé tells the physician that the patient often mentions that they can hear their own thoughts speaking aloud to them. The hallucinations have occurred intermittently for at least 1-month periods. Past medical history is significant for hypertension. Their medications include lisinopril and a daily multivitamin, both of which they frequently neglect. They lost their security job 7 months ago after failing to report to work on time. The patient's vital signs include: blood pressure 132/82 mm Hg; pulse 72/min; respiratory rate 18/min, and temperature 36.7°C (98.1°F). On physical examination, the patient has a flat affect and their focus fluctuates from the window to the door. They are disheveled with a foul smell. They have difficulty focusing on the discussion and do not quite understand what is happening around them. A urine toxicology screen is negative. Which of the following is the correct diagnosis for this patient?

A new parent brings in their 2-week-old patient because of a painful itchy rash on their trunk. Vital signs are within normal limits. A basic chemistry panel reveal sodium 135 mmol/L, potassium 4.1 mmol/L, chloride 107 mmol/L, carbon dioxide 22, blood urea nitrogen 30 mg/dL, creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, and glucose 108 mg/dL. On physical examination of the newborn, there are confluent erythematous patches with tiny vesicles and scaling. Their parent notes that they have been bathing the patient twice a day. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An unconscious middle-aged patient is brought to the emergency department. They are actively bleeding from the rectum. They have no past medical history. At the hospital, their pulse is 110/min, the blood pressure is 90/60 mm Hg, the respirations are 26/min, and the oxygen saturation is 96% at room air. Their extremities are cold. Resuscitation is started with IV fluids and cross-matched blood arranged. Their vitals are stabilized after resuscitation and blood transfusion. Their hemoglobin is 7.6 g/dL, hematocrit is 30%, BUN is 33 mg/dL, and PT/aPTT is within normal limits. A nasogastric tube is inserted, which drains bile without blood. Rectal examination and proctoscopy reveal massive active bleeding, without any obvious hemorrhoids or fissure. The physician estimates the rate of bleeding at 2-3 mL/min. What is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 10-year-old patient is brought to the pediatric clinic because of persistent sinus infections. For the past 5 years, they have had multiple sinus and upper respiratory infections. They have also had recurrent diarrhea throughout childhood. Their temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), the heart rate is 90/min, the respirations are 16/min, and the blood pressure is 125/75 mm Hg. Laboratory studies show abnormally low levels of one immunoglobulin isotype but normal levels of others. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old patient presents to their family doctor worried that they might have a heart condition. For the past 7 months, they have been having short panic attacks where they feel short of breath, sweaty, and feel like their heart wants to jump out of their chest. During these attacks, they feel like they ‘are going crazy’. They have now mapped out all of the places they have had an attack such as the subway, the crowded pharmacy near their house, and an elevator at their work that is especially slow and poorly lit. They actively avoid these areas to prevent an additional episode. They are afraid that during these attacks they may not be able to get the help they need or escape if needed. No significant past medical history. The patient takes no current medications. Their grandfather died of a heart attack at the age of 70 and they are worried that it might run in the family. The patient is afebrile and vital signs are within normal limits. Laboratory results are unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis for this patient’s condition?

An 8-year-old patient is brought in by their parent who is concerned about the patient's behavior. They say the patient's teachers have complained about them bullying other students at school, starting fights, and stealing other children's lunch money. They also say that a neighbor down the street called them 6 months ago and reported that the patient had entered their yard and started viciously kicking their dog. They have no significant past medical history. They are in the 90th percentile for height and weight and have been meeting all developmental milestones. The patient is afebrile and their vital signs are within normal limits. Which of the following adult personality disorders does this patient's diagnosis most likely predict?

An 81-year-old patient is brought to the clinic by their son to be evaluated for memory issues. The patient’s son says they have difficulty remembering recent events and names. They say the patient’s symptoms have progressively worsened over the last several years but became acutely worse just recently. Also, yesterday, the patient complained that they could not see out of their right eye, but today they can. When asked about these concerns, the patient seems to have no insight into the problem and reports feeling well. Their medical history is significant for diabetes mellitus type 2 and hypertension. They had a left basal ganglia hemorrhage 12 years ago and a right middle cerebral artery infarction 4 years ago. Current medications are amlodipine, aspirin, clopidogrel, metformin, sitagliptin, and valsartan. They live with their son and can feed themselves and change their clothes. There is no history of urinary or fecal incontinence. Their vitals include: blood pressure 137/82 mm Hg, pulse 78/min, respiratory rate 16/min, temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F). On physical examination, the patient is alert and oriented. They are unable to perform simple arithmetic calculations and the mini-mental status exam is inconclusive. They can write their name and comprehend written instructions. Muscle strength is 4/5 on the right side. The tone is also slightly reduced on the right side with exaggerated reflexes. Their gait is hemiparetic. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 74-year-old patient presents to the clinic for evaluation of an erythematous and edematous skin rash on their right leg that has progressively worsened over the last 2 weeks. The medical history is significant for hypertension and diabetes mellitus type 2. They take prescribed lisinopril and metformin. The vital signs include: blood pressure 152/92 mm Hg, heart rate 76/min, respiratory rate 12/min, and temperature 37.8°C (100.1°F). On physical exam, the patient appears alert and oriented. Observation of the lesion reveals a poorly demarcated region of erythema and edema along the anterior aspect of the right tibia. Within the region of erythema is a 2–3 millimeter linear break in the skin that does not reveal any serous or purulent discharge. Tenderness to palpation and warmth is associated with the lesion. There are no vesicles, pustules, papules, or nodules present. Ultrasound of the lower extremity is negative for deep vein thrombosis or skin abscess. The blood cultures are pending. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis based on history and physical examination?

A 72-year-old patient presents to the physician with severe lower back pain and fatigue for 3 months. The pain increases with activity. They have no history of a serious illness. They take ibuprofen for pain relief. They do not smoke. The blood pressure is 105/65 mm Hg, the pulse is 86/min, the respirations are 16/min, and the temperature is 36.7℃ (98.1℉). The conjunctivae are pale. Palpation over the 1st lumbar vertebra shows tenderness. The heart, lung, and abdominal examination shows no abnormalities. No lymphadenopathy is palpated. The results of the laboratory studies show: Laboratory test Hemoglobin 9 g/dL Mean corpuscular volume 90 μm3 Leukocyte count 5,500/mm3 with a normal differential Platelet count 350,000/mm3 Serum Calcium 11.5 mg/dL Albumin 3.8 g/dL Urea nitrogen 54 mg/dL Creatinine 2.5 mg/dL Lumbosacral computed tomography (CT) scan shows a low-density lesion in the 1st lumbar vertebra and several similar lesions in the pelvic bones. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 41-year-old patient presents with shortness of breath that is worse when they lie on their left side. About 10 days ago, they had an episode of unexplained loss of consciousness. Past medical history is negative and family history is irrelevant. Clinical examination shows a diastolic murmur, which is prominent when they lie on their left side. Jugular venous distention is present, and chest examination reveals fine crackles that do not clear with coughing. Chest X-ray shows pulmonary congestion, and 2-dimensional echocardiogram shows a mass in the left atrium attached to the atrial septum. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 31-year-old patient presents with significant swelling and redness of their fingers that is causing them significant pain. Their right knee has also been stiff and slightly swollen for the past 6 weeks. They are overall fatigued and have difficulty moving around but have not sought medical attention until now. On physical examination, the distal interphalangeal joints are swollen, warm, and painful; their nails are pitted and cracked. There are also rough, erythematous skin patches seen over their elbows which have been present for the last few months. They report that their father has a similar condition. They both use hydrating creams and topical glucocorticoids with moderate benefit. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old patient presents with painless swelling of the neck for the past week. They report no recent fevers, night sweats, or weight loss. Their past medical history is significant for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection, which was diagnosed last year. They also experienced a head trauma 5 years ago, which has been complicated by residual seizures. Their only medication is daily phenytoin, which was restarted after they had a seizure 3 months ago. Their temperature is 36.8℃ (98.2℉). On physical examination, multiple non-tender lymph nodes, averaging 2 cm in diameter, are found to be palpable in the anterior and posterior triangles of the neck bilaterally. No other lymphadenopathy is noted. The remainder of the physical exam is unremarkable. Laboratory studies show the following: Hemoglobin 14 g/dL Leukocyte count 8000/mm3 with a normal differential Platelet count 250,000/mm3 Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 40 mm/h An excisional biopsy of one of the cervical lymph nodes is performed. The histopathologic analysis is shown in the image. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 28-year-old African American patient comes to the emergency department with intermittent and progressively worsening dizziness with near-fainting incidents for the last 3 weeks. They deny fever, weight loss, nausea, vomiting, or chest pain. Their medical history is significant for a chronic cough and intermittent skin rashes that spontaneously resolved after a few weeks. They do not smoke tobacco but drink alcohol socially. The patient lives alone with no pets. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), blood pressure is 122/80 mm Hg, pulse is 43/min, and respirations are 12/min. On physical examination, cervical lymphadenopathy is noted. No heart murmurs are heard. ECG shows sinus rhythm with 2:1 atrioventricular block and left bundle branch block. Chest X-ray shows prominent hilar lymphadenopathy. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation. They report fever without chills and rigors and deny sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. They have a history of tics and are currently on a low dose of haloperidol. At the hospital, their temperature is 39.6°C (103.2°F); the blood pressure is 126/66 mm Hg, and the pulse is 116/min. They are profusely sweating and generalized rigidity is present. They are confused and disoriented. They are able to move all their limbs. Normal deep tendon reflexes are present with bilateral downgoing plantar responses. A brain MRI is unremarkable. Urine toxicology is negative. The white blood cell count is 14,700/mm3. Creatine kinase is 5600 U/L. Lumbar puncture is performed and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) studies show: CSF opening pressure 22 cm H20 CSF white blood cells 4 cells/mm3 CSF red blood cells 0 cells/mm3 CSF glucose 64 mg/dL CSF protein 48 mg/dL Serum glucose 96 mg/dL What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old African American patient presents to the emergency department with central chest pressure. Their symptoms started 1 day before. The pain was initially intermittent in nature but has become constant and radiates to their jaw and left shoulder. They also complain of some difficulty breathing. The patient was diagnosed with essential hypertension 1 year ago, but they are not taking any medications for it. The patient denies smoking, alcohol, or drug use. Family history is unremarkable. Their blood pressure is 230/130 mm Hg in both arms, the temperature is 36.9°C (98.4°F), and the pulse is 90/min. ECG shows diffuse T wave inversion and ST depression in lateral leads. Laboratory testing is significant for elevated troponin. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 11-year-old patient is brought to their primary care physician by their parent with complaints of constant lower abdominal pain and foul-smelling urine for the past 2 days. The patient has had several previous episodes of simple urinary tract infections in the past. Their vitals signs show mild tachycardia without fever. Physical examination reveals suprapubic tenderness without costovertebral angle tenderness on percussion. Urinalysis reveals positive leukocyte esterase and nitrite. Further questioning reveals that the patient does not use the school toilets and holds their urine all day until they get home. When pressed further, they get teary-eyed and start to cry and complain that other students will make fun of them if they use the bathroom and will spread rumors to the teachers and their friends. They report that though this has never happened in the past it concerns them a great deal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 50-year-old overweight patient presents to their physician with complaints of recurrent episodes of right upper abdominal discomfort and cramping. They say that the pain is mild and occasionally brought on by the ingestion of fatty foods. The pain radiates to the right shoulder and around to the back, and it is accompanied by nausea and occasional vomiting. They admit to having these episodes over the past several years. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6° F), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 67/min, and blood pressure is 122/98 mm Hg. Their physical examination is unremarkable. Lab reports reveal: Hb% 13 gm/dL Total count (WBC): 11,000/mm3 Differential count: Neutrophils: 70% Lymphocytes: 25% Monocytes: 5% ESR: 10 mm/hr Serum: Albumin: 4.2 gm/dL Alkaline phosphatase: 150 U/L Alanine aminotransferase: 76 U/L Aspartate aminotransferase: 88 U/L What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 74-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with sudden onset of abdominal pain that is most felt around the umbilicus. The pain began 16 hours ago and has no association with meals. They have not been vomiting, but they have had several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. They were hospitalized 1 week ago for an acute myocardial infarction. They have had diabetes mellitus for 35 years and hypertension for 20 years. They have smoked 15–20 cigarettes per day for the past 40 years. Their temperature is 36.9°C (98.4°F), blood pressure is 95/65 mm Hg, and pulse is 95/min. On physical examination, the patient is in severe pain, there is a mild periumbilical tenderness, and a bruit is heard over the epigastric area. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old patient presents with convulsions. The patient’s sibling says that they found them like that an hour ago and immediately called an ambulance. They also say that the patient has been extremely distraught and receiving supportive care from a social worker following a sexual assault by a coworker a few days ago. They say that the patient has no history of seizures. The patient has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. The patient’s vital signs include: temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse 101/min, blood pressure 135/99 mm Hg, and respiratory rate 25/min. On physical examination, the patient is rolling from side to side, arrhythmically thrashing around, and muttering strangely. Their eyes are closed, and there is resistance to opening them. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 30-year-old patient comes to the clinic with complaints of increased frequency of urination, especially at night, for about a month. They have to wake up at least 5-6 times every night to urinate and this is negatively affecting their sleep. They also complain of increased thirst and generalized weakness. Past medical history is significant for bipolar disorder. They are on lithium which they take regularly. Blood pressure is 150/90 mm Hg, pulse rate is 80/min, respiratory rate is 16/min, and temperature is 36°C (96.8°F). Physical examination is normal. Laboratory studies show: Na+: 146 mEq/L K+: 3.8 mEq/L Serum calcium: 9.5 mg/dL Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL Urine osmolality: 195 mOsm/kg Serum osmolality: 305 mOsm/kg Serum fasting glucose: 90 mg/dL Which of the following is the best initial test for the diagnosis of their condition?

A 32-year-old patient is brought into the emergency department at 5 AM because of chest pain that woke them up at 3 AM. The pain is constant and has not decreased in intensity during this time. They have no history of any similar episodes. They have systemic lupus erythematosus without major organ involvement. They take prednisone, calcium, alendronate, and hydroxychloroquine. The blood pressure is 120/75 mm Hg, pulse is 85/min, respirations are 19/min, and the temperature is 36.5°C (97.7°F). An examination of the chest including the heart and lungs shows no abnormalities. The electrocardiogram (ECG) shows no abnormalities. Computed tomography (CT) scan of the chest shows esophageal thickening near the mid-portion. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient presents to their family physician with pain on the front of their right knee. The pain started 2 months ago after they began training for a marathon, and it was gradual in onset and has slowly worsened. The pain increases with prolonged sitting and climbing stairs. They deny significant knee trauma. Their only medication is diclofenac sodium as needed for pain. Medical history is unremarkable. The vital signs include: temperature 36.9°C (98.4°F), blood pressure 100/70 mm Hg, and heart rate 78/min. Their body mass index is 26 kg/m2. The pain is reproduced by applying direct pressure to the right patella, and there is increased patellar laxity with medial and lateral displacement. The remainder of the examination is otherwise unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old patient with behavioral changes is brought in by their concerned parents. The patient's parents say that they have been acting very odd and having difficulty academically for the past 4 months. The patient says that they have been worried and distracted because they are certain the government is secretly recording them although they cannot provide a reason why. They mention that they do feel depressed sometimes and no longer get joy out of playing the guitar and their other previous activities. They have no significant past medical history. The patient denies any history of smoking, alcohol consumption, or recreational drug use. They are afebrile, and their vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination is unremarkable. On mental status examination, the patient is slightly disheveled and unkempt. They have a disorganized monotonous speech pattern. They express tangential thinking and have a flat affect. During the exam, it is clear that they suffer from auditory hallucinations. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 28-year-old patient presents to the Emergency Department after a window they were installing fell on them. The patient complains of left ocular pain, blurred vision, and obscured lower portion of the left visual field. The patient’s vital signs are as follows: blood pressure 140/80 mm Hg, heart rate 88/min, respiratory rate 14/min, and temperature 36.9℃ (98.4℉). On physical examination, they have multiple superficial lacerations on their face, arms, and legs. Examination of their right eye shows a superficial upper eyelid laceration. Examination of the left eye shows conjunctival hyperemia, peaked pupil, iridial asymmetry, hyphema, and vitreous hemorrhage. The fundus is hard to visualize due to the vitreous hemorrhage. The visual acuity is 20/25 in the right eye and difficult to evaluate in the left. Which of the following is a proper step to undertake in the diagnosis and management of this patient?

A 13-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department because of vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, and dizziness for the past 3 hours with fever, chills, and muscle pain for the last day. They had presented 5 days ago for an episode of epistaxis caused by nasal picking and was treated with placement of anterior nasal packing. Their parents report that the bleeding stopped, but they forgot to remove the nasal pack. Their temperature is 40.0°C (104.0°F), pulse is 124/min, respirations are 28/min, and blood pressure is 96/68 mm Hg. They look confused, and physical exam shows conjunctival and oropharyngeal hyperemia with a diffuse, erythematous, macular rash over the body that involves the palms and the soles. Removal of the anterior nasal pack shows hyperemia with purulent discharge from the underlying mucosa. Laboratory studies show: Total white blood cell count 30,000/mm3 (30 x 109/L) Differential count Neutrophils 90% Lymphocytes 8% Monocytes 1% Eosinophils 1% Basophils 0% Platelet count 95,000/mm3 (95 x 109/L) Serum creatine phosphokinase 400 IU/L What is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 57-year-old patient presents with a large wound on their right lower leg that has been present for 6 months as shown in the picture. They have had chronically swollen legs for over 10 years. Their mother and brother had similar problems with their legs. They had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years earlier, but have no other past medical history. They have a blood pressure of 126/84 and heart rate of 62/min. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 58-year-old patient presents to the clinic with an abnormal sensation on the left side of their body that has been present for the past several months. At first, the area seemed numb and they recall touching a hot stove and accidentally burning themselves but not feeling the heat. Now they are suffering from a constant, uncomfortable burning pain on their left side for the past week. The pain gets worse when someone even lightly touches that side. They have recently immigrated and their past medical records are unavailable. Last month they had a stroke but they cannot recall any details from the event. They confirm a history of hypertension, type II diabetes mellitus, and bilateral knee pain. They also had cardiac surgery 20 years ago. They deny fever, mood changes, weight changes, and trauma to the head, neck, or limbs. Their blood pressure is 162/90 mm Hg, the heart rate is 82/min, and the respiratory rate is 15/min. Multiple old burn marks are visible on the left hand and forearm. Muscle strength is mildly reduced in the left upper and lower limbs. Hyperesthesia is noted in the left upper and lower limbs. Laboratory results are significant for: Hemoglobin 13.9 g/dL MCV 92 fL White blood cells 7,500/mm3 Platelets 278,000/mm3 Creatinine 1.3 U/L BUN 38 mg/dL TSH 2.5 uU/L Hemoglobin A1c 7.9% Vitamin B12 526 ng/L What is the most likely diagnosis?

A confused and disoriented 32-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their spouse. They were in their usual state of health until yesterday, when they started complaining of fever and headache. This morning they were complaining of worsened headache and were acting odd, prompting their spouse to bring them to the hospital. Their past medical history is unremarkable. At the hospital, their temperature is 39.2°C (102.5°F), pulse is 116/min, and blood pressure is 96/64 mm Hg. Physical examination is notable for neck stiffness and a large scar across their abdomen that their spouse says is from a splenectomy operation following a car accident a few years ago. They have not seen a doctor since that time. A lumbar puncture shows elevated protein, low glucose, and 1,200 WBCs with 95% polymorphonuclear cells; gram staining shows gram-positive diplococci. Which of the following is the most likely risk factor contributing to this patient's underlying diagnosis?

A 14-year-old patient presents with their parent complaining of a swollen, red, painful left knee. Their physician aspirates the joint and discovers frank blood. The patient denies a recent history of trauma to the knee. Upon further discussion, the parent describes that the patient has had multiple swollen painful joints before, often without evidence of trauma. They also mention a history of frequent nosebleeds and gum bleeding following visits to the dentist. Which of the following is the most likely underlying diagnosis?

A 7-year-old patient presents with difficult left eye-opening in the morning, eye discharge, and irritation. These symptoms developed gradually over the past week. They attend a primary school where recently an outbreak of tonsillitis took place. They had otitis media 2 weeks ago treated with ampicillin. At the presentation, the patient’s vital signs are within normal limits. Eye examination reveals bulbar conjunctival injection, mild eyelid edema, and a moderate mucopurulent discharge with crusts on the lower eyelid. There is no corneal or eyelid ulceration. No lymphadenopathy is noted. Which of the following investigations should be performed to establish a diagnosis before the treatment?

A 74-year-old patient returns to their physician to follow-up on laboratory studies obtained for anemia 2 weeks ago. They have no complaints. They have a 20-year history of hypertension and several years of knee osteoarthritis. They walk 2 miles a day. They do not smoke. They drink alcohol moderately. They take hydrochlorothiazide, losartan, and pain killers, including ibuprofen. The vital signs include: temperature 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse 68/min, respiratory rate 12/min, and blood pressure 110/70 mm Hg. The physical examination shows no abnormalities. The laboratory studies show the following: Laboratory test Hemoglobin 10 g/dL Mean corpuscular volume 75 μm3 Leukocyte count 5,000/mm3 Platelet count 350,000/mm3 ESR 18 mm/hr Serum Ferritin 5 μg/L Iron 30 μg/L Total iron-binding capacity 500 μg/dL Calcium (Ca+) 9 mg/dL Albumin 4 g/dL Urea nitrogen 14 mg/dL Creatinine 0.9 mg/dL Monoclonal protein on serum electrophoresis is 12 g/L (non-IgM). Clonal bone marrow plasma cells comprise 4% of the total number of cells. Skeletal survey with magnetic resonance imaging reveals no pathologic findings. In addition to iron deficiency anemia, which of the following diagnosis is most appropriate to consider?

An otherwise healthy 31-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with a several-day history of sharp, central chest pain, which is constant and unrelated to exertion. The pain gets worse on lying down and decreases with sitting forward. They have smoked 10–15 cigarettes daily for the past 7 years. Their blood pressure is 120/50 mm Hg, the pulse is 92/min, and the temperature is 37.1°C (98.7°F). On physical examination, a scratching sound is heard at end-expiration with the patient leaning forward. ECG is shown in the image. Serum troponin is mildly elevated. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old patient presents with a rash on their body. The patient's parent says they noticed the rash onset about 5 hours ago. For the previous 3 days, they say the patient has had a high fever of 39.0°C (102.2°F). Today the fever abruptly subsided but the rash appeared. Vitals are temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F), blood pressure 95/55 mm Hg, pulse 110/min, respiratory rate 30/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air. Physical examination reveals a maculopapular, non-confluent, blanchable rash on the back, abdomen, and chest extending superiorly towards the nape of the patient's neck. Which of the following is this patient's most likely diagnosis?

A 61-year-old patient presents to the office with a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes mellitus type II, hypercholesterolemia, and asthma. Recently, they describe increasing difficulty with breathing, particularly when performing manual labor. They also endorse a new cough, which occurs both indoors and out. They deny any recent tobacco use, despite a 40-pack-year history. They mention that their symptoms are particularly stressful for them since they have been working in the construction industry for the past 30 years. The vital signs include: temperature 36.7°C (98.0°F), blood pressure 126/74 mm Hg, heart rate 74/min, and respiratory rate 14/min. On physical examination you notice clubbing of their digits, wheezing on auscultation, and normal heart sounds. A chest radiograph demonstrates linear opacities at the bilateral lung bases and multiple calcified pleural plaques. What is their most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department because of intermittent sharp right upper quadrant abdominal pain and nausea for the past 10 hours. They have vomited 3 times.
