There is no associated fever, chills, diarrhea, or urinary symptoms. They have 2 children who both attend high school. They appear uncomfortable. They are 165 cm (5 ft 5 in) tall and weigh 86 kg (190 lb). Their BMI is 32 kg/m2. Their temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse is 100/min, and blood pressure is 140/90 mm Hg. They have mild scleral icterus. On physical examination, their abdomen is soft and nondistended, with tenderness to palpation of the right upper quadrant without guarding or rebound. Bowel sounds are normal. Laboratory studies show the following: Blood Hemoglobin count 14 g/dL Leukocyte count 9,000 mm3 Platelet count 160,000 mm3 Serum Alkaline phosphatase 238 U/L Aspartate aminotransferase 60 U/L Bilirubin Total 2.8 mg/dL Direct 2.1 mg/dL Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 43-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department with skin changes on their leg as shown in the image that manifested over the past 24 hours. They accidentally stabbed themselves in the leg 4 days earlier with a knife that was in their pocket. They have a 10-year history of diabetes mellitus. Their medications include metformin. They appear confused. Their blood pressure is 90/70 mm Hg, the pulse is 115/min, the respirations are 21/min, and their temperature is 39.5℃ (103.1℉). The cardiopulmonary examination shows no other abnormalities. The serum creatinine level is 2.5 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most appropriate step in establishing a definitive diagnosis?

A 30-year-old patient presents to the physician because of ongoing diarrhea for the past 1 month. They report that diarrhea has been intermittently present for the past month. The stool is often loose and associated with blood and lower abdominal pain. They deny any recent travel history, and they work at a nursing home as a caretaker. They are not currently on any medications. Clinical examination shows mild tenderness in the suprapubic region, and there is no organomegaly. Findings on colonoscopy include patchy erythema and ulceration in the cecum, ascending, descending, and sigmoid colon. Mucosal biopsy shows colonic crypts with lymphocytic and neutrophilic infiltrates. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old patient with no significant past medical, surgical, social, or family history presents to the clinic with an itchy rash. Their review of systems is otherwise negative. The patient’s blood pressure is 119/80 mm Hg, the pulse is 83/min, the respiratory rate is 15/min, and the temperature is 36.8°C (98.4°F). Physical examination reveals crusting vesicular clusters on their upper back with a base of erythema and surrounding edema. What additional features would be most helpful to confirm the diagnosis?

A 21-year-old patient is brought by their mother to a psychiatrist due to concerns about their behavior. The patient’s mother tells the psychiatrist that she believes that a famous Hollywood celebrity actor loves them and will marry them. When the patient is asked about this, they say that they attended a function at which this actor was the guest of honor six months back, and they waved their hand at them by which they understood that they love them. However, when they try to contact them over the phone, they do not respond, which they say is probably because they are too busy with their career at present. When asked why the successful actor would marry them, they say, “Celebrities often prefer to marry ordinary people and that is why they expressed their interest in me that day”. The patient is otherwise healthy with no known medical condition. They deny any mood disturbances, hallucinations, or anxiety. They are currently working as an assistant manager at a private advertising firm and have a normal socio-occupational life. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 38-year-old patient presents to the physician with fever and malaise for 4 days. They have headaches and joint pain. A pruritic rash appeared on the trunk yesterday. They had blood in their ejaculate twice. Their hearing has become partially impaired. There is no history of serious illnesses or the use of medications. Ten days ago, they traveled to Brazil where they spent most of the time outdoors in the evenings. They did not use any control measures for mosquito bites. Their temperature is 38.2℃ (100.8℉); the pulse is 88/min; the respiratory rate is 13/min, and the blood pressure is 125/60 mm Hg. Conjunctival suffusion is noted. A maculopapular rash is present over the trunk and proximal extremities without the involvement of the palms or soles. Several joints of the hands are tender to palpation. The abdomen is soft with no organomegaly. A peripheral blood smear shows no pathogenic organisms. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 43-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their brother for severe chest pain. The patient recently lost their spouse in a car accident and is still extremely shocked by the event. On physical examination, their blood pressure is 105/67 mm Hg, the heart rate is 96/min and regular, breathing rate is 23/min, and the pulse oximetry is 96%. An S3 heart sound and rales in the lower right and left lung lobes are heard. A 12-lead ECG shows no significant findings. Echocardiography shows an enlarged left ventricle and left atrium. The patient is stabilized and informed about the diagnosis and possible treatment options. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 9-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of short stature. They have always had short stature around the 35th percentile on the growth curve. Over the past year, they have dropped further on the curve, despite maintaining the same diet. They have a history of low birth weight. The vital signs include: respiration rate 18/min, pulse 85/min, and blood pressure 110/65 mm Hg. Their conjunctiva and nail beds are pale. Several hyperpigmented and hypopigmented patches are seen on the back. Chest inspection reveals pectus carinatum and prominent knobs of bone at most costochondral junctions. The thumbs are short, and they have bow legs. There are also petechiae on the lower limbs. The remainder of the physical exam shows no abnormalities. The laboratory results are as follows: Hemoglobin 8.2 g/dL Mean corpuscular volume 105 μm3 Platelet count 35,000/mm3 Serum Na+ 131 mEq/L K+ 2.8 mEq/L Cl- 105 mEq/L Phosphorus (inorganic) 2.5 mg/dL (3.0–4.5 mg/dL) Arterial blood gas analysis on room air: pH 7.30 PCO2+ 33 mm Hg HCO3− 17 mEq/L Urine pH 5.0 Glucose 2+ Ketones Negative Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 41-year-old patient presents to urgent care with complaints of a new rash. On review of systems, they endorse ankle pain bilaterally. Otherwise, they have no additional localized complaints. Physical examination reveals numerous red subcutaneous nodules overlying their shins, bilaterally. Complete blood count shows leukocytes 7,300, Hct 46.2%, Hgb 18.1 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume (MCV) 88 fL, and platelets 209. Chest radiography demonstrates bilateral hilar adenopathy with clear lungs. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to their primary care provider with a 2-month history of insidious onset of left shoulder pain. It only occurs at the extremes of their range of motion and has made it difficult to sleep on the affected side. They have noticed increasing difficulty with activities of daily living, including brushing their hair and putting on or taking off their clothing. They deny a history of shoulder trauma, neck pain, arm/hand weakness, numbness, or paresthesias. Their medical history is remarkable for type 2 diabetes mellitus, for which they take metformin and glipizide. Their physical examination reveals a marked decrease in both active and passive range of motion of the left shoulder, with forwarding flexion to 75°, abduction to 75°, external rotation to 45°, and internal rotation to 15° with significant pain. Rotator cuff strength is normal. AP, scapular Y, and axillary plain film radiographs are reported as normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 47-year-old patient presents with intermittent throbbing headaches. They say that they have had at least 1–2 every week for the last 3 months. They describe the pain as severe, pulsatile, and localized to the right frontotemporal and periorbital areas. They say the headaches usually last for several hours and are made worse by the presence of light. They endorse nausea with occasional vomiting during the most severe episodes. They deny any seizures, loss of consciousness, or focal neurologic deficits. Their past medical history is significant for myocardial infarction (MI) 1 year ago, status post percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty complicated by residual angina, and severe asthma, managed medically. The patient is afebrile, and the vital signs are within normal limits. A physical examination is unremarkable. A noncontrast computed tomography (CT) scan of the head appears normal. Which of the following is the best prophylactic treatment for this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old patient who was diagnosed with arthritis 16 years ago presents with right knee swelling and pain. Their left knee was swollen a few weeks ago, but now with both joints affected, they have difficulty walking and feel frustrated. They also have back pain which makes it extremely difficult to move around and be active during the day. They say their pain significantly improves with rest. They also suffer from dandruff for which they use special shampoos. Physical examination is notable for pitting of their nails. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old graduate student presents to the physician for a 2-month history of persistent thoughts and anxiety that they are going to be harmed by someone on the street. The anxiety worsened after they witnessed a pedestrian being hit by a car 2 weeks ago. They state, “That was a warning sign.” On their way to school, they now often leave an hour earlier to take a detour and hide from people that they think might hurt them. They are burdened by their coursework and fears that their professors are trying to fail them. They say their friends are concerned about them, but claim they do not understand because they were not present at the accident. The patient has no known history of any psychiatric illnesses. On the mental status exam, they are alert and oriented, and they show a full range of affect. Thought processes and speech are organized. Their memory and attention are within normal limits. They deny auditory, visual, or tactile hallucinations. The results of urine toxicology screening are negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 65-year-old Caucasian patient comes to the clinic with complaints of fatigability and persistent headaches for the last month. Their headache is dull, encompassing their whole head, and has been getting worse lately. They have associated diplopia and progressively diminishing peripheral vision. They also complain of difficulty losing weight despite trying to control their diet and exercising regularly. They weigh 91 kg (200 lb) at present and report having gained 9 kg (20 lb) in the past month. Past medical history is insignificant. Blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg, pulse rate is 60/min, respiratory rate is 12/min, temperature is 36.5°C (97.7°F). Physical examination shows bilateral papilledema. There is some pedal edema and their deep tendon reflexes are slow. CT scan shows suprasellar calcifications. Laboratory studies show: Na+ 140 mEq/L K+ 3.8 mEq/L Serum calcium 9.5 mg/dL TSH 0.05 U/mL Free T4 0.2 ng/mL Which of the following is the most probable diagnosis?

A 48-year-old patient presents to the clinic with several weeks of watery diarrhea and right upper quadrant pain with fever. They also endorse malaise, nausea, and anorexia. They are HIV-positive and are currently on antiretroviral therapy. They admit to not being compliant with their current medications. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 70/min, and blood pressure is 100/84 mm Hg. A physical examination is performed which is within normal limits. Their blood tests results are given below: Hb%: 11 gm/dL Total count (WBC): 3,400 /mm3 Differential count: Neutrophils: 70% Lymphocytes: 25% Monocytes: 5% CD4+ cell count: 88/mm3 Stool microscopy results are pending. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with moderate right wrist pain after falling on their outstretched hand. They have numbness in the 3 medial digits. The patient has no known previous medical conditions. Their family history is not pertinent, and they currently take no medications. Physical examination shows their blood pressure is 134/82 mm Hg, the respirations are 14/min, the pulse is 87/min, and the temperature is 36.7°C (98.0°F). When asked to make a fist, the patient is able to flex only the lateral 2 digits. Tapping the anterior portion of their wrist elicits tingling in the medial 3 digits. The patient is taken to get an X-ray. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis for this patient’s injury?

A 61-year-old patient presents to the primary care clinic to establish care. They have not seen a physician for many years. They have no complaints or concerns but, on further questioning, do have some vague abdominal discomfort. They have no known past medical history and take no medications. Their social history is notable for injecting heroin throughout their late-teens and 20s, but they have been clean and sober for over a decade. At the clinic, the vital signs include: heart rate 90/min, respiratory rate 17/min, blood pressure 110/65 mm Hg, and temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F). The physical exam shows a slightly distended abdomen. The laboratory studies are notable for a platelet count of 77,000/uL and an international normalized ratio (INR) of 1.7. Which of the following is the next best step in the diagnosis of this patient?

A 55-year-old patient is brought to the emergency room by their spouse for severe abdominal pain for the past 1 hour. They are unable to give more information about the nature of their pain. Their spouse says that they have peptic ulcer disease and are being treated with antacids without a good response. They add that they vomited repeatedly in the last couple of hours, their vomitus being brown/red in color. Their temperature is 98.6°F (37°C), respiratory rate is 16/min, pulse is 97/min, and blood pressure is 100/68 mm Hg. A physical exam reveals a tense abdomen with a board like rigidity and positive rebound tenderness. An erect abdominal x-ray is ordered. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old patient presents with a rash, oral lesions, and vision problems for 5 days. They say the rash started as a burning feeling on their face and the upper part of their torso, but soon red spots appeared in that same distribution. The spots grew in size and spread to their upper extremities. The patient says the spots are painful but denies any associated pruritus. They say the painful oral lesions appeared about the same time as the rash. For the past 3 days, they also say they have been having double vision and dry, itchy eyes. They report that they had a mild upper respiratory infection for a few days that preceded their current symptoms. The patient denies any chills, hematuria, abdominal or chest pain, or similar symptoms in the past. Past medical history is significant for a severe urinary tract infection diagnosed 3 weeks ago for which they have been taking trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. The vital signs include: temperature 38.3℃ (101.0℉), blood pressure 110/60 mm Hg, respiratory rate 20/min, and pulse 108/min. On physical examination, the patient has severe painful erosions of the oral mucosa. There are multiple fluid-filled vesicles and bullae averaging 3 mm in diameter with a surrounding erythematous ring that involve only the upper torso and extensor surfaces of upper extremities. Several of the lesions have ruptured, resulting in sloughing off of the epidermal layer. There is a prominent conjunctival injection present. Ophthalmic examination reveals mild bilateral corneal abrasions without any evidence of frank ulceration. Laboratory findings are significant for the following: White blood cell (WBC) count 8,500/mm3 Red blood cell (RBC) count 4.20 x 106/mm3 Hematocrit 41.5% Hemoglobin 14.0 g/dL Platelet count 215,000/mm3 C-reactive protein (CRP) 86 mg/L Urine and blood cultures are pending. Which of the following would confirm the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 51-year-old patient with a history of palpitations is being evaluated by a surgeon for epigastric pain. It is discovered that they have an epigastric hernia that needs repair. During their preoperative evaluation, they are ordered to receive lab testing, an electrocardiogram (ECG), and a chest X-ray. These screening studies are unremarkable except for their chest X-ray, which shows a 2 cm isolated pulmonary nodule in the middle lobe of the right lung. The nodule has poorly defined margins, and it shows a dense, irregular pattern of calcification. The patient is immediately referred to a pulmonologist for evaluation of the lesion. The patient denies any recent illnesses and states that they have not traveled outside of the country since they were a child. They have had no sick contacts or respiratory symptoms, and they do not currently take any medications. They do, however, admit to a 20-pack-year history of smoking. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in evaluating this patient’s diagnosis with regard to the pulmonary nodule?

A 75-year-old patient presents to the physician with progressive difficulty reading over the past year. Currently, they avoid driving as they have trouble reading road signs. They have no history of a serious illness and take no medications. The fundoscopic examination shows localized retinal elevation and drusen. A description of the patient’s visual on the Amsler grid is shown. Fluorescein angiography shows early hyperfluorescence. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 31-year-old patient visits the clinic with chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. They also complain of lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by episodes of diarrhea. They deny any recent change in their weight. Bowel movements are preceded by a sensation of urgency, associated with mucus discharge, and followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. The patient went camping several months earlier, and another member of their camping party fell ill recently. Their temperature is 37° C (98.6° F), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 67/min, and blood pressure is 122/98 mm Hg. Their physical examination is unremarkable. A routine stool examination is within normal limits and blood test results show: Hb% 13 gm/dL Total count (WBC): 11,000/mm3 Differential count: Neutrophils: 70% Lymphocytes: 25% Monocytes: 5% ESR: 10 mm/hr What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 18-month-old patient is brought to the doctor’s office for evaluation of abdominal pain. The patient looks emaciated and they are now significantly below their growth chart predicted weight. The family history is non-contributory. The vital signs are unremarkable. On physical examination, a non-tender mass is felt in the upper part of the abdomen. A magnetic resonance image (MRI) scan of their abdomen demonstrates a mass in their right adrenal gland. Biopsy of the mass demonstrates an abundance of small round blue cells. With this biopsy result, which 1 of the following findings would confirm the diagnosis?

A 29-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their spouse due to unusual behavior for the past week. They have noted several incidents when the patient spoke to them so fast that they could not understand what they were saying. They also say that one evening, the patient drove home naked after a night where they said they were ‘painting the town red’. They also say the patient has also been sleeping for about 2 hours a night and has barely had any sleep in the past 2 weeks. They say that the patient goes ‘to work’ in the morning every day, but they suspect that the patient has been doing other things. They deny any knowledge of similar symptoms in the past. On physical examination, the patient appears agitated and is pacing the exam room. They compliment the cleanliness of the floors, recommend the hospital change to the metric system, and ask if anyone else can hear ‘that ringing’. Laboratory results are unremarkable. The patient denies any suicidal or homicidal ideations. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

On routine screening, a 62-year-old patient is found to have positive fecal occult blood tests. They are asymptomatic, but their father died of large intestinal cancer. Abdominal and rectal exams are normal. A colonoscopy subsequently reveals a polyp in the descending colon but no other abnormalities. Excisional biopsy of the polyp shows 75% tubular architecture. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old patient presents to a psychiatrist to discuss a recent event in their life. At a social function 2 days back, they met a person who introduced themselves as having worked with them at another private company 3 years ago. However, they did not recognize them. They also say that they do not remember working at any such company at any time during their life. However, the patient’s partner says that they had indeed worked at that company for three months and had quit due to their boss’s abusive behavior towards them. The person who met them at the function had actually been their colleague at that job. The patient asks the doctor, “How is it possible? I am really not able to recall any memories of having worked at any such company. What’s going on here?”. Their partner adds that after they quit the job, their mood frequently has been low. The patient denies any crying episodes, suicidal ideas, not enjoying recreational activities or feelings of worthlessness. Their appetite and sleep patterns are normal. They are otherwise a healthy patient with no significant medical history and lives a normal social and occupational life. The patient reports no history of smoking, alcohol, or substance use. On physical examination, they are alert and well-oriented to time, place and person. During memory testing, they correctly remember the date of their marriage that took place 5 years back and the food they ate over the last 2 days. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 36-year-old patient presents to the physician with a cough accompanied by expectoration and recurrent wheezing, for the last 2 years. They say that their symptoms have progressed slowly in severity and frequency over this period. There is no history of rhinorrhea, nasal congestion, or high fever. They have been a smoker for the last 5 years. Their environmental history does not suggest that they are at increased risk of developing any occupational lung disease but their house has mold growth in some areas. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), the heart rate is 80/min, the blood pressure is 124/80 mm Hg, and the respiratory rate is 22/min. Auscultation of their chest reveals bilateral wheezing in the infrascapular regions. A high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of their chest shows widespread abnormally hypoattenuating areas and simplification of lung architecture in both lower lobes. Pulmonary vessels are decreased in number and widely dispersed in both lower lobes. Which of the following tests is most likely to be helpful in the diagnosis of this patient?

A 67-year-old patient presents with their partner because of left leg pain and swelling of 3 days’ duration. They have a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and recent hospitalization for congestive heart failure exacerbation. On physical examination, the left calf is 4 cm greater in circumference than the right. Pitting edema is present on the left leg and there are superficial dilated veins. Venous duplex ultrasound shows an inability to fully compress the lumen of the profunda femoris vein. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with a 2-day history of fatigue, exertional dyspnea, and the sensation of their heartbeat roaring in the ears. They inform you that they recently had an acute upper respiratory infection. They are a retired car salesman, and they inform you that they and their partner enjoy traveling to the tropics. Their medical history is significant for gout, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, diabetes mellitus type II, and multiple basal cell carcinomas on their face and neck. They currently smoke 1 pack of cigarettes per day, drink a 6-pack of beer per day, and deny any illicit drug use. Their vital signs include: temperature 36.7°C (98.0°F), blood pressure 126/74 mm Hg, heart rate 111/min, and respiratory rate 23/min. On physical examination, their pulses are bounding, their complexion is pale, and scleral icterus is apparent. The spleen is moderately enlarged. Oxygen saturation was initially 81% on room air, with a new oxygen requirement of 8 L by face mask. Laboratory analysis results show a hemoglobin level of 7.1 g/dL and elevated total bilirubin. Of the following options, which laboratory test can help to make the diagnosis?

A 40-year-old chronic smoker presents to the office complaining of a cough and pleuritic chest pain. They also have had pain in their right shoulder for the past 2 weeks. They deny fever, night sweats, but have noticed a 2.2 kg (5 lb) weight loss in the last month. They have no recent history of travel. Past medical history is unremarkable. On cardiopulmonary examination, bilateral velcro-like crackles are auscultated in the upper to middle lung fields, with normal heart sounds. There is a 3 x 3 cm swelling on the right shoulder with a normal range of motion and intact sensation. 5/5 muscular strength in all extremities is noted. Chest X-ray reveals bilateral nodular opacities in the upper lung lobes and a lytic lesion on the right humeral head. Electron microscopy of the lung biopsy shows the following. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 10-year-old patient presents to the emergency department accompanied by their parents with a swollen and painful right knee after they fell from their bicycle a few hours ago. The patient’s parent says they fell off the bike and struck the ground with their whole weight on their right knee. Immediately, their right knee swelled significantly, and they experienced severe pain. The patient’s past medical history is significant for previous episodes of easy bruising that manifest as small bluish spots, but not nearly as severe. The family history is significant for a relative who had similar symptoms, and who was diagnosed at the age of 13 years old. The patient is afebrile, and the vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, a large bruise is present over the right knee that is extending several inches down the leg. The right tibiofemoral joint is warm to the touch and severely tender to palpation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 45-year-old patient presents to the clinic for the third time in the past 3 weeks asking for an MRI of their lower back. They had initially gone to the gym as advised by their spouse and had started doing some back exercises. The next day, they developed soreness in their lower back and spent the whole day online trying to figure out what was wrong with them. They have been to the emergency department a few times and subsequently has been redirected to the clinic where each time they were thoroughly examined and investigated for all the possible causes. The patient still exhibits worry and would like to get an MRI to make sure everything is ‘okay.’ Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

An 11-year-old patient’s parents brought them to a psychologist upon referral from the patient’s school teacher. The patient frequently bullies their younger classmates despite having been punished several times for this. Their parent also reported that a year prior, they received complaints that the patient shoplifted from local shops in their neighborhood. The patient frequently stays out at night despite strict instructions by their parents to return home by 10 PM. Detailed history reveals that apart from such behavior, they are usually not angry or irritable. Although their abnormal behavior continues despite warnings and punishments, they neither argue with their parents nor teachers and do not display verbal or physical aggression. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old patient presents with acute onset of chest pain, trouble breathing, and abdominal pain. They say they had recently been training for a triathlon competition when, over the past week, they noticed that they were getting more tired than usual. They figured that it was due to their age since most of the people training with them were in their 20s. However, after completing a particularly difficult workout over this last weekend they noticed left-sided chest pain that did not radiate, and abdominal pain, worse on the right side. The pain persisted after they stopped exercising. This morning they noticed red urine. The patient reports similar past episodes of red urine after intense exercise or excessive alcohol intake for the past 5 years, but says it has never been accompanied by pain. Past medical history is significant for a urinary tract infection last week, treated with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Physical examination is significant for a systolic flow murmur loudest at the right upper sternal border and right upper quadrant tenderness without guarding or rebound. Laboratory findings are significant for the following: Hemoglobin 8.5 g/dL Platelets 133,000/µL Total bilirubin 6.8 mg/dL LDH 740 U/L Haptoglobin 25 mg/dL An abdominal MRI with contrast is performed which reveals hepatic vein thrombosis. Which of the following laboratory tests would most likely confirm the diagnosis in this patient?

A 28-year-old patient presents for severe abdominal pain and is diagnosed with appendicitis. They are taken for emergent appendectomy. During the procedure, the patient has massive and persistent bleeding requiring a blood transfusion. The preoperative laboratory studies showed a normal bleeding time, normal prothrombin time (PT), an INR of 1.0, and a normal platelet count. Postoperatively, when the patient is told about the complications during the surgery, they recall that they forgot to mention that they have a family history of an unknown bleeding disorder. The postoperative laboratory tests reveal a prolonged partial thromboplastin time (PTT). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 38-year-old patient presents to their physician for difficulty swallowing for 2 months. They describe food getting stuck down their windpipe and have been feeling very anxious around meal time because they are thinking that they may have esophageal cancer. They have had an influenza-like infection that lasted about 6 weeks in the past 3 months which exacerbated their asthma attacks. They used their puffers to relieve their symptoms and did not seek medical treatment. They are otherwise healthy. On examination, their blood pressure is 118/75 mm Hg, respirations are 17/min, pulse is 78/min, and temperature is 36.7°C (98.1°F). There is no evidence of enlarged lymph nodes or a sore throat. On palpation, the thyroid gland is enlarged and tender. They are a non-smoker with a BMI of 25 kg/m2. They have not used any medications recently. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old patient is brought in by their daughter who is concerned about their recent memory impairment. The patient’s daughter says she has noticed impairment in memory and functioning for the past month. She says that they have forgotten to pay bills and go shopping, and, as a result, the electricity was cut off due to non-payment. She also says that last week, they turned the stove on and forgot about it, resulting in a kitchen fire. The patient has lived by themselves since their spouse died last year. They fondly recall living with their spouse and how much they miss them. They admit that they feel ‘down’ most days of the week living on their own and doesn’t have much energy. When asked about the kitchen fire and problems with the electricity, they get defensive and angry. At the patient’s last routine check-up 3 months ago, they were healthy with no medical problems. Their vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, the patient appears to have a flat affect. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 60-year-old patient presents to the physician for a follow-up examination. During the previous visit, splenomegaly was detected on the abdominal exam, which has been confirmed by abdominal ultrasound. They have no complaints other than fatigue for several months. There is no history of serious illness. Their only medication is acetaminophen for knee pain. The temperature is 36.7℃ (98.1℉), pulse is 68, respirations are 12/min, and blood pressure is 125/70 mm Hg. On physical examination, the spleen size on percussion is 16 cm (6.2 in). Otherwise, the physical examination shows no abnormalities. The laboratory test results are as follows: Hemoglobin 10 g/dL Mean corpuscular volume 90 μm3 Leukocyte count 80,000/mm3 Platelet count 450,000/mm3 The peripheral blood smear shows a predominance of neutrophils and the presence of band cells, myelocytes, promyelocytes, and blasts (< 5%). The cytogenetic study shows t(9;22). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 21-year-old patient presents with the complaints of nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea for 5 days. They add that they have fever and abdominal cramping as well. They had recently attended a large family picnic and describes eating many varieties of cold noodle salads. Their past medical history is insignificant. Their temperature is 37.5°C (99.6°F), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 67/min, and blood pressure is 92/68 mm Hg. Physical examination is non-contributory. Given the clinical information provided and most likely diagnosis, which of the following would be the next best step in the management of this patient?

A 10-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parents because they are concerned about their “strange behavior”. The parents state that they have always been a lonely kid without many friends, but recently they have been having behavioral problems that seem to be unprovoked and are occurring more frequently. The child throws tantrums for no reason and does not respond to punishment or reward. They also have a “strange obsession” with collecting rocks that they find on their way to and from school to the point where their room is filled with rocks. They play alone in their room, lining the rocks up, organizing them by size, shape, or color, and they will randomly bark or make high-pitched noises without provocation. Their teachers say they daydream a lot and are very good at art, being able to recreate their favorite cartoon characters in great detail. On physical assessment, the patient does not make eye contact with the physician but talks incessantly about their rock collection. The child’s grammar and vocabulary seem normal but their speech is slightly labored, and they can’t seem to tell that the physician is not really interested in hearing about their rock collection. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old patient presents to their primary care provider because of fever, diarrhea, and abdominal cramps. They have returned from Dhaka, Bangladesh recently where they were visiting their relatives. They are diagnosed with Shigella infection, and ciprofloxacin is started. They develop severe nausea and weakness 2 days later and complain of passing dark urine. The lab test results reveal a hemoglobin level of 7.9 g/dL, increased unconjugated bilirubin, increased reticulocyte count, increased lactate dehydrogenase, and increased blood urea. Which of the following is the best next step for the diagnosis of this patient’s condition?

A 52-year-old homeless patient is brought to the urgent care clinic with altered mental status and disorientation for the last day. Past medical records are unavailable. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), the respiratory rate is 15/min, the pulse is 107/min, and the blood pressure is 92/67 mm Hg. They have a flapping tremor of the wrists during attempted extension. They are started on intravenous D5 1/2NS and blood is drawn for further testing. Their condition deteriorates overnight. On re-examination the next morning, they have developed visual disturbances with a new horizontal nystagmus and a staggering gait. Their blood tests show: Serum Albumin 3.2 gm/dL Alkaline phosphatase 150 U/L Alanine aminotransferase 76 U/L Aspartate aminotransferase 155 U/L Gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase 202 U/L What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 50-year-old patient presents to their physician with chronic cough, aching joints in their hips and lower back, and malaise over the past 2 months. They describe themselves as being “generally healthy” before the cough began. Past medical history includes hypertension. The patient takes clopamide and a multivitamin daily. Their parents are both well and living in a senior living facility. They do not smoke and only drink alcohol occasionally. During a review of symptoms, the patient described a hiking trip in and around the desert near Phoenix, Arizona, 4 months ago. At the office, their temperature is 38.6°C (101.4°F), heart rate is 102/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 120/82 mm Hg. A focused chest exam reveals mild fremetus and dullness with percussion on the right side. A chest X-ray shows a right-sided consolidation of the lower right lung, and a chest CT shows an irregular opacity measuring 3.8 cm x 3.0 cm in the sub-plural region of the right middle lobe, a small right-sided pleural effusion, and mild right-sided hilar adenopathy. A lung biopsy is performed to rule out cancer and reveals necrotic granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells and spherules with endospores in the surrounding tissues. The laboratory tests show the following results: Hemoglobin 12.9 mg/dL Leukocyte count 9,300/mm3 Platelet count 167,000/mm3 Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 43 mm/hr Periodic acid-Schiff and silver methenamine Positive Acid-fast stain Negative Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 13-month-old patient is brought to the pediatric clinic by their parent due to progressive abdominal distension, poor feeding, and failure to thrive. The perinatal history was uneventful. The family emigrated from Sudan 8 years ago. The vital signs include: temperature 36.8°C (98.2°F), blood pressure 100/55 mm Hg, and pulse 99/min. The physical examination shows conjunctival pallor, hepatosplenomegaly, and parietal and frontal bossing of the skull. The laboratory test results are as follows: Hemoglobin 8.7 g/dL Mean corpuscular volume 62 μm3 Red cell distribution width 12.2% (normal value is 11.5–14.5%) Reticulocyte count 2.1 % Leucocyte count 10,200/mm3 Platelet count 392,000/mm3 The peripheral blood smear shows microcytic red cells, target cells, and many nucleated red cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old patient is brought into the clinic by their parent who is concerned that they may be depressed. The parent states that the patient feels unattractive and does not fit into any of the social groups at school. When talking to the patient, it is discovered that they mostly avoid the kids in school because of fear of rejection. They usually keep to themselves and say they haven’t involved themselves in any group activities since elementary school. The patient’s parent is worried that this kind of behavior might continue or worsen if it progresses into their college years. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

An 11-month-old patient is brought to the physician for the evaluation of recurrent otitis media since birth. The patient’s immunizations are up-to-date. They are at the 5th percentile for height and weight. Physical examination shows multiple petechiae and several eczematous lesions over the scalp and extremities. The remainder of the examination reveals no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show a leukocyte count of 9,600/mm3 (61% neutrophils and 24% lymphocytes), a platelet count of 29,000/mm3, and an increased serum IgE concentration. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient is brought to the trauma bay by emergency services after a motorbike accident in which the patient, who was not wearing a helmet, hit a pole of a streetlight with their head. When initially evaluated by the paramedics, the patient was responsive, albeit confused, opened their eyes spontaneously, and was able to follow commands. An hour later, upon admission, the patient only opened their eyes to painful stimuli, made incomprehensible sounds, and assumed a flexed posture. The vital signs are as follows: blood pressure 140/80 mm Hg; heart rate 59/min; respiratory rate 11/min; temperature 37.0℃ (99.1℉), and SaO2, 95% on room air. The examination shows a laceration and bruising on the left side of the head. There is anisocoria with the left pupil 3 mm more dilated than the right. Both pupils react sluggishly to light. There is an increase in tone and hyperreflexia in the right upper and lower extremities. The patient is intubated and mechanically ventilated, head elevated to 30°, and sent for a CT scan. Which of the following management strategies should be used in this patient, considering their most probable diagnosis?

A 61-year-old patient presents to the urgent care clinic complaining of cough and unintentional weight loss over the past 3 months. They work as a computer engineer, and they inform you that they have been having to meet several deadlines recently and have been under significant stress. Their medical history is significant for gout, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, diabetes mellitus type 2, and pulmonary histoplasmosis 10 years ago. They currently smoke 2 packs of cigarettes/day, drink a 6-pack of beer/day, and they endorse a past history of cocaine use back in the early 2000s but currently deny any drug use. The vital signs include: temperature 36.7°C (98.0°F), blood pressure 126/74 mm Hg, heart rate 87/min, and respiratory rate 18/min. Their physical examination shows minimal bibasilar rales, but otherwise clear lungs on auscultation, grade 2/6 holosystolic murmur, and a benign abdominal physical examination. However, on routine lab testing, you notice that their sodium is 127 mEq/L. Their chest X-ray is shown in the picture. Which of the following is the most likely underlying diagnosis?

A 38-year-old patient presents to an urgent care clinic with the complaint of epigastric discomfort and cramping pain for the past 2 hours. They state that they have experienced similar pain in the past. These episodes occur mostly after meals and often subside several hours after they finish eating. Due to this reason they mostly avoid eating. They say they have lost a few pounds in the last couple of months. They are a smoker and drink alcohol occasionally. Past medical history is insignificant except for chronic knee pain, for which they take over the counter painkillers. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), respiratory rate is 16/min, pulse is 77/min, and blood pressure is 120/89 mm Hg. A physical abdominal exam is unremarkable, including examination of the abdomen. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with fever and easy bruising for 3 days. They have had fatigue for 2 weeks. They have no past medical history, and take no medications. Excessive bleeding from intravenous lines was reported by the nurse. They do not smoke or drink alcohol. The temperature is 38.2°C (102.6°F), pulse is 105/min, respiration rate is 18/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. On physical examination, they have multiple purpura on the lower extremities and several ecchymoses on the lower back and buttocks. Petechiae are noticed on the soft palate. Cervical painless lymphadenopathy is detected on both sides. The examination of the lungs, heart, and abdomen shows no other abnormalities. The laboratory test results are as follows: Hemoglobin 8 g/dL Mean corpuscular volume 90 μm3 Leukocyte count 18,000/mm3 Platelet count 10,000/mm3 Partial thromboplastin time (activated) 60 seconds Prothrombin time 25 seconds (INR: 2.2) Fibrin split products Positive Lactate dehydrogenase, serum 1,000 U/L A Giemsa-stained peripheral blood smear is shown by the image. Intravenous fluids, blood products, and antibiotics are given to the patient. Based on the most likely diagnosis, which of the following is the best therapy for this patient at this time?

A 36-year-old patient presents to their physician with an acute burning retrosternal sensation with radiation to their jaw. This sensation began 20 minutes ago when the patient was exercising at the gym. It does not change with position or with a cough. The patient’s vital signs include: blood pressure is 140/90 mm Hg, heart rate is 84/min, respiratory rate is 14/min, and temperature is 36.6℃ (97.9℉). Physical examination is only remarkable for paleness and perspiration. The patient is given sublingual nitroglycerin, the blood is drawn for an express troponin test, and an ECG is going to be performed. At the moment of performing ECG, the patient’s symptoms are gone. ECG shows increased R amplitude in I, II V3-V6, and ST depression measuring for 0.5 mm in the same leads. The express test for troponin is negative. Which of the following tests would be reasonable to perform next to confirm a diagnosis in this patient?

A 37-year-old patient, otherwise healthy, has a routine CBC done prior to donating blood for the first time. The results are as follows: Hemoglobin 10.8 g/dL Mean corpuscular volume (MCV) 82 μm3 Mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC) 42% Reticulocyte count 3.2% White blood cell count 8,700/mm3 Platelet count 325,000/mm3 The patient is afebrile and their vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, their spleen is just palpable. A peripheral blood smear is shown in the exhibit (see image). A direct antiglobulin test (DAT) is negative. Which of the following best describes the etiology of this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old patient presents to the clinic for hair loss. They were in their usual state of health until earlier this month when they started noticing more and more hair on their pillow in the morning. The problem has only been getting worse since then; they've even started pulling out clumps of hair when they shampoo in the morning. They have no other symptoms, and their past medical history is unremarkable. The physical exam is notable for smooth, circular, non-scarring, hairless patches across their scalp. A firm tug on a bundle of hair causes almost all of the hair to be removed. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to the physician with a cough which they have had for the last 5 years. They also mention that they have been feeling breathless when playing any active sport for the last 1 year. They are a manager in a corporate company and have been a regular smoker for 10 years. They have visited multiple physicians and undergone multiple diagnostic evaluations, without permanent benefit. On physical examination their temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), the heart rate is 88/min, the blood pressure is 122/80 mm Hg, and the respiratory rate is 20/min. Inspection suggests a barrel chest and auscultation reveals the presence of bilateral end-expiratory wheezing and scattered rhonchi. They undergo a detailed diagnostic evaluation which includes a complete blood count, chest radiogram, arterial blood gas analysis, and pulmonary function tests, all of which confirm a diagnosis of chronic obstructive lung disease. After analyzing all the clinical information and diagnostic workup, the physician differentiates between emphysema and chronic bronchitis based on a single clue. Which of the following is the most likely clue that helped the physician in making the differential diagnosis?

A 64-year-old patient presents to an urgent care clinic with edema of their lips and difficulty breathing. They report that they had multiple root canals performed earlier today, and they started to notice swelling of their lips 2 hours ago. The symptoms have now progressed to where they are having trouble breathing. They note similar episodes in the past after minor procedures such as this. The blood pressure is 118/76 mm Hg, the heart rate is 84/min, and the respiratory rate is 16/min. Physical examination is remarkable for edema of their lips and mild inspiratory stridor. The laboratory results are remarkable for a low level of C1 esterase inhibitor. Of the following options, which is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old patient is brought to the clinic by their parent with fever and a rash. The patient’s parent says their symptoms started 1 week ago with the acute onset of fever and a runny nose, which resolved over the next 3 days. Then, 4 days later, they noted a rash on the patient's face, which, after a day, spread to their neck, torso, and extremities. The patient denies any pruritus or pain associated with the rash. No recent history of sore throat, chills, or upper respiratory infection. The patient has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. The vital signs include: temperature 37.2°C (99.9°F) and pulse 88/min. On physical examination, there is a maculopapular rash on the patient's face, torso, and extremities, which spares the palms and soles. The appearance of the rash is shown in the exhibit (see image below). Which of the following would most likely confirm the diagnosis in this patient?

A 39-year-old patient presents to the emergency department complaining of a sharp pain that radiates along their right hemithorax, which worsens with deep inspiration. They say this started abruptly about 6 hours ago. They say that they have not noticed that anything that makes their pain better or worse. They also deny any other symptoms. They work as a long-haul truck driver, and they inform you that they recently returned to the east coast from a trip to Utah. Their medical history is significant for gout, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, diabetes mellitus type 2, and acute lymphoblastic leukemia from when they were a child. They currently smoke 2 packs of cigarettes/day, drink a 6-pack of beer/day, and they deny any illicit drug use. The vital signs include: temperature 36.7°C (98.0°F), blood pressure 126/74 mm Hg, heart rate 98/min, and respiratory rate 23/min. Their physical examination shows minimal bibasilar rales, but otherwise clear lungs on auscultation, normal heart sounds, and a benign abdominal physical examination. Which of the following is the most reasonable 1st step towards ruling out the diagnosis of pulmonary embolism in a low-risk patient?

A 65-year-old patient who lives in New York City presents with headache, fever, and neck stiffness. They received a diagnosis of HIV infection 3 years ago and have been inconsistent with their antiretroviral medications. Recent interferon-gamma release assay testing for latent tuberculosis was negative. A computed tomography of their head is normal. A lumbar puncture shows a white blood cell count of 45/mm3 with a mononuclear predominance, the glucose level of 30 mg/dL, and a protein level of 60 mg/dL. A preparation of their cerebrospinal fluid is shown. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause of their symptoms?

A 32-year-old patient presents with hypertension that has been difficult to control with medications. Their symptoms include fatigue, frequent waking at night for voiding, and pins and needles in the legs. Their symptoms started 2 years ago. Family history is positive for hypertension in their mother. Their blood pressure is 160/100 mm Hg in the right arm and 165/107 mm Hg in the left arm, pulse is 85/min, and temperature is 36.5°C (97.7°F). Physical examination reveals global hyporeflexia and muscular weakness. Lab studies are shown: Serum sodium 147 mEq/L Serum creatinine 0.7 mg/dL Serum potassium 2.3 mEq/L Serum bicarbonate 34 mEq/L Plasma renin activity low Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old patient presents to the physician with fever, cough, weakness, night sweats, and poor appetite for the past 6 months. Medical records suggest that they have lost 7.5 kg (16.5 lb) of weight during this period. There is no history of breathlessness, nasal discharge, nasal obstruction, palpitations, chest pain, or symptoms related to digestion. They were released from prison 9 months ago after serving a 2-year sentence. Their temperature is 38.1°C (100.6°F), pulse is 84/min, respirations are 16/min, and blood pressure is 122/80 mm Hg. Physical examination shows hepatomegaly and generalized lymphadenopathy, and auscultation of the chest reveals diffuse crackles throughout the lung fields bilaterally. On direct ophthalmoscopy, three discrete, yellow-colored, 0.5 mm to 1.0 mm lesions with indistinct borders are seen in the posterior pole. A chest X-ray is shown in the image. Tuberculin skin test with purified protein derivative is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with constant and gnawing lower abdominal pain for 2 days. The pain has been steadily worsening in intensity. They say the pain occasionally radiates to their lower back and groin bilaterally. While they cannot identify any aggravating factors, they feel that the pain improves with their knees flexed. Their medical history is notable for hypertension which is well controlled with medications. They have smoked 40–50 cigarettes daily for 35 years. On examination, there is a palpable pulsatile mass just left of midline below the umbilicus. They are immediately referred for definitive management but during transfer, they become hypotensive and unresponsive. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-month-old patient presents to your office with a 5-day history of blood in their stool. Abdominal pain is notably absent on history obtained from their parents. Past medical history and physical exam findings are not remarkable. Laboratory findings are significant for mild iron deficiency. Which of the following is characteristic of this patient’s diagnosis?

A 56-year-old patient is admitted to the emergency department with sudden onset of pain, left-sided genital swelling, and nausea. The patient states that the symptoms started three hours ago after they lifted up a heavy pack. They say that the swelling had been intermittently present for several years already and was most prominent when physically straining or coughing, but it had never been painful. Past medical history is unremarkable. Patient reports a 26-pack-year history of smoking. Vital signs are as follows: blood pressure 150/90 mm Hg, heart rate 85/min, respiratory rate 14/min, and temperature 37.8℃ (100℉). BMI is 32.9 kg/m2. Patient’s respiratory and cardiovascular exams are within normal limits. The abdomen is moderately distended. There is a tender erythematous genital swelling on the left, which cannot be manually reduced. Which of the following tests should be performed to confirm the diagnosis in this patient?

A 63-year-old patient presents to your outpatient clinic complaining of headaches, blurred vision, and fatigue. They have a blood pressure of 171/91 mm Hg and heart rate of 84/min. Physical examination is unremarkable. Their lab results include K+ of 3.1mEq/L and a serum pH of 7.51. Of the following, which is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 47-year-old patient presents to the clinic with a 3-day history of severe mid-epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back. The patient has hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and hypertriglyceridemia. Prescription medications include enalapril, metformin, sitagliptin, glargine, lispro, and fenofibrate. The patient has not had a cigarette in more than 35 years, and reports only having 1 or 2 drinks during special occasions such as weddings and family reunions. The blood pressure is 146/90 mm Hg, the heart rate is 88/min, the respiratory rate is 10/min, and the temperature is 37.8°C (100.0°F). On physical examination, the patient appears uncomfortable but alert. The visualization of the sclera is negative for jaundice. The neck is supple and non-tender without nodules. There are no heart murmurs. The lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. The palpation of the abdomen elicits pain in the epigastric region. The liver is palpable along the costal margin, and the Murphy’s sign is negative. The laboratory results are as follows: Na+ 138 mEq/L K+ 4.2 mEq/L Cl- 108 mmol/L HCO-3 20 mmol/L BUN 178 mg/dL Cr 1.0 mg/dL Glucose 154 mg/dL LDL 117 mg/dL HDL 48 mg/dL TG 942 mg/dL AST 45 IU/L ALT 48 IU/L GGT 27 IU/L Amylase 110 U/L Lipase 250 U/L According to the clinical vignette, which of the following is the most likely diagnosis of the patient?

A 14-year-old patient who has been otherwise healthy presents to their doctor complaining of feeling easily winded and light-headed at basketball practice. They have never felt this way before and are frustrated because they are good enough to make varsity this year. They deny smoking, alcohol, or recreational drug use. Their parent is very worried because their oldest sibling and family member had both died suddenly while playing sports despite being otherwise healthy. The transthoracic echocardiogram confirms the suspected diagnosis, which demonstrates a preserved ejection fraction and systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve. The patient is advised that they will need to stay hydrated and avoid intense exercise, and they will likely need an ICD due to their family history. Which of the following physical exam findings is consistent with this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 53-year-old patient seeks medical care for superficial erosions and blisters over the skin of their head and trunk. They also have significant involvement of their buccal mucosa, which has made eating difficult. A year earlier, they developed tender sores on the oral mucosa and soft palate of their mouth, which was initially treated as herpes simplex stomatitis. Their condition worsened despite treatment, resulting in the development of eroded areas over their trunk and extremities, with a 10 kg weight loss. Upon further questioning, they deny itching, but they note that the top layer of their skin could be easily removed when firm horizontal pressure was applied. What is the most likely diagnosis for this patient’s condition?

A 53-year-old patient is brought to the clinic by their child for the evaluation of unusual behavior. They are a shopkeeper by profession and sometimes behave very rudely to the customers. Recently, they accused one of the customers of using black magic over their shop. They have been increasingly irritable, forgetting things, and having problems managing their finances over the past 8 months. They are also having difficulty finding words and recalling the names of objects during the conversation. There is no history of recent head trauma, fever, hallucinations, or abnormal limb movements. Past medical history is significant for a well-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus. Family history is unremarkable. They do not smoke or use illicit drugs. Vital signs are stable with a blood pressure of 134/76 mm Hg, a heart rate of 88/min, and a temperature of 37.0°C (98.6°F). On physical examination, they have problems naming objects and planning tasks. Mini-mental state examination (MMSE) score is 26/30. Cranial nerve examination is normal. Muscle strength is normal in all 4 limbs with normal muscle tone and deep tendon reflexes. Sensory examination is also normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 73-year-old patient is brought to their family practitioner by their daughter with the complaints of a spinning sensation for the past 4 weeks. They say that the room appears to be continuously spinning. This has progressively worsened over the last 4 weeks to the point that they have become bed bound and cannot walk without support. These spinning sensations are present throughout the day and do not change with position. They are associated with nausea and vomiting. They deny ear pain, ear discharge, ringing in the ear, hearing disturbances, ear fullness, head trauma, fever, or recent flu-like illness. They have a blood pressure of 133/80 mm Hg, heart rate of 80/min, respiratory rate of 12/min, and temperature of 36.7°C (98.2°F). Their extraocular eye movements are normal in all directions, but a vertical nystagmus is present that does not disappear despite repetitive testing. Hearing tests are within normal limits. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 52-year-old patient presents to the clinic with several days of vomiting and diarrhea. They also complain of headaches, muscle aches, and fever, but deny tenesmus, urgency, and bloody diarrhea. Past medical history is insignificant. When asked about any recent travel they say that they just came back from a cruise ship vacation. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6° F), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 67/min, and blood pressure is 122/98 mm Hg. Physical examination is non-contributory. Microscopic examination of the stool is negative for ova or parasites. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 51-year-old patient presents to the clinic with a history of hematuria and hemoptysis following pneumonia several weeks ago. They work as a hotel bellhop. Their medical history is significant for gout, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, diabetes mellitus type II, and mild intellectual disability. They currently smoke 2 packs of cigarettes per day and deny any alcohol use or any illicit drug use. Their vital signs include: temperature 36.7°C (98.0°F), blood pressure 126/74 mm Hg, heart rate 87/min, and respiratory rate 23/min. Physical examination shows minimal bibasilar rales, but otherwise clear lungs on auscultation, grade 2/6 holosystolic murmur, and benign abdominal findings. Pulmonary function tests demonstrate a restrictive pattern and a current chest radiograph shows bibasilar alveolar infiltrates. Clinical pathology analysis reveals antiglomerular basement membrane antibody, and their renal biopsy shows a linear immunofluorescence pattern. Of the following options, which type of hypersensitivity reaction underlies this patient’s diagnosis?

A 41-year-old patient presents to the emergency department because of brownish discoloration of their urine for the last several days. The review of symptoms includes complaints of increasing abdominal girth, early satiety, and difficulty breathing on exertion. The past medical history includes essential hypertension for 19 years. The medication list includes lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide. They had a right inguinal hernia repair when they were a teenager. They smoke 20–30 cigarettes daily for the last 21 years, and drink alcohol socially. Their father died of a hemorrhagic stroke at the age of 69 years. The vital signs include: temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F), blood pressure 131/88 mm Hg, and pulse 82/min. The physical examination is positive for a palpable right upper quadrant mass. The abdominal ultrasound shows multiple bilateral kidney cysts and hepatic cysts. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with a recent episode of chest pain. They say they were previously well and deny any history of similar symptoms. They report that, at onset, they felt as if they were going to die and say their heart has been beating really fast. There was also profuse sweating, and they say they feel short of breath. They could not recall how long the event lasted but can remember that the symptoms did go away on their own by the time they arrived at the emergency department. Their vitals rapidly returned to normal while giving their medical history and they begin to look and act more calm. No significant past medical history or current medications. Physical examination is unremarkable. Their electrocardiogram and initial cardiac enzymes are normal. Which of the following is necessary to confirm the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 35-year-old patient presents with a 7 month history of insomnia. The patient admitted to having trouble sleeping from a young age but became more aware of how much this is affecting their health after attending a sleep conference earlier this year. They are worried that their health has suffered because of this, and they are also concerned that they will not be able to pay their bills if they were to get sick. They have no past medical or psychiatric condition and are not known to use any recreational drugs. The patient arrived for their appointment an hour early because they were afraid they might miss it. The patient is afebrile and their vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination reveals an irritable middle-aged patient who is tense and somewhat inattentive during the interview. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 25-year-old patient is brought to a psychiatrist’s office by their spouse who states that they are worried about the patient's recent behavior, as it has become more violent. The patient's spouse states that their family drove across the country to visit them and that the patient ‘threatened their parents with a knife’ at dinner last night. Police had to be called to calm them down. They state that the patient has been acting ‘really crazy’ for the last 9 months, and the initial behavior that caused them alarm was the patient's admission that their deceased sibling was talking to them through a decorative piece of ceramic art in the living room. Initially, they thought the patient was joking, but soon realized the patient's complaints of ‘hearing ghosts’ talking to them throughout the house were persisting and ‘getting worse’. There was also a 4-week period where the patient experienced insomnia and an unintentional weight loss of 12 pounds. The patient seemed sad throughout these episodes, and, according to their spouse, was complaining of feeling ‘worthless’. The patient's general hygiene has also suffered from their recent lack of motivation and they insist that the ‘ghosts’ are asking them to kill as many people as they can so they won’t be alone in the house. Their spouse is extremely concerned that the patient may harm themselves or someone else. They state that the patient currently does not take any medications or illicit drugs as far as they know. The patient does not smoke or drink alcohol. The patient themselves does not make eye contact or want to speak to the psychiatrist, allowing their spouse to speak on their behalf. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 79-year-old patient who lives alone is brought to the emergency department by their neighbor because of worsening confusion over the last 2 days. Due to their level of confusion, they are unable to answer questions appropriately. They have had type 2 diabetes mellitus for 29 years for which they take metformin. Vital signs include: blood pressure 111/72 mm Hg, temperature 38.5°C (101.3°F), and pulse 100/min. Their fingerstick blood glucose is 210 mg/dL. On physical examination, they are not oriented to time or place and mistakes the nursing assistant for their cousin. Laboratory results are shown: Hemoglobin 13 g/dL Leukocyte count 16,000/mm3 Segmented neutrophils 70% Eosinophils 1% Basophils 0.3% Lymphocytes 25% Monocytes 4% Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department with minor injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident. They say that they are fine. They also witnessed the death of a teenage girl in the accident who was their sister’s friend. They are able to return to work within a few days. A month later, they present being withdrawn and increasingly irritable. They say recently they have been experiencing depressed moods and higher anxiety than usual. They say that they feel guilty about the girl’s death, stating that they could have saved her if only they had acted quicker. They add that they became extremely anxious while driving by a car accident on the freeway recently, and that, even when watching television or a movie, they feel panicked during a car crash scene. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 51-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician complaining of months of dry mouth and dry eyes. They say the dryness has become so severe that they have difficulty swallowing food. They have a history of hypertension, for which they take hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ), but they have no other medical problems. Family history is significant for their grandmother having systemic lupus erythematosus. The vital signs include: blood pressure 118/76 mm Hg, heart rate 78/min, and respiratory rate 15/min. On physical exam, they have tender parotid glands bilaterally and dry mucous membranes. The presence of serum anti-Ro and anti-La autoantibodies is confirmed at high titers. In addition to their primary diagnosis, which of the following is this patient most at risk for developing in the future?

A 10-year-old patient is brought to the physician because of fever and bloody diarrhea for the past few days. Their parents report that they have become increasingly lethargic and irritable. Their temperature is 38.6°C (101.4°F), pulse is 102/min, and respirations are 22/min. They have no significant past medical history. Their parents say that they mostly only eat a diet of chicken, hamburgers, fries, cheese, and milk. On physical examination, pallor and edema in both legs are present. Their laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 8.9 gm/dL Leukocyte count 9,300/mm3 Platelet count 67,000/mm3 Blood urea nitrogen 43 mg/dL Serum creatinine 2.46 mg/dL Coombs test Negative Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old patient presents to their primary care practitioner, complaining about the presence of white spots in both of their hands. They state that the white spots have expanded in the last few months; they are not tender nor ulcerated. Their past medical history is relevant for hypothyroidism. Upon physical examination, the patient shows hypopigmented macules on both hands and on the back and shoulders adjacent to a patch of skin, with signs of excoriation and scratching. Under the Wood’s lamp, the skin lesions on the hands, back, and shoulders show fluorescence. There are no signs of inflammation in any of the skin lesions. The vital signs of the patient are within normal limits. Which is the most likely diagnosis of this condition?

A 52-year-old patient presents with fatigue, difficulty swallowing solid foods, and frequent choking spells. They say their symptoms gradually onset 3 months ago and have progressively worsened. Past medical history is unremarkable. They report drinking alcohol occasionally but deny smoking or illicit drug use. Their vital signs include: temperature 36.6°C (97.8°F), blood pressure 115/72 mm Hg, pulse 82/min. Physical examination shows conjunctival pallor but is otherwise unremarkable. Laboratory results are significant for the following: Hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL Red cell count 2.5 million/mm3 Mean corpuscular volume 73 μm3 Serum ferritin 9.7 ng/mL A barium swallow study is performed, which shows a proximal esophageal web. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 45-year-old patient is brought to the Emergency Department by their spouse due to increasing confusion. They report that the patient has been urinating a lot for the past month or so, especially at night, and has also been constantly drinking water and tea. Lately, the patient has been more tired than usual as well. The patient's past medical history is significant for bipolar disorder. They take lithium and a multivitamin. The patient has an intrauterine device (IUD). Their blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, pulse rate is 95/min, respiratory rate is 16/min, and temperature is 36°C (96.8°F). At physical examination, the patient is drowsy and disoriented. Their capillary refill is delayed and their mucous membranes appear dry. The rest of the exam is nondiagnostic. Laboratory studies show: Na+: 148 mEq/L K+: 4.2 mEq/L Serum calcium: 11.0 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL Urine osmolality: 190 mOsm/kg Serum osmolality: 280 mOsm/kg Finger-stick glucose: 120 mg/dL Fluid resuscitation is initiated. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old patient is brought in by their parent with reports of trouble at school. Teachers report that for the last 6 months they have been having difficulty finishing tasks, is easily distracted, frequently does not listen, commonly fails to finish schoolwork, has not been able to complete any of the class projects this year, and frequently loses school books and supplies. Teachers also say that they constantly fidget, often leave their seat without permission, have trouble being quiet, talk excessively, frequently interrupt their classmates when trying to answer questions, and have difficulty waiting in line. The parent states that they have also been noticing similar behaviors at home and that their symptoms have been affecting them negatively academically and socially. The patient has no significant past medical history. The patient is in the 90th percentile for height and weight and has been meeting all the developmental milestones. They are afebrile, and their vital signs are within normal limits. A physical examination is unremarkable. Which of the following medications is a first-line treatment for this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old patient is brought to the pediatrician with fever, diarrhea and bilateral red eye for 7 days. Their parents noted that they have never had an episode of diarrhea this prolonged, but several other children at daycare had been ill. Their immunization history is up to date. Their vitals are normal except for a temperature of 37.5°C (99°F). A physical exam is significant for mild dehydration, preauricular adenopathy, and bilateral conjunctival injection with watery discharge. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to clinic with recurrent episodes of abdominal discomfort and pain for the past month. They report that the pain occurs 2-3 hours after meals, usually at midnight, and rates it as moderate to severe in intensity when it occurs. They also complain of being fatigued all the time. Past medical history is insignificant. They are an office secretary and say that the job has been very stressful recently. Their temperature is 98.6°F (37.0°C), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 67/min, and blood pressure is 122/98 mm Hg. Their BMI is 34. A physical examination reveals conjunctival pallor and mild tenderness over the epigastric region. Blood tests show: Hb%: 10 gm/dL Total count (WBC): 11,000 /mm3 Differential count: Neutrophils: 70% Lymphocytes: 25% Monocytes: 5% ESR: 10 mm/hr Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old patient is brought to the doctor’s office by their mother because the patient believes aliens have begun to read their mind and will soon have them performing missions for them. The patient’s mother says that the delusions have been intermittently present for periods of at least 1-month over the past year. When they are not having delusions, she says they still lack expression and have no interest in socializing with their friends or going out. They have no past medical history and take no prescription medications. The patient has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the past 10 years. Since the disturbance, they have not been able to maintain employment and live at home with their mother. Their vitals include: blood pressure 124/82 mm Hg, pulse 68/min, respiratory rate 14/min, temperature 37.3°C (99.1°F). On physical examination, the patient exhibits poor eye contact with a flat affect. Their speech is circumferential, and they are currently experiencing bizarre delusions. The results from a urine drug screen are shown below: Amphetamine negative Benzodiazepine negative Cocaine negative GHB negative Ketamine negative LSD negative Marijuana negative Opioids negative PCP negative Which of the following is the correct diagnosis?

A 68-year-old patient presents to the hospital for an elective right hemicolectomy. They are independently mobile and do their own shopping. They have had type 2 diabetes mellitus for 20 years, essential hypertension for 15 years, and angina on exertion for 6 years. They have a 30-pack-year history of smoking. The operation was uncomplicated. On post-op day 5, they become confused. They have a temperature of 38.5°C (101.3°F), respiratory rate of 28/min, and oxygen saturation of 92% on 2 L of oxygen. They are tachycardic at 118/min and their blood pressure is 110/65 mm Hg. On chest auscultation, they have coarse crackles in the right lung base. Their surgical wound appears to be healing well, and their abdomen is soft and nontender. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 50-year-old patient from India visits their physician complaining of worsening respiratory symptoms. They state that they were diagnosed with emphysema 4 years ago and that, over the past several months, they have developed a chronic productive cough, dyspnea, fatigue, unexplained weight loss, and night sweats. They note that they also have other complaints aside from their lung problems, including sharp, intermittent chest pain and joint pain in their elbows and knees. There is also an erythematous rash on both the lower extremities that features raised lesions; it is determined to be erythema nodosum. Cardiac examination reveals a friction rub, and a computed tomography (CT) scan of the chest reveals cavitation of both lung apices. The patient is isolated for the suspicion of active tuberculosis (TB) infection. A purified protein derivative (PPD) test is negative. Sputum sample staining fails to reveal acid-fast bacilli, but it does reveal yeast forms that are replicating by narrow-based budding. Which of the following would aid in making a correct diagnosis in this patient?

A 62-year-old patient has been receiving amoxicillin for acute sinusitis for 12 days. They develop a macular rash on their neck, back, and torso. The amoxicillin is therefore changed to cephalexin for an additional week.
