The rash resolves, but they return complaining of fatigue, flank pain, and fever that has persisted despite the resolution of the sinusitis. They have a history of essential hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and gastric reflux. They have been on a stable regimen of lisinopril, simvastatin, and omeprazole. Today, their vital signs reveal: temperature 37.9°C (100.2°F), blood pressure 145/90 mm Hg, regular pulse 75/min, and respirations 16/min. The physical examination is unremarkable. Serum urea and creatinine are elevated. Urinalysis shows leukocyturia, but urine bacterial culture is negative. A urine cytospin stained with Hansel’s solution reveals 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old patient presents to the family medicine clinic for some small bumps on their left thigh. The lesions are non-pruritic and have been present for the last 3 weeks. They report feeling fatigued and malaise for the past few months. The patient has no known medical problems and takes no medications. They smoke one pack of cigarettes per day and use intravenous street drugs. Their heart rate is 82/min, the respiratory rate is 14/min, the temperature is 36.7°C (98.1°F), and the blood pressure is 126/80 mm Hg. Auscultation of the heart is without murmurs. Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Three 2-3 mm, dome-shaped, hardened papules are noted on the left thigh. Central umbilication can be observed in each papule. There is a non-tender cervical lymphadenopathy present. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 63-year-old African American patient presents to the emergency department with edema over their face and difficulty breathing. Past medical history is significant for hypertension and dyslipidemia. They recently began lisinopril and atorvastatin several weeks ago. Their father died at 80 years from complications of a stroke and their mother lives in a nursing home. Their blood pressure is 135/92 mm Hg, the heart rate is 101/min, the respiratory rate is 21/min, the temperature is 32.0°C (98.6°F). Clinical pathology results suggest a normal C1 esterase inhibitor level. Of the following options, which is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-year-old patient presents with a 1-month history of gradual onset of pain immediately below their right kneecap. They have recently started playing basketball for the junior varsity team at their school, and they are very excited for the season to begin. Unfortunately, the pain in their knee is exacerbated by all the jumping activity during practice. The patient reports similar pain when climbing up and down the stairs. They deny any previous history of knee injury. Physical examination reveals full range of motion of their knee, but the pain is reproduced when the knee is extended against resistance. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old patient presents to the clinic complaining of a headache, runny nose, and malaise. A few minutes into the interview, they mention that they recently started their job and are glad to work long hours despite the toll on their health. However, they admit that they are finding it difficult to keep up with the workload. They have numerous pending papers to correct. When advised to seek help from other teachers, they exclaim that it needs to be done in a particular way, and only they can do it the right way. This is causing them to perform poorly at work, and they are at risk of being asked to quit their very first job. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 61-year-old patient presents to an outpatient clinic with fatigue and mild neck pain for a month. They add that they are having difficulty swallowing. They deny trouble with their breathing but endorse 5–10 lb of unintentional weight loss over the past few months. On physical exam, the patient’s fingernails appear flat and mild conjunctival pallor is noted. An upper barium esophagram shows an upper esophageal web. A complete blood count reveals: Hb% 10 gm/dL Total count (WBC) 11,000 /mm3 Differential count: Neutrophile 70% Lymphocytes 25% Monocytes 5% ESR 10 mm/hr What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old patient presents with continuous feelings of sadness and rejection. They say that over the past couple of weeks, they have been unable to concentrate on their job and have missed several days of work. They also have no interest in any activity and typically reject invitations to go out with friends. They have no interest in food or playing with their dog. Their partner is concerned about this change in behavior. A few months ago, they were very outgoing and made many plans with friends. They remember being easily distracted and also had several ‘brilliant ideas’ on what they should be doing with their life. They did not sleep much during that week, but now all they want to do is lie in bed all day. They deny any suicidal or homicidal ideations. They have no past medical history and have never been hospitalized. Laboratory tests were normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 32-year-old patient comes to the office complaining of right-sided upper abdominal pain for about 2 weeks. They are also complaining of subjective fever and malaise for the same duration. They have never been out of the United States. Additionally, they describe several episodes of bloody diarrhea and crampy abdominal pain that resolved on their own a few months ago. Travel history is noncontributory. They have been sexually active with 3 partners in the last year and use a condom inconsistently. They were diagnosed with syphilis 4 months ago and were treated with a single shot of penicillin. They have smoked 1 pack of cigarettes per day for the last 10 years and drinks 1–2 beers a day. Temperature is 38.7°C (101.6°F), blood pressure is 137/78 mm Hg, pulse is 98/min, respirations are 14/min, and BMI is 22 kg/m2. On physical examination, their liver is tender and palpable 2 cm below the right costal margin. Laboratory test Hemoglobin 15 g/dL Leucocyte and differential Leucocyte count 12,500/mm3 Neutrophil 60% Lymphocyte 31% Eosinophil 1% Liver function test ALT 100 U/L AST 95 U/L ALP 220 U/L CT scan of the abdomen shows a single cystic lesion on the right lobe of the liver. What is the diagnosis?

A 48-year-old patient presents to the physician because of facial flushing and weakness for 3 months, abdominal discomfort and bloating for 6 months, and profuse watery diarrhea for 1 year. They report that their diarrhea was episodic initially, but it has been continuous for the past 3 months. The frequency ranges from 10 to 12 bowel movements per day, and the diarrhea persists even if they are fasting. They describe the stools as odorless, watery in consistency, and tea-colored, without blood or mucus. They have not been diagnosed with any specific medical conditions, and there is no history of substance use. Their temperature is 36.9°C (98.4°F), heart rate is 88/min, respiratory rate is 18/min, and blood pressure is 110/74 mm Hg. Their physical exam shows decreased skin turgor, and the abdominal exam does not reveal any significant abnormality. Laboratory studies show: Serum glucose 216 mg/dL (12.0 mmol/L) Serum sodium 142 mEq/L (142 mmol/L) Serum potassium 3.1 mEq/L (3.1 mmol/L) Serum chloride 100 mEq/L (100 mmol/L) Serum calcium 11.1 mg/dL (2.77 mmol/L) Their 24-hour stool volume is 4 liters. Which of the following tests is most likely to yield an accurate diagnosis?

A 28-year-old patient presents with depressed mood lasting for most days of the week for the past month. They also mention that they have lost their appetite for the past 3 weeks. They add that their job performance has significantly deteriorated because of these symptoms, and they feel like they will have to quit their job soon. Upon asking about their hobbies, they say that they used to enjoy dancing and music but do not have any desire to do them anymore. The patient’s partner says that they have had many sleepless nights last month. The patient denies any history of smoking, alcohol intake, or use of illicit substances. No significant past medical history. Physical examination is unremarkable. Routine laboratory tests are all within normal limits. Which of the following clinical features must be present, in addition to this patient’s current symptoms, to confirm the diagnosis of a major depressive episode?

A 25-year-old patient is admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) with hematemesis and shock. Five days ago they had a severe fever 40.0℃ (104.0℉), retro-orbital pain, nausea, and myalgias. The high temperatures decreased over a few days, but they developed severe abdominal pain and bleeding gums. A single episode of hematemesis occurred prior to ICU admission. They travel to Latin America every winter. Two weeks ago, they traveled to Brazil and spent most of their time outdoors. They are restless. The temperature is 38.0℃ (100.4℉), the pulse is 110/min, the respiration rate is 33/min, and the blood pressure is 90/70 mm Hg. Conjunctival suffusion is seen. The extremities are cold. A maculopapular rash covers the trunk and extremities. Ecchymoses are observed on the lower extremities. The lung bases reveal absent sounds with dullness to percussion. The abdomen is distended. The liver edge is palpable and liver span is 15 cm. Shifting dullness is present. The laboratory studies show the following: Laboratory test Hemoglobin 16.5 g/dL Leukocyte count 3500/mm3 Segmented neutrophils 55% Lymphocytes 30% Platelet count 90,000/mm3 Serum Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 75 U/L Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 70 U/L Total bilirubin 0.8 mg/dL Direct bilirubin 0.2 mg/dL Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old patient is being evaluated by their primary care physician for chronic, widespread pain that started around 5 months ago. This pain has been accompanied by sleeping issues. Their friend recommended that they try yoga to relieve the pain, but they say this has not helped them at all. They say the symptoms have begun to impact their daily functions and keep them from doing things they used to enjoy. Past medical history includes generalized anxiety disorder, for which they currently take no medication. The patient had been previously medicated with paroxetine for 5 years. On physical examination, several areas of point tenderness are found on the occipital region, elbows, and medial surface of both knees. Laboratory work up is unremarkable. What is the best treatment option for the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 75-year-old patient presents to the physician for their annual blood pressure visit and blood work. They have no complaints other than occasional knee pain. The past medical history includes hypertension. They have had knee osteoarthritis for several years and take occasional acetaminophen for pain control. Their diet is full of vegetables. They exercise every day. They have no history of smoking. They had a sibling who died at the age of 84 due to hematologic malignancy. The temperature is 36.8℃ (98.2℉), and the blood pressure is 125/85 mm Hg. The physical examination shows no abnormalities other than a reduced range of motion and crepitus in both knees. The laboratory test results are as follows: Hemoglobin 15 g/dL Leukocyte count 58,000/mm3 Platelet count 250,000/mm3 Flow cytometry on the peripheral blood reveals an absolute lymphocyte count of 50,000/mm3. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old patient, one day postpartum, has a newborn with bluish discoloration of the lips and fingernails. The newborn's temperature is 37.3°C (99.1°F), the pulse is 166/min, the respirations are 63/min, and the blood pressure is 68/44 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 81%. Examination shows central cyanosis. A grade 2/6 holosystolic murmur is heard over the left lower sternal border. A single second heart sound is present. Supplemental oxygen does not improve cyanosis. An X-ray of the chest shows an enlarged cardiac silhouette with a narrowed mediastinum. Which of the following cardiac defects would be associated with this newborn’s diagnosis?

A 63-year-old African American patient with a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia presents to the emergency department with facial swelling and difficulty breathing. Symptoms began suddenly that morning and continued to worsen. They started taking lisinopril several weeks ago. Their blood pressure is 110/74 mm Hg, heart rate is 94/min, and respiratory rate is 20/min. Physical examination is notable for swelling of their lips and inspiratory stridor. Clinical lab results suggest a normal C1 esterase inhibitor level. Of the following options, which is the most likely diagnosis?

A 41-year-old patient presents to the clinic with the complaints of abdominal discomfort and cramping for the past 4 months. They also mention that they have grossly bloody stool and most of the time an urge to defecate. They have a history of bulimia with laxative abuse several years ago. They admit having lost about 5 lb in the past month. Their temperature is 37° C (98.6° F), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 77/min, and blood pressure is 105/86 mm Hg. On physical examination, a mild conjunctival pallor is evident, and the rectum is erythematous, indurated, and tender. Colonoscopy demonstrates continuous mucosal lesions throughout the rectum to the hepatic flexure of the colon. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 11-year-old patient presents with a 1-day history of frothy brown urine. They have no significant medical history and take no medications. They report that several of their classmates have been sick, and they note that they had a very sore throat with a fever approx. 2 weeks ago. Their blood pressure is 146/94 mm Hg, heart rate is 74/min, and respiratory rate is 14/min. Laboratory analysis reveals elevated serum creatinine, hematuria with RBC casts, and elevated urine protein without frank proteinuria. Physical examination reveals a healthy-looking patient with no abdominal or costovertebral angle tenderness. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient is brought by their spouse with a complaint of an ongoing progressive history of memory problems for 6 months. They are an accountant by profession. They have difficulty remembering things and events, which has affected their job. They began using a diary to aid with remembering their agenda. Their spouse also says that they have wet their pants multiple times in the past 2 months and they avoid going out. They have been smoking 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the past 20 years. Their past medical history is unremarkable. The vital signs include: blood pressure of 134/76 mm Hg, a pulse of 70 per minute, and a temperature of 37.0°C (98.6°F). Their mini-mental state examination (MMSE) result is 22/30. Their extraocular movements are normal. The muscle tone and strength are normal in all 4 limbs. The sensory examination is unremarkable. They have an absent Romberg’s sign. They walk slowly, taking small steps, with feet wide apart as if their feet are stuck to the floor. The CT scan of the head is shown in the image. What is the most likely diagnosis of the patient?

A 38-year-old patient presents with anxiety. They say that, for as long as they can remember, they have been anxious, especially when at work or in social situations, which they have difficulty controlling. They also report difficulty sleeping, irritability, and muscle tension. They say their symptoms have significantly limited their work and personal relationships. They have no other significant past medical history. The patient denies any history of smoking, alcohol consumption or recreational drug use. They are afebrile, and their vital signs are within normal limits. A physical examination is unremarkable. Which of the following medications would be the most appropriate first-line treatment for this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old patient presents to the clinic with several days of flatulence and greasy, foul-smelling diarrhea. They say that they were on a camping trip last week after which their symptoms started. When asked further about their camping activities, they report collecting water from a stream but did not boil or chemically treat the water. The patient also reports nausea, weight loss, and abdominal cramps followed by sudden diarrhea. They deny tenesmus, urgency, and bloody diarrhea. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6° F), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 107/min, and blood pressure is 89/58 mm Hg. A physical examination is performed where nothing significant was found except for dry mucous membranes. Intravenous fluids are started and a stool sample is sent to the lab, which reveals motile protozoa on microscopy, negative for any ova, no blood cells, and pus cells. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An obese 50-year-old patient presents to the emergency department of a rural hospital due to chest pain for the last 12 hours. The pain is substernal, crushing in nature, radiating into their neck, and accompanied by profuse sweating. Their history is significant for hypertension, and they admit poor compliance with their medications. An ECG done at the clinic confirmed the presence of STEMI, and the patient was given aspirin. The ambulance was in an accident on the way to the hospital and by the time the patient reached the angiography suite, the cardiologist decided intervention should be delayed due to the late presentation. Also, the patient’s pain has improved. The patient is admitted and is stable for 3 nights with no dyspnea or edema. Their blood pressure is kept under control while in the hospital. On the fourth night, the patient becomes quite agitated and soon thereafter they are unresponsive. Their pulse cannot be palpated. They have an elevated JVP and upon auscultation, heart sounds are distant. What is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 31-year-old patient presents with a 2-day history of watery diarrhea that began 8 days after their arrival from Africa. None of the other members of their family became ill. They report symptoms of malaise, anorexia, and abdominal cramps followed by watery diarrhea. They deny tenesmus, urgency, and bloody diarrhea. Their temperature is 98.6°F (37°C), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 107/min, and blood pressure is 90/68 mm Hg. A physical examination is performed and is within normal limits. Intravenous fluids are started, and a stool sample is sent to the lab, which comes out to be negative for any ova/parasites, blood cells, or pus cells. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old patient is brought to the behavioral health clinic by their roommate. The patient’s roommate says that the patient has been looking for cameras that aliens planted in their apartment for the past 2 weeks. Approximately 3 months prior to the onset of this episode, the roommate says the patient stopped playing basketball daily because the sport no longer interested them. They stayed in their bedroom most of the day and were often tearful. The roommate recalls the patient talking about death frequently. The patient states they have been skipping many meals and has lost a significant amount of weight as a result. At the time their delusions about the aliens began, the depressive-related symptoms were no longer present. They have no other medical conditions. They do not drink but smokes 2 packs of cigarettes daily for the past 5 years. Their vitals include: blood pressure 130/88 mm Hg, pulse 92/min, respiratory rate 16/min, temperature 37.3°C (99.1°F). On physical examination, the patient seems apathetic and uses an obscure word that appears to be ‘chinterfittle’. Their affect is flat throughout the entire interaction. They are experiencing bizarre delusions but no hallucinations. The patient does not express suicidal or homicidal ideations. Urine drug screen results are provided below: Amphetamine negative Benzodiazepine negative Cocaine negative GHB negative Ketamine negative LSD negative Marijuana positive Opioids negative PCP negative Which of the following is the correct diagnosis?

A 53-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department for confusion. They were in their usual state of health until about 3 hours ago when they tried to use their sandwich to turn off the TV. They also complained to their spouse that they had a severe headache. Past medical history is notable for hypertension, which has been difficult to control on multiple medications. Their temperature is 36.7°C (98°F), the pulse is 70/min, and the blood pressure is 206/132 mm Hg. On physical exam they are alert and oriented only to themselves, repeating over and over that their head hurts. The physical exam is otherwise unremarkable and their neurologic exam is nonfocal. The noncontrast CT scan of the patient’s head is shown. Which of the following diagnostic tests is likely to reveal the diagnosis for this patient?

A 12-year-old patient presents with a 3-day history of frothy brown urine. They do not complain of any other symptoms. They note that 3 weeks ago they had a fever with a sore throat, but they did not receive any treatment at the time. Their blood pressure is 152/94 mm Hg, heart rate is 72/min, respiratory rate is 15/min, and temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F). Review of their medical record shows that their blood pressure was 118/74 mm Hg just 4 weeks ago. Laboratory analysis reveals elevated serum creatinine, hematuria with RBC casts, and elevated urine protein without frank proteinuria. What laboratory test can confirm the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

An 8-year-old patient is brought to the pediatrician by their parent with nausea, vomiting, and decreased frequency of urination. They have acute lymphoblastic leukemia for which they received the 1st dose of chemotherapy 5 days ago. Their leukocyte count was 60,000/mm3 before starting chemotherapy. The vital signs include: pulse 110/min, temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F), and blood pressure 100/70 mm Hg. The physical examination shows bilateral pedal edema. Which of the following serum studies and urinalysis findings will be helpful in confirming the diagnosis of this condition?

A 8-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their parents because they complained of very fast heartbeats. The patient has previously been healthy without any childhood illnesses and has not needed to visit a physician in the past 2 years. On examination, the heart rate is 198/min. Further examination by the physician reveals a grade III holosystolic murmur over the anterior chest wall. ECG is immediately performed after their heart rate is reduced, and shows a short P-R interval with a slow upstroke of the QRS complex. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 65-year-old patient presents with painless swelling of the neck over the past week. They also have noted severe night sweats, which require a change of clothes and bed linens the next day. Their medical history is significant for long-standing hypertension. They received a kidney transplant 6 years ago. Their current medications include amlodipine, metoprolol, furosemide, aspirin, tacrolimus, and mycophenolate. Their family history is significant for a sister, who died last year from lymphoma. A review of systems is positive for a 6-kg (13.2-lb) unintentional weight loss over the past 2 months. Their vital signs include: temperature 37.8℃ (100.0℉) and blood pressure 120/75 mm Hg. On physical examination, there are multiple painless lymph nodes, averaging 2 cm in diameter, palpable in the anterior and posterior triangles of the neck bilaterally. Axillary and inguinal lymphadenopathy is palpated on the right side. Abdominal examination is significant for a spleen of 16 cm below the cost margin on percussion. Laboratory studies are significant for the following: Hemoglobin 9 g/dL Mean corpuscular volume 88 μm3 Leukocyte count 12,000/mm3 Platelet count 130,000/mm3 Creatinine 1.1 mg/dL Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) 1 000 U/L A peripheral blood smear is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 47-year-old morbidly obese patient presents to the Emergency Department with complaints of profound nausea, diarrhea, and malaise. Their past surgical history is significant for undergoing a laparoscopic gastric bypass procedure seven weeks ago for weight reduction. They have lost 15 kg since the surgery and currently, their BMI is 41 kg/m2. Their only medications are vitamins. Blood pressure is 84/40 mm Hg and heart rate is 127/min. They are afebrile. Their abdomen is distended and tympanitic with some diffuse tenderness. An abdominal X-ray and without oral contrast demonstrates a diffusely dilated small-bowel without any obvious distal decompressed bowel nor any abdominal free air. What is this patient’s diagnosis likely related to?

A 4-year-old patient is brought to the physician with a 3-month history of progressive intermittent pain and swelling involving both knees, right ankle, and right wrist. The patient has been undergoing treatment with acetaminophen and ice packs, both of which relieved their symptoms. The affected joints feel "stuck” and are difficult to move immediately upon waking up in the morning. However, the patient can move their joints freely after a few minutes. They also complain of occasional mild eye pain that resolves spontaneously. Five months ago, they were diagnosed with an upper respiratory tract infection that resolved without treatment. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows swollen and erythematous joints, which are tender to touch. Slit-lamp examination shows an anterior chamber flare with signs of iris inflammation bilaterally. Laboratory studies show: Blood parameters Hemoglobin 12.6 g/dL Leukocyte count 8,000/mm3 Segmented neutrophils 76% Eosinophils 1% Lymphocytes 20% Monocytes 3% Platelet count 360,000/mm3 Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 36 mm/hr Serum parameters Antinuclear antibodies 1:320 Rheumatoid factor negative Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old patient presents with a dry cough. The patient’s parent states that the cough started a week ago and has not improved. They say the patient will have fits of forceful coughing that will last for minutes, followed by gasping as they catch their breath. Occasionally, the patient will vomit after one of these episodes. Past medical history is significant for a recent upper respiratory infection 4 weeks ago that has resolved. No current medications. Patient immunization status is incomplete because their parent believes they are harmful. Vitals are temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F), blood pressure 105/65 mm Hg, pulse 101/min, respiratory rate 27/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air. Cardiac exam is normal. Lungs are clear to auscultation. There are conjunctival hemorrhages present bilaterally. Which of the following correctly describes the stage of this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to the internal medicine clinic with complaints of numbness and tingling in their fingers that they first noticed 6 months ago. It has been progressively worsening and has reached the point where it is affecting their normal daily activities, such as brushing their teeth. Their past medical history is significant for sinusitis and allergic rhinitis since the age of 18, as well as episodic wheezing and shortness of breath since they were 30. They were diagnosed with asthma when they were 22 years old, and subsequently with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) when they were 40. Their current medications include albuterol, loratadine, mometasone, and omeprazole. Their blood pressure is 128/86 mm Hg, heart rate is 78/min, and respiratory rate is 16/min. On physical exam, the patient’s skin is mottled and appears to have a diffuse, lace-like, erythematous discoloration of the arms, legs, and trunk. There is also a small papular rash on their right forearm. Bilateral wheezes are heard on auscultation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old patient is brought in by their parent because they are concerned that the patient has been “acting differently recently”. They say the patient no longer seems interested in playing with their friends from preschool, and they have noticed that the patient has stopped making eye contact with others. In addition, they say the patient flaps their hands when excited or angry and only seems to enjoy playing with objects that they can place in rows or rigid patterns. Despite these behaviors, the patient is meeting their language goals for their age (single word use). The patient has no significant past medical history. They are at the 90th percentile for height and weight for their age. They are afebrile and their vital signs are within normal limits. A physical examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 55-year-old patient presents with bloody nasal secretions and shortness of breath. They report having lost 4 kg (8.8 lb) in the last two months with no changes in their diet. They have also been suffering from mild to moderate joint pain in the left knee for the last year. Their past medical history is unremarkable. Their vitals include: blood pressure 120/70 mm Hg, temperature 37.0℃ (98.6℉), pulse 70/min, respiratory rate 14/min. Physical examination is significant for nasal ulcers. Diffuse crackles are present over all lobes of the lung bilaterally. Laboratory findings are significant for the following: Hemoglobin 12.9 g/dL Hematocrit 37.7% Leukocyte count 5500/mm3 Neutrophils 65% Lymphocytes 30% Monocytes 5% Mean corpuscular volume 82.2 μm3 Platelet count 190,000/mm3 Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 35 mm/h C-reactive protein 14 mg/dL Creatinine 3.09 mg/dL The patient is prescribed a corticosteroid nasal spray and oral antibiotics but returns in 2 weeks without any clinical improvement. Which of the following would most likely confirm the diagnosis in this patient?

A 15-year-old patient is brought to the physician with an ongoing pruritic rash for 1 week. The rash is on their right forearm (refer to the image). They have not had a similar rash in the past. They have no history of allergies, and they are not taking any medications. They frequently enjoy gardening in their backyard. They have no household pets. The physical examination reveals no other abnormalities. Given the most likely diagnosis, which of the following is the most appropriate treatment of the condition described in this case?

A 59-year-old patient presents to their family practitioner with their spouse. They have fallen several times over the past 3 months. Standing up from a seated position is especially difficult for them. They also complain of intermittent dizziness, excessive sweating, constipation, and difficulty performing activities of daily living. They deny fever, jerking of the limbs, memory disturbances, urinary incontinence, and abnormal limb movements. Past medical history includes a cholecystectomy 25 years ago and occasional sexual dysfunction. They take a vitamin supplement with calcium and occasionally use medication for sexual dysfunction. While supine, their blood pressure is 142/74 mm Hg and their heart rate is 64/min. After standing, their blood pressure is 118/60 mm Hg and their heart rate is 62/min. They are alert and oriented with a flat affect while answering questions. Extraocular movements are intact in all directions. No tremors are noticed. Muscle strength is normal in all limbs but with increased muscle tone. They are slow in performing intentional movements. Their writing is small and they take slow steps during walking with adducted arms and a slightly reduced arm swing. A trial of levodopa did not improve their symptoms. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 64-year-old patient presents for the scheduled annual physical examination for management of their hypertension. The patient is asymptomatic and their blood pressure is within normal limits throughout the year. They have a past medical history of polyarthrosis, and they are a carrier of hepatitis B antibodies. They do not smoke or drink alcohol. They are currently taking the following medications: enalapril, ranitidine, and lorazepam. The vital signs include: pulse rate 72/min, respiratory rate 14/min, blood pressure 138/76 mm Hg, and temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F). The physical examination shows no abnormalities. The laboratory test results are shown below: Hemoglobin 11.6 g/dL Hematocrit 34.8% MCV 91.4 fL MCH 31.4 pg Platelets 388,000/mm3 Leukocytes 7,300/mm3 ESR 59 mm/h On account of these laboratory test results, the patient was once again questioned for symptoms that would explain the abnormality detected in their laboratory test results. The patient insists that they are asymptomatic. Therefore, further laboratory studies were requested. The additional laboratory test results are shown below: PCR 5.3 mg/dL Serum protein electrophoresis Total proteins 7.4 g/dL Albumin 5.8 g/dL Alpha-1 3.5 g/dL Alpha-2 1 g/dL Beta 0.9 g/dL Gamma 1.7 g/dL The gamma protein was later confirmed as an immunoglobulin G (IgG) kappa paraprotein (1,040 mg/dL). Due to these results a computed tomography (CT) scan was conducted, and it showed moderate osteopathy without any other lesions. A bone marrow biopsy was done that showed 5–10% plasma cells. Which of the following is most likely associated with the diagnosis of this patient?

A 45-year-old patient presents with a 2-year history of fatigue, paresthesia, diarrhea, and abdominal pain. They say they experience 2–3 episodes of non-bloody diarrhea per month associated with crampy abdominal pain. They also have the bilateral tingling sensation of their upper and lower limbs in a glove and stocking pattern which is sometimes associated with the burning sensation of their hands and legs. Past medical history is unremarkable. The patient denies smoking, alcohol consumption, illicit drug use. Their vital signs include: blood pressure 100/60 mm Hg without postural changes, heart rate 92/min, respiratory rate 16/min, temperature 37.0℃ (98.6℉). Laboratory findings are significant for the following: Hgb 7.2 gm/dL MCV 110 fL RBC 3.6 X109/L Platelets 10,000/mm3 Total count 4,200/mm3 Reticulocyte 0.8% A peripheral blood smear demonstrates hypersegmented neutrophils. Anti-intrinsic factor and anti-tissue transglutaminase antibodies were negative. An upper GI series with small bowel follow-through is performed which shows a narrowing of the barium contrast in the lumen of the terminal ileum to the width of a string. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A day after percutaneous coronary intervention for stable angina, a 63-year-old patient develops severe pain in their right small toe. They have no history of a similar episode. They have had diabetes mellitus for 16 years. After the procedure, their blood pressure is 145/90 mm Hg, the pulse is 65/min, the respiratory rate is 15/min, and the temperature is 36.7°C (98.1°F). Physical examination of the femoral artery access site shows no abnormalities. Distal pulses are palpable and symmetric. A photograph of the toe is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old patient presents to the behavioral health clinic for an evaluation after seeing animal-shaped clouds in the form of dogs, cats, and monkeys. The patient says that these symptoms have been present for more than 2 weeks. Past medical history is significant for simple partial seizures for which they take valproate, but they have not had their medication adjusted in several years. Their vital signs include: blood pressure of 124/76 mm Hg, heart rate of 98/min, respiratory rate of 12/min, and temperature of 37.1°C (98.8°F). On physical examination, the patient is alert and oriented to person, time, and place. Affect is not constricted or flat. Speech is of rapid rate and high volume. Pupils are equal and reactive bilaterally. The results of a urine drug screen are as follows: Alcohol positive Amphetamine negative Benzodiazepine negative Cocaine positive GHB negative Ketamine negative LSD negative Marijuana negative Opioids negative PCP negative Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 75-year-old patient presents to the emergency department because of pain in their left thigh and left calf for the past 3 months. The pain occurs at rest, worsens with walking, and is slightly improved by hanging their foot off the bed. They have had hypertension for 25 years and type 2 diabetes mellitus for 30 years. They have smoked 30–40 cigarettes per day for the past 45 years. On examination, the femoral, popliteal, and dorsalis pedis pulses are diminished, but detectable on both sides. The patient’s foot is shown in the image. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 79-year-old patient presents to their physician complaining of a persistent non-productive cough and dyspnea after contracting a cold in the past month. They describe themselves as being “generally healthy” before the cold started. Medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia. The patient takes hydrochlorothiazide, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. Their parents are both deceased. They do not smoke and only drink alcohol occasionally. During a review of symptoms, they described a month-long trip to St. Louis, Missouri, to visit family. At the physician’s office, their temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse is 82/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 130/82 mm Hg. A focused chest exam reveals mild crepitus on the right side. A chest X-ray shows a cavitary lesion in the right lung which is confirmed on chest computed tomography (CT). A lung biopsy is performed to rule out cancer and reveals necrotic granulomatous inflammation with oval yeast in macrophages. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old patient presents with fever, chills, nausea, and urinary urgency and frequency. They say that their symptoms began 4 days ago and have progressively worsened. Their past medical history is significant for a 6-month history of recurrent urinary tract infections (UTIs). Their vital signs include: temperature 39.0°C (102.2°F), blood pressure 100/70 mm Hg, pulse 92/min, and respiratory rate 25/min. On physical examination, there is moderate left costovertebral angle tenderness. Laboratory findings are significant for the following: WBC 8,500/mm3 RBC 4.20 x 106/mm3 Hematocrit 41.5% Hemoglobin 13.0 g/dL Platelet count 225,000/mm3 Urinalysis Color Dark yellow Clarity Turbid pH 6.5 Specific gravity 1.026 Glucose None Ketones None Nitrites Positive Leukocyte esterase Positive Bilirubin Negative Urobilirubin 0.6 mg/dL Protein Trace Blood None WBC 25/hpf Bacteria Many Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A parent brings their 4-year-old child to the physician, as the child has a 7-day history of foul-smelling diarrhea, abdominal cramps, and fever. The parent adds that they have been vomiting as well, and they are very much worried. The child is in daycare, and the parent endorses sick contacts with both family and friends. The child has not been vaccinated as the parents do not think it is necessary. On physical exam, the child appears dehydrated. Stool examination is negative for blood cells, pus, and ova or parasites. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-day-old newborn has failed to pass meconium after 48 hours. There is an absence of stool in the rectal vault. Family history is significant for MEN2A syndrome. Which of the following confirms the diagnosis?

A 52-year-old patient presents to the urgent care center with several hours of worsening abdominal discomfort that radiates to the back. The patient also complains of malaise, chills, nausea, and vomiting. Social history is notable for alcoholism. On physical exam, they are febrile to 39.5°C (103.1℉), and they are diffusely tender on abdominal palpation. Other vital signs include a blood pressure of 126/74 mm Hg, heart rate of 74/min, and respiratory rate of 14/min. Complete blood count is notable for 13,500 white blood cells (WBCs), and their complete metabolic panel shows bilirubin of 2.1 and amylase of 3210. Given the following options, what is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old patient presents to an urgent care clinic with the complaints of bloody diarrhea, mid-abdominal discomfort, and cramping for 3 days. They also have nausea, vomiting, and fever. They report that they had eaten raw oysters at a local seafood restaurant almost 3 days ago, but they deny any other potentially infectious exposures. Their temperature is 37.5°C (99.6°F), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 67/min, and blood pressure is 102/68 mm Hg. Physical examination is non-contributory. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 51-year-old patient who is an alcoholic presents to the emergency department with persistent vomiting. They were found vomiting forcefully next to an empty bottle of vodka. Their medical history is significant for Lyme disease, currently being treated with doxycycline. After a prolonged episode of retching, the patient begins choking and coughing forcefully in between bouts of chest pain in the ER. At this point, the patient is unable to communicate. The patient appears toxic. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 107/min, and blood pressure is 90/68 mm Hg. A quick physical exam reveals fullness at the base of the neck and a crunching, rasping sound on auscultation of the chest. The attending physician orders an upright chest X-ray, showing free mediastinal air. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 58-year-old patient, being treated on the medical floor for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin, develops watery diarrhea. They report at least 9 episodes of diarrhea within the last two days, with lower abdominal discomfort and cramping. Their temperature is 98.6° F (37° C), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 67/min, and blood pressure is 122/98 mm Hg. Their physical examination is unremarkable. Laboratory testing shows: Hb% 13 gm/dL Total count (WBC): 13,400/mm3 Differential count: Neutrophils: 80% Lymphocytes: 15% Monocytes: 5% ESR: 33 mm/hr What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old patient presents with a 7-day history of fever and abdominal pain for the past 4 days. Past medical history is significant for an exchange transfusion for neonatal hyperbilirubinemia and recurrent attacks of pallor during the course of upper respiratory tract infections. Their vital signs include: blood pressure 120/70 mm Hg, pulse 105/min, respiratory rate 40/min, and temperature 37.0℃ (98.6℉). On physical examination, the patient is ill-looking. Conjunctivae are pale and the sclera is icteric. The liver is palpable 2 cm below the costal margin and the spleen is palpable 3 cm below the left costal margin. Laboratory findings show hemoglobin of 5.9 gm/dL, Hct of 20%, and haptoglobin of 28 gm/dL. A peripheral blood smear shows hypochromic anemia, polychromasia, anisocytosis, and occasional Heinz bodies. The reticulocyte count was 15%. A direct Coombs test was negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 55-year-old patient presents for a routine check-up. They currently have no complaints, and their last physical and laboratory studies were unremarkable. Their past medical history is significant for hypercholesterolemia, well managed with rosuvastatin, and hypertension, well managed with hydrochlorothiazide. Their current medications also include aspirin. The patient is afebrile and their vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination reveals some generalized lymphadenopathy. Laboratory findings are significant for the following: WBC 38,000/mm3 RBC 4.20 x 106/mm3 Hematocrit 27.3% Hemoglobin 8.3 g/dL Platelet count 355,000/mm3 A peripheral blood smear and differential shows 92% small normocytic lymphocytes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 52-year-old patient complains of intermittent diffuse abdominal pain that becomes worse after eating meals and several episodes of diarrhea, the last of which was bloody. These symptoms have been present for the previous 6 months but have worsened recently. They have had significant weight loss since the onset of symptoms. Their past medical history includes systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), which has been difficult to manage medically. Vital signs include a blood pressure of 100/70 mm Hg, temperature of 37.1°C (98.8 °F), and pulse of 95/min. On physical examination, the patient appears to be in severe pain, and there is mild diffuse abdominal tenderness. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old African American patient presents with nausea and severe abdominal pain. They deny vomiting. They say that, 2 days ago, their divorce was finalized, so they went to a bar and had multiple shots of tequila and vodka. This morning, upon waking, they noticed their urine was red, which lasted throughout the day. The patient denies any history of similar symptoms. Past medical history is significant for low blood counts diagnosed on routine laboratory work 6 months ago, which was not followed up due to the stress of the divorce. A review of systems is significant for fatigue. Their temperature is 37.2°C (99.0°F), the heart rate is 90/min, the blood pressure is 136/88 mm Hg, and the respiratory rate is 20/min. Physical examination shows scleral icterus. Mucous membranes are pale. Cardiac auscultation reveals a systolic flow murmur loudest along the left sternal border. There is moderate right upper quadrant abdominal tenderness with no rebound or guarding. The remainder of the exam is unremarkable. Laboratory findings are significant for the following: Hematocrit 27% Mean corpuscular volume 81 µm3 Leukocytes 6,000/mm3 Platelets 130,000/µL Haptoglobin 30 mg/dL (50–150 mg/dL) Reticulocyte count 3% Total bilirubin 7.1 mg/dL LDH 766 U/L AST 150 U/L ALT 195 U/L HbA1 96% HbA2 2% HbF 2% CD55 50% of expected The peripheral smear is unremarkable. Which of the following would be the most likely cause of mortality given this patient’s likely diagnosis?

A 49-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with abdominal discomfort, fever, and decreased urination. They have a history of liver cirrhosis due to chronic hepatitis C infection. Their blood pressure is 90/70 mm Hg, pulse is 75/min, and temperature 38°C (100.4°F). On physical examination they are jaundiced, and they have tense ascites with generalized abdominal tenderness. There is pitting edema to the level of their upper thighs. Which of the following excludes the diagnosis of hepatorenal syndrome in this patient?

A 45-year-old patient presents to the physician because of a 1-day history of progressive pain and blurry vision in their right eye. They are struggling to open this eye because of the pain. Their left eye is asymptomatic. They wear contact lenses. They have bronchial asthma treated with inhaled salbutamol. They work as a kindergarten teacher. The vital signs include: temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse 85/min, and blood pressure 135/75 mm Hg. The examination shows a visual acuity in the left eye of 20/25 and the ability to count fingers at 3 feet in the right eye. A photograph of the right eye is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old patient presents following a suicide attempt 2 days ago. They say that their attempt was a result of a fight with their partner and that they slit their wrists in an attempt to keep them from breaking up. In the past, they have had many turbulent relationships, both romantic and in their family life. Their family members describe them as being very impulsive and frequently acting to manipulate people’s feelings. Since they were admitted to the hospital, they have spit at several staff members and alternated between sobbing and anger. They have no significant past medical history. The patient denies any history of smoking, alcohol use, or recreational drug use. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 15-year-old patient is referred to a child psychologist because of worsening behavior and constant disruption in class. They have received multiple reprimands in the past 6 months for not doing the homework their teacher assigned, and they refuse to listen to the classroom instructions. Additionally, their teachers say they are very argumentative and blame other children for not letting them do their work. They were previously well behaved and one of the top students in their class. They deny any recent major life events or changes at home. Their past medical history is noncontributory. Their vital signs are all within normal limits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 77-year-old patient is brought to their primary care provider by their daughter with behavioral changes and an abnormally bad memory for the past few months. The patient's daughter says they sometimes get angry and aggressive while at other times they seem lost and stare at their surroundings. Their daughter also reports that she has seen the patient talking to empty chairs. The patient says they sleep well during the night but still feel sleepy throughout the day. They have no problems getting dressed and maintaining their one bedroom apartment. Past medical history is significant for mild depression and mild osteoporosis. Current medications include escitalopram, alendronic acid, and a multivitamin. The patient is afebrile, and their vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, the patient is alert and oriented and sitting comfortably in their chair. A mild left-hand tremor is noted. Muscle strength is 5 out of 5 in the upper and lower extremities bilaterally, but muscle tone is slightly increased. They can perform repetitive alternating movements albeit slowly. They walk with a narrow gait and have mild difficulty turning. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 30-year-old patient who was recently placed on TMP-SMX for a urinary tract infection presents to urgent care with a new rash. The vital signs include: blood pressure 121/80 mm Hg, pulse 91/min, respiratory rate 18/min, and temperature 36.7°C (98.2°F). Physical examination reveals a desquamative skin covering both of their lower extremities. A basic chemistry panel reveals sodium 139 mmol/L, potassium 3.8 mmol/L, chloride 110 mmol/L, carbon dioxide 47, blood urea nitrogen 23 mg/dL, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, and glucose 103 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old patient is admitted to the emergency department with severe retrosternal chest pain. The pain began suddenly after an episode of self-induced vomiting following a large meal. The patient’s parents say that they are very restricted in the foods they eat and induce vomiting frequently after meals. Vital signs are as follows: blood pressure 100/60 mm Hg, heart rate 98/min, respiratory rate 14/min, and temperature 37.9℃ (100.2℉). The patient is pale and in severe distress. Lungs are clear to auscultation. On cardiac examination, a crunching, raspy sound is auscultated over the precordium that is synchronous with the heartbeat. The abdomen is soft and nontender. Which of the following tests would most likely confirm the diagnosis in this patient?

A 16-year-old patient presents to the clinic accompanied by their parent, with the complaints of high fever, sore throat, and bloody diarrhea for 4 days. They add that they are also nauseous and vomited several times in the past 2 days. They deny any recent travel or eating outside. They recently started a dog-walking business. The parent relates that two of the dogs had been unwell. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), respiratory rate is 16/min, pulse is 77/min, and blood pressure is 100/88 mm Hg. A physical examination is performed and is within normal limits including the abdominal exam. Blood test results are given below: Hb%: 14 gm/dL Total count (WBC): 13,100/mm3 Differential count: Neutrophils: 80% Lymphocytes: 15% Monocytes: 5% What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old patient comes to the emergency department because of colicky pain in the lower abdomen and abdominal distension for the past 12 hours. They have chronic constipation for which they take lactulose and senna laxatives. Their temperature is 37.1°C (98.7°F), blood pressure is 110/60 mm Hg and pulse is 85/min. On physical examination, there is diffuse abdominal distension and tenderness, and bowel sounds are faint. Their plain abdominal radiograph is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 11-year-old patient presents with fever and joint pain for the last 3 days. Their mother says that they had a sore throat 3 weeks ago but did not seek medical care at that time. The family immigrated from the Middle East 3 years ago. The patient has no past medical history. The current illness started with a fever and a swollen right knee that was very painful. The following day, their knee improved but their left elbow became swollen and painful. While in the waiting room, their left knee is also becoming swollen and painful. Vital signs include: temperature 38.7°C (101.6°F), and blood pressure 110/80 mm Hg. On physical examination, the affected joints are swollen and very tender to touch, and there are circular areas of redness on their back and left forearm (as shown in the image). Which of the following is needed to establish a diagnosis of acute rheumatic fever in this patient?

A 67-year-old patient refers to their physician for a follow-up examination. During their last visit 1 month ago, splenomegaly was detected. They have had night sweats for the past several months and have lost 5 kg (11 lb) unintentionally during this period. They have no history of severe illness and take no medications. The vital signs are within normal limits. The examination shows no abnormalities other than splenomegaly. The laboratory studies show the following: Hemoglobin 9 g/dL Mean corpuscular volume 95 μm3 Leukocyte count 12,000/mm3 Platelet count 260,000/mm3 Ultrasound shows a spleen size of 15 cm and mild hepatomegaly. A peripheral blood smear shows teardrop-shaped and nucleated red blood cells (RBCs) and immature myeloid cells. The marrow is very difficult to aspirate but reveals hyperplasia of all 3 lineages. The tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase (TRAP) test is negative. Clonal marrow plasma cells are not seen. JAK-2 is positive. The cytogenetic analysis is negative for translocation between chromosomes 9 and 22. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient repetitively visits the general surgery clinic worried that their inguinal hernia is incarcerated. 2 months ago, they were seen in the emergency department where they presented with a left lower abdominal swelling. The mass was easily reduced and the patient was referred to the general surgery clinic for elective surgical repair. Because their condition was deemed not urgent, they were informed that they were down on the surgical waiting list. Despite this, they continue to visit the clinic and the ED worried that their bowels are ‘trapped and dying.’ Each time they are reassured and any protrusion present is quickly reduced. They have previously frequently visited their primary care physician for complaints of abdominal pain and inconsistent bowel habits, but no etiology could be identified. They continue to intermittently have these symptoms and spend hours every day worrying about what may be going on. They have no other significant past medical history. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnosis?

A 22-year-old patient presents with lower limb weakness for the past 2 days. The patient says that the weakness started in both their feet, manifesting as difficulty walking, but it has progressed to where they cannot move their legs completely and has become bedbound. They also have experienced a recent history of numbness and tingling sensations in both their feet. They deny any recent history of fever, backache, urinary or bowel incontinence, trauma, shortness of breath, or diplopia. Their past medical history is remarkable for a viral flu-like illness 2 weeks ago. The patient is afebrile, and their vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, muscle strength in both lower limbs is 1/5. The muscle strength in the upper limbs is ⅘ bilaterally. Sensation to pinprick is decreased in both lower limbs in a stocking distribution. The sensation is intact in the upper limbs bilaterally. Knee and ankle reflexes are absent bilaterally. The laboratory findings are significant for the following: Hemoglobin 14.2 g/dL White blood cell count 8,250/mm3 Platelet count 258,000/mm3 BUN 14 mg/dL Creatinine 0.9 mg/dL Serum sodium 144 mEq/L Serum potassium 3.9 mEq/L Which of the following tests would most likely confirm the diagnosis in this patient?

A 51-year-old homeless patient presents to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain and cramping for the past 3 hours. They endorse radiation to their back. They add that they vomited multiple times. They admit having been hospitalized repeatedly for alcohol intoxication and abdominal pain. Their temperature is 103.8° F (39.8° C), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 107/min, and blood pressure is 100/80 mm Hg. They refuse a physical examination due to severe pain. Blood work reveals the following: Serum: Albumin: 3.2 gm/dL Alkaline phosphatase: 150 U/L Alanine aminotransferase: 76 U/L Aspartate aminotransferase: 155 U/L Gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase: 202 U/L Lipase: 800 U/L What is the most likely diagnosis of this patient?

A 62-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with hematuria and hemoptysis that started in the morning. They note that they have had frequent lung infections throughout their adult life, the most recent being 2 weeks ago. They also mention that they have had hematuria twice before but never as severe as they are having currently. Their medical history is otherwise non-significant, and their only medication is acetaminophen as needed. Their blood pressure is 136/92 mm Hg, heart rate is 86/min, respiratory rate is 16/min, and temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F). Chest radiography shows a resolving right middle lobe airspace opacity. Their initial laboratory tests are notable for elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level. While in the examination room, the patient develops a spontaneous nosebleed. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient comes to the emergency department with the complaint of pain and swelling of the proximal joint in the third finger of their right hand. The pain is so severe that it woke them up from sleep this morning. They have never had an episode like this before. The patient has smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for the last 25 years and drinks alcohol heavily each weekend. Their friend threw a party last night where they drank 3–4 beers and were unable to drive back home. They have no past medical illness. Their mother died of pancreatic cancer at age 55, and their father died of a stroke 2 years ago. Their temperature is 37.7°C (100°F), blood pressure is 130/70 mm Hg, pulse is 104/min, respiratory rate is 20/min, and BMI is 25 kg/m2. The patient is in moderate distress due to the pain. On examination, the proximal interphalangeal joint of the third finger of their right hand is very tender to touch, swollen, warm, and slightly red in color. Range of motion cannot be assessed due to extreme tenderness. The patient’s right hand is shown in the image. Laboratory investigation Complete blood count: Hemoglobin 14.5 g/dL Leukocytes 16,000/mm3 Platelets 150,000/mm3 ESR 55mm/hr Synovial fluid is aspirated from the joint. The findings are: Appearance Cloudy, dense yellow WBC 30,000 cells/µL Culture Negative Negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals are seen. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old patient presents with 2 days of severe, generalized, abdominal pain that is worse after meals. They are also nauseated and reports occasional diarrhea mixed with blood. Apart from essential hypertension, their medical history is unremarkable. Their vital signs include a temperature of 36.9°C (98.4°F), blood pressure of 145/92 mm Hg, and an irregularly irregular pulse of 105/min. Physical examination is only notable for mild periumbilical tenderness. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old patient is brought to a psychiatrist by their mother. The patient’s mother has become increasingly concerned about them since their high school graduation. Although she says that they had been an excellent student in high school, their grades have begun slipping in their second year in college, and they no longer socialize with friends. When she asked them why they no longer talk to their friends, she states that they told her, “They already know where I am. They can see me. They watch me from my bedroom window, so they already know what I’m doing. We don’t need to talk.” She found this to be bizarre, as nearly all of their friends live hours away. The patient states that they feel fine and don’t understand why everyone thinks they are crazy. The psychiatrist notices reduced spontaneous movements while the patient is speaking and that they speak in a monotone with a voice that is soft in volume. They also appear suspicious and defensive, asking the psychiatrist “why are you asking me that?” after each evaluative question. Their mood is generally flat with little reactivity or engagement during the course of their interview, but they deny any symptoms of depression or psychosis. No significant past medical history. Family history is not available as they were adopted. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?
