clinical_context: A 61-year-old diabetic patient is brought to the emergency department with the complaint of multiple bouts of abdominal pain in the last 24 hours. They say that the pain is dull aching in nature, radiates to the back, and worsens with meals. They also complain of nausea and occasional vomiting. They have been hospitalized repeatedly in the past with similar complaints. Their temperature is 37° C (98.6° F), respiratory rate is 16/min, pulse is 77/min, and blood pressure is 120/89 mm Hg. On physical exam, dark hyperpigmentation of the axillary skin is noted. Their blood test report from last month is given below: Glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c): 9.1% Triglyceride: 675 mg/dL LDL-Cholesterol: 102 mg/dL HDL-Cholesterol: 35 mg/dL Total Cholesterol: 250 mg/dL Serum Creatinine: 1.2 mg/dL BUN: 12 mg/dL Alkaline phosphatase: 100 U/L Alanine aminotransferase: 36 U/L Aspartate aminotransferase: 28 U/L What is the most likely diagnosis in this case?

A 40-year-old patient presents with a lack of concentration at work for the last 3 months. They say that they have been working as a personal assistant to a manager at a corporate business company for the last 2 years. Upon asking why they are not able to concentrate, they answer that their colleagues are always gossiping about them during work hours and that it disrupts their concentration severely. Their partner works in the same company and denies these allegations. They say the other employees are busy doing their own work and have only formal conversations, yet the patient is convinced that they are talking about them. They further add that the patient frequently believes that some advertisements in a newspaper are directed towards them and are published specifically to catch their attention even though they are routine advertisements. The patient denies any mood disturbances, anxiety or hallucinations. Past medical history is significant for a tingling sensation in their legs, 3+ patellar reflexes bilaterally, and absent ankle reflexes bilaterally. They say that they drink alcohol once to twice a month for social reasons but deny any other substance use or smoking. On physical examination, the patient is conscious, alert, and oriented to time, place and person. A beefy red color of the tongue is noted. No associated cracking, bleeding, or oral lesions. Which of the following laboratory tests would be most helpful to identify this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to a rheumatologist with bilateral wrist and knee pain that has been present for the last 10 years. The patient was a professional athlete who retired at age 50. They also note morning stiffness in their joints that lasts approx. 50 minutes. They deny joint swelling, color changes in their digits, dryness of mucous membranes, and constitutional symptoms such as fever and chills. On physical exam, the physician notes several non-tender nodules on the left 1st, 3rd, and 4th distal interphalangeal joints. There is also tenderness with palpation at the base of both thumbs. The patient’s knees are enlarged, bilaterally, and they have pain and crepitus on passive range of motion. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old patient comes to the physician with complaints of fever, headache, and rash, which have gradually worsened over the past 6 days. The patient informs the physician that the rash appeared after 2 days of fever. The rash started at the wrists and ankles and then gradually spread to the trunk, palms, and soles. On examination, the physician notes a maculopapular rash as shown in the image below. Vital signs show a temperature of 39.4°C (103.0°F), a blood pressure of 110/70 mm Hg, and a pulse rate of 86/min. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 31-year-old patient is brought in to the clinic by their sister because she is concerned about their behavior since the death of their mother 2 months ago. The patient’s sister states that they have always been a ‘loner’ and preferred being by themselves than socializing with others. Their social isolation resulted in them being ‘socially awkward’, as described by their family. However, 2 months ago, when they found out about the death of their mother, they showed little emotion and attended her funeral in jeans and a dirty T-shirt which upset the rest of their family. When asked about it, they shrugged and said they were in a hurry to get to the funeral and “just left the house with what I had on.” They do not speak much during the interview, allowing their sister to speak on their behalf. Their sister insists that they have ‘always been like this’, quiet and a complacent child who had no interest in playing with other children. The patient currently lives alone and spends their time repairing and building electrical appliances, and their sister is worried that their self-imposed isolation is making it ‘impossible for them to interact with other people normally’. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 32-year-old patient presents with a 2-month history of increasing lethargy, frequent upper respiratory tract infections, and easy bruising. Past medical history is unremarkable. The patient reports a 14-pack-year smoking history and says they drink alcohol socially. No significant family history. Their vital signs include: temperature 36.8°C (98.2°F), blood pressure 132/91 mm Hg and pulse 95/min. Physical examination reveals conjunctival pallor and scattered ecchymoses on the lower extremities. Laboratory results are significant for the following: Hemoglobin 8.2 g/dL Leukocyte count 2,200/mm3 Platelet count 88,000/mm3 Reticulocyte count 0.5% A bone marrow biopsy is performed, which demonstrates hypocellularity with no abnormal cell population. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 20-year-old college student presents to the emergency room at 4 AM in the morning with complaints of abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea for the past 2 hours. They were studying for their exams last night when they became hungry and ate some food from the afternoon after heating it for a while. They say that their symptoms began an hour after they ate the food. Their temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 106/min, and blood pressure is 90/78 mm Hg. A physical examination is within normal limits except for signs of dehydration. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-year-old patient presents to their pediatrician with complaints of repeated jerking of their neck for the past 2 years. Initially, their parents considered it a sign of discomfort in their neck, but later they noticed that the jerking was more frequent when they were under emotional stress or when they were fatigued. The patient says they can voluntarily control the jerking in some social situations, but when they are under stress, they feel the urge to jerk their neck and they feel better after that. The parents also report that during the past year, there have even been a few weeks when the frequency of the neck jerking had decreased drastically, only to increase again afterwards. On physical examination, they are a physically healthy patient with normal vital signs. Their neurologic examination is normal. The pediatrician also notes that when they make certain movements, the patient partially imitates these movements. The parents are very much concerned about their abnormal movements and insist on a complete diagnostic work-up. After a detailed history, physical examination, and laboratory investigations, the pediatrician confirms the diagnosis of Tourette syndrome. The presence of which of the following findings is most likely to confirm the pediatrician’s diagnosis?

An 18-month-old toddler is brought to the pediatrician by their parent for cough. The parent reports that their child has had a productive-sounding cough and runny nose for the past 2 days. They have also noticed that their child feels warm. On chart review, this is the 4th time this patient is presenting for similar concerns; the 3 previous diagnoses were otitis media (2 episodes) and bacterial sinusitis (1 episode). Their temperature is 38.3°C (101.0°F). Physical examination is notable for cough and purulent sputum from both nares, although their lungs are clear to auscultation. Sputum gram stain shows gram-positive diplococci. Serum immunoglobulin studies show normal levels of IgM and decreased levels of IgG and IgA. Which of the following is the most likely underlying diagnosis in this patient?

A 58-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with severe right leg pain accompanied by tingling and weakness. Their condition started suddenly 3 hours ago when they were watching a movie. Their medical history is remarkable for type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension. They have been smoking 20–30 cigarettes per day for the past 35 years. Their vital signs include a blood pressure of 149/85 mm Hg, a temperature of 36.9°C (98.4°F), and an irregular pulse of 96/min. On physical examination, their right popliteal and posterior tibial pulses are absent. Their right leg is pale and cold. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old patient presents to their physician’s office with a progressive cough. It has been increasing in intensity over the past week. They have also been noticing an increase in the amount of sputum they usually produce, which is thick and yellow. They also complain of increased difficulty in breathing, more so than they previously experienced. They were diagnosed with chronic obstructive lung disease (COPD) about 3 years ago and have been on treatment for it since then. They don’t report any fever, chills, or night sweats. They have observed a foul smell to their sputum. Their blood pressure is 100/65 mm Hg, the respirations are 23/min and the pulse is about 110/min. Currently, their FEV1 is around 48% of the normal predicted value. They are currently receiving a yearly influenza shot and have taken the pneumococcal vaccination at the time of their diagnosis. In spite of this, they have had acute exacerbations of their symptoms 4 times over the last year. Their last episode was 2 months ago, for which they were treated with a short course of antibiotics. They are also currently receiving treatment for diabetes. Which of the following pathogens should be considered before initiating treatment for the current episode?

A 78-year-old patient living in New Jersey is brought to the emergency department in July with a fever for 5 days. Lethargy is present. They have had bloody urine over the last 48 hours but deny any nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain. They have no history of serious illness and take no medications. They have not traveled anywhere outside their city for the past several years. They appear ill. The temperature is 40.8℃ (105.4℉), the pulse is 108/min, the respiration rate is 20/min, and the blood pressure is 105/50 mm Hg. The abdominal exam reveals hepatosplenomegaly. Lymphadenopathy is absent. Petechiae are seen on the lower extremities. Laboratory studies show the following: Laboratory test Hemoglobin 8 g/dL Mean corpuscular volume (MCV) 98 µm3 Leukocyte count 4,200/mm3 Segmented neutrophils 32% Lymphocytes 58% Platelet count 108,000/mm3 Bilirubin, total 5.0 mg/dL Direct 0.7 mg/dL Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 51 U/L Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 56 U/L Alkaline phosphatase 180 U/L Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) 640 U/L (N = 140–280 U/L) Haptoglobin 20 mg/dL (N = 30–200 mg/dL) Urine Hemoglobin + Urobilinogen + Protein + A peripheral blood smear is shown (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old patient presents to the physician with profuse watery diarrhea along with fever and crampy abdominal pain. They have been taking an antibiotic course of cefixime for about a week to treat a respiratory tract infection. At the doctor’s office, their pulse is 112/min, the blood pressure is 100/66 mm Hg, the respirations are 22/min, and the temperature is 38.9°C (102.0°F). Their oral mucosa appears dry and their abdomen is soft with vague diffuse tenderness. A digital rectal examination is normal. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 11.1 g/dL Hematocrit 33% Total leucocyte count 16,000/mm3 Serum lactate 0.9 mmol/L Serum creatinine 1.1 mg/dL What is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 41-year-old patient with a past medical history significant for asthma and seasonal allergies presents with a new rash. They have no significant past surgical, social, or family history. The patient's blood pressure is 131/90 mm Hg, the pulse is 77/min, the respiratory rate is 17/min, and the temperature is 36.9°C (98.5°F). Physical examination reveals a sharply demarcated area of skin dryness and erythema encircling their left wrist. Review of systems is otherwise negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old patient and recent immigrant from Brazil present to the clinic. They have no known past medical, past surgical, or family history. The patient admits to having several regular sexual partners. Today, they complain of a skin rash on their back. They are unclear when it started but became aware when one of their partners pointed it out. A review of systems is otherwise negative. Physical examination reveals numerous hypopigmented skin lesions over their upper back. When questioned, they state that they do not get darker after spending time in the sun. On examination, there is a 5 cm (1.9 in) patch of hypopigmented skin in the center of their back with a fine-scale overlying it. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old patient presents with a limp favoring their right leg. The patient’s parent noticed they had been limping without complaint for the past 6 months. Past medical history is significant for the flu last year. No current medications. All immunizations are up to date. The vital signs include: temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F), blood pressure 100/60 mm Hg, pulse 74/min, respiratory rate 19/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air. The body mass index (BMI) is 17.2 kg/m2. On physical examination, the patient is alert and cooperative. A limp favoring the right leg is noted when the patient is walking. There is mild tenderness on deep palpation of the left lumbar region but no erythema, edema, or warmth. There is a decreased range of motion of the left hip. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 72-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with difficulty breathing for the past 3 hours. They also mention that over the last week they were frequently breathless and fatigued after walking a few blocks. They have had diabetes mellitus and hypertension for the past 10 years, and their regular medications include metformin, glipizide, and lisinopril. However, they did not take their medications last week due to unplanned travel. Review of their medical records reveals an episode of acute viral hepatitis about 6 months ago from which they recovered well. Their temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), the pulse is 108/min, the blood pressure is 170/94 mm Hg, and the respiratory rate is 24/min. On physical examination, periorbital edema is present with pitting edema over both ankles and pretibial regions. Pallor and icterus are absent. Auscultation of the chest reveals crackles over the infrascapular regions bilaterally. Abdominal examination shows tender hepatomegaly. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 81-year-old patient recently moved into an assisted living facility and presents today with itchy blisters in their axilla. They attribute these to a poor diet. They also complain that the nurse practitioner at the facility started them on 4 new medications, in addition to their existing prescriptions. On physical examination, tense axillary bullae are noted that do not rupture with light, gloved touch. On direct immunofluorescence, linear C3 and IgG deposits are seen along the basement membrane. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 54-year-old patient presents to the clinic for epigastric discomfort during the previous month. They state they have not vomited, but reports of having epigastric pain that worsens after most meals. The patient states that their stool “looks black sometimes.” The patient does not report any weight loss. They have a past medical history of gastroesophageal reflux disease, diabetes mellitus, peptic ulcer disease, and Crohn’s disease. The patient takes over-the-counter ranitidine, and holds prescriptions for metformin and infliximab. The blood pressure is 132/84 mm Hg, the heart rate is 64/min, the respiratory rate is 14/min, and the temperature is 37.3°C (99.1°F). On physical examination, the abdomen is tender to palpation in the epigastric region. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to accurately determine the diagnosis of this patient?

A 23-year-old college student presents with their parents for a follow-up appointment. They were recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and were started on risperidone approx. 2 months ago. They report a significant improvement since the start of treatment. Their parents report that their child’s symptoms of delusions, hallucinations, and paranoid behavior have been ameliorated. On physical examination, the patient seems uncomfortable. They frequently fidget and repeatedly cross and uncross their legs. When asked if something is troubling them, they get up and start pacing. They say, “It’s always like this. I cannot sit still. It is frustrating.” What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old patient presents to the clinic for a 3-month history of painful hair loss. They were in their usual state of health until about 3 months ago when they started to develop some painfully itchy spots across their scalp. Since that time these spots have lost hair and scarred, with new spots continuing to form. On further questioning, they share that, for the last couple of years, they have generally felt poorly, specifically noting intermittent fevers, muscle and joint pains, and fatigue. On physical exam, they have several erythematous and scaly plaques across their scalp. These areas have no hair growth, but some do demonstrate hyperpigmentation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 47-year-old patient presents to the clinic for an evaluation of intense itching of their right thigh region for the past few days. They state some ‘red bumps’ just began to form. The patient mentions that they were recently at a business conference in Miami. They have a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes type 2, and hyperlipidemia. They take enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. They do not smoke or drink. Their vitals are within normal limits today. On physical examination, a linear line with 3 red papules is present along the medial aspect of their right thigh. Additionally, there are small rows of bumps on their left leg and right forearm. Excoriations are also apparent in the same region. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 63-year-old patient presents to the clinic concerned about numbness in their bilateral shoulders and arms for the past 8 weeks. The symptoms started when they fell from scaffolding at work and landed on their back. Initial workup was benign and they returned to normal duty. However, their symptoms have progressively worsened since the fall. They deny fever, back pain, limb weakness, preceding vomiting, and diarrhea. They have a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, ischemic heart disease, and a 48-pack-year cigarette smoking history. They take atorvastatin, hydrochlorothiazide, lisinopril, labetalol, and metformin. Their blood pressure is 132/82 mm Hg, the pulse is 72/min, and the respiratory rate is 15/min. All cranial nerves are intact. Muscle strength is normal in all limbs. Perception of sharp stimuli and temperature is reduced on their shoulders and upper arms. The vibratory sense is preserved. Sensory examination is normal in the lower limbs. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old patient comes to the clinic with complaints of joint pain and stiffness for the past few months. Their hands, lower back, and left knee are involved and associated with morning stiffness that improves throughout the day with activities. They also complain that their fingers change color upon exposure to cold. They have also noticed a tightening of the skin on their face and thinning of their lips. They feel tired throughout the day and have taken over-the-counter multivitamins that do not seem to help them much. The patient does not smoke cigarettes and drinks alcohol socially. They were diagnosed with hypertension 1 year ago and have been taking hydralazine for the past year. They lost their parents in a road traffic accident 3 years ago. Temperature is 36.7°C (98°F), blood pressure is 140/85 mm Hg, pulse is 72/min, respirations are 12/min, and BMI is 25 kg/m2. Their skin appears shiny and slightly thickened, especially their face and hands. Laboratory investigation: Complete blood count Hemoglobin 9.5 g/dl Leucocytes 5,500/mm3 Platelets 150,000/mm3 ANA positive Anti-centromere Antibody negative Anti Scl-70 positive Anti Jo-1 negative Anti-histone negative Anti DsDNA negative What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 40-year-old Caucasian patient presents to your office with fever, fatigue, cold fingers, and the rash shown in Figure A. The presence of which of the following antibodies has the highest specificity for diagnosis of this patient's condition?
A 28-year-old patient is found to have 93% HbA, 2% HbF, and 5% HbA2 on hemoglobin electrophoresis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old patient is evaluated for frequent epistaxis and mucous membrane bleeding. Physical examination shows diffuse petechiae on the patient's distal extremities. Peripheral blood smear shows an absence of platelet clumping. An ELISA binding assay reveals that platelet surfaces are deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors. Serum platelet count is normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old patient visits their primary care physician because of progressive weight loss. They have a 20-year history of smoking 2 packs of cigarettes a day and were diagnosed with diabetes mellitus 6 years ago. After physical examination, the physician tells the patient they suspect adenocarcinoma at the head of the pancreas. Which of the following physical examination findings would support the diagnosis:

A 27-year-old patient presents to your office complaining of right arm numbness and weakness. Their past medical history is unremarkable. Their family history, however, is significant for the unexpected death of both their parents at age 59 in a motor vehicle accident last week. On physical exam, their bicep, brachioradialis, and patellar reflexes are 2+ bilaterally. CNS imaging shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old patient is brought to your emergency department under arrest by the local police. The patient was found naked at a busy intersection jumping up and down on top of a car. Interviewing the patient, you discover that they have not slept in 2 days because they do not feel tired. They report hearing voices. The patient was previously hospitalized 1 year ago with auditory hallucinations, paranoia, and a normal mood. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old patient is concerned that they may give birth to another child with Down syndrome. They state that they may not be able to take care of another child with this disorder. Which of the following tests can confirm the diagnosis of Down syndrome in utero?

A 13-year-old patient re-presents to their pediatrician with a new onset rash that began a few days after their initial visit. They initially presented with complaints of sore throat but were found to have a negative strep test. Their parent demanded that they be placed on antibiotics, but this was refused by their pediatrician. The patient's parent, a neurologist, therefore, started them on penicillin. Shortly after starting the drug, the patient developed a fever and a rash. The patient is admitted and their symptoms worsen. Their skin begins to slough off, and the rash covers over 30% of their body. Their oropharynx and corneal membranes are also affected. You examine them at the bedside and note a positive Nikolsky's sign. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 43-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician complaining of a gradually enlarging neck mass. They report that they first developed a firm nodular midline mass on the anterior aspect of their neck two months ago. They are otherwise healthy and take no medications. A fine-needle aspiration is performed and a histological sample of the specimen is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old patient visits their primary care physician with 2+ pitting edema in their legs. They take no medications and do not use alcohol, tobacco, or illicit drugs. 4.5 grams of protein are collected during 24-hour urine excretion. A kidney biopsy is obtained. Examination with light microscopy shows diffuse thickening of the glomerular basement membrane. Electron microscopy shows subepithelial spike and dome deposits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis:

A 22-year-old patient presents to your clinic for evaluation of "skin problems." They complain of severe acne and "spots" all over their face that have persisted for the last 8 years, despite innumerable creams and lotions. They report spending several hours every morning using make-up just to go outside. They wish to learn about cosmetic procedures or surgeries that could solve their problem. While you perceive their concern for their skin to be genuine, upon examination, you note a healthy-appearing, well-nourished patient with a normal complexion, minimal acne and sparse freckles on the nasal bridge. You calculate their BMI to be 21. In addition to making a diagnosis, this patient should be screened for which other disorder?

Two days following the home birth of their child, a parent brings the infant to the pediatric emergency room because of bilious vomiting. They are unable to pass meconium and their abdomen is distended. Endoscopic biopsy of the proximal colon demonstrates an absence of Meissner’s and Auerbach’s plexi in the bowel wall. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 37-year-old patient visited their primary care physician with a nodular mass in their neck. Fine-needle aspiration of the mass demonstrated malignancy and total thyroidectomy was performed. A histological sample of the excised lesion is shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis:

A 3-year-old patient is brought to the family physician by their parents. They are concerned that they have had multiple nosebleeds in the last 6 months and are always sick compared to other children. During this time period they have also noticed the formation of multiple bruises on their extremities and dry-itching skin on their hands, feet, and elbow. On physical exam, the physician notes moderate splenomegaly. What is the most likely diagnosis in this child?

A 62-year-old patient is evaluated for fatigue 6 months after placement of a mechanical valve due to aortic stenosis. They do not drink alcohol or smoke cigarettes. A complete blood count reports hemoglobin of 9.5 g/L and a reticulocyte percentage of 5.8%. Platelet and leukocyte counts are within their normal ranges. The patient’s physician suspects traumatic hemolysis from the patient’s mechanical valve as the cause of their anemia. Which of the following peripheral blood smear findings would most support this diagnosis?

A 58-year-old Caucasian patient presents to their primary care physician with concerns about several recent health changes. The patient has recently gained weight and can't seem to exercise like they used to. They also note that their thinking seems slow. Physical examination shows thickened, dry skin. Serum analysis confirms the physician's suspicions. Which of the following findings was most helpful in the diagnosis?

An 11-year-old patient presents to your office with pitting edema and proteinuria exceeding 3.5g in 24 hours. You suspect that this patient has experienced a loss of polyanions in their glomerular basement membranes. Which of the following findings would confirm your diagnosis?

A 17-year-old African-American patient presents to their family physician after noticing red-tinged urine the week before, when they were suffering from a cold. The patient states that they had experienced that before. Their parent is with them and says that this happens to them on occasion as well. What is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 54-year-old patient is admitted to the hospital for progressive exertional dyspnea and cough productive of tan-colored liquid for 6 months. They have never smoked a day in their life. A lung biopsy is shown in Figure A that demonstrates tall, columnar cells that line the alveoli septa. The most likely diagnosis for this patient is:

A 45-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with complaints of muscle pains, poor sleep, and daytime fatigue. When asked about stressors they state that they "panic" about their job, marriage, children, and finances. When asked to clarify what the "panics" entail, they state that it involves severe worrying. They have had these symptoms since they last saw you one year ago. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient who has smoked 2 packs per day for forty years comes to your practice complaining of a chronic cough, dyspnea, hemoptysis, and difficulty rising from a chair. Based on CXR and biopsy slides shown, you feel that all of the following would be consistent with their diagnosis EXCEPT?

An 8-year-old African-American patient is found to have a holosystolic, harsh-sounding murmur upon physical examination. The murmur is best appreciated at the left sternal border, and is found to be louder when the patient squats. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 61-year-old patient with a past medical history of lung cancer is hospitalized for shortness of breath. During their hospitalization, they are found to be septic and was oozing from their intravenous catheter site. They also develop petechiae on their shoulders and abdomen. Which of the following test results and blood smears is consistent with a diagnosis of disseminated intravascular coagulation?

A 20-year-old college student is brought to their primary care physician by their parents over the New Years holiday because they are concerned about their behavior since right after high school graduation in May the spring before. Prior to this year, they were generally an outgoing and social young person, who now reportedly has been spending the majority of their time alone in their dorm room and room at home, where their parents have overheard them talking to other people when they have no guests. When asked if anything was bothering them at school, they report that at night the voice of the school's mascot encourages them to save the school from the large oak grove that will soon takeover the student union building by setting the trees on fire for all to see. On exam, they appear to be otherwise healthy and their urine toxicology screen is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with gross hematuria and acute, colicky flank pain. They deny any previous episodes of hematuria. They report taking high doses of acetaminophen and aspirin over several weeks due to persistent upper back pain. The patient’s blood pressure and temperature are normal, but they are found to have proteinuria. Physical examination is negative for palpable flank masses. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis:

A 40-year-old patient presents to your office complaining that they are too weak to climb stairs or brush their hair. They deny any headaches or change in vision. A muscle biopsy reveals CD8+ lymphocyte infiltration in the endomysium. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old patient is brought to their pediatrician after recurrent, prolonged upper respiratory infections over a period of several months. Physical exam reveals petechiae on the patient’s legs and arms. Laboratory studies show hemoglobin: 10 g/L, platelet count: 35,000/mm^3, leukocyte count: 6,600/mm^3. A bone marrow aspiration shows an abundance of lymphoblasts indicative of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). Positive immunostaining for which of the following would support a diagnosis of precursor B-cell leukemia?

A 21-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their roommate. Their roommate says that the patient has been acting “strangely” for the past 10 days. They have noticed that the patient has been moving and talking on the phone at all hours of the night. They don’t think that the patient sleeps more than one to two hours a night. They also spend hours pacing up and down the apartment, talking about “trying to save the world.” They also notice that the patient has been speaking very fast. When asking the patient if anything seems different, the patient denies anything wrong, only adding that, “they’ve made great progress on their plans." The patient said they have felt like this on one occasion 2 years ago, and they recalled being hospitalized for about 2 weeks. They deny any history of depression, although they said about a year ago they had no energy and had a hard time motivating themselves to go to class and see their friends for months. They deny hearing any voices or any visual hallucinations. What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 33-year-old patient presents with recent onset of painful urination, fever, and right flank pain. Urinary sediment analysis is positive for the presence of white blood cell casts and Gram-negative bacteria. They have not recently started any new medications. What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 38-year-old patient visits your office complaining of several years of joint swelling and stiffness that is worse in the morning and improves throughout the day. Physical examination reveals bilateral deformities at their proximal interphalangeal and metacarpophalangeal joints. The presence of which of the following in this patient’s serum would most help 'rule in' a diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis:

A one-year-old patient presents to your office accompanied by their parent. On examination of the patient, you observe the findings shown in Figure A. The appearance of the parent's face is depicted in Figure B. What is the most likely diagnosis for the patient?

A 32-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with complaints of chronic headaches that have developed and increased in frequency and severity over the last several months. Additionally, the patient has noted they have been less coordinated over the last few weeks, stumbling and tripping often when they are walking. Physical examination is significant for notably reduced hand grip strength bilaterally as well as decreased pain and temperature sensation along the upper back and down both arms to the hands. A referral to the appropriate specialist is made, and an MRI of the brain and neck is obtained. Results of the MRI are shown in Figures A and B. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 4-year-old Caucasian patient previously diagnosed with asthma presents with recurrent sinusitis, otitis media, and clubbing of the nail bed. Family history is significant for a distant cousin with cystic fibrosis. A "sweat test" is performed and comes back normal. What additional diagnostic test would be helpful in establishing a diagnosis?

A 64-year-old patient with a history of rheumatic fever presents to their primary care clinician complaining of excessive fatigue with walking and difficulty lying flat. They had no prior physical limitations, but recently has been unable to walk more than 3 blocks without needing to stop and rest. Their cardiac exam is notable for a late diastolic murmur heard best at the apex in the left lateral decubitus position with no radiation. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old Caucasian patient presents with anemia, malaise, bloating, and diarrhea. Past genetic testing revealed that this patient carries the HLA-DQ2 allele. The physician suspects that the patient's presentation is dietary in cause. Which of the following findings would definitively confirm this diagnosis?

A 27-year-old patient has a history of periodic bloody diarrhea over several years. Colonoscopy shows sigmoid colon inflammation, and the patient complains of joint pain in their knees and ankles. They suspect inflammatory bowel disease. Which of the following would suggest a diagnosis of Crohn disease:

A 27-year-old patient is brought to the Emergency Department by Fire Rescue after participating in a physical altercation with several commuters on the subway. They appear to be responding to hallucinations and are diaphoretic. Their vitals are as follows: T 100.5F (38C), HR 115, BP 155/90, RR 17. Their past medical history is notable for a previous ED visit for phencyclidine-related agitation. Which of the following physical findings would most strongly suggest the same diagnosis?

A 42-year-old patient presents to your office complaining of dyspnea on exertion. During the interview, the patient notes that they are a contractor specializing in the construction of aviaries at zoos. A radiograph of their chest is shown in Figure A. What is the diagnosis?

A 48-year-old patient presents to the emergency room with mental status changes. Laboratory analysis of the patient's serum shows: Na 122 mEq/L K 3.9 mEq/L HCO3 24 mEq/L BUN 21 mg/dL Cr 0.9 mg/dL Ca 8.5 mg/dL Glu 105 mg/dL Urinalysis shows: Osmolality 334 mOsm/kg Na 45 mEq/L Glu 0 mg/dL Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-year-old patient who recently immigrated to the US is brought to the pediatrician by their parent because they have noticed a recent color change in their eyes as demonstrated in Figure A. They are concerned because the patient has never had significant medical care in their life. Otherwise the patient has no complaints and states that they feel fine. The pediatrician obtains labs which demonstrate: total bilirubin: 5 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 4.5 mg/dL, indirect bilirubin 0.5 mg/dL, AST: 15, ALT: 20, GGT: 10. A liver biopsy is subsequently obtained which is demonstrated in Figure B. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 34-year-old African American patient presents complaining of worsening dyspnea and hemoptysis. Serum ACE (angiotensin converting enzyme) levels are elevated. A chest x-ray shown in Figure A suggests the likely diagnosis. Which of the following findings is consistent with this diagnosis?

A 28-year-old Caucasian patient with a 10 pack-year history of smoking presents with diarrhea and right, lower quadrant colicky pain. You note tender, red nodules on their shins. Radiograph imaging after barium study is shown in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their parent following a seizure. The parent reports that they have had a fever for 3 days prior to convulsing while watching TV. You admit the patient to the hospital for further workup and observation. Three days later, you note the appearance of a papular, non-confluent rash on the patient's back, extending superiorly towards the nape of the patient's neck. The abdomen and chest are shown in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old patient is seen by their pediatrician for developmental delay. One year prior, the patient was able to ride a tricycle, stack 3 blocks, and speak in short sentences. Now, they are unable to feed themselves and have recently started to point to objects they want rather than asking. Physical exam reveals a well-nourished child sitting in a stroller wringing their hands. Vital signs are normal. The patient's parent reports that their 7-year-old sibling is doing well, and that they have no family history of mental retardation or other cognitive disorders. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 51-year-old patient presents complaining of decreased vibratory sense in their lower limbs. Physical exam reveals a widened pulse pressure and a decrescendo murmur occurring after the S2 heart sound. After further questioning, they also report they experienced a maculopapular rash over their trunk, palms and soles many years ago that resolved on its own. In order to evaluate the suspected diagnosis, the physician FIRST tested for which of the following?

A 48-year-old patient presents to their primary physician with the chief complaints of fever, abdominal pain, weight loss, muscle weakness, and numbness in their lower extremities. UA is normal. A biopsy of the sural nerve reveals transmural inflammation and fibrinoid necrosis of small and medium arteries. Chart review reveals a remote history of cigarette smoking as a teenager and Hepatitis B seropositivity. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 73-year-old patient presents with complaints of long standing halitosis. They have recently been having progressive difficulty with swallowing. In the last several weeks, they have also noticed a small amount of regurgitated food on their pillow in the morning. You obtain the radiographic study depicted in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A patient presents to the emergency room in an obtunded state. The patient is a known nurse within the hospital system and has no history of any medical problems. A finger stick blood glucose is drawn showing a blood glucose of 25 mg/dL. The patient's child immediately arrives at the hospital stating that their parent has been depressed recently and that they found empty syringes in the bathroom at the parent's home. Which of the following is the test that will likely reveal the diagnosis?

A 68-year-old patient visits their primary care physician after an episode of syncope during a tennis match. They report exertional dyspnea with mild substernal chest pain. On physical exam a systolic crescendo-decrescendo murmur is heard best at the right 2nd intercostal space. This murmur was not heard at the patient's last appointment six months ago. Which of the following would most support a diagnosis of aortic stenosis?

A 12-year-old patient presents with right flank pain and hematuria. Their older sibling has had several similar episodes in the past. Results of microscopic urinalysis are shown in Figure A. Which of the following tests can be used to help confirm the underlying diagnosis?

A 2-year-old patient with abdominal pain undergoes laparoscopic surgery. An outpouching of tissue is excised from the ileum and sent to the laboratory for evaluation. The pathologist notes inflammation and the presence of mucosa, submucosa, and muscle in the walls of the specimen. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old patient presents with complaints of polydipsia and frequent, large-volume urination. Laboratory testing does not demonstrate any evidence of diabetes; however, a reduced urine osmolality of 120 mOsm/L is measured. Which of the following findings on a desmopressin test would be most consistent with a diagnosis of central diabetes insipidus?

A 45-year-old patient presents with fever, productive cough, and foul-smelling sputum for the past two weeks. Vital signs are T 38.3 C, HR 106, BP 118/64 and RR 16. Oxygen saturation on room air is 90%. Given a diagnosis of aspiration pneumonia, initial chest radiograph findings would most likely include:

A 29-year-old patient presents to the general medicine clinic complaining of dizziness, fatigue, and shortness of breath. One month ago, the patient went on a camping trip in northern Connecticut. On assessment, vital signs are temperature 36.9°C, blood pressure 100/65, heart rate 41, and respiratory rate 16 with an oxygen saturation of 99%. A print of the EKG strip is shown below (Figure A). What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old patient presents to your office for evaluation of a chronic ulcer on the plantar aspect of their right foot. They have a history of peripheral vascular disease and poorly-controlled diabetes mellitus. They state that they have had this ulcer for years, but that it seems to be growing. On examination of their right foot you note the heaped up edges surrounding the ulcer (Figure A). A wedge biopsy reveals irregular masses of anaplastic epidermal cells proliferating down to the dermis and the pathologist reports "keratin pearls". What is the diagnosis?

A 22-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician complaining of a red, itchy rash on their elbows and shoulders for 2 months. They have no history of medical problems, and review of systems is positive only for occasional loose stools. They are appropriately prescribed dapsone, which relieves the rash within hours. What is the diagnosis?

An 18-year-old patient reports to their physician that they are having repeated episodes of a "racing heart beat". They believe these episodes are occurring completely at random. They are experiencing approximately 2 episodes each week, each lasting for only a few minutes. During the episodes they feel palpitations and shortness of breath, then nervous and uncomfortable, but these feelings resolve in a matter of minutes. They are otherwise well. Vital signs are as follows: T 98.8F, HR 60 bpm, BP 110/80 mmHg, RR 12. Included is a copy of their resting EKG. What is the likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient presents to their cardiologist to discuss increasing episodes of dyspnea after climbing stairs. They also now need three pillows at night to sleep. Physical examination reveals an early diastolic murmur best appreciated at the left sternal border with bounding peripheral pulses. The cardiologist is very concerned and immediately refers the patient for a surgical workup. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old patient with a medical history significant for asthma, hypertension, and occasional IV drug use comes to the emergency department with fever. On physical exam, there are findings depicted in figure A, for which the patient cannot account. What test will be most helpful to establish the diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to their primary care doctor with several weeks of headaches and low-grade fevers. Their medical history is notable for a motor vehicle accident when they were in their 20's that required multiple blood transfusions, and three separate courses of antibiotics for pneumonia in the past 2 years. Review of systems reveals 10-pound weight loss in last 3 months. They have notable left-sided weakness while walking into the clinic, and, on further exam, they have markedly slurred speech and cervical, axial, and inguinal lymphadenopathy is present. A head CT is ordered, which is shown in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 21-year-old Caucasian patient presents to your office with wheezing and rhinitis. Laboratory results show peripheral eosinophilia and antibodies against neutrophil myeloperoxidase. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 46-year-old patient presents to a psychiatrist for evaluation. Three months prior, the patient moved to a new apartment building, and since then, they have become increasingly convinced that their doorman has been stealing their packages and going into their apartment while they are not home. They state that objects do not stay where they leave them, and sometimes they expect mail but never receive it. They have filed numerous complaints with their leasing company. The building has 24-hour security footage, however, which has never shown any other person entering their apartment. On further questioning, the patient denies audiovisual hallucinations or changes in sleep, mood, energy levels, or eating. The family reports that their behavior and affect have not changed. The patient works as a pharmacist. They have no psychiatric history, although their father had a history of major depressive disorder. Which of the following is the likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old Caucasian patient presents to your office with hematuria and right flank pain. They have no history of renal dialysis but have a history of recurrent urinary tract infections. You order an intravenous pyelogram, which reveals multiple cysts of the collecting ducts in the medulla. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 37-year-old patient with a history of HIV presents to the emergency room with back pain. They report intermittent fevers for the past week. They report that they chose to come to the emergency room now because the back pain is more severe and they have also started having trouble controlling their bowels. Their vital signs are Temp 38.5 C, HR 100, BP 110/70, RR 16, and O2 99% on room air. Exam of their arm is shown in Figure A. On physical examination of their back and extremities, there is tenderness to palpation along the lower spine, weakness in the bilateral legs (right greater than left), and hyporeflexia bilaterally. Rectal examination reveals saddle anesthesia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 77-year-old patient comes to your office for a routine visit. They are doing well, and their only complaint is the recent appearance of several brown greasy appearing lesions on their forehead (figure A) that they can't seem to peel off. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician. The patient has a history of hypertension, which was found to be the result of an adrenal mass. They are status post resection. On physical exam, vital signs are HR 78 bpm, BP 135/90 mmHg, RR 12 rpm, Sat 100%. Examination of the neck reveals a 2 cm firm, immobile, and nontender mass in the right inferior pole of the thyroid. Laboratory evaluation reveals normal TSH, PTH, and calcium. A biopsy of the lesion is obtained, with H&E staining shown in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old Caucasian patient presents to your office with hypopigmented skin. They undergo a skin biopsy and are found to have an absence of melanocytes in the epidermis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-year-old patient is brought to their pediatrician for evaluation of a red rash. They have no past medical history and have met all developmental milestones. On presentation, they are found to have the rash seen in Figure A on their chest. They are told that they do not need any treatments. Two weeks later, they are found to have dozens of rose-colored spots on their back. These lesions do not cause any symptoms and disappear after another 6 weeks. Which of the following is associated with this patient's most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient comes to the clinic for an annual well-check. Their past medical history includes diabetes and hypertension, which are well-controlled with metformin and losartan, respectively. The patient reports a healthy diet consisting of mainly vegetables and lean meat. They deny smoking or alcohol use. They enjoy taking walks with their partner and sunbathing. Physical examination is unremarkable except for a rough, scaly, sand paper-like plaque on their left dorsal hand with no tenderness or pain. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 74-year-old patient with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus is brought to their primary care doctor by their son who is concerned about the patient's ability to manage their activities of daily living. They have been living alone since their spouse passed away 2 years ago. They have remained an active member of their retirement community's wine club; however, they stopped attending the meetings 3 weeks ago. They are generally able to maintain their house, but their house appears more disorganized over the past 2 weeks. They generally drive short distances but avoid driving long distances as they occasionally get lost when navigating new areas. They feel like their balance is getting worse, but they have not fallen. They have noticed increased urinary urgency over the past 8 months and have had 2 episodes of incontinence. Despite these changes, they report feeling well. They drink 4-6 glasses of wine per day. They were started on multiple medications for worsening anxiety by their psychiatrist 1 month ago. Their BMI is 31 kg/m^2. Their temperature is 99.8°F (37.7°C), blood pressure is 115/65 mmHg, pulse is 95/min, and respirations are 17/min. On examination, they are oriented to person and time but not place or situation. They do not seem to recognize their doctor despite knowing them for many years. They become somnolent intermittently throughout the interview. They can recall 0/3 words after 5 minutes. They have a low-frequency tremor in their right arm that increases in severity with deliberate movement. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 24-year-old patient is brought to the hospital by their mother because they have "not been themselves" for the past 3 months. The patient says they hear voices in their head. The mother said that when she is talking to her child, she can’t seem to make out what they are saying; it is as if their thoughts are disorganized. When talking with the patient, you notice a lack of energy and an apathetic affect. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 45-year-old patient presents to the physician with complaints of intermittent episodes of severe headaches and palpitations. During these episodes, they notice that they sweat profusely and become pale in complexion. They describe the episodes as coming and going within the past 2 months. Their temperature is 99.3°F (37.4°C), blood pressure is 165/118 mmHg, pulse is 126/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 90% on room air. Which of the following would be the first medication given to treat this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 37-year-old patient accompanied by their partner presents to the emergency department after loss of consciousness 30 minutes ago. The partner reports that they were sitting in a chair at home and began having sustained rhythmic contractions of all 4 extremities for approximately 1 minute. During transport via ambulance they appeared confused but arousable. Their partner reports they have no medical conditions, but for the past 2 months they have occasionally complained of episodes of sweating, palpitations, and anxiety. Their sibling has epilepsy and their parent has type 1 diabetes mellitus. Laboratory studies obtained in the emergency department demonstrate the following: Serum: Na+: 136 mEq/L K+: 3.8 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L HCO3-: 19 mEq/L BUN: 16 mg/dL Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL Glucose: 54 mg/dL C-peptide: Low Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 8-year-old patient presents to their primary care provider with several months of headaches and impaired vision. Physical exam reveals a patient in the 10th percentile for height and 43rd percentile for weight; cranial nerve testing demonstrates bitemporal hemianopsia. They undergo a head CT, which shows suprasellar calcifications (Figure A). Given their likely diagnosis, which of the following are also derived from the same germ cell layer?

A 38-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for evaluation of 3 months of increasing fatigue. They state that they feel normal in the morning, but that their fatigue gets worse throughout the day. Specifically, they say that their head drops when trying to perform overhead tasks. They also say that they experience double vision when watching television or reading a book. On physical exam, there is right-sided ptosis after sustaining upward gaze for 2 minutes. Which of the following treatments may be effective in treating this patient's diagnosis?

A 35-year-old patient presents to a psychiatrist for an initial consultation. They report that for the past 3 years, they have experienced several periods of depressed mood. The episodes do not coincide with any specific life events and seem to resolve after 4-6 weeks. During these episodes, they experience a depressed mood, sleep disturbances, and a poor appetite, but they at times are able to enjoy spending time with their children and partner but other times they are distressed and cannot enjoy time with them. Upon further questioning, they also report experiencing occasional episodes of elevated mood over the past ten years. During these episodes, they are very productive at their work as a lawyer and require less sleep than usual. Their past medical history is notable for obesity, type I diabetes mellitus, and rheumatoid arthritis. They are on insulin and take methotrexate. They smoke marijuana occasionally. Their temperature is 99.2°F (37.3°C), blood pressure is 124/80 mmHg, pulse is 78/min, and respirations are 17/min. On exam, they are quiet with a flattened affect, but are cooperative and answer questions thoroughly. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A parent-teacher conference is called to discuss the behavior of a 9-year-old patient. According to the patient's teacher, they have become progressively more disruptive during class. They are performing poorly in school and have trouble focusing. They are destructive to classroom property, tore a classmate's art project, and take other children's lunches regularly. They are avoided by their classmates. Their parent reports that their child can "sometimes be difficult." Recently they placed a rubber band around the cat's tail, resulting in gangrene. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old patient presents to their physician with a complaint of lower back pain and stiffness for the past few months. They describe the pain as being worse in the morning and then gradually improving with activity throughout the day. On physical exam, they have decreased anterior flexion of the lumbar spine. A radiograph of the lumbar spine is obtained and is shown in Figure A. What is the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old patient comes to the clinic complaining of headache and sinus drainage for the past 13 days. They report cold-like symptoms 2 weeks ago that progressively got worse. The patient endorses subjective fever, congestion, sinus headache, cough, and chills. They claim that this is their 5th episode within the past year and are concerned if “there’s something else going on.” Their medical history is significant for asthma that is adequately controlled with their albuterol inhaler. Their laboratory findings are shown below: Serum: Hemoglobin: 16.2 g/dL Hematocrit: 39 % Leukocyte count: 7,890/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 200,000/mm^3 IgA: 54 mg/dL (Normal: 76-390 mg/dL) IgE: 0 IU/mL (Normal: 0-380 IU/mL) IgG: 470 mg/dL (Normal: 650-1500 mg/dL) IgM: 29 mg/dL (Normal: 40-345 mg/dL) What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician complaining of increased fatigue over the last year. They also say that their friends say they appear to be more pale. Their past medical history is significant for 10 years of arthritis. Physical exam reveals spoon-shaped nails as well as conjunctival pallor. Based on clinical suspicion, RBC tests are ordered showing a mean corpuscular volume (MCV) of 75 fl (normal 80-100 fl) and a peripheral blood smear is obtained and found to be normal. Iron studies show a serum iron of 30 micromolar (normal range 50-170) and a serum ferritin of 300 micrograms/liter (normal range 15-200). What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 22-year-old patient presents to a psychiatrist complaining of mood fluctuations. They are accompanied by their mother who reports that the patient recently experienced a 5-day episode of minimal sleep and unusual levels of energy. The patient admits to spending $2,000 of their parent’s money, without asking, on a down payment for a motorcycle. The episode resolved after 5 days, at which point the patient felt guilty and upset. The patient’s medical history is notable for multiple month-long episodes in the past 2 years of feeling sad, sleeping more than usual, being uninterested in their hobbies, and feeling constantly tired and guilty. The patient has a history of severe meningoencephalitis at the age of 17 requiring four days in the intensive care unit. During that episode, they reported seeing monkeys in their hospital room. On exam, they are a well-appearing, cooperative patient in no acute distress. They are alert and oriented with a normal affect. They state that they feel sad and guilty about what happens. They deny suicidal ideation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 17-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parents who are concerned about their bizarre behavior. Over the past three months, they have become withdrawn from their friends and less interested in their classes and extracurricular activities. On several occasions, they have torn apart rooms in their home looking for “bugs” and states that the President is spying on them because aliens have told the government that they are a threat. Although they have always been quite clean in the past, their parent notes that the patient’s room is now malodorous with clothes and dishes strewn about haphazardly. They also say that sometimes they can hear the devil speaking to them from inside their head. They have no medical problems, do not drink alcohol or use any drugs. Physical examination of the patient reveals no abnormalities. On mental status examination, the patient is oriented to person, place and time. They avoid eye contact and reply mostly with monosyllabic responses. They appear distracted, and confirm that they are hearing whispering voices in their head. What is the most appropriate diagnosis for this patient?

A 34-year-old patient with a previous diagnosis of Grave’s disease presents for a check-up. Since their diagnosis 4 months ago, the patient’s symptoms have been relatively well-controlled with medications since starting them 3 weeks ago after an initial unsuccessful course of radioiodine ablation. The patient’s complete blood count reveals decreased absolute neutrophils at 450/mL and a slightly decreased hematocrit of 39%. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient’s abnormal laboratory results?

A 28-year-old patient presents to trauma surgery clinic after undergoing an exploratory laparotomy, femoral intramedullary nail, and femoral artery vascular repair 3 months ago. They suffered multiple gunshot wounds as a victim of a drive-by shooting. They are progressing well with well-healed surgical incisions on examination. They state during their clinic visit that they have been experiencing 6 weeks of nightmares where they "relive the day they were shot." The patient also endorses 6 weeks of flashbacks to "the shooter pointing the gun at them" during the daytime as well. They state that they have had difficulty sleeping and cannot concentrate when performing tasks. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old African American patient presents to their primary care provider complaining of progressively worsening back pain. The pain is localized to the lower back and sometimes wakes them up from sleep. They have a history of hypertension and admit to a 50 pack-year smoking history. Further questioning reveals that they have also experienced fatigue and an unintentional weight loss of 18 pounds over the past year. Laboratory analysis is notable for an elevated alkaline phosphatase. A radiograph of the patient’s spine demonstrates multiple sclerotic lesions in the lumbar vertebral bodies. Which of the following tests would most likely confirm the diagnosis in this patient?

A 67-year-old patient presents with a large, painful, skin lesion on their leg (Figure A). They have had a non-healing ulcer in the same location for several years after a burn, but they note that it has never looked like this before. They have a past medical history of diabetes. They are a 30-pack-year smoker. Vital signs are stable. In addition to the skin lesion, their physical examination is notable for stocking glove neuropathy of the hands and feet. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with a fever and a rash. Their parents state that their symptoms started last night and have been rapidly worsening. The patient is up to date on their vaccinations, and their past medical history is unremarkable. Their temperature is 103°F (39.4°C), blood pressure is 97/48 mmHg, pulse is 160/min, respirations are 28/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A without any lesions on mucosal surfaces. The patient's skin is warm and tender to the touch. Which of the following describes the most likely diagnosis?

A 12-month-old patient is brought in by their parent to the pediatrician for the first time since their 6-month checkup. The parent states that their child had been doing fine, but the parents are now concerned that their child is still not able to stand up or speak. On exam, the patient has a temperature of 98.5°F (36.9°C), pulse is 96/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 100/80 mmHg. The child appears to have difficulty supporting themselves while sitting. The patient has no other abnormal physical findings. They play by themselves and are making babbling noises but do not respond to their own name. They appear to have some purposeless motions. A previous clinic note documents typical development at their 6-month visit and mentioned that the patient was sitting unsupported at that time. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 37-year-old patient presents to their gastroenterologist due to a transaminitis found by their primary care physician (PCP). They report currently feeling well and have no acute concerns. Medical history is significant for ulcerative colitis treated with 5-aminosalicylate. They recently went on a trip to Mexico and experienced an episode of mild diarrhea. The patient is 5 ft 4 in and weighs 220 lbs (99.8 kg). Their temperature is 98°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 138/88 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, and respirations are 18/min. Physical examination is unremarkable. Laboratory testing demonstrates: Leukocyte count: 7,200 /mm^3 Alkaline phosphatase: 205 U/L Aspartate aminotransferase (AST): 120 U/L Alanine aminotransferase (ALT): 115 U/L Perinuclear antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (pANCA): Positive Antimitochondrial antibody: Negative Which of the following is most likely the diagnosis?

A 5-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by their parents after a month of fatigue, difficulty concentrating, and diffuse abdominal pain. The pain has been mild, does not radiate, and was not associated with eating. They deny any nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Their parents recently noticed that they began to drag their feet while walking. They have no significant past medical or surgical history and do not take any medication. Their family recently began renovations on their home 3 months ago. On physical exam, their vital signs are within normal limits. Blood work shows the following findings: Hematocrit: 30% Total iron: 60 µg/dL Ferritin: 215 ng/mL Mean corpuscular volume: 65 µm^3 A peripheral blood smear shown in Figure A. Which of the following diseases involves the same metabolic pathway as the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 12-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with a swollen and painful knee. They say that they were exploring with their friends when they tripped and hit their knee against the ground. They didn't feel like they hit it very hard but it started swelling and becoming very painful. Their parent reports that they have always been prone to bleeding from very minor trauma and that others in the family have had similar problems. Based on clinical suspicion a coagulation panel was obtained showing a prothrombin time (PT) of 10 seconds (normal range 9-11 seconds), a partial thromboplastin time (PTT) of 45 seconds (normal 20-35 seconds), and a normal ristocetin cofactor assay (equivalent to bleeding time). Mixing tests with factor IX and XI do not show complementation, but mixing with factor VIII reverses the coagulation abnormality. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 52-year-old patient presents with several months of fatigue, malaise, dry cough, and occasional episodes of painless hematuria. They recall having had a sore throat several days prior to the onset of these symptoms that resolved without antibiotics. Physical exam is remarkable for diffusely coarse breath sounds bilaterally. Urinalysis reveals 2+ protein, 2+ blood, and numerous red blood cell casts are visible under light microscopy. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old patient presents to their primary care doctor with continued hypertension despite adherence to multiple anti-hypertensive medications. The physician suspects that the patient may have elevated aldosterone levels and wants to initiate a trial of an aldosterone receptor antagonist. The patient is very concerned about side effects, particularly sexual dysfunction and breast tenderness, as they had a friend who took a similar medication and had these side-effects. Which of the following is the best medication to initiate, given their concerns and the physician's diagnosis?

A 4-month-old patient is seen for ongoing lethargy and vomiting. They were born to a 31-year-old parent with a history of hypertension. They have had 7 episodes of non-bloody, non-bilious vomiting and 3 wet diapers over the last 24 hours. Laboratory results are shown below. Serum: Na+: 132 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L K+: 3.2 mEq/L HCO3-: 27 mEq/L BUN: 13 mg/dL Glucose: 30 mg/dL Lactate: 2 mmol/L Urine ketones: < 20 mg/dL Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 10-year-old patient is brought to the physician by their parents due to 2 months of a progressively worsening headache. The headaches were initially infrequent and their parents attributed them to stress from a recent move. However, over the last week the headaches have gotten significantly worse and they had one episode of vomiting this morning when they woke up. Their medical history is remarkable for a hospitalization during infancy for bacterial meningitis. On physical exam, the patient has difficulty looking up. The lower portion of their pupil is covered by the lower eyelid and there is sclera visible below the upper eyelid. A magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A tall, 25-year-old patient is brought to the ED by their friend after sudden difficulty breathing while smoking a cigarette. In the trauma bay they are tachypneic, but able to talk to you. Vital signs show that they are afebrile and tachycardic with blood pressure of 115/60. Physical exam reveals hyperresonance and absent breath sounds over the left upper lung. A chest x-ray is obtained and shown below. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 78-year-old patient presents to the emergency room with crampy abdominal pain and bloating. Their last bowel movement was three days ago and they have not passed gas over the same time period. Their past medical history is notable for Alzheimer's disease, hypertension, and stable angina. They take donezepil, aspirin, enalapril, and metoprolol. Their temperature is 100.8°F (38.2°C), blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg, pulse is 110/min, and respirations are 24/min. On examination, their abdomen is notably distended and tender to palpation. A frontal abdominal radiograph is shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 46-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician with one week of intermittent nausea and vomiting. They do not have any sick contacts, and their medical history is significant only for diabetes well-controlled on metformin. They also complain of some weakness and back/leg pain. They say that they recently returned from traveling abroad and had been administered an antibiotic during their travels for an unknown infection. On presentation, their temperature is 98.6°F (37°C), blood pressure is 119/78 mmHg, pulse is 62/min, and respirations are 25/min. An EKG is obtained showing flattening of the T wave. After further testing, the physician prescribes a thiazide for this patient. Which of the following diseases is also associated with this patient's most likely diagnosis?

A 9-year-old patient is brought to the emergency room by their parent for weakness, diaphoresis, and syncope. Their parent says that they have never been diagnosed with any medical conditions but has been having “fainting spells” over the past month. Routine lab work reveals a glucose level of 25 mg/dL. The patient is promptly given glucagon and intravenous dextrose and admitted to the hospital for observation. The patient’s parent stays with them during their hospitalization. The patient is successfully watched overnight and their blood glucose levels normalize on their morning levels. The care team discusses a possible discharge during morning rounds. One hour later the nurse is called in for a repeat fainting episode. A c-peptide level is drawn and shown to be low. The patient appears ill, diaphoretic, and is barely arousable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this child?

A young Mediterranean teen brings their 4-year-old little sibling to the Emergency Room because of a high temperature. Their parents are on their way to the hospital, but, in the meantime, they provide some of the history. They explain that the child has been running a fever and limping for the past week. This morning, they had trouble awakening them, and they noticed some swelling and redness around their right ankle. In terms of their past medical history, they know the child has something wrong with their blood. They had to receive extra vaccinations as an infant, and they take an antibiotic every day. On exam in the ED, their temperature is 102.4 deg F (39.1 deg C), blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg, pulse is 123/min, and respirations are 22/min. They are lethargic, and their exam is noteworthy for erythema and edema in an area surrounding their distal shin. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 18-year-old patient is seen for a routine physical prior to starting college. They will be moving from Ohio to California, away from their family for the first time. Their temperature is 36.8 deg C (98.2 deg F), pulse is 74/min, and blood pressure is 122/68 mmHg. BMI is 24. On questioning, they reveal that they have a habit of binge eating during times of stress, particularly during exams. They then feel guilty about their behavior and attempt to compensate by going to the gym, sometimes for 4+ hours per day. They are disturbed by this behavior and feel out of control. They deny ever vomiting as a means of losing weight. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old patient thinks poorly of themselves and is extremely sensitive to criticism. They are socially inhibited and have never had a romantic relationship, although they desire one. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old patient presents to the emergency department for chest pain. They say that the chest pain began a few hours prior to presentation and is associated with nausea, abdominal discomfort, and sweating. They have experienced similar symptoms multiple times in the past, which brings them great concern because they believe they may be having a heart attack. This concern has persisted for 2 months. They deny any medications or illicit drug use. Physical examination is unremarkable. An electrocardiogram demonstrates sinus tachycardia with a pulse of 110/min. A parent-teacher conference is called to discuss the behavior of a 9 year-old patient. According to the patient's teacher, they have become progressively more disruptive during class. When asked to help clean up or read out-loud, they reply with "You're not the boss of me." or "You can't make me." They refuse to participate in gym class, but will play the same games during recess. They get along with and are well-liked by their peers. Their parent reports that their child can "sometimes be difficult," but they are helpful around the house and is very good playing with their 7-year-old sibling. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old patient presents to their primary care physician for a checkup. They have felt weaker lately and have lost some weight. They deny any urinary issues. Their BUN at their last visit 4 months ago was 45 mg/dL, and their creatinine was 2.0 mg/dL. Their laboratory studies this visit are seen below: Hemoglobin: 8 g/dL Hematocrit: 29% Leukocyte count: 9,500/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 197,000/mm^3 Serum: Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L K+: 5.9 mEq/L HCO3-: 17 mEq/L BUN: 59 mg/dL Glucose: 99 mg/dL Creatinine: 2.3 mg/dL Ca2+: 9.0 mg/dL Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 18-year-old patient presents to the student health department at their university for recurrent palpitations. The patient had previously presented to the emergency department (ED) for sudden onset palpitations five months ago when they first started college. They had a negative cardiac workup in the ED and they were discharged with a 24-hour Holter monitor which was also negative. They have no history of any medical or psychiatric illnesses. The patient reports that since their initial ED visit, they have had several episodes of unprovoked palpitations associated with feelings of dread and lightheadedness though they cannot identify a particular trigger. Recently, they have begun sitting towards the back of the lecture halls so that they can “quickly escape and not make a scene” in case they get an episode in class. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 43-year-old homeless patient is brought to the emergency room for severe abdominal pain. They are known to the emergency department for repeated visits for alcohol intoxication. They report that the pain started about 3 hours ago and describes it as sharp, piercing, 10/10, and concentrated at the epigastric region with radiation to the back. Their past medical history is unclear given their homeless status. Their temperature is 100.4°F (38°C), blood pressure is 104/80 mmHg, the pulse is 104/min, and respirations are 16/min.
