No lesions are appreciated in oral mucosa. Patient is up to date with vaccinations.

A 2-day-old male is noted to have a rash all over the body and distorted feet at birth. A 24 week ultrasound was remarkable for bilateral shortening of the long bones. Physical examination demonstrates light, fine yellow scales along curvilinear distribution on the chest, bilateral upper and lower extremities on background diffuse erythema. The bilateral feet are turned inward with plantar aspect almost sideways. An X-ray of the knees demonstrate focal dot-like calcifications in the epiphyses.

A 40-year-old male presents for evaluation of spots on the face and stiff fingers. He reports a several year history of blue discoloration of the fingertips when exposed to cold climates after prolonged periods of time with some intermittent numbness. Review of systems is remarkable for difficulty swallowing. Physical examination reveals firm white-yellow papules on the bilateral index fingertips, multiple telangiectasias across the face, and tightened skin around all fingers resulting in near claw like appearance of the hands.

A 12-year-old healthy female presents for evaluation of rash on the chest and back ongoing for the past 4 days. Father reports that he first noticed a larger spot on her right flank, then smaller similar lesions began developing all over the chest and back. He denies any history of eczema for the patient or family history. He denies any new topical products. The rash is not painful or itchy. Father has tried topical over the counter hydrocortisone without any improvement. Physical examination is remarkable for erythematous pink thin papules and plaques with overlying fine thin scale on the back and chest. A larger thin scaly plaque is appreciated on the right flank. A KOH preparation is performed and does not reveal any fungal elements.

A 6-year-old female with past medical history of aortic root dilation presents for evaluation of loose skin that was noticed at birth but has progressively worsened. Family members have noticed the patient's skin is saggy but thought it may be related to overeating. The patient's father reports other family members may have similar skin. Physical examination reveals loose, sagging skin of the cheeks, neck, axilla, thighs. A punch biopsy demonstrates loss of elastic fibers. Arm span width to body height ratio is within normal limits.

A 50-year-old African American female with past medical history of hypertension and hypertension presents for evaluation of light spots on her legs that she initially noticed one year ago. The lesions are not painful or itchy, but she is concerned that they are increasing in frequency. When they first develop they do not significantly grow in size. She has not tried any treatments. Physical examination demonstrates multiple hypopigmented ovoid macules scattered on the distal shins bilaterally.

A 55-year-old male with past medical history of medication non-compliance, non-insulin dependent diabetes, hyperlipidemia, and hypertension presents for evaluation of rash around the eyes that began six months ago. He denies applying any topical products to the area. He denies any trauma, pruritus, or pain. The rash has been stable in size since it first began. He denies any ulcerations or erosions of the rash. He has not tried any treatments. Physical examination is remarkable for well-defined, yellow waxy thin flat topped plaques on the medial upper and lower canthi. A shave biopsy is performed and reveals foamy histiocytes in dermis.

A 6-month-old female with no past medical history presents to the emergency department for evaluation of fevers, difficulty feeding, and skin peeling. Patient's mother reports the patient developed fevers four days ago and then over the past two days developed skin peeling initially around the mouth that then spread to the underarms and groin area. She denies any recent travel, exposure to plants, or any medications. Physical examination is remarkable for periocular crusting, erythema, perioral fissuring, and skin desquamation around the neck, bilateral axilla, groin folds, and popliteal fossas with areas of mild serous crust. Gram stain from a bacterial swab of the the neck does not reveal any bacteria.

A 7-month-old male presents to the emergency department for evaluation of a rash and swelling of the hands and feet. Patient's father reports the patient developed high fevers up to 103 Farenheit over the past six days, rough skin on the chest, back, arms and swelling in the hands and feet. Father denies any recent travel or any medication exposures. Review of systems is positive for conjunctival injection. Physical examination is remarkable for palpable cervical lymph nodes, multiple prominent tongue papillae, diffuse background erythematous patches across the chest, back, and arms. Swelling of the hands and feet is appreciated.

A 34-year-old healthy male presents for evaluation of a bump on his left third finger present over the past nine months. He denies any trauma to the area and first noticed it when getting a manicure. The spot began as a small bump that progressively enlargened with associated depression of the fingernail. Physical examination of the left third finger reveals a translucent nodule along the proximal nail fold with associated longitudinal depression of the nail plate.

A 43-year-old male presents to clinic for evaluation of hair loss along the frontal scalp ongoing over the past year. He reports a twenty year long history of wearing a wig daily and secures his hair in place with tight headband underneath. He denies any significant pain or pruritus in the areas of hair loss. He has tried numerous over the counter oils and shampoos without any improvement. Physical examination reveals significant hair thinning and regression of the hairline with preservation of the hair follicles along the frontotemporal scalp. No significant perifollicular erythema is appreciated.

A 45-year-old female with past medical history of recently diagnosed tinea pedis presents for evaluation of a mildly pruritic rash on the thigh and buttock ongoing over the past five days. She reports the rash initially began as a red dot but rapidly expands in size with some white flakes in the middle. Physical examination is remarkable for multiple bright pink erythematous annular plaques with white thin collarette of scale along the inner margins. A punch biopsy is performed of an annular plaque and does not reveal any fungal hyphae.

A 6-year-old male with history of atopic dermatitis presents with his father for evaluation of a rash on the right lower leg. The patient's dad reports the rash developed over the past two weeks and may be growing in size after having a few weeks of cold like symptoms. He denies any new topical products, fragrances, or dyes. He has not tried any treatments. Physical examination is remarkable for multiple pink flat topped scaly papules coalescing into plaques in a curvilinear distribution on the right posterior thigh and calf. Punch biopsy reveals a lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, superficial perivascular inflammation and deeper lymphocytic perieccrine inflammation.

A 16-year-old female with past medical history of mitral valve prolapse presents for evaluation of loose skin. Patient's parents report a several year history of stretchy skin, poor wound healing with some scars healing with thin overlying skin, and easy bruising. There is a family history of similar symptoms amongst other family members. Physical examination reveals soft, significantly extensible skin diffusely, multiple linear scars with atrophic overlying pink patches, and white-yellow papules along the bilateral inner and outer calcaneus upon standing. The patient is able to touch the tip of her nose with her tongue.

A 30-year-old female presents for evaluation of a dark discoloration on the posterior thighs present for the past month. She denies any topical products applied to the area. She denies any pain or pruritus at the area. She has not tried any treatments. The rash has been stable in size, is constant, and is not significantly growing in size. She works a desk job and reports sitting on a seat warmer over the past several years. Physical examination reveals reticulated lacy brown patches on the posterior thighs and lower buttocks.

A 65-year-old male with past medical history of hypertension, insulin-dependent diabetes, coronary artery disease, and a 30 year smoking year history presents for evaluation of rash ongoing for the past 2 weeks. The patient reports the rash initially began on the upper back and has slowly spread in size. He denies any significant pruritus or pain associated with the rash. He denies using any new topical products. Review of systems is remarkable for twenty pound weight loss, malaise, increasing cough, and shortness of breath. Physical examination reveals symmetric, multiple polycyclic serpiginous concentric pink plaques on the upper back extending onto the lower back. No scale is appreciated.

A 61-year-old female with past medical history of insulin-dependent diabetes, atrial fibrillation not on anticoagulation presents for evaluation of toenail discoloration. She reports a several year history of yellowing and thickening of multiple toenails. She previously was getting her nails clipped at the podiatrist. She has not tried any other treatments. She is an avid swimmer at the local indoor pool. Physical examination reveals hyperkeratotic yellow-white thickening of the bilateral first, second, and third nailplates with significant subungual debris. She denies any rash elsewhere on the body or any history of skin conditions.

A 36-year-old female with a past medical history of poorly controlled Crohn's disease presents for evaluation of a painful non-healing wound on the left lower leg. Patient endorses a pus bump developing on the left leg two months ago which she initially thought was a spider bite but eventually popped open. She was seen at urgent care a month ago and received one week course of cephalexin without any improvement. Local debridement attempts at bedside by the urgent care provider resulted in significant expansion of the ulcer. Physical examination reveals a well demarcated ovoid ulcer on the left distal shin with violaceous, rolled borders and cribriform base with yellow-red exudate.

A 3-year-old male presents with his father for evaluation of a rash present for two days. Father notes the patient developed a runny nose, cough, and fever four days prior to onset of rash which began as small raised red bumps on the chest and progressively spread to arms and legs. Father denies any medication exposures or new topical products. Physical examination reveals multiple juicy, monomorphic erythematous pink scattered papules on the arms, legs, buttock with sparing of the chest and back. The patient is up to date with vaccinations.

A 35-year-old African American male presents for evaluation of a painless tongue growth present for the past three months. He denies biting the site or any inciting trauma. He noted it when brushing his teeth and it has slowly grown in size. Physical examination reveals a pink nodule on the right mid-tongue. An excisional biopsy is performed and reveals pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia and collections of large polygonal cells with abundant cytoplasm and small cytoplasmic inclusions in the dermis.

A 21-year-old female presents for evaluation of a painful rash on her right index finger. She reports a tingling sensation prior to the eruption of red small spots that became more yellow and pus filled. She denies any trauma or topical products applied to the area. She has a history of cold sores on the lips. Physical examination reveals multiple clustered painful, white-yellow vesicles on the right index finger on erythematous pink base.

A 34-year-old male with past medical history of anxiety presents for evaluation of a 4 month history of abnormal nail grooves on the bilateral thumbnails. He denies any trauma that may have incited the nail changes. He does not get his nails done and does not wear nail polish. He admits to frequently rubbing his thumbnails with his index finger when he's nervous. Physical examination demonstrates longitudinal depressions on the bilateral midline thumbnails with horizontal ridges.

A 66-year-old woman comes to the physician for a 3-month history of fatigue. She has hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She had a transient ischemic attack 3 years ago. She drinks 3 beers a day, and sometimes a couple more on social occasions. She currently takes aspirin, simvastatin, hydrochlorothiazide, and metoprolol. Her temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 78, respirations are 19/min, and oxygen saturation on room air is 97%. She is in no distress but shows marked pallor and has multiple pinpoint, red, nonblanching spots on her extremities. On palpation, her spleen is significantly enlarged. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin of 8.0 g/dL, a leukocyte count of 80,000/mm3, and a platelet count of 34,000/mm3. A blood smear shows immature cells with large, prominent nucleoli and pink, elongated, needle-shaped cytoplasmic inclusions. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old woman comes to the emergency department for the evaluation of two episodes of red urine since this morning. She has no pain with urination. She reports lower back pain and fever. Six months ago, she was diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the right knee that she manages with 1–2 tablets of ibuprofen per day. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the past 45 years. She does not drink alcohol. Her temperature is 38.5°C (101.3°F), pulse is 95/min, and blood pressure is 130/80 mm Hg. Physical examination shows faint, diffuse maculopapular rash, and bilateral flank pain. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Urinalysis shows:
Blood +3
Protein +1
RBC 10–12/hpf
RBC cast negative
Eosinophils numerous
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old woman with AIDS comes to the physician because of a 2-day history of decreasing vision and seeing black spots in her right eye. She has no pain and the left eye is asymptomatic. She was treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago with fluconazole. She was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago. Current medications include efavirenz, tenofovir, emtricitabine, azithromycin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, multivitamins, and a nutritional supplement. She is 170 cm (5 ft 7 in) tall and weighs 45 kg (99 lbs); BMI is 15.6 kg/m2. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 89/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. Examination shows cervical lymphadenopathy. There are multiple violaceous plaques seen over her trunk and extremities. Fundoscopic examination shows granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages. Her CD4+ T-lymphocyte count is 36/mm3. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old Asian man comes to the physician for a routine health maintenance examination. On questioning, he has had occasional night sweats during the past 2 months. He has not had fevers or weight loss. Seven months ago, he had an acute myocardial infarction and was treated with percutaneous coronary intervention. He has hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and gastroesophageal reflux disease. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 37 years. Current medications include aspirin, atorvastatin, ramipril, metoprolol, and esomeprazole. He is 178 cm (5 ft 10 in) tall and weighs 89 kg (207 lbs); BMI is 29.7 kg/m2. His temperature is 37.4°C (99.3°F), pulse is 84/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 145/80 mm Hg. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Cardiac examination shows an S4. There is a nontender skin lesion near the right large toenail. A photograph of the lesion is shown. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of progressive right knee pain for the past 3 months. She reports that the pain is worse at night and while doing sports at school. She has not had any trauma to the knee or any previous problems with her joints. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Examination of the right knee shows mild swelling and tenderness without warmth or erythema; the range of motion is limited. She walks with an antalgic gait. Laboratory studies show an alkaline phosphatase of 180 U/L and an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 80 mm/h. An x-ray of the right knee is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old college student comes to the physician because he has been extremely sad for the past 3 weeks and has to cry constantly. Three weeks ago, his girlfriend left him after they were together for 4 years. He has no appetite and has had a 2.3-kg (5.1-lb) weight loss. He has missed several classes because he could not stop crying or get out of bed. He thinks about his ex-girlfriend all the time. He says that he experienced similar symptoms for about 2 months after previous relationships ended. The patient is 158 cm (5 ft 2 in) tall and weighs 45 kg (100 lb); BMI is 18 kg/m2. His temperature is 36.1°C (97°F), pulse is 65/min, and blood pressure is 110/60 mm Hg. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. On mental status examination he appears sad and cries easily. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old man comes to the physician for a follow-up visit. He has a 2-year history of depressed mood and fatigue accompanied by early morning awakening. One week ago, he started feeling a decrease in his need for sleep and now feels rested after about 5 hours of sleep per night. He had two similar episodes that occurred 6 months ago and a year ago, respectively. He reports increased energy and libido. He has a 4-kg (8.8-lb) weight loss over the past month. He does not feel the need to eat and says he derives his energy "from the universe". He enjoys his work as a librarian. He started taking fluoxetine 3 months ago. On mental exam, he is alert and oriented to time and place; he is irritable. He does not have auditory or visual hallucinations. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of fever, malaise, and severe right knee joint pain and swelling for 3 days. She had also had episodes of abdominal pain and epistaxis during this period. Five days ago, she had swelling and pain in her left ankle joint which has since resolved. She reports having a sore throat 3 weeks ago while she was camping in the woods, for which she received symptomatic treatment. Her immunizations are up-to-date. Her temperature is 38.7°C (101.6°F), pulse is 119/min, and blood pressure is 90/60 mm Hg. Examination shows a swollen, tender right knee; range of motion is limited. There are painless 3- to 4-mm nodules over the elbow. Cardiopulmonary examination is normal. Her hemoglobin concentration is 12.3 g/dL, leukocyte count is 11,800/mm3, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate is 58 mm/h. Arthrocentesis of the right knee joint yields clear, straw-colored fluid; no organisms are identified on Gram stain. Analysis of the synovial fluid shows a leukocyte count of 1,350/mm3 with 17% neutrophils. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 73-year-old man is brought to the physician by his son because of increasing forgetfulness over the past 2 years. Initially, he used to misplace keys and forget his dog's name or his phone number. Now, he often forgets about what he has seen on television or read about the day before. He used to go for a walk every morning but stopped one month ago after he became lost on his way back home. His son has prevented him from cooking because he has had episodes of leaving the gas stove oven on after making a meal. He becomes agitated when asked questions directly but is unconcerned when his son reports his history and says he is overprotective of him. He has hypertension, coronary artery disease, and hypercholesterolemia. Current medications include aspirin, enalapril, carvedilol, and atorvastatin. He is alert and oriented to place and person but not to time. Vital signs are within normal limits. Short- and long-term memory deficits are present. His speech rhythm is normal but is frequently interrupted as he thinks of words to frame his sentences. He makes multiple errors while performing serial sevens. His clock drawing is impaired and he draws 14 numbers. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 75-year-old woman comes to the physician for the evaluation of progressive shortness of breath and fatigue over the past month. She reports that she cannot climb more than one flight of stairs without experiencing shortness of breath and dizziness. She has hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the past 50 years. She does not drink alcohol. Her medications include enalapril, atorvastatin, and low-dose aspirin. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 70/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 100/80 mm Hg. Physical examination shows weak peripheral pulses. Cardiac examination is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old man presents to his primary care physician with a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort. His discomfort is relieved by voiding. He voids 10–15 times per day and wakes up 2–3 times per night to void. He has not had any involuntary loss of urine. He has tried cutting down on fluids and taking NSAIDs to reduce the discomfort with minimal relief. His past medical history is significant for bipolar disorder. He is sexually active with his wife but reports that intercourse has recently become painful. Current medications include lithium. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 65/min, and blood pressure is 110/80 mm Hg. Examination shows tenderness to palpation of his suprapubic region. Urinalysis shows:
Color clear
pH 6.7
Specific gravity 1.010
Protein 1+
Glucose negative
Ketones negative
Blood negative
Nitrite negative
Leukocyte esterase negative
WBC 0/hpf
Squamous epithelial cells 2/hpf
Bacteria None
A pelvic ultrasound shows a postvoid residual urine is 25 mL. A cystoscopy shows a normal urethra and normal bladder mucosa. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of a 24-hour history of severe lower abdominal pain. He has had two episodes of nonbloody vomiting today and has been unable to keep down food or fluids. He has not had a bowel movement since the day before. He has hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis. He had a cholecystectomy 5 years ago. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the last 20 years. Current medications include chlorthalidone, atorvastatin, and naproxen. His temperature is 38.8°C (101.8­°F), pulse is 102/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 118/78 mm Hg. He is 1.68 m (5 ft 6 in) tall and weighs 94.3 kg (207.9 lbs); BMI is 33.4 kg/m2. Abdominal examination shows a soft abdomen with hypoactive bowel sounds. There is moderate left lower quadrant tenderness. A tender mass is palpable on digital rectal examination. There is no guarding or rebound tenderness. Laboratory studies show:
Leukocyte count 17,000/mm3
Hemoglobin 13.3 g/dl
Hematocrit 40%
Platelet count 188,000/mm3
Serum
Na+ 138 mEq/L
K+ 4.1 mEq/L
Cl- 101 mEq/L
HCO3- 22 mEq/L
Urea Nitrogen 18.1 mg/dl
Creatinine 1.1 mg/dl
Which of the following is most appropriate to confirm the diagnosis?

A 47-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 3-week history of generalized fatigue, mild fever, abdominal pain, and nausea. He attended the state fair over a month ago, where he tried a number of regional foods, and wonders if it might have been caused by something he ate. He has also noticed darkening of his urine, which he attributes to not drinking enough water recently. He has type 2 diabetes mellitus. He drinks 1–2 beers daily. He works as a nursing assistant in a rehabilitation facility. Current medications include glyburide, sitagliptin, and a multivitamin. He appears tired. His temperature is 38.1°C (100.6°F), pulse is 99/min, and blood pressure is 110/74 mm Hg. Examination shows mild scleral icterus. The liver is palpated 2–3 cm below the right costal margin and is tender. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 10.6 g/dL
Leukocyte count 11600/mm3
Platelet count 221,000/mm3
Serum
Urea nitrogen 26 mg/dL
Glucose 122 mg/dL
Creatinine 1.3 mg/dL
Bilirubin 3.6 mg/dL
Total 3.6 mg/dL
Direct 2.4 mg/dL
Alkaline phosphatase 72 U/L
AST 488 U/L
ALT 798 U/L
Hepatitis A IgG antibody (HAV-IgG) positive
Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) positive
Hepatitis B core IgG antibody (anti-HBc) positive
Hepatitis B envelope antigen (HBeAg) positive
Hepatitis C antibody (anti-HCV) negative
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of increasing swelling of her legs and generalized fatigue for 1 month. During this period she has also had a productive cough and shortness of breath. She has been unable to carry out her daily activities. She has a history of recurrent respiratory tract infections and chronic nasal congestion since childhood. She has a 3-month history of foul-smelling and greasy stools. She is at 4th percentile for height and weight. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 112/min, respirations are 23/min, and blood pressure is 104/64 mm Hg. Examination shows clubbing of her fingers and scoliosis. There is 2+ pitting edema of the lower extremities. Jugular venous distention is present. Inspiratory crackles are heard in the thorax. Cardiac examination shows a loud S2. The abdomen is mildly distended and the liver is palpated 2 cm below the right costal margin. Hepato-jugular reflux is present. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 64-year-old man comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. He has had difficulty reading for the past 6 months. He tried using multiple over-the-counter glasses with different strengths, but they have not helped. He has hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Current medications include insulin and enalapril. His temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 80/min, and blood pressure is 126/84 mm Hg. The pupils are round and react sluggishly to light. Visual acuity in the left eye is 6/60 and in the right eye counting fingers at 6 feet. Fundoscopy shows pallor of the optic disc bilaterally. The cup-to-disk ratio is 0.7 in the left eye and 0.9 in the right eye (N = 0.3). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old woman comes to the physician 3 months after noticing skin changes on her scalp. When she scrapes off the crust of the lesion, it reappears after a few days. Occasionally, her scalp itches or she notices a burning sensation. She had a mole removed on her right forearm 5 years ago. She is a retired winemaker. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows multiple rough patches on her scalp. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old woman comes to the physician for a routine health maintenance examination. She feels well. She underwent appendectomy at the age of 25 years. She has a history of hypercholesterolemia that is well controlled with atorvastatin. She is an avid marathon runner and runs 8 miles per day four times a week. Her father died of myocardial infarction at the age of 42 years. The patient does not smoke or drink alcohol. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. Her abdomen is soft and nontender with a surgical scar in the right lower quadrant. Laboratory studies are within normal limits. An ECG is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old woman is brought to the physician by her son because of gradually progressive yellow discoloration of her skin and generalized pruritus for the past 2 weeks. During this period, her appetite has decreased and she has had a 6.3-kg (14-lb) weight loss. She reports that her stool appears pale and her urine is very dark. Three years ago, she had an episode of acute upper abdominal pain that was treated with IV fluids, NSAIDs, and dietary modification. She has stopped drinking alcohol since then; she used to drink 1–2 beers daily for 40 years. She has smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for the past 50 years. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows yellowing of the conjunctivae and skin. The abdomen is soft and nontender; a soft, cystic mass is palpated in the right upper quadrant. Serum studies show:
Bilirubin, total 5.6 mg/dL
Direct 4.8 mg/dL
Alkaline phosphatase 192 U/L
AST 32 U/L
ALT 34 U/L
Abdominal ultrasonography shows an anechoic cystic mass in the subhepatic region and dilation of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 6-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of a 3-day history of progressive rash. The rash started on her face and now involves the entire body. For the past week, she has had a cough and a runny nose. She is visiting from the Philippines with her family. She is in first grade and spends her afternoons at an after-school child care program. Immunization records are not available. Her temperature is 39.5°C (103°F), pulse is 115/min, and blood pressure is 105/66 mm Hg. Examination shows generalized lymphadenopathy. There is an erythematous maculopapular, blanching, and partially confluent exanthem on her entire body. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 43-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of chest pain. He describes the pain as intermittent and burning-like. He states that he has tried using proton pump inhibitors but has had no relief of his symptoms. He has had a 5-kg (11-lb) weight loss over the past 2 months. His temperature is 36.7°C (98.1°F), pulse is 75/min, and blood pressure is 150/80 mm Hg. Examination shows tightness of the skin of the fingers; there are small nonhealing, nonpurulent ulcers over thickened skin on the fingertips. Fine inspiratory crackles are heard at both lung bases. There is mild tenderness to palpation of the epigastrium. Which of the following is most likely associated with his diagnosis?

A 28-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department with shortness of breath and chest pain, 35 minutes after she was involved in a high-speed motor vehicle collision. She was the helmeted driver of a scooter hit by a truck. On arrival, she is alert and oriented with a Glasgow Coma Scale rating of 14. Her temperature is 37.3°C (99.1°F), pulse is 103/min, respirations are 33/min and blood pressure is 132/88 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 94%. Examination shows multiple abrasions over her abdomen and extremities. There is a 2.5-cm (1-in) laceration on the left side of the chest. There are decreased breath sounds over the left base. Cardiac examination shows no abnormalities. The abdomen is soft and there is tenderness to palpation over the left upper quadrant. Bowel sounds are normal. Her hemoglobin concentration is 13.6 g/dL, leukocyte count is 9,110/mm3, and platelet count is 190,000/mm3. A chest x-ray is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 54-year-old woman comes to the physician because of diarrhea that has become progressively worse over the past 4 months. She currently has 4–6 episodes of foul-smelling stools per day. Over the past 3 months, she has had fatigue and a 5-kg (11-lb) weight loss. She returned from Bangladesh 6 months ago after a year-long business assignment. She has osteoarthritis and hypertension. Current medications include amlodipine and naproxen. She appears pale and malnourished. Her temperature is 37.3°C (99.1°F), pulse is 76/min, and blood pressure is 140/86 mm Hg. Examination shows pale conjunctivae and dry mucous membranes. Angular stomatitis and glossitis are present. The abdomen is distended but soft and nontender. Rectal examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 8.9 g/dL
Leukocyte count 4100/mm3
Platelet count 160,000/mm3
Mean corpuscular volume 110 μm3
Serum
Na+ 133 mEq/L
Cl- 98 mEq/l
K+ 3.3 mEq/L
Creatinine 1.1 mg/dL
IgA 250 mg/dL
Anti-tissue transglutaminase, IgA negative
Stool culture and studies for ova and parasites are negative. Test of the stool for occult blood is negative. Fecal fat content is 22 g/day (N < 7). Fecal lactoferrin is negative and elastase is within normal limits. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 68-year-old man is brought to the physician by his wife for the evaluation of confusion and memory deficits for the last month. During this period, he has also had mild weakness in his left leg. He has hypertension and hyperlipidemia. His current medications include enalapril and atorvastatin. He has smoked two packs of cigarettes daily for the last 45 years. He drinks a glass of wine every day. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 75/min, and blood pressure is 135/85 mm Hg. He is oriented only to person. He recalls 2 out of 3 objects immediately and none after 5 minutes. The patient is unable to lift his eyebrows or to smile. Muscle strength is decreased in the left lower extremity. A T2-weighted MRI scan of the head shows several hyperintense round lesions in the frontal and temporal lobe at the border of the gray and white matter. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 9-year-old girl is brought to the physician for a well-child examination. Her mother says her teachers report her being easily distracted, lagging behind her classmates in most of the subjects, and frequently falling asleep during class. She says that her daughter has complained of leg pain on multiple occasions. She is at the 45th percentile for height and 35th percentile for weight. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows ptosis and a high-arched palate. Muscle strength is decreased in the face and hands. Muscle strength of the quadriceps and hamstrings is normal. Sensation is intact. Percussion of the thenar eminence causes the thumb to abduct and then relax slowly. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department 15 minutes after falling 7 feet onto a flat-top wooden post. On arrival, she is in severe pain and breathing rapidly. Her pulse is 135/min, respirations are 30/min, and blood pressure is 80/40 mm Hg. There is an impact wound in the left fourth intercostal space at the midaxillary line. Auscultation shows tracheal deviation to the right and absent breath sounds over the left lung. There is dullness to percussion over the left chest. Neck veins are flat. Cardiac examination shows no abnormalities. Two large-bore intravenous catheters are placed and intravenous fluid resuscitation is begun. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of chest pain, dry cough, and shortness of breath. She describes two painless masses in her neck, which she says appeared 4 months ago and are progressively increasing in size. During this time, she has had week-long episodes of fever interspersed with 10-day periods of being afebrile. She reports that her clothes have become looser over the past few months. She drinks alcohol occasionally. Her temperature is 38°C (100.4°F), pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 105/60 mm Hg. Physical examination shows two nontender, fixed cervical lymph nodes on either side of the neck, which are approximately 2.2 cm and 4.5 cm in size. The tip of the spleen is palpated 3 cm below the left costal margin. An x-ray of the chest shows discrete widening of the superior mediastinum. Which of the following is most appropriate to confirm the diagnosis?

A 45-year-old woman comes to the physician for a routine health maintenance examination. She feels well. She has type 2 diabetes mellitus. There is no family history of serious illness. She works as an engineer at a local company. She does not smoke. She drinks one glass of red wine every other day. She does not use illicit drugs. Her only medication is metformin. She is 180 cm (5 ft 11 in) tall and weighs 100 kg (220 lb); BMI is 31 kg/m2. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows a soft, nontender abdomen. The liver is palpated 2 to 3 cm below the right costal margin. Laboratory studies show an aspartate aminotransferase concentration of 100 U/L and an alanine aminotransferase concentration of 130 U/L. Liver biopsy shows hepatocyte ballooning degeneration, as well as inflammatory infiltrates with scattered lymphocytes, neutrophils, and Kupffer cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of a 3-week history of generalized fatigue and easy bruising. During the past week, he has also had fever and severe leg pain that wakes him up at night. His temperature is 38.3°C (100.9°F), pulse is 120/min, and respirations are 30/min. Examination shows cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy. The abdomen is soft and nontender; the liver is palpated 3 cm below the right costal margin, and the spleen is palpated 2 cm below the left costal margin. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL
Leukocyte count 63,000/mm3
Platelet count 27,000/mm3
A bone marrow aspirate predominantly shows immature cells that stain positive for CD10, CD19, and TdT. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 36-year-old man with HIV comes to the physician because of a 3-day history of pain and watery discharge in his left eye. He also has blurry vision and noticed that he is more sensitive to light. His right eye is asymptomatic. He had an episode of shingles 7 years ago. He was diagnosed with HIV 5 years ago. He admits that he takes his medication inconsistently. He wears contact lenses. Current medications include abacavir, lamivudine, efavirenz, and a nutritional supplement. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 89/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. Examination shows conjunctival injection of the left eye. Visual acuity is 20/20 in the right eye and 20/80 in the left eye. Extraocular movements are normal. His CD4+ T-lymphocyte count is 90/mm3. A photograph of the left eye after fluorescein administration is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department with fatigue, dry cough, and shortness of breath for 3 days. She reports a slight fever and has also had 3 episodes of watery diarrhea earlier that morning. Last week, she attended a business meeting at a hotel and notes some of her coworkers have also become sick. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She takes atorvastatin, hydrochlorothiazide, and lisinopril. She appears in mild distress. Her temperature is 102.1°F (38.9°C), pulse is 56/min, respirations are 16/min, and blood pressure is 150/85 mm Hg. Diffuse crackles are heard in the thorax. Examination shows a soft and nontender abdomen. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 13.5 g/dL
Leukocyte count 15,000/mm3
Platelet count 130,000/mm3
Serum
Na+ 129 mEq/L
Cl- 100 mEq/L
K+ 4.6 mEq/L
HCO3- 22 mEq/L
Urea nitrogen 14 mg/dL
Creatinine 1.3 mg/dL
An x-ray of the chest shows infiltrates in both lungs. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 5-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of early morning headaches for the past 6 months. During this period, she has had severe nausea and occasional episodes of vomiting. For the past month, she has had difficulty walking and intermittent double vision. She was born at term and has been healthy apart from an episode of sinusitis 8 months ago that resolved spontaneously. She is at the 60th percentile for height and 50th percentile for weight. Her temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 80/min, and blood pressure is 105/64 mm Hg. Examination shows normal muscle strength and 2+ deep tendon reflexes bilaterally. She has a broad-based gait and impaired tandem gait. Fundoscopy shows bilateral swelling of the optic disc. There is esotropia of the left eye. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 1-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of fever and crying while passing urine for 2 days. He was born at term and has been healthy since. Three months ago, he was treated for a urinary tract infection with oral cefixime. His temperature is 39°C (102.2°F), pulse is 144/min, and blood pressure is 85/40 mm Hg. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. His leukocyte count is 14,000/mm3. Urine dipstick shows leukocyte esterase and nitrites; urinalysis shows WBCs and gram-negative rods. Urine culture results are pending. Renal ultrasonography shows hydronephrosis of the left kidney. Empirical antimicrobial therapy is initiated, following which the patient's symptoms improve. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 53-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of intermittent severe left neck, shoulder, and arm pain and paresthesias of the left hand. The pain radiates to the radial aspect of his left forearm, thumb, and index finger. He first noticed his symptoms after helping a friend set up a canopy tent. There is no family history of serious illness. He appears healthy. Vital signs are within normal limits. When the patient extends and rotates his head to the left and downward pressure is applied, he reports paresthesias along the radial aspect of his left forearm and thumb. There is weakness when extending the left wrist against resistance. The brachioradialis reflex is 1+ on the left and 2+ on the right. The radial pulse is palpable bilaterally. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old man is brought to the physician by his wife because of a 1-year history of abnormal behavior. During this time he has been irritable, restless, and has had multiple episodes of hearing voices. Over the past month, he has also had difficulty swallowing. He has a 2-year history of depression. He was let go by his employer 6 months ago because he could no longer handle all his tasks and often forgot about assignments. His father committed suicide at the age of 50. The patient has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily over the past 20 years. He has a history of smoking cocaine for 8 years but stopped 1 year ago. Vital signs are within normal limits. On mental status examination, he is confused and oriented to person and place only. Neurologic examination shows a delayed return to neutral ankle position after triggering the plantar reflex. Physical examination shows irregular, nonrepetitive, and arrhythmic movements of the neck and head. The patient has poor articulation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 36-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 12-month history of upper abdominal pain. The pain is worse after eating, which he reports as 7 out of 10 in intensity. Over the last year, he has also had nausea, heartburn, and multiple episodes of diarrhea with no blood or mucus. Eight months ago, he underwent an upper endoscopy, which showed several ulcers in the gastric antrum, the pylorus, and the duodenum, as well as thick gastric folds. The biopsies from these ulcers were negative for H. pylori. Current medications include pantoprazole and over-the-counter antacids. He appears anxious. Vital signs are within normal limits. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. The abdomen is soft and there is tenderness to palpation in the epigastric and umbilical areas. Test of the stool for occult blood is positive. A repeat upper endoscopy shows persistent gastric and duodenal ulceration with minimal bleeding. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 24-year-old man comes to the physician because of progressively worsening joint pain. He has had diffuse, aching pain in his knees, shoulders, and hands bilaterally for the past few months, but the pain has become much more severe in the past few weeks. He also reports night sweats and generalized malaise. On physical examination, radial and pedal pulses are weak. There are erythematous nodules over the legs that measure 3–5 cm. Laboratory studies show:
Hematocrit 33.2%
Hemoglobin 10.7 g/dL
Leukocyte count 11,300/mm3
Platelet count 615,000/mm3
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 94 mm/h
Serum
C-reactive protein 40 mg/dL (N=0.08–3.1)
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 1-day history of progressive pain and blurry vision of her right eye. She has difficulties opening the eye because of pain. Her left eye is asymptomatic. She wears contact lenses. She has bronchial asthma treated with inhaled salbutamol. She works as a kindergarten teacher. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 85/min, and blood pressure is 135/75 mm Hg. Examination shows a visual acuity in the left eye of 20/25 and the ability to count fingers at 3 feet in the right eye. A photograph of the right eye is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 56-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by his wife because of slurred speech and left facial droop for the past 30 minutes. During this period, he has also had numbness on the left side of his face. He has never had such an episode before. He has hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. His father died of lung cancer 1 week ago. The patient has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 30 years. He drinks one glass of wine daily. His current medications include metformin, sitagliptin, enalapril, and atorvastatin. He is 168 cm (5 ft 6 in) tall and weighs 86 kg (190 lb); BMI is 30.5 kg/m2. He is oriented to time, place, and person. His temperature is 37°C (98.7°F), pulse is 97/min, and blood pressure is 140/90 mm Hg. Examination shows drooping of the left side of the face. His speech is clear. Examination shows full muscle strength. Deep tendon reflexes are 2+ bilaterally. A finger-nose test and his gait are normal. Cardiopulmonary examination shows a right-sided carotid bruit. A complete blood count and serum concentrations of creatinine, glucose, and electrolytes are within the reference ranges. An ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy. A noncontrast CT scan of the brain shows no abnormalities. On the way back from the CT scan, his presenting symptoms resolve. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old woman is brought to the physician by her husband for forgetfulness, confusion, and mood changes for the past 4 months. Her symptoms started with misplacing items such as her wallet and keys around the house. Two months ago, she became unable to manage their finances as it became too difficult for her. Last week, she became lost while returning home from the grocery store. Her husband reports that she shows “no emotion” and that she is seemingly not concerned by her recent symptoms. She has hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and coronary artery disease. Current medications include aspirin, metoprolol, lisinopril, metformin, and rosuvastatin. Her pulse is 56/min and blood pressure is 158/76 mm Hg. Neurologic examination shows loss of sensation on her right leg and an unsteady gait. When asked to stand with her eyes closed and palms facing upward, her right arm rotates inward. An MRI of the brain shows multiple deep white matter lesions. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 9-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his father because of a 3-day history of face and foot swelling, dark urine, and a rash on his hands and feet. The father reports that his son has had a low-grade fever, shortness of breath, and a dry cough for the past 8 days. He has had generalized weakness and pain in his right knee and ankle. He has a ventricular septum defect that was diagnosed at birth. The patient appears lethargic. His temperature is 38.4 (101.1°F), pulse is 130/min, respirations are 34/min, and blood pressure is 110/60 mm Hg. Examination shows small, non-blanching, purple lesions on his palms, soles, and under his fingernails. There is edema of the eyelids and feet. Funduscopic examination shows retinal hemorrhages. Holosystolic and early diastolic murmurs are heard. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 11.3 g/dL
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 61 mm/h
Leukocyte count 15,000/mm3
Platelet count 326,000/mm3
Urine
Blood 4+
Glucose negative
Protein 1+
Ketones negative
Transthoracic echocardiography shows a small outlet ventricular septum defect and a mild right ventricular enlargement. There are no wall motion abnormalities, valvular heart disease, or deficits in the pump function of the heart. Blood cultures grow Streptococcus pyogenes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 58-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 2-year history of progressively worsening pain in his knees and fingers. The knee pain is worse when he walks for longer than 30 minutes. When he wakes up in the morning, his fingers and knees are stiff for about 15 minutes. He cannot recall any trauma to the joints. He was treated with amoxicillin following a tick bite 2 years ago. He is otherwise healthy and only takes a multivitamin and occasionally acetaminophen for the pain. He drinks 1–2 glasses of wine daily. He is 160 cm (5 ft 3 in) tall and weighs 79 kg (174 lb); BMI is 31 kg/m2. His temperature is 36.9°C (98.4°F), pulse is 70/min, and blood pressure is 133/78 mm Hg. Examination of the lower extremities reveals mild genu varum. Range of motion of both knees is limited; there is palpable crepitus. Complete flexion and extension elicit pain. Tender nodules are present on the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints of the index, ring, and little fingers bilaterally. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 49-year-old woman comes to the physician because of tender, red nodules that appeared on her chest 3 days ago. Three weeks ago, she had similar symptoms in her right lower limb and another episode in her left foot; both episodes resolved spontaneously. She also has diarrhea and has had a poor appetite for 1 month. She has a history of dry cough and joint pain, for which she takes albuterol and aspirin as needed. She has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes daily for 15 years. She does not drink alcohol. Physical examination shows a linear, erythematous lesion on the right anterior chest wall, through which a cord-like structure can be palpated. The lungs are clear to auscultation. The abdomen is soft, nontender, and non-distended. Examination of the legs is normal. An ultrasound of the legs shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis of the underlying condition?

A 35-year-old man comes to the physician for the evaluation of increasing weakness and numbness of the upper extremities for 5 days. During the past 2 days, he has had urinary incontinence not related to sneezing or laughing. Last summer, he had weakness and numbness of his right lower extremity that was worse when he was outside; he regained his strength 3 weeks later. He has no history of serious illness. He has had 10 female sexual partners in his lifetime and uses condoms inconsistently. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows an impaired tandem gait. There is mild spasticity and muscle strength is decreased in both upper extremities. Deep tendon reflexes are 4+ bilaterally. The abdominal reflex is absent. Muscle strength in the right lower extremity is mildly decreased. Sensation to vibration and fine touch is decreased over the upper extremities. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 4-year-old girl is brought to the physician in December for episodic shortness of breath and a nonproductive cough for 3 months. These episodes frequently occur before sleeping, and she occasionally wakes up because of difficulty breathing. Her father also reports that she became short of breath while playing with her friends at daycare on several occasions. She is allergic to peanuts. She is at the 55th percentile for height and weight. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows mild scattered wheezing in the thorax. An x-ray of the chest shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old man comes to the physician because of increasing shortness of breath and a non-productive cough for 2 months. He has been unable to perform his daily activities. He has had malaise and bilateral ankle pain during this period. He noticed his symptoms after returning from a vacation to Arizona. He is a research assistant at the university geology laboratory. He is originally from Nigeria and visits his family there twice a year; his last trip was 3 months ago. His temperature is 37.8°C (100°F), pulse is 100/min, respirations are 24/min, and blood pressure is 112/72 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 94%. There is no palpable cervical or axillary lymphadenopathy. The lungs are clear to auscultation. His left eye is notable for ciliary injection and photophobia. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. A complete blood count is within the reference range. An x-ray of the chest is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old girl is brought to the physician for the evaluation of recurrent skin lesions. The episodes of lesions started at the age of 2 months and multiple treatment options have been attempted without success. She has also had several episodes of respiratory tract infections, enlarged lymph nodes, and recurrent fevers since birth. The girl attends daycare. Her older brother has asthma. The patient's immunizations are up-to-date. She is at the 5th percentile for length and 10th percentile for weight. She appears ill. Her temperature is 38°C (100.4°F), pulse is 100/min, and blood pressure is 100/60 mm Hg. Examination shows several raised, erythematous lesions of different sizes over the face, neck, groins, and extremities; some secrete pus. Cervical and axillary lymph nodes are enlarged bilaterally. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 46-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department 15 minutes after being involved in a motor vehicle collision where she was the unrestrained driver. On arrival, she is unconscious. Her respirations are 24/min, and palpable systolic blood pressure is 60 mm Hg, and pulse is 141/min and irregularly irregular. Examination shows multiple ecchymoses over the chest. There is a 3-cm (1.2-in) laceration over the abdomen and a 4-cm (1.6-in) laceration over the scalp. Jugular venous pressure is increased. Bilateral crackles are heard at the lung bases. Cardiac examination shows no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. The abdomen is soft. Two large bore intravenous catheters are inserted and 0.9% saline infusion is begun. Focused assessment with sonography in trauma (FAST) is negative. An electrocardiogram shows absent p-waves. After 5 minutes, her pulse is 160/min and palpable systolic blood pressure is 50 mm Hg. Vasopressors are administered. One hour later, the patient dies. Which of the following was the most likely diagnosis?

A 52-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department with severe epigastric discomfort and left-sided chest pain radiating to the back that began after waking up. She has also vomited several times since the pain began. She underwent an esophagogastroduodenoscopy the previous day for evaluation of epigastric pain. She has ischemic heart disease and underwent a coronary angioplasty 3 years ago. Her mother died of pancreatic cancer when she was 60 years old. Her current medications include aspirin, clopidogrel, metoprolol, ramipril, and rosuvastatin. She is pale, anxious, and diaphoretic. Her temperature is 37.9°C (100.2°F), pulse is 140/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 100/60 mm Hg in her upper extremities and 108/68 mm Hg in her lower extremities. Pulse oximetry on room air shows oxygen saturation at 98%. An S4 is audible over the precordium, in addition to crepitus over the chest. Abdominal examination shows tenderness to palpation in the epigastric area. Serum studies show an initial Troponin I level of 0.031 ng/mL (N < 0.1 ng/mL) and 0.026 ng/mL 6 hours later. A 12-lead ECG shows sinus tachycardia with nonspecific ST-T changes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 9-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his mother because of multiple episodes of staring and facial grimacing that have occurred over the past 3 weeks. There are no precipitating factors for these episodes and they last for several minutes. He does not respond to his family members during these episodes. One week ago, his sister witnessed an episode in which he woke up while sleeping, stared, and made hand gestures. He does not remember any of these episodes but does recall having a vague muddy taste in his mouth prior to the onset of these symptoms. After the episode, he feels lethargic and is confused. Physical and neurologic examinations show no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old man comes to the physician because of stiffness and pain in multiple joints. He says that the fingers on both of his hands have become increasingly stiff and difficult to move over the past 8 months. He also complains of nails that break easily and look spotty as well as chronic back pain. He had a urinary tract infection a year ago that was treated with antibiotics. He is sexually active with 2 female partners and uses condoms inconsistently. His vitals are within normal limits. A photograph of his right hand is shown. There are multiple, well-demarcated red plaques with silvery-white scales over the shins and back. Serum studies show a negative rheumatoid factor and ANA. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25 year-old man is brought to the emergency department by his girlfriend after he cut his forearms with a knife. He has had multiple visits to the emergency department in the past few months for self-inflicted wounds. He claims that his girlfriend is the worst person in the world. He and his girlfriend have broken up 20 times in the past 6 months. He says he cut himself not because he wants to kill himself; he feels alone and empty and wants his girlfriend to take care of him. His girlfriend claims that he is prone to outbursts of physical aggression as well as mood swings. She says that these mood swings last a few hours and vary from states of exuberance and self-confidence to states of self-doubt and melancholy. On examination, the patient appears well-dressed and calm. He has normal speech, thought processes, and thought content. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An otherwise healthy 52-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of palpitations. She says that she can feel her heart beat in her chest all the time. For the past 3 weeks, she has shortness of breath on exertion. She has not had chest pain, orthopnea, or nocturnal dyspnea. She emigrated from Nepal at the age of 25 years. She does not take any medications. Her temperature is 36.5°C (97.7°F), pulse is 103/min, and blood pressure is 138/56 mm Hg. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Cardiac examination is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of a 4-week history of generalized fatigue and malaise. She was born at term and has been healthy since. Her father has a history of recurrent anemia. She appears pale. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F) and pulse is 97/min. Examination shows pale conjunctivae and jaundice. The abdomen is soft and nontender; the spleen is palpated 3–4 cm below the left costal margin. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 9.3 g/dL
Mean corpuscular volume 81.3 μm3
Mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration 39% Hb/cell
Leukocyte count 7300/mm3
Platelet count 200,000/mm3
Red cell distribution width 19% (N = 13–15)
Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 23-year-old man comes to the physician because of increasing pain and swelling of his hands and wrists for 3 days. He has been unable to continue his daily activities like writing or driving. He has had a nonpruritic generalized rash for 4 days. He had fever and a runny nose one week ago which resolved with over-the-counter medication. He is sexually active with a female partner and uses condoms inconsistently. He works as an attendant at an amusement park. His temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 118/72 mm Hg. Examination shows swelling and tenderness of the wrists as well as the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints. Range of motion at the wrists is limited. A lacy macular rash is noted over the trunk and extremities. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies, including erythrocyte sedimentation rate and anti-nuclear antibody and anti-dsDNA serology, show no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 58-year-old woman comes to the physician because of burning pain in her neck and arms for a year. She has also had paresthesias in her hands during this period. She has had increasing weakness in both hands during the past 3 months. She has type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. She was involved in a motor vehicle collision 3 years ago. Current medications include metformin, sitagliptin, enalapril, atorvastatin, and aspirin. She has had 7 sexual partners in her lifetime; she uses condoms inconsistently. She is oriented to time, place, and person. Vital signs are within normal limits. The pupils are equal and reactive to light. Examination of the upper extremities shows decreased muscle strength, absent reflexes, and decreased hand grip with fasciculations bilaterally. Sensation to temperature and pain is absent over the chest and bilateral upper arms. Vibration and joint position sensations are present in the upper limbs. Cranial nerve examination shows no focal findings. Examination of the lower extremities show no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 66-year-old white woman comes to the physician because of a 10-day history of fatigue and lower leg swelling. Over the past 6 months, she has had a 3.6-kg (8-lb) weight loss. She has chronic bronchitis and uses an albuterol inhaler as needed. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 44 years and drinks one alcoholic beverage daily. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 88/min, and blood pressure is 120/75 mm Hg. She appears thin. Examination shows 2+ pretibial edema bilaterally. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL
Leukocyte count 8500/mm3
Platelet count 130,000/mm3
Serum
Urea nitrogen 23 mg/dL
Glucose 77 mg/dL
Creatinine 1.6 mg/dL
Albumin 1.8 mg/dL
Total cholesterol 475 mg/dL
Urine
Blood negative
Glucose negative
Protein 4+
WBC 0–1/hpf
Fatty casts numerous
An x-ray of the chest shows a right upper lobe density. A CT scan of the chest shows a 2.5 x 3.5 x 2-cm right upper lobe mass. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 50-year-old woman comes to the emergency department because of severe lower chest pain for the past hour. The pain radiates to the back and is associated with nausea. She has had two episodes of non-bloody vomiting since the pain started. She has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 30 years. She drinks five to six beers per day. Her medications include enalapril and metformin. Her temperature is 38.5°C (101.3°F), pulse is 110/min, and blood pressure is 90/60 mm Hg. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Examination shows a distended abdomen with epigastric tenderness and guarding but no rebound; bowel sounds are decreased. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 14.5 g/dL
Leukocyte count 5,100/mm3
Platelet count 280,000/mm3
Serum
Na+ 133 mEq/L
K+ 3.5 mEq/L
Cl- 98 mEq/L
Total bilirubin 1.0 mg/dL
Amylase 160 U/L
Lipase 880 U/L (N = 14–280)
An ECG shows sinus tachycardia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 11-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after she was found screaming and clutching her head. She has had nausea and occasional episodes of vomiting for 1 week, fever and left-sided headaches for 2 weeks, and increasing tooth pain over the past 3 weeks. She has no history of ear or sinus infections. She is in moderate distress. Her temperature is 38.7°C (101.7°F), pulse is 170/min, respirations are 19/min, and blood pressure is 122/85 mmHg. She is confused and only oriented to person. The pupils react sluggishly to light. Fundoscopic examination shows papilledema bilaterally. Extraocular movements are normal. Flexion of the neck causes hip flexion. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of a recurrent pruritic rash on her face and scalp. She reports that she has been using a new shaving cream once a week for the past 5 months. A year ago, she was diagnosed with HIV and is currently receiving triple antiretroviral therapy. She drinks several six-packs of beer weekly. Vital signs are within normal limits. A photograph of the rash is shown. A similar rash is seen near the hairline of the scalp and greasy yellow scales are seen at the margins of the eyelids. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 10-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department 15 minutes after she had a seizure. Her mother reports that she complained of sudden nausea and seeing “shiny lights,” after which the corner of her mouth and then her face began twitching. Next, she let out a loud scream, dropped to the floor unconscious, and began to jerk her arms and legs as well for about two minutes. On the way to the hospital, the girl regained consciousness, but was confused and could not speak clearly for about five minutes. She had a fever and sore throat one week ago which improved after treatment with acetaminophen. She appears lethargic and cannot recall what happened during the episode. Her vital signs are within normal limits. She is oriented to time, place, and person. Deep tendon reflexes are 2+ bilaterally. There is muscular pain at attempts to elicit deep tendon reflexes. Physical and neurologic examinations show no other abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her parents because of concerns about her behavior during the past year. Her parents report that she often fails to answer when they call her and has regular unprovoked episodes of crying and screaming. At kindergarten, she can follow and participate in group activities, but does not follow her teacher's instructions when these are given to her directly. She is otherwise cheerful and maintains eye contact when spoken to but does not respond when engaged in play. She gets along well with friends and family. She started walking at the age of 11 months and can speak in two-to-three-word phrases. She often mispronounces words. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old man comes to the physician because of increased urinary frequency over the past month. He also reports having dry mouth and feeling thirsty all the time despite drinking several liters of water per day. He has not had any weight changes and his appetite is normal. He has a history of obsessive compulsive disorder treated with citalopram. He drinks 1–2 cans of beer per day. His vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show:
Serum
Na+ 130 mEq/L
Glucose 110 mg/dL
Osmolality 265 mOsmol/kg
Urine
Osmolality 230 mOsmol/kg
The patient is asked to stop drinking water for 3 hours. Following water restriction, urine osmolality is measured every hour, whereas serum osmolality is measured every 2 hours. Repeated laboratory measurements show a serum osmolality of 280 mOsmol/kg and a urine osmolality of 650 mOsmol/kg. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-month-old boy is brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of progressive difficulty breathing and a dry cough. Five weeks ago, he was diagnosed with diffuse hemangiomas involving the intrathoracic cavity and started treatment with prednisolone. He appears uncomfortable and in moderate respiratory distress. His temperature is 38°C (100.4°F), pulse is 150/min, respirations are 50/min, and blood pressure is 88/50 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 87%. Oral examination shows a white plaque covering the tongue that bleeds when scraped. Chest examination shows subcostal and intercostal retractions. Scattered fine crackles and rhonchi are heard throughout both lung fields. Laboratory studies show a leukocyte count of 21,000/mm3 and an increased serum beta-D-glucan concentration. An x-ray of the chest shows symmetrical, diffuse interstitial infiltrates. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 3-week-old newborn is brought to the physician by her parents because of poor feeding, irritability, and frequent vomiting over the past week. The vomitus is greenish in color and smells strange. Her parents have tried to feed her every 4 hours, but the patient often spits up or refuses to eat. The patient was born at term and had her first bowel movement at 50 hours of life. She has since had one bowel movement daily. She is at the 50th percentile for length, 10th percentile for weight, and 40th percentile for head circumference. She does not appear to be in acute distress. Her temperature is 36.9°C (98.4°F), pulse is 140/min, respirations are 40/min, and blood pressure is 90/60 mm Hg. Physical examination shows that the patient has small, low-set ears, a broad and flat nasal bridge, and a large space between the first and second toes bilaterally. The abdomen is distended. When the finger is removed following a rectal exam, there is an explosive release of stool from the patient's rectum. An x-ray of the abdomen shows a section of dilated colon followed by a segment of colon without stool or air. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 59-year-old man comes to the emergency department 25 minutes after the onset of severe left periorbital pain and blurred vision in the same eye. The pain began soon after he entered a theater to watch a movie. He has a headache and vomited twice on the way to the hospital. Two weeks ago, he had acute sinusitis that resolved spontaneously. He has atrial fibrillation and hypertension. Current medications include metoprolol and warfarin. His temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 101/min, and blood pressure is 140/80 mm Hg. Visual acuity is counting fingers at 3 feet in the left eye and 20/20 in the right eye. The left eye shows conjunctival injection and edematous cornea. The left pupil is mid-dilated and irregular; it is not reactive to light. Extraocular movements are normal. Fundoscopic examination is inconclusive because of severe corneal edema. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 9-month-old infant is brought to the physician because of a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash began on his trunk and spread to his extremities. Five days ago, he was taken to the emergency department for fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. He was born at term and has no history of serious illness. His immunizations are up-to-date. Current medications include acetaminophen. His temperature is 37.2°C (99.0°F) and pulse is 120/min. Examination shows a maculopapular rash that blanches on pressure. A photograph of the rash is shown. Posterior auricular lymphadenopathy is present. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her parents because of 2 episodes of screaming in the night over the past week. The parents report that their daughter woke up suddenly screaming, crying, and aggressively kicking her legs around both times. The episodes lasted several minutes and were accompanied by sweating and fast breathing. The parents state that they were unable to stop the episodes and that their daughter simply went back to sleep when the episodes were over. The patient cannot recall any details of these incidents. She has a history of obstructive sleep apnea. She takes no medications. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 29-year-old African-American female comes to the physician with a 2-week history of progressive fatigue and shortness of breath on exertion. Last week she noticed that her eyes were gradually turning yellow and her urine was dark. She has a family history of type II diabetes. She denies changes in urinary frequency, dysuria, or nocturia. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6° F), blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, and heart rate is 80/min. Examination shows pale conjunctivae, splenomegaly, and jaundice. There is no lymphadenopathy. Laboratory studies show:
Hematocrit 19.5%
Hemoglobin 6.5 g/dL
WBC count 11,000/mm3
Platelet count 300,000/mm3
Reticulocyte count 8%
Serum
Total bilirubin 6 mg/dL
Direct bilirubin 1.0 mg/dL
Urea nitrogen 9 mg/dL
Creatinine 1 mg/dL
Lactate dehydrogenase 365 U/L
Peripheral blood smear shows gross polychromasia with nucleated red blood cells and spherocytes. Direct Coombs' test is positive. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old woman comes to the physician because of painless swelling in her left foot for 4 months. The swelling was initially accompanied by redness, which has since resolved. She has not had fever or chills. She has a history of coronary artery disease, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has had 3 sexual partners over the past year and uses condoms inconsistently. Her mother had rheumatoid arthritis. Current medications include clopidogrel, aspirin, metoprolol, losartan, atorvastatin, and insulin. She is 180 cm (5 ft 11 in) tall and weighs 95 kg (209 lb); BMI is 29 kg/m2. Vital signs are within normal limits. Cardiovascular examination shows no abnormalities. Examination of the feet shows swelling of the left ankle with collapse of the midfoot arch and prominent malleoli. There is no redness or warmth. There is a small, dry ulcer on the left plantar surface of the 2nd metatarsal. Monofilament testing shows decreased sensation along both feet up to the shins bilaterally. Her gait is normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her father because of increasingly withdrawn behavior for the last two years. Her father reports that in the last 2–3 years of high school, his daughter has spent most of her time in her room playing video games. She does not have any friends and has never had a boyfriend. She usually refuses to attend family dinner and avoids contact with her siblings. The patient states that she prefers being on her own. When asked how much playing video games means to her, she replies that “it's okay.” When her father starts crying during the visit, she appears indifferent. Physical and neurologic examinations show no other abnormalities. On mental status examination, her thought process is organized and logical. Her affect is flattened. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 71-year-old woman comes to the physician for a health maintenance examination. Aside from occasional lower back pain in the last couple of years, she feels well. She had a right-sided myocardial infarction 4 years ago. Currently, she has no shortness of breath and has no anginal symptoms. She has a 30 pack-year history of smoking but stopped smoking 10 years ago and does not drink alcohol. Her pulse is 59/min, and her blood pressure is 135/75 mm Hg. Physical examination reveals 1+ lower extremity edema. Cardiac and pulmonary auscultation show no abnormalities. There is no lymphadenopathy. Her laboratory studies show a hemoglobin of 13.2 g/dL and serum protein of 10.1 g/dL. ECG shows known Q wave abnormalities unchanged since the last ECG one year ago. A serum protein electrophoresis with immunofixation is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to establish the diagnosis?

A 16-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of yellowish discoloration of his eyes and generalized fatigue since he returned from a 2-week class trip to Guatemala 2 days ago. During his time there, he had watery diarrhea, nausea, and lack of appetite for 3 days that resolved without treatment. He also took primaquine for malaria prophylaxis. Three weeks ago, he had a urinary tract infection that was treated with nitrofurantoin. His immunizations are up-to-date. His temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 82/min and blood pressure is 110/74 mm Hg. Examination shows scleral icterus. There is no lymphadenopathy. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL
Leukocyte count 6400/mm3
Platelet count 234,000/mm3
Reticulocyte count 1.1%
Prothrombin time 12 sec (INR=1)
Serum
Bilirubin
Total 2.8 mg/dL
Direct 0.2 mg/dL
Alkaline phosphatase 43 U/L
AST 16 U/L
ALT 17 U/L
γ-Glutamyltransferase 38 U/L (N = 5–50)
Anti-HAV IgG positive
Anti-HBs positive
A peripheral blood smear shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 63-year-old woman comes to the physician for the evaluation of a skin lesion on her chest. She first noticed the lesion 2 months ago and thinks that it has increased in size since then. The lesion is not painful or pruritic. She has type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and glaucoma. The patient has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the last 40 years and drinks two to three beers on the weekend. Current medications include metformin, atorvastatin, topical timolol, and a multivitamin. Vital signs are within normal limits. The lesion is partly elevated on palpation and does not change its form on pinching. A photograph of the lesion is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 37-year-old woman comes to the emergency department with her husband because of a 3-day history of severe pain in her right arm. She also reports that she cannot move her right arm. The symptoms began after the patient woke up one morning, having slept on her side. She is otherwise healthy. She works as a waitress and says that she feels exhausted from working several night shifts per week. She adds that she “can barely keep her eyes open” when looking after their daughter the next day.
