Since the onset of the pain, she has been unable to work and is fully dependent on her husband, who took an extra shift to make enough money to pay their monthly bills. The patient appears relaxed but only allows herself to be examined after her husband convinces her. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows 1/5 muscle strength in the right arm. Reflexes are normal. She has no sensation to light touch over the entire right arm and forearm. When a pin prick test is conducted, the patient rapidly withdraws the right arm. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old man comes to the emergency department with his girlfriend 2 hours after an episode of loss of consciousness. He was seated and was being tattooed on his right upper flank when he became diaphoretic, pale, and passed out. According to his girlfriend, the patient slipped to the floor and his arms and legs moved in a jerky fashion for a few seconds. He regained consciousness within half a minute and was alert and fully oriented immediately. He has no history of serious illness. He works as an event manager and has had more stress than usual due to a recent concert tour. He appears well. His temperature is 37°C (98.4°F), pulse is 68/min, respirations are 16/min, and blood pressure is 120/72 mm Hg. His cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. Neurologic examination shows no focal findings. An ECG shows an incomplete right bundle branch block. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 50-year-old woman comes to the emergency department for evaluation of right-sided facial weakness that she noticed after waking up. One month ago, she also experienced right-sided neck pain and headache that began after returning from a hunting trip to New Hampshire the week before. She took ibuprofen to relieve symptoms, which subsided a week later. She has a 5-year history of hypertension controlled with drug therapy. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 35 years and she drinks two beers daily. Her vital signs are within the normal range. Physical examination shows right-sided drooping of the upper and lower half of the face. The patient has difficulties smiling and she is unable to close her right eye. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

An 18-month-old girl is brought to the physician by her parents for the evaluation of passing large amounts of dark red blood from her rectum for 2 days. Her parents noticed that she has also had several episodes of dark stools over the past 3 weeks. The parents report that their child has been sleeping more and has been more pale than usual over the past 24 hours. The girl's appetite has been normal and she has not vomited. She is at the 50th percentile for height and 50th percentile for weight. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 135/min, respirations are 38/min, and blood pressure is 90/50 mm Hg. Examination shows pale conjunctivae. The abdomen is soft and nontender. There is a small amount of dark red blood in the diaper. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 9.5 g/dL
Hematocrit 30%
Mean corpuscular volume 68 μm3
Leukocyte count 7,200/mm3
Platelet count 300,000/mm3
Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 42-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 12 month history of progressive fatigue and shortness of breath with exertion. Five years ago, he emigrated from Eastern Europe. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 20 years. He has a history of using methamphetamines and cocaine but quit 5 years ago. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows jugular venous pulsations 9 cm above the sternal angle. The lungs are clear to auscultation. There is a normal S1 and a loud, split S2. An impulse can be felt with the fingers left of the sternum. The abdomen is soft and nontender. The fingertips are enlarged and the nails are curved. There is pitting edema around the ankles bilaterally. An x-ray of the chest shows pronounced central pulmonary arteries and a prominent right heart border. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 5-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of a 10-day history of intermittent fevers and painful swelling of the right ankle. She has not had trauma to the ankle. She has a history of sickle cell disease and had an episode of dactylitis of her left index finger 3 years ago. Current medications include hydroxyurea and acetaminophen as needed for the ankle pain. Her temperature is 38°C (100.4°F), blood pressure is 125/68 mm Hg, pulse is 105/min, and respirations are 14/min. Examination shows a tender, swollen, and erythematous right ankle with point tenderness over the medial malleolus. X-ray of the right ankle demonstrates marked periosteal thickening and elevation, as well as a central sclerotic lesion with a lucent rim over the right lateral malleolus. A bone biopsy culture confirms the diagnosis. Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?

A previously healthy 60-year-old woman comes to her physician because of progressively worsening shortness of breath for the past 2 months. She does not experience shortness of breath at rest. She also occasionally has a dry cough. She has not had fever, chills, or night sweats. She has smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for the past 40 years. She drinks a beer daily and occasionally more on weekends. She does not use illicit drugs. She is 183 cm (6 ft 0 in) tall and weighs 66 kg (145 lbs); BMI is 19.7 kg/m2. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 94/min, respirations are 21/min, and blood pressure is 136/88 mm Hg. Lung auscultation reveals a prolonged expiratory phase and end-expiratory wheezing. Spirometry shows an FEV1:FVC ratio of 62%, an FEV1 of 60% of predicted, and a total lung capacity of 125% of predicted. The diffusion capacity of the lung (DLCO) is decreased. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department 3 hours after having a 2-minute episode of violent, jerky movements of her right arm at school. She was sweating profusely during the episode and did not lose consciousness. She remembers having felt a chill down her spine before the episode. Following the episode, she experienced weakness in the right arm and was not able to lift it above her head for 2 hours. Three weeks ago, she had a sore throat that resolved with over-the-counter medication. She was born at term and her mother remembers her having an episode of jerky movements when she had a high-grade fever as a toddler. There is no family history of serious illness, although her father passed away in a motor vehicle accident approximately 1 year ago. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 98/min, and blood pressure is 94/54 mm Hg. Physical and neurologic examinations show no abnormalities. A complete blood count and serum concentrations of glucose, electrolytes, calcium, and creatinine are within the reference range. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 30-year-old man comes to the physician because of nervousness and difficulty sleeping over the past 4 weeks. He has difficulty falling asleep at night because he cannot stop worrying about his relationship and his future. Three months ago, his new girlfriend moved in with him. Before this relationship, he had been single for 13 years. He reports that his girlfriend does not keep things in order in the way he was used to. Sometimes, she puts her dirty dishes in the kitchen sink instead of putting them in the dishwasher directly. She refuses to add any groceries to the shopping list when they are used up. She has also suggested several times that they have dinner at a restaurant instead of eating at home, which enrages him because he likes to plan each dinner of the week and buy the required groceries beforehand. The patient says that he really loves his girlfriend but that he will never be able to tolerate her “flaws.” Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. On mental status examination, he is cooperative but appears distressed. His affect has little intensity or range. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old male presents to a counselor at the urging of his parents because they are concerned that he might be depressed. After recently breaking up with his long-term girlfriend, he moved back in with his parents because he could not handle making decisions alone. Soon after their breakup, he started going on 5–7 dates a week. He has been unemployed for 3 years, as his girlfriend took care of all the bills. In the past year, he thought of looking for a job but never felt confident enough to start the process. His dad arranges his doctors appointments and handles his car maintenance. He describes feeling uneasy when he is alone. He has hypothyroidism treated with levothyroxine. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. Vital signs are normal. Mental status exam shows a neutral affect. Neurologic examination shows no focal findings. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old African-American man comes to the physician after an episode of hemoptysis. Over the past 8 months, he has had a nonproductive cough, fatigue, and a 9-kg (20-lb) weight loss. He drinks a glass of wine every night and does not smoke. He has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis. He does not take any medications. He has never traveled out of the country. He works as an accountant. His temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse is 94/min, and blood pressure is 130/90 mm Hg. Lungs are clear to auscultation. An x-ray of the chest shows a 2.5-cm nodule with irregular borders at the apex of the left lung with no mediastinal or hilar enlargement. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department because of a 1-day history of malaise and abdominal pain. Six weeks ago, she had vomiting and watery diarrhea for 2 days that resolved without treatment. Twelve weeks ago, she underwent orthotopic liver transplantation for alcoholic cirrhosis. At the time of discharge, her total serum bilirubin concentration was 1.0 mg/dL. She stopped drinking alcohol one year ago. Her current medications include daily tacrolimus, prednisone, valganciclovir, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Her temperature is 37.7°C (99.9°F), pulse is 95/min, and blood pressure is 150/80 mm Hg. She appears uncomfortable and has mild jaundice. Examination shows scleral icterus. The abdomen is soft and tender to deep palpation over the right upper quadrant, where there is a well-healed surgical scar. Her leukocyte count is 2500/mm3, serum bilirubin concentration is 2.6 mg/dL, and serum tacrolimus concentration is within therapeutic range. Which of the following is the next appropriate step in diagnosis?

A 47-year-old woman comes to the emergency department because of urinary and fecal incontinence for 6 hours. Earlier in the day, she suffered a fall at a construction site and sustained injuries to her back and thighs but did not seek medical attention. She took ibuprofen for lower back pain. Her temperature is 36.9°C (98.4°F), pulse is 80/min, and blood pressure is 132/84 mm Hg. Examination shows tenderness over the lumbar spine, bilateral lower extremity weakness, absent ankle jerk reflexes, and preserved patellar reflexes. There is decreased rectal tone. An ultrasound of the bladder shows a full bladder. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-week history of abdominal bloating and increased frequency of stools. She describes the stools as bulky, foul-smelling, and difficult to flush. She also has a 4-month history of recurrent dull upper abdominal pain that usually lasts for a few days, worsens after meals, and is not relieved with antacids. She has had a 10-kg (22-lb) weight loss in the past 4 months. She has no personal or family history of serious illness. She has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for 37 years. She has a 12-year history of drinking 6 to 8 beers daily. She is 160 cm (5 ft 3 in) tall and weighs 52 kg (115 lb); BMI is 20 kg/m2. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Abdominal examination shows mild epigastric tenderness without rebound or guarding. Bowel sounds are normal. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 72-year-old man comes to the emergency department 4 hours after the sudden onset of a diffuse, dull, throbbing headache. During this time, he also reports blurred vision, nausea, and one episode of vomiting. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. His medications include hydrochlorothiazide, lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. He has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the past 30 years and drinks 1–2 glasses of wine per day. His temperature is 36.6 °C (97.9 °F), pulse is 90/min, respirations are 14/min, and blood pressure is 185/110 mm Hg. Fundoscopic examination shows bilateral blurring of the optic disc margins. Physical and neurologic examinations show no other abnormalities. A complete blood count and serum concentrations of electrolytes, urea nitrogen, and creatinine are within the reference range. Urinalysis shows 2+ protein but no WBCs or RBCs. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of right hip pain that started that afternoon. Her mother reports that she has also been limping since the pain developed. She says that the pain worsens when she moves or walks. She participated in a dance recital yesterday, but her mother believes that she was not injured at the time. She was born at term and has been healthy except for an episode of nasal congestion and mild cough 10 days ago. Her mother has rheumatoid arthritis and her grandmother has osteoporosis. She is at the 50th percentile for height and 50th percentile for weight. Her temperature is 37.5°C (99.6°F), pulse is 105/min, respirations are 16/min, and blood pressure is 90/78 mm Hg. Her right hip is slightly abducted and externally rotated. Examination shows no tenderness, warmth, or erythema. She is able to bear weight. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin concentration of 12.3 g/dL, a leukocyte count of 8,500/mm3, and an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 12 mm/h. Ultrasound of the right hip shows increased fluid within the joint. X-ray of the hips shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old man comes to the physician because of right-sided blurry vision and eye pain for 4 days. He has a 6-day history of low-grade fever, headache, and malaise. One year ago, he was diagnosed with Crohn disease. His only medication is prednisone. His temperature is 38°C (100.4°F), pulse is 84/min, and blood pressure is 112/75 mm Hg. The right eyelid is erythematous and tender; there are multiple vesicles over the right forehead and the tip of the nose. Visual acuity is 20/20 in the left eye and 20/80 in the right eye. Extraocular movements are normal. The right eye shows conjunctival injection and reduced corneal sensitivity. Fluorescein staining shows a corneal lesion with a tree-like pattern. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his mother for a follow-up examination. He has a history of recurrent asthma attacks. The mother reports that her son has also had mild abdominal pain for the past 2 weeks. The patient's current medications include daily inhaled fluticasone and inhaled albuterol as needed. He appears well. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 100/min, and blood pressure is 130/85 mm Hg. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Cardiac examination shows no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Abdominal examination shows a left-sided, nontender, smooth abdominal mass that does not cross the midline. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. A complete blood count and serum concentrations of electrolytes, urea nitrogen, and creatinine are within the reference range. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old woman comes to the emergency department for pain and swelling of her left knee one day after injuring it while playing soccer. While sprinting on the field, she slipped as she attempted to kick the ball and landed on the anterior aspect of her knee. She underwent an appendectomy at the age of 16 years. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows a swollen and tender left knee; range of motion is limited by pain. The tibial tuberosity shows tenderness to palpation. The left tibia is displaced posteriorly when force is applied to the proximal tibia after flexing the knee. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. An x-ray of the left knee joint shows an avulsion fracture of the tibial condyle. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her parents because of a 4.5-kg (10-lb) weight loss during the last 3 months. During this period, she has complained of abdominal pain and fullness, and her parents feel that she has been eating less. Her parents also report that her urine has appeared pink for several weeks. She has been performing poorly in school lately, with reports from teachers that she has not been paying attention in class and has been distracting to other students. She was born at term and has been healthy except for a history of several infantile seizures. Her vital signs are within normal limits. She is at the 60th percentile for height and 20th percentile for weight. Physical examination shows a palpable abdominal mass, abdominal tenderness in the left upper quadrant, and left costovertebral angle tenderness. There are several ellipsoid, hypopigmented macules on the back and legs and a 4-cm raised plaque of rough, dimpled skin on the right lower back that is the same color as the surrounding skin. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old man is brought to the emergency department because of intermittent sharp right upper quadrant abdominal pain and nausea for the past 10 hours. He vomited three times. There is no associated fever, chills, diarrhea, or urinary symptoms. He has two children who both attend high school. He appears uncomfortable. He is 165 cm (5 ft 5 in) tall and weighs 86 kg (190 lb); BMI is 32 kg/m2. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 100/min, and blood pressure is 140/90 mm Hg. He has mild scleral icterus. The abdomen is soft and nondistended, with tenderness to palpation of the right upper quadrant without guarding or rebound. Bowel sounds are normal. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin count 14 g/dL
Leukocyte count 9,000 mm3
Platelet count 160,000 mm3
Serum
Alkaline phosphatase 238 U/L
Aspartate aminotransferase 60 U/L
Bilirubin
Total 2.8 mg/dL
Direct 2.1 mg/dL
Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 24-year-old woman comes to the physician with a wound on her forearm. She says that she injured herself by absentmindedly walking into a glass door. She does not have health insurance. She has had 5 jobs in the past 8 months. She quit each job after 3–4 weeks because she found the work beneath her. She was imprisoned 6 years ago for credit card fraud. She was released from prison on parole a year ago. She was expelled from school at the age of 13 years for stealing school property and threatening to assault a teacher. She has mothered 6 children with 4 men. She says that she does not provide child support because she needs the money for her own personal expenses. The patient's vital signs are within normal limits. Examination of the forearm shows a 6 cm long, 0.5 cm deep wound with neat edges on the dorsal surface of the left forearm. There are bruises on the left shoulder, back, and the proximal phalanges of the right hand. On mental status examination, the patient is alert and calm. Her mood is described as cheerful. Her thought process, thought content, and speech are normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of persistent pain in his right shoulder. The pain is localized to the top of the shoulder and is worse with movement. He has stiffness in the right shoulder that is worse in the morning and usually lasts 20 minutes. The patient reports that he is unable to brush his hair and has stopped going to his regular tennis lessons because of the pain. He does not recall any fall or trauma. When his right arm is passively abducted in an arc, there is pain between 60 and 120 degrees of abduction. When asked to lower the right arm slowly from 90 degrees of abduction, he is unable to hold his arm up and it drops to his side. Passive range of motion is normal. Injection of 5 mL of 1% lidocaine into the right subacromial space does not relieve the pain or improve active range of motion of the right arm. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old woman comes to the emergency department because of decreased vision and black spots in front of her left eye for the past 24 hours. She states that it feels as if 'a curtain is hanging over her eye.' She sees flashes of light intermittently. She has no pain or diplopia. She underwent cataract surgery on the left eye 2 weeks ago. She has hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Her brother has open-angle glaucoma. Current medications include metformin, linagliptin, ramipril, and hydrochlorothiazide. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows a visual acuity in the right eye of 20/25 and the ability to count fingers at 3 feet in the left eye. The pupils are equal and reactive. The corneal reflex is present. The anterior chamber shows no abnormalities. The confrontation test is normal on the right side and shows nasal and inferior defects on the left side. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. The patient is awaiting dilation for fundus examination. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old woman comes to the emergency department because of worsening shortness of breath and a productive cough for 3 days. She sustained trauma to the right hemithorax during a fight 3 weeks ago. She had significant pain and mild shortness of breath following the incident but did not seek medical care. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is a construction worker. Her temperature is 38.4°C (101.1°F), pulse is 95/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 120/75 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 96%. Pulmonary examination shows decreased breath sounds over the right lower lung fields. CT scan of the chest shows fractures of the right 7th and 8th ribs, right pleural splitting and thickening, and a dense fluid collection in the pleural space. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 37-year-old man comes to the physician because of right-sided inguinal pain for the past 8 weeks. During this period, the patient has had increased pain during activities such as walking and standing. He has no nausea, vomiting, or fever. His temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F), pulse is 73/min, and blood pressure is 132/80 mm Hg. The abdomen is soft and nontender. There is a visible and palpable groin protrusion above the inguinal ligament on the right side. Bulging is felt during Valsalva maneuver. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 63-year-old woman comes to the physician for the evaluation of difficulty walking for the last 6 months. She reports weakness in her lower legs that improves with exercise and throughout the day. Three months ago, she started adding flax seeds to her breakfast because she is frequently constipated. She has hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes daily for the last 45 years. Her current medications include enalapril and metformin. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows dry mucous membranes. Muscle strength in the lower extremities is decreased. Sensation to pinprick and light touch is normal. Deep tendon reflexes are 1+ bilaterally. Active muscle contraction or repeated muscle tapping increases reflex activity. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 56-year-old woman comes to the physician for a routine health maintenance examination. She has had mild pain in her left groin for 2 weeks. She was admitted to the hospital 1 month ago for myocardial infarction. Cardiac catheterization and angiography showed occlusion of the left anterior descending artery and she underwent placement of 2 stents. She has hypertension and hypercholesterolemia. There is no family history of serious illness. She has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes daily for 30 years. Current medications include aspirin, clopidogrel, rosuvastatin, and enalapril. Her temperature is 36.7°C (98°F), pulse is 88/min, and blood pressure is 130/84 mm Hg. Examination shows a 3-cm (1.2-in), tender, pulsatile mass in the left thigh, below the inguinal ligament. There is mild erythema of the overlying skin. A loud murmur is heard on auscultation of the mass. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. There is no edema in the lower limbs. Femoral and pedal pulses are palpable bilaterally. Neurologic examination shows no focal findings. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 50-year-old woman comes to the physician for a routine checkup. She has had a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of her neck for 2 months. She does not have a fever or any discharge from the swelling. She underwent a colectomy for colon cancer at the age of 43 years. She has type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. Current medications include insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen. She has worked as a traffic warden for the past 6 years and frequently plays golf. She appears healthy. Her temperature is 37.3°C (99.1°F), pulse is 88/min, and blood pressure is 130/86 mm Hg. Examination of the neck shows a 2.5-cm (1-in) firm, mobile, and painless nodule. The skin over the nodule cannot be pinched. The lungs are clear to auscultation. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. A photograph of the lesion is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old woman develops reduced urine output and a serum creatinine concentration of 2.9 mg/dL three days after being hospitalized for acute diverticulitis. On admission, a complete blood count showed a hemoglobin concentration of 15.5 g/dL and a leukocyte count of 14,000/mm3. Urinalysis showed 2+ proteinuria, and serum studies showed a blood glucose of 145 mg/dL and a creatinine concentration of 1.2 mg/dL. A CT scan of the abdomen confirmed the diagnosis. Therapy with intravenous ketoprofen, piperacillin, and tazobactam was begun, and the patient was placed on bowel rest. She has a history of hypertension, chronic constipation, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Prior to admission, her medications were insulin, metoprolol, and losartan. Today, her temperature is 37.7°C (99.9°F), pulse is 97/min, respirations are 12/min, and blood pressure is 135/87 mm Hg. The abdomen is soft on physical examination, and there is tenderness to palpation of the left lower quadrant. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's current renal findings?

A 4-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of progressive intermittent pain and swelling in both knees and right ankle and wrist for 3 months. He has been taking acetaminophen and using ice packs, both of which relieved his symptoms. The affected joints feel "stuck" and difficult to move when he wakes up in the morning, but he can move them freely after a few minutes. He has also occasional mild eye pain that resolves spontaneously. Five months ago he was diagnosed with upper respiratory tract infection that resolved without treatment. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows that the affected joints are swollen, erythematous, and tender to touch. Slit-lamp examination shows an anterior chamber flare with signs of iris inflammation bilaterally. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 12.6 g/dl
Leukocyte count 8,000/mm3
Segmented neutrophils 76%
Eosinophils 1%
Lymphocytes 20%
Monocytes 3%
Platelet count 360,000/mm3
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 36 mm/hr
Serum
Antinuclear antibodies 1:320
Rheumatoid factor negative
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of blurry vision for 10 hours. He has also had urinary urgency and discomfort while urinating for the past 4 days. He has been feeling increasingly weak and nauseous since yesterday. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and arterial hypertension. One year ago he was treated for an infection of his eyes. He drinks 2–3 glasses of wine weekly. Current medications include captopril, metoprolol, metformin, and insulin. His temperature is 37.5°C (99.5°F), pulse is 107/min, and blood pressure is 95/70 mm Hg. Visual acuity is decreased in both eyes. The pupils are equal and reactive to light. The corneal reflexes are brisk. The mucous membranes of the mouth are dry. The abdomen is soft and not distended. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old girl is brought to the physician because she has excessively dry skin. Her father says that she has had dry, scaly skin since she was 6 months old. He says it is worse in winter and better in summer. There is no associated itching, redness, or discharge. Examination reveals generalized fine scales with coarse skin all over the body, except in the skin creases of the neck and in the cubital and popliteal fossae (see image). There are multiple papular elevations at the base of hair follicles and darkening of the palmar and plantar creases. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old female graduate student comes to the physician for a two-month history of repeated thoughts and anxiety that she is going to be harmed by someone on the street. The anxiety worsened after witnessing a pedestrian getting hit by a car two weeks ago. She says, “That was a warning sign.” On her way to school, she now often leaves an hour earlier to take a detour and hide from people that she thinks might hurt her. She is burdened by her coursework and fears that her professors are meaning to fail her. She says her friends are concerned about her but that they do not understand because they were not present at the accident. The patient has no known history of psychiatric illness. On mental status exam, she is alert and oriented, and shows full range of affect. Thought processes and speech are organized. Her memory and attention are within normal limits. She denies auditory, visual, or tactile hallucinations. Urine toxicology screening is negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 13-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his parents for the evaluation of progressive hair loss over the past 2 months. The parents report that they have noticed increased number of hairless patches on their son's head. The patient denies any itching. There is no personal or family history of serious illness. The patient states that he has been feeling tense since his girlfriend broke up with him. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He does not use illicit drugs. His vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows ill-defined patchy hair loss and hair of different lengths with no scaling or reddening of the scalp. Further examination shows poor hair growth of the eyebrows and eyelashes. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department because of a fall that occurred while she was taking a shower earlier that morning. Her husband heard her fall and entered the bathroom to find all four of her extremities twitching. The episode lasted approximately 30 seconds. She was unsure of what had happened and was unable to answer simple questions on awakening. She has regained orientation since that time. She has hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Current medications include metoprolol and atorvastatin. Her temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 72/min, respirations are 19/min, and blood pressure is 130/80 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 98%. Cranial nerve examination shows no abnormalities. She has 5/5 strength in all extremities. Examination shows full muscle strength. Sensation to pinprick, light touch, and vibration is normal and symmetrical. A noncontrast head CT is performed and shows a slightly hyperdense mass. Follow-up MRI shows a homogeneous, well-circumscribed 4-cm mass with compression of the adjacent white matter, and a hyperintense rim around the mass on T2 weighted imaging. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 18-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by his coach, 30 minutes after injuring his left knee while playing field hockey. He was tackled from the left side and has been unable to bear weight on his left leg since the accident. He fears the left knee may be unstable upon standing. There is no personal or family history of serious illness. The patient appears uncomfortable. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows a swollen and tender left knee; range of motion is limited by pain. The medial joint line is tender to touch. The patient's hip is slightly flexed and abducted, and the knee is slightly flexed while the patient is in the supine position. Gentle valgus stress is applied across the left knee and medial joint laxity is noted. The remainder of the examination shows no further abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a skin lesion on her nose. The patient has had the lesion for 11 months and it has increased in size over the past few months. She is a farmer and lives together with her husband. Her father died of metastatic melanoma at the age of 67 years. The patient has smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for the past 30 years and drinks 1–2 glasses of whiskey on weekends. Her temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F), pulse is 75/min, and blood pressure is 140/78 mm Hg. Examination of the skin shows a nontender lesion at the right root of the nose. An image of the lesion is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 77-year-old man is brought to the physician for gradually increasing confusion and difficulty walking for the past 4 months. His son is concerned because he has been forgetful and seems to be walking more slowly. He has been distracted during his weekly bridge games and his usual television shows. He has also had increasingly frequent episodes of urinary incontinence and now wears an adult diaper daily. He has hyperlipidemia and hypertension. Current medications include lisinopril and atorvastatin. His temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F), pulse is 84/min, respirations are 15/min, and blood pressure is 139/83 mmHg. He is confused and oriented only to person and place. He recalls 2 out of 3 words immediately and 1 out of 3 after five minutes. He has a broad-based gait and takes short steps. Sensation is intact and muscle strength is 5/5 throughout. Laboratory studies are within normal limits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 65-year-old woman comes to the emergency department 1 hour after a loss of consciousness. Her husband said she suddenly fainted while he was adjusting her necktie. She regained consciousness within 30 seconds and was fully alert and oriented. She has had two similar episodes in the last year. She has anxiety and takes alprazolam as needed. She smokes half a pack of cigarettes daily and drinks two glasses of wine with dinner each night. Her temperature is 37.2°C (98.9°F), pulse is 70/min and regular, respirations are 13/min, blood pressure is 130/82 mm Hg when supine and 122/80 mm Hg while standing. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. Neurologic examination shows no focal findings. A complete blood count shows no abnormalities. Bedside cardiac monitoring shows infrequent premature ventricular contractions and QRS voltage below 5 mm in leads II and III. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of abdominal distention and twitching of his feet, which his mother noticed a week ago. The patient has also had a low-grade fever for 5 days. He has not had a bowel movement in 3 days. He was born at term and has been healthy since. He is at the 40th percentile for height and 20th percentile for weight. His temperature is 38.1°C (100.6°F), pulse is 128/min, and blood pressure is 135/82 mm Hg. Examination shows an irregular palpable mass that crosses the midline of the abdomen. The liver is palpated 3 cm below the right costal margin. There are erratic movements of the eyes. A 24-hour urine collection shows elevated homovanillic acid and vanillylmandelic acid levels. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 73-year-old woman comes to the physician because of worsening bilateral lower extremity pain for the past 8 months. The pain begins after walking one to two blocks and radiates bilaterally down the buttocks with cramping and tingling. She reports that the pain is worse while walking downhill and is relieved by sitting and leaning forward. She has hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She had a myocardial infarction at the age of 55 years and an abdominal aortic aneurysm repair at the age of 60 years. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the past 30 years. She does not drink alcohol or use illicit drugs. Her current medications include sitagliptin, metformin, atorvastatin, metoprolol succinate, amlodipine, and hydrochlorothiazide. Her temperature is 37.5°C (99.5°F), pulse is 82/min, respirations are 17/min, and blood pressure is 150/87 mm Hg. Examination shows full muscle strength. Sensation is reduced bilaterally in the feet and toes. Straight leg raise is negative. X-ray of the spine shows degenerative changes. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A previously healthy 17-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department by her mother for further evaluation after elective removal of her wisdom teeth. During the procedure, the patient had persistent bleeding from the teeth's surrounding gums. Multiple gauze packs were applied with minimal effect. The patient has a history of easy bruising. The mother says her brother had similar problems when his wisdom teeth were removed, and that he also has a history of easy bruising and joint swelling. The patient takes no medications. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 108/74 mm Hg. Laboratory studies show:
Hematocrit 35%
Leukocyte count 8,500/mm3
Platelet count 160,000/mm3
Prothrombin time 15 sec
Partial thromboplastin time 60 sec
Bleeding time 6 min
Fibrin split products negative
Serum
Urea nitrogen 20 mg/dL
Creatinine 1.0 mg/dL
Bilirubin
Total 1.0 mg/dL
Direct 0.5 mg/dL
Lactate dehydrogenase 90 U/L
Peripheral blood smear shows normal-sized platelets. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after the sudden onset of severe, migrating anterior chest pain, shortness of breath, and sweating at rest. She has hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Medications include atorvastatin, hydrochlorothiazide, lisinopril, and metformin. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 25 years. She is in severe distress. Her pulse is 110/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 150/85 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 98%. Cardiac examination shows a grade 3/6, high-pitched, blowing, diastolic murmur heard best over the right sternal border. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Femoral pulses are decreased bilaterally. An ECG shows sinus tachycardia and left ventricular hypertrophy. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old man comes to his physician because of fatigue. He has been coming to the office multiple times a month for various minor problems over the past six months. During the appointments, he insists on a first name basis and flirts with his physician. He always dresses very fashionably. When her assistant enters the room, he tends to start fidgeting and interrupt their conversation. When the physician tells him politely that his behavior is inappropriate, he begins to cry, complaining that no one understands him and that if people only listened to him, he would not be so exhausted. He then quickly gathers himself and states that he will just have to keep looking for a physician who can help him, although he has doubts he will ever find the right physician. He does not have a history of self harm or suicidal ideation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 74-year-old Hispanic woman comes to the physician because of a three-week history of dizziness upon standing and a brief loss of consciousness one hour ago. The patient suddenly collapsed on her way to the bathroom after waking up in the morning. She did not sustain any injuries from her collapse. She has a history of gastroesophageal reflux disease, and gout. The patient's mother died of a grand mal seizure at the age of 53 years. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 55 years. She drinks three beers and two glasses of whiskey daily. Current medications include ranitidine, and allopurinol. She is 166 cm (5 ft 5 in) tall and weighs 62 kg (137 lb); BMI is 22.5 kg/m2. She appears pale. Temperature is 36.7°C (98.0°F), pulse is 83/min, and blood pressure is 125/80 mm Hg supine and 100/70 mm Hg one minute after standing with no change in pulse rate. Physical examination shows conjunctival pallor. A plopping sound is heard on auscultation, immediately followed by a low-pitched, rumbling mid-diastolic murmur heard best at the apex. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. An ECG shows regular sinus rhythm. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her foster father because of complaints from her teachers regarding poor performance at school for the past 8 months. She does not listen to their instructions, often talks during class, and rarely completes her school assignments. She does not sit in her seat in the classroom and often cuts in line at the cafeteria. Her foster father reports that she runs around a lot inside the house and refuses to help her brother with chores and errands. She frequently interrupts her foster father's conversations with others and talks excessively. He has found her trying to climb on the roof on multiple occasions. She was placed in foster care because of neglect by her biological parents 3 years ago. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Neurologic examination shows no focal findings. Mental status examination shows a neutral affect. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of fatigue and myalgia. Over the past month, he has had intermittent episodes of nausea. He has a history of intravenous drug use, but he has not used illicit drugs for the past five years. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 14 years and drinks one alcoholic beverage daily. He takes no medications. His last visit to a physician was 4 years ago. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 90/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. Physical examination shows jaundice and hepatosplenomegaly. There are also blisters and erosions on the dorsum of both hands. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 12 g/dL
Leukocyte count 8,300/mm3
Platelet count 250,000/mm3
Serum
Glucose 170 mg/dL
Albumin 3.0 g/dL
Total bilirubin 2.2 mg/dL
Alkaline phosphatase 80 U/L
AST 92 U/L
ALT 76 U/L
Hepatitis B surface antigen negative
Hepatitis B surface antibody positive
Hepatitis B core antibody positive
Hepatitis C antibody positive
Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 48-year-old woman comes to the physician because of worsening shortness of breath and nocturnal cough for the past 2 weeks. On two occasions, her cough was bloody. She had a heart condition as a child that was treated with antibiotics. She emigrated to the US from Kazakhstan 15 years ago. Pulmonary examination shows crackles at both lung bases. Cardiac examination is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 13-year-old Hispanic girl is brought to the physician by her father because of left groin pain for 1 month. The pain radiates to her left knee and is aggravated on walking. She fell during soccer practice 5 weeks ago but did not see a doctor about it and does not recall any immediate and persistent pain after the event. She has hypothyroidism. Her only medication is levothyroxine. Her immunizations are up-to-date. She appears uncomfortable. She is at the 50th percentile for height and at the 95th percentile for weight. Her temperature is 37.1°C (98.9°F), pulse is 77/min, respirations are 14/min, and blood pressure is 100/70 mm Hg. The patient has a left-sided, antalgic gait. The left lower extremity is externally rotated. The left hip is tender to palpation and internal rotation is limited by pain. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 13.1 g/dL
Leukocyte count 9,100/mm3
Platelet count 250,000/mm3
Serum
TSH 3.6 μU/mL
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old boy comes in to the emergency department with his mother for swelling of his left periorbital region. Yesterday morning he woke up with a painful, warm, soft lump on his left eyelid. Eye movement does not worsen the pain. Physical examination shows redness and swelling of the upper left eyelid, involving the hair follicles. Upon palpation, the swelling drains purulent fluid. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

Five days after undergoing an open abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, a 68-year-old man has crampy abdominal pain. During this period, he has also had two episodes of loose, bloody stools. His surgery was complicated by severe blood loss requiring the administration of vasopressors and multiple transfusions. Cefazolin was administered as a perioperative antibiotic. The patient has hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and coronary artery disease. The patient has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes daily for 50 years and drinks 3–4 glasses of wine every week. His current medications include hydrochlorothiazide, atorvastatin, amlodipine, aspirin, and metoprolol. He appears ill. His temperature is 38.0°C (100.4°F), pulse is 110/min, and blood pressure is 96/58 mm Hg. Physical examination shows a distended abdomen with absent bowel sounds. The abdomen is exquisitely tender to palpation in all quadrants. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Cardiac examination shows an S4 gallop. An x-ray of the abdomen shows air-filled distended bowel. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of a progressive rash for 2 days. The rash started behind the ears and now involves the trunk and extremities. Over the past 4 days, she has had mild sore throat, red, itchy eyes, and headache. She was born at term and has been healthy except for recurrent episodes of tonsillitis and occasional asthma attacks. Two weeks ago, she was treated for tonsillitis that resolved with penicillin therapy. She immigrated with her family from Brazil 3 weeks ago. Her immunization status is unknown. The patient appears weak and lethargic. Her temperature is 38°C (100.4°F), pulse is 100/min, and blood pressure is 100/60 mm Hg. Examination shows postauricular and suboccipital lymphadenopathy. There is a non-confluent, pink maculopapular rash over the torso and extremities. Her palms and soles show no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old woman comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. She has a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. She has hypertension and ulcerative colitis which was diagnosed via colonoscopy 5 years ago. Current medications include lisinopril and rectal mesalamine. She is sexually active with 2 male partners and uses condoms inconsistently. Her temperature is 37.3°C (99.1°F), pulse is 86/min, and blood pressure is 130/84 mm Hg. Examination shows scleral icterus and multiple scratch marks on the trunk and extremities. The lungs are clear to auscultation. The abdomen is soft and nontender. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 11.5 g/dL
Leukocyte count 7500/mm3
Platelet count 280,000/mm3
Serum
Na+ 138 mEq/L
Cl- 101 mEq/L
K+ 4.7 mEq/L
Urea nitrogen 18 mg/dL
Glucose 91 mg/dL
Creatinine 0.8 mg/dL
Bilirubin
Total 1.5 mg/dL
Direct 0.9 mg/dL
Alkaline phosphatase 460 U/L
AST 75 U/L
ALT 78 U/L
Anti-nuclear antibody negative
Antimitochondrial antibodies negative
Abdominal ultrasound shows thickening of the bile ducts and focal bile duct dilatation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 56-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of worsening pain in her left buttock. The pain is described as a deep, dull ache that is worse at night. She does not report any recent trauma. She has hyperlipidemia. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the past 30 years and drinks one beer every night. She does not use illicit drugs. Her only medication is simvastatin. Physical examination shows tenderness over the left gluteal region. Neurologic examination shows no focal findings. An x-ray of the pelvis shows a 4-cm, poorly defined, osteolytic lesion in the left ilium with a moth-eaten pattern of bone destruction, multiple well-defined sclerotic lesions, and an aggressive periosteal reaction. The remainder of the physical examination, including rectal examination, shows no abnormalities. Chest x-ray and abdominal ultrasonography show no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old woman comes to the physician because of constipation and decreased appetite during the past several months. In the past 2 weeks, she has also noticed an increasing frequency of urination. She has not had any dysuria or flank pain. She has a history of hypertension, calcium pyrophosphate crystal arthritis, and alcoholic cirrhosis. Current medications include hydrochlorothiazide, rifaximin, lactulose, and naproxen as needed for the joint pain. She quit drinking 5 years ago. She does not smoke cigarettes. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows decreased bowel sounds but is otherwise unremarkable. Serum studies show:
Creatinine 1.1 mg/dL
Calcium 11.8 mg/dL
Phosphorus 2.1 mg/dL
Magnesium 1.6 mg/dL
Total protein 6 g/dL
Albumin 3.1 g/dL
AST 53 U/L
ALT 43 U/L
Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 65-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department after coughing up copious amounts of blood-tinged sputum at her nursing home. She recently had an upper respiratory tract infection that was treated with antibiotics. She has a long-standing history of productive cough that has worsened since she had a stroke 3 years ago. She smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for 40 years until the stroke, after which she quit. The patient appears distressed and short of breath. Her temperature is 38°C (100.4°F), pulse is 92/min, and blood pressure is 145/85 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 92%. Physical examination shows digital clubbing and cyanosis of the lips. Coarse crackles are heard in the thorax. An x-ray of the chest shows increased translucency and tram-track opacities in the right lower lung field. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 21-year-old woman comes to the physician because of pruritus and a hypopigmented rash on her upper body for 5 days. She first noticed the symptoms after returning from a business trip last week in the Bahamas. While she was there, she visited a couple of beaches and went hiking with some coworkers. The rash initially started as a single lesion on her upper back but since then has extended to her shoulders. She has a history of type 1 diabetes mellitus controlled with an insulin pump. She works as an office manager and has no known exposure to melanocytotoxic chemicals. She has been sexually active with three male partners over the past year and uses condoms inconsistently. She is 183 cm (6 ft) tall and weighs 80 kg (176 lb); BMI is 23.9 kg/m2. Her temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), pulse is 78/min, and blood pressure is 130/84 mm Hg. A photograph of the rash is shown. One month ago, her hemoglobin A1C was 7.8%. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 58-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus comes to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of dysphagia and swelling in the neck and lower jaw. She has had tooth pain on the left side over the past week, which has made it difficult for her to sleep. Four weeks ago, she had a 3-day episode of flu-like symptoms, including sore throat, that resolved without treatment. She has a history of hypertension. Current medications include metformin and lisinopril. She appears distressed. She is 180 cm (5 ft 11 in) tall and weighs 100 kg (220 lbs); her BMI is 31.6 kg/m2. Her temperature is 38.4°C (101.1°F), pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 110/80 mm Hg. Oral cavity examination shows a decayed lower left third molar with drainage of pus. There is submandibular and anterior neck tenderness and swelling. Her leukocyte count is 15,600/mm3, platelet count is 300,000/mm3, and fingerstick blood glucose concentration is 250 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old man undergoes a laparoscopic appendectomy for acute appendicitis. During the procedure, a black, discolored liver is noted. Other than the recent appendicitis, the patient has no history of serious illness and takes no medications. He has no medication allergies. He does not drink alcohol or use illicit drugs. He has an uncomplicated postoperative course. At his follow-up visit 3 weeks later, his vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows scleral icterus, which the patient states has been present for many years. Abdominal examination shows healing scars without drainage or erythema. Serum studies show:
Aspartate aminotransferase 30 IU/L
Alanine aminotransferase 35 IU/L
Alkaline phosphatase 47 mg/dL
Total bilirubin 5.2 mg/dL
Direct bilirubin 4.0 mg/dL
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 71-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department because of severe, progressive left leg pain and tingling for 8 hours. The symptoms began while she was watching television. For several months, the patient has noticed calf cramping when going for long walks, as well as occasional foot tingling and numbness, but did not seek medical attention. She has no history of recent injuries. She has poorly-controlled hypertension, hyperlipidemia, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and osteoarthritis. She smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 35 years but quit 15 years ago. She drinks three beers every night. Current medications include lisinopril, metoprolol succinate, atorvastatin, metformin, and ibuprofen. She appears to be in severe pain and is clutching her left leg. Her temperature is 37.4°C (99.3°F), pulse is 110/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 163/94 mm Hg. The lungs are clear to auscultation. There is a harsh II/VI systolic ejection murmur best heard at the right upper sternal border. The abdomen is soft and nontender. The left leg is cool to the touch with decreased popliteal, posterior tibial, and dorsalis pedis pulses. There is 5/5 strength on left hip, knee, and ankle testing. The left hip, knee, and ankle show no gross effusion, erythema, or tenderness to palpation. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 38-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 1-month history of a painless, nonpruritic skin lesion on his right thigh. He initially thought it was an insect bite, but it has slowly increased in size over the past weeks. His temperature is 36.7°C (98°F), pulse is 75/min, and blood pressure is 128/76 mm Hg. Physical examination shows a 0.8-cm hyperpigmented papule. When the skin lesion is squeezed, the surface retracts inwards. A photograph of the lesion is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 61-year-old woman comes to the physician because of fatigue, diarrhea, and crampy abdominal pain for 3 weeks. The abdominal pain is worse after eating. During the past week, she has had up to 4 watery stools daily. She has also had pain in her mouth and gums for 6 days. She has not had nausea, vomiting, or fever. Four months ago, she went on a 1-week trip to the Dominican Republic. She has atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and hypothyroidism. Current medications include levothyroxine, metoprolol, and warfarin. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 40 years. Her temperature is 37.9°C (100.2°F), pulse is 81/min, and blood pressure is 120/75 mm Hg. Examination shows two 1-cm, tender ulcerative lesions in the mouth. Abdominal examination shows mild tenderness to palpation in the right lower quadrant without guarding or rebound. Bowel sounds are normal. Her hemoglobin concentration is 11.5 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume is 77 fL, leukocyte count is 11,800 mm3, and platelet count is 360,000 mm3. Colonoscopy with biopsy of the colonic mucosa is performed. Analysis of the specimen shows non-caseating granulomas and neutrophilic inflammation of the crypts. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old woman comes to the physician because of increasing generalized fatigue for 1 month. She has been unable to do normal household duties or go for her evening walks during this period. She has hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Her father died of liver cancer at the age of 60 years. She does not smoke. She drinks one alcoholic beverage daily. Current medications include atorvastatin, enalapril, metformin, and insulin glargine. She is 170 cm (5 ft 7 in) tall and weighs 100 kg (220 lb); BMI is 34.6 kg/m2. Her temperature is 36.6°C (97.9°F), pulse is 116/min, and blood pressure is 140/90 mm Hg. Examination shows hyperpigmented skin over the nape of the neck and extremities. The liver is palpated 4 cm below the right costal margin. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 10.6 g/dL
Mean corpuscular volume 87 μm3
Leukocyte count 9,700/mm3
Platelet count 182,000/mm3
Serum
Glucose 213 mg/dL
Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL
Albumin 4.1 mg/dL
Total bilirubin 1.1 mg/dL
Alkaline phosphatase 66 U/L
AST 100 U/L
ALT 69 U/L
γ-glutamyl transferase 28 U/L (N=5–50)
Hepatitis B surface antigen negative
Hepatitis C antibody negative
Iron studies
Iron 261 μg/dL
Ferritin 558 ng/dL
Transferrin saturation 83%
Anti-nuclear antibody negative
Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to confirm the diagnosis?

A 58-year-old man comes to the physician because of intermittent painful retrosternal dullness for 4 weeks. The pain is recurrent and occurs when he exerts himself or when he is outside during cold weather. He also experiences shortness of breath and palpitations during these episodes. The symptoms resolve spontaneously when he stops or sits down for a while. Over the past few days, the episodes have increased in frequency. He has hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and osteoarthritis. His left leg was amputated below the knee after a motorcycle accident 25 years ago. He is currently waiting for a new prosthesis and walks with crutches. Current medications include captopril, glyburide, and ibuprofen. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His pulse is 88/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 144/90 mm Hg. Cardiac examination shows no abnormalities. An x-ray of the chest shows no abnormalities. An ECG shows a normal sinus rhythm without any signs of ischemia. Serum cardiac markers are within the reference range. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 15-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her parents for evaluation of her “weird” behavior. The parents report that their daughter tortured their cat to death two weeks ago. Over the past year, she has been accused of stealing a car and setting a fire at her school. She has no history of serious illness. She attends a local high school, and her performance at school is very poor compared to her classmates. She often loses her temper and argues with her teachers. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 2 years. She does not drink alcohol. Her mother has a 10-year history of schizophrenia controlled with medication. On mental status examination, she is oriented to person, place, and time. The pupils are equal and reactive to light. Her speech is normal in rate and rhythm, and her thought process is organized. Short- and long-term memory are intact. Attention and concentration are poor. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after sustaining a fall from his bicycle 1 hour ago. The patient was on his way to work as he lost his balance, hitting his head on the sidewalk. He had an initial loss of consciousness for a couple of minutes following the accident. He currently has nausea and a headache. He has vomited twice during the last 30 minutes. He has no history of a serious illness. The patient does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has never used illicit drugs. He takes no medications. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 50/min, respirations are 10/min, and blood pressure is 160/90 mm Hg. He is oriented to person, place, and time. His lungs are clear to auscultation. Cardiac examination shows bradycardia but no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. The abdomen is soft and nontender. There is a bruise on the right temporal side of the head. While performing the remainder of the physical examination the patient starts having a seizure. Intravenous lorazepam is administered and he is admitted to the intensive care unit. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 32-year-old woman comes to the emergency department for acute pain in the left eye. She reports having awoken in the morning with a foreign body sensation. She had forgotten to remove her contact lenses before sleeping. Following lens removal, she experienced immediate pain, discomfort, and tearing of the left eye. She reports that the foreign body sensation persists and that rinsing with water has not improved the pain. She has been wearing contact lenses for 4 years and occasionally forgets to remove them at night. She has no history of serious medical illness. On examination, the patient appears distressed with pain and photophobia in the left eye. Administration of a topical anesthetic relieves the pain. Visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes. Ocular motility and pupillary response are normal. The corneal reflex is normal and symmetric in both eyes. Which of the following is most likely to establish the diagnosis in this patient?

A 10-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of high-grade fever, myalgia, and generalized fatigue for 3 days. He returned from a vacation to northern Brazil 4 days ago. He took the appropriate medications and immunizations prior to his visit. There is no family history of serious illness. He appears ill. His temperature is 39.4°C (103°F), pulse is 110/min and blood pressure is 94/54 mm Hg. Examination shows jaundice of the conjunctivae and skin. The abdomen is soft and nontender; the spleen is palpated 2 to 3 cm below the left costal margin. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL
Leukocyte count 4,650/mm3
Platelet count 200,000/mm3
Serum
Glucose 56 mg/dL
Creatinine 0.8 mg/dL
Bilirubin
Total 4.7 mg/dL
Direct 0.9 mg/dL
Lactate dehydrogenase 212 U/L
Which of the following is the most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 48-year-old woman is brought to the physician by her husband because she has become increasingly restless and anxious. Her husband says that she has seemed sad and irritable for the past 4 months. She lost her job as a store clerk because she often lied to avoid work, and spent most of her days on the phone placing bets on football games. She avoids all family-related events because she has borrowed money from most of her relatives. She is hopeful that her symptoms will improve once she is able to win some of her money back. She previously smoked 8–10 cigarettes daily but quit 1 month ago. She drinks beer on the weekends. On examination, she is uncooperative and dismissive. She is mildly tremulous. Neurologic examination is normal. She is oriented to person, place, and time. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department after a fall. She has been seen by the triage nurse but has not been evaluated by a physician. She is heard yelling down the hallway, requesting to speak to “whoever is in charge.” She refuses to talk to the emergency resident and insists on talking to the attending physician despite being informed that the attending is currently resuscitating a patient who was in a car accident. She says that she deserves better treatment because she has made numerous contributions to the field of medicine. When asked about her work, she mentions that she was a medical device saleswoman. She is accompanied by her husband, who appears embarrassed. He claims that his wife frequently makes a scene and apologizes for his wife's behavior. On mental status examination, the patient is oriented to person, place, and time. She appears agitated and speaks in short, pressured sentences. There is no disorder of thought process or content. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 20-year-old man comes to the physician because of recurrent abdominal cramps, bloating, and diarrhea for 4 months. He describes his stools as greasy, foul-smelling, and difficult to flush. During this time he has had a 6-kg (13.2-lb) weight loss. He has no personal or family history of serious illness. Physical examination shows pallor and cheilitis. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin concentration of 11 g/dL. Serum concentrations of electrolytes, urea nitrogen, and creatinine are within the reference range. Test of the stool for occult blood is negative and stool microscopy reveals no pathogens and no leukocytes. Analysis of a 24-hour stool sample shows 12 g of fat. The patient is asked to consume 25 g of d-xylose. Five hours later, its concentration is measured in urine at 2 g (N = > 4 g/5 h). The test is repeated after a two-week course of rifaximin, but the urinary concentration of d-xylose remains the same. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-day history of decreased urine output, progressively worsening bilateral pedal edema, and fatigue. She has a 4-month history of persistent lower back pain. She has hypercholesterolemia and stable angina pectoris. Current medications include atorvastatin, aspirin, and ibuprofen. Her pulse is 80/min, respirations are 16/min, and blood pressure is 150/100 mm Hg. Examination shows periorbital and pedal edema and pallor. There is tenderness of the lumbar spinal vertebrae. Straight leg raise test is negative. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 8.9 mg/dl
Serum
Urea nitrogen 20 mg/dl
Creatinine 2.4 mg/dl
Calcium 11.2 mg/dl
Alkaline phosphatase 140 U/L
X-ray of the spine shows diffuse osteopenia and multiple lytic lesions. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 45-year-old man comes to the physician because of shortness of breath while lying on his back over the past month. During this period, he has also had several episodes of bloody coughing. The patient reports that he had a heart problem when he was a child that was treated with antibiotics. He emigrated to the US from Russia 5 years ago. There is no family history of serious illness. Pulmonary examination shows crackles at both lung bases. Cardiac examination is shown. An ECG shows tachycardia and no P waves. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department 35 minutes after being involved in a high-speed motor vehicle collision. On arrival, she is alert, has mild chest pain, and minimal shortness of breath. She has one episode of vomiting in the hospital. Her temperature is 37.3°C (99.1°F), pulse is 108/min, respirations are 23/min, and blood pressure is 90/70 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 92%. Examination shows multiple abrasions over her trunk and right upper extremity. There are coarse breath sounds over the right lung base. Cardiac examination shows no murmurs, rubs, or gallop. Infusion of 0.9% saline is begun. She subsequently develops increasing shortness of breath. Arterial blood gas analysis on 60% oxygen shows:
pH 7.36
pCO2 39 mm Hg
pO2 68 mm Hg
HCO3- 18 mEq/L
O2 saturation 81%
An x-ray of the chest shows patchy, irregular infiltrates over the right lung fields. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 6-week history of tingling pain in the sole of her right foot when she raises it above chest level during exercises. She reports that she started exercising regularly 2 months ago and that her right calf cramps when she uses the incline feature on the treadmill, forcing her to take frequent breaks. The pain completely disappears after resting for a few minutes. She has an 8-year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has smoked two packs of cigarettes daily for 34 years. Her only medication is metformin. Her pulse is 82/min, and blood pressure is 170/92 mm Hg. Straight leg raise test elicits pallor and tingling pain in the right foot. There is no pain in the back. Her muscle strength is normal. Femoral pulses are palpable; right pedal pulses are absent. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old man is brought to the physician by his parents because of irritable mood that started 5 days ago. Since then, he has been staying up late at night working on a secret project. He is energetic despite sleeping less than 4 hours per day. His parents report that he seems easily distracted. He is usually very responsible, but this week he spent his paycheck on supplies for his project. He has never had similar symptoms before. In the past, he has had episodes where he felt too fatigued to go to school and slept until 2 pm every day for 2 weeks at a time. During those times, his parents noticed that he cried excessively, was very indecisive, and expressed feelings of worthlessness. Two months ago, he had an asthma exacerbation and was treated with bronchodilators and steroids. He tried cocaine once in high school but has not used it since. Vital signs are within normal limits. On mental status examination, he is irritable but cooperative. His speech is pressured and his thought process is linear. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old woman comes to the physician for the evaluation of an 8-week history of blood in her stool. Two months ago, she had an episode of bronchitis and was treated with amoxicillin. Since then, she has noticed blood in her stool and on the toilet paper occasionally. The patient has had intermittent constipation for the past 5 years. Six months ago, she had severe left lower quadrant pain and fever that resolved with antibiotic therapy. She underwent a colonoscopy 3 years ago, which did not show any evidence of malignancy. She takes levothyroxine for hypothyroidism. She had smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 45 years, but quit smoking 10 years ago. She drinks one glass of red wine every night. She appears pale. She is 180 cm (5 ft 11 in) tall and weighs 98 kg (216 lb); BMI is 32 kg/m2. Her temperature is 36°C (96.8°F), pulse is 85/min, and blood pressure is 135/80 mm Hg. Physical examination shows pale conjunctivae. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. The abdomen is soft and nontender with no organomegaly. Digital rectal examination shows no masses. Test of the stool for occult blood is positive. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 11 g/dL
Mean corpuscular volume 76 μm3
Red cell distribution width 17% (N = 13–15)
Leukocyte count 5,000/mm3
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department 20 minutes after she sustained a stab wound to her back during an altercation. She reports weakness and numbness of the lower extremities. She has no history of serious illness. On arrival, she is alert and cooperative. Her pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 100/65 mm Hg. Examination shows a deep 4-cm laceration on her back next to the vertebral column at the level of the T10 vertebra. Neurologic examination shows right-sided flaccid paralysis with a diminished vibratory sense ipsilaterally, decreased sensation to light touch at the level of her laceration and below, and left-sided loss of hot, cold, and pin-prick sensation at the level of the umbilicus and below. Deep tendon reflexes of her right lower extremity are 4+ and symmetrical. Babinski sign is absent bilaterally. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 16-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her parents for evaluation because of extreme irritability, fatigue, and loss of appetite for 3 weeks. Five months ago, her grandfather, whom she was very close to, passed away from chronic lymphocytic leukemia. She used to enjoy playing soccer but quit her soccer team last week. When she comes home from school she goes straight to bed and sleeps for 11–12 hours each night. She previously had good grades, but her teachers report that she has been disrespectful and distracted in class and failed an exam last week. She tried alcohol twice at a party last year and she has never smoked cigarettes. Vital signs are within normal limits. On mental status examination, she avoids making eye contact but cooperates with the exam. Her affect is limited and she describes an irritable mood. She is easily distracted and has a difficult time focusing for an extended conversation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 12-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of fever, malaise, and a painful, itchy rash on the right shoulder for 2 weeks. The patient's father says the girl's condition has worsened over the past 4 days. She has a history of atopic dermatitis. She has lived with her father at several public shelters since she separated from her physically abusive mother 2 months ago. Her immunizations are up-to-date. There is cervical lymphadenopathy. Laboratory studies show no abnormalities. A photograph of the rash is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old man comes to the physician because of increasing blurring of vision in both eyes. He says that the blurring has made it difficult to read, although he has noticed that he can read a little better if he holds the book below or above eye level. He also requires a bright light to look at objects. He reports that his symptoms began 8 years ago and have gradually gotten worse over time. He has hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Current medications include glyburide and lisinopril. When looking at an Amsler grid, he says that the lines in the center appear wavy and bent. An image of his retina, as viewed through fundoscopy is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of a painless skin lesion on her neck. The lesion has gradually become darker in color. Sometimes it is itchy. She also noticed one similar lesion on her lower back. She is a retired gardener. She has smoked half a pack of cigarettes daily for 40 years. Her temperature is 36.7°C (98°F), pulse is 72/min, and blood pressure is 123/78 mm Hg. Physical examination shows a 0.8-cm hyperpigmented papule on her neck and a 0.6-cm hyperpigmented papule on her lower back, both of which have a greasy and wax-like appearance. A photograph of the neck is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 73-year-old woman comes in to the emergency department because of nausea and severe pain in her upper abdomen and right shoulder blade for the past day. She was able to eat a little for breakfast but vomited up the meal a couple of hours later. She has type 2 diabetes mellitus treated with metformin. She has smoked half a pack of cigarettes daily for 40 years and drinks 4 beers every week. She appears acutely distressed. Her temperature is 38.8°C (102°F), pulse is 124/min, and blood pressure is 92/68 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 95%. The abdomen is soft and there is tenderness to palpation of the right upper quadrant with soft crepitus. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 14.3 g/dL
Leukocyte count 18,100/mm3
Platelet count 216,000/mm3
Serum
Aspartate aminotransferase (AST, SGOT) 41 U/L
Alanine aminotransferase (ALT, SGPT) 19 U/L
Alkaline phosphatase 110 U/L
Total bilirubin 0.9 mg/dL
Direct bilirubin 0.2 mg/dL
Albumin 4.1 g/dL
Ultrasonography of the right upper quadrant shows a gallbladder with an air-filled, thickened wall and no stones in the lumen. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 37-year-old woman comes to the physician because of increasing swelling and pain of her right knee for the past month. She has not had any trauma to the knee or previous problems with her joints. She has hypertension. Her only medication is hydrochlorothiazide. She works as a carpet installer. She drinks two to three beers daily. She is 170 cm (5 ft 7 in) tall and weighs 97 kg (214 lb); BMI is 33.6 kg/m2. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 88/min, and blood pressure is 122/82 mm Hg. Examination of the right knee shows swelling and erythema; there is fluctuant edema over the lower part of the patella. The range of flexion is limited because of the pain. The skin over the site of her pain is not warm. There is tenderness on palpation of the patella; there is no joint line tenderness. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
