A 40-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of difficulty walking for the past 4 hours. He first noticed his symptoms after getting up this morning and his foot dragging while walking. He feels tired. He has a history of chronic sinusitis. Six months ago, he was diagnosed with asthma. Current medications include an albuterol inhaler and inhaled corticosteroids. His temperature is 38.9°C (102°F), pulse is 80/min, and his blood pressure is 140/90 mm Hg. Auscultation of his lungs shows diffuse wheezing over bilateral lung fields. Physical examination shows tender subcutaneous nodules on the extensor surfaces of the elbows. There are palpable, non-blanching erythematous lesions on both shins. Dorsiflexion of the right foot is impaired. Sensation to pinprick, light touch, and vibration is decreased over the ulnar aspect of the left forearm. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 11.3 g/dL
Leukocyte count 24,500
Segmented neutrophils 48%
Eosinophils 29%
Lymphocytes 19%
Monocytes 4%
Platelet count 290,000/mm3
Serum
Urea nitrogen 32 mg/dL
Creatinine 1.85 mg/dL
Urine
Blood 2+
Protein 3+
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 50-year-old woman comes to the physician for the evaluation of recurrent episodes of chest pain, difficulty breathing, and rapid heart beating over the past two months. During this period, she has had a 4-kg (8.8-lb) weight loss, malaise, pain in both knees, and diffuse muscle pain. Five years ago, she was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B infection and was started on tenofovir. Her temperature is 38°C (100.4°F), pulse is 110/min, and blood pressure is 150/90 mm Hg. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities except for tachycardia. There are several ulcerations around the ankle and calves bilaterally. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 11 g/dL
Leukocyte count 14,000/mm3
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 80 mm/h
Serum
Perinuclear anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies negative
Hepatitis B surface antigen positive
Urine
Protein +2
RBC 6-7/hpf
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 78-year-old woman comes to the physician for evaluation of progressive hearing loss in both ears over the past year. She has difficulties understanding conversations in crowded places and when more than one person talks at the same time. She has no dizziness, ear discharge, ringing noise, or ear pain. She has a history of hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Medications include enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. Vital signs are within normal limits. Otoscopic examination shows pearly gray, translucent tympanic membranes with a normal light reflex. A vibrating 512 Hz tuning fork is placed on the left mastoid process. Once the patient no longer hears a tone, the fork is held over the ipsilateral ear and the patient reports to hear the tone again. The same test is repeated on the right side with similar results. There is no lateralization when a vibrating 512 Hz tuning fork is placed in the middle of the forehead. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department because he has had abdominal pain and vomiting for the past day. The pain is intermittent, diffuse in nature, and worse after meals. He does not have loose or bloody stools. He has had a nonpruritic rash on his legs and swelling of his ankles for 6 days. He was treated with oral amoxicillin for a sore throat 2 weeks ago. His immunizations are up-to-date. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination of the lower extremities shows non-blanching, raised erythematous papules. The left ankle joint is swollen and warm, and its range of motion is limited by pain. Abdominal examination shows tenderness to palpation in the left lower quadrant without guarding or rebound. Bowel sounds are normal. Test of the stool for occult blood is positive. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL
Leukocyte count
11,800/mm3
Platelet count 431,000/mm3
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 45 mm/h
Serum
Glucose 72 mg/dL
Creatinine 0.9 mg/dL
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 6-month history of tinnitus and progressive hearing loss in the left ear. He has type 2 diabetes mellitus and Raynaud syndrome. His current medications include metformin, nifedipine, and a multivitamin. He appears well. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. A vibrating tuning fork is placed on the left mastoid process. Immediately after the patient does not hear a tone, the tuning fork is held over the left ear and he reports hearing the tuning fork again. The same test is repeated on the right side and shows the same pattern. The vibration tuning fork is then placed on the middle of the forehead and the patient hears the sound louder in the right ear. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his parents because they are concerned with his behavior. He has temper outbursts six or seven times per week, which last anywhere between 5 minutes to half an hour or until he becomes tired. According to his mother, he screams at others and throws things in anger “when things don't go his way.” She says these outbursts started when he was 6 and a half years old and even between the outbursts, he is constantly irritable. He had been suspended from school three times in the past year for physical aggression, but his grades have remained unaffected. He appears agitated and restless. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. During the mental status examination, he is uncooperative and refuses to answer questions. What is the most likely diagnosis in this child?

A 28-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after being involved in a high-speed motor vehicle collision in which he was the unrestrained driver. On arrival, he is semiconscious and incoherent. He has shortness of breath and is cyanotic. His pulse is 112/min, respirations are 59/min, and blood pressure is 128/89 mm Hg. Examination shows a 3-cm (1.2-in) laceration on the forehead and multiple abrasions over the thorax and abdomen. There is crepitation on palpation of the thorax on the right. Auscultation of the lung shows decreased breath sounds on the right side. A crunching sound synchronous with the heartbeat is heard best over the precordium. There is dullness on percussion of the right hemithorax. The lips and tongue have a bluish discoloration. There is an open femur fracture on the left. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Arterial blood gas analysis on room air shows:
pH 7.31
PCO2 55 mm Hg
PO2 42 mm Hg
HCO3- 22 mEq/L
O2 saturation 76%
The patient is intubated and mechanically ventilated. Infusion of 0.9% saline is begun. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old woman comes to the physician because of episodes of watery stools for the past 6 weeks. During this period, she has also had recurrent episodes of reddening of the face, neck, and chest that last up to 30 minutes, especially following alcohol consumption. She has hypertension. She smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 20 years but quit 8 years ago. She drinks two glasses of wine daily. Current medications include enalapril. She appears pale. She is 185 cm (6 ft 1 in) tall and weighs 67 kg (147.7 lb); BMI is 19.6 kg/m2. Her temperature is 36.7°C (98°F), pulse is 85/min, and blood pressure is 130/85 mm Hg. Scattered expiratory wheezing is heard throughout both lung fields. Cardiac examination shows no abnormalities. The abdomen is soft and mildly tender. The remainder of the physical examination shows no abnormalities. A complete blood count and serum concentrations of urea nitrogen and creatinine are within the reference range. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 29-year-old man comes to the physician for the evaluation of progressive loss of vision in his left eye and gradual blurring of vision in his right eye over the past 2 months. He also says that he has had occasional headaches and has noticed a decrease in his sense of smell lately. The patient's only medication is fexofenadine for seasonal allergies. He is 158 cm (5 ft 2 in) tall and weighs 61 kg (135 lbs); BMI is 24.7 kg/m2. Vital signs are within normal limits. Visual acuity is 20/40 in the right eye and there is minimal light perception in the left eye. In the swinging flashlight test, both of his eyes dilate as the light moves from the right to left eye. Fundoscopy shows papilledema in the right optic disc and a pale left optic disc. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 36-year-old man, gravida 1, para 1, has back pain and numbness in his lower extremities after an emergency cesarean delivery of a healthy 3856-g (8-lb, 8-oz) newborn female. He had a placental abruption and lost approximately 2000 ml of blood. During the procedure, he received two units of packed red blood cells and intravenous fluids. He has no history of serious illness and takes no medications. He is sexually active with one female partner, and they use condoms inconsistently. He is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. His temperature is 37.2°C (98.9°F), pulse is 90/min, respirations are 15/min, and blood pressure is 94/58 mm Hg. Examination shows decreased sensation to temperature and pinprick below his waist and 0/5 muscle strength in his lower extremities. He feels the vibrations of a tuning fork placed on both of his great toes. Deep tendon reflexes are absent in the lower extremities and 2+ in the upper extremities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 9-year-old boy is brought to his primary care physician because of a 4-month history of early morning headaches and worsening fatigue. The headaches are often accompanied by nausea and sometimes relieved by vomiting. He stopped going to his ballet lessons 2 weeks ago because he was embarrassed about falling frequently and having increasing difficulty performing the steps. His temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F), pulse is 98/min, and blood pressure is 105/65 mm Hg. He has a broad-based gait. While standing with both feet together and raising his arms, closing his eyes does not affect his balance. He is unable to perform rapid, alternating movements with his hands. An MRI of the brain is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 64-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 7.2-kg (16-lb) weight loss over the past 6 months. For the last 4 weeks, he has also had intermittent constipation and bloating. Four months ago, he spent 2 weeks in Mexico with his son. He has never smoked. He drinks one glass of wine daily. He appears thin. His temperature is 38.3°C (101°F), pulse is 80/min, and blood pressure is 136/78 mm Hg. The lungs are clear to auscultation. The abdomen is distended and the liver is palpable 4 cm below the right costal margin with a hard, mildly tender nodule in the left lobe. Test of the stool for occult blood is positive. Serum studies show:
Alkaline phosphatase 67 U/L
AST 65 U/L
ALT 68 U/L
Hepatitis B surface antigen negative
Hepatitis C antibody negative
A contrast-enhanced CT scan of the abdomen is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 6-month history of muscle weakness. During this period, the patient has had low energy, intermittent nosebleeds, and a 5-kg (11-lb) weight loss. She also reports progressive hearing and vision problems. She has a history of pins-and-needles sensation, numbness, and pain in her feet. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows a palpable liver tip 2–3 cm below the right costal margin. There is nontender lymphadenopathy in the groins, axillae, and neck. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 8.8 g/dL
White blood cells 6,300/mm3
Platelet count 98,000/mm3
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 70 mm/h
Serum
Na+ 136 mmol/L
K+ 3.6 mmol/L
Cr 1.3 mg/dL
Ca2+ 8.6 mg/dL
Aspartate aminotransferase 32 U/L
Alanine aminotransferase 36 U/L
Alkaline phosphatase 100 U/L
Lactate dehydrogenase 120 U/L
A serum protein electrophoresis exhibits a sharp, narrow spike of monoclonal IgM immunoglobulin. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old boy is brought to the physician for pain and increasing swelling over his scalp for 1 month. He has not had any trauma to the area. There is no family or personal history of serious illness. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows a 3-cm solitary, tender mass over the right parietal bone. X-ray of the skull shows a solitary osteolytic lesion. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 10.9 g/dL
Leukocyte count 7300/mm3
Serum
Na+ 136 mEq/L
K+ 3.7 mEq/L
Cl- 103 mEq/L
Ca2+ 9.1 mg/dL
Glucose 71 mg/dL
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 36-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department for right upper quadrant abdominal pain that began 3 days ago. The pain is nonradiating and has no alleviating or exacerbating factors. She denies any nausea or vomiting. She immigrated from Mexico 6 months ago and currently works at a pet shop. She has been healthy except for 1 week of bloody diarrhea 5 months ago. She is 182 cm (5 ft 11 in) tall and weighs 120 kg (264 lb); BMI is 36 kg/m2. Her temperature is 101.8°F (38.8°C), pulse is 85/min, respirations are 14/min, and blood pressure is 120/75 mm Hg. Lungs are clear to auscultation. She has tenderness to palpation in the right upper quadrant. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 11.7 g/dL3
Leukocyte Count 14,000/mm
Segmented neutrophils 74%
Eosinophils 2%
Lymphocytes 17%
Monocytes 7%
Platelet count 140,000/mm3
Serum
Na+ 139 mEq/L
Cl- 101 mEq/L
K+ 4.4 mEq/L
HCO3- 25 mEq/L
Urea nitrogen 8 mg/dL
Creatinine 1.6 mg/dL
Total bilirubin 0.4 mg/dL
AST 76 U/L
ALT 80 U/L
Alkaline phosphatase 103 U/L
Ultrasonography of the abdomen shows a 4-cm round, hypoechoic lesion in the right lobe of the liver with low-level internal echoes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 36-year-old man comes to the physician because of a painless lump on his neck for 3 months that has increased in size. He appears healthy. Examination shows a 2.5-cm (1-in) firm, irregular swelling on the left side of the neck that moves with swallowing. There is painless cervical lymphadenopathy. Ultrasound of the neck shows a solitary left lobe thyroid mass with increased vascularity and hyperechogenic punctate regions. A fine needle aspiration biopsy is scheduled for the following week. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 43-year-old woman comes to the physician for evaluation of a headache she has had for the last 6 months. The patient reports that nothing helps to relieve the headache and that it is more severe in the morning. Throughout the last 2 months, she has been unable to maintain lubrication and states that her sexual desire is low. There is no personal or family history of serious illness. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 80/min, and blood pressure is 150/90 mm Hg. Examination shows an enlarged nose, forehead, and jaw and widened hands, fingers, and feet. Her hands are sweaty. Her serum glucose concentration is 260 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 14-year-old girl is brought to the physician for the evaluation of back pain for the past six months. The pain is worse with exercise and when reclining. She attends high school and is on the swim team. She also states that she lifts weights on a regular basis. She has not had any trauma to the back or any previous problems with her joints. She has no history of serious illness. Her father has a disc herniation. Palpation of the spinous processes at the lumbosacral area shows that two adjacent vertebrae are displaced and are at different levels. Muscle strength is normal. Sensation to pinprick and light touch is intact throughout. When the patient is asked to walk, a waddling gait is noted. Passive raising of either the right or left leg causes pain radiating down the ipsilateral leg. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-week history of abdominal pain, loose, non-bloody stools, and intermittent nausea. She also reports intermittent fever. She has not had vomiting, tenesmus, or rectal pain. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Rectal exam is unremarkable. Laboratory studies show a leukocyte count of 15,200/mm3 and an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 44 mm/h. Test of the stool for occult blood and stool studies for infection are negative. A CT scan of the abdomen shows mural thickening and surrounding fat stranding of discrete regions of the terminal ileum and transverse colon. A colonoscopy is performed and biopsy specimens of the affected areas of the colon are taken. Which of the following findings is most specific for this patient's most likely diagnosis?

A 54-year-old woman comes to the physician for the evaluation of difficulty swallowing of both solids and liquids for 1 month. During the past 5 months, she has also had increased weakness of her hands and legs. She sails regularly and is unable to hold the ropes as tightly as before. Ten years ago, she was involved in a motor vehicle collision. Examination shows atrophy of the tongue. Muscle strength is decreased in the right upper and lower extremities. There is muscle stiffness in the left lower extremity. Deep tendon reflexes are 1+ in the right upper and lower extremities, 3+ in the left upper extremity, and 4+ in the left lower extremity. Plantar reflex shows an extensor response on the left foot. Sensation to light touch, pinprick, and vibration is intact. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 31-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department because of fever and increasing confusion for the past day. She has bipolar disorder with psychotic features and hypothyroidism. Current medications are lithium, haloperidol, and levothyroxine. She drinks one beer with dinner every night. Her speech is confused and she is oriented to person only. Her temperature is 40°C (104°F), pulse is 124/min, and blood pressure is 160/110 mm Hg. She appears acutely ill. Examination shows diaphoresis and muscle rigidity. Deep tendon reflexes are 1+ bilaterally. There is minor rigidity of the neck with full range of motion. Her lungs are clear to auscultation. The abdomen is soft and nontender. Her leukocyte count is 15,100/mm3 and serum creatine kinase activity is 1100 U/L. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old woman comes to the emergency department because of recurrent episodes of fatigue, palpitations, nausea, and diaphoresis over the past 6 months. The episodes have become more frequent in the last 2 weeks and she has missed work several times because of them. Her symptoms usually improve after she drinks some juice and rests. She has had a 2-kg (4.5-lb) weight gain in the past 6 months. She has a history of bipolar disorder, hypertension, and asthma. Her brother has type 2 diabetes mellitus and her father has a history of medullary thyroid carcinoma. Her medications include lithium, hydrochlorothiazide, aspirin, and a budesonide inhaler. Her temperature is 36.3°C (97.3°F), pulse is 92/min and regular, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 118/65 mm Hg. Abdominal examination shows no abnormalities. Serum studies show:
Na+ 145 mEq/L
K+ 3.9 mEq/L
Cl- 103 mEq/L
Calcium 9.2 mg/dL
Glucose 88 mg/dL
Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 5-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his father because of multiple episodes of nausea and vomiting that last about 2 hours. During this period, he has had 6–8 episodes of bilious vomiting and abdominal pain. The vomiting was preceded by fatigue. The boy feels well between these episodes. He has missed several days of school and has been hospitalized 2 times during the past 6 months for dehydration due to similar episodes of vomiting and nausea. The patient has lived with his father since his parents divorced 8 months ago. His immunizations are up-to-date. He is at the 60th percentile for height and 30th percentile for weight. He appears emaciated. His temperature is 36.8°C (98.8°F), pulse is 99/min, and blood pressure is 82/52 mm Hg. Examination shows dry mucous membranes. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Abdominal examination shows a soft abdomen with mild diffuse tenderness with no guarding or rebound. The remainder of the physical examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 13-month-old girl is brought to the physician for the evaluation of rectal bleeding that occurred earlier that morning. The patient has also had several itchy and red skin lesions that started on her scalp and spread downwards. The parents report that their daughter has had six episodes of bilateral otitis media since birth. Her immunizations are up-to-date. She is at the 3rd percentile for height and weight. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows several eczematous lesions over the scalp, neck, and upper and lower extremities, as well as multiple red spots that do not blanch on pressure. The remainder of the physical examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 9.4 g/dL
Leukocyte count 11,500/mm3
Platelet count 30,000/mm3
Prothrombin time 14 sec
Partial thromboplastin time 33 sec
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 2-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his mother after he noticed multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on his abdomen. The child attends daycare three times per week, and this past week one child was reported to have similar lesions. His immunizations are up-to-date. His sister had chickenpox one month ago. He is at the 50th percentile for height and the 60th percentile for weight. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows several skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after being involved in a rear-end collision, in which he was the restrained driver of the back car. On arrival, he is alert and active. He reports pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin. Temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 116/min, respirations are 19/min, and blood pressure is 132/79 mm Hg. Physical examination shows tenderness over both knee caps. The right groin is tender to palpation. The right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 63-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of a 1-day history of progressive blurring and darkening of his vision in the right eye. Upon waking up in the morning, he suddenly started seeing multiple dark streaks. He has migraines and type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed at his last health maintenance examination 20 years ago. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 40 years. His only medication is sumatriptan. His vitals are within normal limits. Ophthalmologic examination shows visual acuity of 20/40 in the left eye and 20/100 in the right eye. The fundus is obscured and difficult to visualize on fundoscopic examination of the right eye. The red reflex is diminished on the right. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her parents for a well-child visit. During her last well-child visit 9 months ago, the patient had not begun talking. The parents report that their daughter frequently avoids eye contact and has no friends at daycare. She was born at term and has been healthy except for an episode of otitis media 6 months ago, which was treated with amoxicillin. Her immunizations are up-to-date. She is at the 95 percentile for height, 20 percentile for weight, and 95 percentile for head circumference. She appears shy. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 120/min, and blood pressure is 100/55 mm Hg. Examination shows elongated facial features and large ears. The patient does not speak. She does not follow instruction to build a stack of 2 blocks. Throughout the examination, she continually opens and closes her mother's purse and does not maintain eye contact. Which of the following findings is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 66-year-old woman comes to the emergency department because of a 1-day history of chest pain, palpitations, and dyspnea on exertion. She had a similar episode 3 days ago and was diagnosed with an inferior wall myocardial infarction. She was admitted and a percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty was successfully done that day. A fractional flow reserve test during the procedure showed complete resolution of the stenosis. Laboratory tests including serum glucose, lipids, and blood count were within normal limits. She was discharged the day after the procedure on a drug regimen of aspirin, simvastatin, and isosorbide dinitrate. At the time of discharge, she had no chest pain or dyspnea. Presently, her vitals are normal and ECG at rest shows new T-wave inversion. Which of the following is the most reliable test for rapidly establishing the diagnosis in this patient?

A 71-year-old woman comes to the physician accompanied by her husband because of a 6-month history of worsening episodic upper abdominal pain and an 8-kg (17.6-lb) weight loss. The pain is dull, nonradiating, worse after eating, and occasionally associated with bloating and diarrhea. Her symptoms have not improved despite 4 weeks of treatment with omeprazole. She attributes her weight loss to recently eating very small portions and avoiding fatty foods. She has hypertension and hypercholesterolemia. She underwent a coronary artery bypass graft operation for coronary artery disease 8 years ago. Current medications include lisinopril, metoprolol, atorvastatin, and aspirin. She has smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for 20 years and drinks 1–2 beers daily. Her pulse is 79/min and blood pressure is 138/89 mm Hg. Examination shows a soft abdomen without tenderness to palpation or guarding. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 53-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department following an episode of loss of consciousness 1 hour ago. She had just finished micturating, when she fell down. Her husband heard the noise and found her unconscious on the floor. She regained consciousness after 30 seconds and was able to talk normally with her husband immediately. There was no urinary incontinence. On arrival, she is alert and oriented. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. Neurologic examination shows no focal findings. Serum concentrations of glucose, creatinine, and electrolytes are within the reference range. An electrocardiogram shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-day history of a swollen right knee. Over the past several weeks, she has had similar episodes affecting the right knee and sometimes also the left elbow, in which the swelling lasted an average of 5 days. She has a history of a rash that subsided 2 months ago. She lives in Connecticut with her husband and works as a landscaper. Her temperature is 37.8°C (100°F), pulse is 90/min, respirations are 12/min, and blood pressure is 110/75 mm Hg. Physical examination shows a tender and warm right knee; range of motion is limited by pain. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Her hematocrit is 44%, leukocyte count is 10,300/mm3, and platelet count is 145,000/mm3. Serum electrolyte concentrations are within normal limits. Arthrocentesis is performed and the synovial fluid is cloudy. Gram stain is negative. Analysis of the synovial fluid shows a leukocyte count of 70,000/mm3 and 80% neutrophils. Serologic testing confirms the diagnosis. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

A 23-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by her boyfriend because of acute agitation and bizarre behavior. The boyfriend reports that, over the past 3 months, the patient has become withdrawn and stopped pursuing hobbies that she used to enjoy. One month ago, she lost her job because she stopped going to work. During this time, she has barely left her apartment because she believes that the FBI is spying on her and controlling her mind. She used to smoke marijuana occasionally in high school but quit 5 years ago. Physical and neurologic examinations show no abnormalities. On mental status examination, she is confused and suspicious with marked psychomotor agitation. Her speech is disorganized and her affect is labile. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old boy is brought to the physician because his mother is concerned about his lack of appetite. He has had a 4-kg (8.8-lb) weight loss over the past 4 months. The patient states that he does not “feel like eating so much”. Over the last year his academic performance in school has decreased and he has had a lot of disputes with his parents concerning his future. His mother says that he has also become more nervous and restless. His grandfather had a problem with his thyroid. He is sexually active with two female partners and uses condoms inconsistently. He is at 60th percentile for height and at 15th percentile for weight. He appears thin. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 104/min, and blood pressure is 135/80 mm Hg. The pupils are 9 mm large, round and minimally reactive to light. Deep tendon reflexes are 2+ bilaterally. There is fine tremor of his hands. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 65-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 8-month history of worsening difficulties swallowing food and retrosternal chest discomfort. He reports that he sometimes has a feeling of “food getting stuck” in his throat and hears a “gurgling sound” from his throat while eating. He says that he occasionally coughs up pieces of undigested food. He has noticed a bad taste in his mouth and bad breath. He has not had fever or weight loss. He has been visiting Mexico every year for the past 7 years. He has Raynaud disease treated with nifedipine. His father died because of gastric cancer. He had smoked one-half pack of cigarettes daily for 20 years but stopped 25 years ago. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. His hemoglobin concentration is 14 g/dL, leukocyte count is 9800/mm3, and platelet count is 215,000/mm3. An ECG shows sinus rhythm with no evidence of ischemia. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 25-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 4-day history of bloody stools. During this time, she has not had nausea, vomiting, abdominal cramps, or pain while defecating. She has had recurrent episodes of non-bloody diarrhea for the past 6 months. Her father died of colon cancer at the age of 39 years. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows small, painless bony swellings on the mandible, forehead, and right shin. There are multiple non-tender, subcutaneous nodules with central black pores present over the trunk and face. Fundoscopic examination shows multiple, oval, darkly pigmented lesions on the retina. Colonoscopy shows approximately 150 colonic polyps. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 64-year-old man comes to the physician because of several episodes of dizziness during the last month. The episodes last between 30–40 seconds and during the episodes he feels as though he is spinning. Episodes usually occur immediately after lying down or suddenly sitting up from a reclined position. They also sometimes happen when he suddenly turns his head to look at something. He has no nausea. Last month, he had an upper respiratory tract infection that resolved spontaneously. He has hypertension treated with hydrochlorothiazide. Otoscopic examination shows no abnormalities. There is no lateralization when a vibrating 512 Hz tuning fork is placed in the middle of the forehead. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 63-year-old woman comes to the physician because of increasing generalized fatigue for 3 months. She is having more difficulty with keeping up with her activities of daily living and has lost 2.5 kg (5.5 lb) over the past month. She has hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She does not smoke and drinks two to three beers on weekends. Her medications include lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, and atorvastatin. Her temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 85/min, respirations are 15/min, and blood pressure is 125/73 mm Hg. Examination shows pale conjunctivae. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Her hematocrit is 27.3%, leukocyte count is 4500/mm3, and platelet count is 102,000/mm3. A peripheral blood smear shows numerous blast cells that stain positive for myeloperoxidase, CD33, and CD34. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old woman comes to the physician because of recurrent episodes of nausea and abdominal discomfort for the past 4 months. The discomfort is located in the upper abdomen and sometimes occurs after eating, especially after a big meal. She has tried to go for a walk after dinner to help with digestion, but her complaints have only increased. For the past 3 weeks she has also had symptoms while climbing the stairs to her apartment. She has type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and stage 2 peripheral arterial disease. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the past 45 years. She drinks one to two beers daily and occasionally more on weekends. Her current medications include metformin, enalapril, and aspirin. She is 168 cm (5 ft 6 in) tall and weighs 126 kg (278 lb); BMI is 45 kg/m2. Her temperature is 36.4°C (97.5°F), pulse is 78/min, and blood pressure is 148/86 mm Hg. On physical examination, the abdomen is soft and nontender with no organomegaly. Foot pulses are absent bilaterally. An ECG shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 13-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of a 1-month history of progressive difficulty breathing through her nose and a 2-week history of recurrent severe nosebleeds. When she holds the right nostril shut, she is unable to breathe nasally and her sense of smell is reduced. She has a 6-year history of asthma, which is well controlled with inhaled albuterol. Vital signs are within normal limits. Nasal inspection shows a pink, lobulated mass filling the left nasal cavity. The septum is deviated to the right side. The mass bleeds on touch. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

An 8-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his parents because of difficulty sleeping. One to two times per week for the past 2 months, he has woken up frightened in the middle of the night, yelling and crying. He has not seemed confused after waking up, and he is consolable and able to fall back asleep in his parents' bed. The following day, he seems more tired than usual at school. He recalls that he had a bad dream and looks for ways to delay bedtime in the evenings. He has met all his developmental milestones to date. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old male college student comes to the physician for a sudden loss of visual acuity of his right eye. He noticed that he was unable to read the time on the alarm clock when he woke up in the morning. When he closes his right eye, he is able to see sharply. When he closes his left eye, he has blurry double vision. He does not recall trauma to his eye but has been working long nights on his honors thesis. He has a history of occasional shoulder luxation. He is 180 cm (5 ft 11 in) tall, and weighs 62 kg (136 lbs); his BMI is 19.1 kg/m2. His vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, slender and long fingers are noted. He has several flat, demarcated brownish nevi on his left cheek. Ocular examination shows upward temporal subluxation of his right lens. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 45-year-old man comes to the physician because of right foot pain for 3 months. He has a burning sensation in the plantar area between the third and fourth metatarsals that radiates to the third and fourth digits. He had a right distal radius fracture that was treated with a splint and physical therapy three months ago. He is an account executive and wears high heels to work every day. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination of the right lower extremity shows intact skin. The posterior tibial and dorsalis pedis pulses are palpable. When pressure is applied to the sole of the foot between the metatarsal heads the patient feels pain and there is an audible click. Tapping on the affected area causes pain that shoots into the third and fourth digits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old woman comes to the physician for the evaluation of recurrent episodes of nosebleeds over the past 6 months. The nosebleeds occur spontaneously and stop after 10 minutes after pinching the nose at the nostrils. She has no history of serious illness except for prolonged bleeding following wisdom teeth extraction 2 years ago. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She takes no medications. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination of the nose shows no abnormalities. There are several bruises on the lower extremities. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 15 g/dL
Leukocyte count 6,000/mm3
Platelet count 220,000/mm3
Bleeding time 9 minutes
Prothrombin time 13 sec
Partial thromboplastin time 55 sec
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 59-year-old woman is brought to the emergency room by her husband. Thirty minutes ago, she was carrying heavy moving boxes from her house to a truck when she felt short of breath and suddenly lost consciousness. Her husband states that she fell to the ground and was unresponsive for 15 seconds before she regained consciousness. She was not confused after this episode. She does not have chest pain. On questioning, she recalls experiencing episodic shortness of breath and chest tightness while playing tennis over the past year. These symptoms resolved with rest. She has no personal history of serious illness and takes no medication. Vital signs are within normal limits. Her temperature is 36.7°C (98°F), heart rate is 95/min and pulse is delayed but regular, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 104/80 mm Hg. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 59-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when he climbs stairs and during the night. He has not had chest pain or palpitations. Eight weeks ago, he had fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion. He has a 10-year history of hypertension. He has smoked half a pack of cigarettes daily for 16 years. His only medication is enalapril. His pulse is 78/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 145/95 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 96%. Diffuse end-expiratory wheezes are heard on pulmonary auscultation. An x-ray of the chest shows no abnormalities. Spirometry shows an FEV1:FVC ratio of 65% and an FEV1 of 60%. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 4-month history of persistent cough productive of white phlegm. She coughs consistently throughout the day, and she has not noticed any particular triggers that make it worse. She has also recently experienced some shortness of breath with exertion. She has not had any weight loss, fever, or chills. She had similar symptoms last year, which lasted about 6 months. She has hypertension, for which she takes amlodipine. She has worked in construction for the past 10 years. She has smoked a pack of cigarettes per day for 30 years. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows an end-expiratory wheeze throughout all lung zones. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 43-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of progressive muscle pain and stiffness that worsens with exercise. He also has difficulty climbing stairs, getting out of chairs, and putting things on shelves or in cupboards. He has had constipation, occasional headaches, and a 9-kg (20-lb) weight gain during the past year. He has hypertension controlled with atenolol and amlodipine. He has used calamine lotion for the past 6 months for dry skin. His pulse is 80/min and his blood pressure is 138/76 mm Hg. Physical examination shows weakness of the proximal muscle groups. He has delayed tendon reflex relaxation, with a mounding of the muscle surface occurring just before relaxation. Creatine kinase level is 3,120 U/L. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 60-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of a slowly enlarging painless ulcer on her lower lip. One year ago she had a painful rash near her upper lip that resolved completely with acyclovir therapy. She has a 10-year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus treated with metformin. She has worked in construction for the past 33 years. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 35 years. Examination shows a 0.5 x 0.5 cm nontender ulcer with everted edges on the midline of her lower lip. The erythematous ulcer bleeds upon palpation. She has numerous moles of varying sizes all over her body. There are no palpable cervical lymph nodes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 13-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of progressive left leg pain for 2 months, which has started to interfere with her sleep. Her father has been giving her ibuprofen at night for “growing pains,” but her symptoms have not improved. One week before the pain started, the patient was hit in the thigh by a baseball, which caused her leg to become red and swollen for several days. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows marked tenderness along the left mid-femur. Her gait is normal. Laboratory studies show a leukocyte count of 21,000/mm3 and an ESR of 68 mm/h. An x-ray of the left lower extremity shows multiple lytic lesions in the middle third of the femur, and the surrounding cortex is covered by several layers of new bone. A biopsy of the left femur shows small round blue cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old woman comes to the physician because of progressive fatigue and lower back pain for the past 4 months. The back pain worsened significantly after she had a minor fall while doing yard work the previous day. For the past year, she has had a feeling of incomplete emptying of her bladder after voiding. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows bilateral paravertebral muscle spasm, severe tenderness over the second lumbar vertebra, and mild tenderness over the lower thoracic vertebrae. Neurologic examination shows no abnormalities. Her hemoglobin is 10.5 g/dl, alkaline phosphatase is 110 U/L, and serum calcium is 11.1 mg/dl. An x-ray of the skull is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 67-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 3-week history of fatigue and worsening back and abdominal pain. During this period, he has also had excessive night sweats and a 4.6-kg (10-lb) weight loss. He has had swelling of the neck for 3 days. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows a 4-cm, supraclavicular, nontender, enlarged and fixed lymph node. The spleen is palpated 2 cm below the left costal margin. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 10.4 g/dL
Mean corpuscular volume 87 μm3
Leukocyte count 5,200/mm3
Platelet count 190,000/mm3
Serum
Lactate dehydrogenase 310 U/L
A CT scan of the thorax and abdomen shows massively enlarged paraaortic, axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Histopathologic examination of an excised cervical lymph node shows lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old man is brought to the emergency department because of sudden loss of vision in his right eye that occurred 50 minutes ago. He does not have eye pain. He had several episodes of loss of vision in the past, but his vision improved following treatment with glucocorticoids. He has coronary artery disease, hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and multiple sclerosis. He underwent a left carotid endarterectomy 3 years ago. He had a myocardial infarction 5 years ago. Current medications include aspirin, metoprolol, lisinopril, atorvastatin, metformin, glipizide, and weekly intramuscular beta-interferon injections. His temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F), pulse is 80/min, and blood pressure is 155/88 mm Hg. Examination shows 20/50 vision in the left eye and no perception of light in the right eye. The direct pupillary reflex is brisk in the left eye and absent in the right eye. The indirect pupillary reflex is brisk in the right eye but absent in the left eye. Intraocular pressure is 18 mm Hg in the right eye and 16 mm Hg in the left eye. A white, 1-mm ring is seen around the circumference of the cornea in both eyes. Fundoscopic examination of the right eye shows a pale, white retina with a bright red area within the macula. The optic disc appears normal. Fundoscopic examination of the left eye shows a few soft and hard exudates in the superior and nasal retinal quadrants. The optic disc and macula appear normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old man comes to the physician because of a progressive swelling in his mouth that he first noticed 5 years ago. Initially, the swelling was asymptomatic but has now caused some difficulty while chewing food for the past month. He has no pain. He has not undergone any dental procedures in the past 5 years. He has bronchial asthma. His only medication is an albuterol inhaler. He appears healthy. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 70/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. Examination shows a 1.5-cm smooth, unilobular, bony hard, nontender mass in the midline of the hard palate. There is no cervical or submandibular lymphadenopathy. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 37-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 15 minutes after falling down a flight of stairs. On arrival, he has shortness of breath, right-sided chest pain, right upper quadrant abdominal pain, and right shoulder pain. He is otherwise healthy. He takes no medications. He appears pale. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 115/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 85/45 mm Hg. Examination shows several ecchymoses over the right chest. There is tenderness to palpation over the right chest wall and right upper quadrant of the abdomen. Bowel sounds are normal. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. Neck veins are flat. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

Three days after undergoing open surgery to repair a bilateral inguinal hernia, a 66-year-old woman has new, intermittent upper abdominal discomfort that worsens when she walks around. She also has new shortness of breath that resolves with rest. There were no complications during surgery or during the immediate postsurgical period. Ambulation was restarted on the first postoperative day. She has type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 25 years. Prior to admission, her medications included metformin, simvastatin, and lisinopril. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 80/min, respirations are 16/min, and blood pressure is 129/80 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 98%. The abdomen is soft and shows two healing surgical scars with moderate serous discharge. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. An ECG at rest shows no abnormalities. Cardiac enzyme levels are within the reference range. An x-ray of the chest and abdominal ultrasonography show no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 46-year-old obese woman comes to the emergency room because of paresthesias in her feet and a hypopigmented skin lesion on her knee that she first noticed 6 weeks ago. She has also had fever, fatigue, and malaise for the last week. She has a history of chronic autoimmune thyroiditis for which she takes levothyroxine. She immigrated from Indonesia 3 years ago to join her family in the United States. Her temperature is 38.7°C (101.7°F) and blood pressure is 122/84 mm Hg. Physical exam shows a well-defined hypopigmented skin lesion approximately 3 cm in diameter over the anterior aspect of the right knee. The area has no hair growth and remains dry although she is diaphoretic. There is diminished sensation to light touch and pinprick in the skin lesion when compared to surrounding skin. There is reduced light touch sensation in the big toes bilaterally. After obtaining a skin biopsy of the lesion to confirm the diagnosis, which of the following is the most appropriate initial pharmacotherapy?

A 23-year-old woman comes to the physician because of lightening of her skin on both hands, under her eyes, and on her neck for 2 years. During this period the lesions slowly grew in size. There is no itchiness or pain. She regularly visits her family in India. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows sharply demarcated, depigmented skin patches on the dorsum of both hands, in the periocular region, and on the neck. Sensation of the skin is intact. The lesions fluorescence blue-white under Wood's lamp. Which of the following findings is most likely to be associated with this patient's diagnosis?

A 71-year-old man comes to his doctor because he is having trouble staying awake in the evening. Over the past year, he has noticed that he gets tired unusually early in the evenings and has trouble staying awake through dinner. He also experiences increased daytime sleepiness, fatigue, and difficulty concentrating. He typically goes to bed around 9 PM and gets out of bed between 2 and 3 AM. He does not have any trouble falling asleep. He takes 30-minute to 1-hour daytime naps approximately 3 times per week. He has no history of severe illness and does not take any medication. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old woman comes to the physician because of worsening abdominal pain over the last several months. She has also had recent feelings of sadness and a lack of motivation at work, where she is employed as a computer programmer. She denies suicidal thoughts. She has a history of multiple kidney stones. She has a family history of thyroid cancer in her father and uncle, who both underwent thyroidectomy before age 30. Her temperature is 37°C (98°F), blood pressure is 138/86 mm Hg, and pulse is 87/min. Physical examination shows diffuse tenderness over the abdomen and obesity but is otherwise unremarkable. Serum studies show:
Na+ 141 mEq/L
K+ 3.6 mEq/L
Glucose 144 mg/dL
Ca2+ 12.1 mg/dL
Albumin 4.1 g/dL
PTH 226 pg/mL (normal range 12–88 pg/mL)
Results of a RET gene test return abnormal. The physician refers her to an endocrine surgeon. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

Three days after undergoing coronary bypass surgery, a 67-year-old woman becomes unresponsive and hypotensive. She is intubated, mechanically ventilated, and a central line is inserted. Vasopressin and noradrenaline infusions are begun. A Foley catheter is placed. Six days later, she has high unrelenting fevers. She is currently receiving noradrenaline via an infusion pump. Her temperature is 39.6° (102.3°F), pulse is 113/min, and blood pressure is 90/50 mm Hg. Examination shows a sternal wound with surrounding erythema; there is no discharge from the wound. Crackles are heard at both lung bases. Cardiac examination shows an S3 gallop. Abdominal examination shows no abnormalities. A Foley catheter is present. Her hemoglobin concentration is 10.8 g/dL, leukocyte count is 21,700/mm3, and platelet count is 165,000/mm3. Samples for blood culture are drawn simultaneously from the central line and peripheral IV line. Blood cultures from the central line show coagulase-negative cocci in clusters on the 8th postoperative day, and those from the peripheral venous line show coagulase-negative cocci in clusters on the 10th postoperative day. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 19-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2 day history of blood-speckled stools and a protruding rectal mass. She has no abdominal pain, altered bowel habits, or fever. Her mother has inflammatory bowel disease. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows multiple, small, hyperpigmented maculae on the lips, buccal mucosa, palms, and soles. The abdomen is soft with no organomegaly. Rectal examination shows a 4-cm pedunculated polyp with superficial excoriations on the mucosa. A colonoscopy shows 14 polyps. A biopsy shows hamartomatous mucosal polyps. This patient's diagnosis is most likely associated with which of the following conditions?

A 32-year-old man comes to the physician because of flank pain, myalgia, and reddish discoloration of his urine for the past 2 days. One week ago, he had a fever and a sore throat and was prescribed antibiotics. He is otherwise healthy and has no history of serious illness. His temperature is 37.9°C (100.2°F), pulse is 70/min, and blood pressure is 128/75 mm Hg. Physical examination shows a soft abdomen and no costovertebral angle tenderness. Examination of the mouth and pharynx shows no abnormalities. There is a faint maculopapular rash over the trunk and extremities. Serum creatinine is 2.4 mg/dL. Urinalysis shows:
Protein 2+
Blood 2+
RBC 20–30/hpf
WBC 12/hpf
Bacteria none
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old woman is brought to the physician for worsening mental status over the past 2 months. Her husband reports she was initially experiencing lapses in memory and over the past 3 weeks she has begun having difficulties performing activities of daily living. Yesterday, she became lost heading to the post office down the street. She has hypertension treated with lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide. Vital signs are within normal limits. She is alert but verbally uncommunicative. Muscle strength is normal. Reflexes are 2+ in bilateral upper and lower extremities. She has diffuse involuntary muscle jerking that can be provoked by loud noises. Mental status examination shows a blunt affect. A complete blood count and serum concentrations of glucose, creatine, and electrolytes are within the reference range. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old man comes to the physician for the evaluation of blindness in his right eye that suddenly started 1 hour ago. He has no feeling of pain, pressure, or sensation of a foreign body in the right eye. He has a history of major depressive disorder treated with fluoxetine. The patient attends college and states that he has had a lot of stress lately due to relationship problems with his partner. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He does not use illicit drugs. He appears anxious. His vital signs are within normal limits. Ophthalmologic examination shows a normal-appearing eye with no redness. Slit lamp examination and fundoscopy show no abnormalities. A visual field test shows nonspecific visual field defects. An MRI of the brain shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 10-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department for the evaluation of one episode of vomiting and severe headache since this morning. Her mother says she also had difficulty getting dressed on her own. She has not had any trauma. The patient appears nervous. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 100/min, and blood pressure is 185/125 mm Hg. She is confused and oriented only to person. Ophthalmic examination shows bilateral optic disc swelling. There is an abdominal bruit that is best heard at the right costovertebral angle. A complete blood count is within normal limits. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 17-year-old boy is brought to the physician for the evaluation of fatigue for the past 6 months. During this period, he has had a 5-kg (11-lbs) weight loss. He states that he has no friends. When he is not in school, he spends most of his time in bed. He has no history of serious illness. His father has major depressive disorder. He appears pale and thin. He is at 25th percentile for height, 10th percentile for weight, and 20th percentile for BMI; his BMI is 19.0. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 65/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. Examination shows dry skin, brittle nails, and calluses on the knuckles. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 12.3 g/dL
Serum
Na+ 133 mEq/L
Cl- 90 mEq/L
K+ 3.2 mEq/L
HCO3- 30 mEq/L
Ca+2 7.8 mg/dL
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old man comes to the physician because he feels sad and has had frequent, brief episodes of crying for the last month. During this period, he sleeps in every morning and spends most of his time in bed playing video games or reading. He has not been spending time with friends but still attends a weekly book club and continues to plan his annual family reunion. He stopped going to the gym, eats more, and has gained 4 kg (8.8 lb) over the past 4 weeks. Three weeks ago, he also started to smoke marijuana a few times a week. He drinks one glass of wine daily and does not smoke cigarettes. He is currently unemployed; he lost his job as a physical therapist 3 months ago. His vital signs are within normal limits. On mental status examination, he is calm, alert, and oriented to person, place, and time. His mood is depressed; his speech is organized, logical, and coherent. He denies suicidal thoughts. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 54-year-old man comes to the physician because of a painful skin lesion on his right leg for 1 month. It initially started out as a small red spot but has rapidly increased in size during this period. He remembers an ant bite on his leg prior to the lesion occurring. He was treated for anterior uveitis 8 months ago with corticosteroids. He has Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension. Current medications include insulin, mesalamine, enalapril, and aspirin. He returned from Wisconsin after visiting his son 2 months ago. His temperature is 37.6°C (98°F), pulse is 98/min, and blood pressure is 126/88 mm Hg. Examination shows pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities. There is a 4-cm tender ulcerative lesion on the anterior right leg with a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders. There are dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs. Femoral and pedal pulses are palpated bilaterally. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of a generalized rash for 3 days. During this period, she has had severe itching and was not able to sleep well. She has also had fever, headache, and some muscle pain. Five days ago, she had a runny nose which subsided with over-the-counter medications. She returned from a camping trip 1 week ago. She attends a daycare center. The patient is at the 55th percentile for height and at the 50th percentile for weight. Her temperature is 38.2°C (100.7°F), pulse is 97/min, and blood pressure is 96/60 mm Hg. Examination of the skin shows several macules, papules, and crusted lesions over her face, trunk, and extremities. There are a few fluid-filled vesicles over her abdomen and back. There is no cervical lymphadenopathy. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of watery discharge from his right eye for 2 weeks. He and his parents, who are refugees from Sudan, arrived in Texas a month ago. His immunization status is not known. He is at the 25th percentile for weight and the 50th percentile for height. His temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), pulse is 90/min, and respirations are 18/min. Examination of the right eye shows matting of the eyelashes. Everting the right eyelid shows hyperemia, follicles, and papillae on the upper tarsal conjunctiva. Slit-lamp examination of the right eye shows follicles in the limbic region and the bulbar conjunctiva. There is corneal haziness with neovascularization at the 12 o'clock position. Examination of the left eye is unremarkable. Direct ophthalmoscopy of both eyes shows no abnormalities. Right pre-auricular lymphadenopathy is present. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 33-year-old woman comes to the emergency department because of repeated episodes of severe headache for the past 3 days. She is currently having her 2nd episode of the day. She usually has her first episode in the mornings. The pain is severe and localized to her right forehead and right eye. She had similar symptoms last summer. She works as an analyst for a large hedge fund management company and spends the majority of her time at the computer. She has been under a lot of stress because of overdue paperwork. She also has chronic shoulder pain. She has been using indomethacin every 6 hours for the pain but has had no relief. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 15 years. She appears restless. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows drooping of the right eyelid, tearing of the right eye, and rhinorrhea. The right pupil is 2 mm and the left pupil is 4 mm. There is localized tenderness to her right supraspinatus muscle. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old-woman is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after being involved in a motorcycle accident. She lost control at high speed and was thrown forward onto the handlebars. On arrival, she is alert and responsive. She has abdominal pain and superficial lacerations on her left arm. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows a tender, erythematous area over her epigastrium. The abdomen is soft and non-distended. A CT scan of the abdomen shows no abnormalities. Treatment with analgesics is begun, the lacerations are cleaned and dressed, and the patient is discharged home after 2 hours of observation. Four days later, the patient returns to the emergency department with gradually worsening upper abdominal pain, fever, poor appetite, and vomiting. Her pulse is 91/min and blood pressure is 135/82 mm Hg. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old woman is brought to the physician by her mother because she is worried about her strange behavior. Over the past 3 years, she has been dressing all in black and wears a long black coat, even in the summer. The mother reports that her daughter has always had difficulties fitting in. She does not have any friends and spends most of her time in her room playing online games. She is anxious at college because she is uncomfortable around other people, and her academic performance is poor. Rather than doing her coursework, she spends most of her time reading up on paranormal phenomena, especially demons. She says that she has never seen any demons, but sometimes there are signs of their presence. For example, a breeze in an enclosed room is likely the “breath of a demon”. Mental status examination shows laborious speech. The patient avoids eye contact. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old woman comes to the emergency department for right wrist pain and swelling 2 hours after falling on an outstretched hand while playing softball. The pain worsened when she attempted to pitch after the fall. She has eczema and type 1 diabetes mellitus. Current medications include insulin and topical clobetasol. She appears uncomfortable. Examination shows multiple lichenified lesions over her forearms. The right wrist is swollen and tender; range of motion is limited by pain. There is tenderness to palpation in the area between the tendons of the abductor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis brevis, and extensor pollicis longus muscle. The thumb can be opposed actively towards the other fingers. Muscle strength of the right hand is decreased. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 39-year-old woman comes to the emergency department because of increasing shortness of breath over the past 3 months. She has been unable to climb the 3 flights of stairs to her apartment. Six years ago, she was diagnosed with HIV. She is currently receiving triple antiretroviral therapy, but she says that she often misses doses. Her temperature is 38.1°C (100.6° F), pulse is 90/min, respirations are 22/min, and blood pressure is 160/70 mm Hg. There is a grade 4/6 holodiastolic murmur heard best at the right sternal border. The pupils are 4 mm, round, and not reactive to light. When a pen tip is advanced closer to the face, the pupils constrict. Extraocular movements are intact. When asked to stand, hold her arms in front of her, and close her eyes, she loses her balance and takes a step backward. An x-ray of the chest shows widening of the mediastinum. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 33-year-old man comes to the physician because of vision impairment in his right eye for the past 2 weeks. During this period, he was unable to distinguish colors with his right eye. He also reports pain with eye movement. He has no double vision. He occasionally has headaches that are relieved by ibuprofen. One year ago, he had a similar episode that affected his left eye and resolved spontaneously. He has no history of serious illness. He works at a library and enjoys reading, even in poor lighting conditions. His vital signs are within normal limits. The pupils are equal, round, and reactive to light and accommodation. Without correction, visual acuity is 20/50 in the left eye, and 20/100 in the right eye. With spectacles, the visual acuity is 20/20 in the left eye and 20/100 in the right eye. Slit lamp examination shows no abnormalities. A CT scan of the head shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 4-month history of intermittent lower abdominal cramps associated with diarrhea, bloating, and mild nausea. During this period, he has had a 5-kg (11-lb) weight loss. He feels like he cannot fully empty his bowels. He has no history of serious illness. He has a high-fiber diet. His father is of Ashkenazi Jewish descent. He appears well. His temperature is 36.9°C (98.5°F), pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 130/90 mm Hg. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Cardiac examination shows no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Abdominal examination shows mild tenderness to palpation in the right lower quadrant without guarding or rebound. Bowel sounds are normal. Test of the stool for occult blood is negative. His hemoglobin concentration is 10.5 g/dL, leukocyte count is 12,000 mm3, platelet count is 480,000 mm3, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate is 129 mm/h. A barium enema shows ulceration and narrowing of the right colon. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 1-year history of intermittent buzzing in both his ears. He says he sometimes has episodes of mild dizziness which resolve spontaneously. He has a 15-year history of type 1 diabetes mellitus and episodes of low back pain. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. Current medications include insulin and aspirin. He works as a trombonist for a symphony orchestra. His vital signs are within normal limits. On otoscopic examination, the tympanic membrane appears normal. Bone conduction is greater than air conduction in both ears. Weber test shows no lateralization. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 43-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department because of severe retrosternal pain radiating to the back and left shoulder for 4 hours. The pain began after attending a farewell party for her coworker at a local bar. She had 3–4 episodes of nonbilious vomiting before the onset of the pain. She has hypertension. Her father died of cardiac arrest at the age of 55 years. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the last 23 years and drinks 2–3 beers daily. Her current medications include amlodipine and valsartan. She appears pale. Her temperature is 37° C (98.6° F), pulse is 115/min, and blood pressure is 90/60 mm Hg. There are decreased breath sounds over the left base and crepitus is palpable over the thorax. Abdominal examination shows tenderness to palpation in the epigastric region; bowel sounds are normal. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 16.5 g/dL
Leukocyte count 11,100/mm3
Serum
Na+ 133 mEq/L
K+ 3.2 mEq/L
Cl- 98 mEq/L
HCO3- 30 mEq/L
Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL
An ECG shows sinus tachycardia with left ventricular hypertrophy. Intravenous fluid resuscitation and antibiotics are begun. Which of the following is the most appropriate test to confirm the diagnosis in this patient?

A 5-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of high-grade fever and generalized fatigue for 5 days. Two days ago, she developed a rash on her trunk. She returned from a family hiking trip to Montana 1 week ago. Her immunization records are unavailable. Her temperature is 39.8°C (103.6°F), pulse is 111/min, and blood pressure is 96/60 mm Hg. Examination shows injection of the conjunctivae bilaterally. The tongue and pharynx are erythematous. Tender cervical lymphadenopathy is present on the left. There is a macular rash over the trunk and extremities. Bilateral knee joints are swollen and tender; range of motion is limited by pain. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old woman comes to the physician for decreased exercise tolerance. Over the past four months, she has noticed progressively worsening shortness of breath while walking her dog. She also becomes short of breath when lying in bed at night. Her temperature is 36.4°C (97.5°F), pulse is 82/min, respirations are 19/min, and blood pressure is 155/53 mm Hg. Cardiac examination shows a high-pitch, decrescendo murmur that occurs immediately after S2 and is heard best along the left sternal border. There is an S3 gallop. Carotid pulses are strong. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old girl is brought to the physician for evaluation of pallor and increasing lethargy for 2 days. One week ago, she experienced abdominal pain, vomiting, and bloody diarrhea that have since subsided. The patient's mother states that they returned early from a 6-week roadtrip in Mexico because of these symptoms. Her parents have been giving her oral rehydration solution. Her immunizations are up-to-date. She appears pale. Her temperature is 38.4°C (101.1°F), pulse is 130/min, respirations are 35/min, and blood pressure is 95/50 mm Hg. Examination shows scleral icterus. The abdomen is soft and nontender; there is no rebound or guarding. Bowel sounds are hyperactive. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 8.5 g/dL
Mean corpuscular volume 94 μm3
Leukocyte count 18,000/mm3
Platelet count 45,000/mm3
Prothrombin time 12 sec
Partial thromboplastin time 34 sec
Serum
Urea nitrogen 28 mg/dL
Creatinine 1.6 mg/dL
Bilirubin
Total 2.5 mg/dL
Direct 0.1 mg/dL
Lactate dehydrogenase 1658 U/L
A blood smear shows schistocytes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old boy is brought to the physician for a well-child examination. He has no history of serious illness. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 95/min, and blood pressure is 96/52 mm Hg. Examination shows a 2/6 continuous, low-pitched murmur over the left upper sternal border that radiates towards the neck. The murmur disappears when he flexes his neck. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old man comes to the physician because of increasing pain in the right hip for 2 months. The pain is intermittent, presenting at the lateral side of the hip and radiating towards the thigh. It is aggravated while climbing stairs or lying on the right side. Two weeks ago, the patient was treated with a course of oral prednisone for exacerbation of asthma. His current medications include formoterol-budesonide and albuterol inhalers. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows tenderness to palpation over the upper lateral part of the right thigh. There is no swelling. The patient is placed in the left lateral decubitus position. Abducting the extended right leg against the physician's resistance reproduces the pain. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. An x-ray of the pelvis shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 39-year-old man comes to the physician for difficulty sleeping and poor concentration at work. He sleeps with the lights turned on and wakes up frequently during the night with palpitations and profuse sweating. Three weeks ago he was sexually assaulted in his car. Since the assault he has avoided using his car and only uses public transportation. He also has nightmares of his attacker. He has been sent home from work for yelling at his coworkers. He has Hashimoto thyroiditis. Current medications include levothyroxine. He has been treated for epididymitis in the past. He has tried alcohol and melatonin to help him sleep. Mental status examination shows a depressed mood and a negative affect. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

Note: I swapped "woman" to "man", "she" to "he", "her" to "his", and "pelvic inflammatory disease" (which is a condition that affects women) to "epididymitis" (which is a condition that affects men).

A 69-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a cough for the past 3 months. The cough is mostly dry, but the patient recalls a recent episode in which she coughed up mucus with dark red streaks. She has felt tired for the past few months. Over the past month, she has had poor appetite and a 5-kg (11-lb) weight loss. She also has occasional back pain, which has worsened in recent weeks. She has no recent travel history. She has smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for 30 years. She does not drink alcohol. Her vitals are within normal limits. Auscultation of the lungs reveals wheezing in the lower right lung field. There is no peripheral lymphadenopathy. The liver is of normal size, and the spleen is not palpable. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin concentration of 13.5 g/dL, serum calcium concentration of 12.3 mg/dL, and a total serum protein of 7.0 g/dL. X-rays of the chest are shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old African American man comes to the physician because of fatigue and muscle weakness for the past 5 weeks. During this period, he has had recurrent headaches and palpitations. He has hypertension and major depressive disorder. He works as a nurse at a local hospital. He has smoked about 6–8 cigarettes daily for the past 10 years and drinks 1–2 glasses of wine on weekends. Current medications include enalapril, metoprolol, and fluoxetine. He is 160 cm (5 ft 6 in) tall and weighs 60 kg (132 lb); BMI is 21.3 kg/m2. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 75/min, and blood pressure is 155/85 mm Hg. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Cardiac examination shows no abnormalities. The abdomen is soft and nontender; bowel sounds are normal. His skin is dry and there is no edema in the lower extremities. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 13.3 g/dL
Serum
Na+ 146 mEq/L
Cl- 105 mEq/L
K+ 3.0 mEq/L
HCO3- 30 mEq/L
Urea nitrogen 10 mg/dL
Glucose 95 mg/dL
Creatinine 0.8 mg/dL
Urine
Blood negative
Glucose negative
Protein negative
RBC 0–1/hpf
WBC none
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 55-year-old woman is brought to the physician because of inappropriate behavior for the past 6 months. She has been making inappropriate comments and jokes while talking to friends and family members. She was arrested 3 weeks ago while trying to kiss strangers on the street. She has no interest in talking to her son or playing with her grandchildren. During this period, she has developed a strong desire for chocolate pudding and potato chips and has gained 10 kg (22 lb). She appears unkempt. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination is unremarkable. Mental status examination shows apathy and a blunt affect. She avoids answering questions and instead comments on the individuals she saw in the waiting room. Mini-Mental State Examination score is 28/30. A complete blood count and serum concentrations of glucose, creatine, and electrolytes are within the reference range. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

One week after undergoing sigmoidectomy with end colostomy for complicated diverticulitis, a 67-year-old woman has upper abdominal pain. During the surgery, she was transfused two units of packed red blood cells. Her postoperative course was uncomplicated. Two days ago, she developed fever. She is currently receiving parenteral nutrition through a central venous catheter. She has type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and hypercholesterolemia. She is oriented to person, but not to place and time. Prior to admission, her medications included metformin, valsartan, aspirin, and atorvastatin. Her temperature is 38.9°C (102.0°F), pulse is 120/min, and blood pressure is 100/60 mmHg. Examination shows jaundice of the conjunctivae. Abdominal examination shows tenderness to palpation in the right upper quadrant. There is no rebound tenderness or guarding; bowel sounds are hypoactive. Laboratory studies show:
Leukocytes 13,500 /mm3
Segmented neutrophils 75 %
Serum
Aspartate aminotransferase 140 IU/L
Alanine aminotransferase 85 IU/L
Alkaline phosphatase 150 IU/L
Bilirubin
Total 2.1 mg/dL
Direct 1.3 mg/dL
Amylase 20 IU/L
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?
