A previously healthy 4-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of blisters and redness on her neck and chest for 2 days. She has also had a fever. She is lethargic and has not eaten well since the rash appeared. She has not had coughing, wheezing, or dysuria. She is an only child and there is no family history of serious illness. Her immunizations are up-to-date. Her temperature is 38.9°C (102°F), pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 80/40 mm Hg. Examination shows flaccid blisters over her neck and trunk that rupture easily. Areas of erythematous moist skin are also noted. Twirling an eraser over the trunk results in a blister. Oropharyngeal examination is normal. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 12 g/dL
Leukocyte count 22,000/mm3
Segmented neutrophils 77%
Eosinophils 3%
Lymphocytes 18%
Monocytes 2%
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 60 mm/h
Urinalysis is normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

Shortly after undergoing a bipolar prosthesis for a displaced femoral neck fracture of the left hip acquired after a fall the day before, an 80-year-old man suddenly develops dyspnea. The surgery under general anesthesia with sevoflurane was uneventful, lasting 98 minutes, during which the patient maintained oxygen saturation readings of 96–100% on 8 L of oxygen. He has a history of hypertension, osteoporosis, and osteoarthritis of his right knee. His medications include ramipril, naproxen, ranitidine, and a multivitamin. He appears cyanotic, drowsy, and is oriented only to person. His temperature is 38.6°C (101.5°F), pulse is 135/minute, respirations are 36/min, and blood pressure is 155/95 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 81%. There are several scattered petechiae on the anterior chest wall. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin concentration of 10.5 g/dL, a leukocyte count of 9,000/mm3, a platelet count of 145,000/mm3, and a creatine kinase of 190 U/L. An ECG shows sinus tachycardia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of pain in his right thumb and wrist that radiates to his elbow. It is worse when he holds his infant daughter and improves with the use of an ice pack. Six months ago, he slipped on a wet floor and fell on his right outstretched hand. His father takes methotrexate for chronic joint pain. The patient takes ibuprofen as needed for his current symptoms. Examination of the right hand shows tenderness over the radial styloid with swelling but no redness. There is no crepitus. Grasping his right thumb and exerting longitudinal traction toward the ulnar side elicits pain. Range of motion of the finger joints is normal. There is no swelling, redness, or tenderness of any other joints. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 64-year-old woman comes to the physician 3 days after noticing a lump in her right groin while she was bathing. She has no history of trauma to the region. She has hypercholesterolemia and hypertension treated with atorvastatin and labetalol. She has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes daily for 35 years. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows a 4-cm (1.6-in), nontender, pulsatile mass with a palpable thrill at the right midinguinal point. On auscultation, a harsh continuous murmur is heard over the mass. Femoral and pedal pulses are palpable bilaterally. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of weakness and fatigue for 2 days. He has also noticed that his urine is darker than usual. For the past week, he has had a persistent non-productive cough and low-grade fever. He has seasonal allergies. He drinks one to two glasses of wine on social occasions and does not smoke. His temperature is 37.9°C (100.2°F), pulse is 88/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 110/76 mm Hg. He has conjunctival pallor and scleral icterus. Cardiopulmonary examination shows bibasilar crackles. The remainder of the physical examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show:
Leukocyte count 8,000/mm3
Hemoglobin 7.1 g/dL
Hematocrit 21%
Platelet count 110,000/mm3
MCV 94 μm3
Serum
Total bilirubin 4.3 mg/dL
Direct 1.1 mg/dL
Indirect 3.2 mg/dL
AST 15 U/L
ALT 17 U/L
LDH 1,251 U/L
Haptoglobin 5.8 mg/dL (N = 41–165)
An x-ray of the chest shows bilateral patchy infiltrates. A peripheral blood smear shows spherocytes. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 16-year-old male high school student is brought to the physician by his parents for his repeated behavioral problems at home and school during the past 10 months. His teachers describe his behavior as uncooperative and disruptive as he persistently refuses to answer questions, insults his teachers, and annoys his classmates on a daily basis. At home, his parents try to address his frequent violations of curfew, but attempts at discussing the issue often result in their son losing his temper and screaming at his parents. His grades have deteriorated over the past year. He has no history of psychiatric illness. On questioning, the patient refuses to answer and frequently disrupts the physician’s conversation with the parents. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 3-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of a 3-day history of a pruritic skin rash on her chest. Her father says that she has no history of dermatological problems. She was born at term and has been healthy except for recurrent episodes of otitis media. Her immunizations are up-to-date. She appears pale. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 110/min, respirations are 26/min, and blood pressure is 102/62 mm Hg. Examination shows vesicles and flaccid bullae with thin brown crusts on the chest. Lateral traction of the surrounding skin leads to sloughing. Examination of the oral mucosa shows no abnormalities. Complete blood count is within the reference range. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by her mother because of a change in her personality. The mother reports that over the past 7 months her daughter has become increasingly withdrawn; she has not answered any phone calls or visited her family and friends. She had always been a quiet girl, who needed some time on her own, but she used to meet with friends at least once a week. The patient says that she cannot leave the house because aliens are watching her and “stealing her thoughts”. She does not drink alcohol. She used to smoke marijuana occasionally but quit 1 year ago. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. On mental status examination, it is impossible to follow the patient's sequence of thoughts. She is anxious and has a flat affect. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department for the evaluation of worsening upper abdominal pain that she first noticed this morning after waking up. The pain is of tearing and burning quality and radiates to her back. Yesterday, she underwent an upper endoscopy and was diagnosed with gastritis and a large hiatal hernia. She has hypertension, hypercholesteremia, and a left bundle branch block that was diagnosed 5 years ago. The patient's mother died of myocardial infarction at the age of 70 years, and her father died of aortic dissection at the age of 65 years. The patient smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the past 40 years, but quit 10 years ago. She drinks three beers daily. Current medications include hydrochlorothiazide, amlodipine, atorvastatin, and pantoprazole. The patient appears to be in mild distress. Her temperature is 37.8°C (100.4°F), pulse is 103/min, and blood pressure is 135/89 mm Hg in the left arm and 132/90 mm Hg in the right arm. Cardiopulmonary examination shows crackling with every heartbeat. Abdominal examination shows tenderness to palpation in the epigastric region; bowel sounds are normal. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 16.0 g/dL
Leukocyte count 11,000/mm3
Na+ 140 mEq/L
K+ 4.2 mEq/L
Cl- 101 mEq/L
HCO3- 25 mEq/L
Creatinine 1.3 mg/dL
Alanine aminotransferase 21 U/L
Aspartate aminotransferase 43 U/L
Lipase 40 U/L (N = 14–280)
Troponin I 0.025 ng/mL (N < 0.1)
Chest x-ray shows a large hiatal hernia and mediastinal lucency. A 12-lead EKG shows sinus tachycardia and a left bundle branch block. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 26-year-old nurse comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of fatigue. He has had a lot of stress at work and has been on sick leave for 2 weeks, but states that he would like to return to work. He has had several episodes of lower abdominal pain. He says, "I know I have cancer." He requests a diagnostic laparoscopy. He was diagnosed with peptic ulcer disease 6 months ago. His only medication is omeprazole. The patient appears pale. His temperature is 36.5° C (97.7° F), pulse is 120/min, and blood pressure is 90/65 mm Hg. On mental status examination he is tired and has a depressed mood. Physical examination shows pale conjunctivae and dry mucous membranes. There are numerous crusts along the course of his left arm veins. A grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur is heard along the right-upper sternal border. Abdominal examination shows no abnormalities. There is generalized weakness of the proximal muscles. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 7.5 g/dL
Mean corpuscular volume 89 μm3
Reticulocyte count 13.3%
Serum
Sodium 139 mEq/L
Potassium 3.9 mEq/L
Calcium 8.5 mg/dL
Test of the stool for occult blood is negative. Abdominal ultrasonography show no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old woman comes to the physician because of progressive fatigue and shortness of breath for 2 months. The dyspnea occurs on moderate exertion and during the night; she sometimes wakes up coughing and “gasping for air.” She has also had several episodes of heart pounding and palpitations. Two weeks ago, she had a runny nose and a productive cough. She has type 2 diabetes mellitus and peripheral arterial disease. She has never smoked. She drinks one to two beers occasionally. She has a history of intravenous illicit drugs use but has not used in over 25 years. Current medications include aspirin, atorvastatin, and metformin. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows bilateral basilar rales. Cardiac auscultation is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old woman is brought to the physician because of increasing pain and swelling of the left knee for 2 months. The pain has awoken her from her sleep on multiple occasions. She tried ibuprofen but has had no relief of her symptoms. There is no family or personal history of serious illness. Vital signs are within normal limits. On examination, the left knee is mildly swollen and tender; range of motion is limited by pain. An x-ray of the left knee is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old man comes to the physician because of 1 week of progressive left anterior knee pain. The pain is worse after sitting for a prolonged period of time and while ascending stairs. He first noticed the pain the day after a basketball game. He has often taken painful blows to the side of the knees while playing basketball but does not recall this having happened in the last game. Four weeks ago, he was diagnosed with a chlamydial urinary tract infection and treated with azithromycin. He is sexually active with one female partner; they use condoms inconsistently. His vital signs are within normal limits. He is 178 cm (5 ft 10 in) tall and weighs 62 kg (137 lb); BMI is 19.6 kg/m2. Physical examination shows tenderness over the left anterior knee that is exacerbated with anterior pressure to the patella when the knee is fully extended; there is no erythema or swelling. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old man comes to the physician for right lower abdominal pain for 6 months. He has multiple non-bloody, watery bowel movements daily and experiences abdominal cramping. Sometimes, he feels sudden palpitations, is short of breath, and his face becomes red. He has lost 7 kg over the past 3 months. He went on a 3-week hiking trip to Cambodia 6 months ago. He has smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for 15 years. His temperature is 37˚C (98.6°F), his pulse is 72/min and his blood pressure is 125/70 mm Hg. On physical examination, tiny blood vessels are noted on his face and arms. Lung auscultation shows bilateral wheezing. The abdomen is soft and nondistended. There is localized tenderness to the right lower quadrant, but no rebound tenderness or guarding. Laboratory studies show:
Leukocyte count 4,600 /mm3
Segmented neutrophils 61 %
Eosinophils 2 %
Platelet count 254,000 /mm3
Hemoglobin 13.1 g/dL
Serum
Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 110 IU/L
Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 128 IU/L
C-reactive protein 8 mg/dL (N = 0–10)
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old man comes to the physician because of an increasingly painful swelling behind his right knee for the past 2 months. During this time, he has also had intermittent low-grade fever and he has been more fatigued than usual. He has not had any trauma to the knee. Over the past year, he has had occasional pain in his hands and wrists bilaterally. He has hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He drinks 1–2 glasses of wine daily and occasionally more on weekends. Current medications include enalapril, metformin, and glimepiride. His mother and older brother have osteoarthritis. He is 165 cm (5 ft 5 in) tall and weighs 68 kg (150 lb); BMI is 25 kg/m2. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows a 3-cm nontender mass in the right popliteal fossa that becomes prominent when the knee is extended. There is mild swelling and redness of his right knee joint. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old woman with asthma comes to the physician because of a 1-month history of progressively worsening shortness of breath and cough. She also has a history of chronic sinusitis and foot drop. Current medications include an albuterol inhaler and inhaled corticosteroid. Physical examination shows diffuse wheezing over both lung fields and tender subcutaneous nodules on both elbows. Laboratory studies show a leukocyte count of 23,000/mm3 with 26% eosinophils and a serum creatinine of 1.7 mg/dL. Urine microscopy shows red blood cell casts. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 69-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of severe right hip pain. The pain is worse at night. She has chronic headaches and back pain for which she takes vitamin D, calcium supplements, and ibuprofen. Examination shows hip tenderness and mild sensorineural hearing loss. X-ray of the hip shows a radiolucent lesion in the ilium with a moth-eaten appearance, wide transition zone, and an aggressive periosteal reaction. Wide excision of the lesion is performed. A photomicrograph of a section of the lesion is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 47-year-old man comes to the physician because of repetitive tongue twisting and abnormal movements of the hands and legs that started several days ago. He has a 2-year history of schizophrenia that has been controlled with fluphenazine. Two weeks ago, he was switched to risperidone. Examination shows protrusion of the tongue and smacking of the lips. He makes twisting movements of the arms and frequently taps his right foot. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 73-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after the sudden onset of right-sided body weakness. Her husband reports that she does not seem to understand simple questions. She has type 2 diabetes mellitus and has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for 45 years. The patient speaks fluently, but she answers questions with nonsensical phrases and cannot repeat single words. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old man is brought to the physician by his wife because of persistent sadness for the past 2 months. During this period, he also has had difficulty sleeping and an increased appetite. He had similar episodes that occurred 2 years ago and 9 months ago that each lasted for 4 months. Between these episodes, he reported feeling very energetic and rested after 3 hours of sleep. He often went for long periods of time without eating. He works as a stock market trader and received a promotion 5 months ago. He regularly attends yoga classes on the weekends with his friends. On mental status examination, he has a blunted affect. He denies suicidal thoughts and illicit drug use. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old man with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus comes to the physician because of increasing shortness of breath and a dry cough over the past 6 months. He has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the past 40 years. Chest auscultation shows scattered expiratory wheezes in both lung fields. Spirometry shows an FEV1:FVC ratio of 65% and an FEV1 of 70% of predicted. His diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) is 42% of predicted. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her father because of a 1-month history of pain in her right leg. Her father has been giving her ketorolac at night to improve her sleep, but the pain has not improved. Physical examination shows marked tenderness along the right mid-femur. An x-ray of the right lower extremity shows several lytic lesions in the diaphysis of the femur and a surrounding cortex covered by several layers of new bone. A biopsy of the right femur shows small round blue cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 2-day history of difficulty sleeping. He worries that the lack of sleep will ruin his career prospects as a model. He has been coming to the physician multiple times over the past year for minor problems. He is dressed very extravagantly and flirts with the receptionist. When he is asked to sit down in the waiting room, he begins to cry and says that no one listens to him. When he is called to the examination room, he moves close to the physician, repeatedly intends to touch her cheek, and makes inappropriate comments. He does not have a history of self-harm or suicidal ideation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 5-day history of swelling in her left arm. Two months ago, she was diagnosed with a deep venous thrombosis in the left calf. She has had a 7-kg (15-lb) weight loss in the last 3 months. She has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the past 25 years. Her only medication is warfarin. Physical examination shows warm edema of the left forearm with overlying erythema and a tender, palpable cord-like structure along the medial arm. Her lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Duplex sonography shows thrombosis of the left basilic and external jugular veins. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to confirm the underlying diagnosis?

A 30-year-old man comes to the physician because of increasing weakness in both legs for 7 days. He also reports a tingling sensation in his legs that is exacerbated by taking a hot shower. He is sexually active with one female partner and does not use condoms. His temperature is 37.8°C (100.1°F). Physical examination shows decreased muscle strength and clonus in both lower extremities. Patellar reflex is 4+ bilaterally and plantar reflex shows an extensor response on both sides. Abdominal reflex is absent. An MRI of the brain is shown. Which of the following findings is most likely to further support the diagnosis in this patient?

A 28-year-old man is brought to a counselor by his father after he found out that he is being physically abused by his wife. The father reports that he refuses to end the relationship with his wife despite the physical abuse. He says that he feels uneasy when his wife is not around. He adds, “I'm worried that if I leave her, my life will only get worse.” He has never been employed since they got married because he is convinced that nobody would hire him. His wife takes care of most household errands and pays all of the bills. Physical examination shows several bruises on the thighs and back. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 52-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 6-month history of shortness of breath and nonproductive cough. She has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for 15 years. Cardiopulmonary examination shows fine inspiratory crackles bilaterally. There is clubbing present in the fingers bilaterally. Pulmonary function tests (PFTs) show an FVC of 78% of expected and an FEV1/FVC ratio of 92%. A CT scan of the chest is shown. Which of the following is the most likely underlying diagnosis?

A previously healthy 75-year-old woman comes to the physician with a 6-month history of fatigue, weight loss, and abdominal pain. She drinks 2 oz of alcohol on the weekends and does not smoke. She is retired but previously worked in a factory that produces plastic pipes. Abdominal examination shows right upper quadrant tenderness; the liver edge is palpable 2 cm below the ribs. A liver biopsy specimen shows pleomorphic spindle cells that express PECAM-1 on their surface. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old girl is brought to the physician for recurrent 3–4 minutes episodes of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. She is nonresponsive during these episodes and does not remember them afterward. She recalls a muddy taste in her mouth before the onset of symptoms. One week ago, her brother witnessed an episode where she woke up, stared, and made hand gestures. After the incident, she felt lethargic and confused. Examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 52-year-old man with HIV infection is brought to the emergency department 20 minutes after he had a generalized tonic-clonic seizure. He appears lethargic and confused. A 35-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of a 3-day history of pain in the left cheek. Which of the following is most likely to help establish the diagnosis?

Physical and neurologic examinations show no abnormalities. On mental status examination, she is confused and suspicious with marked psychomotor agitation. Her speech is disorganized and her affect is labile. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 11-year-old boy comes to the physician with his mother because of a 2-day history of passing “cola-colored“ urine. During the past week, his mother noticed episodes of facial swelling. A 32-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of fatigue, muscle weakness, paresthesias, headache, and palpitations. His pulse is 75/min and blood pressure is 152/94 mm Hg. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Serum studies show:
Sodium 144 mEq/L
Potassium 2.9 mEq/L
Bicarbonate 31 mEq/L
Creatinine 0.7 mg/dL
Further evaluation shows low serum renin activity. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her father because of generalized weakness and difficulty walking for the past month. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin concentration of 6.6 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume of 74 μm3, platelet count of 150,000/mm3, and serum total bilirubin of 2 mg/dl. An MRI of the spine shows low signal intensity in all vertebral bodies and a small epidural mass compressing the spinal canal at the level of L1. A CT scan of the head shows osteopenia with widening of the diploic spaces in the skull. A biopsy of the epidural mass shows erythroid colonies with an abundance of megakaryocytes and myeloid cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 11-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his parents because of a mildly pruritic rash on his trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, he developed a low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache, followed by a facial rash 4 days later. The facial rash did not involve the perioral skin. His temperature is 37.4°C (99.3°F). A photograph of the rash on his lower arms is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of a 12-hour history of a severe headache. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. His blood pressure at admission is 180/125 mm Hg. Physical examination shows a bruit in the epigastric region. Fundoscopy shows bilateral optic disc swelling. Which of the following investigations is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 58-year-old white woman with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of a painless lesion on her lower lip. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 20 years. She has worked as a fruit picker for the past 25 years. Her current medications include captopril and metformin. Examination of the oral cavity shows a single ulcer near the vermillion border. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 21-year-old woman comes to the physician because of nervousness and difficulty sleeping over the past 2 weeks. Three months ago, she started a new team project at her job. She says that she has trouble falling asleep at night because she thinks about the project. She insists on checking the work of her teammates and spends several hours each week making elaborate lists and schedules. She refuses to let others take on more tasks because she thinks that only she can complete them satisfactorily. The project deadline has already been postponed once. She says, “My teammates never understand how important it is to do things the right way.” Ever since high school, she has used the majority of her time to plan out assignments and does not have time to regularly participate in social activities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An otherwise healthy 25-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of intermittent palpitations and worsening shortness of breath on exertion. She has not had chest pain or nocturnal dyspnea. The patient is 195 cm (6 ft 5 in) tall and weighs 70 kg (154 lbs); BMI is 18.4 kg/m2. Her pulse is 110/min and blood pressure is 140/60 mm Hg. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Cardiac examination is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 31-year-old woman comes to the emergency department because of chest pain for the last 3 hours. She describes the pain as a sharp, substernal chest pain that radiates to the right shoulder; she says “Please help me. I'm having a heart attack.” She has been admitted to the hospital twice over the past week for evaluation of shortness of breath and abdominal pain but left the hospital the following day on both occasions. The patient does not smoke or drink alcohol but is a known user of intravenous heroin. She has been living in a homeless shelter for the past 2 weeks after being evicted from her apartment for failure to pay rent. Her temperature is 37.6°C (99.6°F), pulse is 90/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 125/85 mm Hg. The patient seems anxious and refuses a physical examination of her chest. Her cardiac troponin I concentration is 0.01 ng/mL (N = 0–0.01). An ECG shows a normal sinus rhythm with nonspecific ST-T wave changes. While the physician is planning to discharge the patient, the patient reports numbness in her arm and insists on being admitted to the ward. On the following day, the patient leaves the hospital without informing the physician or the nursing staff. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by his neighbors 30 minutes after they found him unconscious in his yard. His neighbors report that he has been spending more time at home by himself because he recently lost his job. On arrival, he is unable to provide a history. He appears anxious. His pulse is 76/min, respirations are 13/min, and blood pressure is 114/72 mm Hg. Examination shows significant weakness of the left upper and lower extremities. He is unable to plantarflex the ankle while supine. He is able to stand on his toes. His gait is unsteady. Deep tendon reflexes are 3+ and symmetric. A CT scan of the head shows no abnormalities. An MRI of the brain and MR angiography show no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department by her father because of a sudden loss of consciousness. She has asthma and has been hospitalized multiple times. Her father has type 2 diabetes mellitus. She is somnolent and diaphoretic. Serum studies show a glucose concentration of 22 mg/dL and a potassium concentration of 2.4 mEq/L. A dextrose infusion is administered, after which her glucose concentration normalizes and her symptoms improve. She is admitted to the hospital for further observation. Overnight, she has another episode of decreased consciousness. Serum studies taken during the episode show a glucose concentration of 19 mg/dL, an insulin concentration of 108 mIU/L (N=2.6–24.9), and a C-peptide concentration of 0.3 ng/mL (N = 0.8–3.1). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 64-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department because of a 2-hour history of nausea, vomiting, and retrosternal pain that radiates to the back. Abdominal examination shows tenderness to palpation in the epigastric area. A CT scan of the patient's chest is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old woman comes to the physician because of an episode of bloody vomiting this morning and a 1-week history of burning upper abdominal pain. Two weeks ago, she sustained a head injury and was in a coma for 3 days. An endoscopy shows multiple, shallow hemorrhagic lesions predominantly in the gastric fundus and greater curvature. Biopsies show patchy loss of epithelium and an acute inflammatory infiltrate in the lamina propria that does not extend beyond the muscularis mucosa. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of dizziness, nausea, and vomiting for 4 days. His temperature is 37.3°C (99.1°F), pulse is 100/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Arterial blood gas analysis on room air shows:
pH 7.58
PCO2 43 mm Hg
PO2 96 mm Hg
HCO3- 32 mEq/L
The most appropriate next step in diagnosis is measurement of which of the following?

A 55-year-old woman comes to the physician because of fatigue and worsening abdominal pain for 4 weeks. She also reports excessive night sweats and a 5.4-kg (12-lb) weight loss during this time. She has a neck swelling for 4 days. Physical examination shows a nontender, enlarged, and fixed supraclavicular lymph node. There is splenomegaly. A CT scan of the thorax and abdomen shows massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Analysis of an excised cervical lymph node shows lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 47-year-old man comes to the physician because of body aches for the past 9 months. He also has stiffness of the shoulders and knees that is worse in the morning and tingling in the upper extremities. Examination shows marked tenderness over the posterior neck, bilateral mid trapezius, and medial aspect of the left knee. A complete blood count and erythrocyte sedimentation rate are within the reference ranges. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae and then spread to his trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, he was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and was started on amoxicillin. He has no history of adverse drug reactions and immunizations are up-to-date. His temperature is 37.5°C (99.5°F), pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. Physical examination shows periorbital edema and multiple erythematous, annular plaques of variable sizes over his entire body. One of the lesions in the right popliteal fossa has an area of central clearing and the patient's father reports that it has been present for over 24 hours. Urinalysis is normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 5-month history of a pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. He has no history of serious illness and takes no medications. A skin biopsy of the rash shows intraepidermal accumulation of edematous fluid and widening of intercellular spaces between keratinocytes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 71-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 4-month history of worsening cough and a 4.5-kg (10-lb) weight loss. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 35 years. Physical examination shows wheezing over the right lung fields. Laboratory studies show a serum calcium concentration of 12.5 mg/dL. X-rays of the chest are shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a progressive swelling and pain in her right ring finger for the past 2 days. The pain began while playing football, when her finger got caught in the jersey of another player who forcefully pulled away. Examination shows that the right ring finger is extended. There is pain and swelling at the distal interphalangeal joint. When the patient is asked to make a fist, her right ring finger does not flex at the distal interphalangeal joint. There is no joint laxity. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 69-year-old white woman comes to the physician because of a 15-day history of fatigue and lower leg swelling. Over the past 8 months, she has had a 3.8-kg (8.3-lb) weight loss. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 48 years. Vital signs are within normal limits. She appears thin. Examination shows 2+ pretibial edema bilaterally. An x-ray of the chest shows a right upper lobe density. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 11.3 g/dL
Leukocyte count 8600/mm3
Platelet count 140,000/mm3
Serum
Urea nitrogen 25 mg/dL
Glucose 79 mg/dL
Creatinine 1.7 mg/dL
Albumin 1.6 mg/dL
Total cholesterol 479 mg/dL
Urine
Blood negative
Glucose negative
Protein 4+
WBC 0–1/hpf
Fatty casts numerous
Light microscopic examination of a kidney biopsy reveals thickening of glomerular capillary loops and the basal membrane. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 49-year-old man comes to the physician with a 2-month history of mild abdominal pain, nausea, and several episodes of vomiting. He often feels full after eating only a small amount of food. Abdominal examination shows mild right upper quadrant tenderness and a liver span of 16 cm. Ultrasonography shows a 5 x 4 cm hyperechoic mass in the left lobe of the liver. The mass is surgically excised. A photomicrograph of the resected specimen is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-month-old girl is brought to the emergency department by her father because of an 8-hour history of difficulty feeding and decreased arousability. Her father says that the symptoms began after she rolled over and fell from the bed. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows regions of purple discoloration in the T4–T10 dermatomes bilaterally and tense fontanelles. Fundoscopy shows bilateral optic disc swelling with dot-and-blot hemorrhages extending to the ora serrata. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

Three days after undergoing laparoscopic colectomy, a 67-year-old woman reports swelling and pain in her right leg. She was diagnosed with colon cancer 1 month ago. Her temperature is 38.5°C (101.3°F). Physical examination shows swelling of the right leg from the ankle to the thigh. There is no erythema or rash. Which of the following is likely to be most helpful in establishing the diagnosis?

A previously healthy 25-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 3-week history of fever, recurrent headaches, and anorexia. One month ago, he returned from a camping trip in Chile. His temperature is 39.3°C (102.8°F). Examination shows a swelling in the left periorbital region and axillary, cervical, and inguinal lymphadenopathy. A blood sample is obtained. Processing of the sample with which of the following methods is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A previously healthy 4-year-old boy is brought to the physician for evaluation of a 3-week history of recurrent vomiting and difficulty walking. Examination shows a broad-based gait and bilateral optic disc swelling. An MRI shows an intracranial tumor. A ventriculoperitoneal shunt is placed, and surgical excision of the tumor is performed. A photomicrograph of a section of the tumor is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 1-month history of double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and weakness when trying to brush his hair. He reports that these symptoms are worse after he exercises and disappear after he rests for a few hours. Physical examination shows drooping of his right upper eyelid that worsens when the patient is asked to gaze at the ceiling for 2 minutes. There is diminished motor strength in the upper extremities. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 13-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of a 4-month history of worsening dizziness, nausea, and feeling clumsy. An MRI of the brain shows a well-demarcated, 4-cm cystic mass in the posterior fossa. The patient undergoes complete surgical resection of the mass. Pathologic examination of the surgical specimen shows parallel bundles of cells with eosinophilic, corkscrew-like processes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 69-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 3-week history of headache and worsening vision. Ophthalmologic examination shows a visual acuity of 20/120 in the right eye and 20/80 in the left eye. Physical examination shows no other abnormalities. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin of 14.2 g/dL and total serum calcium of 9.9 mg/dL. A photomicrograph of a peripheral blood smear is shown. Serum electrophoresis shows increased concentration of a pentameric immunoglobulin. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old man is brought to the physician by his mother because she has been worried about her son's strange behavior for the past 2 years. He does not have any friends and spends most of his time alone in his room. He usually wears a long, black, hooded cloak. He is anxious at college because he is uncomfortable around other people, and his academic performance is poor. He collects rare crystals and says that they support his “sixth sense.” Mental status examination shows slow, hesitant speech, and he avoids eye contact. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 18-month-old girl is brought to the physician by her father because of a 2-day history of fever and a pruritic rash that started on her trunk and then progressed to her face and extremities. She has not received any childhood vaccinations because her parents believe that they are dangerous. Her temperature is 38.0°C (100.4°F). A photograph of the rash is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by ambulance 30 minutes after his neighbor found him unconscious on a running trail. His neighbor reports that he has been training for a marathon since the beginning of the summer. He is alert and oriented but becomes irritable when realizing that he is at a hospital and refuses to answer questions. He appears tired. He is 174 cm (5 ft 7 in) tall and weighs 51 kg (112 lb). His temperature is 35.5°C (96°F), pulse is 44/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 84/48 mm Hg. Examination shows dry, scaly skin and dry mucous membranes. Cardiopulmonary examination shows a high-frequency, mid-to-late systolic murmur that is heard best at the apex. His hemoglobin concentration is 11.9 g/dL. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 2-year-old girl is brought to the emergency room by her father because of persistent crying and refusal to move her right arm. The episode began 30 minutes ago after the father lifted her up by the arms. She appears distressed and is inconsolable. On examination, her right arm is held close to her body in a flexed and pronated position. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An otherwise healthy 45-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 1-year history of episodic abdominal cramps, bloating, and flatulence. The symptoms worsen when he has pizza or ice cream and have become more frequent over the past 4 months. Lactose intolerance is suspected. Which of the following findings would most strongly support the diagnosis of lactose intolerance?

A 38-year-old woman comes to the physician because of persistent sadness and difficulty concentrating for the past 6 weeks. During this period, she has also had difficulty sleeping. She adds that she has been “feeling down” most of the time since her boyfriend broke up with her 4 years ago. Since then, she has only had a few periods of time when she did not feel that way, but none of these lasted for more than a month. She reports having no problems with appetite, weight, or energy. She does not use illicit drugs or alcohol. Mental status examination shows a depressed mood and constricted affect. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old woman comes to the physician with a 3-month history of right flank pain. Urinalysis shows 60 RBC/hpf. Renal ultrasound shows a 3 cm, well-defined mass in the upper pole of the right kidney. A photomicrograph of a section of the resected mass is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her father because of painless lesions on her face that she has had since shortly after birth. They recently moved to the USA from Indonesia where they had limited access to healthcare. A photograph of the lesions is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 16-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her host parents for evaluation of a progressively pruritic rash over her shoulders and buttocks for the past 6 months. She recently came to the United States from Nigeria to attend a year of high school. She reports that it has been increasingly difficult for her to read the whiteboard during classes. Physical examination shows symmetrically distributed papules 4–8 mm in diameter, excoriation marks, and patchy hyperpigmentation over her shoulders, waist, and buttocks. There is nontender inguinal lymphadenopathy and several firm, nontender subcutaneous nodules along the right iliac crest. Six skin snip biopsies are taken from the pelvic girdle, buttocks, and thigh, and are then incubated in saline. After 24 hours, microscopic examination shows motile microfilariae. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old woman comes to the physician because of fatigue and a 5-kg (11-lb) weight loss over the past 6 months despite a good appetite. She takes no medications. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs. Physical examination shows hepatosplenomegaly and diffuse, nontender lymphadenopathy. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin concentration of 11 g/dL and a leukocyte count of 16,000/mm3. A direct antiglobulin (Coombs) test is positive. A photomicrograph of a peripheral blood smear is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old boy is brought to the physician for intermittent fevers and painful swelling of the left ankle for 2 weeks. He has no history of trauma to the ankle. He has a history of sickle cell disease. Current medications include hydroxyurea and acetaminophen for pain. His temperature is 38.4°C (101.2°F) and pulse is 112/min. Examination shows a tender, swollen, and erythematous left ankle with point tenderness over the medial malleolus. A bone biopsy culture confirms the diagnosis. Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?

A 38-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of progressive headache, blurry vision, and nausea for 1 day. Four days ago, he was diagnosed with a right middle ear infection. He appears lethargic. His temperature is 39.1°C (102.3°F), and blood pressure is 148/95 mm Hg. Ophthalmologic examination shows bilateral swelling of the optic disc. The corneal reflex in the right eye is absent. Sensation to touch is reduced on the upper right side of the face. Serum studies show increased concentrations of fibrin degradation products. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old boy who emigrated from Pakistan 2 weeks ago is brought to the emergency department because of lower limb weakness for one-day. One week ago, he had a 3-day episode of flu-like symptoms that resolved without treatment. He has not yet received any routine childhood vaccinations. Deep tendon reflexes are 1+ in the right lower extremity and absent in the left lower extremity. Analysis of cerebrospinal fluid shows a leukocyte count of 38 cells/mm3 (68% lymphocytes), a protein concentration of 49 mg/dL, and a glucose concentration of 60 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 66-year-old woman comes to the physician for a follow-up examination after a below-knee amputation of the right lower leg. Three weeks ago, she had an acute arterial embolism that could not be revascularized in time to save the leg. She now reports episodic hot, shooting, and tingling pain in the right lower leg that began shortly after the amputation. She has type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the past 30 years. Her current medications are metformin and prophylactic subcutaneous heparin. Her temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 78/min, and blood pressure is 135/88 mm Hg. Physical examination shows a slightly erythematous stump with clean sutures. The skin overlying the stump is warm and well-perfused. Muscle strength and sensation are normal throughout the remaining extremity and the left lower extremity. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 16-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his father because of concerns about his behavior during the past 2 years. He does not have friends and spends most of the time reading by himself. His father says that he comes up with excuses to avoid family dinners and other social events. He states that he likes reading and feels more comfortable on his own. On mental status examination, his thought process is organized and logical. His affect is flat. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old woman comes to the physician because of progressive swelling of the left lower leg for 4 months. One year ago, she had an episode of intermittent fever and tender lymphadenopathy that occurred shortly after she returned from a trip to India and resolved spontaneously. Physical examination shows 4+ nonpitting edema of the left lower leg. Her leukocyte count is 8,000/mm3 with 25% eosinophils. A blood smear obtained at night confirms the diagnosis. Treatment with diethylcarbamazine is initiated. Which of the following is the most likely route of transmission of the causal pathogen?

A 62-year-old man is brought to the physician because of 6 months of progressive weakness in his arms and legs. During this time, he has also had difficulty swallowing and holding his head up. Examination shows pooling of oral secretions. Muscle strength and tone are decreased in the upper extremities. Deep tendon reflexes are 1+ in the right upper and lower extremities, 3+ in the left upper extremity, and 4+ in the left lower extremity. Sensation to light touch, pinprick, and vibration are intact. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 56-year-old woman comes to the physician for a follow-up examination one week after a chest x-ray showed a solitary pulmonary nodule. She has no history of major medical illness. She has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the past 30 years. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. A tuberculin skin test is negative. A CT scan of the chest shows a 2.1-cm well-circumscribed, calcified nodule in the periphery of the right lower lung field. A CT-guided biopsy of the lesion is performed. Histological examination of the biopsy specimen shows regions of disorganized hyaline cartilage interspersed with myxoid regions and clefts of ciliated epithelium. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 81-year-old woman is brought to the physician by her son after she was found wandering on the street. For the last 3 months, she often has a blank stare for several minutes. She also claims to have seen strangers in the house on several occasions who were not present. She has hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and was diagnosed with Parkinson disease 8 months ago. Her current medications include carbidopa-levodopa, hydrochlorothiazide, and atorvastatin. Her blood pressure is 150/85 mm Hg. She has short-term memory deficits and appears confused and disheveled. Examination shows bilateral muscle rigidity and resting tremor in her upper extremities. She has a slow gait with short steps. Microscopic examination of the cortex of a patient with the same condition is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 61-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of intermittent fever, easy fatiguability, and a 4.4-kg (9.7-lb) weight loss. Physical examination shows conjunctival pallor. The spleen is palpated 5 cm below the left costal margin. Laboratory studies show a leukocyte count of 75,300/mm3 with increased basophils, a platelet count of 455,000/mm3, and a decreased leukocyte alkaline phosphatase score. A peripheral blood smear shows increased numbers of promyelocytes, myelocytes, and metamyelocytes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 59-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after having a seizure. Her husband reports that the patient has been having recurrent headaches and has become increasingly irritable over the past 3 months. Physical examination shows a spastic paresis of the right lower extremity. The Babinski sign is present on the right side. An MRI of the brain is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of fatigue, weight loss, and multiple painless swellings on her neck and axilla. She reports that her swellings become painful after she drinks alcohol. Physical examination shows nontender cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy. A lymph node biopsy specimen shows giant binucleate cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her father for the evaluation of abdominal pain and trouble sleeping for the past 6 months. Her father says she complains of crampy abdominal pain every morning on school days. She started attending a new school 7 months ago and he is concerned because she has missed school frequently due to the abdominal pain. She also has trouble falling asleep at night and asks to sleep in the same room with her parents every night. She has not had fever, vomiting, diarrhea, or weight loss. She sits very close to her father and starts to cry when he steps out of the room to take a phone call. Abdominal examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-week history of productive cough, fever, and lethargy. She also has several skin lesions over her body. Her symptoms began 3 weeks after she returned from a camping trip in Kentucky. Three years ago, she underwent kidney transplantation for polycystic kidney disease. Current medications include sirolimus and prednisone. Her temperature is 38°C (100.4°F). Diffuse crackles are heard over the lung fields. There are 4 white, verrucous skin patches over her chest and upper limbs. A photomicrograph of a skin biopsy specimen from one of the lesions is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 61-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of a cough productive of clear mucoid sputum. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 33 years. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Chest x-ray shows a 2-cm solid nodule in the periphery of the lower left lobe. A bronchial biopsy of the mass shows numerous mucin-filled epithelial cells lining the alveolar basement membrane. The cells have prominent nucleoli, coarse chromatin, and some cells have multiple nuclei. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her father because she claims to have spoken to her recently-deceased grandmother. The grandmother, who lived with the family and frequently watched the girl for her parents, died 2 months ago. The girl was taken out of preschool for 3 days after her grandmother's death but has since returned. Her teachers report that the girl is currently doing well, completing her assignments, and engaging in play with other children. When asked about how she feels, the girl becomes tearful and says, “I miss my grandma. I sometimes talk to her when my dad is not around.” Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old female presents to her primary care physician after an injury during a rugby game. The patient states that she was tackled and ever since then has had pain in her knee. The patient has tried NSAIDs and ice to no avail. The patient has no past medical history and is currently taking a multivitamin, fish oil, and a whey protein supplement. On physical exam you note a knee that is heavily bruised. It is painful for the patient to bear weight on the knee, and passive motion of the knee elicits some pain. There is laxity at the knee to varus stress. The patient is wondering when she can return to athletics. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old man presents to clinic in emotional distress. He states he has been unhappy for the past couple of months and is having problems with his sleep and appetite. Additionally, he reports significant anxiety regarding thoughts of dirtiness around the house. He states that he cleans all of the doorknobs 5-10 times per day and that, despite his actions, the stress related to cleaning is becoming worse. What is this patient's diagnosis?

A 17-year-old female presents to the emergency department for eye pain. The patient states that she has had left eye pain for the past week that has been steadily worsening. The patient denies any changes to her vision, trouble moving her left eye, or recent trauma. The patient smokes one pack of cigarettes a day, drinks alcohol socially, and has had unprotected sex with two females and four males this past month. Her current medications include loratadine, nasal saline spray, and diphenhydramine. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 100/55 mmHg, pulse is 72/min, respirations are 11/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. On physical exam, you note a healthy young woman. Cardiopulmonary exam is within normal limits. Her physical exam reveals the finding in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old woman comes into your office for an eye exam. The patient states she has had some trouble seeing over the last few weeks. She denies a history of pain. She has a history of HIV. She states that she was diagnosed with HIV about 20 years ago due to her intravenous drug usage. She has not used any drugs in the past 10 years, but states she also does not take her medications. Her last CD4+ count (6 months ago) was 42. Her vitals are normal and Figure A shows her fundoscopic exam. On eye exam, the patient has both some central and peripheral vision loss. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old woman is brought to the emergency room by her husband because she has been acting confused for the past day. She is febrile, with an oral temperature of 103.6 deg F; vital signs are otherwise stable. Her physical exam is significant for the finding shown in Figure A; she has never noticed lesions like these before. She also has subtle right-sided weakness affecting upper and lower extremities. Labs reveal: hemoglobin 7.0 g/dL, hematocrit 21%, white blood count of 10.2 x 10^3 µL, and platelet count of 20 x 10^3 per µL. PT/INR and PTT are normal. A peripheral blood smear is shown in Figure B. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A mother brings her 4-year-old daughter to her pediatrician. Over the last eight months, her daughter has been exhibiting several "odd" behaviors. Most importantly, she repeatedly says that she is playing games with a friend named "Steven," though she is certain that he does not exist. She has often found her acting out magical scenarios as though someone else is present, when no one is there. What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 25-year-old female patient presents to your clinic in significant distress. She states she has excruciating, stabbing pain around the left side of her head, and her left eye will not stop tearing. These types of headaches have been occurring for the past week every morning when she awakens and last around 60 minutes. She denies any aura, nausea, or vomiting. She denies any other past medical history. What is this patient's diagnosis?

A 22-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician with itchy eyes. The patient recently moved to the northern US and states that she has experienced bilateral itching and watering of her eyes. She states that it is very distracting and is making it hard for her to work. The patient denies any recent sick contacts and lives alone. She works as a machinist and is currently struggling with her finances. The patient has a past medical history of asthma, and her current medications include albuterol, fluticasone, fish oil, and whey protein supplements. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 100/65 mmHg, pulse is 60/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Cardiopulmonary exam is within normal limits. You notice the bilateral findings seen in Figure A. Otoscopy reveals bilateral clear tympanic membranes. The rest of the patient's physical exam is within normal limits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 52-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician. The woman has been feeling very tired lately and thinks that she looks more pale. The physician orders a complete blood count, which shows: Hgb 8.5 g/dL; WBC 1,200/microliter; platelets 70,000/microliter. The patient is referred for bone marrow biopsy, which shows the findings in Figure A. Which of the following is the correct diagnosis?

A 68-year-old woman presents with a 6-month history of worsening fatigue and weight loss. She is especially concerned about a recent episode in which she noticed a blurring of her vision and headache; she also notes that her “memory is not as good as it used to be,” which her husband confirms. Physical exam is notable only for pallor and general weakness. Laboratory studies reveal anemia as well as an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate. Serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP) reveals a sharp, narrow spike of monoclonal IgM; serum IgM concentration is 6.3 g/dL. What is the most likely diagnosis in this case?

A 45-year-old non-English-speaking, Asian female presents to your office. She shows you a lesion on her elbow (Figure A). She has been having decreased sensation in that area and now cannot feel sharp pinpricks on your physical exam. The lesion is biopsied (Figure B). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old woman with a history of chronic kidney disease presents to her primary care physician complaining of recurrent chest pain with activity. The patient used to have chest pain when she mowed her lawn. Now she gets chest pain whenever she walks short distances such as to get her mail. The pain resolves on its own when the patient sits and rests. Her temperature is 98.2°F (36.8°C), blood pressure is 157/98 mm Hg, pulse is 80/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for an obese woman who is in no distress. An initial ECG is unchanged from a previous ECG. The patient's first troponin is 0.06 ng/mL which is unchanged from previous troponins. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old African American girl is brought into the emergency department by her father. The father states that the girl was diagnosed with a urinary tract infection by her PCP and provided with medications a few days ago. Today, she started having abdominal pain and shortness of breath. On exam, the patient has normal vitals, but has mild jaundice and states that she is short of breath. Her father states that his sister had had a similar episode when she was treated for malaria. The child's CBC is significant for a hemoglobin of 8.7 and her MCV is 90. Figure A shows the peripheral smear. Coombs test is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old girl is brought to the pediatrician by her father for complaints of a diffuse, itchy rash over her abdomen, back, and upper legs. The rash first appeared about 1 week ago. She has otherwise been well, and she has no known sick contacts. On exam she is afebrile and cooperative. Her skin exam (Figure A) is notable for a single large, well-circumscribed pink plaque over her mid-abdomen, and many pink papules of varying sizes over her abdomen, back, and thighs. On follow-up a month later, the rash has largely resolved without intervention. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old man presents to the emergency department complaining of ear pain. He states it started a few days ago and it has been gradually worsening. He also endorses subjective fevers and neck stiffness. The patient is an adamant swimmer and swims 2-3 times per day. He has a history of diabetes, hypertension, and morbid obesity. His temperature is 103°F (39.4°C), blood pressure is 177/99 mmHg, pulse is 110/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old young woman presents to her primary care physician for weakness and tingling in her hand. The patient is an avid bodybuilder and has noticed that her grip strength has gradually worsened in both hands with symptoms worse at the end of a long workout. The patient has a past medical history of anabolic steroid use in high school. Her current medications include a multivitamin, fish oil, and whey protein supplements. On physical exam, you note a muscular young woman with female pattern hair loss. The patient has a loss of sensation bilaterally over the volar surface of the 4th and 5th digits and over the medial aspect of the volar forearm. The patient has 3/5 grip strength of her left hand and 2/5 grip strength of her right hand. There is also notable weakness of finger adduction and abduction. The rest of the patient's physical exam is within normal limits.

Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old patient comes into your clinic with a new concern. She states that about 20 years ago, she was shot in her right quadriceps while serving in the military. Since then, she has had a wound that partially heals, but has never closed completely. Now, the patient describes the wound as somewhat different. She states it is ulcerated with elevated edges and has been bleeding. You perform a full thickness biopsy of the lesion as shown in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old high school student presents to your office for recent mood and skin changes. The patient is a high school senior who is competing on the wrestling team and recently has lost weight to drop two weight classes over the past several months. She states she has dry, cracking, and irritated skin, as well as a sensation of tingling in her hands and feet. The patient also states that she has not been feeling herself lately. She finds herself more irritable and no longer enjoys many of the activities she once enjoyed. She finds that she often feels fatigued and has trouble concentrating. The patient does not have a significant past medical history and is not on any current medications. The patient admits to drinking alcohol and smoking marijuana on special occasions. She states that she uses supplements that her other team members use. Physical exam is significant for acne, dry, cracked skin around the patient's mouth in particular, and decreased sensation in her lower extremities. Laboratory values are as follows:

Serum:
Na+: 137 mEq/L
Cl-: 101 mEq/L
K+: 4.1 mEq/L
HCO3-: 24 mEq/L
BUN: 15 mg/dL
Glucose: 79 mg/dL
Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL
Ca2+: 9.2 mg/dL
Mg2+: 1.5 mEq/L
Homocysteine: 11.2 µmol/L (normal: 4.6 to 8.1 µmol/L)
AST: 11 U/L
ALT: 11 U/L
Alkaline phosphatase: 27 U/L
Albumin: 4.5 g/dL
Total protein: 6.9 g/dL
Total bilirubin: 0.5 mg/dL
Direct bilirubin: 0.3 mg/dL

Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 18-year-old man comes to see his primary care physician for a physical for school. He states he has not had any illnesses last year and is on his school's volleyball team. He exercises daily, does not use any drugs, and has never smoked cigarettes. On physical exam you note bruising around the patient's neck, and what seems to be burn marks on his back and thighs. The physician inquires about these marks. The patient explains that these marks are the result of his sexual activities. He states that in order for him to be aroused he has to engage in acts such as hitting, choking, or anything else that he can think of. The physician learns that the patient lives with his girlfriend and that he is in a very committed relationship. He is currently monogamous with this partner. The patient is studying with the hopes of going to law school and is currently working in a coffee shop. The rest of the patient’s history and physical is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old man presents to his family physician with a complaint of painful joints for the past 2 weeks. He reports symmetric bilateral joint pain in his hands, knees, and ankles. He has never had this before, and his past medical history is notable only for asthma. He states the pain is worse in the morning and improves throughout the day. Review of systems is notable for a recent low-grade fever with malaise. He works as a school teacher and is sexually active with men and women. His temperature is 97.9°F (36.6°C), blood pressure is 120/84 mmHg, pulse is 70/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. The patient is instructed to take ibuprofen and acetaminophen for his joint pain. He returns 1 month later stating that he has not needed to take the medications as his pain has been absent for the past 3 days. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old female with no significant medical history comes to your office complaining of pain and stiffness in her hands upon wakening in the morning. You perform an x-ray (Figure A). What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 75-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician with a painful rash. She notes her side began to hurt several days prior without any visible skin changes; however, over the past 2 days a rash has developed. The patient's past medical history is only notable for diabetes mellitus type II. She was recently started on an antibiotic for sinusitis as well. In her spare time, she goes hiking and recently returned from a hiking trip 2 days ago. She is currently sexually active with both men and women. Her temperature is 99.0°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 154/88 mmHg, pulse is 83/min, respirations are 12/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old female with no significant medical history comes to your office complaining of pain and stiffness in her hands upon wakening in the morning for the past several months. The stiffness generally lasts one to two hours, per the patient. You perform an x-ray (Figure A). What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician with shortness of breath. The patient has had worsening shortness of breath for the past year. She has a past medical history of asthma and constipation. Her current medications include albuterol and sodium docusate. The patient was an officer in the navy and currently lives at home with her husband. She has a 52 pack-year smoking history. Pulmonary function testing is performed at this visit as revealed in Figure A. The results of this test at this visit are revealed by the blue loop, as compared to her results 12 years ago as seen in the green dotted loop of Figure A. Which of the following is a possible diagnosis for this patient's presentation?

49-year-old woman complains of no symptoms, but on a routine complete blood count (CBC) has a white blood cell count of 40,000 per uL. A peripheral blood smear demonstrates leukocytosis with myeloid cells present at various stages of differentiation, with more mature cells present at a greater percentage than less mature cells (Figure A). What is the likely diagnosis?

A 1-week old child is brought into your office for a normal check-up when you notice bruising on her arm. The father states the child was born at home and had a "natural birth". He also states that the child is eating and having yellow seedy stools 4-8 times per day. He took lamotrigine for his seizures, but he had regular check-ups and was told everything was normal. He does state that he has noticed that the child bruises easily. On exam, the vitals are normal, but the child has pin-point spots on her arms where she was held by the father that do not disappear with pressure (Figure A). Her PT and aPTT are elevated, but the bleeding time is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old male patient comes to your office complaining of white spots on his tongue. He reports that he first noticed them about one week ago. He denies pain or difficulty swallowing. His past medical history is significant for asthma, hepatitis C, and heroin abuse. He had previously been homeless and only recently went to the doctor one month ago for the first time in over five years. At that time, his primary care physician prescribed sofosbuvir, an albuterol inhaler, and daily inhaled fluticasone, which he has been using as directed. He is sexually active with one female partner. His last HIV test was negative, and he does not have a history of sexually transmitted diseases. He denies current alcohol or intravenous drug use. He smokes a pack a day of cigarettes and reports he has been smoking since he was 16. On physical examination, you note lesions on his oral mucosa that are easily scraped off, as shown in Figure A.

Which of the following is the best treatment for this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old athlete comes into your office for pain in her right foot. She states that she has no prior medical history and takes no medications. She is an avid runner and runs in marathons, but recently switched to barefoot running from her normal shoes. She runs around 50 miles per week and states that her pain is getting worse and worse with each run. On exam, her vitals are within normal limits, but there is pain upon palpation of the second metatarsal of her right foot. Her pulses and sensation are intact in all extremities. Figure A is an anteriorposterior (AP) radiograph of her right foot. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by ambulance. The patient was found unconscious in her bedroom after a suicide attempt. The patient had cut her wrists using a kitchen knife. The patient is unresponsive and pale. Her temperature is 96°F (35.6°C), blood pressure is 70/35 mmHg, pulse is 190/min, respirations are 19/min, and oxygen saturation is 92% on room air. Pressure is applied to her bilateral wrist lacerations. Her Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) is 7. A full trauma assessment is performed and reveals no other injuries. IV fluids are started as well as a rapid transfusion sequence. Norepinephrine is administered. Repeat vitals demonstrate that her blood pressure is 100/65 mmHg and pulse is 100/min. The patient is responsive and seems mildly confused. Resuscitation is continued and the patient's GCS improves to 15. Thirty minutes later, the patient's GCS is 11. Her temperature is 103°F (39.4°C), blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg, pulse is 122/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. The patient complains of flank pain. Laboratory values are ordered and demonstrate the following:

Hemoglobin: 9 g/dL
Hematocrit: 27%
Leukocyte count: 10,500 cells/mm^3 with normal differential
Haptoglobin: 11 mg/dL
Platelet count: 198,000/mm^3

Serum:
Na+: 139 mEq/L
Cl-: 101 mEq/L
K+: 4.4 mEq/L
HCO3-: 23 mEq/L
BUN: 27 mg/dL
Glucose: 99 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.5 mg/dL
Ca2+: 10.0 mg/dL
Bilirubin: 3.2 mg/dL
AST: 22 U/L
ALT: 15 U/L

Which of the following describes the most likely diagnosis?

A 1-year-old girl presents to her pediatrician for episodes of crying and being hunched over. She has also had decreased oral intake during this time. She is generally healthy and has no medical issues. Her temperature is 97.0°F (36.1°C), blood pressure is 94/54 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. The child appears well and is playing; however, while in the office she has another spell of crying and being hunched over. An ultrasound is performed as seen in Figure A. Which of the following vaccines is associated with this patient's most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old woman is undergoing a bone marrow transplantation for treatment of a non-Hodgkin lymphoma that has been refractory to several rounds of chemotherapy and radiation over the past 2 years. She has been undergoing a regimen of cyclophosphamide and total body irradiation for the past several weeks in anticipation of her future transplant. This morning, she reports developing a productive cough and is concerned because she noted some blood in her sputum this morning. The patient also reports pain with inspiration. Her temperature is 101°F (38.3°C), blood pressure is 115/74 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 19/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. A chest radiograph and CT are obtained and shown in Figures A and B respectively. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old woman presents to the emergency department complaining of excruciating pain of her left calf. She states that she was bitten by a spider three days ago; however, yesterday her calf became swollen, red, and extremely painful. Her vital signs are: T 102.8 F, HR 112 bpm, and BP 134/76. On exam, her distal left leg is swollen, extremely tender to palpation, and appears purples and dusky. You note crepitus is present. A biopsy is performed and the results are shown in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old is brought into the emergency room after a bicycle vs motored vehicle accident. She was unconscious after hitting the side of her head on the road, but recovered consciousness after a few minutes. She started to ride her bicycle again, but then developed a severe headache with nausea and vomiting, at which time she called EMS. While in the hospital, the patient is confused and cannot provide a history. She quickly loses consciousness and her CT scan is displayed in Figure 1. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 11-year-old boy is brought into the clinic by his parents, who are distraught over his behavior. They state that over the past several months he has started to act oddly, combing the hair of his toy action figures for hours without stopping and repetitively counting his steps in the house. He is often brought to tears when confronted about these behaviors. The patient has no past medical history. When questioned about family history, the father states he has needed close medical follow-up in the past, but declines to elaborate. The patient's vital signs are all within normal limits. On physical exam the patient is a well nourished 11-year-old boy in no acute distress. He has occasional motor tics, but the remainder of the exam is benign. What is the diagnosis in this patient?

A 70-year-old man presents to his primary care physician with sudden episodes of dizziness that resolve in certain positions. On further questioning he describes a false sense of motion with occasional spinning sensation consistent with vertigo. He denies any recent illnesses or hearing loss aside from presbycusis. His vital signs are normal. During the physical exam the patient reports an episode of vertigo after transitioning from sitting to supine and horizontal nystagmus is concurrently noted. What is the mostly likely diagnosis?

A 39-year-old man comes into your office with multiple complaints of recent onset. He has been feeling fatigued and has started having leg and thigh pain bilaterally, along with weakness. In addition, he states that he recently started noticing some redness around his eyes along with a rash on his shoulders as shown in Figure A. Of note, he takes simvastatin for his hyperlipidemia, and took a short course of steroids recently for an allergic reaction. His vitals are within normal limits. His CK is 400 U/L, ESR is 70 mm/hr, and ferritin is 500 mcg/L. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a severe headache. He states it is 10/10 in intensity and states that it is associated with chewing. He describes it as a dull pain over the sides of his head. The patient is otherwise healthy and is not currently taking any medications. His temperature is 97.0°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 111/74 mmHg, pulse is 83/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for pain and tenderness over the mandibular and temporal region that is worsened when the patient opens and closes his mouth. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
