A 23-year-old man is brought to his primary care physician for being excessively sad and withdrawn lately. The patient states he was recently in a relationship for the past 5 months that just ended. He states he did everything right in the relationship including cooking, cleaning, organizing, and being there for her. The relationship ended 1 week ago and since then, the patient has not known what to do with himself. He says he counted on his partner to structure his day and give him things to do and simply can not manage without her. He has not been doing laundry, cooking, or bathing during this time. This has happened to him multiple times in the past. He has begun writing songs about his breakup to cope, but it is not working. His temperature is 98.8°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, pulse is 82/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a sad young man and the finding in Figure A which is on his other arm as well. Which of the following is the most likely defense mechanism utilized in this patient's underlying diagnosis?

A 45-year-old female with no significant medical history comes to your office complaining of pain and stiffness in her hands upon awakening in the morning. She says the pain and stiffness tends to go away an hour or so after waking up. On physical exam, you note scaly rashes on her elbows bilaterally. You obtain radiographs, shown in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old female smoker with a history of peripheral vascular disease and a below the knee amputation, presents to the emergency room with excruciating abdominal pain and vomiting for the last 6 hours. Vital signs are T 101.0 F HR 136 BP 150/96 RR 18 Sat 93% on room air. Abdominal exam shows a non-distended, exquisitely tender abdomen which the patient refuses to allow you to examine. While assessing peripheral pulses you note that they are irregular. A digital rectal exam is Guiac positive. Laboratory values are notable for a leukocytosis and a lactic acid of 6.8 mmol/L. An ECG is shown in Figure A. What is the next best step in diagnosis?

A 62-year-old homeless woman presents to the emergency department with severe chest pain. The patient states she has felt unwell for the past several days and endorses lower back pain, chest pain, pain with swallowing, a cough, and a subjective fever. Several weeks ago, the patient had dental pain which she has been treating by drinking alcohol. Her temperature is 104°F (40.0°C), blood pressure is 114/64 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 92% on room air. Exam is notable for submandibular erythema and a coarse, rasping sound when auscultating the heart sounds. A CT of the chest is performed as seen in Figure A and an ECG is performed as seen in Figure B. Laboratory values are notable for a troponin of 1.0 ng/mL (normal < 0.4 ng/mL) and a creatinine of 2.5 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old female presents to clinic complaining of coughing up small amounts of blood daily for the past week. She denies smoking, sick contacts, or recent travel. Chest radiographs demonstrate interstitial pneumonia with patchy alveolar infiltrates suggestive of multiple bleeding sites. Urinalysis is positive for blood and protein. A positive result is returned for anti-glomerular basement membrane antibody (anti-GBM Ab). What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 64-year-old female presents to her primary care physician with a chief complaint of left knee pain. She describes acute-onset knee pain last evening that was accompanied by redness of the skin around the joint. She denies any precipitating injury or recent activity that could have caused this pain. She describes a similar episode that occurred in her right knee 2 months ago; she did not seek medical treatment, and the pain mitigated after 5 days. Physical examination is significant for the following: left knee is warm-to-touch, erythematous, and extremely tender to palpation; range of motion in flexion and extension is limited by pain; crepitus noted with passive movement of the knee joint. The patient is noted to be afebrile with all vital signs within normal limits. Aspiration of the left knee joint is ordered and reveals the findings shown in Figure A. Which of the following findings could also be seen in this patient, associated with their current diagnosis?

A 68-year-old female is admitted to your care four days after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) for a myocardial infarction (MI). The patient has a history of insulin-controlled diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. Of note, the patient states that after the surgery, she had resolution of her chest pain, but she has started experiencing chest pain again. The patient states that the pain is exacerbated by deep breaths but feels better when she leans forward compared to lying down flat. On exam, her vitals are normal, and there are no murmurs heard on auscultation. Her CK-mB returns as normal, and her repeat electrocardiogram (ECG) is shown in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 45-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a 1-week history of a painful mass in his neck. The patient reports the mass has slowly been enlarging over this time span and has become more painful to the touch. He also reports night sweats, weight loss, and diarrhea. Review of systems is notable only for a minor cold a few weeks ago. His temperature is 100°F (37.8°C), blood pressure is 122/80 mmHg, pulse is 160/min, respirations are 19/min, and oxygen saturation is 100% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a diffusely enlarged thyroid that is tender to the touch. An ECG is performed as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 69-year-old female presents to her primary care physician for pain in her arm. The patient states that her father recently died of a heart attack which motivated her to join her local gymnasium. After completing a set of weight lifting, she felt a "pop" in her right arm, followed by pain. Since the incident, she has been unable to carry items or lift her arm over her head without difficulty and pain. The patient has a past medical history of obesity, diabetes, hypertension, and constipation. Her current medications include lisinopril, metformin, insulin, and fiber supplements. On physical exam, you note pain with flexion of the forearm and abduction of the arm with 1/5 strength. There is also weakness of abduction of the affected arm with 3/5 strength. Inspection of the upper extremity reveals the finding in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old is brought into your office by her mother. Her mother states that she is having 10-20 episodes per day where she stops responding to her mother and is found staring out of the window. During these periods, she blinks more frequently than normal, but returns to her normal self afterwards. These episodes last 30 to 60 seconds. Her mother states that all of her milestones have been normal and she had an uncomplicated birth. Her mother also denies any other recent illness. On exam, her vitals are normal. During one of these episodes in the office, her EEG shows three-per-second spike and wave discharge. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old female presents to your office for her annual physical exam. She has no complaints at this time and her chronic hypertension is well controlled. You notice a.5cm papule on the patient's eyelid that has a pink pearly appearance, rolled borders, and overlying telangiectasias. On further questioning, you find out the patient was a door-to-door saleswoman and spent a lot of time outdoors, and she did not wear sunscreen. She has fair skin and blonde hair. The patient states that she first noticed the lesion about 6 months prior, and it has grown slightly since then. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old Caucasian male presents to his primary care physician for evaluation of progressive weakness and shortness of breath. He has had progressive shortness of breath over the last year with an intermittent non-productive cough. In addition, he complains of difficulty raising his arms to brush his hair. His temperature is 99.6°F (37.6°C), pulse is 80/min, blood pressure is 130/85 mmHg, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. Neurologic exam shows 4/5 strength in the deltoid muscles bilaterally. Diffuse dry crackles are heard on lung auscultation. A faint erythematous rash is noted on the malar cheeks, periorbital areas, lateral proximal thighs, and the elbows. Which of the following tests is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 55-year-old obese man is admitted to your floor for chronic fevers. He states he has had fevers of over 101F as measured on his oral thermometer for the past month. His vitals are T 100.9 F, HR 95 and regular, RR 16, BP 150/95. On history he states that he has a history of diabetes and is noncompliant with his insulin. He was recently treated for a foot infection with antibiotics, but his fevers have remained. His last HbA1C was 8.5%. On exam, the patient has no gross deficits, but does admit to pain in his left lower leg and foot. Physical exam reveals a Grade IV ulcer, as displayed in Figure A. He states he has severe pain when bearing weight on his left leg. Otherwise, all extremities have diminished pulses and sensation. There is no erythema in the surrounding area and no areas of fluctuance. Figure B shows AP and lateral radiographs of the patient's left leg. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old female is brought to the pediatrician by her father, who relates a primary complaint of a recent history of five independent episodes of vomiting over the last 10 months, most recently 3 weeks ago. Each time, she has awoken early in the morning appearing pale, feverish, lethargic, and complaining of severe nausea. This is followed by 8-12 episodes of non-bilious vomiting over the next 24 hours. Between these episodes she returns to normal activity. She has no significant past medical history and takes no other medications. Review of systems is negative for changes in vision, gait disturbance, or blood in her stool. Her family history is significant only for migraine headaches. Vital signs and physical examination are within normal limits. Initial complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel, and abdominal radiograph were unremarkable. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old male presents to the emergency department with two days of severe abdominal pain and fever. The patient has a history of gallstones, for which he was scheduled to have a cholecystectomy in two weeks. On physical exam, his abdomen is tender to palpation over the epigastrium, without rebound or guarding. The patient is noticeably jaundiced. Laboratory evaluation is notable for a leukocytosis and a total bilirubin of 6.4 mg/dL. What is the diagnosis in this patient?

A 56-year-old man presents to his primary care physician for dizziness. He says that his symptoms began approximately 1 month prior to presentation and are associated with nausea and ringing of the ears. He describes his dizziness as a spinning sensation that has a start and end and lasts approximately 25 minutes. This dizziness is severe enough that he cannot walk or stand. His symptoms are fluctuating, and he denies any tunnel vision or feelings of fainting. However, he has abruptly fallen to the ground in the past and denied losing consciousness. Medical history is significant for a migraine with aura treated with zolmitriptan, type 2 diabetes managed with metformin, and hypertension managed with lisinopril. His blood pressure is 125/75 mmHg, pulse is 88/min, and respirations are 16/min. On physical exam, when words are whispered into his right ear, he is unable to repeat the whispered words aloud; however, this is normal in the left ear. Air conduction is greater than bone conduction with Rinne testing, and the sound of the tuning fork is loudest in the left ear on Weber testing. Which of the following is most likely the diagnosis?

A 6-year-old girl is brought to the pediatrician complaining of itchy eyes. The father states that he has noted that she has been tearing and that both of her eyes have been red for the past 4 days. The patient denies any pain but has had a runny nose for the past week. The father states that she has not had any sick contacts, and she has been home from school for summer vacation. He notices that her symptoms seem to improve in the evening after she showers. Her temperature is 97.0°F (36.1°C), blood pressure is 100/66 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old previously healthy male is brought to your office by his mother. The mother reports the child has been crying and pulling at his right ear over the past 2 days, and reports the patient has been febrile the past 24 hours. The patient’s past medical history is unremarkable, although the mother reports the patient had a “common cold” a week ago which resolved without intervention. His temperature is 101.6 deg F (38.7 deg C), blood pressure is 100/70 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, and respirations are 22/min. Otoscopic exam is seen in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old male presents to his primary care physician complaining of headaches in his left temple and scalp area, neck stiffness, occasional blurred vision, and pain in his jaw when chewing. The appropriate medical therapy is initiated, and a subsequent biopsy of the temporal artery reveals arteritis. Five months later, the patient returns to his physician with a complaint of weakness, leading to difficulty climbing stairs, rising from a chair, and combing his hair. The patient states that this weakness has worsened gradually over the last 2 months. He reports that his headaches, jaw pain, and visual disturbances have resolved. Physical examination is significant for 4/5 strength for both hip flexion/extension as well as shoulder flexion/extension/abduction. Initial laboratory work-up reveals ESR and creatine kinase levels within normal limits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient's current presentation?

A 32-year-old man comes in to see his physician because he has had undiagnosed abdominal pain for the past 3 and a half years. His pain is not related to meals and does not correspond to a particular time of day, although he does report nausea and bloating. In the past two years he has had two endoscopies, a colonoscopy, and an exploratory laproscopy - without any results. He is very concerned because his mother has a history of colon cancer. The patient has been unable to work or maintain a social life because he's constantly worrying about his condition. What is this patient's most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old woman is brought to her primary care provider by her concerned husband. He reports she has had this "thing" on her eye for years and refuses to seek care. She denies any pain or discharge from the affected eye. A picture of her eye is shown below. Given the diagnosis, what are you most likely to discover when taking this patient's history?

A 71-year-old woman presents to her primary care doctor for a lesion on her skin. The patient states she is generally healthy but has noticed this lesion enlarging over the past several months. She worked in the navy and is not currently taking any medications. Her temperature is 98.1°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 123/83 mmHg, pulse is 85/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A on the patient's head. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old man who is an established patient presents to your office. He is complaining of increased urination and increased thirst. He has recently began taking several over-the-counter vitamins and supplements. On further review, he reports he has also been having abdominal pain and constipation. He denies significant weight changes. His fingerstick blood glucose in your office is 96 mg/dL.

Which of the following test is most likely to provide the diagnosis?

A 28-year-old homeless female with a past medical history significant for asthma comes to your clinic complaining of a chronic rash on her scalp and feet. She describes the rash as “dry and flaky,” and reports it has been present for at least a year. She was using a new dandruff shampoo she got over the counter, with little improvement. The patient reports it is extremely itchy at night, to the point that she can't sleep. On exam, you note a scaly patch of alopecia, enlarged lymph glands along the posterior aspect of her neck, and fine scaling in between her toes and on the heel and sides of her foot. Her temperature is 99°F (37°C), blood pressure is 118/78 mmHg, and pulse is 81/min. Which of the following is the most accurate test for the suspected diagnosis?

A 7-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with swelling around his eye. This has happened to him before but has never been this severe. The lesion started a few days ago but has become increasingly red and painful. Physical exam reveals the lesion in Figure A which is tender to palpation. His cranial nerves are intact and there is no pain with extraocular movements. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old female presents to the emergency department after a motor vehicle accident. The patient was an unrestrained driver in a head-on collision. She has a past medical history of asthma, depression, and anxiety. She is not currently taking any medications. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg, pulse is 115/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. The patient's cardiopulmonary exam is within normal limits. The patient is breathing on her own and has strong distal pulses. Ultimately, the patient is discharged with follow up instructions after no significant fractures or injuries are found. The patient then presents 4 months later to her primary doctor with weakness. The patient's strength in her upper extremities is 1/5. She has reduced sensation in her upper extremities as well. The patient's lower extremities reveal 5/5 strength with intact sensation. A chest radiograph and basic labs are ordered. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old man presents with sudden-onset pain in his lower back. He says he was exercising in the gym several hours ago when he felt a sharp pain. The pain is radiating down the side of his leg and into his foot. On physical exam, his vital signs are as follows: HR 95, BP 120/70, T 37.2 degrees C. He has extreme pain shooting down his leg with a straight leg raise. His sensation to light touch and pin-prick is intact throughout. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-month-old infant is brought to the office by her parents who are concerned of a recent rash. The infant is crying and has a erythematous, pruritic rash that affects her face, forearms, thighs, and scalp as noted in Figure A. The patient's vitals are T 97.8, HR 110, BP 90/60, RR 18. Of note, the father admits to a medical history of significant allergies, and the mother suffers from asthma, treated by albuterol. Which of the following is the best diagnosis?

A 29-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician with complaints of pain in her joints. She states it started a few days ago and has persisted since. She states that she is otherwise healthy and is not currently taking any medications. The patient is in the military and is currently in basic training. Review of systems is notable for discomfort with urination. Her temperature is 99.0°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 133/90 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. The knee and ankle joints demonstrate pain with passive range of motion, but there are no signs of erythema, edema, or crepitus. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old man presents to the clinic for malaise. He has been in his usual state of health until 2 weeks ago, when he noticed weakness and dyspnea upon exertion. He denies any orthopnea, paroxymal noctural dyspnea, or weight loss. He endorses occasional fevers but has not checked his temperature at home. He also reports worsening pain in his eyes that occasionally causes headaches and occasional joint pain. His temperature is 98.6°F (37°C), blood pressure is 120/70 mmHg, pulse is 70/min, and respirations are 15/min. Physical exam shows injected sclera bilaterally. He denies pain with eye movement. His lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Cardiac auscultation reveals an S3 with an occasionally split S2. A chest radiograph is obtained and shown in Figure A. His lower extremities reveal skin findings shown in Figure B. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old boy presents to the emergency department for a cough, fever, and a runny nose. The patient is an immigrant from Lebanon and has never seen a doctor before. He has been given antibiotics for infections every few months for similar symptoms in the past. He has seasonal allergies and has always been sick since he was a child. His temperature is 101°F (38.3°C), blood pressure is 100/64 mmHg, pulse is 89/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 96% on room air. Physical exam is notable for bilateral coarse breath sounds. He appears well otherwise. A chest radiograph is performed as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 36-year-old woman presents to the emergency room with subacute worsening of chronic chest pain and shortness of breath with exertion. The patient is generally healthy, lifts weights regularly, and does not smoke. Her temperature is 97.8°F (36.6°C), blood pressure is 122/83 mm Hg, pulse is 80/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Cardiac auscultation reveals a crescendo-decrescendo murmur heard right of the upper sternal border with radiation into the carotids. An ECG shows left axis deviation and meets criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy. An initial troponin is < 0.01 ng/mL. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old female presents to the emergency department with a 2-day onset of right-lower quadrant and right flank pain. She also states that over this period of time she has felt dizzy, light-headed, and short of breath. She denies any recent trauma or potential inciting event. Her vital signs are as follows: T 37.1 C, HR 118, BP 74/46, RR 18, SpO2 96%. Physical examination is significant for an irregularly irregular heart rhythm as well as bruising over the right flank. The patient's medical history is significant for atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. Her medication list includes atorvastatin, losartan, and coumadin. IV fluids are administered in the emergency department, resulting in an increase in blood pressure to 100/60 and decrease in heart rate to 98. Which of the following would be most useful to confirm this patient's diagnosis and guide future management?

A 25-year-old male with Hodgkin's lymphoma presents with a several day history of edema. Lab studies show:

Serum Na+: 140 mmol/L
Serum K+: 3.5 mmol/L
Serum albumin: 1.9 g/dL
Total serum bilirubin: 1.0 mg/dL
Serum creatinine: 1.2 mg/dL

Urinalysis shows 4+ proteinuria and fatty casts. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old boy presents to his pediatrician with a rash and intermittent abdominal pain and swelling of his legs and arms. He has also begun to complain of pain in his knees and hands with no history of trauma. His temperature is 97.6°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 100/80 mmHg, pulse is 89/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A as well as symmetric swelling in the joints of the upper extremities. His abdomen is currently nontender and not painful. Laboratory studies are pending, and the results of a urinalysis are notable only for positive blood and protein in the urine. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 75-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and diabetes presents to her primary care physician for blurry vision and difficulty driving at night. The patient reports a gradual blurring of vision in both eyes over the last 10 years. She states that she is retired and was not bothered by the blurriness but is now having difficulty driving at night due to glare from oncoming traffic. The patient denies any eye pain, flashes, floaters, tearing, redness, or periods of complete vision loss. She lives at home alone, smokes 1 pack per day, drinks 2 alcoholic drinks every night, and eats mostly canned food. Her temperature is 98.5°F (36.9°C), blood pressure is 184/110 mmHg, pulse is 70/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Cranial nerves II-XII are grossly intact and the patient has a stable gait. The patient's vision is 20/100 in both eyes. Slit-lamp exam is performed as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 47-year-old male with a history of hypertension presents to your outpatient clinic for numbness, tingling in his right hand that has been slowly worsening over the last several months. He has tried using a splint but receives minimal relief. He is an analyst for a large consulting firm and spends most of his workday in front of a computer. Upon examination, you noticed that the patient has a prominent jaw and his hands appear disproportionately large. His temperature is 99 deg F (37.2 deg C), blood pressure is 154/72 mmHg, pulse is 87/min, respirations are 12/min. A fasting basic metabolic panel shows: Na: 138 mEq/L, K: 4.1 mEq/L, Cl: 103 mEq/L, CO2: 24 mEq/L, BUN: 12 mg/dL, Cr: 0.8 mg/dL, Glucose: 163 mg/dL. Which of the following tests would be most helpful in identifying the underlying diagnosis?

A 7-year-old girl presents to an urgent care center for a rash that began approximately 2 days ago. According to her father, it began as a pink rash on her face and has subsequently spread to her trunk. The child was adopted and has not yet begun care with her pediatrician. Her temperature is 100.2°F (37.9°C), blood pressure is 104/74 mmHg, pulse is 99/min, respirations are 19/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the rash in Figure A and posterior cervical lymphadenopathy. The child is otherwise interactive and is quietly playing with toys. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 43-year-old Caucasian male with a long history of uncontrolled migraines presents to general medical clinic with painless hematuria. He is quite concerned because he has never had symptoms like this before. Vital signs are stable, and his physical examination is benign. He denies any groin pain, flank pain, or costovertebral angle tenderness. He denies any recent urinary tract infections or dysuria. Urinary analysis confirms hematuria and a serum creatinine returns at 3.0. A renal biopsy reveals papillary necrosis and a tubulointerstitial infiltrate. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician complaining of intense itching on the back of her left calf. She states that she noticed a red and blistering rash this morning and does not recall experiencing a similar rash in the past. Her social history is notable for a job at the zoo. Her temperature is 97.7°F (36.5°C), blood pressure is 120/74 mmHg, pulse is 70/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Her physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. Which of the following findings would be found in the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old female presents with a recent onset of upsetting dreams, anxiety, and disturbing flashbacks. The patient reports that she returned from active duty in Iraq 3 months ago and was adjusting to life back at home until about 7 weeks ago when she began having intense fear of loud noises and seeing sudden flashbacks to bombing attacks she endured during her time in Iraq. She had to take a leave from her army instructor duties as she was not able to handle the familiar settings of practice shooting ranges and sudden loud explosions during battalion training. After refusing to leave her house, she was finally persuaded by her husband to visit your clinic. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old woman presents to the emergency department after experiencing a motor vehicle accident. The patient was the front seat passenger in a head on collision. The patient is responsive only to painful stimuli. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg, pulse is 150/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. The patient is started on IV fluids and is given blood products. A FAST exam reveals no signs of intra-abdominal bleeding. A chest radiograph is ordered as seen in Figure A. A pelvic binder is placed and fluid and blood resuscitation is continued. Fifteen minutes later her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 110/70 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. The patient is now able to respond to questions. The patient's lab values are ordered and are as below:

Serum:
Na+: 137 mEq/L
Cl-: 102 mEq/L
K+: 4.2 mEq/L
HCO3-: 24 mEq/L
BUN: 20 mg/dL
Glucose: 110 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
Ca2+: 9.6 mg/dL
AST: 12 U/L
ALT: 14 U/L

Hemoglobin: 11 g/dL
Hematocrit: 30%
Leukocyte count: 6,500 cells/mm^3 with normal differential
Platelet count: 255,000/mm^3

The patient suddenly becomes short of breath. A chest radiograph is ordered as seen in Figure B. A FAST exam is repeated and is within normal limits. Repeat lab values are ordered as below:

Hemoglobin: 13 g/dL
Hematocrit: 36%
Leukocyte count: 6,000 cells/mm^3 with normal differential
Platelet count: 250,000/mm^3

Which of the following best describes the most likely diagnosis?

A 15-year-old boy presents to his physician with dyspnea and fatigue for several months. His past medical history is insignificant. He denies smoking, alcohol, and drug use and does not take any medications except for doxycycline for acne. His temperature is 97.6°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 120/81 mmHg, pulse is 95/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical examination is notable for a palpable spleen below the left seventh intercostal space and scleral icterus. Laboratory tests are ordered as seen below.

Hemoglobin: 10 g/dL
Hematocrit: 30%
Leukocyte count: 7,500/mm^3 with normal differential
Platelet count: 207,000/mm^3
Total bilirubin: 7.0 mg/dL
Direct bilirubin: 1.4 mg/dL
Lactate dehydrogenase: 450 U/L (normal value 80-280 U/L)
Haptoglobin: 15 mg/dL (normal value is 30-220 mg/dL)
Reticulocyte count: 10%

A peripheral blood smear is shown in Figure A. A direct Coomb test is negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 16-year-old Caucasian girl presents to your family practice office complaining of itchiness. She denies other symptoms. She also denies tobacco, alcohol, or other illicit drug use and is not sexually active. She has no other significant past medical or surgical history aside from a meniscal repair from a wrestling injury sustained two years ago from which she has recovered fully. Vitals are T 98.3, HR 67, BP 110/70. On exam you note several pruritic, erythematous, slightly raised annular patches with central clearing on her back.

Which of the following additional tests or features are sufficient to make the diagnosis of this girl's skin lesion?

A 34-year-old man presents to the clinic complaining of a rash that appeared on his left forearm after a scratch three days ago. This is not the first time he has experienced such a rash, as the patient states he had a similar looking lesion on his elbows three years ago. Upon further questioning, he states that his older brother has had problems with his skin, but he is unsure of the diagnosis. On physical exam you find a circular and scaly, pearl-colored rash superimposed over an abrasion on his left forearm (Figure A). Of note, the patient has the following nail appearance (Figure B). What is the diagnosis in this patient?

A 13-year-old male comes to your office complaining of dry, scaling skin (Figure A). He is particularly concerned about the appearance of his skin around his peers. He indicates that he did not start having problems until he was 5 years of age, after which his skin has progressively become drier and scalier. He has tried all types of over-the-counter moisturizers with no resolution. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old man presents to the medicine clinic with swelling around the right side of his chin and neck (Image A). He reports pain when moving his jaw and chewing. His symptoms developed two days after receiving an uncomplicated tonsillectomy. He has been followed by a general medical physician since birth and has received all of his standard health maintenance procedures. Vital signs are stable with the exception of a temperature of 38.4 degrees Celcius. The area in question on the right side is exquisitely tender. The remainder of his exam is benign. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old man with a past medical history of diabetes and obesity presents to the clinic with joint pain. He has severe pain in both of his knees for which he has been taking ibuprofen daily. His temperature is 98.2°F (36.8°C), blood pressure is 177/109 mmHg, pulse is 80/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. Radiography of the knee shows the finding in Figure B. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old boy is brought into your clinic with a 5 day history of decreased oral intake, body aches and lymphadenopathy. He has no significant medical history. Upon further questioning you find that the patient frequently plays outside, where he enjoys chasing the neighborhood cats and dogs. He has had no recent sick contacts or travel to foreign countries. The patient's vital signs are: temperature 100.4F, HR 80, BP 105/75 and RR 15. Physical exam is significant for a 1-cm erythematous and tender lymph node in the right posterior cervical area (Figure 1). There is a nearly healed scratch in the right occipital region. What is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 53-year-old female presents to your office for abdominal discomfort. The patient states she first noticed pain on her right flank several months ago, and it has been gradually getting worse. For the past week, she has also noticed blood in her urine. Prior to this episode, she has been healthy and does not take any medications. The patient denies fever, chills, and dysuria. She has a 40 pack-year smoking history. Vital signs are T 37 C, HR 140/90 mmHg, HR 84/min, RR 14/min, O2 98%. Physical exam is unremarkable. CBC reveals a hemoglobin of 17 and hematocrit of 51%, and urinalysis is positive for red blood cells, negative for leukocytes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-year-old girl presents to her family physician with a 1-day history of a rash. She denies any history of a similar rash or any dermatologic diagnoses in the past. The father states that their family was in upstate New York for the past week; however, the child has had no other new events or exposures. Her temperature is 98.0°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 104/74 mmHg, pulse is 87/min, respirations are 12/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. Which of the following diagnoses shares the same pathophysiology as this patient's diagnosis?

A 38-year-old man with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus, obesity, and hyperlipidemia presents to his primary care physician for evaluation of new bilateral blisters on his hands. He says that he first noticed these blisters shortly after returning from a weekend trip to the beach two weeks prior. He denies any fevers, joint pains, or other skin rash during this period. The patient works in the adult entertainment industry. On examination, there are multiple flaccid blisters of the bilateral dorsal hands with hemorrhagic crusts, mild scarring, and hyperpigmentation. In addition, increased hair growth is noted on the bilateral malar cheeks. His temperature is 99.1° F (37.3° C), pulse is 95/min, blood pressure is 130/87 mmHg, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. His laboratory results are:

Serum:
Na+: 140 mEq/L
K+: 4.5 mEq/L
Cl-: 100 mEq/L
HCO3-: 21 mEq/L
BUN: 20 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
Glucose: 104 mg/dL

Leukocyte count: 9,000/mm^3
Hemoglobin: 12.4 g/dL
Platelets: 400,000/mm^3

Anti-nuclear antibody titer 1:320

Which of the following would confirm the diagnosis in this patient?

A 9-year-old boy is brought to the pediatrician by his mother who is concerned about a new rash. His son is otherwise feeling well, is up to date on vaccinations, and has not traveled recently. The family lives in an old apartment building. He is currently excelling in school and has many friends. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old woman presents to clinic complaining of 3 months of weight loss, epigastric pain after meals, diarrhea, and acholic stools. On physical exam she has jaundice and a right upper quadrant mass, but no abdominal tenderness. She has a palpable left supraclavicular node. She also has multiple tender areas of inflamed skin on her chest wall and legs. The patient states that these patches change location over time. CT scan of her abdomen is seen in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 36-year-old male with a history of end stage renal disease secondary to poorly controlled type I diabetes on peritoneal dialysis presents to his nephrologist's office with chest pain, shortness of breath, and extreme fatigue. He has a history of inadequate dialysis due to poor compliance. In the office, the patient's vitals are BP: 94/58; HR: 90; RR: 20; T: 98.0 F. EKG is shown below (Figure A). The patient is immediately taken to the emergency department. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old man presents to an outpatient clinic during winter for persistent rhinorrhea. He states it is persistent and seems to be worse when he goes outside. Otherwise, he states he is generally healthy and only has a history of constipation. His temperature is 98.7°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 144/91 mmHg, pulse is 82/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Nasal sputum cytology reveals eosinophilia and boggy turbinates. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 79-year-old woman is admitted to the intensive care unit for hospital acquired pneumonia, a COPD flare, and acute heart failure requiring intubation and mechanical ventilation. On her first night in the intensive care unit, her temperature is 99.7°F (37.6°C), blood pressure is 107/58 mm Hg, and pulse is 150/min which is a sudden change from her previous vitals. Physical exam is notable for jugular venous distension and a rapid heart rate. The ventilator is checked and is functioning normally. Which of the following is the best next step in management for the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old female presents to your office one day after an injury. Yesterday she tried to play basketball with her grandchildren and she was doing well until she jumped to get the ball and landed awkwardly on her right foot, after which she could not bear weight on her foot. On exam, her right foot is significant for swelling with tenderness to palpation anterior to the Achilles tendon. The patient has no tenderness over her medial or lateral malleoli. Figure A is a radiograph of her right foot with the area of traumatic injury. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 49-year-old female presents to her primary care physician for the first time in twelve years. Her chief complaint is a new onset of diarrhea, which nothing seems to improve. She first noticed this diarrhea about a month ago. She complains of greasy stools, which leave a residue in her toilet bowl. Review of systems is notable for alcohol consumption of 12-16 cans of beer per day for the last two decades. Additionally, the patient endorses losing 12 lbs unintentionally over the last month. Vital signs are within normal limits and stable. Exam demonstrates a female who appears older than stated age; abdominal exam is notable for epigastric tenderness to palpation. What is the next step in diagnosis?

A 30-year-old previously healthy female presents to your office with complaints of facial pressure and rhinorrhea for the past 3 weeks. The patient reports that several weeks prior, she had a “common cold” which resolved. However, she has since developed worsening facial pressure, especially over her cheeks and forehead. She reports over 1 week of green tinged rhinorrhea. Her temperature is 100.1 deg F (37.8 deg C), blood pressure is 120/70 mmHg, pulse is 85/min, and respirations are 15/min. Nasal exam reveals edematous turbinates and purulent discharge. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old child is brought to the emergency room by her parents in severe pain. They state that she fell on her outstretched right arm while playing with her friends. She is unable to move her right arm which is being supported by her left. On exam, her vitals are normal. Her right extremity reveals normal pulses without swelling in any compartments, but there is crepitus above the elbow upon movement. The child is able to flex and extend her wrist, but this is limited by pain. The child has decreased sensation along her thumb and is unable to make the "OK" sign with her thumb and index finger. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old man presents to his primary care physician for foot pain. The patient states that he has pain in his foot and toes whenever he exerts himself or is at work. The patient is an executive at a medical device company and works 60 hours/week. He is currently training for a marathon. He has a past medical history of anxiety, constipation, and irritable bowel syndrome. His current medications include clonazepam, sodium docusate, and hyoscyamine. His temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 100/60 mmHg, pulse is 50/min, respirations are 10/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Cardiac and pulmonary exams are within normal limits. Examination of the lower extremity reveals 5/5 strength with 2+ reflexes. Palpation of the interdigital space between the third and fourth toes elicits pain and a clicking sound. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old girl presents to the general pediatrics clinic with hip pain. The pain started several weeks ago on her left side and has worsened over the past several days. Her right hip is painless. Her temperature is 98.0°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 107/68 mm Hg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 16/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam reveals an antalgic gait, decreased range of motion in the left hip, and mild thigh muscle atrophy. A radiograph is shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 15-year-old boy is brought into his pediatrician's office by his father because the father thinks his son has attention issues. The father explains that his son started high school four months ago and had lackluster grades in a recent progress report despite having earned consistent top marks in middle school. The father complains that his son never talks to him at home anymore. The patient yells at his father in the exam room, and the father is escorted out of the room. The patient scoffs that his father is so overbearing, ruining his good days with criticism. He begins to chew gum and states that he hates hanging out with the boys on the football squad. He denies experiencing physical abuse from anyone or having a sexual partner. He has seen kids smoke marijuana underneath the football field bleachers, but does not go near them and denies smoking cigarettes. He denies any intention to harm himself or others, thinks his grades went down because his teachers are not as good as his middle school teachers, and states he thinks he learns best by watching explanations through online videos. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 21-year-old woman presents to the clinic complaining of feeling tired during the day. She is concerned as her grades in school have worsened and she does not want to lose her scholarship. Upon further questioning, the patient describes frequently experiencing a dreamlike state before falling asleep and after waking up. She also has frequent nighttime awakenings where she finds herself unable to move. She denies snoring. The patient does not drink alcohol or abuse any other drugs. The patient's BMI is 21 kg/m2, and her vital signs are all within normal limits. What is this patient's diagnosis?

An 18-year-old female with a history of recurrent pharyngitis presents to your clinic with fever, sore throat and decreased oral intake. The patient states that her symptoms have been present for about 1-week, although over the past couple of days they have gotten much worse. The patient's vital signs are as follows: temperature is 102.2 deg F (39.0 deg C), pulse is 94/min, blood pressure is 110/68 mmHg and respirations are 14/min. On physical exam the patient appears uncomfortable, barely opening her mouth when speaking. There is tender lymphadenopathy bilaterally. Examination of the oropharynx is demonstrated in Figure A. A heterophile test is performed and later comes back negative. What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

An 8-year old girl is brought to the pediatrician by her distraught father who is concerned about "light spots" that first appeared 4 months ago and have been slowly expanding over different parts of her body. She is not bothered by these areas, and they do not itch, burn, or bleed. She has otherwise been well. There is no family history of this skin condition, though her father has a history of hypothyroidism. Her skin exam is notable for smooth, hypopigmented patches over her bilateral knuckles, knees, and inner thighs, as seen in Figure A. Her exam is also notable for a tuft of leukotrichia over her occiput, as seen in Figure B. Which of the following will help to confirm the diagnosis?

A 17-year-old boy presents to his primary care physician with a concern for a puffy cheek. He has noticed he has had a puffy cheek for the past month despite exercising more often and eating a healthy diet. The patient states he is an otherwise healthy student, does not smoke, and is not sexually active. His temperature is 97.9°F (36.6°C), blood pressure is 114/74 mmHg, pulse is 105/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a healthy young man with a nontender abdomen. Exam reveals the finding in Figure A as well as poor dentition. His BMI is 26 kg/m^2 and he has normal development for his age. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below.

Hemoglobin: 10 g/dL
Hematocrit: 30%
Leukocyte count: 12,900/mm^3 with normal differential
Platelet count: 191,000/mm^3

Serum:
Na+: 139 mEq/L
Cl-: 100 mEq/L
K+: 3.0 mEq/L
HCO3-: 29 mEq/L
BUN: 23 mg/dL
Glucose: 99 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.2 mg/dL
Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL

Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 53-year-old farmer presents to the clinic for evaluation of a pigmented lesion on her arm. She states that she first noticed the lesion last year, but she believes that it has been slowly growing in size. She otherwise does not have any complaints and is generally healthy. Which of the following findings on physical exam would suggest a malignant diagnosis?

A 32-year-old male who was previously healthy is brought to the emergency department by his concerned fiancee who states that he is acting very abnormally. She states that over the past day he has developed a fever, become progressively more confused, and is "just not acting like himself." On exam, he exhibits altered mental status. His vitals are demonstrated as: T: 39 deg C, HR: 102 bpm, BP: 130/90 mmHg, RR: 12, SaO2: 100%. The emergency physician obtains a lumbar puncture which demonstrates the following CSF analysis: normal opening pressure, elevated lymphocyte count, elevated protein, elevated RBCs, and normal glucose. An MRI is obtained to confirm the diagnosis and is illustrated in Figure A. Which of the following organisms is most likely responsible for this patient's presentation?

A mother brings her 3-year-old daughter to the doctor because she is worried that she might be harming herself by constantly banging her head on the wall. She has been exhibiting this behavior for a few months. She is also worried because she has started to speak less than she used to and does not respond when her name is called. She seems aloof during playtime with other children and seems to have lost interest in most of her toys. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old male presents to his primary care physician with right knee pain for the last week. He states that he first noticed it after a long flight on his way back to the United States from Russia, where he had run a marathon along a mountain trail. The patient describes the pain as dull, aching, and localized to the front of his kneecap, and it worsens with sitting but improves with standing. Aspirin has not provided significant relief. The patient has a history of a torn anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) on the right side from a soccer injury three years ago. In addition, he was treated for gonorrhea last month after having intercourse with a new partner. At this visit, the patient’s temperature is 98.5°F (36.9°C), blood pressure is 112/63 mmHg, pulse is 75/min, and respirations are 14/min. Which of the following is most likely to establish the diagnosis?

A 60-year-old woman with a history of chronic back pain presents to the emergency department with abdominal pain. She states her back pain has been worsening recently requiring more pain medications. Her temperature is 97.6°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 122/80 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 12/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. The patient is laying still on her back and is moaning in pain. There is notable tenderness in all quadrants with rebound tenderness. The patient's heart rate is 90/min after receiving hydromorphone. A radiograph is performed as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old IV drug user comes into the emergency department after four days of pain in her right ankle. The patient is lethargic and unable to answer any questions about her medical history. Her vitals are HR 110, T 101.5, RR 20, BP 100/60. Her physical exam is notable for track marks in her toes and her right ankle is erythematous and swollen. Moving any part of the right foot creates a 10/10 pain. A radiograph reveals no evidence of fractures. A Gram stain of the joint fluid aspirate demonstrates purple cocci in clusters. The fluid is yellow, opaque, with more than 70,000 cells/mm^3 (80% neutrophils). What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 43-year-old woman with a history of hepatitis C and current intravenous drug use presents with 5 days of fever, chills, headache, and severe back pain. On physical exam, temperature is 100.6 deg F (38.1 deg C), blood pressure is 109/56 mmHg, pulse is 94/min, and respirations are 18/min. She is thin and diaphoretic with pinpoint pupils, poor dentition, and track marks on her arms and legs. A high-pitched systolic murmur is heard, loudest in the left sternal border and with inspiration. She is admitted to the hospital and started on broad-spectrum antibiotics. One of the blood cultures drawn 12 hours ago returns positive for Staphylococcus aureus. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to confirm the diagnosis?

69-year-old woman with no significant past medical history except for hypertension receives an X-ray of her skull (Figure A) after her car was rear-ended in a parking lot resulting in neck soreness. No fracture but what is the likely diagnosis of this incidental finding?

A 25-year-old woman comes into your office for a yearly physical exam and check up. She has no current complaints and states that her family is healthy. She was originally born in Italy and is up to date with all of her vaccinations. Her physical exam is within normal limits and her vitals are HR 80, BP 125/70, T 97.9 F, RR 11. Her CBC is significant for Hgb 12.0, Hct 35, WBC 6.5, and Plts 210. Upon obtaining the differential for her low hemoglobin, you see an MCV of 65 along with a reticulocyte count of 4%. Her iron studies are within normal limits. Figure A shows her peripheral blood smear. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old female with a history of ulcerative colitis presents to the emergency room with four-day history of nausea, bloody diarrhea, and abdominal pain. She is on medical management with 5-aminosalicylic acid (5 ASA). Examination shows an ill appearing woman with a tense, tympanitic abdominal exam. She is unable to be fully examined due to the abdominal pain. Vitals are T 38.2 C, HR 102 bpm BP 133/92 mmHg,2 RR 20 bpm, and O2 Sat 100% on room air. In the ED an abdominal radiograph is shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the diagnosis?

A 69-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician for pain when she walks. She states that the pain is the worst in her left great toe but is also present in her hips and knees. She says that her symptoms are worse with activity and tend to improve with rest. Her symptoms have progressively worsened over the past several years. She has a past medical history of obesity, type II diabetes mellitus, smoking, and hypertension. She drinks roughly ten beers per day. Her current medications include metformin, insulin, lisinopril, and hydrochlorothiazide. The patient has a recent travel history to Bangkok where she admits to having unprotected sex. On physical exam, examination of the lower extremity results in pain. There is crepitus of the patient's hip when her thigh is flexed and extended. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old man presents to the emergency department with jaundice and diffuse abdominal pain. He denies any previous medical problems and says he does not take any medications, drugs, or supplements. His temperature is 97.6°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 133/87 mmHg, pulse is 86/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 100% on room air. Physical exam is notable for sclera which are icteric and there is tenderness to palpation over the right upper quadrant. Laboratory studies are ordered as seen below.

Hepatitis B surface antigen: Positive
Hepatitis B surface IgG: Negative
Hepatitis B core antigen: Positive
Hepatitis B core IgG: Positive
Hepatitis B E antigen: Positive
Hepatitis B E IgG: Positive

Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 43-year-old man presents to a new primary care physician complaining of anxiety. He has been worrying non-stop recently about the possibility that his wife will lose her job as a teacher. His wife, who is present, assures the physician that her job is entirely secure and states that he has "fretted" for their entire marriage, though the exact topic causing his anxiety varies over time. He also worries excessively about everyday tasks, such as whether he will catch the train on time and whether their house in Southern California is sufficiently earthquake-proof. He has no way to overcome these worries. He endorses other symptoms including poor sleep (associated with racing thoughts about his various worries), fatigue, and impaired concentration at work, all of which have been present for at least the past year. His vital signs are within normal limits and there are no abnormalities on physical exam. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old woman with a history of chronic constipation presents to the emergency department with a two-day history of left lower quadrant abdominal pain. She is found to have a temperature of 100.8F, BP 140/90, HR 85, and RR 16. On physical examination, she is tender to light palpation in the left lower quadrant and exhibits voluntary guarding. Rectal examination reveals heme-positive stool. Laboratory values are unremarkable except for a WBC count of 12,500 with a left shift. Which of the following tests would be most useful in the diagnosis of this patient's disease?

An obese 42-year-old male presents to his primary care physician with a complaint of left knee pain for the past 3 months. He describes the pain as affecting the inside part of the knee as well as the front of his knee, below the kneecap. He denies any inciting injury or trauma to the knee but reports that the pain is worse when he is climbing up stairs or rising from a chair. Physical examination is significant for localized tenderness to palpation over the left anteromedial proximal tibia, 6 cm inferior to the joint line. There is no joint effusion noted. Valgus stress testing is negative for any pain or instability of the knee joint. Radiographs of the left knee are obtained and reveal only mild arthritis, without evidence of any fractures or bony lesions. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 54-year-old African American woman presents to the emergency department with shortness of breath. She was at home watching television when her symptoms began. She has a past medical history of COPD, alcohol abuse, diabetes, asthma, obesity, pancreatitis, peripheral neuropathy, and hypertension. She has a 30 pack-year smoking history as well. Her current medications include albuterol, insulin, nicotine patches, duloxetine, hydroxyurea, and lisinopril. Chest radiography confirms the diagnosis of a spontaneous pneumothorax. A chest tube is placed, and the patient is transferred to the medical floor. Laboratory results are ordered and are seen below:

Hemoglobin: 9 g/dL
Platelet count: 180,000/mm^3
Mean corpuscular volume: 125 µm^3
Reticulocyte count: 0.3%

Serum:
Na+: 139 mEq/L
Cl-: 102 mEq/L
K+: 4.2 mEq/L
HCO3-: 24 mEq/L
BUN: 20 mg/dL
Glucose: 133 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.4 mg/dL
Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL
Vitamin B12: 197 ng/L
AST: 22 U/L
ALT: 10 U/L
Troponins: undetectable

On the medical floor, the patient complains of continued fatigue and minor chest pain. A peripheral smear is ordered as seen in Figure A. An EKG is ordered and demonstrates a right bundle branch block which is unchanged from previous EKGs. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old man with a psychiatric history of bipolar disorder is brought into the emergency department by emergency medical services. The patient is unconscious, but the mother states that he walked into the patient's room with the patient lying on the floor and an empty bottle of unknown pills next to him. The patient has previously tried to commit suicide 2 years ago. Upon presentation, the patient's vitals are HR 110, BP 105/60, T 99.5, RR 22. The patient soon has 5 episodes non-bilious non-bloody vomiting. Upon physical exam, he has pain in the right upper quadrant and his liver function tests are AST 1050 U/L, ALT 2050 U/L, ALP 55 U/L, Total Bilirubin 0.8 mg/dL, Direct Bilirubin 0.2 mg/dL. You are awaiting his toxicology screen. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old woman with a history of alcohol abuse and cirrhosis presents to the emergency department with profuse vomiting. The patient is aggressive, combative, emotionally labile, and has to be chemically restrained. The patient continues to vomit and blood is noted in the vomitus. Her temperature is 99.2°F (37.3°C), blood pressure is 139/88 mmHg, pulse is 106/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 100% on room air. The patient complains of sudden onset chest pain during her physical exam. A crunching and rasping sound is heard while auscultating the heart. Which of the following is the pathophysiology of the most likely diagnosis?

A 37-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician with a chief complaint of diarrhea. The patient states that her symptoms have worsened recently. She works as a farmer and is dressed in tattered and old denim. She lives alone, and this is the first time she has come to town in years. The patient’s diet is mostly dairy products and some meat products. She denies any systemic symptoms and states that diarrhea tends to occur right after a meal. She also claims that at times she struggles to fall asleep, and sometimes she feels she lacks energy. The patient is instructed to avoid consuming dairy products for a week and to return with a report of her symptoms. As you set up the return appointment with this patient you notice that she is rather emotionless. She also states that she lacks anybody that she can list as an emergency contact so she leaves that section of her medical forms blank. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician for a follow-up appointment. The patient was the front seat driver in a head-on collision which resulted in a femur and pelvic fracture which was treated appropriately. The patient spent 3 weeks in the hospital and was then discharged 2 weeks ago. The patient has a past medical history of diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidemia. She smokes 3 packs of cigarettes per day and drinks 4 alcoholic beverages every night. The patient says that she has been attempting to engage in sexual activities with her husband but has been unable to do so. She states this has never been a problem for her before. She also reports new-onset minor headaches and trouble sleeping for which she is taking trazodone. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 12-year-old boy presents to his primary care physician with left knee pain for the past 6 weeks. He recently joined the field hockey team at his school. The pain is the most severe when he is running up and down the stairs at the school stadium. The pain decreases when he goes home and rests after practice. He additionally admits to tripping and landing on his left knee 5 days ago. Physical exam shows a knee with a healing abrasion over the left patella. The tibial tuberosity is tender to palpation. A radiograph of the knee is presented in figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 11-year-old girl presents to the emergency department with heavy drooling. The patient was being watched by her babysitter when he found her in this manner. Her temperature is 99.1°F (37.3°C), blood pressure is 107/58 mmHg, pulse is 119/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a young girl in acute distress who is drooling. The girl states she is in pain and can’t swallow. The patient’s tongue seems abnormally enlarged and erythematous. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with epigastric pain. The patient states that she was at home watching television when her symptoms began. Otherwise, the patient has no complaints. The patient has a past medical history of obesity, hypertension, alcohol abuse, diabetes, and constipation. Her current medications include insulin, metformin, lisinopril, and sodium docusate. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 160/95 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Laboratory values and an abdominal ultrasound are ordered and are currently pending. An abdominal radiograph is ordered as seen in Figure A. On physical exam, the patient is clinically intoxicated. Cardiopulmonary exam is within normal limits. The patient is started on IV fluids and given morphine. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old man presents to his primary care physician for knee pain. The pain started yesterday and has not improved since then. The patient is generally in good health. He attends college and plays soccer for his school's team. Three days ago, he was slide tackled during a game and his leg was struck from the outside. He fell to the ground and sat out for the rest of the game. It was not until yesterday that he noticed swelling in his knee. He also feels as if his knee is unstable and does not feel confident bearing weight on his leg during athletic activities. His past medical history is notable for asthma, which is currently treated with an albuterol inhaler. On physical exam, you note bruising over his leg, knee, and lateral thigh, and edema of his knee. Passive range of motion of the knee is notable only for minor clicking and catching of the joint. The patient's gait appears normal, though the patient states that his injured knee does not feel stable. Further physical exam is performed and imaging is ordered. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with pain in her right eye. The patient states that her eye hurts and that she cannot see well. She cannot remember when her symptoms started or what caused them. The patient has a past medical history of schizophrenia and IV drug abuse. Her current medications include intramuscular haloperidol and nicotine patches. The patient has a 20 pack-year smoking history. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 120/68 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. On physical exam, you note a poorly kempt woman and the findings in Figure A. Pain is elicited upon examination of cranial nerve III in the right eye. The patient is unable to read a chart on the wall of the exam room and complains of double vision. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 46-year-old man arrives at your clinic complaining of a 5-month history of fatigue and “numbness.” He describes a “tingling” sensation in his fingers and feet, and says sometimes he cannot feel them at all. He admits to being an IV heroin user with his last use being yesterday evening. The patient has also been homeless for three years. He reports that he was sexually assaulted at a shelter, so he is afraid to go back. Instead, he buys his own meals, when he can, with donations. The patient is currently sexually active with two female partners. He has never had testing for sexually transmitted diseases. The patient reports blurry vision, but admits he has not been to an eye doctor for over five years. He denies fever, headache, palpitations, night sweats, abdominal pain, urinary symptoms, or rashes. On exam, the patient appears emaciated. Neurologic examination shows a decreased vibratory sense and proprioception in the fingers and toes. Pupils are equally reactive to light and accommodation. The patient has mild difficulty rising from a chair without using his upper extremities to assist. A CBC is drawn, and results include:

Leukocyte count and differential:
Leukocyte count: 4,400/mm^3
Segmented neutrophils: 60%
Bands: 3%
Eosinophils: 2%
Basophils: < 1%
Lymphocytes: 26%
Monocytes: 7%
Hemoglobin: 9.5 g/dL
Platelet count: 250,000/mm^3
Mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration: 32%
Mean corpuscular volume: 123 µm^3
Reticulocyte count:.8%

A peripheral blood smear is drawn and shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old female presents to her primary care physician for stiffness in her arm. She states that she has been having trouble combing her hair and reaching objects that are high on the shelf. The patient has a past medical history of diabetes mellitus type II, obesity, and hypertension. Her current medications include metformin, insulin, lisinopril, and hydrochlorothiazide. The patient admits to leading a sedentary life in which she tends to stay home and watch television. She does not engage in any physical or strenuous activity. On physical exam the patient has decreased passive and active range of motion of her shoulder. Strength of the patient's upper extremity is 4/5. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old man presents to his primary care physician for a wellness check-up. He states that recently he has been feeling well other than headaches that occur occasionally, which improve with ibuprofen and rest. He has a past medical history of hypertension and headaches and is currently taking hydrochlorothiazide. His temperature is 99.2°F (37.3°C), blood pressure is 157/108 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam reveals a young man who appears healthy. A normal S1 and S2 are auscultated on cardiac exam, and his lungs are clear with good air movement bilaterally. From his previous visit, it was determined that he has an elevated aldosterone and low renin level. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below.

Serum:
Na+: 139 mEq/L
Cl-: 100 mEq/L
K+: 3.7 mEq/L
HCO3-: 29 mEq/L
BUN: 20 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL

Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old woman with a history of chronic hepatitis C infection, hypertension, type II diabetes mellitus, and congestive heart failure presents to her primary care physician with complaints of a new rash. She states that she first noticed the rash two weeks prior, and endorses intermittent itchiness. The patient works as a butcher at a local meat processing shop and is sexually active with several partners. She does not use barrier protection. The patient’s temperature is 98.6°F (37.0°C), pulse is 90/min, blood pressure is 155/95 mmHg, and respirations are 12/min. Physical exam is notable for Figure A. Fine, lace-like white lines are also noted on the patient’s buccal mucosa. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with dizziness. She states she has experienced a sustained sensation of the room spinning that is low grade and constant since this morning. The patient occasionally feels nauseous and has been taking diphenydramine to sleep which helps with her symptoms. The patient is generally healthy, has no other medical conditions, and only endorses eating more garlic recently to get over a cold she had a few days ago. Her temperature is 98.7°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 122/81 mmHg, pulse is 82/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a healthy woman. The patient is sat upright, her head is turned slightly to the right, and she is laid back flat rapidly. This does not provoke any symptoms even when repeated on the left side. A nystagmus is notable on cranial nerve exam as well as bilateral decreased hearing. The patient’s tandem gait is unstable; however, her baseline gait appears unremarkable despite the patient stating she has a sustained sensation of imbalance. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old female is brought to the pediatrician by her parents because of the rash shown in Figure A. The parents report that their child had an episode of pharyngitis one week ago. The child reports feeling nauseated recently and says her knees have been bothering her. Past medical history is insignificant. A stool sample is positive for occult blood. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with a fever, chills, cough, and aches that started 3 days ago. She has also experienced night sweats and chills during this time frame. This morning, she noticed warts and a few small bleeding lesions on her skin. The patient has a past medical history of type I diabetes and asthma and is currently taking insulin, albuterol, and fluticasone. She is generally healthy and just returned from a trip visiting family in the southeastern United States. Her temperature is 102°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 129/82 mmHg, pulse is 107/min, respirations are 19/min, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. Physical exam demonstrates an ill appearing young woman. Pulmonary exam is notable for bilateral coarse breath sounds. Dermatologic exam reveals the findings in Figure A. A chest radiograph is obtained as seen in Figure B. Further diagnostic studies and tests are sent off and are currently pending. Which of the following is the best treatment for the most likely diagnosis?

A 47-year-old woman presents to her ophthalmologist for abnormal vision. The patient was discharged from the hospital 2 weeks ago after a motor vehicle accident where she was given 1L of blood. She also underwent several surgical procedures including enucleation of the right globe and exploratory abdominal laparotomy to stop internal bleeding. Currently, she states that she has noticed decreased vision in her left eye. The patient has a past medical history of poorly controlled diabetes, asthma, and atopic dermatitis. Her temperature is 98.9°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 167/108 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. Physical exam is notable for 20/200 vision in the patient's left eye, which is worse than usual. The patient's left eye appears red and irritated. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 69-year-old man presents to the emergency department in severe abdominal pain. He states he was discharged from the hospital three days ago after being treated for a kidney infection with intravenous antibiotics. Over the last five days, he has developed watery diarrhea and has been in almost constant pain which has now increased to an intensity of 10/10. On exam, his vitals are T 102.3F, HR 125, BP 89/45, RR 20. He has pain with palpation along his lower quadrants with questionable guarding. His CBC is significant for a white blood cell (WBC) count of 25,000 cells/mcL along with Na 140, K 3.3, Cl 90 and HCO3- 15. His lactic acid is 3.6 mmol/L. Figure A illustrates a radiograph of his abdomen. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old man presents to the emergency department with abdominal pain. The patient states that he has pain in his back that radiates to his abdomen. The pain started yesterday and is episodic. He describes the pain as a 10/10 when it occurs. The patient has a past medical history of asthma, anxiety, and chlamydia that was appropriately treated. His current medications include fluoxetine. The patient's lab values are ordered as seen below.

Hemoglobin: 14 g/dL
Hematocrit: 40%
Leukocyte count: 8,500 cells/mm^3 with normal differential
Platelet count: 225,000/mm^3

Serum:
Na+: 140 mEq/L
Cl-: 100 mEq/L
K+: 4.9 mEq/L
HCO3-: 24 mEq/L
BUN: 22 mg/dL
Glucose: 89 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.2 mg/dL
Ca2+: 10.0 mg/dL
AST: 11 U/L
ALT: 11 U/L

Urine:
Color: amber
Nitrites: negative
Na+: 12 mmol/24 hours
Beta-hCG: positive
Red blood cells: 11/hpf

Which of the following is the best test for this patient's most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old man presents to the emergency department for muscle weakness. He states that he was at a rave when he was found down by one of his friends. His friend waited with him to recover, but he has felt ill and abnormally weak. The patient admits to using MDMA, marijuana, and alcohol. Physical exam reveals a young man who responds slowly to your questions. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below.

Urine:
Color: Amber
Marijuana: Positive
Cocaine: Positive
MDMA: Positive
Blood: Positive

An ECG is ordered as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old woman presents to the ED complaining of worsening abdominal pain over the last few hours. She also reports nausea, but denies fever, vomiting, or changes in the appearance of her bowel movements. Her medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, coronary artery disease, stroke, atrial fibrillation, and peptic ulcer disease. Due to her recurrent bleeding peptic ulcers, she does not take warfarin. Her surgical history is significant for an appendectomy as a child. Her medications include metformin, lisinopril, metoprolol, and omeprazole. She has a 50-pack-year history of smoking. Her temperature is 37.6 C (99.7 F), blood pressure is 146/80 mm Hg, pulse is 115/min, and respiratory rate is 20/min. On physical exam, she is in acute distress due to the pain. Pulmonary auscultation reveals scattered wheezes and decreased air entry. Her heart rate is irregularly irregular, with no murmurs, rubs or gallops. Abdominal exam is significant for decreased bowel sounds and diffuse tenderness. Initial laboratory evaluation is as follows:
Na 138 mEq/L, Cl 101 mEq/L, HCO3 12 mEq/L, BUN 21 mg/dL, Cr 0.9 mg/dL, glucose 190 mg/dL, amylase 240 U/L (normal < 65 U/L).
What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 28-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with lower extremity weakness. She was in her usual state of health until 10 days ago. She then began to notice her legs were “tiring out” during her workouts. This progressed to difficulty climbing the stairs to her apartment. She has asthma and uses albuterol as needed. She has no significant surgical or family history. She smokes marijuana daily but denies use of other recreational drugs. She is sexually active with her girlfriend of 2 years. She has never traveled outside of the country but was camping 3 weeks ago. She reports that she had diarrhea for several days after drinking unfiltered water from a nearby stream. On physical examination, she has 1/5 strength in her bilateral lower extremities. She uses her arms to get up from the chair. Achilles and patellar reflexes are absent. A lumbar puncture is performed, and results are as shown below:

Cerebral spinal fluid:
Color: Clear
Pressure: 15 cm H2O
Red blood cell count: 0 cells/µL
Leukocyte count: 3 cells/ µL with lymphocytic predominance
Glucose: 60 mg/dL
Protein: 75 mg/dL

A culture of the cerebral spinal fluid is pending. Which of the following is the part of the management for the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old man presents to the emergency department with shortness of breath. He is an immigrant and does not speak English, but it is clear he is struggling to breathe. You observe the patient struggling to breathe and coughing up large amounts of mucous. A phone call to his home nurse reveals that he has a past medical history of diabetes for which he is not currently taking his medications. He also states the patient recently recovered from a long flight back from his native country where he was visiting a relative in prison. His temperature is 99.1°F (37.3°C), blood pressure is 167/108 mmHg, pulse is 112/min, respirations are 25/min, and oxygen saturation is 78% on room air. A chest radiograph is obtained as seen in Figure A. Physical exam reveals a distressed man who is not cooperative with the exam secondary to his discomfort. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
