A 22-year-old man presents to his primary care provider complaining of a facial rash. He says the rash began 3 weeks ago after hiking in the White Mountains of New Hampshire this summer. Since that time he has also experienced pain in his hands and wrists that is worse in the morning and accompanied by subjective fevers. He denies chest pain, shortness of breath, nausea, or vomiting. Vital signs are 99.6°F (37.6°F), blood pressure is 134/82 mmHg, pulse is 88/min, and respirations are 18/min. Examination demonstrates a rash on the patient's face that spares the nasolabial folds along with oral ulcers. The metacarpophalangeal joints are tender to palpation, and range of motion is limited by pain. Complete blood count demonstrates normocytic anemia with thrombocytopenia. Which of the following is the next best step in diagnosis?

A 62-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician for a regular checkup. The patient worked as a farmer her entire life but recently retired. Since then, she has been sailing the world. She endorses a recent 7 pound weight loss which she attributes to her sailing activities. Otherwise, the patient has no other complaints and feels that she is doing well. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension. Her current medications include atorvastatin, lisinopril, and aspirin. The patient smokes cigarettes and drinks alcohol occasionally. On physical exam, you note an elderly woman in no current distress. Abdominal exam reveals mild epigastric bruising which the patient attributes to sailing. Musculoskeletal exam demonstrates crepitus of the patient's hips. Dermatologic exam reveals the finding in Figure A which the patient has not noticed before, as well as diffuse minor bruises which the patient attributes to her recreational activities. The patient's gait is stable, and she demonstrates 5/5 strength in her upper and lower extremities. Which of the following is the most likely underlying diagnosis for this patient's presentation?

A 27-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician with worsening cough and asthma. The patient reports that she was in her usual state of health until 1 month ago, when she developed a cold. Since then her cold has improved, but she continues to have a cough and worsening asthma symptoms. She says that she has been using her rescue inhaler 3 times a day with little improvement. She is studying for an accounting exam and states that her asthma is keeping her up at night and making it hard for her to focus during the day. The patient admits to smoking tobacco. Her smoking has increased from a half pack per day since she was 17 years old to 1 pack per day during the past month to cope with the stress of her exam. The patient’s temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 110/74 mmHg, pulse is 75/min, and respirations are 15/min with an oxygen saturation of 97% on room air. Physically examination is notable for mild expiratory wheezes bilaterally. Labs are obtained, as shown below:

Serum:
Na+: 144 mEq/L
Cl-: 95 mEq/L
K+: 4.3 mEq/L
HCO3-: 23 mEq/L
Urea nitrogen: 24 mg/dL
Glucose: 100 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.6 mg/dL

Leukocyte count and differential:
Leukocyte count: 13,000/mm^3
Segmented neutrophils: 63%
Eosinophils: 15%
Basophils: < 1%
Lymphocytes: 20%
Monocytes: 1.3%
Hemoglobin: 13.5 g/dL
Hematocrit: 50%
Platelets: 200,000/mm^3

Urinalysis reveals proteinuria and microscopic hematuria. Which of the following is associated with the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old Caucasian female presents to her primary care physician for routine care. She has a longstanding history of diabetes mellitus type 2, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia for which she takes metformin, amlodipine, and atorvastatin. She is generally happy with her health, but does complain of mild discomfort in her chest after dinner each night as well as intermittent itching of her upper back. She smokes one pack of cigarettes per day and drinks two glasses of wine on the weekends. She works as a landscaper at her local golf course. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), pulse is 70/min, blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, and respirations are 12/min. The most recent hemoglobin A1c from two years prior was 6.4% and her fasting fingerstick glucose in the office today is 120 mg/dL. Physical exam is notable for a well-appearing overweight individual with a lesion on her upper back (Figure A). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old man presents to the emergency department complaining of a “curtain” suddenly obscuring his vision in his right eye. He reports for the past few weeks, he has experienced intermittent episodes of seeing flashes of light as well as floaters blocking his visual field. He denies any eye pain or irritation. He notes that since he was a child, he has relied on wearing glasses with thick lenses due to a high degree of myopia. Which of the following images on ophthalmoscopy corresponds with this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with chest pain. She states that her symptoms started a few days ago and have been gradually worsening. The patient admits to drinking alcohol recently and has been vomiting frequently. The patient has a past medical history of alcohol abuse and regularly presents to the emergency department. Her temperature is 102°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 107/65 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for foul-smelling breath and poor dentition with erythema and edema of the patient’s gums. Pain is elicited when the patient swallows and the patient complains that her voice has sounded different recently. Crepitus is palpated in the submandibular region. Dermatologic exam reveals the finding in Figure A. The patient’s ECG demonstrates a left bundle branch block which is consistent with previous ECGs. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 59-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning causing her to experience several episodes of nausea and vomiting. Upon arriving, the patient’s symptoms have resolved. She states her symptoms occurred as she was going to bed. She has never experienced this before, but felt extremely dizzy for roughly 3 minutes. She currently feels at her baseline. The patient is otherwise healthy and only has a history of eczema. Her temperature is 97.7°F (36.5°C), blood pressure is 134/85 mmHg, pulse is 85/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a healthy woman with a normal gait. The patient has a physiologic nystagmus and her cranial nerve exam is unremarkable. The patient’s head is turned to the left and she is laid back on the stretcher, which exacerbates severe symptoms with a nystagmus notable. The patient’s symptoms improve after 2 minutes of being in this position. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old woman with a body mass index of 45 kg/m^2 presents to her primary care doctor with right hip pain. She asserts that the pain is instigated by walking up and down stairs around a construction site which she oversees. On physical exam, her hips are symmetric and equal with no tenderness to palpation bilaterally. Her left lower extremity appears grossly normal with full range of motion. Her right knee appears symmetric, but the patient whimpers when the anteromedial part of the tibial plateau is pressed. No other parts of her knee are tender. No tenderness is elicited with extension, flexion, varus, and valgus movements of the knee. McMurray's test is negative with both internal and external rotation of the right leg. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old woman is found unconscious outside her home by a passing neighbor and is brought to the emergency department by ambulance. Cardio-pulmonary resuscitation is performed and the patient awakens but remains somnolent and confused. She is unable to answer questions or provide any medical history. Her temperature is 98.2°F (36.8°C), blood pressure is 108/62 mmHg, pulse is 110/min and respirations are 20/min. Physical exam shows decreased arousal. Pupils are round, symmetric, and reactive to light bilaterally. Fundoscopy is normal. The patient winces to palpation of the epigastric region and bilateral costovertebral angles. Initial labs are drawn and are shown below:

Serum:
Na+: 137 mEq/L
K+: 3.1 mEq/L
Cl-: 92 mEq/L
HCO3-: 6 mEq/L
BUN: 36 mg/dL
Glucose: 100 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.7 mg/dL

clinical_context: A 62-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with skin lesions. The patient states that she has felt itchy recently, then noticed skin lesions that broke out this morning prompting her to come to the emergency department. The patient states that she recently went camping and hiking in the woods. The patient drinks 1-2 beers per day and smokes 1 pack of cigarettes per day. She is currently sexually active with multiple partners and does not use condoms. The patient was discharged 1 week ago for pneumonia which was treated with azithromycin; however, she feels that her symptoms may be returning. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 157/78 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. On physical exam, you note the findings in Figure A on the patient's arm. The skin lesions are thick and do not break when pressure is applied. Which of the following best describes the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old girl is brought in to the pediatrician by her father because he is concerned that she is not gaining weight. He reports that the patient has a good appetite, eats a varied diet of solid foods, and drinks 2 cups of milk a day. The patient’s father also reports that she has foul-smelling stools over 6 times a day. The patient has a history of recurrent bronchiectasis and chronic sinusitis. On physical examination, multiple nasal polyps are appreciated and scattered rhonchi are heard over both lung fields. The patient is below the 25th percentile in height and weight. Genetic testing is ordered to confirm the suspected diagnosis. Which of the following is most common complication associated with the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old woman with a past medical history of HIV on antiretroviral therapy presents to the emergency department with a rash. She was recently treated for streptococcal pharyngitis, smokes 1 pack of cigarettes per day, and uses IV drugs regularly. The patient lives alone, owns 2 cats, and enjoys hiking and outdoor activities. She states that the rash was initially localized but has been spreading. She states that it is tender to the touch. The patient's vitals are within normal limits, and physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old female comes to the emergency department complaining of blood in her urine and severe back pain. She reports that the pain is left-sided, colicky, and began acutely this morning. The pain occasionally radiates to her left groin. She also reports increased urinary frequency and an episode of blood-tinged urine. According to the patient, this has happened multiple times before. Her medical history is also notable for hypertension, type II diabetes mellitus, and obstructive sleep apnea. Her current medications include aspirin, metformin, and lisinopril. The patient’s temperature is 100.4°F (38°C), blood pressure is 148/85 mmHg, pulse is 71/min, and respirations are 14/min with an oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. Physical examination is significant for left-sided costovertebral angle tenderness. A urine dipstick is heme-positive. A urinalysis is pending. Labs are drawn, as shown below:

Serum:
Na+: 144 mEq/L
Cl-: 95 mEq/L
K+: 4.3 mEq/L
HCO3-: 23 mEq/L
Urea nitrogen: 18 mg/dL
Glucose: 142 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL
Calcium: 7.8 mg/dL

A radiograph is obtained, as shown in Figure A. In addition to increasing fluid intake, which of the following can help the patient prevent future episodes of the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department by her parents for worsening symptoms. The patient recently saw her pediatrician for an acute episode of sinusitis. At the time, the pediatrician prescribed decongestants and sent the patient home. Since then, the patient has developed a nasal discharge with worsening pain. The patient has a past medical history of asthma which is well controlled with albuterol. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 90/48 mmHg, pulse is 124/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. On physical exam, you note a healthy young girl. Cardiopulmonary exam is within normal limits. Inspection of the patient's nose reveals a unilateral purulent discharge mixed with blood. The rest of the patient's exam is within normal limits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old woman presents to the emergency department after a motor vehicle accident. The patient was at a stop when she was rear-ended from behind by a vehicle traveling at 11 miles per hour. The patient complains of severe back pain but states she otherwise feels well. The patient is currently seeing a physical therapist who is giving her exercises to alleviate the back pain that is present every morning, relived by activity, and worse with inactivity. She is a student at the university and is struggling with her grades. Her temperature is 98.4°F (36.9°C), blood pressure is 117/78 mmHg, pulse is 116/min, respirations are 12/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam demonstrates a decreased range of motion of the patient's spine and tenderness to palpation over the vertebrae. The rest of the exam is deferred due to pain. The patient is requesting a note to excuse her from final exams and work. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 61-year-old man presents to the emergency department with complaint of sudden onset, painless vision loss in his left eye upon waking up this morning. The patient says that he had no visual abnormalities prior to the incident and has had 20/20 vision in both eyes since undergoing cataract surgery the previous year. His past medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia. An ophthalmology consult is called, and fundoscopic examination confirms the diagnosis (Figure A). Which of the following is the most likely cause for this patient’s vision loss?

A 47-year-old woman presents to the emergency department due to a rash. She states the rash started last night and is very concerning to her. The patient cannot remember being exposed to any environmental stimuli such as new detergents or poison ivy. The patient recently started following with a primary care provider who is helping her manage her arthritis and a new onset cough. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 127/68 mmHg, pulse is 125/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the findings of coalescing erythematous macules, bullae, desquamation, and mucositis only on the upper half of her back. Cardiopulmonary exam and abdominal exam are within normal limits. Inspection of the patient’s oropharynx reveals ulcers and erythema. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old girl is brought in by her father to her pediatrician for headache and nausea. Her headaches began approximately 3 weeks ago and occur in the morning. Throughout the 3 weeks, her nausea has progressively worsened, and she had 2 episodes of emesis 1 day ago. On physical exam, cranial nerves are grossly intact, and her visual field is intact. The patient has a broad-based gait and difficulty with heel-to-toe walking, as well as head titubation. Fundoscopy demonstrates papilledema. A T1 and T2 MRI of the brain is demonstrated in Figures A and B, respectively. Which of the following is most likely the diagnosis?

A 24-year-old man presents to his primary care physician for a wellness exam. He currently has no acute concerns but has been feeling hopeless, has a poor appetite, difficulty with concentration, and trouble with sleep. He says that he has poor self-esteem and that his symptoms have been occurring for the past 3 years. He has had moments where he felt better, but it lasted a few weeks out of the year. He currently lives alone and does not pursue romantic relationships because he feels he is not attractive. He has a past medical history of asthma. His mother is alive and healthy. His father committed suicide and suffered from major depressive disorder. On physical exam, the patient has a gloomy demeanor and appears restless and anxious. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 71-year-old male arrives to your clinic complaining of sudden vision loss. He reports that he had been in his usual state of health, until waking up this morning unable to see out of his right eye. He denies pain, but reports his right eye “feels funny.” The patient’s medical history is significant for a previous myocardial infarction, hypertension, and osteoporosis. His current medications include aspirin, metoprolol, rovustatin, lisinopril, and alendronate. The patient’s temperature is 98°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 145/86 mmHg, pulse is 62/min, and respirations are 12/min with an oxygen saturation of 98% O2 on room air. On physical exam, the patient's pupils are symmetrical in size and equally reactive to light with accommodation. Fundoscopic exam of the right eye is shown in Figure A. Left optic fundus is unremarkable. Of the following, what is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with joint pain. She states that since yesterday she has had joint pain, and today she noticed a rash. The patient does not have a significant past medical history. The patient smokes cigars, drinks 1 to 4 drinks per day, is sexually active, and uses cocaine occasionally. Her temperature is 101°F (38.3°C), blood pressure is 125/65 mmHg, pulse is 80/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam reveals pustular skin lesions and an inflamed and painful right knee that is warm to the touch. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment for the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old man presents to his primary care provider for fatigue. He states that he has felt fatigued for the past 6 months and has tried multiple diets and sleep schedules to improve his condition, but none have succeeded. He has no significant past medical history. He is currently taking a multivitamin, folate, B12, iron, fish oil, whey protein, baby aspirin, copper, and krill oil. His temperature is 98.8°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 107/58 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Laboratory values are as seen below.

Hemoglobin: 8 g/dL
Hematocrit: 24%
Leukocyte count: 6,500/mm^3 with normal differential
Platelet count: 147,000/mm^3

Physical exam is notable for decreased proprioception in the lower extremities and 4/5 strength in the patient's upper and lower extremities. Which of the following is the best next step in management to confirm the diagnosis?

A 19-year-old university student presents to the student clinic with painful joints. She states that over the past week her right wrist has become increasingly stiff. This morning she noticed pain and stiffness in her left ankle and left knee. The patient has celiac disease and takes a daily multivitamin. She says she is sexually active with multiple male and female partners. She smokes marijuana but denies intravenous drug abuse. She recently traveled to Uganda to volunteer at a clinic that specialized in treating patients with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). She also went on an extended hiking trip last week in New Hampshire. Physical exam reveals swelling of the right wrist and a warm, swollen, erythematous left knee. The left Achilles tendon is tender to palpation. There are also multiple vesicopustular lesions on the dorsum of the right hand. No vaginal discharge is appreciated. Arthrocentesis of the left knee is performed. Synovial fluid results are shown below:

Synovial fluid:
Appearance: Cloudy
Leukocyte count: 40,000/mm^3 with neutrophil predominance

Gram stain is negative. A synovial fluid culture is pending. Which of the following is the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old African American male presents to his primary care physician with complaints of shortness of breath, fevers, and generalized joint pains. Vital signs are all stable and within normal limits. Physical examination is significant for cervical lymphadenopathy, coarse breath sounds bilaterally, and lesions on his bilateral legs, shown in Figure A. A chest radiograph is obtained and is shown in Figure B. Which of the following findings would be most consistent with this patient's likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by her coworker for loss of consciousness. While working in her office, she fell from her chair, hit her head on a carpeted floor, and began to have generalized tonic-clonic seizures. The episode lasted approximately 3 minutes, and she felt confused afterwards. Upon interviewing the patient, she does not recall what happened prior or during the convulsive episode. She currently endorses a headache and tongue pain. She denies bowel or bladder incontinence. She reports having night sweats and an unintentional 15-pound loss over the course of 2 months. She denies any alcohol use but reports to have smoked 1 pack of cigarettes per day for the past 15 years, and previously worked as a farmer. Physical examination is notable for mild left-sided weakness, bilateral tongue bites, and findings demonstrated in Figure A. A non-contrast CT scan of the head is demonstrated in Figure B. Which of the following is most likely the diagnosis?

A 41-year-old man comes to the office for an evaluation of a rash. He reports the rash started 2 months ago on his knees and the rash has now appeared on his elbows. He denies pain or burning, but says the areas are mildly itchy and when he scratches them, they bleed. The patient is embarrassed because he works as a massage therapist. He reports some fatigue, but attributes it to stress. He denies headache, weight loss, or joint pains. He has seasonal allergies and takes daily loratadine. He had a tonsillectomy as a child. His brother has alopecia and his daughter has vitiligo. He smokes 1 pack a day and denies alcohol or other recreational drug use. He is sexually active with his wife of 15 years. On physical examination, there are symmetric erythematous plaques with overlying scales on the extensor surfaces of bilateral knees and elbows. One of the plaques is shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old female with a past medical history of IV drug use and obesity presents to the emergency department with fever. She reports fatigue and nasal congestion for about one week, which she thinks she caught from her brother who has an upper respiratory infection. She has no history of cardiac disease and endorses recent IV drug use. Her temperature is 101.8°F (38.8°C), blood pressure is 132/87 mmHg, pulse is 106/min, respirations are 15/min, and SpO2 is 97%. On physical exam, she appears to be in moderate distress. Her lungs are clear to auscultation, she has distant cardiac sounds, and the physical exam finding in Figure A is seen. Two sets of blood cultures drawn 12 hours apart are both positive for Staphylococcus aureus.

Which of the following would be necessary to confirm the diagnosis of this patient’s illness?

A 6-year-old girl presents to her primary care physician with hip pain that started this morning. The patient claims the pain is severe and is stopping her from skateboarding. The patient recently recovered from an upper respiratory infection that she caught from her siblings but has otherwise been healthy. The patient has a past medical history of obesity. Her temperature is 98.1°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 100/55 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. On physical exam, you note an obese girl in no acute distress. Cardiopulmonary exam is within normal limits. Inspection of the hip reveals no abnormalities or swelling. The hip exhibits a normal range of motion and physical exam only elicits minor pain. The patient's gait appears normal and pain is elicited when the patient jumps or runs. Which of the following is the best next step in management for this patient's most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician for fatigue, weight loss, and diffuse pruritus. The patient has a past medical history of multiple admissions for severe abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea as well as several episodes of ascending cholangitis which were successfully treated. She is currently a member of Alcoholics Anonymous. Her temperature is 98.2°F (36.8°C), blood pressure is 124/75 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Urinalysis is notable only for a dark urine sample with no red blood cells present. A rectal exam reveals pale stool and grossly visible blood. Physical exam is otherwise notable for pruritis, jaundice, and scleral icterus. Which of the following is the most likely underlying diagnosis?

A 17-year-old girl presents to her primary care physician for eye pain. The patient states that it has been going on for the past 3 days and has been steadily worsening. She recently suffered a superior orbital fracture secondary to playing football without a helmet that required no treatment other than to refrain from contact sports. That patient's past medical history is non-contributory, and her vitals are within normal limits. Physical exam demonstrates pain and swelling inferior to the patient's eye near the lacrimal duct. When pressure is applied to the area expressible pus is noted. Cranial nerves II-XII are grossly intact. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 69-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician with hip and back pain. The patient states that this weekend she had a barbecue. When she was lifting a heavy object she suddenly felt pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as in her buttocks but states that at times it travels down her leg. The patient states that it feels, "electrical." The patient has a past medical history of obesity, diabetes, depression, anxiety, diverticulosis, constipation, and a surgical repair of her anterior cruciate ligament. Her current medications include metformin, insulin, lisinopril, fluoxetine, and sodium docusate. Which of the following is most likely to help confirm the diagnosis?

A 30-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician complaining of headaches. She states that over the past month she has been trying to study for an accounting exam, but she finds it increasingly more difficult to focus due to her headaches. She also complains of lower extremity muscle cramping. She has no significant past medical history and takes ibuprofen and acetaminophen as needed. The patient’s temperature is 98°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 168/108 mmHg, and pulse is 75/min. Labs are obtained, as shown below:

Serum:
pH (VBG): 7.50
Na: 146 mEq/L
K+: 3.2 mEq/L
Cl-: 104 mEq/L
HCO3-: 32 mEq/L
Urea nitrogen: 20 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
Glucose: 85 mg/dL

An ultrasound reveals a hypoechoic lesion within the right adrenal gland. A 2 cm right-sided homogeneous adrenal mass is confirmed with computed tomography. Which of the following findings is associated with the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician with a chief complaint of "failing health." She states that she typically can converse with animals via telepathy, but is having trouble right now due to the weather. She has begun taking an assortment of Peruvian herbs to little avail. Otherwise she is not currently taking any medications. The patient lives alone and works in a health food store. She states that her symptoms have persisted for the past eight months. On physical exam, you note a healthy young woman who is dressed in an all burlap ensemble. When you are obtaining the patient's medical history there are several times she is attempting to telepathically connect with the animals in the vicinity. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A purified protein derivative test revealing a 20 mm wheal and a chest radiograph with hilar lymphadenopathy support a diagnosis of active tuberculosis. The patient is started on appropriate therapy.
