A 70-year-old man presents to an ophthalmology clinic for bilaterally blurred vision. His symptoms have progressed gradually over several years, but he recently became concerned when he noticed that he could no longer read his newspaper without the help of a magnifying glass. He also mentions that his eyes have been “playing tricks on him,” pointing out that the edges of the examination table appear curved, when he knows they are usually straight. Physical exam is unremarkable. Fundoscopic exam (shown in Figure A) is similar in both eyes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old homeless woman is brought to the emergency department after she was found unconscious at the park. The patient's past medical history is unknown; however, she was admitted to the emergency department 2 times over the past year for severe pain treated with hydromorphone and IV fluids. Her temperature is 100°F (37.8°C), blood pressure is 97/48 mmHg, pulse is 140/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. The patient smells of alcohol and is covered in emesis. Basic laboratory values are ordered as seen below.

Hemoglobin: 6 g/dL
Hematocrit: 20%
Leukocyte count: 6,500/mm^3 with normal differential
Platelet count: 197,000/mm^3
Reticulocyte count: 0.4%

Which of the following is associated with the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician complaining of subjective fever, cough, and night sweats. She states that over the past 2 months she has “not felt like myself.” She has lost 12 lbs over this time period. Two weeks ago, she started experiencing night sweats and cough. This morning she decided to take her temperature and reports it was “high.” She has a history of HIV and admits to inconsistently taking her anti-retrovirals. A chest radiograph reveals a cavitary lesion in the left upper lobe. An interferon-gamma release assay is positive, and the patient is started on appropriate antimicrobial therapy. A month later she is seen in clinic for follow-up. Lab work is obtained, as shown below:

Leukocyte count: 11,000/mm^3 with normal differential
Hemoglobin: 9.2 g/dL
Platelet count: 400,000/mm^3
Mean corpuscular volume (MCV): 75 µm^3

Based on these results, a peripheral smear is sent and shows Pappenheimer bodies. Which of the following is the most accurate test for the patient’s diagnosis?

A 28-year-old man presents to the emergency department with lateral knee pain that started this morning. The patient is a college student who is currently on the basketball team. He states his pain started after he twisted his knee. His current medications include albuterol and ibuprofen. The patient's vitals are within normal limits and physical exam is notable for tenderness to palpation over the lateral right knee. When the patient lays on his left side and his right hip is extended and abducted it does not lower to the table in a smooth fashion and adduction causes discomfort. The rest of his exam is within normal limits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 12-month-old girl is brought in by her father who is worried about pallor. He says that the patient has always been fair-skinned, but over the past month relatives have commented that she appears more pale. The father says that the patient seems to tire easy, but plays well with her older sister and has even started to walk. He denies bloody or black stools, easy bruising, or excess bleeding. He states that she is a picky eater, but she loves crackers and whole milk. On physical examination, pallor of the conjunctiva is noted. There is a grade II systolic ejection murmur best heard over the lower left sternal border that increases when the patient is supine. Labs are drawn as shown below:

Leukocyte count: 6,500/mm^3 with normal differential
Hemoglobin: 6.4 g/dL
Platelet count: 300,000/mm^3
Mean corpuscular volume (MCV): 71 µm^3
Reticulocyte count: 2.0%

Serum iron: 34 mcg/dL
Serum ferritin: 6 ng/mL (normal range 7 to 140 ng/mL)
Total iron binding capacity (TIBC): 565 mcg/dL (normal range 240 to 450 mcg/dL)

On peripheral blood smear, there is microcytosis, hypochromia, and mild anisocytosis without basophilic stippling. Which of the following is the next best step in management for the patient’s diagnosis?

A 59-year-old woman presents to her ophthalmologist for an annual eye exam. The patient reports feeling well and has noticed some changes in her visual acuity. Medical history is significant for hypertension, type II diabetes, and ankylosing spondylitis. She is currently taking lisinopril, metformin, and naproxen. Family history is significant for glaucoma in her mother and father. Her intraocular pressure is 17 mmHg in the left eye and 18 mmHg in the right eye. The patient undergoes a slit-lamp examination and the findings are shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 52-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a headache and dizziness for the past month. The patient reports that about 4 weeks ago she developed a “nagging” headache. She thought she had a cold, so she tried over the counter ibuprofen that provided only mild and temporary relief. Recently, she also started feeling dizzy and nauseous, which only resolves when she steps outside to shovel the snow. The patient’s medical history is significant for hypertension, type II diabetes mellitus, and asthma. Her medications include amlodipine, metformin, glimepiride, and a fluticasone/salmeterol inhaler. The patient has been living at her upstate cabin for the past 5 weeks but denies other recent travel. She denies smoking tobacco or illicit drug use. The patient’s temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 130/78 mmHg, pulse is 72/min, and respirations are 16/min with an oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. The patient is currently asymptomatic while sitting in the office, and physical examination is unremarkable. Labs are drawn, as shown below:

Hemoglobin: 20 g/dL
Hematocrit: 60%
Leukocyte count: 10,050 cells/mm^3 with normal differential
Platelet count: 350,000/mm^3

Which of the following underlies the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old woman presents to her pediatrician for a wellness checkup. She has no complaints and states that she was recently hired as a construction worker. The patient has a past medical history of asthma and antisocial personality disorder. She is not currently taking any medications. She admits to smoking 1 pack of cigarettes per day. Her temperature is 98.8°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 127/78 mmHg, pulse is 70/min, respirations are 16/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the findings in Figure A. Which of the following is the diagnostic finding for this patient's most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with fatigue and a change in her memory. The patient and her husband state that over the past several weeks the patient has been more confused and irritable and has had trouble focusing. She has had generalized and non-specific pain in her muscles and joints and is constipated. Her temperature is 99.3°F (37.4°C), blood pressure is 172/99 mmHg, pulse is 79/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is unremarkable. Laboratory studies are ordered as seen below.

Hemoglobin: 9.0 g/dL
Hematocrit: 30%
Leukocyte count: 6,500/mm^3 with normal differential
Platelet count: 166,000/mm^3
MCV: 78 fL

Serum:
Na+: 141 mEq/L
Cl-: 103 mEq/L
K+: 4.6 mEq/L
HCO3-: 25 mEq/L
BUN: 20 mg/dL
Glucose: 99 mg/dL
Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL
Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL

Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old woman presents to the emergency department for abdominal pain. The patient states that she has had abdominal pain for a while, but it became unbearable today and she is concerned. She also endorses a weight loss of 20 pounds this past month and complains of bulky and foul-smelling stools. The patient is homeless and is currently living by a local wash where she obtains her drinking water and cleans her clothes. She admits to recently eating raw meat that she found. The patient has a past medical history of alcohol abuse, malnutrition, Wernicke-Korsakoff psychosis, IV drug use, and a recent hospitalization for intoxication of unknown etiology. The patient is not taking any medications currently. Her temperature is 99.1°F (37.3°C), blood pressure is 100/67 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 11/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. On physical exam, the patient complains of epigastric tenderness. Cardiopulmonary exam is within normal limits. The patient is started on IV fluids, thiamine, folate, magnesium, and dextrose. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below:

Hemoglobin: 9.0 g/dL
Hematocrit: 25%
Leukocyte count: 5,500 cells/mm^3 with normal differential
Platelet count: 222,000/mm^3

Serum:
Na+: 137 mEq/L
Cl-: 102 mEq/L
K+: 4.1 mEq/L
HCO3-: 24 mEq/L
BUN: 24 mg/dL
Glucose: 68 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.4 mg/dL
Ca2+: 9.8 mg/dL
Amylase: 22 U/L
Lipase: 22 U/L
Aspartate aminotransferase (AST): 58 U/L
Alanine aminotransferase (ALT): 18 U/L

A computed tomography (CT) scan is obtained as seen in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old homeless woman presents to the emergency department for a rash. She states she has noticed the rash for the past several weeks and that it has not been improving. The patient has no history of medical care and no previous diagnoses. Review of systems is positive for a persistent dry cough and recent weight loss. Her temperature is 100°F (37.8°C), blood pressure is 107/68 mmHg, pulse is 110/min, respirations are 16/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old woman presents to the emergency department after a head on motor vehicle collision. The patient is currently not responding to questions and is subsequently intubated. An initial FAST exam is negative. Her temperature is 97.5°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 62/42 mmHg, and pulse is 185/min. A massive transfusion protocol is initiated. The patient’s vitals improve to a pulse of 100/min and a blood pressure of 92/62. A chest radiograph is performed as seen in Figure A. After the chest radiograph has been performed, the patient’s vitals are 60/45 mmHg with a pulse of 178/min. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician for a skin rash that has recently developed and is very itchy. The patient has a past medical history of asthma, seasonal allergies, constipation, anxiety, and depression. Her current medications include albuterol, fluticasone, diphenhydramine, fluoxetine, metformin, and clonazepam. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 139/67 mmHg, pulse is 80/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Pulmonary exam is notable for mild wheezes and good air movement. Cardiac exam reveals a normal rate and rhythm. Dermatologic exam reveals the findings seen in Figure A. Which of the following best describes the most likely diagnosis?

A 15-year-old female presents to her primary care doctor for "eye pain." She states that she has noticed her left eye hurting more over the past four days. She normally wears disposable contact lenses daily but could not wear them because of the heightened sensation of something foreign in her eye. She has noticed occasional sensitivity to light. She denies any headaches, changes in vision, or pain with eye movement. She further denies any frank ocular or oral discharge but feels like something might pop if she squeezes hard enough. An image of her left eye is seen in Figure A. The right eye is completely healthy appearing. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 43-year-old woman is asked to be seen in the hospital for a worsening rash. She was admitted to the hospital 3 days ago after a fall. Her blood alcohol level at the time was 0.16%. Two days ago she noticed a rash forming on her legs. Since then, the rash has worsened. She denies pain or bleeding but endorses mild pruritis. Her medical history is significant for alcohol abuse, intravenous drug use, and hepatitis C. She does not take any medications. The patient’s temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 130/74 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, and respirations are 16/min. On physical examination, there is an abrasion on her right elbow and her right hip. There is no drainage or fluctuance. She has 1+ pitting edema of her bilateral lower extremities. The patient’s right leg is shown in Figure A, which is nearly identical to the left leg. There are also a few scattered violaceous papules on her buttocks. The appearance of the rash does not change with palpation. A skin biopsy is obtained, which reveals neutrophils perivascularly and within the vessel walls along with edema and fibrinoid necrosis. Immunofluorescence shows deposition of fibrinogen, C3, IgG, and IgM within the vessel walls. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with dizziness. She states she has experienced a sustained sense of disequilibrium for the past 2 days. She feels that the floor is unstable/moving. The patient is otherwise healthy and does not have any other medical diagnoses. The patient is currently taking vitamin C as multiple family members are currently ill and she does not want to get sick. Her temperature is 98.1°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 120/83 mmHg, pulse is 73/min, respirations are 16/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a horizontal nystagmus. The Dix-Hallpike maneuver does not provoke symptoms and examination of the patient’s cranial nerves is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with fever, nausea, and vomiting. The patient states that her symptoms started last night and have persisted to this morning. She has a past medical history of asthma, and her current medications include albuterol and fluticasone. Her temperature is 102°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 110/60 mmHg, pulse is 95/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. On physical exam, the patient seems uncomfortable. She requests that the lights in the room stay turned off during the physical exam. The patient's cardiac exam demonstrates a normal rate and rhythm, and her pulmonary exam is clear to auscultation bilaterally. Musculoskeletal exam reveals diminished mobility of the neck in all four directions, with flexion of the neck causing the patient discomfort. Lumbar puncture is performed and results are seen below.

Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF):
Cell count: 175/mm^3
Cl-: 119 mEq/L
Glucose: 49 mg/dL
Pressure: 150 mmH2O
Total protein: 55 mg/dL

Which of the following is the best treatment for this patient's most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old man presents to the emergency department with retrosternal pain that started this evening. The patient states that his symptoms started as he was going to bed after taking his medications. He describes the pain as sudden in onset, worse with swallowing, and not associated with exertion. The patient has a past medical history of diabetes, anemia, and congestive heart failure and is currently taking metoprolol, insulin, metformin, iron, and lisinopril. His temperature is 99.2°F (37.3°C), blood pressure is 125/63 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 100% on room air. Physical exam is notable for an obese man who appears uncomfortable. An initial electrocardiogram (ECG) demonstrates sinus rhythm, and a set of troponins are pending. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old man presents to his primary care physician with a chief complaint of joint and muscle pain. He states that he has a general aching/pain in his joints that lasts all day. He states that the pain is constant and is not relieved by rest or activity. In addition, the patient complains of pain in his hands at times. Finally, he occasionally notices trouble swallowing when he is eating. The patient has a past medical history of anxiety and is not currently taking any medications. On physical exam you note a healthy young man with a sunburn. His hands are mildly edematous, and you note the findings in Figure A. Laboratory values are ordered and are below:

Serum:
Na+: 145 mEq/L
K+: 4.4 mEq/L
Cl-: 100 mEq/L
HCO3-: 24 mEq/L
BUN: 9 mg/dL
Glucose: 70 mg/dL
Creatinine:.7 mg/dL
Ca2+: 10 mg/dL
Mg2+: 1.8 mEq/L

Which of the following antibodies is most likely to aid in making the diagnosis in this patient?

A 27-year-old man presents with acute abdominal pain in his right upper quadrant. The pain came on suddenly while he was eating dinner. After this pain he began feeling dizzy and came to the emergency department. In the ED, his blood pressure is 75/40 mmHg, pulse is 100/minute, and he is afebrile. On physical exam, he feels too light-headed to ambulate. He demonstrates normal bowel sounds with tenderness upon palpation in the right upper quadrant. The patient is deemed too unstable for imaging. An abdominal radiograph and CT are reviewed from a recent previous visit to the ED for mild abdominal pain, and are shown in Figures A and B, respectively. Which of the following specific additional findings in his history supports the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old girl is brought to her pediatrician by her father who is worried about her clumsiness. He states that over the past 3 months he has noticed progressive weakness. She used to climb trees and run outside with her cousins, but now she says she gets “too tired.” He’s recently noticed her starting to “walk funny,” despite having “muscular legs.” Upon physical examination, the patient has calf muscle hypertrophy. She uses her arms to rise out of the chair. Labs are obtained that show an elevated creatine kinase. Genetic analysis detects a dystropin gene mutation. A muscle biopsy is performed that reveals reduced dystrophin. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old nurse presents with left-sided chest pain and nonproductive cough. She thinks both the chest pain and the cough began about two months ago. She recently joined a meditation group and found that the deep breathing exercises exacerbate her chest pain. The patient denies headaches, fever, or chills. She reports a 3 lb weight loss over the last two weeks, which she attributes to a change in her diet that she and her husband recently started. The patient drinks a glass or two of whiskey on the weekends and is a non-smoker. The patient’s medical history is significant for type II diabetes and Hodgkin lymphoma. She was treated with chemotherapy and radiation 25 years ago without complications. Her current medications include metformin and glyburide. Her HbA1c is 7.5%. Her temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 121/82 mmHg, pulse is 86/min, respirations are 12/min, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. Physical exam is notable for coarse rhonchi in the left lung. There is no appreciable lymphadenopathy. A chest radiograph is performed, which is shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 25-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician with lower back pain. She states that she has had the pain for the past two years. The patient works as a butcher, and recently was moving heavy meat carcasses. The patient states that her pain is worse in the morning and that nothing improves it aside from swimming. The patient has a past medical history of anabolic steroid abuse, acne, hypertension and obesity. Her current medications are hydrochlorothiazide, ibuprofen, topical benzoyl peroxide, and acetaminophen. On physical exam there is no tenderness upon palpation of the spine. There is limited range of motion of the spine in all 4 directions. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 66-year-old woman presents to the clinic for evaluation of a new skin lesion on her hand. She is concerned because the lesion has grown rapidly over the previous 2 weeks. She endorses traumatizing the area and notes that there was some bleeding. Her past medical history is significant for chronic renal failure for which she received a renal transplant 5 years prior, as well as multiple surgeries for skin cancers. Her current medications include aspirin, atorvastatin, prednisone, tacrolimus, and mycophenolate mofetil. Physical exam is notable for a 2 x 2.5 cm nodular lesion of the dorsal hand (Figure A). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 80-year-old woman comes to the clinic for a follow-up visit. She has a long history of diabetes mellitus and recently had her diabetic screening exams (including a hemoglobin A1c of 7.2%), a normal foot examination, and normal lipid levels. Although she failed metformin and sulfonylurea therapy, the patient's diabetes is now well-controlled with glargine and insulin lispro. The patient states that she still drives and can see highway billboards and signs without trouble. She rarely reads, opting to spend her retirement playing golf. During the patient's eye exam one month ago, the ophthalmologist's fundoscopic examination revealed scattered bright yellow drusen seen in Figure A. Visual examination today is 20/40 OD (right eye) and 20/40 OS (left eye). Two years ago, her visual acuity was 20/20 in both eyes. She states that she just has dry eyes and needs to blink several times in order to get a perfect visual exam score. She denies any floaters, diplopia, or blurred vision. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 75-year-old man presents to the physician with a complaint of a frequent need to void at nighttime, which has been disrupting his sleep. He notes embarrassingly that he is often unable to reach the bathroom in time, and experiences urinary leakage throughout the night as well as during the day. The patient undergoes urodynamic testing and a urinalysis is obtained which is normal. He is instructed by the physician to perform behavioral training to improve his bladder control. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis contributing to this patient’s symptoms?

A 68-year-old woman is brought to her primary care physician's office by her husband due to "itchy" blisters. He reports that they were gardening yesterday when his wife began complaining of generalized itching. She then woke up this morning with multiple pruritic blisters. Her husband tried using calamine lotion with no significant improvement. The patient’s medical history is significant for early dementia, asthma, hypertension, and inflammatory bowel syndrome. Her medications include aspirin and lisinopril. Her temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 121/82 mmHg, pulse is 86/min, respirations are 12/min, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. Physical examination shows areas of excoriation and tense bullae on her arms. A punch biopsy is obtained for immunofluorescence, which is shown in Figure A. Which of the following is associated with this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with vomiting. She states that she has experienced severe vomiting starting last night that has not been improving. She states that her symptoms improve with hot showers. The patient has presented to the emergency department with a similar complaint several times in the past as well as for intravenous drug abuse. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 127/68 mmHg, pulse is 110/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is deferred as the patient is actively vomiting. Which of the following is associated with the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old female presents to her primary care physician with pain along the bottom of her foot. The patient is a long-time runner but states that the pain has been getting worse recently. She states that when running and at rest she has a burning and aching pain along the bottom of her foot that sometimes turns to numbness. Taking time off from training does not improve her symptoms. The patient has a past medical history of surgical repair of her Achilles tendon, ACL, and medial meniscus. She is currently not taking any medications. The patient lives with her husband and they both practice a vegan lifestyle. On physical exam the patient states that she is currently not experiencing any pain in her foot but rather is experiencing numbness/tingling along the plantar surface of her foot. Strength is 5/5 and reflexes are 2+ in the lower extremities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with pain and a rash on her finger. She states that it started a week ago and thinks it is associated with cutting her finger on a pipe. She is generally healthy and has no past medical history. Her temperature is 98.7°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 129/82 mmHg, pulse is 83/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A, and there is pain with palpation of the finger. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with severe pain. The patient, who is a construction worker, was at work when she suddenly experienced severe pain in her arms, legs, chest, and back. She has experienced this before and was treated 2 months ago for a similar concern. Her temperature is 100°F (37.8°C), blood pressure is 127/68 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for tenderness to palpation of the patient's legs, chest, abdomen, and arms. Laboratory values are obtained and shown below.

Hemoglobin: 10 g/dL
Hematocrit: 30%
Leukocyte count: 8,500/mm^3 with normal differential
Platelet count: 199,000/mm^3

Serum:
Na+: 139 mEq/L
Cl-: 100 mEq/L
K+: 4.9 mEq/L
HCO3-: 25 mEq/L
BUN: 23 mg/dL
LDH: 327 U/L
Glucose: 99 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL
AST: 12 U/L
ALT: 10 U/L

Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 77-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with a change in her mental status. The patient’s son states that she can cook and clean up after herself and only needs help paying bills. Yesterday the patient seemed fine; however, this morning he noticed that she struggled to perform simple tasks and was forgetful while cooking, leaving the stove on. They recently returned from a trip to Mexico and admit to drinking unfiltered water and eating local cuisines while abroad. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension and diabetes. Her temperature is 97.5°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 187/118 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 16/min, and oxygen saturation is 100% on room air. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with nausea and vomiting. The patient states that she has felt nauseous for the past week and began vomiting last night. She thought her symptoms would resolve but decided to come in when her symptoms worsened. She feels that her symptoms are exacerbated with large fatty meals and when she drinks alcohol. Her husband recently returned from a cruise with symptoms of vomiting and diarrhea. The patient has a past medical history of poorly managed diabetes, constipation, anxiety, dyslipidemia, and hypertension. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 197/128 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. Physical exam reveals a systolic murmur heard loudest along the left upper sternal border. Abdominal exam reveals an obese, tympanitic and distended abdomen with a 3 cm scar in the right lower quadrant. Vascular exam reveals weak pulses in the lower extremities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician with left hip pain, stiffness, and hearing loss. The patient has a past medical history of diabetes and obesity. She played professional football when she was younger and is currently retired. The patient lives at home alone and admits to having lost some weight recently. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 167/98 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. A CT scan of the head is shown in Figure A, completed as a part of the workup for migraine at a recent emergency department visit. Physical exam reveals bilateral hearing loss but is otherwise unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with altered mental status. She was at work as a construction worker when her coworkers found her down at the work site. The patient recently underwent anesthesia for an appendectomy several months ago. She also has a past medical history of schizophrenia well controlled with haloperidol and is currently taking phenytoin for epilepsy. She is also currently taking propranolol for anxiety and hyperthyroidism. Her temperature is 106°F (41.1°C), blood pressure is 109/62 mmHg, pulse is 170/min, respirations are 23/min, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. Physical exam is notable for an altered woman with a Glasgow Coma Scale of 10. She has minimal muscle tone and is incoherent when answering questions. The patient is covered in sweat and dirt. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old man presents to the emergency department with eye pain. He states that for the past 2 days he has experienced severe eye pain and discharge from his eye. The patient has a past medical history of type I diabetes and is currently taking insulin. His temperature is 102°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 127/68 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. Examination of cranial nerve III elicits pain. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old child with a history of abdominal and thigh pain that runs in her family is brought into the emergency room by her father. Her father states they have a "blood disease." He also states the child was coughing and had fever to 101.1 F over the last three days and has been suddenly feeling much worse. On exam, the vitals are HR 110, BP 100/60, RR 20, T 101.5 F. CBC is significant for Hgb 3.2, WBC 2.1, Hct 10, Plts 30000. The reticulocyte count is 1% and the MCV is 81. Bone marrow biopsy shows hypocellular marrow with fatty tissue. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old girl presents to the emergency department with a fever and a rash. This morning the patient was irritable and had a fever which gradually worsened throughout the day. She also developed a rash prior to presentation. She was previously healthy and is not currently taking any medications. Her temperature is 102.0°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 90/50 mmHg, pulse is 160/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a scarlatiniform rash with flaccid blisters that rupture easily, covering more than 60% of the patient’s body surface. The lesions surround the mouth but do not affect the mucosa, and palpation of the rash is painful. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old man presents to your clinic with a 6-month history of pain in his hands. The pain is worse in the morning but is present throughout the day despite his use of ibuprofen. Additionally, his left 4th finger recently began to swell and is particularly painful. He has also begun to notice changes in his nails, which have become brittle. Prior to the onset of symptoms, he made multiple visits to the clinic with complaints of pain in his lower back and ankles that was eventually well controlled with ibuprofen. His temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), pressure is 138/88 mmHg, pulse is 78/min, and respirations are 18/min. Inspection of the hands demonstrates the physical examination findings present in Figure A. Additionally, a rash on the right elbow is identified and pictured in Figure B. The distal interphalangeal joints of the left hand are tender to palpation, as is the second distal interphalangeal joint of the right hand. The Achilles tendons are tender bilaterally, and ultrasonography is consistent with mild Achilles tendonitis bilaterally. Testing for HLA-B27 is positive. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old woman presents to the emergency department after a motor vehicle collision. She was the front seat unrestrained driver in a head-on collision. The patient has a Glasgow Coma Scale of 5 and is subsequently intubated. Physical exam is notable for subcutaneous emphysema in the clavicular area. Needle decompression and chest tube placement are performed, and the patient is stabilized after receiving 2 units of blood and 2 liters of fluid. Chest radiography demonstrates proper tube location and resolution of the pneumothorax. The patient is transferred to the trauma intensive care unit. On the unit, a repeat chest radiograph is notable for a recurrent pneumothorax with the chest tube in place. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 69-year-old woman is brought to clinic by her son for poor memory. He states that over the past two years her memory has been slowly declining though she has been able to take care of herself, pay her own rent, and manage her finances. However, two months ago he noticed a sharp decline in her cognitive functioning as well as her gait. Then one month ago, he noticed a similar decline in her functioning again that came on suddenly. The patient has a past medical history of diabetes mellitus type II, hypertension, obesity, and dyslipidemia. Current medications include hydrochlorothiazide, lisinopril, metformin, and glipizide. Her blood pressure is 165/95 mmHg, pulse is 82/minute, she is afebrile, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Cardiac exam reveals a crescendo-decrescendo murmur heard in the left upper sternal border that radiates to the carotids. Abdominal exam is benign, and neurologic exam reveals an unsteady gait. Which of the following findings is associated with the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old woman is brought into clinic by her daughter for increasing confusion. The daughter states that over the past 2 weeks, she has noticed that the patient “seems to stare off into space.” She reports she has multiple episodes a day during which she will walk into a room and forget why. She is also worried about her balance. She endorses that she has had several falls, the worst being 3 weeks ago when she tripped on the sidewalk getting the mail. The patient denies loss of consciousness, pre-syncope, chest pain, palpitations, urinary incontinence, or bowel incontinence. She complains of headache but denies dizziness. She reports nausea and a few episodes of non-bloody emesis but denies abdominal pain, constipation, or diarrhea. The patient’s medical history is significant for atrial fibrillation, diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis. She takes aspirin, warfarin, insulin, lisinopril, simvastatin, and ibuprofen. She drinks a half glass of whisky after dinner every night and smokes a cigar on the weekends. On physical examination, she is oriented to name and place but not to date. She is unable to spell "world" backward. When asked to remember 3 words, she recalls only 2. There are no motor or sensory deficits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department for a headache. The patient’s parent states that she normally has headaches in the morning; however, they tend to dissipate as the day goes on. They state she is otherwise healthy. The patient’s vitals are unremarkable. Physical exam is notable for a healthy young child. Notably, her gait is ataxic and she seems uncoordinated. An MRI scan of the head is performed as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with back pain. The patient states that she has gradually worsening back pain that seems to have worsened after moving furniture the other day. She also states that while she walks, she feels numbness and weakness in her legs. The only time the patient states her back pain is improved is when she is riding her bike or pushing a cart at the grocery store. The patient has a past medical history of osteoporosis, dyslipidemia, and diabetes. She drinks 3 alcoholic drinks every day and has a 44 pack-year smoking history. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 157/108 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a non-tender spine with normal mobility in all 4 directions. Radiography of the spine and basic labs are ordered. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 37-year-old machinist presents to her primary care physician with eye problems. The patient states that she has had a mass in her eye that has persisted for the past month. The patient has a past medical history of blepharitis treated with eye cleansing and squamous cell carcinoma of the skin treated with Mohs surgery. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 157/102 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a firm and rubbery nodule palpable inside the patient's left eyelid. Physical exam does not elicit any pain. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 58-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician complaining of a facial rash. She states that she has had the rash for at least 10 years. The rash is on both cheeks and spreads across her nose. It normally comes and goes, but is exacerbated by sun exposure. The patient was recently fired, and is embarrassed of her rash, which has prevented her from accepting job interviews. She has tried various over the counter lotions and soaps with little improvement. She has no other complaints. Her medical history is significant for mild osteoarthritis and coronary artery disease. She takes aspirin, simvastatin, and ibuprofen. On physical examination, you note telangiectasias on her bilateral eyelids. The rash is shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician for fatigue. She states she has not felt like herself recently and had to take a few days off of work secondary to fatigue. She has lost 10 pounds over the past month. She drinks 4 drinks per day and smokes 1 pack of cigarettes per day, which she has done for the past 20 years. Her temperature is 99.0°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 128/65 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 11/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below.

Hemoglobin: 9 g/dL
Hematocrit: 27%
Leukocyte count: 2,500/mm^3 with normal differential
Platelet count: 293,000/mm^3

A biopsy of the bone marrow is performed which demonstrates hypocellular and fibrotic bone marrow and a peripheral smear is performed as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old woman is sent to the emergency department by her primary care physician for hypertension. She was at a general health maintenance appointment when her blood pressure was found to be 180/115 mmHg; thus, prompting her primary doctor to send her to the emergency room. The patient is otherwise currently asymptomatic and states that she feels well. The patient has no other medical problems other than her hypertension and her labs that were drawn last week were within normal limits. Her temperature is 98.3°F (36.8°C), blood pressure is 197/105 mmHg, pulse is 88/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is unremarkable. Laboratory values are redrawn at this visit and shown below.

Hemoglobin: 15 g/dL
Hematocrit: 46%
Leukocyte count: 3,400/mm^3 with normal differential
Platelet count: 177,000/mm^3

Serum:
Na+: 139 mEq/L
Cl-: 102 mEq/L
K+: 4.0 mEq/L
HCO3-: 24 mEq/L
BUN: 29 mg/dL
Glucose: 139 mg/dL
Creatinine: 2.3 mg/dL
Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL

Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician for fatigue. The patient states that she has not been sleeping well and requests sleep medication to help her with her fatigue. She recently changed her diet to try to increase her energy and has been on a vegetarian diet for the past several months. The patient has no significant past medical history. She smokes 1 pack of cigarettes per day and drinks 5 alcoholic beverages per day. The patient has lost 12 pounds since her last visit 1 month ago. Physical exam demonstrates a tired woman. She appears thin, and her skin and sclera are icteric. Abdominal ultrasound is notable for a thin-walled and enlarged gallbladder. A urine sample is collected and is noted to be amber in color. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old female arrives to the emergency room complaining of chest pain and difficulty breathing. She reports the dyspnea started two months ago after having the flu. At first, the difficulty breathing occurred whenever she went up and down one flight of stairs, but since then the dyspnea has gotten progressively worse. This morning she developed chest pain and difficulty breathing while sitting at the kitchen table. The patient’s medical history is significant for hypertension, type II diabetes mellitus, and rheumatoid arthritis. Her medications include aspirin, lisinopril, metformin, and sulfasalazine. The patient’s temperature is 97°F (36.1°C), blood pressure is 130/78 mmHg, pulse is 88/min, and respirations are 14/min with an oxygen saturation of 97% O2 on room air. On physical exam, you note jugular venous distension during both inspiration and expiration, mild abdominal distention, and 2+ bilateral lower extremity edema. Radiography is demonstrated in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old woman presents to the gastroenterologist for chronic diarrhea and weight loss. She reports that the diarrhea began 3 months ago. She denies seeing blood in her stool but states that her stool is foul-smelling and often “floats in the bowl.” She reports that since her symptoms began she “can’t wear pants without belts.” She has not weighed herself recently. Her normal diet consists of mainly red meats, cheese, fast food, and sugary, carbonated drinks. The patient recently immigrated from Barbados 1 year ago but has not been back since. Her medical history includes arthritis and hypothyroidism. She takes aspirin and levothyroxine. The patient’s temperature is 100.9°F (38.3°C), blood pressure is 130/78 mmHg, pulse is 82/min, and respirations are 14/min. Physical examination reveals skin hyperpigmentation and swollen, painful elbows and knees. A fecal occult blood is positive. A colonoscopy is done with a biopsy and Periodic acid-Schiff staining, as shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the best long-term therapy for the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician with fatigue that has gradually been worsening over the past month. The patient rarely sees her physician and came in today as she is unable to go to her exercise classes anymore. She also endorses joint pain in her right knee and hip that has been gradually worsening. The patient's vitals are notable only for hypertension. Physical exam reveals a fatigued appearing woman. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below:

Hemoglobin: 8 g/dL
Hematocrit: 25%
Leukocyte count: 1,500/mm^3 with normal differential
Platelet count: 47,000/mm^3

A peripheral smear is performed as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old college student presents to her student health clinic complaining of a scaly rash on her right inner thigh. She reports that the rash is itchy and first appeared 4 months ago. A similar rash occurred last year, which improved with a topical cream she purchased over the counter, but she does not remember the name. The patient has a history of attention deficient disorder and atopic dermatitis. Her medications include methylphenidate and betamethasone. The patient has been a wrestler since high school and currently wrestles for the university. She reports she is doing well in her classes. She admits to smoking marijuana recreationally and having a few beers on the weekends with her friends. She went to Costa Rica for a 2-week mission trip 6 months ago. Physical exam reveals a lesion as shown in Figure A. Potassium hydroxide scrapings of the lesion confirm the diagnosis. Which of the following is the best treatment for the patient's most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old girl is brought in to your clinic by her father, who is complaining of his daughter’s “dry scalp and hair loss.” He reports a scaling spot on her scalp developed around 2 months ago, soon after moving to a new school, which then became a larger bald spot. He denies that anyone in the household is exhibiting similar symptoms, but does recall a note that came home from school warning of a lice outbreak. Thus far, he has only tried daily baths with little improvement. The patient denies pain or itchiness, but the father reports he does notice her scratching her scalp. The father also reports that since his daughter has started at the new school, he has noticed an increase in her tics including excessive blinking and clearing of her throat. The patient's medical history is significant for asthma, allergic rhinitis, and attention deficient hyperactivity disorder. Her current medications include fluticasone, salmeterol, loratadine, and methylphenidate. Family history includes obsessive compulsive disorder in her older brother. The father also reports his mother had a debilitating skin and joint disorder. On examination, you note swollen lymph glands at the back of the patient's ears and neck, and there are residual black dots within a patch of alopecia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old man presents to the emergency department after an episode of light-headedness. He was using the bathroom when he felt light-headed and fell to the floor. His son found him and brought him into the emergency department right away. The patient has a past medical history of obesity and diabetes mellitus. He came to the emergency department 1 week ago for a similar complaint. The patient states that he has otherwise felt well with the exception of fatigue, constipation, an odd sensation in his chest, and a decreased appetite and desire to drink recently causing him to lose 10 pounds. His temperature is 98.0°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 122/88 mmHg, pulse is 92/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam reveals a cardiopulmonary exam within normal limits and stable gait. The patient has an obese abdomen with abdominal distension. Strength is 5/5 in the upper and lower extremities. Which of the following is associated with the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with back pain. She is currently intoxicated but states that she is having severe back pain and is requesting morphine and lorazepam. The patient has a past medical history of alcohol abuse, drug seeking behavior, and IV drug abuse and does not routinely see a physician. Her temperature is 102°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 127/68 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for tenderness over the thoracic and lumbar spine. The pain is exacerbated with flexion of the spine. The patient’s laboratory values are notable for the findings below.

Hemoglobin: 12 g/dL
Hematocrit: 36%
Leukocyte count: 16,500/mm^3 with normal differential
Platelet count: 197,000/mm^3

Serum:
Na+: 139 mEq/L
Cl-: 100 mEq/L
K+: 4.3 mEq/L
HCO3-: 25 mEq/L
BUN: 20 mg/dL
Glucose: 99 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL
CRP: 5.2 mg/L

Further imaging is currently pending. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-month-old girl is brought to the ED by her father because of abdominal pain. Two weeks ago, he noticed she had a fever and looser stools, but both resolved after a few days. One week ago, she began to experience periodic episodes during which she would curl up into a ball, scream, and cry. The episodes lasted a few minutes, and were occasionally followed by vomiting. Between events, she was completely normal. He says the episodes have become more frequent over time, and this morning, he noticed blood in her diaper. In the ED, her vitals are within normal ranges, and her physical exam is normal. After confirming the diagnosis with an abdominal ultrasound, what is the next step in management?

A 52-year-old female presents to her primary care physician at the insistence of her husband who reports that she has been complaining of vague abdominal pain over the last several months. He asks if you think his wife's skin appears yellow. Vitals signs and laboratory findings are as follows: T 98.7F, HR 73, BP 114/68, RR 14, O2 100%. Hemoglobin 9.7, Hematocrit 31.2, WBC 6, Platelets 146. Amylase and lipase are within normal limits. You order a CT scan (Figure A). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by her husband for altered mental status. He reports that she was in her usual state of health until 3 days ago when she developed a headache and fever. Then today he found her lying in the bedroom in the dark. When he turned on the light, she covered her eyes. Other than that, she was minimally responsive. The patient is adopted and does not know her family history. Her husband reports that she occasionally has a beer or two with dinner, and works as a landscaper. The patient’s temperature is 103°F (39.5°C), blood pressure is 131/78 mmHg, pulse is 84/min, and respirations are 14/min with an oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. Physical examination is notable for neck stiffness and a rash that is shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the best treatment for the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old man presents to the physician with complaints of fatigue, weakness, and loss of appetite for the past 3-4 months despite attempts to adjust his sleep schedule to accommodate more rest. As part of his work up, a peripheral blood smear is obtained and is shown in Figure A. On physical examination, the patient has a smooth, swollen tongue and diminished vibratory sensation in his lower extremities. Given the patient’s most likely diagnosis, which of the following associated pathologies should be screened for in this patient?

A 23-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with bloody vomitus. The patient is an alcoholic and has presented similarly before. She is given ondansetron; however, she continues to vomit. The patient complains of sudden substernal chest pain and dysphagia after another bout of vomiting. Her temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 117/60 mmHg, pulse is 122/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is notable for an uncomfortable woman with subcutaneous emphysema in the patient’s neck and supraclavicular areas. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old girl presents to her pediatrician for a wellness checkup. The patient states she feels well and has been excelling in school. She is in her school's wrestling and football team and is currently sexually active with her boyfriend. Physical exam reveals an energetic young woman with the finding seen in Figure A, which is coarse upon palpation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 10-year-old boy is admitted to the medical floor for a respiratory infection. The patient lives in a foster home and has been admitted many times. Since birth, the patient has had repeated episodes of pain/pressure over his frontal sinuses and a chronic cough that produces mucus. He was recently treated with amoxicillin for an infection. The patient is in the 25th percentile for height and weight which has been constant since birth. His guardians state that the patient has normal bowel movements and has been gaining weight appropriately. The patient has a history of tricuspid stenosis. He also recently had magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of his chest which demonstrated dilation of his airways. His temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 90/58 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 94% on room air. Physical exam is notable for bruises along the patient's shins which the guardians state are from playing soccer. The rest of the exam is deferred because the patient starts crying. Which of the following findings is associated with this patient's most likely underlying diagnosis?

A 55-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with painful skin lesions. The patient has had similar lesions for the past several months but states they have worsened recently. She has a past medical history of diabetes, a middle ear infection, and urinary tract infection, which were treated with antibiotics. The patient has allergies to latex and sulfa drugs. She works as a mountain ranger and regularly hikes through forestry. Her temperature is 98.4°F (36.9°C), blood pressure is 167/108 mmHg, pulse is 95/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam demonstrates the lesions seen in Figure A which separate and break open when minimal pressure is applied. Oral mucosal erosions are also seen upon inspection of the oropharynx. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old woman is seen in the hospital for a sacral rash. The patient has been hospitalized for the past 3 weeks for a heart failure exacerbation. When the nurse went to bathe her this morning, she noticed a red rash over her sacrum. The patient reports mild discomfort and denies pruritus. The patient has chronic kidney disease, urinary incontinence, ischemic cardiomyopathy, gout, and poor mobility. Her current medications include aspirin, furosemide, metoprolol, lisinopril, spironolactone, and prednisone that was started for a recent gout flare. The patient’s temperature is 97°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 110/62 mmHg, pulse is 68/min, and respirations are 13/min with an oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. On physical examination, there is a 4 cm x 6 cm patch of non-blanchable erythema over the patient’s sacrum that is mildly tender to palpation. Labs are obtained, as shown below:

Leukocyte count: 10,000/mm^3 with normal differential
Hemoglobin: 15.2 g/dL
Platelet count: 400,000/mm^3

Serum:
Na: 138 mEq/L
K+: 4.3 mEq/L
Cl-: 104 mEq/L
HCO3-: 25 mEq/L
BUN: 26 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.5 mg/dL
Glucose: 185 mg/dL

A hemoglobin A1c is pending. Which of the following is the best management for the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old immigrant from Nigeria presents to the emergency department for sudden, severe pain and swelling in his lower extremity. He was at a rehabilitation hospital when his symptoms became apparent. The patient has a past medical history of obesity, diabetes, bipolar disorder, and tonic-clonic seizures. His current medications include metformin, insulin, lisinopril, and valproic acid. The patient is a prominent IV drug and alcohol user who has presented to the ED many times for intoxication. On physical exam you note anasarca and asymmetric lower extremity swelling. Based on the results of a doppler ultrasound of his swollen lower extremity, heparin is started. The patient is then transferred to the general medicine floor for continued management. Laboratory studies are shown below.

Serum:
Na+: 137 mEq/L
K+: 5.5 mEq/L
Cl-: 100 mEq/L
HCO3-: 24 mEq/L
Urea nitrogen: 22 mg/dL
Ca2+: 5.7 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.7 mg/dL
Glucose: 70 mg/dL

What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 58-year-old woman presents with her husband to her primary care physician for an annual check-up. The patient reports that she has been in her usual state of health except for a recent worsening of her seasonal allergies. Her husband states that this happens every spring and that her symptoms include sneezing, runny nose, and watery eyes. The husband also asks about a lesion on the patient’s face that he noticed several weeks ago when the patient was wiping her nose. The patient has a history of hypertension and well-controlled diabetes. She takes lisinopril, aspirin, and metformin as prescribed. The patient’s temperature is 98°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 130/78 mmHg, pulse is 72/min, and respirations are 14/min. Physical examination is notable for mild conjunctival injection bilaterally and a nodule located inferior to the left nasal ala, as shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the best therapy for the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-week-old female presents to the emergency department with vomiting. Her parents report that she suddenly started vomiting this morning and has shown no interest in feeding since then. They describe the vomitus as green and without any traces of blood. Prior to today, the patient was feeding, voiding and stooling well. She was noted to have surpassed her birth weight at her last office visit one week ago. In the emergency room, her temperature is 97.6°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 78/56 mmHg, pulse is 148/min, and respirations are 44/min. On physical exam, the patient is in mild distress. She has no dysmorphic features, and her mucous membranes are dry. Her abdomen is soft and distended. Bowel sounds are hypoactive. An abdominal radiograph is performed and can be seen in Figure A.

Which of the following is the best next step in the diagnosis of this condition?

A 34-year-old man arrives to your office complaining of a recurrent rash. The first time the patient noticed the rash was after going in the water at the beach six weeks ago. He reports that since then, he has developed similar appearing pink and itchy rashes on his arms and legs. He states that the rashes eventually resolve on their own. The patient works as a forest ranger at a national park. His medical history is significant for systemic lupus erythematous and asthma. His current medications include NSAIDS and an albuterol inhaler. He reports that he has seasonal allergies but no food intolerances. His temperature is 98°F (36.7°C), pulse is 70/min, blood pressure is 118/77 mmHg, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Upon physical examination, you appreciate diffuse, mild expiratory wheezes. There is no evidence of airway obstruction. When ice is placed on his leg, a rash appears, as pictured in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old woman is brought into the emergency department after a car ran into her while she was riding her bike. The patient is conscious and alert. She states that her arm is in pain and she is requesting morphine. The patient's past medical history is non-contributory and she is not currently on any medications. Her temperature is 97.5°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 124/65 mmHg, pulse is 122/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. An initial splint is placed. A radiograph is performed and physical exam is notable for the findings in Figure A when the patient is asked to extend her fingers. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his parents due to observations of rapid, random, horizontal and vertical eye movements along with occasional jerking movements of his limbs and head. CT scan reveals an abdominal mass that crosses the midline. Further work-up reveals elevated 24-hour urinary homovanillic acid and vanillylmandelic acid. Which of the following diseases pathologically originates from the type of cells as this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old man presents to clinic complaining of multiple symptoms including skin lesions and worsening bone pain. He just returned from a 6-month stay in Guatemala, where he volunteered to build homes in an underdeveloped community. While he was there, he developed scaling papulonodular skin lesions on his left hand and right wrist. He also complains of bone pain, specifically in his right forearm and right thigh, and a persistent dry cough. He states he has been very tired lately, which is why it took him so long to see a doctor when he returned from his trip. Since returning, he has been living in Arizona for the past 2 weeks with his brother who owns 2 parrots and a dog. The patient’s temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 110/68 mmHg, pulse is 88/min, and respirations are 17/min with an oxygen saturation of 97% on room air. His complete blood count reveals pancytopenia. A peripheral blood smear shows evidence of lymphoblasts. A computed tomography of the chest reveals multiple, centrilobular nodules in the left upper lobe. A radiograph of the right thigh and right upper extremity shows osteolytic bone lesions. A biopsy of the skin lesion on his left hand is obtained, and the results are shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old man presents to the emergency department with weakness. He states that at the end of the day he feels so fatigued and weak that he can hardly care for himself. He currently feels this way. The patient has had multiple illnesses recently and has been traveling, hiking, and camping. His temperature is 98.0°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 124/84 mmHg, pulse is 82/min, respirations are 12/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for 2/5 strength of the upper extremities and 4/5 strength of the lower extremities. Visual exam is notable for mild diplopia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician concerned about her weight. She states she has been gaining weight though does not feel she has changed her diet. The patient also states she has felt fatigued lately and not herself. She denies taking any medications or using any illicit substances at baseline. Her temperature is 99.2°F (37.3°C), blood pressure is 177/108 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for an obese woman with striae on her abdomen. A 24-hour urine free cortisol is collected and demonstrates an elevated cortisol level; however, a high dose of dexamethasone when administered results in no attenuation of cortisol release. A CT scan of the abdomen is within normal limits. Which of the following is associated with the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department for bowling at a local bowling alley while inappropriately dressed. The patient refused to speak with police and was seen conversing with inanimate objects in the back of the police car. The patient states that her clothes were contaminated by assassins who have been tracking her for years. The patient refuses to answer any further questions, and continues to whisper toward someone else. The patient has a past medical history of homelessness, alcohol abuse, marijuana use, and cocaine abuse. Physical exam is notable for a healthy young woman who seems mistrustful of all hospital personnel. The patient is started on a medication and is transferred to the psychiatric inpatient unit. The patient’s condition improves, but she still often speaks of a contamination that is on her clothes and skin that is coming from external parties. The patient is started on a new medication. She is then sent to group therapy, followed by physical activity in the yard. The physician is called over when the patient is found down in the recreation yard while she was exercising. The patient is not responsive, and her limbs seem to resist passive force. Her temperature is 104°F (40°C), pulse is 112/min, blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. Which of the following best describes the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician for a routine physical exam. She is concerned about a burning sensation that she feels in her throat whenever she eats large meals and is concerned she may have esophageal cancer like her uncle. The patient has a past medical history of irritable bowel syndrome and constipation. Her current medications include whey protein supplements, fish oil, a multivitamin, and sodium docusate. The patient is concerned about her performance in school and fears she may fail out. She recently did poorly on an exam and it has caused her significant stress. She also is worried that her boyfriend is going to leave her. The patient claims that she thought she was going to be an incredible doctor some day, but now she feels like a terrible person. The patient also states that she feels guilty about her grandfather's death which occurred 1 year ago and she often reexperiences the funeral in her mind. She regularly has trouble sleeping for which she takes melatonin. The patient has been praying every 4 hours with the hopes that this will make things go better for her. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old man presents to his primary care provider for shoulder pain. He reports that he initially thought the pain was due to "sleeping funny" on the arm, but that the pain has now lasted for 4 weeks. He denies trauma to the joint and says that the pain is worse when reaching overhead to retrieve things from his kitchen cabinets. On physical exam, the patient's shoulders are symmetric, and the right lateral shoulder is tender to palpation. The shoulder has full passive and active range of motion, although pain is reproduced on active abduction of the right arm above 90 degrees. Pain is also reproduced on passively internally rotating and then lifting the shoulder. The patient is able to resist elbow flexion without pain, and he otherwise has 5/5 strength. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old woman presents to the emergency department after a motor vehicle accident. She was the unrestrained front seat driver in a head on collision. The patient is unresponsive and her medical history is unknown. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 67/38 mmHg, pulse is 190/min, respirations are 33/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. The patient is started on IV fluids, blood products, and norepinephrine. A FAST exam is performed and a pelvic binder is placed. One hour later, her temperature is 98.3°F (36.8°C), blood pressure is 119/66 mmHg, pulse is 110/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. The patient is currently responsive. Management of the patient's pelvic fracture is scheduled by the orthopedic service. While the patient is waiting in the emergency department she suddenly complains of feeling hot, aches, and a headache. The patient's temperature is currently 101°F (38.3°C). She has not been given any pain medications and her past medical history is still unknown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

Her medical history is significant for rheumatoid arthritis. She takes methotrexate and acetaminophen as needed. The patient’s temperature is 98°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 168/108 mmHg, and pulse is 75/min. Physical examination is notable for periorbital edema, hepatomegaly, and bilateral 1+ pitting lower extremity edema. Labs and a urinalysis are obtained, as shown below:

An abdominal ultrasound reveals an enlarged liver with heterogeneous echogenicity and enlarged kidneys with increased echogenicity in the renal parenchyma. A biopsy of the kidney is obtained. Which of the following biopsy findings is associated with the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 12-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department by her father for a rash. The patient had a sore throat a few days ago with symptoms initially well-controlled with lozenges. However, today she had a rash covering her body, which prompted her presentation. The father states that he did smear an herbal remedy on the rash with no alleviation in symptoms and also gave her a single dose of amoxicillin left over from a previous infection. The patient is up to date on her vaccinations and has no past medical conditions. Her temperature is 101°F (38.3°C), blood pressure is 102/68 mmHg, pulse is 97/min, respirations are 19/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the findings in Figures A and B. The rash seen in Figure B is very coarse. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old woman presents to the emergency department for shortness of breath. She was at home working on her car when she suddenly felt very short of breath, which failed to improve with rest. She states she was working with various chemicals and inhalants while trying to replace a broken piece in the engine. The patient was brought in by paramedics and is currently on 100% O2 via nasal cannula. The patient has a 52 pack-year smoking history and drinks 2 to 3 alcoholic drinks every night. She has a past medical history of asthma but admits to not having seen a physician since high school. Her temperature is 98.2°F (36.8°C), blood pressure is 157/108 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 29/min, and oxygen saturation is 77%. Physical exam demonstrates tachycardia with a systolic murmur heard best along the right upper sternal border. Breath sounds are diminished over the right upper lobe. Bilateral lower extremity pitting edema is noted. Which of the following best describes the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician after noticing a new growth on her back. Her husband first saw it several weeks ago and they thought it was a scab that would resolve, but it has persisted. The patient denies any itching or pain. She has a past medical history of gastroesophageal reflux for which she takes omeprazole. She is also an active smoker with a 45 pack-year history. The patient has a family history of colon cancer in her father and stroke in her mother. At this visit, the patient’s temperature is 98.6°F (37.0°C), pulse is 76/min, blood pressure is 128/85 mmHg, and respirations are 13/min. Cardiopulmonary and abdominal exams are unremarkable. Skin examination of her back is shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old woman with a history of IV drug and alcohol abuse presents to the emergency department with back pain. She states that her symptoms started 3 days ago and have been gradually worsening. Her temperature is 102°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 127/68 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for tenderness over the mid thoracic spine. Laboratory values are only notable for a leukocytosis and an elevated ESR and CRP. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old man with type II diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and hypothyroidism presents to the emergency room with 6 months of worsening headaches and vision changes. Initially, his headaches were dull and infrequent, but they now occur daily and have become quite severe. He states that his symptoms are worse in the morning. They do not improve substantially with ibuprofen or acetaminophen. The patient requests prescription medication as he can no longer tolerate the pain. He has also been experiencing fatigue, nausea, increased thirst, and frequent urination. His current medications include insulin, metformin, atorvastatin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, and levothyroxine. He confirms that he has been taking all his medications as prescribed. He also reveals that his peripheral vision has been getting worse, though he thinks this may be due to old age. His temperature is 97.9°F (36.6°C), blood pressure is 139/89 mmHg, pulse is 82/min, respirations are 11/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for mild impairment of his lateral visual fields. A non-contrast CT scan of the head is performed and shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old student has an appointment with her primary care physician for an annual check-up. She is in her usual state of health. She says her sophomore year of college went well, and she’s currently been home working as a lifeguard for the summer. She asks about a good sunscreen to prevent her “sun-spots.” She reports that every summer for the last 2 years she has developed an “uneven” rash that sometimes is itchy but is otherwise asymptomatic. The rash never bothered her until recently when her friends and other pool attendees started asking if she's "peeling from a bad sunburn." Her past medical history is significant for well-controlled type I diabetes mellitus. She is currently on insulin. Physical examination shows cutaneous lesions on the chest and upper extremities, which are depicted in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

He also states that he has had abdominal pain and trouble focusing at work as well as a recent cough and fever which he attributes to allergies. A 22-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by police after she was found undressing herself outside in 110°F weather. The patient recently started college and has presented to the emergency department once before for polysubstance intoxication. She does not comply with any commands, and it is not possible to freely manipulate her extremities due to rigidity. Her mucous membranes are dry. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old woman presents to her nearby clinic for a non-healing and painful leg ulcer. The sore started approximately 3 weeks ago as a tender nodule. She first noticed the bump after hitting her shin during a soccer game. The lesion later “opened up” into an ulceration. The patient also complains of lower back pain and intermittent diarrhea for the past four months. The patient’s medical history is non-significant except for chlamydia for which she was successfully treated. She uses acetaminophen for the back pain but takes no other medications.
