A 55-year-old female bodybuilder presents to the emergency department with weakness of her right arm. The patient states she has experienced these symptoms for a few weeks; however, today her hand felt so weak she dropped her cup of tea. The patient has a past medical history of diabetes. She drinks 2-7 alcoholic drinks per day and has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes per day since she was 25. The patient admits to using anabolic steroids. She has lost 17 pounds since she last came to the emergency department 1 month ago. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 177/108 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam reveals decreased sensation in the right arm and 2/5 strength in the right arm and 5/5 strength in the left arm. The patient states that she is experiencing a dull aching and burning pain in her right arm during the exam. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old woman presents to the emergency department after an episode of syncope. She states that for the past month ever since starting a new job she has experienced an episode of syncope or near-syncope every morning while she is getting dressed. The patient states that she now gets dressed, shaves is not applicable in this context as it typically refers to male grooming, however the original text does mention the patient shaves, so it should be replaced with a more neutral or female-specific grooming activity, and puts on her makeup or gets ready sitting down to avoid falling when she faints. She has never had this before and is concerned it is stress from her new job as she has been unemployed for the past 5 years. She is wondering if she can get a note for work since she was unable to head in today secondary to her presentation. The patient has no significant past medical history and is otherwise healthy. Her temperature is 99.2°F (37.3°C), blood pressure is 122/83 mmHg, pulse is 92/min, respirations are 16/min, and oxygen saturation is 100% on room air. Cardiopulmonary and neurologic exams are within normal limits. An initial ECG and laboratory values are unremarkable as well. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old woman presents to the emergency department after a motor vehicle collision. The patient was the back seat restrained passenger in a vehicle that was rear ended at 25 miles/hour. The patient has a past medical history of diabetes, hypertension, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Her temperature is 97.5°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 97/68 mmHg, pulse is 130/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. The patient is subsequently worked up receiving a chest radiograph, ECG, FAST exam, and serum chemistries. A cardiac catheterization reveals equilibration in diastolic pressure across all cardiac chambers. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 66-year-old woman is brought into the emergency department by her son for a change in behavior. Yesterday the patient seemed more confused than usual and was asking the same questions repetitively. Her symptoms have not improved over the past 24 hours, thus the decision to bring her in today. Last year, the patient was almost completely independent but she then suffered a "series of falls," after which her ability to care for herself declined. After this episode she was no longer able to cook for herself or pay her bills but otherwise had been fine up until this episode. The patient has a past medical history of myocardial infarction, hypertension, depression, diabetes mellitus type II, constipation, diverticulitis, and peripheral neuropathy. Her current medications include metformin, insulin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, sodium docusate, atorvastatin, metoprolol, fluoxetine, and gabapentin. On exam you note a confused woman who is poorly kept. She has bruises over her legs and her gait seems unstable. She is alert to person and place, and answers some questions inappropriately. The patient's pulse is 90/minute and her blood pressure is 170/100 mmHg. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 15-year-old female teenager is brought in to see her pediatrician by her father to examine the patient's acne. The patient asserts that she maintains excellent hygiene. She uses mild soap and water to wash her face and has not manually disturbed any skin lesion. However, her father noticed that one of her "acne" ruptured while eating dinner, producing a foul odor and a cheese-like white exudate. The patient has a past medical history of asthma and eczema. Her current medications include albuterol, fluticasone, and topical corticosteroids as needed. Examination of the patient's face reveals a firm, movable, nontender lesion shown in Figure A. The remainder of her scalp, face, and neck are unremarkable. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a headache. He states that he felt a bad headache come on this morning while he was gardening and carrying heavy pots, and it has not been improving. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension and diabetes which is currently being treated by his primary care physician. His temperature is 99.0°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 157/99 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 16/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. A head CT is ordered as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the best explanation for the most likely diagnosis?

A 69-year-old female presents to her primary care physician for a general checkup. The patient works as a farmer and gardens in her spare time. The patient has a past medical history of poorly managed diabetes mellitus type II, and irritable bowel syndrome. Her current medications include lisinopril, metformin, insulin, fiber supplements, and a multivitamin. On physical exam you note an obese lady. Inspection of the patient's scalp reveals the finding in Figure A. The patient is sent home and instructed to keep a blood glucose journal and to return with it in three months.

Three months later, the patient returns with her glucose journal. In addition, she complains of a cut on her scalp that is not seeming to heal. The patient's glucose journal reveals an average blood glucose of 175 mg/dL. On inspection of the patient's scalp, you note the finding in Figure B. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 41-year-old female presents to her primary care provider after seeing bright red blood in the toilet bowl after her last two bowel movements. She reports that the second time she also noticed some blood mixed with her stool. The patient denies abdominal pain and any changes in her stool habits. She notes a weight loss of eight pounds in the last two months. Her past medical history is significant for an episode of pancreatitis two years ago for which she was hospitalized for several days. Which of the following is the best next step in diagnosis?

A 27-year-old woman presents to the emergency room with persistent fever, nausea, and vomiting for the past 3 days. While waiting to be seen, she quickly becomes disoriented and agitated. Upon examination, she has visible signs of difficulty breathing with copious oral secretions and generalized muscle twitching. The patient’s temperature is 104°F (40°C), blood pressure is 90/64 mmHg, pulse is 88/min, and respirations are 18/min with an oxygen saturation of 90% on room air. When the nurse tries to place a nasal cannula, the patient becomes fearful and combative. The patient is sedated and placed on mechanical ventilation. A 25-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with altered mental status. The patient has not been feeling well since yesterday, and this morning her roommate found her unarousable. The patient is generally healthy and is a college athlete. She recently broke her nose in a soccer game, and it is currently healing with only gauze in her nose to stop occasional bleeding. She otherwise has no significant medical history. Her temperature is 102°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 87/58 mmHg, pulse is 130/min, respirations are 24/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old African American man presents to his primary care physician for a wellness checkup. He states that he has lost 20 pounds over the past 2 months yet has experienced an increased appetite during this period. He endorses hyperhidrosis and increased urinary volume and frequency. Physical exam is notable for an anxious man and a regular and tachycardic pulse. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below.

A 62-year-old woman comes to the office complaining of dysphagia that started 4-5 months ago. She reports that she initially had difficulty swallowing only solid foods. More recently, she has noticed some trouble swallowing liquids. The patient also complains of fatigue, a chronic cough that worsens at night, and burning chest pain that occurs after she eats. She says that she has used over-the-counter antacids for “years” with mild relief. She denies any change in diet, but says she has “gone down a pant size or 2.” The patient has hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She takes amlodipine and atorvastatin. She smoked 1 pack of cigarettes a day for 12 years while in the military but quit 35 years ago. She drinks 1-2 beers on the weekend while she is golfing with her friends. Her diet consists mostly of pasta, pizza, and steak. The patient's temperature is 98°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 143/91 mmHg, and pulse is 80/min. Her BMI is 32 kg/m^2. Physical examination reveals an obese woman in no acute distress. No masses or enlarged lymph nodes are appreciated upon palpation of the neck. Cardiopulmonary examination is unremarkable. An endoscopy is performed, which identifies a lower esophageal mass. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 31-year-old woman presents to the general health clinic for a routine checkup. She admits to being in good health and has no medical concerns. She drinks alcohol regularly and smokes marijuana occasionally. She has been sexually active for the past 10 years and has had over 25 sexual partners, both male and female. A 32-year-old man presents to the emergency department due to severe, intractable headaches, and bilateral ocular pain. A 33-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with a fever and fatigue. She states that she has not felt well since she returned from a hiking trip in Alabama. She is generally healthy and has no other medical conditions. Her temperature is 101°F (38.3°C), blood pressure is 127/85 mmHg, pulse is 108/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam including a full dermatologic inspection is unremarkable. Laboratory studies are ordered as seen below.

A 27-year-old woman presents to the emergency department after a motor vehicle collision. The patient was the front seat unrestrained driver in a head on collision. A 44-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with dizziness. She states her symptoms started a few days ago and have been gradually worsening. A 55-year-old woman presents to the emergency department after a motor vehicle collision. The patient has a Glasgow coma scale of 7 and is immediately intubated. A 24-year-old woman is brought by ambulance to the emergency department after a motor vehicle accident. She was the front seat driver in a head on collision. She is currently unconscious. Otherwise, she is a college student in good health. The patient is resuscitated. A FAST exam is notable for free fluid in Morrison’s pouch. An initial assessment demonstrates only minor bruises and scrapes on her body. After further resuscitation the patient becomes responsive and begins vomiting. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 66-year-old man presents to the emergency department complaining of palpitations. He says that he has been experiencing palpitations and lightheadedness for the past 6 months, but before this morning the episodes usually resolved on their own. The patient’s medical history is significant for a transient ischemia attack 2 months ago, hypertension, and diabetes. He takes aspirin, metformin, and lisinopril. He states his grandfather died of a stroke, and his mom has a "blood disorder." An electrocardiogram is obtained that shows an irregularly irregular rhythm with rapid ventricular response, consistent with atrial fibrillation. He is given intravenous metoprolol, which resolves his symptoms. In addition to starting a beta-blocker for long-term management, the patient meets criteria for anticoagulation. Both unfractionated heparin and warfarin are started. Five days later, the patient begins complaining of pain and swelling of his left lower extremity. The father reports that the patient is shy but cooperates well with her siblings and other children. She can say her first and last name and just started counting. Which of the following is the most appropriate test to confirm the diagnosis?

A 55-year-old woman with a past medical history of diabetes and hypertension presents to the emergency department with chest pain. Her symptoms started yesterday and seem to be worsened by exertion. A 7-year-old girl presents to her primary care physician for a general checkup. The patient has been feeling poorly for the past several weeks and has been losing weight. On exam, you note a fatigued appearing child who has lost 10 pounds since her last appointment. Left upper quadrant tenderness and a mass is noted on abdominal exam. A 17-year-old boy comes to the primary care clinic with his father complaining of right knee pain. On physical examination, there is tenderness at the inferior pole of the patella, without swelling or overlying skin changes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with anxiety and trouble swallowing. She states that her symptoms have slowly been getting worse over the past year, and she now struggles to swallow liquids. She recently recovered from the flu. Review of systems is notable only for recent weight loss. The patient has a 33 pack-year smoking history and is a former alcoholic. Physical exam is notable for poor dental hygiene and foul breath. A 65-year-old man presents to his family doctor complaining of chronic cough with occasional chest pain. A 30-year-old woman is brought into the emergency room for complaints of acute onset chest pain and shortness of breath. A 69-year-old woman with no significant past medical history presents to her primary care doctor for a travel evaluation. She plans to tour countries in the Middle East and Southeast Asia as part of her post-retirement celebration and requests recommendations on necessary immunizations. She denies any history of venous thromboembolism, previous surgeries, or dependence on any medications. She regularly rows, runs outside, and regularly participates in competitions to stay in shape. A 25-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with back pain. She states that it started yesterday and has been gradually getting worse. A 22-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with a sore throat. She says her symptoms have persisted for the past several days and have become so severe that she can no longer eat food. A 27-year-old woman is brought into the emergency department by ambulance. The patient was at an appointment to receive welfare when she began acting abnormally. The patient was denied welfare. Her temperature is 102°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 106/68 mmHg, pulse is 167/min, respirations are 25/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. The child appears very ill and confused. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old man presents to the emergency department after a motor vehicle collision. He was the front seat unrestrained driver in a head on collision at 25 miles per hour. His temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 129/66 mmHg, pulse is 127/min, respirations are 16/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. The primary and secondary survey are performed and are only notable for bruising along his chest wall bilaterally. An initial pelvic radiograph, an electrocardiogram (ECG) are performed and are unremarkable. A chest radiograph is performed and is notable for a sternal fracture and several rib fractures. The patient is given morphine and his heart rate subsequently improves to 80/min. The patient is observed in the emergency department over the next 6 hours and his laboratory values and a repeat ECG return within normal limits. The patient suddenly complains of shortness of breath. His temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 127/68 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 28/min, and oxygen saturation is 91% on room air. A repeat chest radiograph is performed as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician for a wellness checkup. The patient states she has been doing well and currently has no concerns. The patient's son states that he feels she is abnormally fatigued and has complained of light-headedness whenever she gardens. She also admits that she fainted once. The patient has a past medical history of type II diabetes, hypertension, and constipation. She recently had a "throat cold" that she recovered from with rest and fluids. Her temperature is 98.9°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 167/98 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 12/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam reveals a systolic murmur heard best along the right upper sternal border. An ECG is performed and demonstrates no signs of ST elevation. Cardiac troponins are negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old woman presents to the emergency department after losing consciousness at a jiu jitsu competition. The patient was choked and lost consciousness briefly for roughly 10 seconds before returning to her baseline level of consciousness without any confusion. She is presenting to the emergency department for further evaluation. The patient generally does not see her primary care physician but is otherwise healthy. Her temperature is 99.3°F (37.4°C), blood pressure is 122/88 mmHg, pulse is 77/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Basic laboratory studies are performed and are unremarkable. An ECG is performed as seen in Figure A. Current cardiac troponins are pending. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old female college student presents to the emergency room with persistent vague abdominal pain, vomiting, and nausea. Notably, she also reports getting full with meals sooner than usual. She has recently been pledging at a sorority and has participated in binge drinking, marijuana use, cocaine use, and intramural sports. She admits to sharing drinks and paraphernalia with other sorority members and states that several of them have been ill recently. The patient has a past medical history of asthma and depression. She admits to using large amounts of ibuprofen recently to control pain secondary to minor orthopedic injuries from intramural sports. Physical exam demonstrates mild tachycardia and epigastric tenderness. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 127/68 mmHg, pulse is 105/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. A CT scan is performed and shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old man is brought by ambulance to the emergency department after being hit by a car while walking on the sidewalk. He is conscious and denies any pain, bleeding, or memory loss. The patient states that he is a veterinarian for farm animals, primarily horses. His temperature is 98.7°F (37°C), blood pressure is 120/70 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, and respirations are 15/min. Physical exam reveals a small bruise over his right elbow and right upper quadrant as well as some scrapes on his right lateral thigh. Radiography of his right arm, hip, and knee are unremarkable. Abdominal ultrasound reveals no free fluid, but demonstrates a 6 x 4 cm cystic mass in the right hepatic lobe seen in Figure A. Computed tomography confirmed the cystic mass size and location. His complete blood count is shown below:

Leukocyte count and differential:
Leukocyte count: 13,000 /mm^3
Segmented neutrophils: 60%
Bands: 0 %
Eosinophils: 10%
Basophils: 6%
Lymphocytes: 18%
Monocytes: 6%

Hemoglobin: 14 g/dL
Platelet count: 160,000 /mm^3

What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old female immigrant presents to her primary care physician for a new patient visit. The patient reports chronic fatigue but states that she otherwise feels well. Her past medical history is not known, and she is not currently taking any medications. The patient admits to drinking 7 alcoholic beverages per day and smoking 1 pack of cigarettes per day. Her temperature is 99.4°F (37.4°C), blood pressure is 157/98 mmHg, pulse is 99/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 100% on room air. Physical exam demonstrates mild pallor but is otherwise not remarkable. Laboratory studies are ordered as seen below.

Hemoglobin: 9 g/dL
Hematocrit: 33%
Leukocyte count: 6,500/mm^3 with normal differential
Platelet count: 190,000/mm^3
Mean corpuscular volume (MCV): 60 femtoliters
Free iron: 272 mcg/dL
Total iron binding capacity (TIBC): 175 mcg/dL
Ferritin: 526 ng/mL
Reticulocyte count: 2.8%

Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician for a change in her behavior over the past few months. Initially, the patient was noted to be behaving inappropriately including using foul language and grabbing people unexpectedly. This has progressed to a worsening of her memory and trouble caring for herself. Her temperature is 98.1°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 162/103 mmHg, pulse is 83/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for an elderly woman who laughs inappropriately at times and who is a poor historian. When she is engaged in conversation, she exhibits word finding difficulty and is rather inattentive. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old woman is accompanied by her husband to the primary care clinic for hand tremors. She states that she first noticed the tremor of her left hand 1 year ago. Since then, the tremor has been worsening and now she can hardly relax when trying to read. Her husband says that he is also worried about her memory. He had to take over the finances several weeks ago after learning that she had forgotten to pay the bills for the past few months. The patient’s medical history is significant for hypertension. She takes aspirin and amlodipine. Her mother had schizophrenia. The patient drinks 1-2 beers a night and is a former cigar smoker. On physical examination, she speaks softly and has reduced facial expressions. She has a resting tremor that is worse on the left, and she resists manipulation of her bilateral upper extremities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with increased fatigue. She states that she has been feeling very tired lately but today lost consciousness while walking up the stairs. She reports mild abdominal distension/discomfort, weight loss, a persistent cough, and multiple episodes of waking up drenched in sweat in the middle of the night. The patient does not see a primary care physician but admits to smoking 2 to 3 packs of cigarettes per day and drinking 1 to 3 alcoholic beverages per day. She recently traveled to Taiwan and Nicaragua. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 177/98 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. On physical exam, you note a fatigued appearing elderly woman who is well-groomed. Cardiopulmonary exam reveals mild expiratory wheezes. Abdominal exam is notable for a non-pulsatile mass in the left upper quadrant. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below.

Hemoglobin: 12 g/dL
Hematocrit: 36%
Leukocyte count: 105,500/mm^3
Platelet count: 197,000/mm^3

Serum:
Na+: 139 mEq/L
Cl-: 100 mEq/L
K+: 4.3 mEq/L
HCO3-: 25 mEq/L
BUN: 20 mg/dL
Glucose: 92 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.4 mg/dL
Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL
Leukocyte alkaline phosphatase score: 25 (range 20 - 100)
AST: 12 U/L
ALT: 17 U/L

Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 78-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician for persistent back pain. The patient states that she has had back pain for awhile; however, this past weekend she was helping her son move heavy furniture. Since the move, her symptoms have been more severe. The patient states that the pain is constant and occurs throughout the day. On review of systems, the patient endorses a recent 15 pound weight loss and constipation. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 137/79 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Cardiovascular exam is notable for a murmur at the right sternal border that radiates to the carotids. Pulmonary exam reveals mild bibasilar crackles. Musculoskeletal exam is notable for mild midline tenderness of the lower thoracic spine and the upper segment of the lumbar spine. No bruising or signs of external trauma are observable on the back. Symptoms are not exacerbated when the patient is lying down and her straight leg is lifted. Strength is 5/5 in the lower and upper extremities. The patient's sensation is intact bilaterally in her lower and upper extremities. Laboratory values are ordered and return as seen below.

Hemoglobin: 11 g/dL
Hematocrit: 34%
Leukocyte count: 10,500/mm^3 with normal differential
Platelet count: 288,000/mm^3

Serum:
Na+: 139 mEq/L
Cl-: 100 mEq/L
K+: 4.3 mEq/L
HCO3-: 25 mEq/L
BUN: 20 mg/dL
Glucose: 99 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.6 mg/dL
Ca2+: 11.8 mg/dL
AST: 12 U/L
ALT: 12 U/L

Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 59-year-old man presents to the emergency department with sudden onset abdominal pain that started this morning. The patient has a past medical history of alcoholism, obesity, and peptic ulcer disease and his current medications include ibuprofen, acetaminophen, and naproxen. His temperature is 98°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 117/58 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 16/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is notable for diffuse abdominal tenderness with a positive Murphy sign and epigastric tenderness. The patient is currently vomiting and smells of alcohol. A radiograph is obtained as seen in Figure A and laboratory values are pending. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old man presents from home hospice with a change in his mental status. He has seemed more confused lately and is unable to verbalize his symptoms. His temperature is 102°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 117/65 mmHg, pulse is 110/min, respirations are 19/min, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a right upper quadrant mass that elicits discomfort when palpated. Ultrasound is notable for pericholecystic fluid and gallbladder wall thickening without any gallstones. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with a sensation of fluttering in her chest. She has had these symptoms intermittently in the past, but states that this time her symptoms have been persistent. She is currently studying for exams and has been drinking roughly 10 cups of coffee per day. Her temperature is 98°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 115/60 mmHg, pulse is 124/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is only notable for tachycardia. An electrocardiogram (ECG) is obtained as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old man presents to the emergency department with confusion starting this morning. His wife states that he initially complained of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and fatigue after eating. He has vomited 3 times and progressively became more confused. His past medical history is notable for morbid obesity, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, a sleeve gastrectomy 1 month ago, and depression with multiple suicide attempts. His temperature is 98.0°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 104/54 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. His physical exam is notable for generalized confusion. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below.

Serum:
Na+: 139 mEq/L
Cl-: 100 mEq/L
K+: 3.9 mEq/L
HCO3-: 24 mEq/L
BUN: 22 mg/dL
Glucose: 41 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL
C-peptide level: normal

Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old woman presents to the emergency department for chest pain. She was working in her yard when her symptoms started. She initially felt a "pull" in her chest. This was followed by her feeling light headed. The patient has no past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. Her temperature is 98.4°F (36.9°C), blood pressure is 137/77 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. An ECG is performed as seen in Figure A. Initial laboratory values and troponins are pending. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 24-year-old woman presents to the emergency department after a motor vehicle accident. She was the unrestrained driver in a head-on collision. The patient was ejected from the front seat and found by paramedics outside her car. In the trauma bay, the patient is started on IV fluids, blood products, and vasopressors. A FAST exam and chest radiograph are performed (Figure A), and multiple lacerations are repaired. After the initial resuscitation, her temperature is 98.4°F (36.9°C), blood pressure is 107/58 mmHg, pulse is 122/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. The patient is conscious and complains of severe left shoulder pain and shortness of breath. She also vomits several times. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old woman with a history of diabetes mellitus, COPD, and a ST-elevation myocardial infarction currently on dialysis presents with shortness of breath for the past 2 hours. The patient missed her recent dialysis appointment and has been noncompliant with her other medications. The patient found out her best friend died this morning and has felt worse since this event. Her temperature is 98.7°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 87/48 mmHg, pulse is 130/min, respirations are 27/min, and oxygen saturation is 92% on room air. A bedside ultrasound demonstrates an anechoic rim surrounding the heart with poor cardiac squeeze, global hypokinesis, and right ventricular collapse with pleural sliding. Laboratory values are notable for 2 cardiac troponins that measure 0.72 ng/mL and 0.71 ng/mL. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old woman presents to the emergency department after an episode of syncope. She states that she was at home when she suddenly felt weak and experienced back pain that has been persistent. She states that she vomited forcefully several times after the episode. The patient has a past medical history of diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, and depression. She smokes 1.5 packs of cigarettes per day and drinks 10 alcoholic beverages each night. Her temperature is 97.5°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 107/48 mmHg, pulse is 130/min, respirations are 19/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. A chest radiograph is within normal limits. Physical exam is notable for abdominal tenderness and a woman resting in an antalgic position. Urinalysis is currently pending but reveals a concentrated urine sample. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old woman presents to the emergency department after an episode of palpitations followed by syncope. She awoke after being unconscious for several seconds but still has a sensation of palpitations. The patient is not currently followed by a primary care doctor but states that she has never had any health problems. Her temperature is 98.5°F (36.9°C), blood pressure is 133/91 mmHg, pulse is 95/min, respirations are 19/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. An electrocardiogram (ECG) is performed as seen in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with chest pain and shortness of breath. She has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes, and obesity. Her temperature is 98.6°F (37.0°C), blood pressure is 177/118 mmHg, pulse is 127/min, respirations are 11/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. An electrocardiogram is performed and the patient is started on aspirin and metoprolol. The patient is treated appropriately and transferred to the medical floor. On the second day of her hospitalization, the patient reports having abdominal pain. Her serum lipase is 272 U/L and her creatinine is 1.6 mg/dL. Physical exam is notable for the finding in Figure A. She is requesting pain medication for her abdominal pain. Which of the following is the most likely underlying diagnosis?

A 24-year-old man presents to his primary care physician with a longstanding history of diarrhea. He reports recurrent, foul-smelling, loose stools and a 35 lb weight loss over the past 3 years. He also states that two months ago, he developed an "itchy, bumpy" rash on his elbows and forearms which has since resolved. He denies recent camping trips or travel outside of the country. On physical exam he appears thin, his conjunctiva and skin appear pale, and his abdomen is mildly distended. Which of the following tests would confirm this patient's diagnosis?

A 27-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with a chief concern of abdominal pain and diarrhea. The patient states that for the past 4 days she has experienced abdominal pain, diarrhea, weakness and a subjective fever. She also endorses a weight loss of 11 pounds during this time. The patient has a past medical history of celiac disease, constipation, and depression. Her current medications include fish oil, a multivitamin, sodium docusate, and fluoxetine. Her temperature is 98.5°F (36.9°C), blood pressure is 110/75 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a young woman in mild distress. Cardiac and pulmonary exams are within normal limits. Abdominal exam is notable for generalized tenderness and increased bowel sounds. Oral exam is notable for multiple shallow painful ulcers. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below:

Hemoglobin: 12 g/dL
Hematocrit: 36%
Leukocyte count: 8,000 cells/mm^3 with normal differential
Platelet count: 227,500/mm^3

Serum:
Na+: 141 mEq/L
Cl-: 101 mEq/L
K+: 4.5 mEq/L
HCO3-: 24 mEq/L
BUN: 17 mg/dL
Glucose: 82 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL
Ca2+: 10.1 mg/dL
AST: 12 U/L
ALT: 11 U/L

A stool guaiac test is performed which returns positive. The patient is started on IV fluids and morphine. Which of the following best describes the most likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old girl is brought to the pediatrician by her father for an initial visit. She recently immigrated from Cambodia. Through an interpreter, the patient reports 6 months of mild exertional dyspnea. She denies chest pain or palpitations. Her medical history is unremarkable and she has never had any surgeries. Her family history is significant for hypertension and diabetes. Her mother died of tuberculosis. The patient’s vaccination history is unknown. Her temperature is 98°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 113/71 mmHg, and pulse is 82/min. Her BMI is 24 kg/m^2. Physical examination shows a well-nourished, cooperative girl without any grossly dysmorphic features. Cardiac auscultation reveals a grade II systolic ejection murmur along the left upper sternal border and a mid-diastolic rumble along the left sternal border. S1 is normal and the splitting of S2 does not change with inspiration. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 74-year-old man with a past medical history of hypertension, peripheral artery disease, and migraine headaches presents to the emergency department with a two hour history of severe abdominal pain. The patient cannot recall any similar episodes, although he notes occasional abdominal discomfort after eating. He describes the pain as sharp periumbilcal pain. He denies recent illness, fever, chills, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. His last normal bowel movement was yesterday evening. His temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 110/min, blood pressure is 140/80 mmHg, and respirations are 20/min. On exam, the patient is grimacing and appears to be in significant discomfort. Heart and lung exams are within normal limits. The patient’s abdomen is soft and non-distended with diffuse periumbilical pain on palpation. There is no rebound tenderness or guarding, and bowel sounds are present. The rest of the exam is unremarkable. Labs in the emergency room show:

Serum:
Na+: 144 mEq/L
Cl-: 105 mEq/L
K+: 3.7 mEq/L
HCO3-: 20 mEq/L
BUN: 15 mg/dL
Glucose: 99 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.2 mg/dL
Ca2+: 10.7 mg/dL
Phosphorus: 5.2 mg/dL
Lactate: 7.0 mmol/L
Amylase: 240 U/L

Hemoglobin: 13.4 g/dL
Hematocrit: 35%
Leukocyte count: 12,100 cells/mm^3 with normal differential
Platelet count: 405,000/mm^3

What is the next best step in diagnosis?

A 25-year-old woman presents to the emergency department for a fever and abdominal pain. The patient states that her pain has been worsening over the past week in the setting of a fever. She has a past medical history of IV drug abuse and multiple admissions for septic shock. Her temperature is 102°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 94/54 mmHg, pulse is 133/min, respirations are 22/min, and oxygen saturation is 100% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a murmur over the left upper sternal border. Abdominal exam reveals left upper quadrant tenderness. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below.

Hemoglobin: 15 g/dL
Hematocrit: 44%
Leukocyte count: 16,700/mm^3
Platelet count: 299,000/mm^3

Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old woman presents to the physician with progressive weight loss for the last 3 months. She also says she frequently sweats profusely at night and has a recurring low-grade fever, for which she takes acetaminophen. The patient denies any symptoms like cough, breathlessness, or gastrointestinal symptoms. Her temperature is 37.1ºC  (98.8ºF), pulse is 76/min, blood pressure is 116/78 mm Hg, and respiratory rate is 13/min. On physical examination, she has generalized pallor. Bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy is present. Examination of her abdomen reveals non-tender hepatosplenomegaly in the right upper quadrant. Laboratory evaluation confirms the diagnosis of Hodgkin’s lymphoma. Which of the following viral infections is most likely to have played a role in the pathogenesis of this patient’s malignancy?

A 70-year-old woman is at her dermatologist’s office for the treatment of a severely pruritic erythroderma with scaling on her buttocks that has been slowly progressing over the past two weeks. The patient works as a truck driver and has a history of hypertension treated with enalapril. The patient reports having tried an over-the-counter cream on the rash without improvement. The vital signs are within normal range. On physical exam, she has multiple confluent and well-demarcated pink patches on her buttocks and legs with some scaling and enlarged inguinal lymph nodes. The dermatologist orders a skin biopsy that reveals Pautrier microabscesses. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 11-month-old girl presents with a scaly erythematous rash on her back for the past 2 days. No significant past medical history. Family history is significant for the fact that the patient’s parents are first-degree cousins. In addition, her older sibling had similar symptoms and was diagnosed with a rare unknown skin disorder. On physical examination, whitish granulomatous plaques are present in the oral mucosa, which exhibit a tendency to ulcerate, as well as a scaly erythematous rash on her back. A complete blood count reveals that the patient is anemic. A plain radiograph of the skull shows lytic bone lesions. Which of the following immunohistochemical markers, if positive, would confirm the diagnosis in this patient?

A 68-year-old woman presents to the emergency department complaining of difficulty in breathing for the past 2 days. She has had recurrent episodes of bacterial pneumonia in the right lower lobe during the last 6 months. Her last episode of pneumonia started 7 days ago for which she is being treated with antibiotics. She has a 35-pack-year smoking history. Past medical history is significant for hypertension for which she takes lisinopril. Physical examination reveals decreased breath sounds and dullness to percussion in the right lung base. Chest X-ray reveals a large right-sided pleural effusion, and chest CT scan shows a large mass near the hilum of the right lung. Cytologic examination of pleural fluid shows evidence of malignancy. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis of this patient?

A 73-year-old woman presents to the office, complaining of “weird blisters” on her right hand, which appeared 2 weeks ago. The patient says that she initially had a rash, which progressed to blisters. She denies any trauma or known contact with sick people. She is worried because she hasn’t been able to garden since the rash appeared, and she was planning on entering her roses into an annual competition this month. Her vital signs are stable. On physical exam, the patient has multiple bullae accompanied by red, papular lesions on her right hand, which progress to her forearm. The right axillary lymph nodes are swollen and tender. What is the treatment for the most likely diagnosis of this patient?

A 19-year-old man with a known history of malabsorption presents with a painful red tongue, red eyes, and cracked lips. He says his symptoms gradually onset 4 months ago after moving away from home for college. He also complains of photophobia, spontaneous lacrimation, and itchy dermatitis. Past medical history is significant for a long-standing malabsorption syndrome, which he says that he hasn’t been able to maintain his normal diet or take his vitamins regularly due to his busy schedule. The patient is afebrile and vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, he has a malnourished appearance with significant pallor. Conjunctival injection is present bilaterally. Which of the following diagnostic tests will be most helpful to support the diagnosis of the most likely vitamin deficiency in this patient?

A 50-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department due to chest pain and shortness of breath for the last 2 hours. She describes the chest pain as squeezing in nature and radiating towards her left arm. It is associated with nausea and sweating. She has a similar history in the past, which is mostly aggravated with strenuous activities and relieved with sublingual nitroglycerin. She has a history of uncontrolled diabetes and hypercholesterolemia for the last 10 years. Her last HbA1c was 8.0 %. Her blood pressure is 150/90 mm Hg, pulse rate is 90/min, respiratory rate is 20/min, and temperature is 36.8°C (98.3°F). Oxygen saturation in room air is 98%. ECG shows ST-segment elevation in leads I, II, and aVF. She is being prepared for coronary angioplasty. Elevation in which of the following enzymes is most significant in the diagnosis of this patient?

A 5-year-old boy presents with a rash and a persistent fever of 41.0°C (105.8°F), not relieved by Tylenol. The patient’s father says that his symptoms started 5 days ago and have not improved. The rash started on his trunk and now is present everywhere including the palms and soles. His birth history is normal. His pulse is 120/min and respiratory rate is 22/min. On physical examination, the patient is agitated and ill-appearing. There is significant swelling of the distal upper and lower extremities bilaterally. The pharynx is hyperemic (see image). Generalized edema with non-palpable cervical lymphadenopathy is noted. Muscle tone is normal. Remainder of exam is unremarkable. Laboratory findings are significant for the following:
Laboratory test
Hb 9 g/dL
RBC 3.3/mm3
Neutrophilic leukocytosis 28,000/mm3
Normal platelet count 200,000/mm3
Serum ɣ-GT increased
Hyperbilirubinemia 2.98 mg/dL
AST and ALT are normal, but there is markedly increased serum CRP. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 25-year-old man presents with abdominal pain and discomfort for the past 3 days. He was diagnosed with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) a couple of years ago, managed until recently with imipramine, psyllium, and loperamide. 5 days ago, because he had developed alternating diarrhea and constipation, bloating, and abdominal pain on his medication, he was started on alosetron. His current temperature is 39.0°C (102.2°F), the heart rate is 115/min, the blood pressure is 90/60 mm Hg and the respiratory rate is 22/min. Abdominal examination shows diffuse tenderness to palpation with guarding but no rebound. Bowel sounds are hypoactive on auscultation. A fecal occult blood test is positive and laboratory tests show his white cell count to be 15,800/µL. Arterial blood gas (ABG) analysis reveals a metabolic acidosis Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 34-year-old woman presents to a clinic with complaints of abdominal discomfort and blood in the urine for 2 days. She has had similar abdominal discomfort during the past 5 years, although she does not remember passing blood in the urine. She has had hypertension for the past 2 years, for which she has been prescribed medication. There is no history of weight loss, skin rashes, joint pain, vomiting, change in bowel habits, and smoking. On physical examination, there are ballotable flank masses bilaterally. The bowel sounds are normal. Renal function tests are as follows:
Urea 50 mg/dL
Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL
Protein Negative
RBC Numerous
The patient underwent ultrasonography of the abdomen, which revealed enlarged kidneys and multiple anechoic cysts with well-defined walls. A CT scan confirmed the presence of multiple cysts in the kidneys. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 16-year-old girl presents after suffering a tonic-clonic seizure. She says it had a duration of 2 minutes and a postictal period of 10 minutes. Patient denies any similar episodes in the past. Past medical history is unremarkable. Family history is significant for her father and older sister who died of colorectal cancer at ages 40 and 20, respectively. On physical examination, the patient is drowsy but arousable and responsive to commands. Both pupils are symmetrical and responsive to light. An MRI of the brain reveals an infratentorial hypointense cerebellar mass with a small cystic area. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 7-year-old girl with a sore throat, fever, and generalized malaise is admitted to the pediatric floor. On physical examination, she has diffuse white exudate on both tonsils, and also a palpable spleen with mild hepatomegaly. Her blood smear shows large and abundant lymphocytes with blue-gray cytoplasm, irregular nuclei, and dark chromatin with inconspicuous nucleoli. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old woman presents to her primary care provider for evaluation of nocturnal cough and dyspnea. She has been a smoker for the past 15 years with a 7.5-pack-year smoking history. She has no significant medical history and takes no medications. Her blood pressure is 118/76 mm Hg, the heart rate is 84/min, the respiratory rate is 15/min, and the temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F). A sputum sample shows Charcot-Leyden crystals and Curschmann spirals. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old woman presents to the office with complaints of epigastric discomfort for the past 6 months. She adds that the discomfort is not that bothersome as it does not interfere with her daily activities. She does not have any other complaints at the moment. The past medical history is insignificant. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She recently came back from a trip to South America where she visited a relative who owned a sheep farm. On physical examination, she has a poorly palpable epigastric non-tender mass with no organomegaly. The hepatitis B and C serology are negative. The liver CT scan and MRI are shown. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old girl presents with a recent history of frequent falls. The images below depict her movements when she tries to get up from the floor. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 13-year-old girl has been suspended 5 times this year for arguing with teachers. She has presented a pattern of negativism and hostility that has lasted for about 8 months. When asked about the suspensions, she admits that she loses her temper easily and often blames the principal for not being fair to her. She usually finds an argument before finishing her homework. At home, she goes out of her way to annoy her siblings. She gets furious if her legal guardian finds out about it and confiscates her smartphone. Which of the following is an additional behavior characteristic of this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old man presents to a surgeon with a painless, slowly growing ulcer in the periauricular region for the last 2 months. On physical examination, there is an irregular-shaped ulcer, 2 cm x 1 cm in its dimensions, with irregular margins and crusting over the surface. The man is a fair-skinned individual who loves to go sunbathing. There is no family history of malignancy. After a complete physical examination, the surgeon performs a biopsy of the lesion under local anesthesia and sends the tissue for histopathological examination. The pathologist confirms the diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma of the skin. When he asks about the cause, the surgeon explains that there are many possible causes, but it is likely that he has developed squamous cell carcinoma on his face due to repeated exposure to ultraviolet rays from the sun, especially ultraviolet B (UVB) rays. If the surgeon’s opinion is correct, which of the following mechanisms is most likely involved in the pathogenesis of the condition?

A 51-year-old man is brought to the emergency department because of an aggressive cough with copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum. He says he has had this cough for about 11 years with exacerbations similar to his presentation today. He also reports that his cough is worse in the morning. He was evaluated multiple times in the past because of recurrent bouts of bronchitis that have required treatment with antibiotics. He is a non-smoker. On physical examination, the blood pressure is 125/78 mm Hg, pulse rate is 80/min, respiratory rate is 16/min, and temperature is 36.7°C (98.0°F). Chest auscultation reveals crackles and wheezing over the right middle lobe and the rest of his physical examinations are normal. The chest X-ray shows irregular opacities in the right middle lobe and diffuse airway thickening. Based on this history and physical examination, which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old patient presents to a medical office for a consultation regarding a mole on his nose that is increasing in size. He also complains of frequent headaches, which he associates with stress on the job. He works as a civil engineer and spends much of his time outside. His past medical history is positive for bronchial asthma; nevertheless, his vitals are stable. The mole is 8 mm in diameter, has irregular borders, and is brown in color. A biopsy is performed and sent for genetic analysis. A mutation is found. A mutation in which gene is characteristic of this patient’s main diagnosis?

A 40-year-old man presents to his family physician with a 3-week history of swollen neck. The small, round, and painless swelling, which was detected 3 weeks ago in the middle of his neck, has now increased in size. The swelling is associated with sweaty palms and soles, insomnia, irritability, nervousness, and fatigue; however, the patient does not complain of fever, cervical lymphadenopathy, weight loss, vision problems, or body swelling. The patient’s medical history is negative for similar symptoms or a thyroid disorder. The vital signs are within normal limits. Local examination reveals a 3 x 3 cm round, non-tender, non-fluctuant, and non-pulsatile swelling in the anterior triangle of his neck. The patient carries a total white blood cell count of 10,200/mm3, including 70% neutrophils, 30% lymphocytes, and zero eosinophils. The erythrocyte sedimentation rate is 20 mm/hr (normal, 0–29 mm/hr). What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old woman presents to the clinic with right-sided chest pain and difficulty breathing for the past 10 days. When it began, the pain was mild, but as time went on, it increased to a level at which the woman found it difficult to breathe. Two years ago, she was diagnosed with clear cell carcinoma of the kidney. Vital signs include: pulse rate is 72/min, blood pressure is 122/80 mm Hg, respiratory rate is 16/min, and temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F). On physical examination, the trachea appears to have deviated to the left, respiratory movements are diminished, there is decreased resonance on percussion, and there is an absence of breath sounds over the right hemithorax. Which of the following is the most likely clinical diagnosis in this patient?

A 78-year-old woman presents to the hospital because of shortness of breath and chest pain that started a few hours ago. 3 weeks ago she had surgery for a total hip replacement with a prosthesis. The patient was treated with prophylactic doses of low-weight heparin until she was discharged. She did not have a fever, expectoration, or any accompanying symptoms. She has a history of right leg deep vein thrombosis that occurred 5 years ago. Her vital signs include: heart rate 110/min, respiratory rate 22/min, and blood pressure 150/90 mm Hg. There were no significant findings on the physical exam. Chest radiography was within normal limits. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 11-month-old girl with a history of recurrent pneumonia, ear infections, and diarrhea presents to the clinic with another chest cold. You send a blood specimen to flow cytometry for analysis. The result is Bruton’s X-linked Agammaglobulinemia. Which combination of markers was helpful to make this diagnosis?

A 28-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with diffuse abdominal pain and nausea for the past 5 hours. The pain started with a dull ache but is now quite severe. She notes that she “just doesn’t feel like eating” and has not eaten anything for almost a day. Although the nausea is getting worse, the patient has not vomited. She notes no medical issues in the past and is not currently taking any medications. She admits to drinking alcohol (at least 2–3 bottles of beer per day after work and frequent binge-drinking weekends with friends). She says that she does not smoke or use illicit drugs. Vital signs include: pulse rate 120/min, respiratory rate 26/min, and blood pressure 100/70 mm Hg. On examination, the patient’s abdomen is diffusely tender. Her breath smells like alcohol, with a fruity tinge to it. Bowel sounds are present. No other findings are noted. Fingerstick glucose is 76mg/dL. After the examination, the patient suddenly and spontaneously vomits. Which of the following is the underlying mechanism of the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 60-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by police officers because she was acting strangely in public. The patient was found talking nonsensically to characters on cereal boxes in the store. Past medical history is significant for multiple hospitalizations for alcohol-related injuries and seizures. The patient’s vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows a disheveled woman who is oriented to person, but not time or place. Neurologic examination shows nystagmus and severe gait ataxia. A T1/T2 MRI is performed and demonstrates evidence of damage to the mammillary bodies. The patient is given the appropriate treatment for recovering most of her cognitive functions. However, significant short-term memory deficits persist. The patient remembers events from her past such as the school and college she attended, her current job, and the names of family members quite well. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 7-year-old girl presents to the clinic with her father, who notes that the way in which she plays has changed and that she has been limping, favoring her left leg. When asked, the patient states that her left knee hurts. She is afebrile and vital signs are stable. The patient is well nourished and meeting all developmental milestones. On physical examination, the knee has a full range of motion; however, passive motion elicits pain in the left hip. An X-ray is performed and reveals a flattened left femoral head. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 51-year-old white woman is not relevant to this case. 

Output: Parents bring an 11-month-old baby to the clinic because the baby has a fever of 39.0°C (102.2°F). The baby is irritated and crying constantly. He is up to date on immunizations. A complete physical examination reveals no significant findings, and all laboratory tests are negative. Five days after resolution of his fever, he develops a transient maculopapular rash. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old man presents to the office complaining of bloating and consistent fatigue. Past medical notes on his record show that he has seen several doctors at the clinic in the past year for the same concerns. During the discussion, he admits that coming to the doctor intensifies his anxiety and he does not enjoy it. However, he came because he fears that he has colon cancer and says, “There’s gotta be something wrong with me, I can feel it.” Past medical history is significant for obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). He sees a therapist a few times a month. His grandfather died of colon cancer at 75. Today, his blood pressure is 120/80 mm Hg, heart rate is 90/min, respiratory rate is 18/min, and temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F). Physical examination reveals a well-nourished, well-developed man who appears anxious and tired. His heart has a regular rhythm and his lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. His abdomen is soft, non-tender, and non-distended. No masses are palpated, and a digital rectal examination is unremarkable. Laboratory results are as follows:
Serum chemistry 
Hemoglobin 13 g/dL 
Hematocrit
38%
MCV 90 fl
TSH
4.1 μU/mL
Fecal occult blood test  negative
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old girl with Down syndrome presents with her father. The patient’s father says that she isn’t playing or eating as much as she used to and seems lethargic. Expected developmental delays are present and stable. Physical examination reveals dry mucous membranes and abdominal distention with no tenderness to palpation. An abdominal radiograph is shown in the image below. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 52-year-old Caucasian woman presents to the clinic for evaluation of a mole on her back that she finds concerning. She states that her husband noticed the lesion and believes that it has been getting larger. On inspection, the lesion is 10 mm in diameter with irregular borders. A biopsy is performed. Pathology reveals abnormal melanocytes forming nests at the dermo-epidermal junction and discohesive cell growth into the epidermis. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old school teacher visits his doctor because of disfiguring skin lesions that started to appear in the past few days. The lesions are mostly located on his chest, shoulders, and back. They are 2–5 mm in diameter, droplike, erythematous papules with fine silver scales. Besides a sore throat and laryngitis requiring amoxicillin several weeks ago, he has no significant medical history. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 9-year-old girl is brought to a physician by her father for evaluation of generalized weakness, increased urination, and increased thirst. The father mentions that her girl is always tired, and seems to be getting worse. She prefers watching television rather than going out and playing with other kids. Furthermore, she has had frequent episodes of constipation since birth. Except for frequent cravings for salty foods, the girl eats a regular diet. The patient was delivered healthy and is fully immunized. The medical history is unremarkable, and she takes no medications. She has no siblings. Her mother is a banker and her father is a librarian. The pulse is 90/min, the blood pressure is 110/75 mm Hg, and the respiratory rate is 15/min. She is in the bottom 10th percentile for height and weight according to her age. The remainder of the physical examination is unremarkable. She recently had a urinalysis that showed elevated urinary calcium excretion.
Additional lab testing results are as follows:
Serum electrolytes
Sodium 135 mEq/L
Potassium 3.2 mEq/L
Chloride 95 mEq/L
Plasma renin activity 10 ng/mL/hr (normal, 0.5–3.3 ng/mL/hr)
Plasma aldosterone concentration 20 ng/dL (normal, 2–9 ng/dL)
What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old female engineer presents to the office with shortness of breath on exertion and a dry cough that she has had for about a year. She is a heavy smoker with a 25-pack-years history. Her vitals include: heart rate 95/min, respiratory rate 26/min, and blood pressure 110/75 mm Hg. On examination, she presents with nail clubbing and bilateral and persistent crackling rales. The chest radiograph shows basal reticulonodular symmetric images, with decreased lung fields. The pulmonary function tests show the following: diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide (DLCO) is 43% and reference SaO2 is 94% and 72%, at rest and with exercise, respectively. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old man presents with pruritus and progressive weakness for the past 3 months. He says he feels excessively tired during the daytime and is losing interest in activities that used to be fun. The patient reports a history of heavy alcohol use and drinks around 20 ounces per week. Laboratory studies show:
Proteins 6.5 g/dL
Albumin 4.5 g/dL
Globulin 1.9 g/dL
Bilirubin 5.8 mg/dL
Serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 86 U/L
Serum aspartate transaminase (AST) 84 U/L
Serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP) 224 U/L
Antinuclear antibody (ANA) positive
Antimitochondrial antibody (AMA) positive
anti-HBs positive
anti-HBc negative
Which is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 35-year-old African American woman presents with fever, abdominal pain, and severe weakness since yesterday. On physical examination, the patient is jaundiced and shows a generalized pallor. Past medical history is significant for recently receiving anti-malaria prophylaxis before visiting Nigeria. Laboratory tests show normal glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) levels. Peripheral smear shows the presence of bite cells and Heinz bodies. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 38-year-old woman presents with pruritus and jaundice. Past medical history is significant for ulcerative colitis diagnosed 2 years ago, well managed medically. She is vaccinated against hepatitis A and B and denies any recent travel abroad. On physical examination, prominent hepatosplenomegaly is noted. Which of the following would confirm the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 21-year-old woman is brought to the office by her parents due to concerns about her behavior. They describe their daughter as aloof and a loner who earns average to below average grades in school. Today, her heart rate is 90/min, respiratory rate is 17/min, blood pressure is 110/65 mm Hg, and temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F). On physical examination, she appears gaunt and anxious. Her heart has a regular rhythm, and her lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. CMP, CBC, and TSH are normal. A urine toxicology test is negative. During the examination, she avoids eye contact and appears detached. When asked about her social life, she claims that she does not care about making friends and prefers to be alone. She says she enjoys going to the movies, but she enjoys doing this alone. She has not had a romantic partner before and takes little pleasure in intimacy. She denies experiencing hallucinations or delusions. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 10-month-old infant is brought in by her parents because she is vomiting and not passing stool. Her parents say she has vomited multiple times over the past couple of hours, but the most recent vomit was green. The patient has no significant past medical history. On physical examination, the patient is irritable and crying. On palpation in the periumbilical region, an abdominal mass is present. Emergency laparotomy is performed, which shows a part of the patient’s intestine folded into the section adjacent to it. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 55-year-old woman presents with severe fatigue and fever. Her past medical history is significant for a recent history of mononucleosis from which she fully recovered 8 weeks ago. On physical examination, the patient seems pale. A chest radiograph shows multiple enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes. A biopsy of one of the enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes is performed and shows the presence of multinucleated cells with an ‘owl-eye’ appearance in a hypocellular background. This patient’s most likely condition is very aggressive and associated with a very poor prognosis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 32-year-old man presents to his family physician with a long history of depression, irritability, and, more recently, personality changes. As his partner comments, he has stopped engaging in activities he used to enjoy like dancing, drumming lessons, and yoga. The patient denies changes in skin pigmentation and assures he keeps a balanced diet low in fat and carbohydrates. During the physical examination, jaundice and dark rings encircling the iris of the eye are noted, as well as hepatomegaly and gait disturbances. For a follow-up visit, the patient brings a battery of laboratory tests that includes a complete blood count showing normocytic normochromic anemia, a negative Coombs, normal iron levels, normal fasting glucose levels, elevated aminotransferases from the liver biochemical tests, bilirubin, and decreased serum ceruloplasmin levels. Antinuclear antibodies are negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old woman presents an urgent care clinic because she coughed up blood this morning. Although she had a persistent cough for the past 3 weeks, she had never coughed up blood until now. Her voice is hoarse and admits that it has been like that for the past few months. Both her past medical history and family history are insignificant. She has smoked a pack of cigarettes a day since the age of 20 and drinks wine every night before bed. Her vitals are: heart rate of 78/min, respiratory rate of 14/min, temperature of 36.5°C (97.8°F), blood pressure of 140/88 mm Hg. An indirect laryngoscopy reveals a rough vegetating lesion on the free border of the right vocal cord. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old woman who works as a resident in general surgery presents feeling "burned out" for the last 2 months. She says she has been working extremely long hours under stressful conditions, which makes her irritable, edgy, unfocused, and forgetful. She says she also has severe anxiety about how these symptoms are affecting her performance at work, making it difficult for her to sleep even when she has time off. The patient is referred for counseling and is prescribed some mild sleep aids. At follow-up a few months later, she says she is feeling much improved due to improved staffing at the hospital and a more manageable workload. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 32-year-old woman comes to the emergency room because of severe breathlessness for the past few hours. Over the course of a few years, she has been treated for asthma by several physicians, but her symptoms have continued to progress. She doesn’t smoke and never did. Both her father who died at the age of 40 years and her uncle (father’s brother), died with chronic obstructive pulmonary disorder. She has never smoked in her life. Her respiratory rate is 19/min and temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F). On physical examination, the patient has significantly longer exhalation than inhalation. Her expiratory time is longer than 6 seconds. Clubbing is present. Chest auscultation reveals bilateral crackles. Mild hepatomegaly is present. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old woman who recently emigrated as a refugee from Somalia presents with fever, weight loss, fatigue, and exertional chest pain. She says her symptoms began 3 weeks ago and that her appetite has decreased and she has lost 3 kg (6.6 lb) in the last 3 weeks. She denies any history of cardiac disease. Her past medical history is unremarkable. The patient admits that she has always lived in poor hygienic conditions in overcrowded quarters and in close contact with cats. Her vital signs include: blood pressure 120/60 mm Hg, pulse 90/min, and temperature 38.0°C (100.4°F). Physical examination reveals generalized pallor. A cardiac examination reveals an early diastolic murmur loudest at the left third intercostal space. Abdominal examination reveals a tender and mildly enlarged spleen. Prominent axillary lymphadenopathy is noted. Laboratory investigations reveal a WBC count of 14,500/μL with 5% bands and 93% polymorphonuclear cells. An echocardiogram reveals a 5-mm vegetation on the aortic valve with moderate regurgitation. Three sets of blood cultures are taken over 24 hours followed by empiric antibiotic therapy with gentamicin and vancomycin. The blood cultures show no growth after 5 days. Following a week of empiric therapy, the patient continues to deteriorate. Which of the following would most likely confirm the diagnosis in this patient?

A 76-year-old woman presents to her physician with her son for evaluation of memory loss and disorientation that has become progressively worse over the last few years. The patient’s son states that the memory loss started with her mother forgetting things ''here and there'' and the memory loss has progressed to the patient forgetting the names of loved ones and getting lost in familiar places. The medical history is non-contributory. On examination, the patient is awake and alert but only oriented to self (not time or place). The cardiopulmonary and neurologic exams are within normal limits. Routine lab work is performed to rule out infection and is found to be within normal limits. Four years later the patient passes away and an autopsy is performed to confirm the presumptive diagnosis. Brain biopsy slides are shown. What histologic features confirm this patient’s diagnosis?

A 10-year-old girl presents to the emergency department with sudden shortness of breath. She was playing in the school garden and suddenly started to complain of abdominal pain. She then vomited a few times. An hour later in the hospital, she slowly developed a rash on her chest, arms, and legs. Her breathing became faster with audible wheezing. On physical examination, her vital signs are as follows: the temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), the blood pressure is 100/60 mm Hg, the pulse is 130/min, and the respiratory rate is 25/min. A rash is on her right arm, as shown in the image. After being administered appropriate treatment, the girl improves significantly, and she is able to breathe comfortably. Which of the following is the best marker that could be measured in the serum of this girl to help establish a definitive diagnosis?

A 28-year-old woman presents with a yellow coloration of her skin. She says she feels well and denies any recent history of nausea, fatigue or fever, or discoloration of her urine or stool. The patient reports episodes with similar symptoms in the past. Family history is significant for similar symptoms in her father. The patient is afebrile and vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, she is jaundiced. Scleral icterus is present. Laboratory findings are significant only for an unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia. Liver enzymes are normal, and there is no bilirubin present in the urine. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment for this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old man presents to the clinic with complaints of occasional low-grade fever and joint pain for 1 month. He also complains of morning stiffness in the proximal interphalangeal joints of both hands, which lasts for 5 to 10 minutes. He recently noticed a pink rash on his nose and cheekbones. His family history is significant for similar complaints in his mother. He is not taking any medications. On examination, his temperature is 37.6°C (99.6°F), pulse is 74/min, blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg, and respirations are 18/min. Aphthous ulcers are noted on his oral mucosa. Which of the following tests would be most specific for confirming the diagnosis in this patient?

A 28-year-old woman is referred to the dermatologist for 2 months of increasing appearance of multiple smooth, circular patches of complete hair loss on her scalp. She says that the patches have associated pruritus and a burning sensation, and are not improving with the over-the-counter products recommended by her hair stylist. She denies pulling her hair intentionally. Physical examination reveals no epidermal inflammation or erythema, and no fluorescence is detected under Wood’s lamp. A punch biopsy shows a peribulbar lymphocytic inflammatory infiltrate surrounding anagen follicles, resembling a swarm of bees. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 45-year-old construction worker presents to her primary care physician with a painful and swollen wrist joint. A joint aspiration shows crystals, which are shown in the accompanying picture. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 16-month-old girl is brought to the pediatrician after her parents noticed the appearance of a rash on her face, torso, and limbs. The girl has been ill for almost 2 weeks, initiating with fever, malaise, coryza, headache, nausea, diarrhea, and a rash on both of her cheeks. Physical examination is unremarkable except for an erythematous maculopapular rash on the face, trunk, and extremities with a reticular pattern (as shown in the photograph). What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old woman presents with substernal chest pain for the past hour. She describes the chest pain as severe, squeezing in nature, diffusely localized to the substernal area and radiating down her left arm. She also has associated nausea, dizziness, and diaphoresis. She denies any recent history of fever, chest trauma, palpitations, or syncope. Past medical history is significant for gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), managed medically with a proton pump inhibitor for the last 3 months. She also has uncontrolled diabetes mellitus type 2 and hypercholesterolemia diagnosed 10 years ago. Her last HbA1c was 8.0. The vital signs include: blood pressure 140/90 mm Hg, pulse 100/min, respiratory rate 20/min, temperature 36.8°C (98.3°F) and oxygen saturation 98% on room air. She is administered sublingual nitroglycerin which lessens her chest pain. Chest radiograph seems normal. Electrocardiogram (ECG) shows ST-segment elevation in anterolateral leads. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis of this patient?

A 26-year-old woman presents to the behavioral health clinic for assistance overcoming her fear of public speaking. She has always hated public speaking. Two weeks ago, she was supposed to present a research project at school but had to leave the podium before the presentation. She recalled that her heart was racing, her palms were sweating, and that she could not breathe. These symptoms resolved on their own after several minutes, but she felt too embarrassed to return to college the next day. This had also happened in high school where, before a presentation, she started sweating and felt palpitations and nausea that also resolved on their own. She is scheduled for another presentation next month and is terrified. She states that this only happens in front of large groups and that she has no problems communicating at small gatherings. Other than her fear of public speaking, she has a normal social life and many friends. She enjoys her classes and a part-time job. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old woman presents to the emergency department due to sudden chest pain and difficulty breathing for the past 3 hours. The pain is felt in the retrosternal area and radiates up to her left shoulder and arm; it worsens on inspiration, and is relieved when she is leaning forward. Her heart rate is 61/min, respiratory rate is 16/min, temperature is 36.5°C (97.7°F), and blood pressure is 115/78 mm Hg. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Pericardial friction rub is heard on auscultation. Laboratory results show elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels. An ECG is performed. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old woman, with a recent ischemic stroke due to a right middle cerebral artery thromboembolism, presents for evaluation. In addition to the abnormal neurologic findings, there are significant hepatosplenomegaly and multiple lymphadenopathies. Laboratory findings are significant for the following:
Hemoglobin  9.5 g/dL
Erythrocyte count 13,600/mm³
Platelet count 95,000/mm³
Urinalysis reveals the presence of Bence-Jones proteins. Bone marrow biopsy shows numerous small lymphocytes mixed with plasmacytoid dendritic cells and plasma cells, increased numbers of mast cells, and the presence of Russell bodies and Dutcher bodies in plasma cells. A diagnosis of lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma is confirmed after further laboratory evaluation. Which of the following infectious agents would most likely be found in this patient, as well?

A 50-year-old woman presents to her primary care provider complaining of smelling abnormal odors on several occasions. She says that she smells burnt rubber even though there is nothing burning and no one around her can smell what she does. This symptom has been intermittently bothering her for the past 6 months.
