Also during this period, she had occasional nosebleeds. She works as a high school teacher. Although her work gets a little stressful around the exam season, she says she is able to cope well. Family history is unremarkable. She does not smoke or drink alcohol and denies the use of any medication. Physical examination reveals unilateral nasal obstruction with some dried blood in the nasal passage. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old woman presented to the hospital with right upper quadrant abdominal pain. She has a history of hepatitis B. She underwent a CT of her abdomen which revealed a large mass (11.3 cm x 7.2 cm in diameter) with a metastatic retroperitoneal lymph node. She was diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma and initially received radiotherapy while on the transplant list to prevent local expansion of her malignancy. 3 months after radiotherapy, the patient experienced hematemesis and melena. She was admitted to the emergency department for evaluation. Her vitals were: blood pressure 84/56 mmHg, heart rate 92/min, and respiratory rate 20/min. Laboratory evaluation revealed severe anemia with a hemoglobin level of 5.7 g/dL, INR 1.8 and platelets of 68,000 cells/mm3. She received a blood transfusion. An endoscopic examination demonstrated diffuse edematous hyperemic mucosa and multiple hemorrhagic patches with active oozing in the antrum. What is the most likely diagnosis for the lesions seen in endoscopy?

A 55-year-old truck driver is brought to a physician by her husband. He states that his wife developed a fever and began feeling weak 3 days ago, but has refused medical help. She has been unable to go to work because of her symptoms. The patient has been previously hospitalized for a tricuspid valve replacement surgery 1 year ago and takes aspirin daily. The medical history is also relevant for myocardial infarction 3 years ago and hypertension for the past 10 years, for which she takes lisinopril. Her blood pressure is 140/80 mm Hg, the pulse is 82/min, the respirations are 18/minute, and the temperature is 37.2°C (98.9°F). On examination, several hemorrhages are noted on the nail beds of several fingers. Which of the following findings would be most helpful in establishing a diagnosis?

A 3-year-old boy is brought to the pediatrician by his parents who are concerned that he is not developing normally. They say he does not talk and avoids eye contact. He prefers to sit and play with blocks by himself rather than engaging with other children. They also note that he will occasionally have violent outbursts in inappropriate situations. He is otherwise healthy. In the office, the patient sits quietly in the corner of the room stacking and unstacking blocks. Examination of the patient shows a well-developed male with no physical abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 25-year-old woman presents to the office for a 3-day history of fever and fatigue. Upon further questioning, she says that she also had constant muscular pain, headaches, and fever during these days. She adds additional information by giving a history of regular unprotected sexual relationship with multiple partners. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. The heart rate is 102/min, respiratory rate is 18/min, temperature is 38.0°C (100.4°F), and blood pressure is 120/80 mm Hg. On physical examination, she is icteric and hepatosplenomegaly is evident with diffuse muscular and abdominal tenderness particularly in the right upper quadrant. The serologic markers show the following pattern:
Anti-HAV IgM negative
HBsAg positive
Anti-HBs negative
IgM anti-HBc positive
Anti-HCV negative
Anti-HDV negative
What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old chronic smoker presents to the physician with a complaint of worsening left shoulder pain for several months which has become acutely worse the past 2 weeks and now radiates down her left arm. Physical examination reveals a palpable 2 x 1.5 cm supraclavicular lymph node along with decreased grip strength in her left hand. Examination of the face reveals partial ptosis of the left eyelid and miosis of the left eye. Laboratory testing shows the following values:
Sodium (Na+) 135 mEq/L
Potassium (K+) 3.6 mEq/L
Chloride (Cl-) 100 mEq/L
BUN 12 mg/dL
Creatinine (Cr) 0.6 mg/dL
Magnesium (Mg2+) 1.5 mg/dL
Phosphate 3 mg/dL
Calcium (Ca2+) 8.5 mg/dL
An X-ray of the chest reveals a soft tissue mass at the apex of the left lung with possible involvement of the first rib. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 75-year-old man presents with episodic abdominal pain following meals for the past few years. He says these episodes have worsened over the past month. Past medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed 30 years ago, managed with metformin. His most recent HbA1C last month was 10%. Vital signs include: blood pressure 110/70 mm Hg, pulse 80/min, and respiratory rate 16/min. Physical examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 24-year-old man presents with fever, abdominal pain, and bloody bowel movements. He says his symptoms onset 2 days ago and have not improved. He describes the abdominal pain as moderate, cramping in character, and poorly localized. 1 week ago, he says he was on a camping trip with his friends and had barbecued chicken which he thought tasted strange. The patient denies any chills, hemoptysis, hematochezia, or similar symptoms in the past. The vital signs include: pulse 87/min and temperature 37.8°C (100.0°F). Physical examination is significant for moderate tenderness to palpation in the periumbilical region with no rebound or guarding. Stool is guaiac positive. Which of the following is a complication associated with this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 14-year-old girl is brought to the office by her parents because she states that for the past 2 months she has been feeling constantly tired, and also noticed a dull pain in the pit of her stomach. The patient has no relevant family history. The vital signs include a heart rate of 105/min, a respiratory rate of 16/min, a temperature of 37.0°C (98.6°F), and a blood pressure of 111/66 mm Hg. On physical exam, the abdomen is distended with hepatomegaly 5 cm underneath the xiphoid process. The complete blood count results are as follows:
Hemoglobin 17.6 g/dL
Hematocrit 64%
RBC 6.02 x 1012/L
Leukocyte count
26,300/mm3
Neutrophils 55%
Bands 2%
Eosinophils 1%
Basophils 0%
Lymphocytes 29%
Monocytes 2%
Platelet count 480,000/mm³
Erythropoietin < 1.0 mU/mL
The coagulation test results are as follows:
Partial thromboplastin time (activated) 30.9 s
Prothrombin time 14.0 s
The abdominal Doppler ultrasound imaging is shown in the picture. What is the most likely etiology of this patient’s diagnosis?

A 24-year-old man of Ashkenazi Jewish descent presents with recurrent bloody diarrhea and abdominal pain. He says he feels well otherwise. Review of systems is significant for a 4 kg weight loss over the past month. Physical examination is significant for multiple aphthous oral ulcers. Colonoscopy reveals a cobblestone pattern of lesions of the mucosa of the intestinal wall involving the sigmoid colon. The patient is informed of the diagnosis and medication to treat his condition is prescribed. On a follow-up visit 6 weeks later, the patient presents with non-productive cough, chest pain, dyspnea on exertion, and worsening oral lesions. A chest radiograph reveals a diffuse interstitial pattern. Which of the following enzymes is inhibited by the medication most likely prescribed for his initial diagnosis?

A 70-year-old woman presents for her annual check-up. She says she feels well except for occasional abdominal pain. She describes the pain as 4/10–5/10 in intensity, diffusely localized to the periumbilical and epigastric regions, radiating to the groin. The pain occurs 1–2 times a month and always subsides on its own. The patient denies any recent history of fever, chills, nausea, vomiting, change in body weight, or change in bowel and/or bladder habits. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and peripheral vascular disease, managed with lisinopril and simvastatin. The patient reports a 40-pack-year smoking history and 1–2 alcoholic drinks a day. The blood pressure is 150/100 mm Hg and the pulse is 80/min. Peripheral pulses are 2+ bilaterally in all extremities. Abdominal exam reveals a bruit in the epigastric region along with mild tenderness to palpation with no rebound or guarding. There is also a pulsatile abdominal mass felt on deep palpation at the junction of the periumbilical and the suprapubic regions. The remainder of the physical exam is normal. Laboratory studies show:
Serum total cholesterol 175 mg/dL
Serum total bilirubin 1 mg/dL
Serum amylase 25 U/L
Serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 20 U/L
Serum aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 16 U/L
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 24-year-old woman presents to the office for a physical exam and drug screening requested by her parole officer. She has a history of multiple run-ins with the law, including theft, destruction of property, and assault and battery. Patient confesses that she has always been the 'problem child' in her home and always got into trouble with authority figures. Past medical records reveal testimonies from her mother describing episodes of physically aggressive behavior in school starting at before 12. Although a single parent, her mother states there were no stressful changes or issues at home. Today's urine toxicology screens are negative. Which of the following is most likely this patient’s diagnosis?

A 9-year-old girl is brought in by her father because of bruising on her torso and limbs. The patient’s father denies any other symptoms and says she is otherwise healthy. Physical examination shows multiple petechiae and bruising on the torso and extremities bilaterally. The remainder of the physical exam is unremarkable. A complete blood count is normal. Her coagulation profile reveals:
Prothrombin time (PT) 12 sec
Activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) 60 sec
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 1-year-old, pale-looking girl presents with high-grade fever and ecchymosis, which she has been experiencing for the past 2 weeks. The girl has achieved all developmental milestones on time and has no history of medical illness in the past. Lab investigations reveal the following:
Hemoglobin 5.5 g/dL
WBC 112,000/mm3
Platelets 15,000/mm3
ESR 105/1st hour
The girl is referred to a hematologist, who suspects that she may be suffering from the neoplastic proliferation of immature B cells. The physician decides to do a flow cytometry analysis. Detection of which of the following markers would help confirm the suspected diagnosis?

A 30-year-old woman who recently emigrated from Southeast Asia presents with heartburn and a bad taste in her mouth. She says the symptoms have been present for the last 6 months and are much worse at night. She describes the pain as moderate to severe, burning in character, and localized to the epigastric region. She mentions that 1 month ago, she was tested for Helicobacter pylori back in her country and completed a course of multiple antibiotics, but there has been no improvement in her symptoms. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 58-year-old woman with a history of hepatitis C infection presents to her physician because of unintentional weight loss and weakness. She has lost 6.8 kg (15 lb) within the last 6 months. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows jaundice, splenomegaly, and caput medusae. A complete metabolic panel is ordered. Which of the following tests is the most likely to result in a diagnosis?

A 35-year-old woman, with a history of neurofibromatosis type 2 (NF2) diagnosed 2 years ago, presents with hearing loss in the right ear and tinnitus. Patient says that symptoms have been gradually progressive. She has difficulty hearing speech as well as loud sounds. She also gives a history of occasional headaches and vertigo on and off for 1 month, which is unresponsive to paracetamol. Her vitals include: blood pressure 110/78 mm Hg, temperature 36.5°C (97.8°F), pulse 78/min and respiratory rate 11/min. Tuning fork tests reveal the following:
  Left Right
Rinne’s test  Air conduction > bone conduction  Air conduction > bone conduction
Weber test Lateralized to left ear 
Other physical examination findings are within normal limits. An MRI of the head is ordered which is as shown in image 1. A biopsy is done which shows cells staining positive for S100 but negative for glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP). The histopathological slide is shown in image 2. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old boy is brought to a clinic with complaints of fever and sore throat for 2 days. This morning, he developed a rash on his face and neck which is progressing towards the trunk. The teachers in his school report that none of his classmates has similar symptoms. He has a normal birth history. On physical examination, the child looks healthy. The heart rate is 90/min, respiratory rate is 20/min, temperature is 39.0°C (102.2°F), and blood pressure is 90/50 mm Hg. An oropharyngeal examination reveals circumoral pallor with a red tongue, as shown in the photograph below. The chest and cardiac examinations are within normal limits. No hepatosplenomegaly is noted. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old girl is brought to the office by her father because of a large head contusion and altered mental status. At first, the father says his daughter got injured when a “pot fell from a shelf onto her head.” Later, he changes the story and says that she hit her head after “tripping over a football.” Physical examination shows cracks in the suture lines of the skull, and there is a flattened appearance to the bone. The patient’s mother arrives to inquire on how her daughter is “recovering from her fall down the stairs.” Upon request to interview the patient alone, the parents refuse, complaining loudly about the request. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 5-year-old girl is brought to the office by her father with complaints of facial puffiness and “frothy” urine for 4 days. The puffiness first started in her eyes and then spread to the face. Her father does not provide any history of similar symptoms in the past. Past medical history is non-significant. Her birth history is uneventful and all her vaccinations are up to date. The vital signs include: blood pressure 100/62 mm Hg, pulse 110/min, temperature 36.7°C (98.0°F), and respiratory rate 16/min. On examination, there is pitting edema of the upper and lower extremities bilaterally.
Urinalysis results are as follows:
pH 6.2
Color light yellow
RBC none
WBC 3–4/HPF
Protein 4+
Cast Fat globules
Glucose absent
Crystal none
Ketone absent
Nitrite absent
24-hour urine protein excretion 4.1 g
A renal biopsy is sent which shows normal glomeruli on light microscopy. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old woman goes to her primary care provider for a checkup after some blood work showed lymphocytosis 3 months ago. She says she has been feeling a bit more tired lately but doesn’t complain of any other symptoms. Past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She takes lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, and atorvastatin. Additionally, her right hip was replaced three years ago due to osteoarthritis. Family history is noncontributory. She drinks socially and does not smoke. Today, she has a heart rate of 95/min, respiratory rate of 17/min, blood pressure of 135/85 mm Hg, and temperature of 36.8°C (98.2°F). On physical exam, she looks well. Her heartbeat has a regular rate and rhythm and lungs that are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Additionally, she has mild lymphadenopathy of her cervical lymph nodes. A complete blood count with differential shows the following:
Leukocyte count 5,000/mm3
Red blood cell count 3.1 million/mm3
Hemoglobin 11.0 g/dL
MCV 95 um3
MCH 29 pg/cell
Platelet count 150,000/mm3
Neutrophils 40%
Lymphocytes 40%
Monocytes 5%
A specimen is sent for flow cytometry that shows a population that is CD 5, 19, 20, 23 positive. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old woman presents with episodic abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea for the past week. She says that the abdominal pain is diffusely localized to the periumbilical region and is dull and cramping in character. She also reports episodes of painful, bloody diarrhea up to 7 times per day. A colonoscopy is performed and shows continuous erythema, superficial ulcers, and pseudopolyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon. A biopsy is taken and sent for histological evaluation. One of the slides from the biopsy is shown in the image below. Which of the following histopathologic findings characteristic of this patient’s most likely diagnosis is marked by the yellow circle?

A 54-year-old gardener with diabetes mellitus from the Northeast Jillin Province in China acquired a small scratch from a thorn while working in her flower garden. After 3 weeks, she noticed a small pink, painless bump at the site of a scratch. She was not concerned by the bump; however, additional linearly-distributed bumps that resembled boils began to appear 1 week later that were quite painful. When the changes took on the appearance of open sores that drained clear fluid without any evidence of healing (as shown on the image), she finally visited her physician. The physician referred to the gardener for a skin biopsy to confirm her working diagnosis and to start treatment as soon as possible. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 65-year-old woman presents with pain in her left thigh for a week. She describes the pain as dull and constant, boring in nature, and localized deep below the thigh muscle. She says it is worse at night. Physical examination is significant for tenderness and warmth over the anterior aspect of the left thigh. A plain radiograph of the left femur shows increased cortical thickness with widened intercortical space. Laboratory studies show:
Alkaline phosphatase
925 U/L
Serum calcium
9.2 mg/dL
Serum phosphorus 4.4 mg/dL
Findings on bone biopsy are shown in the image. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 52-year-old woman presents with a 5-week history of multiple cutaneous ulcers on her left forearm and neck, which she first noticed after returning from a 2-month stay in rural Peru. She does not recall any trauma or arthropod bites. The lesions began as non-pruritic erythematous papules that became enlarged, ulcerated, and crusted. There is no history of fever or abdominal pain. She has been sexually active with a single partner since their marriage at 24 years of age. The physical examination reveals erythematous, crusted plaques with central ulceration and a raised border. There is no fluctuance, drainage, or sporotrichoid spread. A punch biopsy was performed, which revealed an ulcerated lesion with a mixed inflammatory infiltrate. Amastigotes within dermal macrophages are seen on Giemsa staining. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old woman presents to the office because of extreme fatigue for the past 2 days. She is also worried about her skin looking yellow. She does not have any other complaints and denies fever and headache. She admits to using illicit intravenous drugs in the past. She does not have any immunization records because she moved from Africa to the US at the age of 18. Her vital signs are as follows: heart rate 72/min, respiratory rate 14/min, temperature 37.9°C (100.2°F), and blood pressure 100/74 mm Hg. Physical examination is not significant except for mild diffuse abdominal tenderness. Her blood is drawn for routine tests and shows an alanine aminotransferase level (ALT) of 2,000 IU/L. A hepatitis viral panel is ordered which shows:
Anti-HAV IgM negative
HBsAg positive
Anti-HBs negative
IgM anti-HBc positive
Anti-HCV negative
Anti-HDV negative
What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old man who was recently ill with an upper respiratory infection presents to the emergency department with weakness in his lower limbs and difficulty breathing. His symptoms began with a burning sensation in his toes along with numbness. He claims that the weakness has been getting worse over the last few days and now involving his arms and face. Currently, he is unable to get up from the chair without some assistance. His temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), the blood pressure is 145/89 mm Hg, the heart rate is 99/min, the respiratory rate is 12/min, and the oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. On physical examination, he has diminished breath sounds on auscultation of bilateral lung fields with noticeably poor inspiratory effort. Palpation of the lower abdomen reveals a palpable bladder. Strength is 3 out of 5 symmetrically in the lower extremities bilaterally. The sensation is intact. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old woman presents with sexual dysfunction. Past medical history is significant for diabetes mellitus type 1 diagnosed 25 years ago, managed with insulin, and for donating blood 6 months ago. The patient denies any history of smoking or alcohol use. She is afebrile, and her vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows a bronze-colored hyperpigmentation on the dorsal side of the arms bilaterally. Nocturnal clitoral tumescence is not applicable in this context, however, the original mention of nocturnal penile tumescence being negative would translate to an assessment of sexual function relevant to the patient's gender. Routine basic laboratory tests are significant for a moderate increase in glycosylated hemoglobin and hepatic enzymes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

An 82-year-old man presents to the emergency department because of excruciating right flank pain and fever for the past 2 days. He states that he is having trouble urinating. His past medical history is unremarkable. A urinalysis is performed and comes back positive for leukocytes and gram-negative bacilli. A contrast computed tomography of the abdomen is performed and reveals a large retroperitoneal mass compressing the right ureter, leading to hydronephrosis of the right kidney. The mass is excised. Histopathologic evaluation of the mass is shown in the image below, and it is determined to be malignant. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 52-year-old man presents with erosions in his mouth that are persistent and painful. He says that symptoms appeared gradually 1 week ago and have progressively worsened. He also notes that, several days ago, flaccid blisters appeared on his skin, which almost immediately transformed to erosions as well. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 49-year-old man otherwise healthy presents to the outpatient department with swelling of the neck. Family history is negative for any thyroid disorders. Physical examination shows a nontender thyroid gland with a nodule on the right side. The thyroid gland is mobile on deglutition. Cervical lymphadenopathy is present. Fine needle aspiration and cytology show empty appearing nuclei with central clearing, nuclear grooves and branching structures interspersed with calcific bodies. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 31-year-old woman is referred to a neurologist due to her gradually increasing eccentric behavior and involuntary movements, especially the movements of her arms and hands. She also has difficulty with her short-term memory. Past medical history is otherwise noncontributory. Her father had similar symptoms before he died but those symptoms started at the age of 33. Her blood pressure is 125/92 mm Hg, pulse is 90/min, respiratory rate 12/min, and temperature is 36.6°C (97.9°F). Physical exam reveals involuntary writhing movements of hands, slow eye movements, and sporadic rigidity. The physician explains that this is an inherited disorder where the symptoms occur progressively at an earlier age than the parent and often with increased severity in the future generations. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis of this patient?

A 35-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by his coworkers after a sudden onset of vision loss. He is a lawyer and lost 3 cases in the past week. Yesterday, he experienced weakness and paralysis of his left wrist. Past medical history is significant for acid reflux. Physical examination reveals 2/4 in reflexes and 5/5 in muscular strength in all extremities. He appears indifferent to his current situation and presents with a flat affect. Slurring of words is absent. CT without contrast and MRI of the brain are unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old man presents with a history of repeated episodes of discoloration of the fingers over the last 3 years. He mentions that the episodes are usually triggered by exposure to cold, which leads to a sequential white, blue, and red discoloration of his fingers, followed by resolution of the symptoms. During an episode, he experiences pain and numbness in the affected fingers. The episodes are usually of short duration and do not interfere with his life, so he did not seek medical advice till now. Which of the following additional clinical features in this patient would most likely support the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old man presents to the office because of shortness of breath and chest tightness on exertion which he noticed for the past 2 months. He was diagnosed with asthma 1 month ago but says that the asthma medication has not improved his breathing. He does not smoke and works as a hotel manager. Examination shows mildly jaundiced conjunctivae, several spider nevi on his upper torso, and a barrel-chested appearance. A chest X-ray is obtained. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old woman presents with “yellowing” of the skin. She says she has been having intermittent upper abdominal pain, which is relieved by Tylenol. She also recalls that she has lost some weight over the past several months but can not quantify the amount. Her past medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus. She reports a 40-pack-year smoking history. The patient is afebrile and vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination reveals mild jaundice and a palpable gallbladder. Laboratory findings are significant for the following:
Total bilirubin 13 mg/dL
Direct bilirubin: 10 mg/dL
Alkaline phosphatase (ALP): 560 IU/L
An ultrasound of the abdomen reveals a hypoechoic mass in the epigastric region. The patient is scheduled for a CT abdomen and pelvis with specific organ protocol for further evaluation. Which of the following best describes this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

During a humanitarian medical mission in rural Vietnam, a medical resident encounters a 50-year-old woman with a year-long history of a pruritic rash on her upper body and face, along with numbness and tingling sensation of both of her palms. She mostly works on her family’s rice farm, where she also takes care of livestock. A physical examination revealed multiple erythematous macules and papules on the face, arms, chest, and back, as well as thinning of the eyebrows and loss of some eyelashes. Additional findings include hypopigmented macules around the elbows, which are insensitive to light touch, temperature, and pinprick. The grip strength is slightly diminished bilaterally with the conservation of both bicipital reflexes. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old man presents with facial flushing, weakness, and chronic diarrhea for the past month. He denies any history of smoking, alcohol use, or recreational drug use. The patient was on a trip to Thailand 2 years ago with his family but denies any recent travel. His blood pressure is 120/88 mm Hg, pulse is 78/min, temperature is 37.2°C (99.0°F), and respiratory rate is 16/min. Laboratory findings are unremarkable, except for a potassium level of 3.3 mmol/L and serum calcium of 11 mg/dL. The attending physician suspects that this might be a case of a genetic mutation in the menin 1 gene on chromosome 11 and orders a genetic analysis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 26-year-old female professional soccer player is brought to the emergency department due to an episode of syncope during a game. She has felt increasing shortness of breath during the past 3 months. During the past week, she has been feeling chest pain upon exertion. She also tells the doctor that her brother had a sudden death a couple of years ago. Her heart rate is 98/min, respiratory rate is 18/min, temperature is 36.5°C (97.7°F), and blood pressure is 110/72 mm Hg. On physical examination, there is a harsh crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur immediately after S1; it is best heard on the apex, and it radiates to the axilla. There is also an early diastolic murmur heard in early diastole, which is best heard with the bell of the stethoscope. When the Valsalva maneuver is performed, the murmur becomes louder. An ECG and an echocardiogram are performed, which confirm the diagnosis. What is the most likely cause of this patient’s condition?

A 21-year-old man presents to the emergency room with right arm pain and limited range of motion. He does not recall trauma to the arm. He also complains of diarrhea and nausea. He is sexually active with one female partner and admits to having pain during intercourse. There is vague and diffuse tenderness to palpation in all four abdominal quadrants. No erythema or edema is noted on the right arm. The fecal occult test is negative. Past records show that this patient has been in the ER 7 times in the past year with similar symptoms. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician with complaints of fluctuating mood for the past 2 years. She feels great and full of energy for some months when she is very creative with tons of ideas just racing through her mind. She is noted to be very talkative and distracted by her different ideas. During these times, she is very productive and able to accomplish much at work and home. However, these periods are frequently followed by a prolonged depressed mood. During this time, she has low energy, poor concentration, and low self-esteem. The accompanying feeling of hopelessness from these cycling “ups” and “downs” have her eating and sleeping more during the “downs.” She does not remember a period within the last 2 years where she felt “normal.” What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old woman, who was previously healthy, is taken to the emergency department due to agitation during the past 24 hours. During the past week, her family members noticed a yellowish coloring of her skin and eyes. She occasionally uses cocaine and ecstasy, and she drinks alcohol (about 20 g) on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behavior and does not use appropriate protection. Physical examination shows heart rate of 94/min, respiratory rate of 13/min, temperature of 37.0°C (98.6°F), and blood pressure of 110/60 mm Hg. The patient shows psychomotor agitation, and she is not oriented to time and space. Other findings include asterixis, jaundice on the skin and mucous membranes, and epistaxis. The rest of the physical examination is normal. The laboratory tests show:
Hemoglobin 16.3 g/dL
Hematocrit 47%
Leukocyte count 9,750/mm3
Neutrophils 58%
Bands 2%
Eosinophils 1%
Basophils 0%
Lymphocytes 24%
Monocytes 2%
Platelet count 365,000/mm3
Bilirubin 25 mg/dL
AST 600 IU/L
ALT 650 IU/L
TP activity < 40%
INR 1,5
What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old student presents to the college health clinic with a 1-week history of fever, sore throat, nausea, and fatigue. She could hardly get out of bed this morning. There are no pets at home. She admits to having recent unprotected sex. The vital signs include: temperature 38.3°C (101.0°F), pulse 72/min, blood pressure 118/63 mm Hg, and respiratory rate 15/min. On physical examination, she has bilateral posterior cervical lymphadenopathy, exudates over the palatine tonsil walls with soft palate petechiae, an erythematous macular rash on the trunk and arms, and mild hepatosplenomegaly. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 12-year-old girl presents with recurrent joint pain that migrates from joint to joint and intermittent fever for the last several weeks. She also says that she has no appetite and has been losing weight. The patient is afebrile, and vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, she is pale with diffuse petechial bleeding and bruises on her legs. An abdominal examination is significant for hepatosplenomegaly. Ultrasound of the abdomen confirms hepatosplenomegaly and also shows multiple enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes. A complete blood count (CBC) shows severe anemia and thrombocytopenia with leukocytosis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 35-year-old man visits his primary care provider with complaints of easy fatigability, breathlessness on exertion, and altered sensations in his lower limbs. Past medical history is positive for hypertension. He takes hydrochlorothiazide and lisinopril, testosterone (note: the original medication ethinyl estradiol-progestin is typically used for birth control in women and would need to be adjusted to a medication more relevant to a male patient, but without further context, the exact replacement is unclear), and a multivitamin every day. Family history is noncontributory. He drinks alcohol almost every day and smokes cigarettes when he drinks. Today his heart rate is 95/min, respiratory rate is 17/min, blood pressure is 130/92 mm Hg, and temperature of 37.0°C (98.6°F). Overall, he has marked pallor with slight bluing of his lips and distal fingertips. His heart has a regular rate and rhythm and his lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Additionally, he has loss of touch, and vibration sense in both of his lower limbs. His CBC is as follows:
Hemoglobin 8.0 g/dL
MCV 112 fL
WBC 2,500/mm3
Platelets 95,000/mm3
What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 12-year-old boy presents to the pediatric dermatologist with an expanding, but otherwise asymptomatic erythematous patch on his right shoulder, which he first noticed 3 days ago. The boy states the rash started as a small red bump but has gradually progressed to its current size. No similar lesions were observed elsewhere by him or his mother. He has felt ill and his mother has detected intermittent low-grade fevers. During the skin examination, a target-like erythematous patch, approximately 7 cm in diameter, was noted on the left shoulder (as shown in the image). Another notable finding was axillary lymphadenopathy. On further questioning it was revealed that the patient went camping with his grandfather approximately 11 days ago; however, he does not recall any insect bites or exposure to animals. The family has a pet cat living in their household. Based on the history and physical examination results, what is the most likely diagnosis?

A 52-year-old man presents with mild epigastric pain and persistent heartburn for the past 2 months. An endoscopy is performed and reveals inflammation of the stomach mucosa without evidence of ulceration. A biopsy is performed and reveals intestinal metaplasia with destruction of a large number of parietal cells. He is diagnosed with chronic atrophic gastritis. Which of the following is characteristic of this patient’s diagnosis?

A 75-year-old man presents to his primary care physician with his son because he is convinced that people are stealing from him. His son claims he has been misplacing his medications and money throughout the house. He recently lost his wife to old age and has become reclusive and no longer wants people to visit. Physical examination is unremarkable and the patient is oriented to person, time, and place. A mini-mental status examination (MMSE) is performed and he has difficulty recalling words after 5 minutes and also has problems with serial subtraction. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 44-year-old woman is brought to the clinic by her husband insisting that his wife has been acting strange lately. She is a dentist by profession and has no known medical conditions. For the past 6 weeks, she has insisted on listening to the 6 PM news on the radio. She is adamant that the news anchor is referencing her life during the broadcasts. Apart from this, her husband states that his wife is fine. She and her husband deny the use of any prescribed medications or illicit drugs. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol only on social occasions. Physical examination and routine laboratory investigations are normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70 year-old-woman comes to the clinic for generalized fatigue. She says that she is more tired than before and has difficulty catching her breath while walking upstairs. She feels tired quickly doing her usual activity such as gardening and shopping. She does not have any symptoms of fever, change in bowel habits, abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, or weight loss. Her appetite is normal. Her last colonoscopy was done 10 years ago and it was normal. Her blood pressure is 116/74 and heart rate is 87/min. On physical examination, her conjunctivae are pale. A routine blood test shows iron deficiency anemia with hemoglobin of 10 gm/dL. Her stool is positive for occult blood. She is then sent for a colonoscopy (image is shown). What is the most likely diagnosis for the above condition?

A 67-year-old woman presents with fatigue, progressive abdominal distention and yellow skin coloration for the past 2 weeks. She denies fever, chills, or other symptoms. Past medical history is unremarkable. She reports heavy alcohol consumption for the past several years but says she quit recently. On physical examination, the patient appears jaundiced and is ill-appearing. There is shifting dullness presents on abdominal percussion with a positive fluid wave. Sclera are icteric. Bilateral gynecomastia is not a typical finding in women, however, this case may present with other signs. Laboratory findings are significant for the following:
Hgb 13 g/dL
Leukocyte count 4,500/mm3
Platelets 86,000/mm3
Aspartate transaminase (AST) 108 U/L
Alanine transaminase (ALT) 55 U/L
GGT 185 U/L
Urea 23 mg/dL
Iron 120 μg/dL
Ferritin 180 μg/dL
Transferrin saturation 40%
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient? 

Note: The term "gynecomastia" typically refers to the enlargement of breast tissue in males. In females, breast tenderness or other breast-related symptoms might be described, but gynecomastia specifically is a condition more commonly associated with men. The description provided in the original text would need adjustment to accurately reflect a female patient's presentation, potentially mentioning changes in breast tissue or other relevant symptoms. However, to strictly follow the instructions given without adding or interpreting beyond the provided text, the term "gynecomastia" remains as is, acknowledging the inconsistency in the context of a female patient.

A 40-year-old farmer from Ohio seeks evaluation at a clinic with complaints of a chronic cough, fevers, and anorexia of several months duration. On examination, she has generalized lymphadenopathy with hepatosplenomegaly. A chest radiograph reveals local infiltrates and patchy opacities involving all lung fields. Fine needle aspiration of an enlarged lymph node shows the presence of intracellular yeast. A fungal culture shows the presence of thick-walled spherical spores with tubercles and microconidia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 16-year-old girl presents with a long-standing history of anemia. Past medical history is significant for prolonged neonatal jaundice and multiple episodes of jaundice without fever. On physical examination, the patient shows generalized pallor, scleral icterus, and splenomegaly. Her hemoglobin is 10 g/dL, and examination of a peripheral blood smear shows red cell basophilic stippling. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 14-month-old Caucasian girl is admitted to the pediatric clinic with an 8-month history of diarrhea, abdominal tenderness and concomitant failure to thrive. One of the possibilities that may cause these symptoms is Crohn’s disease, and on the basis of the attending pediatrician’s experience, the pre-test probability of this diagnosis was estimated at 40%. According to Fagan’s diagram (picture), if the likelihood ratio of a negative test result (LR-) is 0.04, what is the chance that this is the right diagnosis?

A 31-year-old man presents with pruritic vesicles on the right side of his torso. He notes that the lesions appeared 2 days ago and have not improved. One day prior to their appearance, he says that he experienced a burning sensation in the affected area. The patient is afebrile and vital signs are within normal limits. Upon physical examination, there are painful vesicles noted that are localized to the right T10 skin dermatome. Which of the following complications is associated with this patient’s likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old man was referred to a dermatology clinic due to a changing discoloration of his fingers from white to red to blue. Although he has not had any recent changes in his daily routines, he also complains of increasing fatigue, muscle weakness, and weight loss. He has a blood pressure of 126/77 mm Hg, respiratory rate of 14/min, and heart rate of 88/min. Physical examination reveals regular heart and lung sounds. Anti-U1 RNP antibodies and increased creatinine kinase were found in his serum. What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 14-year-old girl is brought to the office by her step-parents because she was recently caught beating a stray cat in an alley near her home. She has a police record which includes vandalism, shoplifting, and running away on two occasions. She has also received several detentions and threats of expulsion from school due to bullying and being too aggressive with the younger students. Past medical history is significant for a history of ADHD previously treated with methylphenidate, but now she does not take anything. Her biological family placed her and her brother into the foster care system. Her step-parents try to provide support and nurturing home life but the patient is very resistant and often acts out. What is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

An 18-month-old girl is presented to the emergency department by her parents due to swelling in her right knee after playing in the park. Her parents say there was no obvious injury. After questioning, the father says that an aunt of hers had similar problems. The vital signs include heart rate 146/min, respiratory rate 26/min, temperature 37.1°C (98.8°F) and blood pressure 90/52 mm Hg. On physical examination, the swelling of the right knee is evident. The rest of the physical findings are unremarkable. The ultrasound is compatible with the hemarthrosis of the right knee. The complete blood count (CBC) results are as follows:
Hemoglobin 12.2 g/dL
Hematocrit 36%
Leukocyte count 7,300/mm3
Neutrophils 45%
Bands 3%
Eosinophils 1%
Basophils 0%
Lymphocytes 44%
Monocytes 2%
Platelet count 200,000/mm³
The coagulation test results are as follows:
Partial thromboplastin time (activated) 52.0 s
Prothrombin time 14.0 s
Reticulocyte count 1.2%
Thrombin time < 2 seconds deviation from control
What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old woman from Thailand presents with low-grade fever, chronic cough, and night sweats for 3 months. She describes the cough as productive and producing white sputum that is sometimes streaked with blood. She also says she has lost 10 lb in the last 3 months. Past medical history is unremarkable. The patient denies any smoking history, alcohol, or recreational drug use. The vital signs include blood pressure 115/75 mm Hg, heart rate 120/min, respiratory rate 20/min, and temperature 36.6℃ (97.8℉). On physical examination, the patient is ill-looking and thin with no pallor or jaundice. Cardiopulmonary auscultation reveals some fine crackles in the right upper lobe. A chest radiograph reveals a right upper lobe homogeneous density. Which of the following tests would be most helpful in making a definitive diagnosis of active infection in this patient?

A 58-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with severe chest pain and uneasiness. She says that symptoms onset acutely half an hour ago while she was watching television. She describes the pain as being 8/10 in intensity, sharp in character, localized to the center of the chest and retrosternal, and radiating to the back and shoulders. The patient denies any associated change in the pain with breathing or body position. She says she has associated nausea but denies any vomiting. She denies any recent history of fever, chills, or chronic cough. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes mellitus for which she takes lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, simvastatin, and metformin. She reports a 30-pack-year smoking history and has 1–2 alcoholic drinks during the weekend. Family history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and an ST elevation myocardial infarction in her father and paternal uncle. Her blood pressure is 220/110 mm Hg in the right arm and 180/100 mm Hg in the left arm. On physical examination, the patient is diaphoretic. Cardiac exam reveals a grade 2/6 diastolic decrescendo murmur loudest over the left sternal border. Remainder of the physical examination is normal. The chest radiograph shows a widened mediastinum. The electrocardiogram (ECG) reveals non-specific ST segment and T wave changes. Intravenous morphine and beta-blockers are started. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 30-year-old patient comes to the emergency room with a chief complaint of left chest pain and a productive cough with purulent sputum for 1 week. She also complains of shortness of breath. She said she had been previously diagnosed with influenza but did not follow the doctor’s instructions. Her vitals include: heart rate 70/min, respiratory rate 22/min, temperature 38.7°C (101.7°F), blood pressure 120/60 mm Hg, and SO2 80%. Her hemogram and chest X-ray findings are as follows:
Hemoglobin 14 mg/dL
Hematocrit 45%
Leukocyte count 12,000/mm3
Neutrophils 82%
Lymphocytes 15%
Monocytes 3%
Platelet count 270,000/mm3
Chest X-ray alveolar infiltrates in the left base with air bronchograms
What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old woman presents to the office for shortness of breath. The shortness of breath started a year ago and is exacerbated by physical activity. She has been working in the glass manufacturing industry for 20 years. Her vital signs include: heart rate 72/min, respiratory rate 30/min, and blood pressure 130/80 mm Hg. On physical exam, there are diminished respiratory sounds on both sides. On the chest radiograph, interstitial fibrosis with reticulonodular infiltrate is found on both sides, and there is also an eggshell calcification of multiple adenopathies. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old man presents to your office complaining of difficulty swallowing, and he describes that "there is something in the back of his throat". Furthermore, he also feels an "achy" chest pain that has been getting progressively worse over the last few weeks. He denies having any fever, shortness of breath, cough, abdominal pain, heartburn, nausea, or vomiting. The patient has a history of wrist fracture as a child, migraines, and a recent diagnosis of myasthenia gravis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old woman visits the office with complaints of fever and abdominal pain for the past 6 days. She is also concerned about her weight loss as she weighs 3.6 kg (8 lb) less, today, than she did 2 months ago. She has a previous history of being admitted to the hospital for recurrent cholangitis. The vital signs include: heart rate 97/min, respiratory rate 17/min, temperature 39.0°C (102.2°F), and blood pressure 114/70 mm Hg. On physical examination, there is tenderness on palpation of the right upper quadrant. The laboratory results are as follows:
Hemoglobin 16 g/dL
Hematocrit 44%
Leukocyte count 18,000/mm3
Neutrophils  60%
Bands 4%
Eosinophils 2%
Basophils 1%
Lymphocytes  27%
Monocytes 6%
Platelet count 345,000/mm3
Aspartate aminotransferase (AST)  57 IU/L
Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 70 IU/L
Alkaline phosphatase 140 U/L
Total bilirubin 8 mg/dL
Direct bilirubin 5 mg/dL
An ultrasound is also done to the patient which is shown in the picture. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 13-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his parents for 5 days of abdominal pain, fever, vomiting, and mild diarrhea. His parents have been giving him acetaminophen in the past 3 days, which they stopped 24 hours ago when they noted blood in their son's urine. Upon admission, the patient has a fever of 39.6°C (103.3°F) and is hemodynamically stable. While waiting for the results of the laboratory tests, the patient develops intense left flank pain, and nausea and vomiting intensifies. His condition rapidly deteriorates with an abnormally high blood pressure of 180/100 mm Hg, a heart rate of 120/min, and labored breathing leading to ventilatory failure. Under these conditions, the ER team immediately transfers the patient to the pediatric ICU, however, the patient dies shortly after. The pathologist shares with you some excerpts from his complete blood count and peripheral smear report:
Hemoglobin 7 mg/dL
Mean 14.0 g/dL (-2SD: 13.0 g/dL)
MCV 85 fL; 80–96 fL
Platelets 60,000; 150,000–450,000
Peripheral smear Schistocytes (+); Schistocytes (-)
White blood cells 12,900; 4,500–11,000
What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by the police after she was found running around a local park naked and screaming late at night. During intake, the patient talks non-stop about the government spying on her and her family, but provides little useful information besides her name and date of birth. Occasionally she refers to herself in the third person. She refuses to eat anything and will only drink clear fluids because she is afraid of being poisoned. A medical records search reveals that the patient has been treated for psychotic behavior and occasional bouts of severe depression for several years. Today, her heart rate is 90/min, respiratory rate is 19/min, blood pressure is 135/85 mm Hg, and temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F). On physical exam, she appears gaunt and anxious. Her heart has a regular rate and rhythm and her lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. CMP, CBC, and TSH are normal. A urine toxicology test is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old woman presents with a history of intermittent fever for the last 2 days. She says her episodes of fever are accompanied by shaking and chills. She mentions that her father has been recently recovered from chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum malaria, which was treated successfully with quinine. On physical examination, her temperature is 38.9°C (102°F), pulse rate is 110/min, blood pressure is 116/80 mm Hg, and respiratory rate is 18/min. Examination of her abdomen reveals splenomegaly. Her blood sample is sent for the examination of the peripheral smear, which confirms the diagnosis of Plasmodium falciparum malaria. The patient is placed on treatment with oral quinine. After 5 days, the patient returns with improved symptoms of malaria but with complaints of a headache, tinnitus, nausea, and dizziness. The patient mentions that she has been taking a drug for the last 3 months to control her dyspepsia symptoms. Which of the following drugs is most likely to have caused the above-mentioned symptoms in this patient?

A 37-year-old patient is being evaluated for involuntary movements, difficulty swallowing food, and personality change. She has entered a clinical trial that is studying the interaction of certain neuromediators in patients with similar (CAG) n trinucleotide repeat disorders. The laboratory results of 1  of the candidates for the clinical trial are presented below:
Acetylcholine ↓
Dopamine ↑
Gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) ↓
Norepinephrine unchanged
Serotonin unchanged
Which trinucleotide disorder most likely represents the diagnosis of this patient?

A 55-year-old man presents with severe pruritus and fatigue. He denies any similar symptoms in the past. No significant past medical history. Upon physical examination, scleral icterus is present, and significant hepatosplenomegaly is noted. Mild peripheral edema is also present. Laboratory findings are significant for elevated serum levels of bilirubin, aminotransferases, alkaline phosphatase (ALP), γ-glutamyl transpeptidase (GGTP), immunoglobulins, as well as cholesterol (especially HDL fraction). Antiviral antibodies are not present. The erythrocyte sedimentation rate is also elevated. Anti-mitochondrial antibodies are found. A liver biopsy is performed, and the histopathologic examination shows bile duct injury, cholestasis, and granuloma formation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 79-year-old woman presents to the office due to shortness of breath with moderate exertion and a slightly productive cough. She has a medical history of 25 years of heavy smoking. Her vitals include: heart rate 89/min, respiratory rate 27/min, and blood pressure 120/90 mm Hg. The physical exam shows increased resonance to percussion, decreased breath sounds, and crackles at the lung base. Chest radiography shows signs of pulmonary hyperinflation. Spirometry shows a forced expiratory volume in the first second (FEV1) of 48%, a forced vital capacity (FVC) of 85%, and an FEV1/FVC ratio of 56%. According to these results, what is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old woman presents to the office for evaluation of a lesion on her upper arm that appeared a few months ago and has not healed. A patient appears healthful but has a history of cardiovascular disease. She states that her friend at the industrial ammunition factory where she works told her she should “get it looked at.” The patient admits to some nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea over the past year, but she states that she “feels fine now.” On physical examination, the lesion is an erythematous, scaly, ulcerated plaque on the flexor surface of her upper arm. The rest of the exam is within normal limits. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old man complains of fatigue and pallor. He says symptoms that started several months ago and have been becoming more serious with time. He reports that he has been exercising regularly and has been adhering to a strict vegan diet. The patient has no significant past medical history and takes no current medications. He denies any smoking history, alcohol use, or recreational drug use. He is tachycardic, but otherwise, his physical examination is unremarkable. A complete blood count (CBC) shows anemia with a low MCV (mean corpuscular volume), and a peripheral blood smear shows small erythrocytes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 47-year-old woman visits the outpatient clinic with complaints of heartburn and chest pain for the past 6 months. Her pain is retrosternal and was initially only associated with intake of solid foods, but it now occurs with liquids as well. Antacids do not relieve her pain anymore. She is worried about the pain as it is getting worse with time. She also had an unintentional weight loss of 2.7 kg (6 lb) during this period. Physical examination including the abdominal examination is normal. Laboratory investigations reveal:
Hgb 10 mg/dL
White blood cell total count 5 x 109/L
Platelet count 168 x 109/ L
Hematocrit 38%
Red blood cell count 4.2 x 1012/ L
Esophagogastroduodenoscopy reveals an exophytic mass in the lower third of the esophagus with ulcerations and mucous plugs. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 10-month-old girl is brought to the clinic with a history of recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. Her father reports that her wheezing is exacerbated by crying, feeding, and flexion of the neck, and is relieved by extension of the neck. Occasionally she vomits after feeding. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old man presents to the office with complaints of intense anal pain every time he has a bowel movement. The pain has been present for the past 4 weeks, and it is dull and throbbing in nature. It is associated with mild bright red bleeding from the rectum that is aggravated during defecation. He has no relevant past medical history. When asked about his sexual history, he reports practicing anal intercourse. The vital signs include heart rate 98/min, respiratory rate 16/min, temperature 37.6°C (99.7°F), and blood pressure 110/66 mm Hg. On physical examination, the anal sphincter tone is markedly increased, and it’s impossible to introduce the finger due to severe pain. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 43-year-old man presents for a routine checkup. He says he has been uncontrollably grimacing and smacking his lips for the past 2 months, and these symptoms have been getting progressively worse. Past medical history is significant for schizophrenia, managed medically with clozapine. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 44-year-old woman presents to a clinic for the evaluation of difficulty swallowing for the past few days. She says that she has noticed progressively worsening chest pain when she attempts to swallow solids or liquids. She works from a home office, has not had any recent sick contacts, and is currently not sexually active. Her medical history includes AIDS. Her current medications include emtricitabine, rilpivirine, and tenofovir. Her temperature is 38.1°C (100.6°F),  pulse is 72/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 136/84 mm Hg. A physical examination is notable for a dry mouth with red mucosa and no distinct plaques or patches, and a supple neck with no masses or cervical lymphadenopathy. An esophagogastroduodenoscopy shows small white patches within the esophageal lumen. A biopsy of one of the lesions is performed and the microscopic appearance of the finding is shown below. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old woman presents to the office complaining of a sore throat, difficulty swallowing, and difficulty opening her mouth for the past 5 days. She states that she had symptoms like this before and "was given some antibiotics that made her feel better". She is up to date on her immunizations. On examination, her temperature is 39.5°C (103.2°F) and she has bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy. An oropharyngeal exam is difficult, because the patient finds it painful to fully open her mouth. However, you are able to view an erythematous pharynx as well as a large, unilateral lesion superior to the left tonsil. A rapid antigen detection test is negative. Which of the following is a serious complication of the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old nursing home staff presents to the emergency room with complaints of palpitations and chest pain for the past 2 days. He was working at the nursing home for the last year but has been trying to get into modeling for the last 6 months and trying hard to lose weight. He is a non-smoker and occasionally drinks alcohol on weekends with friends. On examination, he appears well nourished and is in no distress. The blood pressure is 150/84 mm Hg and the pulse is 118/min. An ECG shows absent P waves. All other physical findings are normal. What is the probable diagnosis?

A 68-year-old woman from California presents for a routine checkup. She does not have any complaints. She says that she has tried to keep herself healthy and active by jogging and gardening since her retirement at age 50. She adds that she spends her mornings in the park and her afternoons in her garden. She has no significant medical history. The patient denies any smoking history and drinks alcohol occasionally. On physical examination, the following lesion is seen on her scalp (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old boy is brought by his parents to the office for bloody diarrhea and a seizure. The parents say he started having fever, abdominal pain, and diarrhea about 3 days ago, but the bloody diarrhea started 12 hours ago. The seizure was the last symptom to appear 3 hours ago, and it consisted of repetitive movement of arms and legs with loss of consciousness. His 4-year-old sister had a similar case with bloody diarrhea 2 weeks ago. His vital signs include: blood pressure is 130/85 mm Hg, his respiratory rate is 25/min, his heart rate is 120/min, and his temperature is 39.2°C (102.6°F). On physical examination, he looks pale and sleepy, the cardiopulmonary auscultation is normal, the abdomen is painful on palpation, and the skin assessment reveals the presence of disseminated pinpoint petechiae. The urinalysis show hematuria. The Coombs test is negative. The complete blood count results are as follows:
Hemoglobin 7 g/dL
Hematocrit 25 %
Leukocyte count 17,000/mm3
Neutrophils 70%
Bands 2%
Eosinophils 1%
Basophils 0%
Lymphocytes 22%
Monocytes 5%
Platelet count 7,000/mm3
His coagulation tests are as follows:
Partial thromboplastin time (activated) 30 seconds
Prothrombin time 12 seconds
Reticulocyte count 1 %
Thrombin time < 2 seconds deviation from control
What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old man presents with exertional dyspnea and fatigue for the past 3 months. His past medical history is significant for multiple episodes of mild diarrhea for many years, which was earlier diagnosed as irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). He denies any current significant gastrointestinal symptoms. The patient is afebrile and vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination reveals oral aphthous ulcers and mild conjunctival pallor. Abdominal examination is unremarkable. There is a rash present on the peripheral extremities bilaterally (see image). Laboratory findings are significant for evidence of microcytic hypochromic anemia. FOBT is negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

An 82-year-old man presents with 2 months of foul-smelling, greasy diarrhea. He says that he also has felt very tired recently and has had some associated bloating and flatus. He denies any recent abdominal pain, nausea, melena, hematochezia, or vomiting. He also denies any history of recent travel and states that his home has city water. Which of the following tests would be most appropriate to initially work up the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 35-year-old man with a history of Crohn disease presents for a follow-up appointment. He says that lately, he has started to notice difficulty walking. He says that some of his friends have joked that he appears to be walking as if he was drunk. Past medical history is significant for Crohn disease diagnosed 2 years ago, managed with natalizumab for the past year because his intestinal symptoms have become severe and unresponsive to other therapies. On physical examination, there is gait and limb ataxia present. Strength is 4/5 in the right upper limb. A T1/T2 MRI of the brain is ordered and is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 50-year-old woman is evaluated for a 2-year history of intermittent, nonproductive, chronic cough, as well as mild dyspnea with exertion. She has a 20-pack-year history of smoking and is a current smoker. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which she has controlled with diet and exercise. She also takes lisinopril. On physical examination, blood pressure is 125/76 mm Hg, pulse rate is 78/min, respiratory rate is 15/min, oxygen saturation is 98% (breathing room air), and her BMI is 25 kg/m2. There is no jugular venous distention. Heart sounds are normal, and there is no murmur. Auscultation of the lungs reveals faint, bilateral wheezing. No peripheral edema is noted. The remainder of the examination is normal. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis for this patient?

A 54-year-old man presents with increasing shortness of breath on exertion for the past few months. He also complains of associated fatigue and some balance issues. The patient denies swelling of his feet and difficulty breathing at night or while lying down. Physical examination is significant for conjunctival pallor. A peripheral blood smear reveals macrocytosis and hypersegmented granulocytes. Which of the following substances, if elevated in this patient’s blood, would support the diagnosis of vitamin B12 deficiency?

A 10-year-old boy with previously diagnosed sickle cell anemia presents to the emergency room with a low-grade fever, malaise, petechiae on his arms, and a rash on his face. He regularly takes hydroxyurea and receives blood transfusions to treat his condition. His blood tests show a hemoglobin of 4.0 g/dL, MCV of 87 fl, and 2% reticulocyte count. An attempted bone marrow biopsy was  a dry, empty tap. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 18-month-old girl presents to the clinic with her father for evaluation of a rash around the eyes and mouth. Her father states that the rash appeared 2 weeks ago and seems to be very itchy because the girl scratches her eyes often. The patient is up to date on all of her vaccinations and is meeting all developmental milestones. She has a history of asthma that was recently diagnosed. On examination, the patient is playful and alert. She has scaly, erythematous skin surrounding both eyes and her mouth. Bilateral pupils are equal and reactive to light and accommodation, and conjunctiva is clear, with no evidence of jaundice or exudates. The pharynx and oral mucosa are within normal limits, and no lesions are present. Expiratory wheezes can be heard in the lower lung fields bilaterally. What is this most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 25-year-old woman of Mediterranean descent makes an appointment with her physician because her skin and sclera have become yellow. She complains of fatigue and fever that started at the same time icterus appeared. On examination, she is tachycardic and tachypneic. The oxygen (O2) saturation is < 90%. She has increased unconjugated bilirubin, hemoglobinemia, and an increased number of reticulocytes in the peripheral blood. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 10-year-old girl is brought to a pediatric clinic by her parents with pain and weakness in the lower extremities for the past 3 weeks. The patient’s father says that she has been active until the weakness and pain started during her soccer practice sessions. She says she also experiences muscle cramps, especially at night. Her father adds that, recently, the patient constantly wakes up in the night to urinate and is noticeably thirsty most of the time. The patient denies any recent history of trauma to her legs. Her vaccinations are up to date and her family history is unremarkable. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination is unremarkable. Laboratory findings are shown below:
Laboratory test
Serum potassium 3.3 mEq/L
Serum magnesium  1.3 mEq/L
Serum chloride 101 mEq/L
pH 7.50
Pco2 38 mm Hg
HCO3- 20 mEq/L
Po2 88 mm Hg
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 35-year-old woman presents with a mass on the central part of her neck. She reports it has been growing steadily for the past 2 weeks, and she has also been experiencing fatigue and recurrent fevers. No significant past medical history. The patient denies any smoking history, or alcohol or recreational drug use. She denies any recent travel in the previous 6 months. On physical examination, there are multiple enlarged submandibular and cervical lymph nodes that are firm, mobile, and non-tender. A biopsy of one of the lymph nodes is performed and shows predominantly lymphocytes and histiocytes present in a pattern ‘resembling popcorn’. A flow cytometry analysis demonstrates cells that are CD19 and CD20 positive and CD15 and CD30 negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

An 11-year-old girl presents to the office with her mother for the evaluation of weight loss, rash, and several weeks of bloating and diarrhea. The mother states that the patient’s father had similar symptoms at her age. On physical examination, the patient is pale with dry mucous membranes. There is a vesicular rash on the bilateral lower extremities which she says is ‘very itchy’. Which of the following laboratory findings would confirm the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 50-year-old woman presents to the office with complaints of fever and chills for 4 weeks. She adds that she is fatigued all the time and has generalized weakness. She has drenching night sweats and has had 2 episodes of non-bilious vomiting over the past few days. She traveled to the Netherlands for 4 days a month ago. Her symptoms started a few days after she returned home. Laboratory testing revealed the following:
Hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL
Hematocrit 29%
Leukocyte count 2,950/mm3
Neutrophils  59%
Bands  3%
Eosinophils 1%
Basophils  0%
Lymphocytes 31%
Monocytes  4%
Platelet count  60,000/mm3
Unconjugated bilirubin 12 mg/dL
Alanine aminotransferase 200 IU/L
Aspartate aminotransferase 355 IU/L
The peripheral blood smear showed basophilic ring- and pear-shaped structures inside many red cells and extracellular basophilic rings on Wright-Giemsa staining. Further evaluation revealed parasitemia and a few schistocytes, poikilocytes, and merozoites in tetrad formation. The findings are most consistent with which diagnosis?

A 5-year-old boy presents for a routine checkup. The patient’s parents say he has been looking pale and tired lately. His family history is unremarkable. Upon physical examination, several bruises are seen, as well as petechial bleeding on his limbs. A complete blood count shows leukocytosis with severe anemia and thrombocytopenia. A peripheral blood smear shows 35% blasts. Ultrasonography of the abdomen shows hepatosplenomegaly and a chest radiograph reveals a mediastinal mass. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 46-year-old man presents with a 5-month history of worsening dry cough, occasional shortness of breath, and fatigue. He says he is now having trouble walking a full block. For the past week, he also has noticed bilateral swelling of the lower legs. He denies chest pain, fever, chills, syncope, or bloody sputum. Current vitals include: temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse 63/min, blood pressure 128/91 mm Hg and respiratory rate 15/min. On physical examination, there is elevated jugular venous pressure, decreased breath sounds bilaterally at the lung bases, and 1+ non-pitting edema bilaterally in the lower extremities. Crepitus is noted over both lung bases bilaterally. A loud 3/6 pansystolic murmur is heard at the apex radiating towards the axilla. S3 and S4 sounds are noted at the left sternal border and cardiac apex. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 4-month-old female infant is brought in because she rejects food and is losing weight. She had several upper respiratory tract infections during the last 2 months. Upon examination, hepatosplenomegaly is noted, as well as mild hypotonia. During the next few weeks, hepatosplenomegaly progresses, the girl fails to thrive, and she continues to reject food. She has a blood pressure of 100/70 mm Hg and heart rate of 84/min. Blood tests show pancytopenia and elevated levels of transaminases. Slit lamp examination shows bilateral cherry-red spots on the macula. Chest X-ray shows a reticulonodular pattern and calcified nodules. Biopsy of the liver shows foamy histiocytes. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old Hispanic woman presents to the office for a regular health checkup. She has been waiting for her hip replacement surgery for osteoarthritis, which she was diagnosed with for the past 5 years. She admits to having taken high doses of painkillers for hip pain management, but now they don’t provide any pain relief. Her vital signs include: blood pressure 110/70 mm Hg, pulse 78/min, temperature 36.7°C (98.1°F), and respiratory rate 10/min. On physical examination, there is a limited range of motion of her right hip.
The laboratory results are as follows:
Hemoglobin 12 g/dL
Red blood cell 5.1 million cells/µL
Hematocrit 45%
Total leukocyte count 6,500 cells/µL
Neutrophils 71%
Lymphocyte 14%
Monocytes 4%
Eosinophil 11%
Basophils 0%
Platelets 240,000 cells/µL
Urinalysis shows:
pH 6.2
Color light yellow
RBC 7–8/ HPF
WBC 10-12 /HPF
Protein 1+
Cast none
Glucose absent
Crystal none
Ketone absent
Nitrite negative
24-hr urine protein excretion 0.9 g
Urine for culture No growth noted after 48 hours of inoculation at 37.0°C (98.6°F)
What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 13-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department with respiratory distress, fever, and a productive cough. Past medical history is significant for a history of recurrent bronchopneumonia since the age of 5, managed conservatively with antibiotics and mucolytic therapy. The patient’s weight was normal at birth, but she suffered from a failure to thrive, although there was no neonatal history of chronic diarrhea or jaundice. Her current vitals are a respiratory rate of 26/min, a pulse of 96/min, a temperature of 38.8℃ (101.8°F), a blood pressure of 90/60 mm Hg, and oxygen saturation of 88% on room air. On physical examination, there is coarse crepitus bilaterally and both expiratory and inspiratory wheezing is present. The chest radiograph shows evidence of diffuse emphysema. A sweat chloride test and nitro tetrazolium test are both within normal limits. A complete blood count is significant for the following:
WBC 26300/mm3
Neutrophils 62%
Lymphocytes 36%
Eosinophils 2%
Total bilirubin 0.8 mg/dL
Direct bilirubin 0.2 mg/dL
SGOT 100 U/L
SGPT 120 U/L
ALP 200 U/L
Results of serum protein electrophoresis are shown in the figure. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 70-year-old Caucasian man presents with a 2-week history of blood-tinged sputum. His past medical history is significant for peptic ulcer disease for which he underwent triple-drug therapy. He is a lifetime non-smoker and worked as a teacher before retiring at the age of 60 years. A review of systems is significant for a weight loss of 6.8 kg (15 lb) over the last 5 months. His vitals include: blood pressure 135/85 mm Hg, temperature 37.7°C (99.9°F), pulse 95/min, and respiratory rate 18/min. Physical examination is unremarkable. A contrast CT scan of the chest shows an irregular mass in the peripheral region of the inferior lobe of the right lung. A CT-guided biopsy is performed and reveals malignant tissue architecture and gland formation with a significant amount of mucus. Which of the following is the most significant risk factor for this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 7-day-old newborn girl presents to the emergency department with a history of fever, irritability, and generalized erythema. During the first 2 days of clinical manifestations, the parents of the child tried to control the symptoms using acetaminophen; however, the newborn continued to be ill, and blisters were noticeable around the buttocks, hands, and feet. During the physical examination, the vital signs include body temperature 39.0°C (102.3°F), heart rate 130/min, and respiratory rate 45/min. Ears, nose, and oral mucosa preserved their integrity, while the skin presents with diffuse blanching erythema and flaccid blisters with a positive Nikolsky’s sign. What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 25-year-old construction worker presents to the office due to a yellowish discoloration of her skin and eyes for the past 2 weeks. She also complains of nausea and loss of appetite for the same duration. The past medical history is insignificant. She is a smoker, but recently has grown a distaste for smoking. The vital signs include: heart rate 83/min, respiratory rate 13/min, temperature 36.5°C (97.7°F), and blood pressure 111/74 mm Hg. On physical examination, there is mild hepatomegaly. The results of the hepatitis viral panel are as follows:
Anti-HAV IgM positive
HBsAg negative
IgM anti-HBc negative
Anti-HCV negative
HCV-RNA negative
Anti-HDV negative
Anti-HEV negative
What is the most common mode of transmission for this patient’s diagnosis?

A 26-year-old woman presents to the office complaining of persistent epigastric pain for the past 2 months. She states that her pain is worse a few hours after she eats. Her father had similar symptoms. Past medical history is insignificant. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. The vital signs include blood pressure 120/90 mm Hg, heart rate 83/min, and temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F). Physical examination is insignificant except for mild epigastric tenderness. A metabolic panel reveals the following:
Serum sodium 136 mEq/L
Serum potassium 4.2 mEq/L
Calcium 13.2 mg/dL
Bicarbonate 26 mEq/L
Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy reveals multiple duodenal ulcers. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 56-year-old woman presents to the emergency room with severe substernal chest pain associated with a 2-hour history of breathlessness and sweating. An electrocardiogram shows an ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. Cardiac enzyme levels confirm a diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction. The patient is rushed to the catheter lab for angioplasty with stenting. The patient complains of recurrent chest pain in the ICU 56 hours post-angioplasty. Which of the following enzymes facilitates the patient’s diagnosis based on her current symptoms?

A 4-month-old neonate boy is brought to the pediatrician because of feeding problems and recurrent infections. He has a blood pressure of 104/65 mm Hg and heart rate of 91/min. On physical examination, he has a cleft palate, malformed jaw, structural cardiac abnormalities, and diminished cell-mediated responses. Laboratory investigations reveal hypocalcemia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

On the 4th day of hospital admission due to pneumonia, a 69-year-old man develops non-bloody diarrhea and abdominal pain. He is currently treated with ceftriaxone. Despite the resolution of fever after the first 2 days of admission, his temperature is now 38.5°C (101.3°F). On physical examination, he has mild generalized abdominal tenderness without abdominal guarding or rebound tenderness. Laboratory studies show re-elevation of leukocyte counts. Ceftriaxone is discontinued. Given the most likely diagnosis in this patient, which of the following is the most sensitive test?

A 20-year-old woman comes to the clinic complaining of fever and a sore throat for 5 days. She receives oral penicillin from her primary doctor.
