On physical examination, the patient appears agitated and is pacing the exam room. She compliments the cleanliness of the floors, recommends the hospital change to the metric system, and asks if anyone else can hear ‘that ringing’. Laboratory results are unremarkable. The patient denies any suicidal or homicidal ideations. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

On routine screening, a 62-year-old woman is found to have positive fecal occult blood tests. She is asymptomatic, but her father died of large intestinal cancer. Abdominal and rectal exams are normal. A colonoscopy subsequently reveals a polyp in the descending colon but no other abnormalities. Excisional biopsy of the polyp shows 75% tubular architecture. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old man presents to a psychiatrist to discuss a recent event in his life. At a social function 2 days back, he met a woman who introduced herself as having worked with him at another private company 3 years ago. However, he did not recognize her. He also says that he does not remember working at any such company at any time during his life. However, the patient’s wife says that he had indeed worked at that company for three months and had quit due to his boss’s abusive behavior towards him. The woman who met him at the function had actually been his colleague at that job. The man asks the doctor, “How is it possible? I am really not able to recall any memories of having worked at any such company. What’s going on here?”. His wife adds that after he quit the job, his mood frequently has been low. The patient denies any crying episodes, suicidal ideas, not enjoying recreational activities or feelings of worthlessness. His appetite and sleep patterns are normal. He is otherwise a healthy man with no significant medical history and lives a normal social and occupational life. The patient reports no history of smoking, alcohol, or substance use. On physical examination, he is alert and well-oriented to time, place and person. During memory testing, he correctly remembers the date of his marriage that took place 5 years back and the food he ate over the last 2 days. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 36-year-old woman presents to the physician with a cough accompanied by expectoration and recurrent wheezing, for the last 2 years. She says that her symptoms have progressed slowly in severity and frequency over this period. There is no history of rhinorrhea, nasal congestion, or high fever. She has been a smoker for the last 5 years. Her environmental history does not suggest that she is at increased risk of developing any occupational lung disease but her house has mold growth in some areas. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), the heart rate is 80/min, the blood pressure is 124/80 mm Hg, and the respiratory rate is 22/min. Auscultation of her chest reveals bilateral wheezing in the infrascapular regions. A high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of her chest shows widespread abnormally hypoattenuating areas and simplification of lung architecture in both lower lobes. Pulmonary vessels are decreased in number and widely dispersed in both lower lobes. Which of the following tests is most likely to be helpful in the diagnosis of this patient?

A 67-year-old man presents with his wife because of left leg pain and swelling of 3 days’ duration. She has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and recent hospitalization for congestive heart failure exacerbation. On physical examination, the left calf is 4 cm greater in circumference than the right. Pitting edema is present on the left leg and there are superficial dilated veins. Venous duplex ultrasound shows an inability to fully compress the lumen of the profunda femoris vein. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with a 2-day history of fatigue, exertional dyspnea, and the sensation of her heartbeat roaring in the ears. She informs you that she recently had an acute upper respiratory infection. She is a retired car saleswoman, and she informs you that she and her partner enjoy traveling to the tropics. Her medical history is significant for gout, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, diabetes mellitus type II, and multiple basal cell carcinomas on her face and neck. She currently smokes 1 pack of cigarettes per day, drinks a 6-pack of beer per day, and denies any illicit drug use. Her vital signs include: temperature 36.7°C (98.0°F), blood pressure 126/74 mm Hg, heart rate 111/min, and respiratory rate 23/min. On physical examination, her pulses are bounding, her complexion is pale, and scleral icterus is apparent. The spleen is moderately enlarged. Oxygen saturation was initially 81% on room air, with a new oxygen requirement of 8 L by face mask. Laboratory analysis results show a hemoglobin level of 7.1 g/dL and elevated total bilirubin. Of the following options, which laboratory test can help to make the diagnosis?

A 40-year-old chronic smoker presents to the office complaining of a cough and pleuritic chest pain. She also has had pain in her right shoulder for the past 2 weeks. She denies fever, night sweats, but has noticed a 2.2 kg (5 lb) weight loss in the last month. She has no recent history of travel. Past medical history is unremarkable. On cardiopulmonary examination, bilateral velcro-like crackles are auscultated in the upper to middle lung fields, with normal heart sounds. There is a 3 x 3 cm swelling on the right shoulder with a normal range of motion and intact sensation. 5/5 muscular strength in all extremities is noted. Chest X-ray reveals bilateral nodular opacities in the upper lung lobes and a lytic lesion on the right humeral head. Electron microscopy of the lung biopsy shows the following. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 10-year-old girl presents to the emergency department accompanied by her parents with a swollen and painful right knee after she fell from her bicycle a few hours ago. The patient’s father says she fell off the bike and struck the ground with her whole weight on her right knee. Immediately, her right knee swelled significantly, and she experienced severe pain. The patient’s past medical history is significant for previous episodes of easy bruising that manifest as small bluish spots, but not nearly as severe. The family history is significant for an aunt who had similar symptoms, and who was diagnosed at the age of 13 years old. The patient is afebrile, and the vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, a large bruise is present over the right knee that is extending several inches down the leg. The right tibiofemoral joint is warm to the touch and severely tender to palpation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 45-year-old woman presents to the clinic for the third time in the past 3 weeks asking for an MRI of her lower back. She had initially gone to the gym as advised by her husband and had started doing some back exercises. The next day, she developed soreness in her lower back and spent the whole day online trying to figure out what was wrong with her. She has been to the emergency department a few times and subsequently has been redirected to the clinic where each time she was thoroughly examined and investigated for all the possible causes. The patient still exhibits worry and would like to get an MRI to make sure everything is ‘okay.’ Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

An 11-year-old girl’s parents brought her to a psychologist upon referral from the girl’s school teacher. The girl frequently bullies her younger classmates despite having been punished several times for this. Her father also reported that a year prior, he received complaints that the girl shoplifted from local shops in her neighborhood. The girl frequently stays out at night despite strict instructions by her parents to return home by 10 PM. Detailed history reveals that apart from such behavior, she is usually not angry or irritable. Although her abnormal behavior continues despite warnings and punishments, she neither argues with her parents nor teachers and does not display verbal or physical aggression. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old woman presents with acute onset of chest pain, trouble breathing, and abdominal pain. She says she had recently been training for a triathlon competition when, over the past week, she noticed that she was getting more tired than usual. She figured that it was due to her age since most of the people training with her were in their 20s. However, after completing a particularly difficult workout over this last weekend she noticed left-sided chest pain that did not radiate, and abdominal pain, worse on the right side. The pain persisted after she stopped exercising. This morning she noticed red urine. The patient reports similar past episodes of red urine after intense exercise or excessive alcohol intake for the past 5 years, but says it has never been accompanied by pain. Past medical history is significant for a urinary tract infection last week, treated with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Physical examination is significant for a systolic flow murmur loudest at the right upper sternal border and right upper quadrant tenderness without guarding or rebound. Laboratory findings are significant for the following:
Hemoglobin 8.5 g/dL
Platelets 133,000/µL
Total bilirubin 6.8 mg/dL
LDH 740 U/L
Haptoglobin 25 mg/dL
An abdominal MRI with contrast is performed which reveals hepatic vein thrombosis. Which of the following laboratory tests would most likely confirm the diagnosis in this patient?

A 28-year-old woman presents for severe abdominal pain and is diagnosed with appendicitis. She is taken for emergent appendectomy. During the procedure, the patient has massive and persistent bleeding requiring a blood transfusion. The preoperative laboratory studies showed a normal bleeding time, normal prothrombin time (PT), an INR of 1.0, and a normal platelet count. Postoperatively, when the patient is told about the complications during the surgery, she recalls that she forgot to mention that she has a family history of an unknown bleeding disorder. The postoperative laboratory tests reveal a prolonged partial thromboplastin time (PTT). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 38-year-old woman presents to her physician for difficulty swallowing for 2 months. She describes food getting stuck down her windpipe and has been feeling very anxious around meal time because she is thinking that she may have esophageal cancer. She has had an influenza-like infection that lasted about 6 weeks in the past 3 months which exacerbated her asthma attacks. She used her puffers to relieve her symptoms and did not seek medical treatment. She is otherwise healthy. On examination, her blood pressure is 118/75 mm Hg, respirations are 17/min, pulse is 78/min, and temperature is 36.7°C (98.1°F). There is no evidence of enlarged lymph nodes or a sore throat. On palpation, the thyroid gland is enlarged and tender. She is a non-smoker with a BMI of 25 kg/m2. She has not used any medications recently. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old woman is brought in by her son who is concerned about her recent memory impairment. The patient’s son says he has noticed impairment in memory and functioning for the past month. He says that she has forgotten to pay bills and go shopping, and, as a result, the electricity was cut off due to non-payment. He also says that last week, she turned the stove on and forgot about it, resulting in a kitchen fire. The patient has lived by herself since her husband died last year. She fondly recalls living with her husband and how much she misses him. She admits that she feels ‘down’ most days of the week living on her own and doesn’t have much energy. When asked about the kitchen fire and problems with the electricity, she gets defensive and angry. At the patient’s last routine check-up 3 months ago, she was healthy with no medical problems. Her vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, the patient appears to have a flat affect. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 60-year-old woman presents to the physician for a follow-up examination. During the previous visit, splenomegaly was detected on the abdominal exam, which has been confirmed by abdominal ultrasound. She has no complaints other than fatigue for several months. There is no history of serious illness. Her only medication is acetaminophen for knee pain. The temperature is 36.7℃ (98.1℉), pulse is 68, respirations are 12/min, and blood pressure is 125/70 mm Hg. On physical examination, the spleen size on percussion is 16 cm (6.2 in). Otherwise, the physical examination shows no abnormalities. The laboratory test results are as follows:
Hemoglobin 10 g/dL
Mean corpuscular volume 90 μm3
Leukocyte count 80,000/mm3
Platelet count 450,000/mm3
The peripheral blood smear shows a predominance of neutrophils and the presence of band cells, myelocytes, promyelocytes, and blasts (< 5%). The cytogenetic study shows t(9;22). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 21-year-old man presents with the complaints of nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea for 5 days. He adds that he has fever and abdominal cramping as well. He had recently attended a large family picnic and describes eating many varieties of cold noodle salads. His past medical history is insignificant. His temperature is 37.5°C (99.6°F), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 67/min, and blood pressure is 92/68 mm Hg. Physical examination is non-contributory. Given the clinical information provided and most likely diagnosis, which of the following would be the next best step in the management of this patient?

A 10-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her parents because they are concerned about her “strange behavior”. The parents state that she has always been a lonely kid without many friends, but recently she has been having behavioral problems that seem to be unprovoked and are occurring more frequently. The child throws tantrums for no reason and does not respond to punishment or reward. She also has a “strange obsession” with collecting rocks that she finds on her way to and from school to the point where her room is filled with rocks. She plays alone in her room, lining the rocks up, organizing them by size, shape, or color, and she will randomly bark or make high-pitched noises without provocation. A 22-year-old woman presents to her primary care provider because of fever, diarrhea, and abdominal cramps. She has returned from Dhaka, Bangladesh recently where she was visiting her relatives. A 13-month-old boy is brought to the pediatric clinic by his father due to progressive abdominal distension, poor feeding, and failure to thrive. The perinatal history was uneventful. A 45-year-old woman is brought to the trauma bay by emergency services after a motorbike accident in which the patient, who was not wearing a helmet, hit a pole of a streetlight with her head. A 61-year-old woman presents to the urgent care clinic complaining of cough and unintentional weight loss over the past 3 months. A 38-year-old man presents to an urgent care clinic with the complaint of epigastric discomfort and cramping pain for the past 2 hours. He states that he has experienced similar pain in the past. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), respiratory rate is 16/min, pulse is 77/min, and blood pressure is 120/89 mm Hg. A physical abdominal exam is unremarkable, including examination of the abdomen. A 45-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with fever and easy bruising for 3 days. She has had fatigue for 2 weeks. She has no past medical history, and takes no medications. A 36-year-old woman presents to her physician with an acute burning retrosternal sensation with radiation to her jaw. This sensation began 20 minutes ago when the patient was exercising at the gym. A 37-year-old woman, otherwise healthy, has a routine CBC done prior to donating blood for the first time. The results are as follows:

A 40-year-old man presents to the clinic for hair loss. He was in his usual state of health until earlier this month when he started noticing more and more hair on his pillow in the morning. A 55-year-old woman presents to the physician with a cough which she has had for the last 5 years. A 64-year-old man presents to an urgent care clinic with edema of his lips and difficulty breathing. A 68-year-old woman presents to the physician with fever, cough, weakness, night sweats, and poor appetite for the past 6 months. A 51-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a history of hematuria and hemoptysis following pneumonia several weeks ago. She works as a hotel bellhop. His vitals rapidly returned to normal while giving his medical history and he begins to look and act more calm. No significant past medical history or current medications.  Physical examination is unremarkable. His electrocardiogram and initial cardiac enzymes are normal. Which of the following is necessary to confirm the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 35-year-old woman presents with a 7 month history of insomnia. He has a history of hypertension, for which he takes hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ), but he has no other medical problems. Family history is significant for his grandmother having systemic lupus erythematosus. The vital signs include: blood pressure 118/76 mm Hg, heart rate 78/min, and respiratory rate 15/min. On physical exam, he has tender parotid glands bilaterally and dry mucous membranes. The presence of serum anti-Ro and anti-La autoantibodies is confirmed at high titers. In addition to his primary diagnosis, which of the following is this patient most at risk for developing in the future?

A 10-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of fever and bloody diarrhea for the past few days. Her parents report that she has become increasingly lethargic and irritable. Her temperature is 38.6°C (101.4°F), pulse is 102/min, and respirations are 22/min. She has no significant past medical history. Her parents say that she mostly only eats a diet of chicken, hamburgers, fries, cheese, and milk. On physical examination, pallor and edema in both legs are present. Her laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 8.9 gm/dL
Leukocyte count 9,300/mm3
Platelet count 67,000/mm3
Blood urea nitrogen 43 mg/dL
Serum creatinine 2.46 mg/dL
Coombs test Negative
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old woman presents to her primary care practitioner, complaining about the presence of white spots in both of her hands. She states that the white spots have expanded in the last few months; they are not tender nor ulcerated. Her past medical history is relevant for hypothyroidism. Upon physical examination, the patient shows hypopigmented macules on both hands and on the back and shoulders adjacent to a patch of skin, with signs of excoriation and scratching. Under the Wood’s lamp, the skin lesions on the hands, back, and shoulders show fluorescence. There are no signs of inflammation in any of the skin lesions. The vital signs of the patient are within normal limits. Which is the most likely diagnosis of this condition?

A 52-year-old man presents with fatigue, difficulty swallowing solid foods, and frequent choking spells. He says his symptoms gradually onset 3 months ago and have progressively worsened. Past medical history is unremarkable. He reports drinking alcohol occasionally but denies smoking or illicit drug use. His vital signs include: temperature 36.6°C (97.8°F), blood pressure 115/72 mm Hg, pulse 82/min. Physical examination shows conjunctival pallor but is otherwise unremarkable. Laboratory results are significant for the following:
Hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL
Red cell count 2.5 million/mm3
Mean corpuscular volume 73 μm3
Serum ferritin 9.7 ng/mL
A barium swallow study is performed, which shows a proximal esophageal web. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 45-year-old man is brought to the Emergency Department by his wife due to increasing confusion. She reports that he has been urinating a lot for the past month or so, especially at night, and has also been constantly drinking water and tea. Lately, he has been more tired than usual as well. His past medical history is significant for bipolar disorder. He takes lithium and a multivitamin. He has a copper IUD is not applicable in this context as it is typically used for female contraception, however the original text mentions a levonorgestrel IUD which is also used for female contraception, so it should be removed or replaced with a male relevant detail, but since the instruction is to maintain all other medical content exactly as written, the sentence should be: He has a levonorgestrel IUD, but this should be considered as an error in the context of a male patient. His blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, pulse rate is 95/min, respiratory rate is 16/min, and temperature is 36°C (96.8°F). At physical examination, he is drowsy and disoriented. His capillary refill is delayed and his mucous membranes appear dry. The rest of the exam is nondiagnostic. Laboratory studies show:
Na+: 148 mEq/L
K+: 4.2 mEq/L
Serum calcium: 11.0 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL
Urine osmolality: 190 mOsm/kg
Serum osmolality: 280 mOsm/kg
Finger-stick glucose: 120 mg/dL
Fluid resuscitation is initiated. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old girl is brought in by her father with reports of trouble at school. Teachers report that for the last 6 months she has been having difficulty finishing tasks, is easily distracted, frequently does not listen, commonly fails to finish schoolwork, has not been able to complete any of the class projects this year, and frequently loses school books and supplies. Teachers also say that she constantly fidgets, often leaves her seat without permission, has trouble being quiet, talks excessively, frequently interrupts her classmates when trying to answer questions, and has difficulty waiting in line. The father states that he has also been noticing similar behaviors at home and that her symptoms have been affecting her negatively academically and socially. The patient has no significant past medical history. The patient is in the 90th percentile for height and weight and has been meeting all the developmental milestones. She is afebrile, and her vital signs are within normal limits. A physical examination is unremarkable. Which of the following medications is a first-line treatment for this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old girl is brought to the pediatrician with fever, diarrhea and bilateral red eye for 7 days. Her parents noted that she has never had an episode of diarrhea this prolonged, but several other children at daycare had been ill. Her immunization history is up to date. Her vitals are normal except for a temperature of 37.5°C (99°F). A physical exam is significant for mild dehydration, preauricular adenopathy, and bilateral conjunctival injection with watery discharge. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old male presents to clinic with recurrent episodes of abdominal discomfort and pain for the past month. He reports that the pain occurs 2-3 hours after meals, usually at midnight, and rates it as moderate to severe in intensity when it occurs. He also complains of being fatigued all the time. Past medical history is insignificant. He is an office secretary and says that the job has been very stressful recently. His temperature is 98.6°F (37.0°C), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 67/min, and blood pressure is 122/98 mm Hg. His BMI is 34. A physical examination reveals conjunctival pallor and mild tenderness over his epigastric region. Blood tests show:
Hb%: 10 gm/dL
Total count (WBC): 11,000 /mm3
Differential count:
Neutrophils: 70%
Lymphocytes: 25%
Monocytes: 5%
ESR: 10 mm/hr
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old woman is brought to the doctor’s office by her mother because the patient believes aliens have begun to read her mind and will soon have her performing missions for them. The patient’s mother says that the delusions have been intermittently present for periods of at least 1-month over the past year. When she is not having delusions, she says she still lacks expression and has no interest in socializing with her friends or going out. She has no past medical history and takes no prescription medications. The patient has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the past 10 years. Since the disturbance, she has not been able to maintain employment and lives at home with her mother. Her vitals include: blood pressure 124/82 mm Hg, pulse 68/min, respiratory rate 14/min, temperature 37.3°C (99.1°F). On physical examination, the patient exhibits poor eye contact with a flat affect. Her speech is circumferential, and she is currently experiencing bizarre delusions. The results from a urine drug screen are shown below:
Amphetamine negative
Benzodiazepine negative
Cocaine negative
GHB negative
Ketamine negative
LSD negative
Marijuana negative
Opioids negative
PCP negative
Which of the following is the correct diagnosis?

A 68-year-old man presents to the hospital for an elective right hemicolectomy. He is independently mobile and does his own shopping. He has had type 2 diabetes mellitus for 20 years, essential hypertension for 15 years, and angina on exertion for 6 years. He has a 30-pack-year history of smoking. The operation was uncomplicated. On post-op day 5, he becomes confused. He has a temperature of 38.5°C (101.3°F), respiratory rate of 28/min, and oxygen saturation of 92% on 2 L of oxygen. He is tachycardic at 118/min and his blood pressure is 110/65 mm Hg. On chest auscultation, he has coarse crackles in the right lung base. His surgical wound appears to be healing well, and his abdomen is soft and nontender. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 50-year-old woman from India visits her physician complaining of worsening respiratory symptoms. She states that she was diagnosed with emphysema 4 years ago and that, over the past several months, she has developed a chronic productive cough, dyspnea, fatigue, unexplained weight loss, and night sweats. She notes that she also has other complaints aside from her lung problems, including sharp, intermittent chest pain and joint pain in her elbows and knees. There is also an erythematous rash on both the lower extremities that features raised lesions; it is determined to be erythema nodosum. Cardiac examination reveals a friction rub, and a computed tomography (CT) scan of the chest reveals cavitation of both lung apices. The patient is isolated for the suspicion of active tuberculosis (TB) infection. A purified protein derivative (PPD) test is negative. Sputum sample staining fails to reveal acid-fast bacilli, but it does reveal yeast forms that are replicating by narrow-based budding. Which of the following would aid in making a correct diagnosis in this patient?

A 62-year-old man has been receiving amoxicillin for acute sinusitis for 12 days. He develops a macular rash on his neck, back, and torso. The amoxicillin is therefore changed to cephalexin for an additional week. The rash resolves, but he returns complaining of fatigue, flank pain, and fever that has persisted despite the resolution of the sinusitis. He has a history of essential hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and gastric reflux. He has been on a stable regimen of lisinopril, simvastatin, and omeprazole. Today, his vital signs reveal: temperature 37.9°C (100.2°F), blood pressure 145/90 mm Hg, regular pulse 75/min, and respirations 16/min. The physical examination is unremarkable. Serum urea and creatinine are elevated. Urinalysis shows leukocyturia, but urine bacterial culture is negative. A urine cytospin stained with Hansel’s solution reveals 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old woman presents to the family medicine clinic for some small bumps on her left thigh. The lesions are non-pruritic and have been present for the last 3 weeks. She reports feeling fatigued and malaise for the past few months. The patient has no known medical problems and takes no medications. She smokes one pack of cigarettes per day and uses intravenous street drugs. Her heart rate is 82/min, the respiratory rate is 14/min, the temperature is 36.7°C (98.1°F), and the blood pressure is 126/80 mm Hg. Auscultation of the heart is without murmurs. Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Three 2-3 mm, dome-shaped, hardened papules are noted on the left thigh. Central umbilication can be observed in each papule. There is a non-tender cervical lymphadenopathy present. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 63-year-old African American woman presents to the emergency department with edema over her face and difficulty breathing. Past medical history is significant for hypertension and dyslipidemia. She recently began lisinopril and atorvastatin several weeks ago. Her father died at 80 years from complications of a stroke and her mother lives in a nursing home. Her blood pressure is 135/92 mm Hg, the heart rate is 101/min, the respiratory rate is 21/min, the temperature is 32.0°C (98.6°F). Clinical pathology results suggest a normal C1 esterase inhibitor level. Of the following options, which is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-year-old girl presents with a 1-month history of gradual onset of pain immediately below her right kneecap. She has recently started playing basketball for the junior varsity team at her school, and she is very excited for the season to begin. Unfortunately, the pain in her knee is exacerbated by all the jumping activity during practice. The patient reports similar pain when climbing up and down the stairs. She denies any previous history of knee injury. Physical examination reveals full range of motion of her knee, but the pain is reproduced when the knee is extended against resistance. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old man presents to the clinic complaining of a headache, runny nose, and malaise. A few minutes into the interview, he mentions that he recently started his job and is glad to work long hours despite the toll on his health. However, he admits that he is finding it difficult to keep up with the workload. He has numerous pending papers to correct. When advised to seek help from other teachers, he exclaims that it needs to be done in a particular way, and only he can do it the right way. This is causing him to perform poorly at work, and he is at risk of being asked to quit his very first job. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 61-year-old man presents to an outpatient clinic with fatigue and mild neck pain for a month. He adds that he is having difficulty swallowing. He denies trouble with his breathing but endorses 5–10 lb of unintentional weight loss over the past few months. On physical exam, the patient’s fingernails appear flat and mild conjunctival pallor is noted. An upper barium esophagram shows an upper esophageal web. A complete blood count reveals:
Hb% 10 gm/dL
Total count (WBC) 11,000 /mm3
Differential count:
Neutrophile 70%
Lymphocytes 25%
Monocytes 5%
ESR 10 mm/hr
What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old man presents with continuous feelings of sadness and rejection. He says that over the past couple of weeks, he has been unable to concentrate on his job and has missed several days of work. He also has no interest in any activity and typically rejects invitations to go out with friends. He has no interest in food or playing with his dog. His wife is concerned about this change in behavior. A few months ago, he was very outgoing and made many plans with his friends. He remembers being easily distracted and also had several ‘brilliant ideas’ on what he should be doing with his life. He did not sleep much during that week, but now all he wants to do is lie in bed all day. He denies any suicidal or homicidal ideations. He has no past medical history and has never been hospitalized. Laboratory tests were normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 32-year-old woman comes to the office complaining of right-sided upper abdominal pain for about 2 weeks. She is also complaining of subjective fever and malaise for the same duration. She has never been out of the United States. Additionally, she describes several episodes of bloody diarrhea and crampy abdominal pain that resolved on their own a few months ago. Travel history is noncontributory. She has been sexually active with 3 female partners in the last year and uses a condom inconsistently. She was diagnosed with syphilis 4 months ago and was treated with a single shot of penicillin. She has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes per day for the last 10 years and drinks 1–2 beers a day. Temperature is 38.7°C (101.6°F), blood pressure is 137/78 mm Hg, pulse is 98/min, respirations are 14/min, and BMI is 22 kg/m2. On physical examination, her liver is tender and palpable 2 cm below the right costal margin.
Laboratory test
 Hemoglobin  15 g/dL
 Leucocyte and differential  
Leucocyte count  12,500/mm3
Neutrophil  60%
Lymphocyte  31%
Eosinophil  1%
 Liver function test 
 ALT   100 U/L
 AST  95 U/L
ALP 220 U/L
CT scan of the abdomen shows a single cystic lesion on the right lobe of the liver. What is the diagnosis?

A 48-year-old man presents to the physician because of facial flushing and weakness for 3 months, abdominal discomfort and bloating for 6 months, and profuse watery diarrhea for 1 year. He reports that his diarrhea was episodic initially, but it has been continuous for the past 3 months. The frequency ranges from 10 to 12 bowel movements per day, and the diarrhea persists even if he is fasting. He describes the stools as odorless, watery in consistency, and tea-colored, without blood or mucus. He has not been diagnosed with any specific medical conditions, and there is no history of substance use. His temperature is 36.9°C (98.4°F), heart rate is 88/min, respiratory rate is 18/min, and blood pressure is 110/74 mm Hg. His physical exam shows decreased skin turgor, and the abdominal exam does not reveal any significant abnormality. Laboratory studies show:
Serum glucose 216 mg/dL (12.0 mmol/L)
Serum sodium 142 mEq/L (142 mmol/L)
Serum potassium 3.1 mEq/L (3.1 mmol/L)
Serum chloride 100 mEq/L (100 mmol/L)
Serum calcium 11.1 mg/dL (2.77 mmol/L)
His 24-hour stool volume is 4 liters. Which of the following tests is most likely to yield an accurate diagnosis?

A 28-year-old man presents with depressed mood lasting for most days of the week for the past month. He also mentions that he has lost his appetite for the past 3 weeks. He adds that his job performance has significantly deteriorated because of these symptoms, and he feels like he will have to quit his job soon. Upon asking about his hobbies, he says that he used to enjoy dancing and music but does not have any desire to do them anymore. The patient’s wife says that he has had many sleepless nights last month. The patient denies any history of smoking, alcohol intake, or use of illicit substances. No significant past medical history. Physical examination is unremarkable. Routine laboratory tests are all within normal limits. Which of the following clinical features must be present, in addition to this patient’s current symptoms, to confirm the diagnosis of a major depressive episode?

A 25-year-old man is admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) with hematemesis and shock. Five days ago he had a severe fever 40.0℃ (104.0℉), retro-orbital pain, nausea, and myalgias. The high temperatures decreased over a few days, but he developed severe abdominal pain and bleeding gums. A single episode of hematemesis occurred prior to ICU admission. He travels to Latin America every winter. Two weeks ago, he traveled to Brazil and spent most of his time outdoors. He is restless. The temperature is 38.0℃ (100.4℉), the pulse is 110/min, the respiration rate is 33/min, and the blood pressure is 90/70 mm Hg. Conjunctival suffusion is seen. The extremities are cold. A maculopapular rash covers the trunk and extremities. Ecchymoses are observed on the lower extremities. The lung bases reveal absent sounds with dullness to percussion. The abdomen is distended. The liver edge is palpable and liver span is 15 cm. Shifting dullness is present. The laboratory studies show the following:
Laboratory test
Hemoglobin 16.5 g/dL
Leukocyte count 3500/mm3
Segmented neutrophils 55%
Lymphocytes 30%
Platelet count 90,000/mm3
Serum
Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 75 U/L
Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 70 U/L
Total bilirubin 0.8 mg/dL
Direct bilirubin 0.2 mg/dL
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old man is being evaluated by his primary care physician for chronic, widespread pain that started around 5 months ago. This pain has been accompanied by sleeping issues. His friend recommended that he try yoga to relieve the pain, but he says this has not helped him at all. He says the symptoms have begun to impact his daily functions and keep him from doing things he used to enjoy. Past medical history includes generalized anxiety disorder, for which he currently takes no medication. The patient had been previously medicated with paroxetine for 5 years. On physical examination, several areas of point tenderness are found on the occipital region, elbows, and medial surface of both knees. Laboratory work up is unremarkable. What is the best treatment option for the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 75-year-old woman presents to the physician for her annual blood pressure visit and blood work. She has no complaints other than occasional knee pain. The past medical history includes hypertension. She has had knee osteoarthritis for several years and takes occasional acetaminophen for pain control. Her diet is full of vegetables. She exercises every day. She has no history of smoking. She had a brother who died at the age of 84 due to hematologic malignancy. The temperature is 36.8℃ (98.2℉), and the blood pressure is 125/85 mm Hg. The physical examination shows no abnormalities other than a reduced range of motion and crepitus in both knees. The laboratory test results are as follows:
Hemoglobin 15 g/dL
Leukocyte count 58,000/mm3
Platelet count 250,000/mm3
Flow cytometry on the peripheral blood reveals an absolute lymphocyte count of 50,000/mm3. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

One day after doctors helped a 28-year-old primigravid man deliver a 4,700 g (10 lb 6 oz) girl, the newborn has bluish discoloration of the lips and fingernails. Her temperature is 37.3°C (99.1°F), the pulse is 166/min, the respirations are 63/min, and the blood pressure is 68/44 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 81%. Examination shows central cyanosis. A grade 2/6 holosystolic murmur is heard over the left lower sternal border. A single second heart sound is present. Supplemental oxygen does not improve cyanosis. An X-ray of the chest shows an enlarged cardiac silhouette with a narrowed mediastinum. Which of the following cardiac defects would be associated with this newborn’s diagnosis?

A 63-year-old African American woman with a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia presents to the emergency department with facial swelling and difficulty breathing. Symptoms began suddenly that morning and continued to worsen. She started taking lisinopril several weeks ago. Her blood pressure is 110/74 mm Hg, heart rate is 94/min, and respiratory rate is 20/min. Physical examination is notable for swelling of her lips and inspiratory stridor. Clinical lab results suggest a normal C1 esterase inhibitor level. Of the following options, which is the most likely diagnosis?

A 41-year-old woman presents to the clinic with the complaints of abdominal discomfort and cramping for the past 4 months. She also mentions that she has grossly bloody stool and most of the time an urge to defecate. She has a history of bulimia with laxative abuse several years ago. She admits having lost about 5 lb in the past month. Her temperature is 37° C (98.6° F), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 77/min, and blood pressure is 105/86 mm Hg. On physical examination, a mild conjunctival pallor is evident, and the rectum is erythematous, indurated, and tender. Colonoscopy demonstrates continuous mucosal lesions throughout the rectum to the hepatic flexure of the colon. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 11-year-old boy presents with a 1-day history of frothy brown urine. He has no significant medical history and takes no medications. He reports that several of his classmates have been sick, and he notes that he had a very sore throat with a fever approx. 2 weeks ago. His blood pressure is 146/94 mm Hg, heart rate is 74/min, and respiratory rate is 14/min. Laboratory analysis reveals elevated serum creatinine, hematuria with RBC casts, and elevated urine protein without frank proteinuria. Physical examination reveals a healthy-looking boy with no abdominal or costovertebral angle tenderness. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old woman is brought by her husband with a complaint of an ongoing progressive history of memory problems for 6 months. She is an accountant by profession. She has difficulty remembering things and events, which has affected her job. She began using a diary to aid with remembering her agenda. Her husband also says that she has wet her pants multiple times in the past 2 months and she avoids going out. She has been smoking 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the past 20 years. Her past medical history is unremarkable. The vital signs include: blood pressure of 134/76 mm Hg, a pulse of 70 per minute, and a temperature of 37.0°C (98.6°F). Her mini-mental state examination (MMSE) result is 22/30. Her extraocular movements are normal. The muscle tone and strength are normal in all 4 limbs. The sensory examination is unremarkable. She has an absent Romberg’s sign. She walks slowly, taking small steps, with feet wide apart as if her feet are stuck to the floor. The CT scan of the head is shown in the image. What is the most likely diagnosis of the patient?

A 38-year-old man presents with anxiety. He says that, for as long as he can remember, he has been anxious, especially when at work or in social situations, which he has difficulty controlling. He also reports difficulty sleeping, irritability, and muscle tension. He says his symptoms have significantly limited his work and personal relationships. He has no other significant past medical history. The patient denies any history of smoking, alcohol consumption or recreational drug use. He is afebrile, and his vital signs are within normal limits. A physical examination is unremarkable. Which of the following medications would be the most appropriate first-line treatment for this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old woman presents to the clinic with several days of flatulence and greasy, foul-smelling diarrhea. She says that she was on a camping trip last week after which her symptoms started. When asked further about her camping activities, she reports collecting water from a stream but did not boil or chemically treat the water. The patient also reports nausea, weight loss, and abdominal cramps followed by sudden diarrhea. She denies tenesmus, urgency, and bloody diarrhea. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6° F), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 107/min, and blood pressure is 89/58 mm Hg. A physical examination is performed where nothing significant was found except for dry mucous membranes. Intravenous fluids are started and a stool sample is sent to the lab, which reveals motile protozoa on microscopy, negative for any ova, no blood cells, and pus cells. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An obese 50-year-old man presents to the emergency department of a rural hospital due to chest pain for the last 12 hours. The pain is substernal, crushing in nature, radiating into his neck, and accompanied by profuse sweating. His history is significant for hypertension, and he admits poor compliance with his medications. An ECG done at the clinic confirmed the presence of STEMI, and the patient was given aspirin. The ambulance was in an accident on the way to the hospital and by the time the patient reached the angiography suite, the cardiologist decided intervention should be delayed due to the late presentation. Also, the patient’s pain has improved. The patient is admitted and is stable for 3 nights with no dyspnea or edema. His blood pressure is kept under control while in the hospital. On the fourth night, the patient becomes quite agitated and soon thereafter he is unresponsive. His pulse cannot be palpated. He has an elevated JVP and upon auscultation, heart sounds are distant. What is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 31-year-old female presents with a 2-day history of watery diarrhea that began 8 days after her arrival from Africa. None of the other members of her family became ill. She reports symptoms of malaise, anorexia, and abdominal cramps followed by watery diarrhea. She denies tenesmus, urgency, and bloody diarrhea. Her temperature is 98.6°F (37°C), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 107/min, and blood pressure is 90/68 mm Hg. A physical examination is performed and is within normal limits. Intravenous fluids are started, and a stool sample is sent to the lab, which comes out to be negative for any ova/parasites, blood cells, or pus cells. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old woman is brought to the behavioral health clinic by her roommate. The patient’s roommate says that the patient has been looking for cameras that aliens planted in their apartment for the past 2 weeks. Approximately 3 months prior to the onset of this episode, the roommate says the patient stopped playing basketball daily because the sport no longer interested her. She stayed in her bedroom most of the day and was often tearful. The roommate recalls the patient talking about death frequently. The patient states she has been skipping many meals and has lost a significant amount of weight as a result. At the time her delusions about the aliens began, the depressive-related symptoms were no longer present. She has no other medical conditions. She does not drink but smokes 2 packs of cigarettes daily for the past 5 years. Her vitals include: blood pressure 130/88 mm Hg, pulse 92/min, respiratory rate 16/min, temperature 37.3°C (99.1°F). On physical examination, the patient seems apathetic and uses an obscure word that appears to be ‘chinterfittle’. Her affect is flat throughout the entire interaction. She is experiencing bizarre delusions but no hallucinations. The patient does not express suicidal or homicidal ideations. Urine drug screen results are provided below:
Amphetamine negative
Benzodiazepine negative
Cocaine negative
GHB negative
Ketamine negative
LSD negative
Marijuana positive
Opioids negative
PCP negative
Which of the following is the correct diagnosis?

A 53-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department for confusion. She was in her usual state of health until about 3 hours ago when she tried to use her sandwich to turn off the TV. She also complained to her husband that she had a severe headache. Past medical history is notable for hypertension, which has been difficult to control on multiple medications. Her temperature is 36.7°C (98°F), the pulse is 70/min, and the blood pressure is 206/132 mm Hg. On physical exam she is alert and oriented only to herself, repeating over and over that her head hurts. The physical exam is otherwise unremarkable and her neurologic exam is nonfocal. The noncontrast CT scan of the patient’s head is shown. Which of the following diagnostic tests is likely to reveal the diagnosis for this patient?

A 12-year-old girl presents with a 3-day history of frothy brown urine. She does not complain of any other symptoms. She notes that 3 weeks ago she had a fever with a sore throat, but she did not receive any treatment at the time. Her blood pressure is 152/94 mm Hg, heart rate is 72/min, respiratory rate is 15/min, and temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F). Review of her medical record shows that her blood pressure was 118/74 mm Hg just 4 weeks ago. Laboratory analysis reveals elevated serum creatinine, hematuria with RBC casts, and elevated urine protein without frank proteinuria. What laboratory test can confirm the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

An 8-year-old girl is brought to the pediatrician by her father with nausea, vomiting, and decreased frequency of urination. She has acute lymphoblastic leukemia for which she received the 1st dose of chemotherapy 5 days ago. Her leukocyte count was 60,000/mm3 before starting chemotherapy. The vital signs include: pulse 110/min, temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F), and blood pressure 100/70 mm Hg. The physical examination shows bilateral pedal edema. Which of the following serum studies and urinalysis findings will be helpful in confirming the diagnosis of this condition?

An 8-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his parents because he complained of very fast heartbeats. The patient has previously been healthy without any childhood illnesses and has not needed to visit a physician in the past 2 years. On examination, the heart rate is 198/min. Further examination by the physician reveals a grade III holosystolic murmur over the anterior chest wall. ECG is immediately performed after his heart rate is reduced, and shows a short P-R interval with a slow upstroke of the QRS complex. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 65-year-old woman presents with painless swelling of the neck over the past week. She also has noted severe night sweats, which require a change of clothes and bed linens the next day. Her medical history is significant for long-standing hypertension. She received a kidney transplant 6 years ago. Her current medications include amlodipine, metoprolol, furosemide, aspirin, tacrolimus, and mycophenolate. Her family history is significant for her brother, who died last year from lymphoma. A review of systems is positive for a 6-kg (13.2-lb) unintentional weight loss over the past 2 months. Her vital signs include: temperature 37.8℃ (100.0℉) and blood pressure 120/75 mm Hg. On physical examination, there are multiple painless lymph nodes, averaging 2 cm in diameter, palpable in the anterior and posterior triangles of the neck bilaterally. Axillary and inguinal lymphadenopathy is palpated on the right side. Abdominal examination is significant for a spleen of 16 cm below the cost margin on percussion. Laboratory studies are significant for the following:
Hemoglobin 9 g/dL
Mean corpuscular volume 88 μm3
Leukocyte count 12,000/mm3
Platelet count 130,000/mm3
Creatinine 1.1 mg/dL
Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) 1 000 U/L
A peripheral blood smear is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 47-year old morbidly obese man presents to the Emergency Department with complaints of profound nausea, diarrhea, and malaise. His past surgical history is significant for undergoing a laparoscopic gastric bypass procedure seven weeks ago for weight reduction. He has lost 15 kg since the surgery and currently, his BMI is 41 kg/m2. His only medications are vitamins. Blood pressure is 84/40 mm Hg and heart rate is 127/min. He is afebrile. His abdomen is distended and tympanitic with some diffuse tenderness. An abdominal X-ray and without oral contrast demonstrates a diffusely dilated small-bowel without any obvious distal decompressed bowel nor any abdominal free air. What is this patient’s diagnosis likely related to?

A 4-year-old boy is brought to the physician with a 3-month history of progressive intermittent pain and swelling involving both knees, right ankle, and right wrist. The patient has been undergoing treatment with acetaminophen and ice packs, both of which relieved his symptoms. The affected joints feel "stuck” and are difficult to move immediately upon waking up in the morning. However, the patient can move his joints freely after a few minutes. He also complains of occasional mild eye pain that resolves spontaneously. Five months ago, he was diagnosed with an upper respiratory tract infection that resolved without treatment. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows swollen and erythematous joints, which are tender to touch. Slit-lamp examination shows an anterior chamber flare with signs of iris inflammation bilaterally. Laboratory studies show:
Blood parameters
Hemoglobin 12.6 g/dL
Leukocyte count 8,000/mm3
Segmented neutrophils 76%
Eosinophils 1%
Lymphocytes 20%
Monocytes 3%
Platelet count 360,000/mm3
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 36 mm/hr
Serum parameters
Antinuclear antibodies 1:320
Rheumatoid factor negative
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old girl presents with a dry cough. The patient’s father states that the cough started a week ago and has not improved. He says the patient will have fits of forceful coughing that will last for minutes, followed by gasping as she catches her breath. Occasionally, the patient will vomit after one of these episodes. Past medical history is significant for a recent upper respiratory infection 4 weeks ago that has resolved. No current medications. Patient immunization status is incomplete because her father believes they are harmful. Vitals are temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F), blood pressure 105/65 mm Hg, pulse 101/min, respiratory rate 27/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air. Cardiac exam is normal. Lungs are clear to auscultation. There are conjunctival hemorrhages present bilaterally. Which of the following correctly describes the stage of this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old woman presents to the internal medicine clinic with complaints of numbness and tingling in her fingers that she first noticed 6 months ago. It has been progressively worsening and has reached the point where it is affecting her normal daily activities, such as brushing her teeth. Her past medical history is significant for sinusitis and allergic rhinitis since the age of 18, as well as episodic wheezing and shortness of breath since she was 30. She was diagnosed with asthma when she was 22 years old, and subsequently with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) when she was 40. Her current medications include albuterol, loratadine, mometasone, and omeprazole. Her blood pressure is 128/86 mm Hg, heart rate is 78/min, and respiratory rate is 16/min. On physical exam, the patient’s skin is mottled and appears to have a diffuse, lace-like, erythematous discoloration of the arms, legs, and trunk. There is also a small papular rash on her right forearm. Bilateral wheezes are heard on auscultation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old girl is brought in by her father because he is concerned that she has been “acting differently recently”. He says she no longer seems interested in playing with her friends from preschool, and he has noticed that she has stopped making eye contact with others. In addition, he says she flaps her hands when excited or angry and only seems to enjoy playing with objects that she can place in rows or rigid patterns. Despite these behaviors, she is meeting her language goals for her age (single word use). The patient has no significant past medical history. She is at the 90th percentile for height and weight for her age. She is afebrile and her vital signs are within normal limits. A physical examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 55-year-old woman presents with bloody nasal secretions and shortness of breath. She reports she has lost 4 kg (8.8 lb) in the last two months with no changes in her diet. She has also been suffering from mild to moderate joint pain in the left knee for the last year. Her past medical history is unremarkable. Her vitals include: blood pressure 120/70 mm Hg, temperature 37.0℃ (98.6℉), pulse 70/min, respiratory rate 14/min. Physical examination is significant for nasal ulcers. Diffuse crackles are present over all lobes of the lung bilaterally. Laboratory findings are significant for the following:
Hemoglobin 12.9 g/dL
Hematocrit 37.7%
Leukocyte count 5500/mm3
Neutrophils 65%
Lymphocytes 30%
Monocytes 5%
Mean corpuscular volume 82.2 μm3
Platelet count 190,000/mm3
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 35 mm/h
C-reactive protein 14 mg/dL
Creatinine 3.09 mg/dL
The patient is prescribed a corticosteroid nasal spray and oral antibiotics but returns in 2 weeks without any clinical improvement. Which of the following would most likely confirm the diagnosis in this patient?

A 15-year-old girl is brought to the physician with an ongoing pruritic rash for 1 week. The rash is on her right forearm (refer to the image). She has not had a similar rash in the past. She has no history of allergies, and she is not taking any medications. She frequently enjoys gardening in their backyard. They have no household pets. The physical examination reveals no other abnormalities. Given the most likely diagnosis, which of the following is the most appropriate treatment of the condition described in this case?

A 59-year-old woman presents to her family practitioner with her husband. She has fallen several times over the past 3 months. Standing up from a seated position is especially difficult for her. She also complains of intermittent dizziness, excessive sweating, constipation, and difficulty performing activities of daily living. She denies fever, jerking of the limbs, memory disturbances, urinary incontinence, and abnormal limb movements. Past medical includes a cholecystectomy 25 years ago and occasional decreased libido. She takes a vitamin supplement with calcium and occasionally uses hormone replacement therapy. While supine, her blood pressure is 142/74 mm Hg and her heart rate is 64/min. After standing, her blood pressure is 118/60 mm Hg and her heart rate is 62/min. She is alert and oriented with a flat affect while answering questions. Extraocular movements are intact in all directions. No tremors are noticed. Muscle strength is normal in all limbs but with increased muscle tone. She is slow in performing intentional movements. Her writing is small and she takes slow steps during walking with adducted arms and a slightly reduced arm swing. A trial of levodopa did not improve her symptoms. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 64-year-old man presents for the scheduled annual physical examination for management of his hypertension. The patient is asymptomatic and his blood pressure is within normal limits throughout the year. He has a past medical history of polyarthrosis, and he is a carrier of hepatitis B antibodies. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is currently taking the following medications: enalapril, ranitidine, and lorazepam. The vital signs include: pulse rate 72/min, respiratory rate 14/min, blood pressure 138/76 mm Hg, and temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F). The physical examination shows no abnormalities. The laboratory test results are shown below:
Hemoglobin 11.6 g/dL
Hematocrit 34.8%
MCV 91.4 fL
MCH 31.4 pg
Platelets 388,000/mm3
Leukocytes 7,300/mm3
ESR 59 mm/h
On account of these laboratory test results, the patient was once again questioned for symptoms that would explain the abnormality detected in his laboratory test results. The patient insists that he is asymptomatic. Therefore, further laboratory studies were requested. The additional laboratory test results are shown below:
PCR 5.3 mg/dL
Serum protein electrophoresis
Total proteins 7.4 g/dL
Albumin 5.8 g/dL
Alpha-1 3.5 g/dL
Alpha-2 1 g/dL
Beta 0.9 g/dL
Gamma 1.7 g/dL
The gamma protein was later confirmed as an immunoglobulin G (IgG) kappa paraprotein (1,040 mg/dL). Due to these results a computed tomography (CT) scan was conducted, and it showed moderate osteopathy without any other lesions. A bone marrow biopsy was done that showed 5–10% plasma cells. Which of the following is most likely associated with the diagnosis of this patient?

A 45-year-old man presents with a 2-year history of fatigue, paresthesia, diarrhea, and abdominal pain. He says he experiences 2–3 episodes of non-bloody diarrhea per month associated with crampy abdominal pain. He also has the bilateral tingling sensation of his upper and lower limbs in a glove and stocking pattern which is sometimes associated with the burning sensation of his hands and legs. Past medical history is unremarkable. The patient denies smoking, alcohol consumption, illicit drug use. His vital signs include: blood pressure 100/60 mm Hg without postural changes, heart rate 92/min, respiratory rate 16/min, temperature 37.0℃ (98.6℉). Laboratory findings are significant for the following:
Hgb 7.2 gm/dL
MCV 110 fL
RBC 3.6 X109/L
Platelets 10,000/mm3
Total count  4,200/mm3
Reticulocyte 0.8%
A peripheral blood smear demonstrates hypersegmented neutrophils. Anti-intrinsic factor and anti-tissue transglutaminase antibodies were negative. An upper GI series with small bowel follow-through is performed which shows a narrowing of the barium contrast in the lumen of the terminal ileum to the width of a string. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A day after percutaneous coronary intervention for stable angina, a 63-year-old man develops severe pain in his right small toe. He has no history of a similar episode. He has had diabetes mellitus for 16 years. After the procedure, his blood pressure is 145/90 mm Hg, the pulse is 65/min, the respiratory rate is 15/min, and the temperature is 36.7°C (98.1°F). Physical examination of the femoral artery access site shows no abnormalities. Distal pulses are palpable and symmetric. A photograph of the toe is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old woman presents to the behavioral health clinic for an evaluation after seeing animal-shaped clouds in the form of dogs, cats, and monkeys. The patient says that these symptoms have been present for more than 2 weeks. Past medical history is significant for simple partial seizures for which she takes valproate, but she has not had her medication adjusted in several years. Her vital signs include: blood pressure of 124/76 mm Hg, heart rate of 98/min, respiratory rate of 12/min, and temperature of 37.1°C (98.8°F). On physical examination, the patient is alert and oriented to person, time, and place. Affect is not constricted or flat. Speech is of rapid rate and high volume. Pupils are equal and reactive bilaterally. The results of a urine drug screen are as follows:
Alcohol positive
Amphetamine negative
Benzodiazepine negative
Cocaine positive
GHB negative
Ketamine negative
LSD negative
Marijuana negative
Opioids negative
PCP negative
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 75-year-old woman presents to the emergency department because of pain in her left thigh and left calf for the past 3 months. The pain occurs at rest, worsens with walking, and is slightly improved by hanging her foot off the bed. She has had hypertension for 25 years and type 2 diabetes mellitus for 30 years. She has smoked 30–40 cigarettes per day for the past 45 years. On examination, the femoral, popliteal, and dorsalis pedis pulses are diminished, but detectable on both sides. The patient’s foot is shown in the image. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 79-year-old man presents to his physician complaining of a persistent non-productive cough and dyspnea after contracting a cold in the past month. He describes himself as being “generally healthy” before the cold started. Medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia. The patient takes hydrochlorothiazide, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. His parents are both deceased. He does not smoke and only drinks alcohol occasionally. During a review of symptoms, he described a month-long trip to St. Louis, Missouri, to visit family. At the physician’s office, his temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse is 82/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 130/82 mm Hg. A focused chest exam reveals mild crepitus on the right side. A chest X-ray shows a cavitary lesion in the right lung which is confirmed on chest computed tomography (CT). A lung biopsy is performed to rule out cancer and reveals necrotic granulomatous inflammation with oval yeast in macrophages. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old man presents with fever, chills, nausea, and urinary urgency and frequency. He says that his symptoms began 4 days ago and have progressively worsened. His past medical history is significant for a 6-month history of recurrent urinary tract infections (UTIs). His vital signs include: temperature 39.0°C (102.2°F), blood pressure 100/70 mm Hg, pulse 92/min, and respiratory rate 25/min. On physical examination, there is moderate left costovertebral angle tenderness. Laboratory findings are significant for the following:
WBC 8,500/mm3
RBC 4.20 x 106/mm3
Hematocrit 41.5%
Hemoglobin 13.0 g/dL
Platelet count 225,000/mm3
Urinalysis
Color Dark yellow
Clarity Turbid
pH 6.5
Specific gravity 1.026
Glucose None
Ketones None
Nitrites Positive
Leukocyte esterase Positive
Bilirubin Negative
Urobilirubin 0.6 mg/dL
Protein Trace
Blood None
WBC 25/hpf
Bacteria Many
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A mother brings her 4-year-old girl to the physician, as the girl has a 7-day history of foul-smelling diarrhea, abdominal cramps, and fever. The mother adds that she has been vomiting as well, and she is very much worried. The child is in daycare, and the mother endorses sick contacts with both family and friends. The girl has not been vaccinated as the parents do not think it is necessary. On physical exam, the child appears dehydrated. Stool examination is negative for blood cells, pus, and ova or parasites. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-day-old newborn girl has failed to pass meconium after 48 hours. There is an absence of stool in the rectal vault. Family history is significant for MEN2A syndrome. Which of the following confirms the diagnosis?

A 52-year-old man presents to the urgent care center with several hours of worsening abdominal discomfort that radiates to the back. The patient also complains of malaise, chills, nausea, and vomiting. Social history is notable for alcoholism. On physical exam, he is febrile to 39.5°C (103.1℉), and he is diffusely tender on abdominal palpation. Other vital signs include a blood pressure of 126/74 mm Hg, heart rate of 74/min, and respiratory rate of 14/min. Complete blood count is notable for 13,500 white blood cells (WBCs), and his complete metabolic panel shows bilirubin of 2.1 and amylase of 3210. Given the following options, what is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old man presents to an urgent care clinic with the complaints of bloody diarrhea, mid-abdominal discomfort, and cramping for 3 days. He also has nausea, vomiting, and fever. He reports that he had eaten raw oysters at a local seafood restaurant almost 3 days ago, but he denies any other potentially infectious exposures. His temperature is 37.5°C (99.6°F), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 67/min, and blood pressure is 102/68 mm Hg. Physical examination is non-contributory. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 51-year-old woman alcoholic presents to the emergency department with persistent vomiting. She was found vomiting forcefully next to an empty bottle of vodka. Her medical history is significant for Lyme disease, currently being treated with doxycycline. After a prolonged episode of retching, the patient begins choking and coughing forcefully in between bouts of chest pain in the ER. At this point, the patient is unable to communicate. The patient appears toxic. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 107/min, and blood pressure is 90/68 mm Hg. A quick physical exam reveals fullness at the base of the neck and a crunching, rasping sound on auscultation of the chest. The attending physician orders an upright chest X-ray, showing free mediastinal air. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 58-year-old male, being treated on the medical floor for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin, develops watery diarrhea. He reports at least 9 episodes of diarrhea within the last two days, with lower abdominal discomfort and cramping. His temperature is 98.6° F (37° C), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 67/min, and blood pressure is 122/98 mm Hg. His physical examination is unremarkable. Laboratory testing shows:
Hb%   13 gm/dL
Total count (WBC):   13,400/mm3
Differential count:    
  Neutrophils: 80%
  Lymphocytes: 15%
  Monocytes: 5%
ESR:   33 mm/hr
What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old girl presents with a 7-day history of fever and abdominal pain for the past 4 days. Past medical history is significant for an exchange transfusion for neonatal hyperbilirubinemia and recurrent attacks of pallor during the course of upper respiratory tract infections. Her vital signs include: blood pressure 120/70 mm Hg, pulse 105/min, respiratory rate 40/min, and temperature 37.0℃ (98.6℉). On physical examination, the patient is ill-looking. Conjunctivae are pale and the sclera is icteric. The liver is palpable 2 cm below the costal margin and the spleen is palpable 3 cm below the left costal margin. Laboratory findings show hemoglobin of 5.9 gm/dL, Hct of 20%, and haptoglobin of 28 gm/dL. A peripheral blood smear shows hypochromic anemia, polychromasia, anisocytosis, and occasional Heinz bodies. The reticulocyte count was 15%. A direct Coombs test was negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 55-year-old woman presents for a routine check-up. She currently has no complaints, and her last physical and laboratory studies were unremarkable. Her past medical history is significant for hypercholesterolemia, well managed with rosuvastatin, and hypertension, well managed with hydrochlorothiazide. Her current medications also include aspirin. The patient is afebrile and her vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination reveals some generalized lymphadenopathy. Laboratory findings are significant for the following:
WBC 38,000/mm3
RBC 4.20 x 106/mm3
Hematocrit 27.3%
Hemoglobin 8.3 g/dL
Platelet count 355,000/mm3
A peripheral blood smear and differential shows 92% small normocytic lymphocytes.
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 52-year-old man complains of intermittent diffuse abdominal pain that becomes worse after eating meals and several episodes of diarrhea, the last of which was bloody. These symptoms have been present for the previous 6 months but have worsened recently. He has had significant weight loss since the onset of symptoms. His past medical history includes systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), which has been difficult to manage medically. Vital signs include a blood pressure of 100/70 mm Hg, temperature of 37.1°C (98.8 °F), and pulse of 95/min. On physical examination, the patient appears to be in severe pain, and there is mild diffuse abdominal tenderness. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old African American woman presents with nausea and severe abdominal pain. She denies vomiting. She says that, 2 days ago, her divorce was finalized, so she went to a bar and had multiple shots of tequila and vodka. This morning, upon waking, she noticed her urine was red, which lasted throughout the day. The patient denies any history of similar symptoms. Past medical history is significant for low blood counts diagnosed on routine laboratory work 6 months ago, which was not followed up due to the stress of the divorce. A review of systems is significant for dyspareunia and chronic fatigue. Her temperature is 37.2°C (99.0°F), the heart rate is 90/min, the blood pressure is 136/88 mm Hg, and the respiratory rate is 20/min. Physical examination shows scleral icterus. Mucous membranes are pale. Cardiac auscultation reveals a systolic flow murmur loudest along the left sternal border. There is moderate right upper quadrant abdominal tenderness with no rebound or guarding. The remainder of the exam is unremarkable. Laboratory findings are significant for the following:
Hematocrit 27%
Mean corpuscular volume 81 µm3
Leukocytes 6,000/mm3
Platelets 130,000/µL
Haptoglobin 30 mg/dL (50–150 mg/dL)
Reticulocyte count 3%
  Total bilirubin 7.1 mg/dL
LDH 766 U/L
AST 150 U/L
ALT 195 U/L
HbA1 96%
HbA2 2%
HbF 2%
CD55 50% of expected
The peripheral smear is unremarkable. Which of the following would be the most likely cause of mortality given this patient’s likely diagnosis?

A 49-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with abdominal discomfort, fever, and decreased urination. She has a history of liver cirrhosis due to chronic hepatitis C infection. Her blood pressure is 90/70 mm Hg, pulse is 75/min, and temperature 38°C (100.4°F). On physical examination she is jaundiced, and she has tense ascites with generalized abdominal tenderness. There is pitting edema to the level of her upper thighs. Which of the following excludes the diagnosis of hepatorenal syndrome in this patient?

A 45-year-old woman presents to the physician because of a 1-day history of progressive pain and blurry vision in her right eye. She is struggling to open this eye because of the pain. Her left eye is asymptomatic. She wears contact lenses. She has bronchial asthma treated with inhaled salbutamol. She works as a kindergarten teacher. The vital signs include: temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse 85/min, and blood pressure 135/75 mm Hg. The examination shows a visual acuity in the left eye of 20/25 and the ability to count fingers at 3 feet in the right eye. A photograph of the right eye is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old man presents following a suicide attempt 2 days ago. He says that his attempt was a result of a fight with his girlfriend and that he slit his wrists in an attempt to keep her from breaking up with him. In the past, he has had many turbulent relationships, both romantic and in his family life. His family members describe him as being very impulsive and frequently acting to manipulate people’s feelings. Since he was admitted to the hospital, he has spit at several staff members and alternated between sobbing and anger. He has no significant past medical history. The patient denies any history of smoking, alcohol use, or recreational drug use. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 15-year-old girl is referred to a child psychologist because of worsening behavior and constant disruption in class. She has received multiple reprimands in the past 6 months for not doing the homework her teacher assigned, and she refuses to listen to the classroom instructions. Additionally, her teachers say she is very argumentative and blames other children for not letting her do her work. She was previously well behaved and one of the top students in her class. She denies any recent major life events or changes at home. Her past medical history is noncontributory. Her vital signs are all within normal limits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 77-year-old man is brought to his primary care provider by his daughter with behavioral changes and an abnormally bad memory for the past few months. The patient’s daughter says he sometimes gets angry and aggressive while at other times he seems lost and stares at his surroundings. His daughter also reports that she has seen her father talking to empty chairs. The patient says he sleeps well during the night but still feels sleepy throughout the day. He has no problems getting dressed and maintaining his one bedroom apartment. Past medical history is significant for mild depression and mild osteoporosis. Current medications include escitalopram, alendronic acid, and a multivitamin. The patient is afebrile, and his vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, the patient is alert and oriented and sitting comfortably in his chair. A mild left-hand tremor is noted. Muscle strength is 5 out of 5 in the upper and lower extremities bilaterally, but muscle tone is slightly increased. He can perform repetitive alternating movements albeit slowly. He walks with a narrow gait and has mild difficulty turning. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 30-year-old woman who was recently placed on TMP-SMX for a urinary tract infection presents to urgent care with a new rash. The vital signs include: blood pressure 121/80 mm Hg, pulse 91/min, respiratory rate 18/min, and temperature 36.7°C (98.2°F). Physical examination reveals a desquamative skin covering both of her lower extremities. A basic chemistry panel reveal sodium 139 mmol/L, potassium 3.8 mmol/L, chloride 110 mmol/L, carbon dioxide 47, blood urea nitrogen 23 mg/dL, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, and glucose 103 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old boy is admitted to the emergency department with severe retrosternal chest pain. The pain began suddenly after an episode of self-induced vomiting following a large meal. The patient’s parents say that he is very restricted in the foods he eats and induces vomiting frequently after meals. Vital signs are as follows: blood pressure 100/60 mm Hg, heart rate 98/min, respiratory rate 14/min, and temperature 37.9℃ (100.2℉). The patient is pale and in severe distress. Lungs are clear to auscultation. On cardiac examination, a crunching, raspy sound is auscultated over the precordium that is synchronous with the heartbeat. The abdomen is soft and nontender. Which of the following tests would most likely confirm the diagnosis in this patient?

A 16-year-old woman presents to the clinic accompanied by her father, with the complaints of high fever, sore throat, and bloody diarrhea for 4 days. She adds that she is also nauseous and vomited several times in the past 2 days. She denies any recent travel or eating outside. She recently started a dog-walking business. The father relates that two of the dogs had been unwell. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), respiratory rate is 16/min, pulse is 77/min, and blood pressure is 100/88 mm Hg. A physical examination is performed and is within normal limits including the abdominal exam. Blood test results are given below:
Hb%: 14 gm/dL
Total count (WBC): 13,100/mm3
Differential count:
Neutrophils: 80%
Lymphocytes: 15%
Monocytes: 5%
What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old woman comes to the emergency department because of colicky pain in the lower abdomen and abdominal distension for the past 12 hours. She has chronic constipation for which she takes lactulose and senna laxatives. Her temperature is 37.1°C (98.7°F), blood pressure is 110/60 mm Hg and pulse is 85/min. On physical examination, there is diffuse abdominal distension and tenderness, and bowel sounds are faint. Her plain abdominal radiograph is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
