An 11-year-old woman presents with fever and joint pain for the last 3 days. Her mother says that she had a sore throat 3 weeks ago but did not seek medical care at that time. The family immigrated from the Middle East 3 years ago. The patient has no past medical history. The current illness started with a fever and a swollen right knee that was very painful. The following day, her knee improved but her left elbow became swollen and painful. While in the waiting room, her left knee is also becoming swollen and painful. Vital signs include: temperature 38.7°C (101.6°F), and blood pressure 110/80 mm Hg. On physical examination, the affected joints are swollen and very tender to touch, and there are circular areas of redness on her back and left forearm (as shown in the image). Which of the following is needed to establish a diagnosis of acute rheumatic fever in this patient?

A 67-year-old woman refers to her physician for a follow-up examination. During her last visit 1 month ago, splenomegaly was detected. She has had night sweats for the past several months and has lost 5 kg (11 lb) unintentionally during this period. She has no history of severe illness and takes no medications. The vital signs are within normal limits. The examination shows no abnormalities other than splenomegaly. The laboratory studies show the following:
Hemoglobin 9 g/dL
Mean corpuscular volume 95 μm3
Leukocyte count 12,000/mm3
Platelet count 260,000/mm3
Ultrasound shows a spleen size of 15 cm and mild hepatomegaly. A peripheral blood smear shows teardrop-shaped and nucleated red blood cells (RBCs) and immature myeloid cells. The marrow is very difficult to aspirate but reveals hyperplasia of all 3 lineages. The tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase (TRAP) test is negative. Clonal marrow plasma cells are not seen. JAK-2 is positive. The cytogenetic analysis is negative for translocation between chromosomes 9 and 22. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old man repetitively visits the general surgery clinic worried that his inguinal hernia is incarcerated. 2 months ago, he was seen in the emergency department where he presented with a left lower abdominal swelling. The mass was easily reduced and the patient was referred to the general surgery clinic for elective surgical repair. Because his condition was deemed not urgent, he was informed that he was down on the surgical waiting list. Despite this, he continues to visit the clinic and the ED worried that his bowels are ‘trapped and dying.’ Each time he is reassured and any protrusion present is quickly reduced. He has previously frequently visited his primary care physician for complaints of abdominal pain and inconsistent bowel habits, but no etiology could be identified. He continues to intermittently have these symptoms and spends hours every day worrying about what may be going on. He has no other significant past medical history. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnosis?

A 22-year-old woman presents with lower limb weakness for the past 2 days. The patient says that the weakness started in both her feet, manifesting as difficulty walking, but it has progressed to where she cannot move her legs completely and has become bedbound. She also has experienced a recent history of numbness and tingling sensations in both her feet. She denies any recent history of fever, backache, urinary or bowel incontinence, trauma, shortness of breath, or diplopia. Her past medical history is remarkable for a viral flu-like illness 2 weeks ago. The patient is afebrile, and her vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, muscle strength in both lower limbs is 1/5. The muscle strength in the upper limbs is ⅘ bilaterally. Sensation to pinprick is decreased in both lower limbs in a stocking distribution. The sensation is intact in the upper limbs bilaterally. Knee and ankle reflexes are absent bilaterally. The laboratory findings are significant for the following:
Hemoglobin 14.2 g/dL
White blood cell count  8,250/mm3
Platelet count 258,000/mm3
BUN 14 mg/dL
Creatinine  0.9 mg/dL
Serum sodium 144 mEq/L
Serum potassium 3.9 mEq/L
Which of the following tests would most likely confirm the diagnosis in this patient?

A 51-year-old homeless woman presents to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain and cramping for the past 3 hours. She endorses radiation to her back. She adds that she vomited multiple times. She admits having been hospitalized repeatedly for alcohol intoxication and abdominal pain. Her temperature is 103.8° F (39.8° C), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 107/min, and blood pressure is 100/80 mm Hg. She refuses a physical examination due to severe pain. Blood work reveals the following:
Serum:    
  Albumin: 3.2 gm/dL
  Alkaline phosphatase: 150 U/L
  Alanine aminotransferase: 76 U/L
  Aspartate aminotransferase: 155 U/L
  Gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase: 202 U/L
  Lipase: 800 U/L
What is the most likely diagnosis of this patient?

A 62-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with hematuria and hemoptysis that started in the morning. She notes that she has had frequent lung infections throughout her adult life, the most recent being 2 weeks ago. She also mentions that she has had hematuria twice before but never as severe as she is having currently. Her medical history is otherwise non-significant, and her only medication is acetaminophen as needed. Her blood pressure is 136/92 mm Hg, heart rate is 86/min, respiratory rate is 16/min, and temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F). Chest radiography shows a resolving right middle lobe airspace opacity. Her initial laboratory tests are notable for elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level. While in the examination room, the patient develops a spontaneous nosebleed. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old woman comes to the emergency department with the complaint of pain and swelling of the proximal joint in the third finger of her right hand. The pain is so severe that it woke her up from sleep this morning. She has never had an episode like this before. The patient has smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for the last 25 years and drinks alcohol heavily each weekend. Her friend threw a party last night where she drank 3–4 beers and was unable to drive back home. She has no past medical illness. Her mother died of pancreatic cancer at age 55, and her father died of a stroke 2 years ago. Her temperature is 37.7°C (100°F), blood pressure is 130/70 mm Hg, pulse is 104/min, respiratory rate is 20/min, and BMI is 25 kg/m2. The patient is in moderate distress due to the pain. On examination, the proximal interphalangeal joint of the third finger of her right hand is very tender to touch, swollen, warm, and slightly red in color. Range of motion cannot be assessed due to extreme tenderness. The patient’s right hand is shown in the image.
Laboratory investigation
Complete blood count:
Hemoglobin 14.5 g/dL
Leukocytes 16,000/mm3
Platelets 150,000/mm3
ESR     55mm/hr
Synovial fluid is aspirated from the joint. The findings are:
Appearance Cloudy, dense yellow
WBC 30,000 cells/µL
Culture Negative
Negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals are seen. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old woman presents with 2 days of severe, generalized, abdominal pain that is worse after meals. She is also nauseated and reports occasional diarrhea mixed with blood. Apart from essential hypertension, her medical history is unremarkable. Her vital signs include a temperature of 36.9°C (98.4°F), blood pressure of 145/92 mm Hg, and an irregularly irregular pulse of 105/min. Physical examination is only notable for mild periumbilical tenderness. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old woman is brought to a psychiatrist by her mother. The patient’s mother has become increasingly concerned about her since her high school graduation. Although she says that she had been an excellent student in high school, her grades have begun slipping in her second year in college, and she no longer socializes with friends. When she asked her why she no longer talks to her friends, she states that she told her, “They already know where I am. They can see me. They watch me from my bedroom window, so they already know what I’m doing. We don’t need to talk.” She found this to be bizarre, as nearly all of her friends live hours away. The patient states that she feels fine and doesn’t understand why everyone thinks she is crazy. The psychiatrist notices reduced spontaneous movements while the patient is speaking and that she speaks in a monotone with a voice that is soft in volume. She also appears suspicious and defensive, asking the psychiatrist “why are you asking me that?” after each evaluative question. Her mood is generally flat with little reactivity or engagement during the course of her interview, but she denies any symptoms of depression or psychosis. No significant past medical history. Family history is not available as she was adopted. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 61-year-old diabetic man is brought to the emergency department with the complaint of multiple bouts of abdominal pain in the last 24 hours. He says that the pain is dull aching in nature, radiates to the back, and worsens with meals. He also complains of nausea and occasional vomiting. He has been hospitalized repeatedly in the past with similar complaints. His temperature is 37° C (98.6° F), respiratory rate is 16/min, pulse is 77/min, and blood pressure is 120/89 mm Hg. On physical exam, dark hyperpigmentation of the axillary skin is noted. His blood test report from last month is given below:
Glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c): 9.1%
Triglyceride: 675 mg/dL
LDL-Cholesterol: 102 mg/dL
HDL-Cholesterol: 35 mg/dL
Total Cholesterol: 250 mg/dL
Serum Creatinine: 1.2 mg/dL
BUN:  12 mg/dL
Alkaline phosphatase: 100 U/L
Alanine aminotransferase: 36 U/L
Aspartate aminotransferase: 28 U/L
What is the most likely diagnosis in this case?

A 40-year-old man presents with a lack of concentration at work for the last 3 months. He says that he has been working as a personal assistant to a manager at a corporate business company for the last 2 years. Upon asking why he is not able to concentrate, he answers that his colleagues are always gossiping about him during work hours and that it disrupts his concentration severely. His wife works in the same company and denies these allegations. She says the other employees are busy doing their own work and have only formal conversations, yet he is convinced that they are talking about him. She further adds that her husband frequently believes that some advertisements in a newspaper are directed towards him and are published specifically to catch his attention even though they are routine advertisements. The patient denies any mood disturbances, anxiety or hallucinations. Past medical history is significant for a tingling sensation in his legs, 3+ patellar reflexes bilaterally, and absent ankle reflexes bilaterally. He says that he drinks alcohol once to twice a month for social reasons but denies any other substance use or smoking. On physical examination, the patient is conscious, alert, and oriented to time, place and person. A beefy red color of the tongue is noted. No associated cracking, bleeding, or oral lesions. Which of the following laboratory tests would be most helpful to identify this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old woman presents to a rheumatologist with bilateral wrist and knee pain that has been present for the last 10 years. The patient was a professional athlete who retired at age 50. She also notes morning stiffness in her joints that lasts approx. 50 minutes. She denies joint swelling, color changes in her digits, dryness of mucous membranes, and constitutional symptoms such as fever and chills. On physical exam, the physician notes several non-tender nodules on the left 1st, 3rd, and 4th distal interphalangeal joints. There is also tenderness with palpation at the base of both thumbs. The patient’s knees are enlarged, bilaterally, and she has pain and crepitus on passive range of motion. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old man comes to the physician with complaints of fever, headache, and rash, which have gradually worsened over the past 6 days. The patient informs the physician that the rash appeared after 2 days of fever. The rash started at the wrists and ankles and then gradually spread to the trunk, palms, and soles. On examination, the physician notes a maculopapular rash as shown in the image below. Vital signs show a temperature of 39.4°C (103.0°F), a blood pressure of 110/70 mm Hg, and a pulse rate of 86/min. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 31-year-old woman is brought in to the clinic by her brother because he is concerned about her behavior since the death of their mother 2 months ago. The patient’s brother states that she has always been a ‘loner’ and preferred being by herself than socializing with others. Her social isolation resulted in her being ‘socially awkward’, as described by her family. However, 2 months ago, when she found out about the death of their mother, she showed little emotion and attended her funeral in jeans and a dirty T-shirt which upset the rest of their family. When asked about it, she shrugged and said she was in a hurry to get to the funeral and “just left the house with what I had on.” She does not speak much during the interview, allowing her brother to speak on her behalf. Her brother insists that she has ‘always been like this’, quiet and a complacent child who had no interest in playing with other children. The patient currently lives alone and spends her time repairing and building electrical appliances, and her brother is worried that her self-imposed isolation is making it ‘impossible for her to interact with other people normally’. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 32-year-old woman presents with a 2-month history of increasing lethargy, frequent upper respiratory tract infections, and easy bruising. Past medical history is unremarkable. The patient reports a 14-pack-year smoking history and says she drinks alcohol socially. No significant family history. Her vital signs include: temperature 36.8°C (98.2°F), blood pressure 132/91 mm Hg and pulse 95/min. Physical examination reveals conjunctival pallor and scattered ecchymoses on the lower extremities. Laboratory results are significant for the following:
Hemoglobin 8.2 g/dL
Leukocyte count 2,200/mm3
Platelet count 88,000/mm3
Reticulocyte count 0.5%
A bone marrow biopsy is performed, which demonstrates hypocellularity with no abnormal cell population. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 20-year-old female college student presents to the emergency room at 4 AM in the morning with complaints of abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea for the past 2 hours. She was studying for her exams last night when she became hungry and ate some food from the afternoon after heating it for a while. She says that her symptoms began an hour after she ate the food. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), respiratory rate is 15/min, pulse is 106/min, and blood pressure is 90/78 mm Hg. A physical examination is within normal limits except for signs of dehydration. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-year-old boy presents to his pediatrician with complaints of repeated jerking of his neck for the past 2 years. Initially, his parents considered it a sign of discomfort in his neck, but later they noticed that the jerking was more frequent when he was under emotional stress or when he was fatigued. The patient says he can voluntarily control the jerking in some social situations, but when he is under stress, he feels the urge to jerk his neck and he feels better after that. The parents also report that during the past year, there have even been a few weeks when the frequency of the neck jerking had decreased drastically, only to increase again afterwards. On physical examination, he is a physically healthy male with normal vital signs. His neurologic examination is normal. The pediatrician also notes that when she makes certain movements, the patient partially imitates these movements. The parents are very much concerned about his abnormal movements and insist on a complete diagnostic work-up. After a detailed history, physical examination, and laboratory investigations, the pediatrician confirms the diagnosis of Tourette syndrome. The presence of which of the following findings is most likely to confirm the pediatrician’s diagnosis.

A 18-month-old toddler is brought to the pediatrician by his mother for cough. The mother reports that her son has had a productive-sounding cough and runny nose for the past 2 days. He has also noticed that his son feels warm. On chart review, this is the 4th time this patient is presenting for similar concerns; the 3 previous diagnoses were otitis media (2 episodes) and bacterial sinusitis (1 episode). His temperature is 38.3°C (101.0°F). Physical examination is notable for cough and purulent sputum from both nares, although his lungs are clear to auscultation. Sputum gram stain shows gram-positive diplococci. Serum immunoglobulin studies show normal levels of IgM and decreased levels of IgG and IgA. Which of the following is the most likely underlying diagnosis in this patient?

A 58-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with severe right leg pain accompanied by tingling and weakness. Her condition started suddenly 3 hours ago when she was watching a movie. Her medical history is remarkable for type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension. She has been smoking 20–30 cigarettes per day for the past 35 years. Her vital signs include a blood pressure of 149/85 mm Hg, a temperature of 36.9°C (98.4°F), and an irregular pulse of 96/min. On physical examination, her right popliteal and posterior tibial pulses are absent. Her right leg is pale and cold. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old woman presents to her physician’s office with a progressive cough. It has been increasing in intensity over the past week. She has also been noticing an increase in the amount of sputum she usually produces, which is thick and yellow. She also complains of increased difficulty in breathing, more so than she previously experienced. She was diagnosed with chronic obstructive lung disease (COPD) about 3 years ago and has been on treatment for it since then. She doesn’t report any fever, chills, or night sweats. She has observed a foul smell to her sputum. Her blood pressure is 100/65 mm Hg, the respirations are 23/min and the pulse is about 110/min. Currently, her FEV1 is around 48% of the normal predicted value. She is currently receiving a yearly influenza shot and has taken the pneumococcal vaccination at the time of her diagnosis. In spite of this, she has had acute exacerbations of her symptoms 4 times over the last year. Her last episode was 2 months ago, for which she was treated with a short course of antibiotics. She is also currently receiving treatment for diabetes. Which of the following pathogens should be considered before initiating treatment for the current episode?

A 78-year-old man living in New Jersey is brought to the emergency department in July with a fever for 5 days. Lethargy is present. He has had bloody urine over the last 48 hours but denies any nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain. He has no history of serious illness and takes no medications. He has not traveled anywhere outside his city for the past several years. He appears ill. The temperature is 40.8℃ (105.4℉), the pulse is 108/min, the respiration rate is 20/min, and the blood pressure is 105/50 mm Hg. The abdominal exam reveals hepatosplenomegaly. Lymphadenopathy is absent. Petechiae are seen on the lower extremities. Laboratory studies show the following:
Laboratory test
Hemoglobin 8 g/dL
Mean corpuscular volume (MCV) 98 µm3
Leukocyte count 4,200/mm3
Segmented neutrophils 32%
Lymphocytes 58%
Platelet count 108,000/mm3
Bilirubin, total 5.0 mg/dL
Direct 0.7 mg/dL
Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 51 U/L
Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 56 U/L
Alkaline phosphatase 180 U/L
Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) 640 U/L (N = 140–280 U/L)
Haptoglobin 20 mg/dL (N = 30–200 mg/dL)
Urine
Hemoglobin +
Urobilinogen +
Protein +
A peripheral blood smear is shown (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old woman presents to the physician with profuse watery diarrhea along with fever and crampy abdominal pain. She has been taking an antibiotic course of cefixime for about a week to treat a respiratory tract infection. At the doctor’s office, her pulse is 112/min, the blood pressure is 100/66 mm Hg, the respirations are 22/min, and the temperature is 38.9°C (102.0°F). Her oral mucosa appears dry and her abdomen is soft with vague diffuse tenderness. A digital rectal examination is normal. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 11.1 g/dL
Hematocrit 33%
Total leucocyte count 16,000/mm3
Serum lactate 0.9 mmol/L
Serum creatinine 1.1 mg/dL
What is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 41-year-old man with a past medical history significant for asthma and seasonal allergies presents with a new rash. He has no significant past surgical, social, or family history. The patient's blood pressure is 131/90 mm Hg, the pulse is 77/min, the respiratory rate is 17/min, and the temperature is 36.9°C (98.5°F). Physical examination reveals a sharply demarcated area of skin dryness and erythema encircling his left wrist. Review of systems is otherwise negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old woman and recent immigrant from Brazil present to the clinic. She has no known past medical, past surgical, or family history. The patient admits to having several regular sexual partners. Today, she complains of a skin rash on her back. She is unclear when it started but became aware when one of her partners pointed it out. A review of systems is otherwise negative. Physical examination reveals numerous hypopigmented skin lesions over her upper back. When questioned, she states that they do not get darker after spending time in the sun. On examination, there is a 5 cm (1.9 in) patch of hypopigmented skin in the center of her back with a fine-scale overlying it. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old girl presents with a limp favoring her right leg. The patient’s father noticed she had been limping without complaint for the past 6 months. Past medical history is significant for the flu last year. No current medications. All immunizations are up to date. The vital signs include: temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F), blood pressure 100/60 mm Hg, pulse 74/min, respiratory rate 19/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air. The body mass index (BMI) is 17.2 kg/m2. On physical examination, the patient is alert and cooperative. A limp favoring the right leg is noted when the patient is walking. There is mild tenderness on deep palpation of the left lumbar region but no erythema, edema, or warmth. There is a decreased range of motion of the left hip. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 72-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with difficulty breathing for the past 3 hours. She also mentions that over the last week she was frequently breathless and fatigued after walking a few blocks. She has had diabetes mellitus and hypertension for the past 10 years, and her regular medications include metformin, glipizide, and lisinopril. However, she did not take her medications last week due to unplanned travel. Review of her medical records reveals an episode of acute viral hepatitis about 6 months ago from which she recovered well. Her temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), the pulse is 108/min, the blood pressure is 170/94 mm Hg, and the respiratory rate is 24/min. On physical examination, periorbital edema is present with pitting edema over both ankles and pretibial regions. Pallor and icterus are absent. Auscultation of the chest reveals crackles over the infrascapular regions bilaterally. Abdominal examination shows tender hepatomegaly. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 81-year-old woman patient recently moved into an assisted living facility and presents today with itchy blisters in her axilla. She attributes these to a poor diet. She also complains that the nurse practitioner at the facility started her on 4 new medications, in addition to her existing prescriptions. On physical examination, tense axillary bullae are noted that do not rupture with light, gloved touch. On direct immunofluorescence, linear C3 and IgG deposits are seen along the basement membrane. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 54-year-old woman presents to the clinic for epigastric discomfort during the previous month. She states she has not vomited, but reports having epigastric pain that worsens after most meals. The patient states that her stool “looks black sometimes.” The patient does not report any weight loss. She has a past medical history of gastroesophageal reflux disease, diabetes mellitus, peptic ulcer disease, and Crohn’s disease. The patient takes over-the-counter ranitidine, and holds prescriptions for metformin and infliximab. The blood pressure is 132/84 mm Hg, the heart rate is 64/min, the respiratory rate is 14/min, and the temperature is 37.3°C (99.1°F). On physical examination, the abdomen is tender to palpation in the epigastric region. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to accurately determine the diagnosis of this patient?

A 23-year-old college student presents with her parents for a follow-up appointment. She was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and was started on risperidone approx. 2 months ago. She reports a significant improvement since the start of treatment. Her parents report that their daughter’s symptoms of delusions, hallucinations, and paranoid behavior have been ameliorated. On physical examination, the patient seems uncomfortable. She frequently fidgets and repeatedly crosses and uncrosses her legs. When asked if something is troubling her, she gets up and starts pacing. She says, “It’s always like this. I cannot sit still. It is frustrating.” What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old man presents to the clinic for a 3-month history of painful hair loss. He was in his usual state of health until about 3 months ago when he started to develop some painfully itchy spots across his scalp. Since that time these spots have lost hair and scarred, with new spots continuing to form. On further questioning, he shares that, for the last couple of years, he has generally felt poorly, specifically noting intermittent fevers, muscle and joint pains, and fatigue. On physical exam, he has several erythematous and scaly plaques across his scalp. These areas have no hair growth, but some do demonstrate hyperpigmentation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 47-year-old woman presents to the clinic for an evaluation of intense itching of her right thigh region for the past few days. She states some ‘red bumps’ just began to form. The patient mentions that she was recently at a business conference in Miami. She has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes type 2, and hyperlipidemia. She takes enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. She does not smoke or drink. Her vitals are within normal limits today. On physical examination, a linear line with 3 red papules is present along the medial aspect of her right thigh. Additionally, there are small rows of bumps on her left leg and right forearm. Excoriations are also apparent in the same region. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 63-year-old woman presents to the clinic concerned about numbness in her bilateral shoulders and arms for the past 8 weeks. The symptoms started when she fell from scaffolding at work and landed on her back. Initial workup was benign and she returned to normal duty. However, her symptoms have progressively worsened since the fall. She denies fever, back pain, limb weakness, preceding vomiting, and diarrhea. She has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, ischemic heart disease, and a 48-pack-year cigarette smoking history. She takes atorvastatin, hydrochlorothiazide, lisinopril, labetalol, and metformin. Her blood pressure is 132/82 mm Hg, the pulse is 72/min, and the respiratory rate is 15/min. All cranial nerves are intact. Muscle strength is normal in all limbs. Perception of sharp stimuli and temperature is reduced on her shoulders and upper arms. The vibratory sense is preserved. Sensory examination is normal in the lower limbs. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old man comes to the clinic with complaints of joint pain and stiffness for the past few months. His hands, lower back, and left knee are involved and associated with morning stiffness that improves throughout the day with activities. He also complains that his fingers change color upon exposure to cold. He has also noticed a tightening of the skin on his face and thinning of his lips. He feels tired throughout the day and has taken over-the-counter multivitamins that do not seem to help him much. The patient does not smoke cigarettes and drinks alcohol socially. He was diagnosed with hypertension 1 year ago and has been taking hydralazine for the past year. He lost his parents in a road traffic accident 3 years ago. Temperature is 36.7°C (98°F), blood pressure is 140/85 mm Hg, pulse is 72/min, respirations are 12/min, and BMI is 25 kg/m2. His skin appears shiny and slightly thickened, especially his face and hands.
Laboratory investigation:
Complete blood count
Hemoglobin 9.5 g/dl
Leucocytes 5,500/mm3
Platelets 150,000/mm3
ANA positive
Anti-centromere Antibody negative
Anti Scl-70 positive
Anti Jo-1 negative
Anti-histone negative
Anti DsDNA negative
What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 40-year-old Caucasian male presents to your office with fever, fatigue, cold fingers, and the rash shown in Figure A. The presence of which of the following antibodies has the highest specificity for diagnosis of this patient's condition?
A 28-year-old female is found to have 93% HbA, 2% HbF, and 5% HbA2 on hemoglobin electrophoresis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old female is evaluated for frequent epistaxis and mucous membrane bleeding. Physical examination shows diffuse petechiae on the patient’s distal extremities. Peripheral blood smear shows an absence of platelet clumping. An ELISA binding assay reveals that platelet surfaces are deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors. Serum platelet count is normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old female visits her primary care physician because of progressive weight loss. She has a 20-year history of smoking 2 packs of cigarettes a day and was diagnosed with diabetes mellitus 6 years ago. After physical examination, the physician tells the patient she suspects adenocarcinoma at the head of the pancreas. Which of the following physical examination findings would support the diagnosis:

A 27-year-old man presents to your office complaining of right arm numbness and weakness. His past medical history is unremarkable. His family history, however, is significant for the unexpected death of both his parents at age 59 in a motor vehicle accident last week. On physical exam, his bicep, brachioradialis, and patellar reflexes are 2+ bilaterally. CNS imaging shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old woman is brought to your emergency department under arrest by the local police. The patient was found naked at a busy intersection jumping up and down on top of a car. Interviewing the patient, you discover that she has not slept in 2 days because she does not feel tired. She reports hearing voices. The patient was previously hospitalized 1 year ago with auditory hallucinations, paranoia, and a normal mood. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old G2P1 male is concerned that he may father another child with Down syndrome. He states that he may not be able to take care of another child with this disorder. Which of the following tests can confirm the diagnosis of Down syndrome in utero?

A 13-year-old girl re-presents to her pediatrician with a new onset rash that began a few days after her initial visit. She initially presented with complaints of sore throat but was found to have a negative strep test. Her father demanded that she be placed on antibiotics, but this was refused by her pediatrician. The girl's mother, a neurologist, therefore, started her on penicillin. Shortly after starting the drug, the girl developed a fever and a rash. The patient is admitted and her symptoms worsen. Her skin begins to slough off, and the rash covers over 30% of her body. Her oropharynx and corneal membranes are also affected. You examine her at the bedside and note a positive Nikolsky's sign. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 43-year-old male presents to his primary care physician complaining of a gradually enlarging neck mass. He reports that he first developed a firm nodular midline mass on the anterior aspect of his neck two months ago. He is otherwise healthy and takes no medications. A fine-needle aspiration is performed and a histological sample of the specimen is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 57-year-old male visits his primary care physician with 2+ pitting edema in his legs. He takes no medications and does not use alcohol, tobacco, or illicit drugs. 4.5 grams of protein are collected during 24-hour urine excretion. A kidney biopsy is obtained. Examination with light microscopy shows diffuse thickening of the glomerular basement membrane. Electron microscopy shows subepithelial spike and dome deposits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis:

A 22-year-old male presents to your clinic for evaluation of "skin problems." He complains of severe acne and "spots" all over his face that have persisted for the last 8 years, despite innumerable creams and lotions. He reports spending several hours every morning using make-up just to go outside. He wishes to learn about cosmetic procedures or surgeries that could solve his problem. While you perceive his concern for his skin to be genuine, upon examination, you note a healthy-appearing, well-nourished male with a normal complexion, minimal acne and sparse freckles on the nasal bridge. You calculate his BMI to be 21. In addition to making a diagnosis, this patient should be screened for which other disorder?

Two days following the home birth of his son, a father brings the infant to the pediatric emergency room because of bilious vomiting. She is unable to pass meconium and her abdomen is distended. Endoscopic biopsy of the proximal colon demonstrates an absence of Meissner’s and Auerbach’s plexi in the bowel wall. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 37-year-old male visited his primary care physician with a nodular mass in his neck. Fine-needle aspiration of the mass demonstrated malignancy and total thyroidectomy was performed. A histological sample of the excised lesion is shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis:

A 3-year-old girl is brought to the family physician by her parents. They are concerned that she has had multiple nosebleeds in the last 6 months and is always sick compared to other children. During this time period they have also noticed the formation of multiple bruises on her extremities and dry-itching skin on her hands, feet and elbow. On physical exam the physician notes moderate splenomegaly. What is the most likely diagnosis in this child?

A 62-year-old man is evaluated for fatigue 6 months after placement of a mechanical valve due to aortic stenosis. He does not drink alcohol or smoke cigarettes. A complete blood count reports hemoglobin of 9.5 g/L and a reticulocyte percentage of 5.8%. Platelet and leukocyte counts are within their normal ranges. The patient’s physician suspects traumatic hemolysis from the patient’s mechanical valve as the cause of his anemia. Which of the following peripheral blood smear findings would most support this diagnosis?

A 58-year-old Caucasian male presents to his primary care physician with concerns about several recent health changes. The patient has recently gained weight and can't seem to exercise like he used to. He also notes that his thinking seems slow. Physical examination shows thickened, dry skin. Serum analysis confirms the physician's suspicions. Which of the following findings was most helpful in the diagnosis?

An 11-year-old girl presents to your office with pitting edema and proteinuria exceeding 3.5g in 24 hours. You suspect that this patient has experienced a loss of polyanions in her glomerular basement membranes. Which of the following findings would confirm your diagnosis?

A 17-year-old African-American female presents to her family physician after noticing red-tinged urine the week before, when she was suffering from a cold. The patient states that she had experienced that before. Her father is with her and says that this happens to him on occasion as well. What is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 54-year-old male is admitted to the hospital for progressive exertional dyspnea and cough productive of tan-colored liquid for 6 months. He has never smoked a day in his life. A lung biopsy is shown in Figure A that demonstrates tall, columnar cells that line the alveoli septa. The most likely diagnosis for this patient is:

A 45-year-old man presents to his primary care physician with complaints of muscle pains, poor sleep, and daytime fatigue. When asked about stressors he states that he "panics" about his job, marriage, children, and finances. When asked to clarify what the "panics" entail, he states that it involves severe worrying. He has had these symptoms since he last saw you one year ago. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old man who has smoked 2 packs per day for forty years comes to your practice complaining of a chronic cough, dyspnea, hemoptysis, and difficulty rising from a chair. Based on CXR and biopsy slides shown, you feel that all of the following would be consistent with his diagnosis EXCEPT?

An 8-year-old African-American female is found to have a holosystolic, harsh-sounding murmur upon physical examination. The murmur is best appreciated at the left sternal border, and is found to be louder when the patient squats. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 61-year-old female with a past medical history of lung cancer is hospitalized for shortness of breath. During her hospitalization, she is found to be septic and was oozing from her intravenous catheter site. She also develops petechiae on her shoulders and abdomen. Which of the following test results and blood smears is consistent with a diagnosis of disseminated intravascular coagulation?

A 20-year-old college student is brought to her primary care physician by her parents over the New Years holiday because they are concerned about her behavior since right after high school graduation in May the spring before. Prior to this year, she was generally an outgoing and social young woman, who now reportedly has been spending the majority of her time alone in her dorm room and room at home, where her mother and father have overheard her talking to other people when she has no guests. When asked if anything was bothering her at school, she reports that at night the voice of the school's mascot encourages her to save the school from the large oak grove that will soon takeover the student union building by setting the trees on fire for all to see. On exam, she appears to be otherwise healthy and her urine toxicology screen is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old male presents to the emergency department with gross hematuria and acute, colicky flank pain. He denies any previous episodes of hematuria. He reports taking high doses of acetaminophen and aspirin over several weeks due to persistent upper back pain. The patient’s blood pressure and temperature are normal, but he is found to have proteinuria. Physical examination is negative for palpable flank masses. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis:

A 40-year-old female presents to your office complaining that she is too weak to climb stairs or brush her hair. She denies any headaches or change in vision. A muscle biopsy reveals CD8+ lymphocyte infiltration in the endomysium. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old female is brought to her pediatrician after recurrent, prolonged upper respiratory infections over a period of several months. Physical exam reveals petechiae on the patient’s legs and arms. Laboratory studies show hemoglobin: 10 g/L, platelet count: 35,000/mm^3, leukocyte count: 6,600/mm^3. A bone marrow aspiration shows an abundance of lymphoblasts indicative of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). Positive immunostaining for which of the following would support a diagnosis of precursor B-cell leukemia?

A 21-year-old male is brought to the emergency department by his roommate. His roommate says that the patient has been acting “strangely” for the past 10 days. He has noticed that the patient has been moving and talking on the phone at all hours of the night. He doesn’t think that the patient sleeps more than one to two hours a night. He also spends hours pacing up and down the apartment, talking about “trying to save the world.” He also notices that the patient has been speaking very fast. When asking the patient if anything seems different, the patient denies anything wrong, only adding that, “he’s made great progress on his plans." The patient said he has felt like this on one occasion 2 years ago, and he recalled being hospitalized for about 2 weeks. He denies any history of depression, although he said about a year ago he had no energy and had a hard time motivating himself to go to class and see his friends for months. He denies hearing any voices or any visual hallucinations. What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 33-year-old male presents with recent onset of painful urination, fever, and right flank pain. Urinary sediment analysis is positive for the presence of white blood cell casts and Gram-negative bacteria. He has not recently started any new medications. What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 38-year-old male visits your office complaining of several years of joint swelling and stiffness that is worse in the morning and improves throughout the day. Physical examination reveals bilateral deformities at his proximal interphalangeal and metacarpophalangeal joints. The presence of which of the following in this patient’s serum would most help 'rule in' a diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis:

A one-year-old girl presents to your office accompanied by her father. On examination of the girl, you observe the findings shown in Figure A. The appearance of her mother's face is depicted in Figure B.

What is the most likely diagnosis for the girl?

A 32-year-old female presents to her primary care physician with complaints of chronic headaches that have developed and increased in frequency and severity over the last several months. Additionally, the patient has noted she has been less coordinated over the last few weeks, stumbling and tripping often when she is walking. Physical examination is significant for notably reduced hand grip strength bilaterally as well as decreased pain and temperature sensation along the upper back and down both arms to the hands. A referral to the appropriate specialist is made, and an MRI of the brain and neck is obtained. Results of the MRI are shown in Figures A and B. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 4-year-old Caucasian boy previously diagnosed with asthma presents with recurrent sinusitis, otitis media, and clubbing of the nail bed. Family history is significant for a distant cousin with cystic fibrosis. A "sweat test" is performed and comes back normal. What additional diagnostic test would be helpful in establishing a diagnosis?

A 64-year-old man with a history of rheumatic fever presents to his primary care clinician complaining of excessive fatigue with walking and difficulty lying flat. He had no prior physical limitations, but recently has been unable to walk more than 3 blocks without needing to stop and rest. His cardiac exam is notable for a late diastolic murmur heard best at the apex in the left lateral decubitus position with no radiation. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old Caucasian male presents with anemia, malaise, bloating, and diarrhea. Past genetic testing revealed that this patient carries the HLA-DQ2 allele. The physician suspects that the patient's presentation is dietary in cause. Which of the following findings would definitively confirm this diagnosis?

A 27-year-old male has a history of periodic bloody diarrhea over several years. Colonoscopy shows sigmoid colon inflammation, and the patient complains of joint pain in his knees and ankles. You suspect inflammatory bowel disease. Which of the following would suggest a diagnosis of Crohn disease:

A 27-year-old male is brought to the Emergency Department by Fire Rescue after participating in a physical altercation with several commuters on the subway. He appears to be responding to hallucinations and is diaphoretic. His vitals are as follows: T 100.5F (38C), HR 115, BP 155/90, RR 17. His past medical history is notable for a previous ED visit for phencyclidine-related agitation. Which of the following physical findings would most strongly suggest the same diagnosis?

A 42-year-old female presents to your office complaining of dyspnea on exertion. During the interview, the patient notes that she is a contractor specializing in the construction of aviaries at zoos. A radiograph of her chest is shown in Figure A. What is the diagnosis?

A 48-year-old male presents to the emergency room with mental status changes.
Laboratory analysis of the patient's serum shows:
Na 122 mEq/L
K 3.9 mEq/L
HCO3 24 mEq/L
BUN 21 mg/dL
Cr 0.9 mg/dL
Ca 8.5 mg/dL
Glu 105 mg/dL

Urinalysis shows:
Osmolality 334 mOsm/kg
Na 45 mEq/L
Glu 0 mg/dL

Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-year-old girl who recently immigrated to the US is brought to the pediatrician by her father because he has noticed a recent color change in her eyes as demonstrated in Figure A. He is concerned because she has never had significant medical care in her life. Otherwise the girl has no complaints and states that she feels fine. The pediatrician obtains labs which demonstrate: total bilirubin: 5 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 4.5 mg/dL, indirect bilirubin 0.5 mg/dL, AST: 15, ALT: 20, GGT: 10. A liver biopsy is subsequently obtained which is demonstrated in Figure B. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 34-year-old African American male presents complaining of worsening dyspnea and hemoptysis. Serum ACE (angiotensin converting enzyme) levels are elevated. A chest x-ray shown in Figure A suggests the likely diagnosis. Which of the following findings is consistent with this diagnosis?

A 28-year-old Caucasian man with a 10 pack-year history of smoking presents with diarrhea and right, lower quadrant colicky pain. You note tender, red nodules on his shins. Radiograph imaging after barium study is shown in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old female is brought to the emergency department by her father following a seizure. The father reports that she has had a fever for 3 days prior to convulsing while watching TV. You admit the patient to the hospital for further workup and observation. Three days later, you note the appearance of a papular, non-confluent rash on the patient's back, extending superiorly towards the nape of the patient's neck. The abdomen and chest are shown in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old boy is seen by his pediatrician for developmental delay. One year prior, the patient was able to ride a tricycle, stack 3 blocks, and speak in short sentences. Now, he is unable to feed himself and has recently started to point to objects he wants rather than asking. Physical exam reveals a well nourished child sitting in a stroller wringing his hands. Vital signs are normal. The patient's father reports that his 7-year-old daughter is doing well, and that they have no family history of mental retardation or other cognitive disorders. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 51-year-old woman presents complaining of decreased vibratory sense in her lower limbs. Physical exam reveals a widened pulse pressure and a decrescendo murmur occurring after the S2 heart sound. After further questioning, she also reports she experienced a maculopapular rash over her trunk, palms and soles many years ago that resolved on its own. In order to evaluate the suspected diagnosis, the physician FIRST tested for which of the following?

A 48-year-old female presents to her primary physician with the chief complaints of fever, abdominal pain, weight loss, muscle weakness, and numbness in her lower extremities. UA is normal. A biopsy of the sural nerve reveals transmural inflammation and fibrinoid necrosis of small and medium arteries. Chart review reveals a remote history of cigarette smoking as a teenager and Hepatitis B seropositivity. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 73-year-old woman presents with complaints of long standing halitosis. She has recently been having progressive difficulty with swallowing. In the last several weeks, she has also noticed a small amount of regurgitated food on her pillow in the morning. You obtain the radiographic study depicted in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A patient presents to the emergency room in an obtunded state. The patient is a known nurse within the hospital system and has no history of any medical problems. A finger stick blood glucose is drawn showing a blood glucose of 25 mg/dL.

The patient's son immediately arrives at the hospital stating that his father has been depressed recently and that he found empty syringes in the bathroom at the father's home. Which of the following is the test that will likely reveal the diagnosis?

A 68-year-old female visits her primary care physician after an episode of syncope during a tennis match. She reports exertional dyspnea with mild substernal chest pain. On physical exam a systolic crescendo-decrescendo murmur is heard best at the right 2nd intercostal space. This murmur was not heard at the patient's last appointment six months ago. Which of the following would most support a diagnosis of aortic stenosis?

A 2-year-old male with abdominal pain undergoes laparoscopic surgery. An outpouching of tissue is excised from the ileum and sent to the laboratory for evaluation. The pathologist notes inflammation and the presence of mucosa, submucosa, and muscle in the walls of the specimen. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old female presents with complaints of polydipsia and frequent, large-volume urination. Laboratory testing does not demonstrate any evidence of diabetes; however, a reduced urine osmolality of 120 mOsm/L is measured. Which of the following findings on a desmopressin test would be most consistent with a diagnosis of central diabetes insipidus?

A 45-year-old female alcoholic presents with fever, productive cough, and foul-smelling sputum for the past two weeks. Vital signs are T 38.3 C, HR 106, BP 118/64 and RR 16. Oxygen saturation on room air is 90%. Given a diagnosis of aspiration pneumonia, initial chest radiograph findings would most likely include:

A 29-year-old woman, who is a computer programmer, presents to the general medicine clinic complaining of dizziness, fatigue, and shortness of breath. One month ago, the patient went on a camping trip in northern Connecticut. On assessment, vital signs are temperature 36.9°C, blood pressure 100/65, heart rate 41, and respiratory rate 16 with an oxygen saturation of 99%. A print of the EKG strip is shown below (Figure A). She denied any previous medical conditions.

A 62-year-old woman presents to your office for evaluation of a chronic ulcer on the plantar aspect of her right foot. She has a history of peripheral vascular disease and poorly-controlled diabetes mellitus. She states that she has had this ulcer for years, but that it seems to be growing. On examination of her right foot you note the heaped up edges surrounding the ulcer (Figure A). A wedge biopsy reveals irregular masses of anaplastic epidermal cells proliferating down to the dermis and the pathologist reports "keratin pearls". What is the diagnosis?

A 22-year-old man presents to his primary care physician complaining of a red, itchy rash on his elbows and shoulders for 2 months. He has no history of medical problems, and review of systems is positive only for occasional loose stools. He is appropriately prescribed dapsone, which relieves the rash within hours. What is the diagnosis?

An 18-year-old female reports to her physician that she is having repeated episodes of a "racing heart beat". She believes these episodes are occurring completely at random. She is experiencing approximately 2 episodes each week, each lasting for only a few minutes. During the episodes she feels palpitations and shortness of breath, then nervous and uncomfortable, but these feelings resolve in a matter of minutes. She is otherwise well. Vital signs are as follows: T 98.8F, HR 60 bpm, BP 110/80 mmHg, RR 12. Included is a copy of her resting EKG. What is the likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old female presents to her cardiologist to discuss increasing episodes of dyspnea after climbing stairs. She also now needs three pillows at night to sleep. Physical examination reveals an early diastolic murmur best appreciated at the left sternal border with bounding peripheral pulses. The cardiologist is very concerned and immediately refers the patient for a surgical workup. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old man with a medical history significant for asthma, hypertension, and occasional IV drug use comes to the emergency department with fever. On physical exam, there are findings depicted in figure A, for which the patient cannot account. What test will be most helpful to establish the diagnosis?

A 55-year-old female presents to her primary care doctor with several weeks of headaches and low-grade fevers. Her medical history is notable for a motor vehicle accident when she was in her 20's that required multiple blood transfusions, and three separate courses of antibiotics for pneumonia in the past 2 years. Review of systems reveals 10-pound weight loss in last 3 months. She has notable left-sided weakness while walking into the clinic, and, on further exam, she has markedly slurred speech and cervical, axial, and inguinal lymphadenopathy is present. A head CT is ordered, which is shown in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 21-year-old Caucasian female presents to your office with wheezing and rhinitis. Laboratory results show peripheral eosinophilia and antibodies against neutrophil myeloperoxidase. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 46-year-old man presents to a psychiatrist for evaluation. Three months prior, the patient moved to a new apartment building, and since then, he has become increasingly convinced that his doorman has been stealing his packages and going into his apartment while he is not home. He states that objects do not stay where he leaves them, and sometimes he expects mail but never receives it. He has filed numerous complaints with his leasing company. The building has 24-hour security footage, however, which has never shown any other person entering his apartment. On further questioning, the patient denies audiovisual hallucinations or changes in sleep, mood, energy levels, or eating. The family reports that his behavior and affect have not changed. The patient works as a pharmacist. He has no psychiatric history, although his father had a history of major depressive disorder. Which of the following is the likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old Caucasian female presents to your office with hematuria and right flank pain. She has no history of renal dialysis but has a history of recurrent urinary tract infections. You order an intravenous pyelogram, which reveals multiple cysts of the collecting ducts in the medulla. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 37-year-old female with a history of HIV presents to the emergency room with back pain. She reports intermittent fevers for the past week. She reports that she chose to come to the emergency room now because the back pain is more severe and she has also started having trouble controlling her bowels. Her vital signs are Temp 38.5 C, HR 100, BP 110/70, RR 16, and O2 99% on room air. Exam of her arm is shown in Figure A. On physical examination of her back and extremities, there is tenderness to palpation along the lower spine, weakness in the bilateral legs (right greater than left), and hyporeflexia bilaterally. Rectal examination reveals saddle anesthesia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 77-year-old woman comes to your office for a routine visit. She is doing well, and her only complaint is the recent appearance of several brown greasy appearing lesions on her forehead (figure A) that she can't seem to peel off. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old female presents to her primary care physician. The patient has a history of hypertension, which was found to be the result of an adrenal mass. She is status post resection. On physical exam, vital signs are HR 78 bpm, BP 135/90 mmHg, RR 12 rpm, Sat 100%. Examination of the neck reveals a 2 cm firm, immobile, and nontender mass in the right inferior pole of the thyroid. Laboratory evaluation reveals normal TSH, PTH, and calcium. A biopsy of the lesion is obtained, with H&E staining shown in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old Caucasian female presents to your office with hypopigmented skin. She undergoes a skin biopsy and is found to have an absence of melanocytes in the epidermis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-year-old girl is brought to her pediatrician for evaluation of a red rash. She has no past medical history and has met all developmental milestones. On presentation, she is found to have the rash seen in Figure A on her chest. She is told that she does not need any treatments. Two weeks later, she is found to have dozens of rose-colored spots on her back. These lesions do not cause any symptoms and disappear after another 6 weeks. Which of the following is associated with this patient's most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old man comes to the clinic for an annual well-check. His past medical history includes diabetes and hypertension, which are well-controlled with metformin and losartan, respectively. The patient reports a healthy diet consisting of mainly vegetables and lean meat. He denies smoking or alcohol use. He enjoys taking walks with his wife and sunbathing. Physical examination is unremarkable except for a rough, scaly, sand paper-like plaque on his left dorsal hand with no tenderness or pain. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 74-year-old man with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus is brought to his primary care doctor by his son who is concerned about the patient's ability to manage his activities of daily living. He has been living alone since his wife passed away 2 years ago. He has remained an active member of his retirement community's wine club; however, he stopped attending the meetings 3 weeks ago. He is generally able to maintain his house, but his house appears more disorganized over the past 2 weeks. He generally drives short distances but avoids driving long distances as he occasionally gets lost when navigating new areas. He feels like his balance is getting worse, but he has not fallen. He has noticed increased urinary urgency over the past 8 months and has had 2 episodes of incontinence. Despite these changes, he reports feeling well. He drinks 4-6 glasses of wine per day. He was started on multiple medications for worsening anxiety by his psychiatrist 1 month ago. His BMI is 31 kg/m^2. His temperature is 99.8°F (37.7°C), blood pressure is 115/65 mmHg, pulse is 95/min, and respirations are 17/min. On examination, he is oriented to person and time but not place or situation. He does not seem to recognize his doctor despite knowing him for many years. He becomes somnolent intermittently throughout the interview. He can recall 0/3 words after 5 minutes. He has a low-frequency tremor in his right arm that increases in severity with deliberate movement. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 24-year-old man is brought to the hospital by his mother because he has "not been himself" for the past 3 months. The patient says he hears voices in his head. The mother said that when she is talking to her son he can’t seem to make out what he is saying; it is as if his thoughts are disorganized. When talking with the patient, you notice a lack of energy and an apathetic affect. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 45-year-old woman presents to the physician with complaints of intermittent episodes of severe headaches and palpitations. During these episodes, she notices that she sweats profusely and becomes pale in complexion. She describes the episodes as coming and going within the past 2 months. Her temperature is 99.3°F (37.4°C), blood pressure is 165/118 mmHg, pulse is 126/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 90% on room air. Which of the following would be the first medication given to treat this patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 37-year-old man accompanied by his wife presents to the emergency department after loss of consciousness 30 minutes ago. The wife reports that he was sitting in a chair at home and began having sustained rhythmic contractions of all 4 extremities for approximately 1 minute. During transport via ambulance he appeared confused but arousable. His wife reports he has no medical conditions, but for the past 2 months he has occasionally complained of episodes of sweating, palpitations, and anxiety. His brother has epilepsy and his mother has type 1 diabetes mellitus. Laboratory studies obtained in the emergency department demonstrate the following:

Serum:
Na+: 136 mEq/L
K+: 3.8 mEq/L
Cl-: 100 mEq/L
HCO3-: 19 mEq/L
BUN: 16 mg/dL
Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL
Glucose: 54 mg/dL
C-peptide: Low

Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old boy presents to his primary care provider with several months of headaches and impaired vision. Physical exam reveals a male in the 10th percentile for height and 43rd percentile for weight; cranial nerve testing demonstrates bitemporal hemianopsia. He undergoes a head CT, which shows suprasellar calcifications (Figure A). Given his likely diagnosis, which of the following are also derived from the same germ cell layer?

A 38-year-old man presents to his primary care physician for evaluation of 3 months of increasing fatigue. He states that he feels normal in the morning, but that his fatigue gets worse throughout the day. Specifically, he says that his head drops when trying to perform overhead tasks. He also says that he experiences double vision when watching television or reading a book. On physical exam, there is right-sided ptosis after sustaining upward gaze for a 2 minutes. Which of the following treatments may be effective in treating this patient's diagnosis?

A 35-year-old man presents to a psychiatrist for an initial consultation. He reports that for the past 3 years, he has experienced several periods of depressed mood. The episodes do not coincide with any specific life events and seem to resolve after 4-6 weeks. During these episodes, he experiences a depressed mood, sleep disturbances, and a poor appetite, but he at times is able to enjoy spending time with his children and wife but other times he is distressed and cannot enjoy time with them. Upon further questioning, he also reports experiencing occasional episodes of elevated mood over the past ten years. During these episodes, he is very productive at his work as a lawyer and requires less sleep than usual. His past medical history is notable for obesity, type I diabetes mellitus, and rheumatoid arthritis. He is on insulin and takes methotrexate. He smokes marijuana occasionally. His temperature is 99.2°F (37.3°C), blood pressure is 124/80 mmHg, pulse is 78/min, and respirations are 17/min. On exam, he is quiet with a flattened affect, but is cooperative and answers questions thoroughly. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A parent-teacher conference is called to discuss the behavior of a 9-year-old girl. According to the girl's teacher, she has become progressively more disruptive during class. She is performing poorly in school and has trouble focusing. She is destructive to classroom property, tore a classmate's art project, and takes other children's lunches regularly. She is avoided by her classmates. Her father reports that his daughter can "sometimes be difficult." Recently she placed a rubber band around the cat's tail, resulting in gangrene. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old woman presents to her physician with a complaint of lower back pain and stiffness for the past few months. She describes the pain as being worse in the morning and then gradually improving with activity throughout the day. On physical exam, she has decreased anterior flexion of the lumbar spine. A radiograph of her lumbar spine is obtained and is shown in Figure A. What is the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old man comes to the clinic complaining of headache and sinus drainage for the past 13 days. He reports cold-like symptoms 2 weeks ago that progressively got worse. The patient endorses subjective fever, congestion, sinus headache, cough, and chills. He claims that this is his 5th episode within the past year and is concerned if “there’s something else going on.” His medical history is significant for asthma that is adequately controlled with his albuterol inhaler. His laboratory findings are shown below:

Serum:
Hemoglobin: 16.2 g/dL
Hematocrit: 39 %
Leukocyte count: 7,890/mm^3 with normal differential
Platelet count: 200,000/mm^3
IgA: 54 mg/dL (Normal: 76-390 mg/dL)
IgE: 0 IU/mL (Normal: 0-380 IU/mL)
IgG: 470 mg/dL (Normal: 650-1500 mg/dL)
IgM: 29 mg/dL (Normal: 40-345 mg/dL)

What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old female presents to her primary care physician complaining of increased fatigue over the last year. She also says that her friends say she appears to be more pale. Her past medical history is significant for 10 years of arthritis. Physical exam reveals spoon shaped nails as well as conjunctival pallor. Based on clinical suspicion RBC tests are ordered showing an mean corpuscular volume (MCV) of 75 fl (normal 80-100 fl) and a peripheral blood smear is obtained and found to be normal. Iron studies shows a serum iron of 30 micromolar (normal range 50-170) and a serum ferritin of 300 micrograms/liter (normal range 15-200). What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 22-year-old woman presents to a psychiatrist complaining of mood fluctuations. She is accompanied by her mother who reports that the patient recently experienced a 5-day episode of minimal sleep and unusual levels of energy. The patient admits to spending $2,000 of her parent’s money, without asking, on a down payment for a motorcycle. The episode resolved after 5 days, at which point the patient felt guilty and upset. The patient’s medical history is notable for multiple month-long episodes in the past 2 years of feeling sad, sleeping more than usual, being uninterested in her hobbies, and feeling constantly tired and guilty. The patient has a history of severe meningoencephalitis at the age of 17 requiring four days in the intensive care unit. During that episode, she reported seeing monkeys in her hospital room. On exam, she is a well-appearing, cooperative female in no acute distress. She is alert and oriented with a normal affect. She states that she feels sad and guilty about what happens. She denies suicidal ideation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 17-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her parents who are concerned about her bizarre behavior. Over the past three months, she has become withdrawn from her friends and less interested in her classes and extracurricular activities. On several occasions, she has torn apart rooms in their home looking for “bugs” and states that the President is spying on her because aliens have told the government that she is a threat. Although she has always been quite clean in the past, her father notes that the patient’s room is now malodorous with clothes and dishes strewn about haphazardly. She also says that sometimes she can hear the devil speaking to her from inside her head. She has no medical problems, does not drink alcohol or use any drugs. Physical examination of the girl reveals no abnormalities. On mental status examination, the girl is oriented to person, place and time. She avoids eye contact and replies mostly with monosyllabic responses. She appears distracted, and confirms that she is hearing whispering voices in her head. What is the most appropriate diagnosis for this patient?

A 34 year-old-female with a previous diagnosis of Grave’s disease presents for a check-up. Since her diagnosis 4 months ago, the patient’s symptoms have been relatively well-controlled with medications since starting them 3 weeks ago after an initial unsuccessful course of radioiodine ablation. The patient’s complete blood count reveals decreased absolute neutrophils at 450/mL and a slightly decreased hematocrit of 39%. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient’s abnormal laboratory results?

A 28-year-old female presents to trauma surgery clinic after undergoing an exploratory laparotomy, femoral intramedullary nail, and femoral artery vascular repair 3 months ago. She suffered multiple gunshot wounds as a victim of a drive-by shooting. She is progressing well with well-healed surgical incisions on examination. She states during her clinic visit that she has been experiencing 6 weeks of nightmares where she "relives the day she was shot." The patient also endorses 6 weeks of flashbacks to "the shooter pointing the gun at her" during the daytime as well. She states that she has had difficulty sleeping and cannot concentrate when performing tasks. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old African American female presents to her primary care provider complaining of progressively worsening back pain. The pain is localized to the lower back and sometimes wakes her up from sleep. She has a history of hypertension and admits to a 50 pack-year smoking history. Further questioning reveals that she has also experienced fatigue and an unintentional weight loss of 18 pounds over the past year. A 10-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his parents due to 2 months of a progressively worsening headache. The headaches were initially infrequent and his parents attributed them to stress from a recent move. A tall, 25-year-old woman is brought to the ED by her friend after sudden difficulty breathing while smoking a cigarette. In the trauma bay she is tachypneic, but able to talk to you. A chest x-ray is obtained and shown below. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 78-year-old female presents to the emergency room with crampy abdominal pain and bloating. Her last bowel movement was three days ago and she has not passed gas over the same time period. Her past medical history is notable for Alzheimer's disease, hypertension, and stable angina. She takes donezepil, aspirin, enalapril, and metoprolol. A frontal abdominal radiograph is shown in Figure A. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 46-year-old man presents to his primary care physician with one week of intermittent nausea and vomiting. He does not have any sick contacts, and his medical history is significant only for diabetes well-controlled on metformin. He also complains of some weakness and back/leg pain. He says that he recently returned from traveling abroad and had been administered an antibiotic during his travels for an unknown infection. On presentation, his temperature is 98.6°F (37°C), blood pressure is 119/78 mmHg, pulse is 62/min, and respirations are 25/min. An EKG is obtained showing flattening of the T wave. After further testing, the physician prescribes a thiazide for this patient. Which of the following diseases is also associated with this patient's most likely diagnosis?

A 9-year-old girl is brought to the emergency room by her father for weakness, diaphoresis, and syncope. Her father says that she has never been diagnosed with any medical conditions but has been having “fainting spells” over the past month. Routine lab work reveals a glucose level of 25 mg/dL. The patient is promptly given glucagon and intravenous dextrose and admitted to the hospital for observation. The patient’s father stays with her during her hospitalization. The patient is successfully watched overnight and her blood glucose levels normalize on her morning levels. The care team discusses a possible discharge during morning rounds. One hour later the nurse is called in for a repeat fainting episode. A c-peptide level is drawn and shown to be low. The patient appears ill, diaphoretic, and is barely arousable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this child?

A young Mediterranean teen brings his 4-year-old little sister to the Emergency Room because of a high temperature. Their parents are on their way to the hospital, but, in the meantime, he provides some of the history. He explains that she has been running a fever and limping for the past week. This morning, he had trouble awakening her, and he noticed some swelling and redness around her right ankle. In terms of her past medical history, he knows she has something wrong with her blood. She had to receive extra vaccinations as an infant, and she takes an antibiotic every day. On exam in the ED, her temperature is 102.4 deg F (39.1 deg C), blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg, pulse is 123/min, and respirations are 22/min. She is lethargic, and her exam is noteworthy for erythema and edema in an area surrounding her distal shin. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 18-year-old female is seen for a routine physical prior to starting college. She will be moving from Ohio to California, away from her family for the first time. Her temperature is 36.8 deg C (98.2 deg F), pulse is 74/min, and blood pressure is 122/68 mmHg. BMI is 24. On questioning, she reveals that she has a habit of binge eating during times of stress, particularly during exams. She then feels guilty about her behavior and attempts to compensate by going to the gym, sometimes for 4+ hours per day. She is disturbed by this behavior and feels out of control. She denies ever vomiting as a means of losing weight. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old man thinks poorly of himself and is extremely sensitive to criticism. He is socially inhibited and has never had a romantic relationship, although he desires one. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old woman presents to the emergency department for chest pain. She says that the chest pain began a few hours prior to presentation and is associated with nausea, abdominal discomfort, and sweating. She has experienced similar symptoms multiple times in the past, which brings her great concern because she believes she may be having a heart attack. This concern has persisted for 2 months. This has caused her to avoid taking long train rides or driving on divided highways. Approximately 7 months ago her parents divorced. Medical history is significant for obesity. She denies any medications or illicit drug use. Physical examination is unremarkable. An electrocardiogram demonstrates sinus tachycardia with a pulse of 110/min. Which of the following is most likely the diagnosis?

A parent-teacher conference is called to discuss the behavior of a 9 year-old girl. According to the girl's teacher, she has become progressively more disruptive during class. When asked to help clean up or read out-loud, she replies with "You're not the boss of me." or "You can't make me." She refuses to participate in gym class, but will play the same games during recess. She gets along with and is well-liked by her peers. Her father reports that his daughter can "sometimes be difficult," but she is helpful around the house and is very good playing with her 7-year-old brother. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old man presents to his primary care physician for a checkup. He has felt weaker lately and has lost some weight. He denies any urinary issues. His BUN at his last visit 4 months ago was 45 mg/dL, and his creatinine was 2.0 mg/dL. His laboratory studies this visit are seen below:

An 18-year-old woman presents to the student health department at her university for recurrent palpitations. The patient had previously presented to the emergency department (ED) for sudden onset palpitations five months ago when she first started college. She had a negative cardiac workup in the ED and she was discharged with a 24-hour Holter monitor which was also negative. She has no history of any medical or psychiatric illnesses. The patient reports that since her initial ED visit, she has had several episodes of unprovoked palpitations associated with feelings of dread and lightheadedness though she cannot identify a particular trigger. Recently, she has begun sitting towards the back of the lecture halls so that she can “quickly escape and not make a scene” in case she gets an episode in class. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 43-year-old homeless woman is brought to the emergency room for severe abdominal pain. She is known to the emergency department for repeated visits for alcohol intoxication. She reports that the pain started about 3 hours ago and describes it as sharp, piercing, 10/10, and concentrated at the epigastric region with radiation to the back.
