A physical examination demonstrates epigastric tenderness and the finding shown in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 19-year-old college student is brought to the emergency department by her roommates after being found unconscious on their dorm room floor. Her temperature is 102.0°F (38.9°C) and blood pressure is 85/64 mmHg. On physical examination, she has multiple rose-colored spots on the skin covering her abdomen and lower limbs. Lab tests reveal hyperkalemia and an arterial blood gas test that reads pH: 7.04, pCO2: 30.1 mmHg, pO2: 23.4 mmHg. What is the most likely diagnosis for this patient’s condition?

A 17-year-old teenage girl is brought to the emergency room for severe right upper quadrant (RUQ) pain for the past 5 hours. She denies any precipitating events and reports a sharp, 8/10, constant pain at the RUQ. She denies any past episodes. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she is up to date on her vaccinations. Her mother reports a “blood disease” on her father’s side. Which of the following laboratory findings will confirm this patient’s diagnosis?

A 45 year old construction worker complains of several weeks of diffuse abdominal pain, constipation, generalized fatigue and irritability. Her vital signs are normal. On examination you notice some distal extremity weakness and thin, a grey-blue line visible along the margin of the gums (Figure A). Red blood cells demonstrate microcytosis, hypochromasia and basophilic with visible dots (Figure B). What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-year-old female is brought to your psychiatric clinic after she was caught stealing her peers’ belongings multiple times by her teacher. She is a straight-A student with many friends and is an outstanding football player. She describes her family as very loving and gets along with her older siblings. She also states that she has no ill will towards anyone she stole from in class. Although never caught, she admits that she would often steal things in stores or locker rooms when no one was looking in order to satisfy an intense impulse. Which of the following is the best diagnosis for this patient?

A 14-year-old previously healthy female presents to your office with complaints of two months of dull, aching pain in her right leg that has recently become worse. While she experiences the pain constantly, she notes that it is sometimes so bad at night that it awakes her from her sleep. Though an avid soccer player, she has been unable to participate this season due to the pain and difficulty running. She cannot think of any particular trauma that might have precipitated this pain. Vitals are all within normal range. Physical examination reveals localized tenderness below the knee with mild swelling and reduced range of motion. You order an X-ray of the painful limb, which is shown in Figure A. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old Caucasian man presents with a three-month history of weight loss, anxiety, and tremors. He recalls frequent heart palpitations and new discomfort while being outside in the heat. His labs include a TSH level of 0.1 mIU/L. Additionally, the patient’s serum is positive for antibodies that stimulate the TSH receptor. What process is unique to this patient’s diagnosis?

An 85-year-old woman presents to her primary care provider after feeling "lightheaded." She said she helped her husband in the garden for the first time, but that while moving some bags of soil she felt like she was going to faint. She had a big breakfast of oatmeal and eggs prior to working in the garden. She has no significant past medical history and takes a baby aspirin daily. Physical exam reveals an elderly, well-nourished, well-built woman with no evidence of cyanosis or tachypnea. Vital signs show normal temperature, BP 150/70, HR 80, RR 18. Cardiac exam reveals crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur. What is the most likely cause of this patient's diagnosis?

A 5-year-old girl is brought to the emergency room by her parents due to worsening cough, fever, and difficulty breathing in the past 2 days. Physical exam reveals a barking cough and use of accessory muscles for breathing. After a full clinical workup, she is diagnosed with an upper respiratory infection caused by a parainfluenza virus. Which of the following findings in the clinical workup of this patient supported the diagnosis?

A 55-year-old female was picked up by police in the public library for harassing the patrons and for public nudity. She displayed disorganized speech and believed that the books were the only way to her salvation. Identification was found on the woman and her brother was called to provide more information. He described that she recently lost her house and got divorced within the same week although she seemed fine three days ago. The woman was sedated with diazepam and chlorpromazine because she was very agitated. Her labs returned normal and within three days, she appeared normal, had no recollection of the past several days, and discussed in detail how stressful the past two weeks of her life were. She was discharged the next day. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnosis for this female?

A 31-year-old Caucasian female presents to her physician's complaining of heartburn and diarrhea for 2 months. She reports a history of tumors of the parathyroid and pituitary glands. A 56-year-old woman is brought to the emergency room for severe chest pain over the past hour. She reports 10/10, burning pain that is retrosternal and concentrated around the mid-chest region. Her husband claims that she has been throwing up for the past several hours from what seems like a “stomach bug,” with the latest 2 episodes of emesis being bright red. The patient denies trauma, fever, recent infections, urinary changes or diarrhea but endorses lightheadedness and shortness of breath. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and diabetes. A computed tomography (CT) with IV and oral contrast of the chest and abdomen is obtained and its results are shown in Figure A. What is the most specific physical examination findings for this patient’s diagnosis?

A 55-year-old female visited her primary care physician complaining of chest pain and progressive shortness of breath worsened by exertion. Her vital signs were within normal limits. She reports that she worked in a naval shipyard for 10 years during her twenties. A CT scan of her chest shows diffuse thickening of the pleura and a diagnosis of mesothelioma is made. Assuming this diagnosis is correct, which of the following is most likely to also be present in this patient?

A 28-year-old Caucasian man presents to your office with recurrent abdominal cramping on his left side for 6 months. He additionally reports bloody diarrhea and tenesmus. You suspect ulcerative colitis. Which of the following findings would most strongly confirm your diagnosis?

A 59-year-old woman presents to the physician complaining of a blistering rash on her hands that comes and goes. At different times, the rash has affected her hands, legs, inguinal creases, and the corners of her mouth. Her past medical history is significant for a blood clot in her left lower extremity. On further questioning, she admits that she has been feeling very depressed for the past few months even though there haven’t been any major changes in her life that she can think of that would have caused these feelings. On physical exam, temperature is 98.4°F (38.9°C), blood pressure is 118/75 mmHg, pulse is 65/min, and respirations are 12/min. She is slender and appears tired. Her skin exam is remarkable for the findings shown in Figure A. Her blood glucose is 280 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 54-year-old man presents to his primary care physician complaining of watery diarrhea for the last 3 weeks. He reports now having over 10 bowel movements per day. He denies abdominal pain or rash. A basic metabolic profile is notable for the following: Na: 127 mEq/L; K 2.1 mEq/L; Glucose 98 mg/dL. Following additional work-up, octreotide was started with significant improvement in symptoms and laboratory values. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 39-year-old woman presents to a primary care clinic for a routine physical exam. She denies any complaints. She has a long beard and hair, wears several copper bracelets, and a crystal amulet. When asked about her diet, she discloses eating mostly canned foods, which she has stockpiled in her cabin in case there is a natural disaster or "apocalypse" (though she admits that this is highly unlikely). She has a few close friends, but feels awkward when meeting new people. She seems happy overall and has many long-standing interests, including hiking and astrology. She has been steadily employed as a data scientist and a paranormal investigator. She has never been diagnosed with a mental illness, though she has a family history of schizophrenia. Review of systems is negative for depressed mood, anxiety, or hallucinations. Thought process is linear and reality testing is intact. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A 15-year-old male presents to your office for evaluation of a painful neck mass. The family reports the patient has had a midline neck mass for many years, but had become painful over the past week with erythema at the overlying skin. The patient denies subjective fevers at home. The patient has an otherwise unremarkable past medical history. His temperature is 100.1 deg F (37.8 deg C), blood pressure is 110/70 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, and respirations are 15/min. Clinical exam is seen in Figure A. The mass is noted to rise with deglutition and tongue protrusion. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old male with hypertension and diabetes presents with severe chest pain. He describes the pain as sharp at the mid-sternum without radiation. An 8-year-old girl is brought to the pediatric emergency department by her parents with a complaint of abdominal pain and diarrhea for the past week. Her parents note that they attended a neighbor’s barbecue last weekend, but otherwise have not eaten any new foods or changed their usual diet. The patient is admitted to the hospital unit for further work-up. The provider team finds that the patient’s blood is positive for Shiga-like toxin and notes the following lab values: creatinine of 4.2 mg/dL, platelet count of 50,000/mm^3, and hemoglobin of 6.0 g/dL. A 26-year-old woman with HIV and a recent CD4+ count of 800 presents to her PCP with fever, cough, and dyspnea. Her temperature is 102.6°F (39.2°C), pulse is 75/min, respirations are 24/min, and blood pressure is 135/92 mmHg. The chest radiography is notable for bilateral diffuse interstitial infiltrates. For definitive diagnosis, the physician obtains a sputum sample. A 5-year-old patient is brought to the emergency department by her parents for concerning behavior. The patient has her eyes open during these episodes but does not respond to her parents’ voice or her name. These episodes last between 1-2 minutes after which the patient appears to return back to awareness. The patient is confused after these episodes and appears not to know where she is for about 15 minutes. These episodes occur once every few days and the most recent one happened about 10 minutes before the patient arrived to the emergency department. On arrival, the patient is mildly confused and does not know where she is or what recently happened. She is slow to respond to questions and appears tired. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

A 27-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with general weakness and fatigue. She states that she has not felt well for several days and can't take care of herself anymore due to fatigue. The patient has a past medical history of IV drug abuse, alcohol abuse, and multiple minor traumas associated with intoxication. Her temperature is 104°F (40°C), blood pressure is 127/68 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, respirations are 19/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. A murmur is heard on cardiac exam. The patient is treated appropriately and transferred to the inpatient floor and recovers over the next several days. The patient has been unable to eat solids, though she has been drinking large amounts of juice. On day 5 of her stay, the patient states she feels much better. She is no longer febrile. Her only concern is profuse and watery diarrhea and severe abdominal pain which she has been experiencing since yesterday. The patient is started on IV fluids and given oral fluid replacement as well. Which of the following is associated with the most likely underlying diagnosis?

A 34-year-old female with a history of alcohol use is brought to the emergency department by ambulance after being found down on a Saturday night. She is difficult to arouse and has slurred speech when awake. She is febrile to 102°F (38.9 °C) and complains of right upper quadrant pain. Physical exam reveals shifting dullness in the abdomen and a palpable, tender liver edge. Lab tests show:

Alanine aminotransferase (ALT): 112 U/L

Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg): Negative

A 14-year-old female of eastern European descent presents to the free clinic at a university hospital for a respiratory infection, which her mother explains occurs quite frequently. A urinalysis revealed large amounts of heparan and dermatan sulfate. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 28-year-old woman presents to the physician complaining of recent unintentional weight loss, flatulence, and foul-smelling stools. She reports having severe abdominal cramping that is worse in her right upper abdomen as well as intermittent bloody stools. She is prescribed a medication and advised to refrain from alcohol consumption to avoid adverse effects of the drug. Which of the following findings on pathology would most likely correspond to the patient’s diagnosis?

A 21-year-old female presents to the ED with a stab wound to the right neck. The patient is alert and responsive, and vital signs are stable. Which of the following neurologic findings would most likely support the diagnosis of right-sided spinal cord hemisection?

A 4-year-old girl presents to the ophthalmologist for a down- and inward dislocation of the lens in her left eye. On physical exam, the girl has a marfanoid habitus and mental retardation.
